body:
This documentation update records the final validation state for the skill bundle merged in #781 and adds a safe activation precondition for the GitHub CLI preview. It does not change skill instructions, plugin manifests, package code, or runtime behavior.

Setup safety:

- Before `pascal update`, save or otherwise persist active project work and disconnect editor and agent clients from the local service.
- `pascal update` may stop and restart the managed editor and MCP processes.
- Keeping the same `PASCAL_HOME` preserves persisted project data in that directory, but it does not preserve unsaved or unbound in-memory changes, undo history, or active client sessions.
- Both public setup references retain the one-active-client boundary and explain why `pascal update` is required to activate the preview instead of reusing an older healthy service.

- The one-run D02 automatic-routing baseline failed at frozen 94/100 against its 95/100 threshold. It was 94/96 on structurally valid observations; four budget-limit invalid observations count as failures. Both positive classes were 25/25. The two semantic false activations used the full per-class and combined negative activation allowances, with no headroom. Each Pascal skill had 25/26 precision.
- Forty-six terminal cost receipts total $6.7027235. Fifty-four early Skill captures have unknown cost, not zero cost.

The D02 run has no prior-version comparison, so this update makes no routing-improvement or automatic-routing promotion claim. Independent post-run audit reproduced the score byte-for-byte, verified all 388 manifest entries, and found no material defect.

title: Carry collections through Save Build / Load Build
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #734 — Save Build / Load Build dropped collections on both sides. Same shape as #729 (materials):

- `handleSaveBuild` now includes `collections` in the saved `sceneData`.
- `validateBuildJson` gets a `collections` pass: each entry is checked against the `Collection` shape (`id`, `name`, `nodeIds: string[]`, optional `color`/`controlNodeId`); invalid entries are skipped with an `invalid_collections` warning that names the skipped ids, a non-object `collections` is ignored with a warning. Valid entries land on `parsed.collections`.
- `handleConfirmImport` passes `parsed.collections` through to `setScene` (which already accepted `extra.collections`).

## How to test

1. Create a collection in the editor, Save Build, then Load Build the same file → the collection is still there (before: gone).
2. `bun --cwd packages/core run test` — 4 new tests in `validate-build-json.test.ts` under `collections` (carry-through, per-entry skip with warning, non-object warning, absent → omitted from `parsed`).
3. Reverting the `validate-build-json.ts` change makes 3 of those tests fail; with it they pass. Full `packages/core` suite: 1430 pass / 0 fail. `packages/editor` tests: 836 pass / 0 fail, `tsc --noEmit` for `packages/editor` clean.

## Screenshots / screen recording

n/a — no UI change, only the saved file contents and the import pass.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (verified via the package test suites + `tsc --noEmit` instead; happy to add a clip if you'd like one)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to build JSON validation and settings-panel save/import wiring; no auth or security paths, and invalid collection data is warn-and-skip rather than hard-failing import.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **collections being dropped** on Save Build and Load Build, mirroring the existing materials round-trip.
> 
> **Save Build** now writes `collections` from the scene store into the exported JSON alongside nodes, materials, and plugins. **Load Build** passes `parsed.collections` into `setScene` after import validation.
> 
> **`validateBuildJson`** gains a collections pass: valid entries (required `id`, `name`, `nodeIds: string[]`, optional `color` / `controlNodeId`) appear on `parsed.collections`; bad entries are skipped with an **`invalid_collections`** warning that lists skipped ids; a non-object `collections` field is ignored with a warning; absent collections stay omitted from `parsed`. Four unit tests cover carry-through, partial skip, invalid top-level shape, and omission when missing.

title: perf(editor): instance the ceiling corner brackets per level
body:
## perf(editor): instance the ceiling corner brackets per level (perf row 11)

Select mode mounted three transparent meshes per ceiling corner for every ceiling on the level (1 236 meshes on
the rich 4× fixture, each with its own material and R3F handlers). The brackets are a deliberate
discoverability affordance, so they stay on every ceiling — but they now render as **two `InstancedMesh`
per level** (normal + highlighted opacity) sharing the unit box, with `instanceColor` for the gray/indigo
tints and per-instance R3F over/out events. Drag/snap/SFX/live-override/`ceiling:click` lifecycle is
unchanged.

**Measured** (rich 4×, load pose, pointer parked, headless Chromium, rebuilt dist):

| idle | build tool | select mode |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| main | 9.1 ms / 1 646 objects | 10.6 ms / 1 738 objects |
| this PR (+ #mixer PR) | 8.9 ms / 1 646 | **8.4 ms / 1 614** |

and Maxi): ≤ 0.009 % pixels differ, outline colour census identical. E2E: perf-regression-pack,

title: fix(mcp): declare 2020-12 dialect for tools/list schemas
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #696 — every tool call against the local `@pascal-app/mcp` server fails on clients that enforce JSON Schema 2020-12, because `tools/list` declares `draft-07`.

The MCP SDK's `McpServer` builds each tool's `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` with `toJsonSchemaCompat` and no `target`, so the compat layer falls back to `draft-07`. There's no version bump or `registerTool` option that changes this. The generated schemas contain no draft-07-only keywords (`definitions`, `dependencies`, `$ref`), so the fix re-registers the `tools/list` handler after tool registration and retargets the declared `$schema` to `https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema` on the way out — the approach the maintainer outlined in the issue.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/core && bun run build` (mcp tests import built `@pascal-app/core/schema`)
2. `cd ../mcp && bun test`

New regression test `src/tools/schema-dialect.test.ts` asserts the raw `tools/list` payload only declares 2020-12 (validating through the SDK client — as the existing contract test does — would not catch this, since the client uses the SDK's own validator).

## Validation (real results)

- `bun test` (packages/mcp): **357 pass, 0 fail** (52 files)
- New test alone: pass
- RED→GREEN: removing `normalizeToolSchemaDialect(server)` makes the new test fail with the raw dialect showing `http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#`; restoring it turns it green.
- `biome check` clean on the changed files; `tsc -p tsconfig.json` clean.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — headless MCP/server change, covered by the test above.

- [x] I've tested this locally (`bun test`)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (`bun check`)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (CHANGELOG)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: perf(nodes): batch ceiling undersides and slab bodies (charter row 16)
body:
## Metric

**rich-4× idle frame CPU** (charter backlog row 16): ceilings and slabs — 696 opaque, level-parented, one-geometry-per-node meshes on that fixture — draw through the per-level `BatchedMesh` containers of `shared/node-batch/` like items, columns, doors and windows already do.

Same-load PR-vs-main pairs (the machine ran at load average ~7 all afternoon, so absolute numbers are inflated and only back-to-back pairs are quoted):

| fixture | idle frame CPU | idle draws | hover CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| rich 4× (the metric) | 9.1 → 8.3 ms (−9 %; −15 % in a second pair) | 4 343 → 3 219 | 10.1 → 8.8 |
| rich 2× | **9.3 → 4.9 ms (−47 %)** | 2 580 → 2 018 | 8.4 → 5.0 |
| Maxi 8× | **15.2 → 10.9 ms (−28 %)** | 5 472 → 1 376 | 15.9 → 11.8 |
| tower 2×18 | 6.0 → 5.4 ms (−10 %) | 4 219 → 1 147 | 6.6 → 5.9 |
| Maxi 1×/2×/4× | within the noise band at 2–4 ms | 999 → 487 / 1 587 → 563 / 2 877 → 833 | — |

Like-gesture edit receipts (wall/door body moves, undo) are flat or better; every fixture ends at dirty 0 with zero phantom marks. One receipt regressed deterministically (rich-2×, moving the wall behind a ceiling-hosted light: 32 frames vs 6–9) and turned out to be a real bug this batching exposed: the grid raycaster never enabled `BATCHED_LAYER`, so the ground ray under a dragged wall missed the now-batched slab, the wall jumped 8.5 m and created a bridge wall (135 walls re-marked). Fixed in dd745a0e (291 ms / 8 frames after, main 336 / 8), and the same guard was applied to every non-hover raycaster that can hit batched sources first-person door/window targeting, item/column support caps, accessory placement, door/window paint, wall paint — 7a64290f; the support-cap and door/window ones were already exposed on main for the kinds batched since #760. The audit table of all 35 raycasters lives in the private charter folder.

## What it took (beyond adding two kinds)

- **Ceiling dirty marks were consumed before the batch could see them.** `viewer/src/systems/ceiling/ceiling-system.tsx` consumed at `useFrame` priority 0; the batch snapshots pending marks at 1. It now consumes at 2 like `GeometrySystem` (definition `system.priority` orders components, not frames — `node-definitions.md` said otherwise and is corrected).
- **The coloured ceiling underside was `transparent: true` with opacity 1** (introducing commit 967a905e calls it opaque; no fade). Now opaque, so it batches in the default textures-on appearance. Blend order against glass changes by a few hundred pixels (parity below).
- **Slab default side materials were created fresh per slab**, so sides could never share a batch or a GLB material. They now use the viewer default cache; the legacy slab cache marks its materials as cached so rebuild disposal skips shared instances, and a cache clear rebuilds slabs and releases batches before disposing (after the next frame).
- **Surfaces move through `useLiveTransforms`, and paint previews swap materials on every fan-out target, without dirty marks.** Both release now and defer joins; a paint commit ends its holds through a single owner (`paint-preview-owner.ts`) — the first cut leaked the hold forever on commit and reached columns/doors/windows too; an apply() that throws after the scene write ends holds without restoring stale materials.
- **Shadow flags are part of the container identity** (ceilings cast none, slabs cast and receive); `externalSelectedIds` release like local selection; hidden-level candidates are re-offered when the level comes back.
- **Rebuilt surface geometry replaces instead of appending.** `release()` used to keep obsolete packed geometry in `used` until an overflow rebuilt the whole bucket. Surfaces now own a stable slot with 25 % headroom and rejoin via `setGeometryAt` when the new geometry fits; overflow rebuilds size from live geometry only; multi-node releases flush once per frame; an emptied container survives the quiet window; released surfaces on a level wait while any wall there carries a live override and until the wall queue drains, then join in one wave. Counters under `__pascalPerf.batchStats()` (releases, joins, replacements, overflow rebuilds, bytes copied).
- **Found by the bake gate, pre-existing:** the merged wall batch never carried `pascalExport = 'strip'`, so a capture that landed while it was sewn exported 80 k duplicate wall vertices. Fixed (separate commit).
- Perf receipts for `drag:move` now carry the moved node id (scope `nodeId`), so the matrix runner can refuse to diff unlike gestures.

## Gates

- **Editing:** private e2e gate 9/9 (perf-regression pack ×5, batched-wall click, hidden-wall click, floor placement, slab room paint), twice.
- **Visual:** `outline-parity.ts` poses H/S/SH/SI on rich 4× + Maxi 1×: 0.36–0.46 % pixels differ, localized to window glass, glass-room seams and two small floor patches; selection census identical on the stable poses (the 3a/3b batching row accepted 0.4 % of the same kind).
- **Bake:** rich-2× raw GLB node/mesh/texture/animation sets identical to main's minus the leaked `wall-batch` meshes; materials 91 → 60 (deduplicated slab defaults), −1.1 MB.
- Unit: `bun test packages/nodes --randomize --seed=1` 2 127 pass; discriminating tests for every mechanism above (the new node-batch tests were written to fail without each fix).
- Four independent review rounds (read-only recon → audit → perf diagnosis → audit of the fix round) closed one blocker and eight should-fixes; the two diagnoses are recorded in the charter.

## Follow-ups filed (idea inbox, not changed here)

- The editor's standalone undo marks every node dirty on top of core's changed-node diff (`history.ts` `refreshSceneAfterHistoryJump`), releasing every batched member on every level per undo.
- Window move on rich-4× spends 12–17 s in long tasks on main and on this branch alike.

Charter: `plans/performance/editor-scalable-scene-runtime.md` row 16 (private PR follows with the evidence row, dashboard refresh and the gesture-aware runner).

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large changes to batch membership, material cache lifecycle, and many editor raycast paths; regressions would show up as wrong placement, paint, or support surfaces rather than auth/data issues.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends **level `BatchedMesh` batching** to **ceilings and slabs** (alongside items, columns, doors/windows), with a reworked batch store: per-shadow containers, reserved geometry slots for mutable surfaces, coalesced releases, and deferred empty-container disposal. Sources stay mounted but draw-hidden; **live transforms**, **slot paint previews**, **external selection**, and **material cache clears** now release and re-offer batch members on the same rules as hover/selection.
> 
> **Raycasting** for tools and walkthrough no longer misses batched floors/slabs: non-hover raycasters call **`setSurfaceRaycastLayers`** so hits still use source meshes when batch draws take over. **Ceiling rebuild timing** moves to frame priority **2** so the batch’s priority-1 dirty snapshot sees geometry changes; ceiling underside materials are **opaque** so they can batch in the default appearance.

Wall merged batches and node batches are tagged **`pascalExport: 'strip'`** for GLB capture.

title: Fail closed on missing furniture-fit inputs
body:
The furniture-fit skill could answer a decisive missing measurement with speculative conditional thresholds. This release makes the input gate fail closed: it preserves supplied values, requests only the blocking input, permits a minimal read-only scene lookup only when that lookup can resolve the value from measured evidence, and blocks assessment or mutation until the input is resolved.

It also releases the skill as `furniture-fit` 0.1.2 in plugin bundle 0.1.3 and corrects the hosted Claude/Codex setup examples. Claude setup now guards an existing `PASCAL_API_KEY` instead of assigning a placeholder; Codex guidance explicitly requires replacing the placeholder and documents that Codex stores the environment-variable name.

- `bun scripts/validate-skills.ts`
- `claude plugin validate . --strict`

Both missing-input cases made zero Pascal MCP calls; the complete-input case used the real read-only candidate collision path and preserved graph hash, version, and export bytes.

The earlier invalid ambient-Codex judge receipt and the failed D02/submission cohorts remain unchanged. ## What does this PR do?

Adds exactly one structured, blocker-aware `nextAction` to furniture-fit reports. title: perf: drain initial wall builds within the time budget (charter row 6)
body:
## Metric

**Maxi 8× time-to-first-clean after load** (charter backlog row 6; the row's `settled < 8 s` target contains a 3 s runner quiet window, so the runner now reports `firstCleanMs` alongside it).

Three back-to-back PR-vs-main pairs, same machine (a fourth under load average 21–24 discarded as starved); third pair = this tip:

| fixture | first clean | settled | same-gesture endpoint-drag settle | idle frame |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Maxi 8× (472 walls) | 4 900 → 3 930 ms (−20 %); 4 836 → 4 251 (−12 %); 5 639 → 4 283 (−24 %) | 8 441 → 7 312; 8 681 → 7 608; 9 534 → **7 633** | 420 → 435 ms | 6.8 → 6.3; 8.7 → 6.6 ms |
| Maxi 4× | −8 % / −14 % / −4 % | 6 775 → 6 117 | 342 → 365; 349 → 370 ms | flat |
| rich 4× | −13 % / −5 % / −11 % | 7 815 → 6 942 | window 308 → 292; wall body 510 → 516 | 11.3 → 9.0 ms |

## What changed

- **Initial-build state** for the wall system, entered from `setScene`'s hydration token and left on the first frame with no dirty wall and an empty pending-neighbour queue (a document write, live override/transform, or canvas pointer/wheel ends it early). Exposed read-only via `isWallInitialBuildActive()`.
- **While active:** walls are consumed by the existing 8 ms time budget without the 8-per-frame count cap (heavy ≥ 6-opening walls still get their own frame), and a wall's *first* build does not enqueue neighbour re-invalidation — every neighbour is itself queued for its own first build, and a test proves junction geometry identical to the capped path. Opening-completion re-dirtying is unchanged. After initial build everything returns to today's scheduling.
- **Counters** under `__pascalPerf.batchStats().wallDrain` (walls consumed per frame, exit reasons, pending-neighbour length, first-build vs re-invalidation) and a `wall-initial-build` span.
- **Fix found by the receipt sensor** (1137afc1): the first cut's hydration invalidation was a nested scene write, so the first edit after load reached space reconciliation twice and re-invalidated the whole level (same-gesture endpoint drag 422 → 1 598 ms). Invalidation now happens atomically with the document write; the regression fixture rebuilds 4 walls instead of 48.
- Batching during the drain (bounded join waves while walls are dirty) is deliberately left for a follow-up.

## Gates

- e2e: 9/9 against the PR dists (perf-regression pack ×5, batched-wall click, hidden-wall click, undo/redo graph, floor placement)
- Unit: core 1 430 / viewer+nodes 2 681 pass (`--randomize --seed=1`); `tsc --noEmit` core/viewer/nodes clean; biome clean.
- No rendering change → no pixel/bake gate. Independent audit: no blocker, four should-fixes closed in the second round (token published after normalization; interaction capture spans the lazy mount and remounts; bounded stall exit for never-registering walls; `?perf`-gated, allocation-free diagnostics) plus a pre-existing core test-fixture ordering flake fixed (three seeds green).
- Docs: `wiki/architecture/systems.md` describes the initial-build scheduling.

Charter: `plans/performance/editor-scalable-scene-runtime.md` row 6 (private PR follows with the evidence row and the runner's first-clean / undo-phase sampling).

title: Keep MCP tool callback updates inside host executors
body:
## Description

`RegisteredTool.update({ callback })` could replace a regular tool handler after registration and bypass the host executor. Returned registrations from both `registerTool()` and deprecated `tool()` now re-wrap callback replacements.

String renames fail closed while `executeTool` is configured. The SDK updater closes over the original name, so repeated renames and later `remove()` cannot be made reliable through its public registration API. Failed rename attempts leave the original registered tool wrapped and removable. Experimental task-based tool registration remains outside this hook and is not used by `createPascalMcpServer`.

## Validation

title: perf: scope undo/redo invalidation to changed geometry and cleared previews (charter row 7)
body:
## Metric

**rich-4× `undo` receipt after a wall-body move < 2 s** (charter backlog row 7). Three same-load pairs, main vs this branch:

| fixture | undo receipt | frames | first clean after dispatch |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| rich 4× | 2 312 → **204 ms**, 2 720 → 210, 2 340 → 208 (2nd undo 2 666 → 673, 3 191 → 605, 2 690 → 615) | 84–87 → 5–6 | 1 611 → 125 ms |
| rich 2× | 1 045 → **141 ms**, 895 → 314, 895 → 129 | 41–42 → 7–8 | 690 → 34 ms |
| tower 2×18 | 2 299 → **206 ms**, 2 723 → 168, 2 378 → 247 | 90–92 → 6–11 | 1 661 → 121 ms |
| Maxi 8× | 3 999 (often a 5 s timeout) → **551 ms** (body move); endpoint undo 4 787 → 2 119 — the remaining closure is the pre-existing slab-tracker cascade | 142 → 14; 158 → 63 | 2 842 → 407 ms |

Idle frame and like-gesture edit receipts unchanged; batch membership identical at dispatch and settle except the affected walls' openings.

## Why

The editor's standalone undo/redo (`history.ts` `refreshSceneAfterHistoryJump`, introduced by ffa78f13 to restore canonical geometry after imperative previews) cleared live previews and then marked **every** scene node dirty on top of core's temporal changed-node/parent diff. One undo of a one-wall move rebuilt all 356 walls through the progressive pipeline. The runner's new undo sampling showed it directly: 10 ms after dispatch on Maxi 1×, 134 nodes of every kind were dirty for a one-wall move.

## What changed — scoped invalidation

1. **Editor history**: surviving ids captured from live transforms/overrides (incl. republished surface holes) plus their surviving direct parents are marked; the loop over every node is gone. Drafting cancellation, empty-command behaviour and the collab-delegate path are untouched.
2. **Core temporal diff** (`history-invalidation.ts`, pure + 20 tests): changed nodes plus old and new direct parents; for every changed wall the union of `getAdjacentWallIds` over the **before and after** layouts (one hop: corners, T-junctions, curves — former neighbours re-miter); on wall thickness/height/curve change or add/remove, the hosted doors, windows and wall-side items of either snapshot (CSG holes, proxy depth, offsets); the existing deletion rule and dirty-id pruning kept.
3. **Existing scene-write subscribers keep owning their dependencies** (spatial grid, slab tracker, space detection, stair/elevator openings — each verified to fire on the temporal write). One gap closed in `spatial-grid-sync.ts`: floor-placed objects overlapping either rendered boundary of an affected slab are marked; unrelated levels stay clean.
4. Batching untouched: a one-wall undo releases only that wall's and its neighbours' openings (test).

Finding 11's "GPU queue backlog" turned out to be an accounting artefact of the `queue` row (overlapping submit-to-completion latencies summed), so no backpressure change is included.

## Gates

- e2e: 11/11 against the branch dists (undo/redo graph, perf-regression pack ×5, batched-wall and hidden-wall clicks, floor and wall placement, slab room paint). Independent audit: one blocker (undo/redo with a live wall preview left the preview-joined neighbour's miter stale — history now computes the closure of the effective override-merged layout before clearing) and one should-fix (linker-agnostic history probes for the private CI) closed; the new slab-boundary rule limited to changed boundary bands; endpoint-move closure pinned by test.
- Unit: core+viewer+nodes+editor 5 006 pass (`--randomize --seed=1`); 20 dependency cases (disconnect/reconnect corner, T, reverse-T, curved endpoints; thickness/height; reparent; delete/restore), 11 real undo/redo cases with microtask flush, 2 spatial temporal cases; `tsc --noEmit` clean; biome clean. A pre-existing editor-store test-ordering flake is fixed in the second commit.
- Docs: `wiki/architecture/systems.md` describes scoped history invalidation and the subscriber owners.

Charter: `plans/performance/editor-scalable-scene-runtime.md` row 7 (private PR follows with the evidence row and the runner's undo sampling).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01Jmmz2AMwTzcnKsSHHPEMhN

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes undo/redo dirty marking and spatial slab-boundary invalidation—easy to miss dependents if the closure is wrong—but behavior is heavily tested and narrows rebuild scope rather than widening it.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Undo/redo no longer marks the whole scene dirty.** A new pure closure (`getHistoryDirtyNodeIds`) drives both core’s temporal subscriber and the editor’s preview cleanup: changed nodes, parents, one-hop wall neighbours in before/after layouts, hosted openings/items on host dimension changes, and deletion sibling rules—replacing per-node scans and a stale “last snapshot” tracker with layouts taken from the temporal stacks.
> 
> **Editor `runUndo`/`runRedo`** capture override-merged layout before the jump, clear live transforms/overrides, then mark only the preview→committed dependency closure (including neighbours that existed only in the discarded preview) plus surviving preview targets and parents—not every node.
> 
> **Spatial grid sync** closes a gap for history/temporal writes: when walls or slabs change context but a slab’s stored polygon is unchanged, it diffs **rendered** slab bands and dirties floor-placed consumers overlapping only the gained/lost bands; slab reparent also refreshes covering dependents on both old and new levels.
> 
> Tests and docs expand around dependency closure, temporal slab support, and subprocess-based editor history probes; `getHistoryDirtyNodeIds` is exported from core.

title: chore(skills): harden ClawHub bundles
body:
## What does this PR do?

ClawHub publishes every regular file in a skill folder unless an ignore policy excludes it. The two Pascal skills had clean dry-run bundles but no scoped policy protecting future local secrets, build output, reports, screenshots, or generated lockfiles.

This adds `.clawhubignore` to both canonical skill folders and makes `scripts/validate-skills.ts` require the shared safety patterns. Validation rejects all active negation rules and the later-loaded legacy `.clawdhubignore`, preventing either mechanism from reopening protected paths. A focused test suite covers the canonical files, missing exclusions, broad and targeted re-inclusions, whitespace-prefixed negations, and the legacy-file override.

The ignored files do not change either published payload fingerprint.

## How to test

1. Run `bun test scripts/clawhub-ignore-policy.test.ts`.
2. Run `bun scripts/validate-skills.ts`.
3. Run `bun check`, `bun run test`, and `claude plugin validate . --strict`.

5. Install both local folders with OpenClaw 2026.9.3 and confirm `skills info` reports them eligible and model-visible.

An adversarial ClawHub fixture confirmed that appending `!dist/` and `!dist/reincluded.txt` would otherwise add the protected file and change the bundle fingerprint. The validator now rejects that policy. Normal dry-runs retain the prior fingerprints:

title: fix(editor): type optional ancestor traversal for consumers
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #617. A consumer compiling the raw editor TypeScript with `strict: true` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: false` infers the ancestor traversal variable as `AnyNode`, then rejects the later `undefined` assignment with TS2322. Explicitly typing it as `AnyNode | undefined` makes the traversal compile with either setting. The added import is type-only; runtime behavior is unchanged.

## How to test

1. Compile the affected ancestor traversal with TypeScript 6.0.3, `strict: true`, and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: false`.
2. Confirm the original source reports TS2322 and this change removes it.
3. Repeat with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`; both revisions should compile.

Adds `pascal agent claim`, which lets an autonomous hosted Pascal agent request its existing 15-minute claim code from the CLI and open the human claim page. title: feat(editor): streamline connected pipe and duct drafting
body:
## What does this PR do?

- **Pipe and duct connection snapping**
  - Issue: Drawing a run near an existing socket still required manual alignment, especially in the floor plan.
  - Fixed: Run tools now snap to visible connection points in both 2D and 3D using a consistent screen-distance threshold.

- **Run direction controls**
  - Issue: Angled and vertical routes were difficult to choose from the cursor alone.
  - Fixed: Direction guides support horizontal, diagonal, wall-plane, and vertical choices, with pointer selection and keyboard cycling.

- **Inline pipe fittings**
  - Issue: Adding a fitting to an existing straight pipe required rebuilding the run around it.
  - Fixed: Hovering a compatible fitting over a pipe previews the insertion, and clicking splits the pipe and inserts the fitting as one undoable change.

- **Automatic run end caps**
  - Issue: New pipe and duct runs could be left with visually open ends, and caps did not follow later endpoint edits.
  - Fixed: Free ends receive matching caps automatically, while connected caps are removed and remaining caps follow endpoint moves.

- **Pool plumbing workflows**
  - Issue: Pool inlets, skimmers, and drains required repeated manual pipe construction and overlapping routes were hard to manage.
  - Fixed: The editor now loads the pool plugin build with automatic connection routes, route status and removal controls, shape support, and separated pipe elevations.
  - The plugin release artifact is stored in the repository so installs do not depend on a developer's local filesystem.

- **Portable CLI runtime size**
  - Issue: The standalone build copied the pool plugin's vendored installation archive into the published CLI after the plugin code was already bundled, pushing `cli-smoke` over its compressed-size limit.
  - Fixed: Runtime staging removes vendored source archives, and the compressed budget now accommodates the pool plugin's shipped client code while retaining the unpacked-size and file-count limits.

- **Run selection and hanger controls**
  - Issue: Marquee selection could miss path-based runs, and automatic hanger controls used extra panel text.
  - Fixed: Pipe and duct footprints participate in box selection, and hanger generation uses a compact mode control while drafting.

- **System checks panel**
  - Issue: Distribution-system findings were dense and difficult to scan or locate in the scene.
  - Fixed: The panel now groups findings, shows error and warning totals, filters categories, and provides direct locate actions.

- **WebGPU handle stability**
  - Issue: Recreating and disposing shared handle geometry could leave WebGPU render pipelines with missing vertex buffers.
  - Fixed: Handle geometry and materials are cached by their stable visual variants and reused safely.

- **Plugin-facing tool boundaries**
  - Issue: Run planning and floor-plan projection data crossed package boundaries through global scene reads and core view-specific state.
  - Fixed: Planners receive scene snapshots through the registry API, while screen projection metadata stays in the editor layer.

## How to test

1. Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, then run `bun dev` and open the editor at `http://localhost:3002`.
   - The editor should load successfully with the pool plugin available.

2. Draw a DWV pipe or duct near an existing open socket in both 3D and floor-plan views.
   - The endpoint should snap to the nearby socket, including sockets above or below the current drawing plane.

3. Start a run and choose diagonal, wall-plane, or vertical directions with the guides and keyboard controls.
   - The preview and committed run should follow the selected direction without floating status badges.

4. Choose a compatible pipe fitting, hover it over the middle of a straight pipe, and click.
   - The preview should show the insertion, and the committed result should contain two pipe sections joined through the fitting. Undo and redo should treat it as one change.

5. Draw a free pipe and duct, then drag either endpoint.
   - Matching end caps should be created automatically and should remain aligned after the endpoint moves.

6. Create pools with different supported outlines and automatically connect inlets, skimmers, and drains.
   - Each group should produce one extendable outlet, avoid overlapping other generated routes, show a connected state, and allow its generated connection to be deleted.

7. Box-select across pipe and duct runs, then open System checks from a selected distribution item.
   - Path runs should be selected, and findings should be filterable with working locate buttons.

8. Repeatedly select, resize, and draw items while using WebGPU rendering.
   - Handle arrows should remain visible without vertex-buffer or post-processing errors.

9. Run the automated checks.
   - `bun run lint`, `bun run check-types`, and `bun run build` should pass.
   - The exact `cli-smoke` workflow should pass with a 107.6 MB compressed artifact.
   - The focused run, fitting, snapping, end-cap, and floor-plan tests should report 69 passing tests.

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches scene mutation paths (atomic applyChanges, end caps, inline pipe splits) and cross-package drafting APIs; regressions could affect MEP editing and portable CLI size gates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Wires the **pool plugin** into the editor (discovery, host panel, transpile, vendored tarball) and hardens **builtin plugin loading** so HMR cannot re-register duplicate node kinds against the persistent registry.
> 
> **Pipe and duct drafting** gets screen-space port snapping (including floor-plan `screenProjection` on grid events), length grid snapping, **Tab** direction cycling, **H** for hanger mode via shared run-hanger state, and leaner run cursors (no inline hanger/preset HUD). ## What does this PR do?

Adds the generic host contracts needed by the public [Environment plugin](https://github.com/AxiomeCG/environment) and includes the plugin in the standalone app, using the same pinned GitHub dependency and bootstrap registration pattern as Nature, Mint, and Bones. The plugin remains external; neither its implementation nor its lab is embedded in Pascal's reusable host packages.

- Core: site-scoped floorplan contributions, fill rules, asynchronous bake hooks, and per-definition selection-highlight control.
- Viewer: registered presentation contributions, atmosphere and ground-replacement ownership, explicit static-export participation, and public rendering layers.
- Editor: project-local presentation persistence, site-aware 2D/PDF output, registered-tool cancellation on uninstall, configurable model export, and portable GLB/USDZ output.
- Documents the public contracts and preserves existing terrain controls. Fixes elevation-guide test cleanup exposed by the new lifecycle integration test.
- Standalone app: pins `@pascal-app/plugin-environment` to public commit `5c50258da30ac05264d4babf596d0aa99cc4be51`, registers its node plugin, editor panel, and viewer presentation, and includes its source in Next.js transpilation and Tailwind scanning. Updates the lockfile, setup instructions, and changelog. No sibling checkout, local tarball, or synchronization script is required.
- Preserves the follow-up export and scene-slot review corrections from `31f3ec4e`.

The host changes were reconciled with upstream `main` at `d21fa364`, preserving the upstream save shortcut and presentation persistence. Plugin installation in the standalone app is now included in this PR. The app uses the compatible host packages built from this workspace, so testing this branch does not require an npm release. The Environment lab and package publication remain separate; external package consumers still need a compatible beta.6-or-later host release.

## How to test

### Standalone app integration

1. Check out `AxiomeCG:feat/environment-host-api`, then run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun dev` from the repository root. Open `http://localhost:3002` (or the URL printed by Next.js).
2. Open **+ → Plugins**. Environment appears alongside Nature, Bones, Mint, and Streetscape. On a new project it is installed by default; existing projects can enable it with **Install**.
3. Open **Environment** in the sidebar. Verify **Site View**, then choose **Catalogue** to see Ground Cover, Atmosphere, Surroundings, Build, Terrain, Surface, and Water.
4. In **+ → Plugins → Environment**, uninstall and reinstall it. Its sidebar entry disappears and returns, the panel opens again, and the installation persists after reloading the page.
5. Run `bun x turbo run check-types --filter=./apps/editor` and `bun x turbo run build --filter=./apps/editor`. Run `bun test lib` from `apps/editor`. The app integration passed type checking, production build, and all 41 existing app tests. Native Chrome verification covered the actual catalogue, both panel views, uninstall/reinstall, and reload persistence. The standard unfiltered `bun dev` startup also rendered the catalogue with Environment installed.

The production build reports a non-fatal Turbopack filesystem-tracing warning in the unchanged MCP SQLite storage code.

### Earlier host-only verification record

The following results predate the standalone app integration; the full repository suite was not rerun for this dependency/bootstrap-only addition.

1. Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run check`, `bun run check-types`, `bun run test`, and `bun run build`. All pass locally. The final full test run reports 16 successful Turbo tasks, 5,713 passing tests, one existing skipped test, and zero failures; unchanged tasks use Turbo's cache.

Before the cleanup fix, the elevation test leaked a guide and the 3D lifecycle test failed with `document is not defined`; its 2D/3D uninstall assertions remain intact. An initial parallel suite run also hit the existing wall-scheduling test's 10-second timeout; that test passed in the serial run, without changing its timeout.

Exercise a site-scoped plugin in 2D and PDF; uninstall it during an active placement gesture and confirm the gesture cancels without deleting existing nodes or reactivating automatically after reinstall. Exercise model-export exclusions and project switching with registered presentation configuration.
4. For downstream compatibility, use the Environment repository's documented `PASCAL_EDITOR_ROOT` / `check-types:pascal` / `test:pascal` workflow against this checkout. Current Environment passed type checking and all 316 tests against this candidate. A temporary copy of its standalone lab, aliased to this exact host checkout and its dependencies, also mounted the portability fixture with the real `WebGPUBackend / WebGPURenderer`. The temporary app and installed plugin fixture were removed afterward; no lab-specific source is included here.

title: skills: make skills/ the Claude plugin root
body:
## What does this PR do?

A fresh `claude plugin install pascal-agent-skills@pascal` produced a **1.2 GB** plugin cache. The marketplace entry used `"source": "./"`, so the monorepo root was the plugin root, and Claude Code runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` inside any cached plugin whose root has `package.json` + `bun.lock` (documented, cannot be disabled, 60 s timeout). Every Claude Code user would either download the editor's full `node_modules` or hit the timeout with a partial tree.

Fix: `skills/` is now the Claude plugin root. `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.mcp.json` move into `skills/`, the marketplace entry points at `./skills`, and the plugin manifest lists `./pascal-3d` and `./furniture-fit`. Nothing else moves: skills.sh tree URLs, the Codex/Cursor Agent Plugins layout (root `plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/`), ClawHub and Gemini are unchanged. The validator asserts the new root, the bundle list in both the marketplace entry and the plugin manifest, and ignores the two dot-entries inside `skills/` while still rejecting any other non-skill directory.

Also sets `displayName` to `Pascal` across the Claude, Cursor and OpenAI manifests so directory listings match product plugins listed by brand; the identifier stays `pascal-agent-skills`.

Measured with a throwaway `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: cache **1.2 GB → 196 KB**, `claude plugin details` shows both skills and the `pascal` MCP server. Codex (`codex plugin marketplace add`) still resolves and installs 0.1.8 and ignores the dot-entries.

Known follow-up, not in this PR: Codex/Cursor installs still copy the whole repo root because the Agent Plugins spec fixes `skills/` and `mcp.json` at the plugin root; recorded in the private repo's meta-todos with the two options (move the bundle under a subdirectory, or a dedicated distribution repo).

## How to test

1. `bun run skills:validate` and `claude plugin validate . --strict` and `claude plugin validate ./skills --strict` all pass.
2. `export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/pascal-plugin-test && claude plugin marketplace add pascalorg/editor && claude plugin install pascal-agent-skills@pascal && du -sh $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/plugins/cache/pascal/pascal-agent-skills/0.1.8` → a few hundred KB, no `node_modules`.
3. `claude plugin details pascal-agent-skills@pascal` lists `furniture-fit`, `pascal-3d` and MCP server `pascal`.

title: perf(core): guard bulk slab changes in the spatial-grid subscriber
body:
## What does this PR do?

The spatial-grid subscriber runs `markNodesOverlappingSlab` for every slab a store write adds, removes or reshapes: two full node scans per slab, so a scene load, reload, paste or import is O(slabs × nodes). On a 4,645-slab scene (7,143 nodes) that scan alone blocked the main thread for ~5 s on every load — a real-Chrome CPU profile showed 5.9 s inclusive inside this scan out of a 7 s `setScene` block, enough for Chrome's "Page Unresponsive" dialog on a loaded machine.

When one write changes 32 or more slabs, this dirties every node any slab could affect once — walls, ceilings, stairs and level-hosted floor-placed kinds, a superset of the per-slab marks — and skips the per-slab scans. `setScene` marks every node dirty right after `set()` regardless, so load-time behaviour is unchanged; single-slab edits keep the targeted rules (`markSlabChangeDependents`, covering-below, deck stairs).

**Measurement caveat:** the numbers were taken with an equivalent patch applied to the published `@pascal-app/core@1.0.0-beta.5` (before #805), not re-taken on this source. Same mechanism. Max main-thread freeze on that scene went 6.4 s → 0.4–0.9 s; time to a ready model 31.7 s → ~21 s. Happy to re-run on a fixture you prefer.

## How to test

1. `bun test --cwd packages/core src/hooks/spatial-grid/spatial-grid-sync.test.ts` — new `bulk slab-change guard` block: 31 added interior plates leave a non-overlapping wall clean (per-slab path); 32 mark it (superset path); a 3,000-slab write stays linear (well under 1.5 s, versus seconds unguarded); later single-slab edits stay targeted.
2. Load a scene with hundreds of slab nodes with `?perf` and compare the `setScene` span before and after.
3. Full core suite passes (1,490 tests); `tsc --build` and `bun check` clean.

title: perf(viewer): give the initial wall build a 48 ms frame budget
body:
## What does this PR do?

#800 lifted the 8-walls-per-frame cap during the initial wall build but kept the 8 ms time budget, which exists to protect a drag. The initial build has no gesture to protect, and each of its frames also pays a full render of the still-unbatched scene (the level wall batch merges only once a level stops changing), so every extra frame spent draining walls costs a whole scene render.

This gives the initial build its own budget, 48 ms (about three display frames, still two orders of magnitude under a perceptible freeze), checked between walls exactly as before. The interactive tiers (8 ms / 8 walls) are unchanged, and a heavy wall (≥ 6 openings) still takes its own frame. `shouldDeferWallRebuild` gains an optional `initialBuild` flag so the test can pin both tiers, and `wiki/architecture/systems.md` records the budget.

**Measurement caveat:** the numbers come from an equivalent change (a 48 ms / 128-wall tier for 64+ pending walls) applied to the published `@pascal-app/viewer@1.0.0-beta.5`, which predates #800 and has no initial-build state; this PR is narrower and applies the wider budget only inside #800's initial build. On a 1,600-wall scene in Chrome (WebGPU on Metal) that change halved time to a ready model in an interleaved A/B (17.6/18.3 s → 8.2/8.8 s) and cut main-thread long-task time roughly 3× (~12 s → 4 s). Not re-taken on this source; happy to re-run on your fixture.

## How to test

1. `bun test --cwd packages/viewer src/systems/wall/` — new case in `wall-progressive-budget.test.ts`; the lifecycle probes now simulate 24 ms per wall (was 4) so the budget exit is still exercised, and the recorded span expectation moves 28 → 68 accordingly. Full viewer suite: 311 pass.
2. Load a scene with 1,000+ walls with `?perf`; `__pascalPerf.batchStats().wallDrain` shows walls consumed per frame rising from ~6 to ~35 during initial build, and first-clean arriving in a fraction of the frames.
3. Drag a wall after load: the 8 ms / 8-wall behaviour is unchanged.

A constant is the smallest change. A frame-time-adaptive budget (spend as long as the last render took) would self-tune but needs a render-time signal in the wall system; glad to follow up either way.

title: skills: bundle the hosted Pascal MCP server with a key prompt
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a second MCP server to the Claude Code plugin: `pascal-hosted` → `https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer ${user_config.pascal_api_key}`. The plugin manifest declares `userConfig.pascal_api_key` (sensitive, optional), so Claude prompts for the key once at install (`--config pascal_api_key=…` or the `/plugin` configure flow), stores it in the OS keychain, and substitutes it at runtime only. The local `pascal` stdio server is unchanged, so people without an account keep the local path. The skills now say: use `pascal-hosted` for anything in the person's Pascal account (including Capture scans), `pascal` for local work, never both for one task.

Validator: the portable `mcp.json` must declare only `pascal` (identical to the Claude one, since `${user_config.*}` is Claude-specific); `skills/.mcp.json` may add only `pascal-hosted` with exactly this URL and header template; `userConfig` must be exactly `pascal_api_key` with `sensitive: true`, `required: false`, no default. Literal bearer tokens, extra headers, redirected URLs and extra options are rejected (51 policy tests).

Verified in a throwaway `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: `claude plugin details` lists `pascal, pascal-hosted`; the key was stored in the macOS Keychain and appears nowhere in the config dir; `claude mcp list` shows the hosted server rejected with `Invalid or revoked API key` for a bogus key versus a different error with no key, proving substitution. No account or real key was created.

Step 1 of the hosted-first direction. Step 2 is OAuth 2.1 on the hosted MCP (auth plan Phase 2), after which the header goes away and Claude Code/Cowork sign in natively; Claude Code already reports it disables OAuth fallback only because a header is configured.

## How to test

1. `bun run skills:validate`, `claude plugin validate . --strict`, `claude plugin validate ./skills --strict`.
2. `export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/t && claude plugin marketplace add pascalorg/editor && claude plugin install pascal-agent-skills@pascal --config pascal_api_key=<a real key from https://editor.pascal.app/settings>` then `claude mcp list` → `pascal-hosted … ✔ Connected`.

title: ci(release): graduate prerelease versions on stable bumps

## What does this PR do?

`bump_version` in `release.yml` split `1.0.0-beta.5` on dots for stable bumps, so `major` gave `2.0.0`, `minor` gave `1.1.0`, `patch` failed on `0-beta` arithmetic, and `none` would have published a beta version to `latest`. title: fix(ifc-converter): preserve imported beam geometry
body:
## What does this PR do?

IFC import explicitly skipped every beam because Pascal has no dedicated beam node. The bundled Duplex model therefore lost all eight `IFCBEAM` elements. Import `IFCBEAM` and `IFCBEAMSTANDARDCASE` as editable blocks using their actual triangulated geometry, preserving I-sections, slopes, mapped parts, and IFC metadata. Convert web-ifc's meter-based coordinates into the converter's scene frame and containing-storey coordinates, and pin the imported elevation so overlapping slabs cannot lift beams again. The converter UI also includes blocks in its type counts.

Beams remain editable through block controls; this does not add parametric beam authoring. Elements without renderable geometry are reported and do not stop the remaining import.

## How to test

1. Run `bun run build --filter=@pascal-app/ifc-converter`, then `bun test packages/ifc-converter/tests`. All 21 tests pass, including both cleanup modes, millimeter units, nested rotated placements, upper-storey offsets, sloped standard-case beams, mapped parts, duplicate IDs, uncontained beams, missing representations, and JSON schema round trips. The same Duplex fixture produces 0 beams on `main` and 8 on this branch.
2. Run `bun check` and `bun run check-types --filter=ifc-converter-app`. Both pass with Node.js 24. The converter application's production build also passes with Node.js 24 (`cd apps/ifc-converter && bun run build`).
3. Run `bun dev` in `apps/ifc-converter`, open `http://localhost:3003/?file=01-duplex.ifc#try`, and confirm the `8 blocks` count. Search for `IFCBEAM` and inspect a result: its original name, Global ID, containing level, material, and properties are retained. title: perf(editor): re-encode fitting thumbnails as 256px webp
body:
## What does this PR do?

`apps/editor/public/icons/fittings/` held 16 PNGs at 1254×1254 RGBA — **11 MB** — for thumbnails that render at **56 CSS px** in the MEP tool-options grid (`size-14`, `width={56} height={56}`). Every other icon under `public/icons` is already a small webp, and this one directory was 11 MB of the 64.6 MB packed CLI runtime, served on every editor page load that opens the MEP tools.

Each PNG is re-encoded as a 256×256 lossy webp with alpha:

```sh
cwebp -q 85 -m 6 -alpha_q 100 -resize 256 256 <name>.png -o <name>.webp
```

256 px is 4.5× the CSS size, so it stays crisp at 2× and 3× DPR — the portable build sets `images.unoptimized`, so the raw file is what the browser scales.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `public/icons/fittings/` | 11 MB (16 PNG, 1254²) | 164 KB (16 webp, 256²) |

title: feat(cli): ship a small CLI that downloads the web editor runtime
body:
## What does this PR do?

Splits `@pascal-app/cli` into a small npm package plus a web-runtime archive that is downloaded on first need, and makes MCP-only mode work with no web runtime at all.

Today the published CLI is **65 MB compressed / 102 MB unpacked** because `stage-runtime` copies the standalone Next editor app into `dist/runtime`. The CLI code itself is 0.1 MB. Every agent host that only wants `pascal mcp connect` pays for a Next server it never starts.

**After this PR: 0.46 MB compressed / 2.46 MB unpacked / 68 files.**

### 1. MCP-only mode needs no web runtime

`pascal mcp connect` now starts (or attaches to) the managed MCP service on its own. The new `src/mcp-service.ts` owns the service lifecycle — spawn, loopback bearer token, `run/mcp.json` state, health check, reuse, stop — which `editor-process.ts` previously did as a child of the editor process. `connectManagedMcp` no longer calls `startEditor()` and no longer requires `editorHealthy`. `editorUrl` values keep their existing `PASCAL_EDITOR_ORIGIN` fallback, and starting the editor later repoints the running service at the real origin (restart + repoint) rather than leaving a stale one.

`src/process-control.ts` holds the pid/signal helpers both lifecycles now share.

### 2. The package is split

`dist/` ships CLI code, `services/pascal-mcp.mjs` (2.3 MB, unchanged), and a new `dist/runtime-source.json`:

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0-beta.1",
  "url": "https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/releases/download/@pascal-app/cli@1.0.0-beta.1/pascal-web-runtime-1.0.0-beta.1.tar.gz",
  "sha256": "b92fe413e519c46af559e4b9c41baaf17c3a70dd8df23b6099fcac0c0228b5b9",
  "size": 67340245
}
```

### 3. Download on first need

`ensureWebRuntime` (`src/runtime-download.ts`) resolves, in order:

1. `--runtime <path|archive>` (new flag on `editor`, `start`, `update`, `install`)
2. `PASCAL_BUNDLED_RUNTIME_DIR` (existing)
3. an already-installed runtime for this exact CLI version under the data dir
4. download `runtime-source.json.url` with streamed progress, verify SHA-256, extract, install

Verification is **fail-closed**: a mismatch throws `runtime_digest_mismatch` and deletes the downloaded temp file (a caller-supplied archive is left alone). Everything then hands off to the untouched `installBundledRuntime` seam, so the atomic temp-dir install, manifest validation, `.install-*` reaping and `runtime-install.lock` are reused verbatim — concurrent first runs serialise on the existing lock.

`src/http-download.ts` does the transfer on `node:https` with no new dependency: manual redirect following, https-only, `HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` (including `*`, `.suffix`, `host:port` forms) through a `CONNECT` tunnel agent. On network failure the error names the archive URL, the expected digest, `pascal editor --runtime <archive>` and `HTTPS_PROXY`.

`src/tar.ts` is a small deterministic tar writer/reader: sorted names, zeroed mtime/uid/gid, ustar + GNU long-name entries, gzip level 9. Extraction rejects path traversal, absolute and drive-letter paths, symlinks, hard links and bad header checksums with `invalid_runtime_archive`.

### 4. Build and release plumbing

`stage-runtime` now also writes `build/pascal-web-runtime-<version>.tar.gz` + `.sha256` and `dist/runtime-source.json`. Two independent runs produced the identical digest above.

Release ordering in `release.yml`:

1. `Validate portable editor runtime` builds the editor and stages the archive (unchanged step, new side effects).
2. `Publish CLI` **guards before publishing**: the archive, its `.sha256`, `dist/services/pascal-mcp.mjs` and a `dist/runtime-source.json` whose `version` equals `$CLI_VERSION` must all exist. Then `npm publish`.
3. `Commit version bumps & tag` pushes `main` + the `@pascal-app/cli@<version>` tag atomically.
4. A new `Upload the CLI web runtime release asset` step creates the GitHub release for that tag if absent (`--prerelease` on the beta dist-tag) and `gh release upload --clobber`s the archive + digest.

The asset upload has to follow the tag push (the release hangs off the tag), so there is a residual window of roughly 30–60 s between `npm publish` and the asset being live during which a brand-new install would fail its download. The pre-publish guards make that window a scheduling artefact rather than a correctness one, and `gh release upload --clobber` makes re-running the job idempotent. Worth a follow-up if we ever want it closed properly (publish to a staging dist-tag, upload, then retag).

### 5. Budgets

`smoke-packed-runtime.ts` now checks npm package ≤ 3 MB compressed / ≤ 10 MB unpacked / ≤ 250 files and the archive ≤ 70 MB. Measured: **0.46 MB / 2.46 MB / 68 files** and a **64.2 MB** archive (106 MB installed). Archive headroom is only ~8%, so a materially larger editor build will trip the budget deliberately.

### 6. Docs and tests

`packages/cli/README.md` gains a `## The web editor runtime` section (what downloads when, sizes, the resolution order, digest verification, the offline `curl` + `--runtime` recipe, proxy support, and that agent tools need none of it). `SETUP.md`, the root `README.md` and both skill `references/setup.md` local sections say `pascal mcp connect` needs no runtime download; the skill statements are version-qualified so they do not contradict the currently published `1.0.0-beta.1`. Frontmatter untouched, bundles still standalone, `bun run skills:validate` passes. `CHANGELOG.md` has one Unreleased line.

38 new unit tests across `tar.test.ts` (9), `runtime-download.test.ts` (22) and `mcp-service.test.ts` (7) cover digest verification, the resolution order, the `runtime-source.json` validation table, proxy resolution, extraction safety, and MCP-without-a-runtime including concurrent starts and origin repointing. The download tests point at an unroutable `https://127.0.0.1:1`, so the suite stays offline.

## How to test

1. Build the editor once and stage the split artifacts:
   ```bash
   PASCAL_PORTABLE_BUILD=1 bun run build --filter editor
   cd packages/cli && bun run build && bun run stage-runtime
   ```
2. Run the smoke test — phase 1 is MCP-only with no runtime present, phase 2 tampers a byte in the archive, phase 3 installs it through `--runtime`:
   ```bash
   bun run smoke-runtime
   ```
   ```
   MCP-only mode exposed 46 tools and stored a scene with no web runtime installed.
   Tampered archive rejected: The Pascal web runtime archive does not match the digest published with this CLI.
   Editor installed from pascal-web-runtime-1.0.0-beta.1.tar.gz on port 56428, MCP on port 56431, and a scene round-tripped between MCP and the CLI.
   Packed CLI smoke passed (0.5 MB compressed, 2.5 MB unpacked, 68 files).
   Web runtime archive pascal-web-runtime-1.0.0-beta.1.tar.gz (64.2 MB) verified against https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/releases/download/@pascal-app/cli@1.0.0-beta.1/pascal-web-runtime-1.0.0-beta.1.tar.gz
   ```
3. `cd packages/cli && bun test` → 102 pass, 0 fail, 288 expect() calls across 11 files.
4. `bun run check` (clean, 2142 files), `bun run check-types` (clean), `bun run skills:validate` (2 skills + 51 policy tests).
5. Confirm the package size yourself: `cd packages/cli && npm pack --dry-run --json` → `size 487831`, `unpackedSize 2583923`, `entryCount 68`.

Reviewers who want to exercise the real download path need the release asset to exist, which only happens on the next CLI release; until then `--runtime build/pascal-web-runtime-<version>.tar.gz` covers the same code path minus the transfer.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not applicable — CLI and release plumbing only, no visual surface.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how users install and verify the editor (download, digest, release asset ordering) and splits MCP vs editor lifecycle; strong tests and fail-closed verification, but a brief npm-publish-before-asset window remains.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`@pascal-app/cli` shrinks to a ~0.5 MB npm package** that ships the CLI and bundled MCP service; the Next.js web editor is published per version as a **GitHub release archive** referenced by `dist/runtime-source.json` (URL, size, SHA-256).
> 
> **Editor commands** (`editor`, `start`, `update`, etc.) gain **`--runtime`** and call **`ensureWebRuntime`**: resolve an override or installed copy, or **download once**, **verify digest fail-closed**, extract via new **`tar.ts`**, then reuse existing install/lock logic. **`http-download.ts`** handles HTTPS-only transfers with **`HTTPS_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY`**.
> 
> **MCP is decoupled from the web runtime**: **`mcp-service.ts`** manages its own process and `run/mcp.json`; **`pascal mcp connect`** no longer starts the editor. Editor start still brings MCP up and can **repoint** `PASCAL_EDITOR_ORIGIN` when the editor port changes.
> 
> **Release workflow** requires the staged archive, digest, MCP bundle, and matching `runtime-source.json` **before** `npm publish`, then **uploads the runtime tarball** to the `@pascal-app/cli@<version>` GitHub release after the tag is pushed. **`stage-runtime`** writes `build/pascal-web-runtime-*.tar.gz` and drops MCP from the runtime tree (manifest **schema v2**). Docs, changelog, and expanded smoke/unit tests reflect the split and offline path.
>

title: feat(plugins): add optional hosted auth to the Cursor plugin
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds **optional** hosted authentication to the Cursor plugin so a Cursor user can reach their hosted Pascal projects, Pascal Capture scans, and shared workspaces with an API key — while the local, no-account `pascal mcp connect` path keeps working untouched.

Research came first, and it changed the plan: **only Cursor can carry a hosted credential in a plugin manifest.** Claude Code already could, ClawHub already declares the key optional, and the portable Agent Plugins / Codex format structurally cannot. Details and citations below.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.cursor-plugin/mcp.json` | **New.** Cursor-dialect config: `pascal` (identical to the portable server) plus `pascal-hosted` → `https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp` with `Authorization: Bearer ${PASCAL_API_KEY}` |
| `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` | Declares `variables.PASCAL_API_KEY` (string, title, description naming Settings → API keys and what it unlocks), **absent from `required`**; `mcpServers` now points at `./.cursor-plugin/mcp.json` |
| `mcp.json` (portable) | **Unchanged, deliberately** — see "What the formats do not support" |
| `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` | **Unchanged** — the portable interface block did not change, and Codex plugins have no variable/credential mechanism |
| `skills/*/SKILL.md` | **Unchanged** — `metadata.openclaw.envVars[].required: false` already declares the key optional |
| `scripts/validate-skills.ts` | New Cursor policy (below); portable and Claude policies stay strict |
| `skills/*/references/setup.md`, `skills/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` | Docs, one hosted paragraph per host |

Why Cursor gets its own file rather than sharing the root one: the root `mcp.json` is the Agent Plugins document Codex parses, and it can hold neither the credential nor Cursor's `http` keyword. Cursor documents a custom `mcpServers` path for exactly this case. This mirrors the pattern `skills/.mcp.json` already uses for Claude Code.

## Research findings

### 1. Cursor plugins — supports optional credentials

- Substitution syntax is the **bare `${VAR}`**, and the docs call out that it is explicitly *not* the shell form: "`${POSTGRES_URL}` is a plugin variable placeholder (**not shell `${env:...}`**)." (<https://cursor.com/docs/reference/plugins.md#variables>, MCP servers section)
- `variables` is a restricted JSON Schema: "The top level must be `{ "type": "object", "properties": { ... } }`. Only a fixed set of JSON Schema keywords is accepted (`type`, `title`, `description`, `default`, `enum`, `const`, `properties`, `required`, `items`, and common length/numeric constraints)."
- **Optionality**: `required` is an accepted keyword, so omitting the variable from it makes it optional. Values are set by an admin in the dashboard under **Plugins** → **Configure**, at install time or later — not a local prompt.
- Real example confirming the syntax and `mcpServers: "./mcp.json"`: `gh api repos/cursor/plugins/contents/third_party/github/mcp.json` → `"Authorization": "Bearer ${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}"` with `variables.properties.GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` + `"required": ["GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN"]`.
- Cursor's `mcpServers` accepts "a path, an inline config object, or an array of either" (published `schemas/plugin.schema.json`), which is what lets us redirect to `./.cursor-plugin/mcp.json`.
- Cursor uses `"type": "http"` for remote servers and otherwise infers transport from `command`/`url`. Across all 77 plugins in `cursor/plugins` there are **zero** occurrences of `streamable-http`.
- Precedent note: 12 of those 77 plugins declare `variables`, and **all 12 mark them required**. An optional plugin variable is schema-valid but has no upstream precedent, so the local-only path is worth a manual check once this is installed in a real Cursor workspace.

### 2. Agent Plugins spec — forbids it outright

From `spec/1.0.0.md` (and identically `1.1.0.md`) at <https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-spec>, §7.2.3 and §9.2:

> Clients MUST NOT perform placeholder or environment-variable expansion in `url`, header names, or header values.

> Header values are visible package data, not a portable secret mechanism. Plugins MUST NOT embed credentials or other secrets in `headers`.

> Agent Plugins v1 defines no OAuth configuration or portable credential-reference fields. Authorization discovery, user interaction, and credential storage are client-managed.

> Unrecognized placeholder-like text MUST remain literal. Clients MUST NOT perform any other placeholder or environment-variable expansion.

Only `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` expand, and only in stdio `args`/`env`/`cwd`. The remote transport keyword is `streamable-http` or `sse` — **`http` is not valid** (<https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json>). There is no notion of an optional server.

So a `${PASCAL_API_KEY}` header in the portable file would be a double violation *and* would ship the literal string `Bearer ${PASCAL_API_KEY}` to the server.

### 3. OpenAI / Codex plugins — no mechanism, and it strips the header

The plugin build docs (<https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins.md>) show only an unauthenticated remote server and say authentication "remain[s] part of the MCP server integration you built"; there is no bearer-token, header-variable, or secret-prompt field. Codex's implementation confirms why:

- `codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/agent_plugin_config.rs` lists `authorization` in `CLIENT_OWNED_HTTP_HEADERS` and drops it: `configured_headers.retain(|name, _| !CLIENT_OWNED_HTTP_HEADERS.iter().any(|owned| name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(owned)))`. Remaining headers map to `http_headers`; `bearer_token_env_var` is never emitted from plugin config.
- `codex-rs/core-plugins/src/agent_plugin_mcp_overlay.rs` — the `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` overlay merges only **stdio** `env_vars`; it `continue`s past any non-stdio transport. So the overlay cannot reach a remote server either.

**Verified empirically** with Codex 0.153.4 using a throwaway plugin that declared both an `Authorization` and a control header:

```
$ codex mcp get probe-hosted --json
"transport": {
  "type": "streamable_http",
  "url": "https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp",
  "bearer_token_env_var": null,
  "http_headers": { "X-Probe-Kept": "yes" },     <-- Authorization silently dropped
```

Codex also does not prompt for missing env vars. Hosted Pascal accepts only `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_*`/`sk_test_*` and advertises no authorization server (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` intentionally omits `authorization_servers`), so a headerless `streamable-http` entry would 401 forever with no user-facing fix. Adding one would be strictly worse than omitting it, so the portable file keeps just the local server.

### 4. ClawHub / OpenClaw — already correct, no change needed

Per <https://docs.openclaw.ai/clawhub/skill-format.md>, optional env vars must use `envVars` with `required: false`, and "Do not add optional entries to `requires.env`, because `requires.env` means the skill cannot run without them." Both `SKILL.md` files already do exactly that:

```yaml
openclaw:
  primaryEnv: PASCAL_API_KEY
  envVars:
    - name: PASCAL_API_KEY
      required: false
```

No `requires.env` is declared. `skills/VALIDATION.md` already records OpenClaw 2026.9.3 reporting both skills eligible without a hosted credential. Frontmatter `description` fields were not touched.

## What the formats simply do not support

- **Codex / portable Agent Plugins**: no way to ship an optional (or any) credential for a remote MCP server. Spec-forbidden, and Codex strips it. Documented in both `setup.md` files; users run `codex mcp add pascal --url https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp --bearer-token-env-var PASCAL_API_KEY`.
- **A single shared `mcp.json`**: irreconcilable. Cursor needs `http` + `${VAR}`; the spec needs `streamable-http` + no expansion. Hence the Cursor-specific file.
- **Cursor optional-variable UX**: no docs statement on what the UI shows for an unfilled optional variable. Behaviour when unset is documented as "local server works, `pascal-hosted` returns 401".
- **Pre-existing, not fixed here**: `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` fails Cursor's published `plugin.schema.json` on `author.url` (`author` sets `additionalProperties: false`, allowing only `name` and `email`); 0 of 77 official plugins set it. title: perf: per-slab invalidation, candidate-scoped temporal reconciliation and rotation-stable surface planning (row 17)
body:
## Metric

**Maxi 8× endpoint-drag undo receipt** (charter backlog row 17), measured with the runner's new deterministic `--gesture endpoint`. Same-load pairs on the as-generated fixture, main `77aef84e` vs this branch, dists verified per arm:

| Maxi 8× (472 walls) | forward settle | undo | undo dispatch long task | first clean after undo |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| endpoint drag #1 | 410 ms / 12 frames → 339 / 9 | 1 870 / 65 → **372 / 11** | 507 → 122 ms | 1 172 → 249 ms |
| endpoint drag #2 | 417 / 13 → 389 / 11 | 1 901 / 64 → **369 / 12** | 620 → 117 ms | 1 179 → 237 ms |
| body move (control) | 1 956 / 68 → 358 / 5 | 478 / 12 → nothing to undo¹ | — | — |
| rich-4× body move (control) | 432 / 6 → 427 / 5 | 563 / 5 → 287 / 5 | 407 → 168 ms | — |

¹ The runner's body gesture on the wall it picks here is snapped to zero displacement by the move tool. Main still records three history entries for that no-op commit (the rotated-polygon rewrites below) and spends 12 frames undoing them; this branch records nothing, so Cmd+Z is correctly a no-op (verified in the UI: endpoints identical before/after/undo, no errors).

## Why

A mark-provenance run (temporary `markDirty` tally by writer × kind) on the endpoint undo showed two over-markers:

- `SlabSystems` signed the whole level and re-marked **every slab on the level** (72) on any wall endpoint/thickness/curve change.
- Temporal writes ran space reconciliation on the **full-level path** (forward edits are candidate-scoped), which rewrote 40 unchanged auto slabs + 40 ceilings with identical polygons in rotated vertex order; those read as support changes and `markSlabChangeDependents` marked **252 overlapping walls**.

The second one is scene-state dependent: a save after any full-level pass normalises the stored rings into extractor order and the cascade disappears until the traversal order changes again (forward edits traverse the index, undo walks `level.children`). On a normalised copy of the scene main's endpoint undo is 582 / 14 and 544 / 14; this branch is 374 / 11 and 344 / 11 there.

## What changed

1. `packages/nodes/src/slab/dependency-tracker.ts` (+ `system.tsx`): per-slab derived-polygon signatures (adopted wall bands incl. curve/thickness, sibling seams, elevation, thickness/recessed, level/building transforms) — only slabs whose own inputs changed are marked. Tracker and renderer build the same wall context through a shared `slabPolygonContextForLevel` (a tie in `matchEdgeWallBand` used to be resolvable differently).
2. `packages/core/src/store/use-scene.ts`: undo/redo run reconciliation candidate-scoped to the temporal diff's changed nodes; a fixture-backed test asserts the scoped path yields the same graph as the full-level path, and structural tests cover a closing-wall delete/undo/redo, a split/move/merge cycle and a two-step jump.
3. `packages/core/src/lib/space-detection.ts`: the indexed path's surface scoping rejects strictly disjoint bounding boxes before sampling its 12×12 coverage grid (3 090 of 3 136 pairs on the Maxi body case), and both surface planners keep the stored ring when the extracted one is only a cyclic rotation of it. Reconciliation call on the fixture, median of 10: endpoint undo 96 ms / 80 surface writes → 4.3 ms / 0; body 94 / 80 → 4.3 / 0.

No deletion or covering-dependent marks were involved; those rules are untouched.

## Gates

- e2e: 10/10 against the branch dists (undo/redo graph, perf-regression pack ×5, batched-wall and hidden-wall clicks, floor placement, slab room paint).
- Unit: core 1 511 pass on the tip (5 201 across core/viewer/nodes/editor on the previous tip); `tsc --noEmit` clean; biome clean.
- Two independent audits: the first found one blocker (tracker wall order vs renderer order on adoption ties → shared context builder + tied-wall test) and two should-fixes (per-write derivation cost 0.100 → 0.079 ms via cached inputs and shared wall bands; discriminating structural temporal tests), all closed; the second audited the bbox/rotation commit against its spec and found nothing.

Charter: `plans/performance/editor-scalable-scene-runtime.md` row 17 (private PR follows with the evidence row and the runner's `--gesture` option).

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes slab render-input preparation and auto surface sync equality rules; behavior is guarded by new tests but affects undo/reconciliation paths and anything consuming the new slab context APIs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **prepared, cacheable slab polygon context** so render-time floor outlines can be built once per level and narrowed per slab via bounding-box overlap (`prepareSlabPolygonContext`, `scopeSlabPolygonContext`, `slabPolygonContextChanges`, `slabPolygonContextForLevel`). `getRenderableSlabPolygon` accepts that prepared context; wall and sibling seam data are cached with bounds for cheaper scoped work without changing the full-context polygon result (property test added).

Auto slab/ceiling planners treat polygons that differ only by **cyclic vertex rotation** as unchanged (`sameTuplePolygonRotation`), avoiding no-op polygon rewrites that churn history and downstream invalidation.

title: refactor(packages): fold capture packages into core and viewer
body:
## What does this PR do?

Folds the two beta-only capture packages into `core` and `viewer` as subpath exports, so 1.0.0 ships **seven** packages instead of nine: core, viewer, editor, nodes, mcp, ifc-converter, cli.

| Was | Is now |
|---|---|
| `@pascal-app/capture-protocol` | `@pascal-app/core/capture` |
| `@pascal-app/capture-viewer` | `@pascal-app/viewer/capture` |
| `@pascal-app/capture-viewer/preview` | `@pascal-app/viewer/capture/preview` |

Neither package was ever published to npm, so **no npm consumer migrates** — only in-repo and workspace consumers change import paths. The full named-export surface of each entry point is unchanged.

- `packages/capture-protocol/src/*` → `packages/core/src/capture/*`. It is pure zod/TS, so core keeps its no-Three.js layer rule (`packages/core/src/architecture.test.ts` now walks it). `src/schema/nodes/scan.ts` imports `../../capture/schema` directly, and `@pascal-app/capture-protocol` is gone from core's dependencies (zod stays at core's `>=4.5.4 <4.6`).
- `packages/capture-viewer/src/*` → `packages/viewer/src/capture/*`, with `@pascal-app/capture-protocol` imports rewritten to `@pascal-app/core/capture`. The three formerly self-referential `@pascal-app/viewer` imports (`ErrorBoundary`, `useNodeEvents`, `useViewer`, `useGLTFKTX2`) now use relative paths. capture-viewer's peers were already a subset of viewer's, so no peer or dependency changes were needed.
- Tests moved with the code: 41 tests across 9 files, unchanged.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: both packages removed from the `package` input choices, the bump/sync/echo loops, `RELEASE_PACKAGES`, the two "Build & publish" steps, and the commit/tag lists. Publish order stays core → viewer → editor → nodes → mcp → ifc-converter → cli, and the `elif npm view` idempotency guards are untouched. The per-package version env exports are generated by the bump loop, so they disappear with the list entries.
- Docs: `README.md` (install snippet, repo tree, package table), `AGENTS.md` repo-shape table, `wiki/architecture/capture-runtime.md` ownership boundaries, and the capture sections previously in the two package READMEs now live in `packages/core/README.md` and `packages/viewer/README.md`. `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased records the fold.
- `bun.lock` regenerated (`-47 lines`); no other manifest referenced the packages, and `turbo.json`, root `package.json` workspaces, and `biome.jsonc` all match by glob so they needed no edit. `ci.yml` / `mcp-ci.yml` never named either package.

### One follow-up consequence worth reviewing

The old packages exported their **TypeScript source** under the `react-native`/`browser` conditions so Metro could consume them from a clean checkout without generated `dist`. The new subpaths follow core's and viewer's existing convention instead — `types`/`import`/`default` all point at `dist` — because every other `@pascal-app/core` and `@pascal-app/viewer` subpath does, and pointing a condition at `./src` would require publishing 4.7 MB of TypeScript in both tarballs.

Consequence for the private monorepo's Expo capture app (handled in the follow-up import PR, not here): it must add `@pascal-app/core` + `@pascal-app/viewer` as workspace dependencies, and `editor/packages/{core,viewer}/dist` must exist before Metro bundles. `dev:editor-packages` already builds both, so `bun dev` is fine; a Metro-only or EAS invocation needs the package build first.

## How to test

1. `bun install && bun run build` — `packages/core/dist/capture/index.d.ts`, `packages/viewer/dist/capture/index.d.ts` and `packages/viewer/dist/capture/preview.d.ts` are emitted, and `npm pack --dry-run` in both packages includes them.
2. `bun run test` — 13/13 turbo tasks pass (core 1530, viewer 338, editor 933, nodes 2535, mcp 361, cli 102, ifc-converter 13, app 41). `bun test packages/core/src/capture packages/viewer/src/capture` runs the 41 moved tests.
3. `bun run check` — clean (2156 files). `bun run skills:validate` — clean.
4. Release gate: `PASCAL_PORTABLE_BUILD=1 bun run build --filter editor`, then in `packages/cli` `bun run build && bun run build-runtime && bun run stage-runtime && bun run smoke-runtime` — packed CLI smoke passes (46 MCP tools, digest verified, scene round-tripped).
5. `ruby -ryaml -e 'YAML.load_file(".github/workflows/release.yml")'` parses.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not applicable — no visual change; the capture runtime renders exactly as before from its new location.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)

title: ci(release): drop registry-url so npm uses OIDC trusted publishing

## What does this PR do?

Release run 34624024769 failed at "Build & publish core" with `E404 Not Found - PUT …/@pascal-app/core`. The job's environment shows `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX` and `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG: …/_temp/.npmrc`: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` writes an `.npmrc` whose `_authToken` falls back to that placeholder when no token is provided, so npm authenticated with a fake token (masked as 404) and never attempted the OIDC trusted-publishing exchange.
