title: feat(assets): add conservative explicit cleanup for local files
body: ## What does this PR do? Adds conservative, explicit cleanup for local `asset://` data related to #733. Core exposes deletion, enumeration, sweeping, and reference collectors; the editor host API inventories the live graph, local draft, and every persisted scene before an explicitly requested sweep. Uncertain or malformed inventories abort cleanup. The host API has no automatic caller. Hosts must ensure a complete scene inventory, no in-flight writes or uploads, and enough API rate budget. This does not fully fix #733 or delete assets when an individual node is removed. This revision rebases the existing contribution onto `main` (`d7d0b436f2bda4bfb38fa3d083c1d1816ec7481c`), regenerates `bun.lock` with the repository's Bun 1.4.4, and aligns the editor test dependency with core's `fake-indexeddb ^6.2.6`. New public-API regression tests exercise both legacy `File` values and the proposed `{ assetVersion: 1, bytes, type }` records: listing sees both, deletion preserves unrelated keys, and explicit sweeping preserves referenced record payloads. ## How to test 1. Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` with Bun 1.4.4 and a supported Node version. The lockfile was regenerated with `bun install`; the pre-push frozen-lockfile dry run passed. 2. Run `bun test packages/core/src/lib/asset-storage.test.ts packages/core/src/lib/local-asset-lifecycle.test.ts apps/editor/lib/local-asset-gc.test.ts`. All 28 tests passed, covering asset storage, nested references, inventory aborts, and the live graph re-read. 3. Run `bun run check-types` and `bun run check`. All 14 type-check/build dependency tasks passed; Biome passed with existing warnings. `bun x --no-install turbo run build --filter=@pascal-app/core` also passed. At `a0adc5ff`, the core build, 28 focused tests, and 14 pre-push type-check/build tasks passed locally on Windows. The keep-set now includes deeply nested plugin fields and graph-level references, and a malformed node map aborts the sweep. The [CI run](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/actions/runs/45581669042) and [MCP CI run](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/actions/runs/45581669514) passed. These include Linux tests and builds, lint, type checks, and macOS CLI smoke coverage. The new record tests verify enumeration/deletion/sweeping, not loading the record format proposed by #912. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch ## Review questions - **Delete then recreate / shared URL:** No timer runs after a node delete. Explicit GC retains any URL found in the complete persisted inventory or the re-read live graph, including materials. There is no per-node or cross-scene reference counter. - **Page reload:** There is no pending timer to survive reload. Orphans remain until a host explicitly runs GC under the conditions above. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Incorrect sweeps could delete origin-shared `asset://` data still referenced by other scenes; mitigation is strict null-on-uncertainty, but callers must invoke GC only under safe conditions. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a0adc5ffac27aed42085206f9bb123e079a3359f. title: fix(editor): improve duct routing and parametric controls
body:
## What does this PR do?

- **Rectangular and oval duct wall clearance**
  - Issue: Rectangular and oval ducts could be placed partly inside a wall because placement clearance used only the profile height.
  - Fixed: Placement and wall attachments now use the largest profile dimension, with a small wall standoff for non-round ducts.

- **Keep a run on its starting wall**
  - Issue: Continuing a duct or pipe run could move onto another wall when the cursor crossed the room.
  - Fixed: The run stays constrained to the wall face where its first point was placed.

- **Automatic endcap cleanup**
  - Issue: Deleting a duct or pipe left its automatically generated endcap behind.
  - Fixed: Deleting a run removes its automatic endcap while preserving manually placed endcaps.

- **Parametric inspector controls**
  - Issue: Inspector groups and action buttons did not support the desired initial layout and grouping.
  - Fixed: Groups can specify their initial expansion state, and parametric actions use a two-column layout where appropriate.

1. Run the editor with `bun run dev`.
   - The editor should start at http://localhost:3002.

2. Draw round, rectangular, and oval duct runs against a wall.
   - All profiles should remain outside the wall, and continuing a run should stay on its starting wall face.

3. Delete a duct or pipe with an automatic endcap.
   - The automatic endcap should be deleted with the run; manually placed endcaps should remain.

4. Open a parametric inspector with multiple groups and actions.

title: fix(editor): make model export survive runtime userData and KTX2 normal maps
body:
Two regressions from #831's new portable export path, both hit from Settings → Export GLB and shared by the bake exporter.

## 1. `structuredClone` on live userData

`cloneSceneForExport` (and the portable-export clones) copied every object's userData with `structuredClone`, which throws on the first function it meets. Live scenes keep runtime resources in userData — the pool plugin's water-effect material, the environment plugin's grass uniforms — and their `RenderObject` dispose listeners are functions, so the export died with `()=>{this.dispose()} could not be cloned`.

`cloneExportUserData` deep-copies plain data and drops functions and three resources (Object3D / Material / Texture / BufferGeometry / Node). Exports only read plain markers back out of userData.

## 2. Compressed normal maps

The normaliser bakes `normalScale` into normal-map pixels on the CPU, which KTX2 library materials cannot provide: `Compressed normal map "NormalGL_…" must be baked before portable export`. A pre-pass now decompresses exactly the normal maps that will be canonicalised (WebGPUTextureUtils, injectable via `decompressTexture`).

The same pass stops canonicalising by-reference placeholders in the viewer bake. Baking the scale into a 1×1 placeholder dropped both the `pascalTextureRef` and the strength, so every stamped normal map with a non-unit scale — every glTF-loaded item, whose loader sets `normalScale.y = -1` — lost its normal map in the baked artifact. Placeholders keep their texture and scalar scale for the packer.

## Open question (not changed here)

For glTF-loaded items, canonicalising the loader's `(1, -1)` scale into pixels inverts the green channel of the exported normal map relative to the glTF convention. Worth a look from whoever owns the portable path: it may need to skip the sign flip and export the scalar scale instead.

## Tests

`export-user-data.test.ts` (new), regression cases in `glb-export.test.ts` and `portable-export.test.ts`; 51 tests green, `tsgo --noEmit` clean.

Compressed normals are GPU-decompressed once (default `WebGPUTextureUtils`, overridable via **`decompressTexture`**). In **reference** texture mode, normals stamped with **`pascalTextureRef`** are **preserved**—not decompressed or canonicalized—so placeholders keep their ref and scale (e.g. glTF `(1, -1)`).

title: feat(editor): Send to Blender from the settings panel
body:
Adds a **Send to Blender** button under Settings → Export, next to the export buttons. It hands the live scene to the [Pascal Blender add-on](https://github.com/pascalorg/blender-addon) listening on loopback, so a scene lands in an open Blender without a download step.

## Flow

1. Probe `GET http://127.0.0.1:27412/pascal/health` (and four fallback ports), one second each.
2. Run the same portable GLB export as *Export GLB* (same "Include in file" choices) with `download: false`.
3. `POST /pascal/import` with the blob and `X-Pascal-Project-Name` / `X-Pascal-Project-Id` headers.
4. Poll `GET /pascal/import/<id>` until Blender reports `done` or `failed`, then show its summary.

Messages cover the two failure modes users will actually hit: Blender not listening (link to the add-on), and Blender open but this origin not allowed yet (the add-on's Pascal tab shows an Allow button for it).

## Code

- `lib/send-to-app.ts` — protocol client (`probeLocalApp`, `sendGlbToLocalApp`, `waitForLocalImport`) with injectable `fetch`; unit tests in `send-to-app.test.ts`.
- Settings panel: the button, a step label while it runs, and a new optional `projectName` prop used as the scene name in Blender.

## Verified

Headless Chromium against the local community app with a headless Blender 5.2.1 running the add-on: Wawa House exported, posted, imported — "Sent to Blender. Imported Pascal scene: 1251 objects, 2 levels, 12 zones." Chrome's private-network preflight is answered by the add-on. Firefox and Safari not yet exercised.

## Open point

The portable export is static by design since #831, so the Blender copy has no door/window open clips (the viewer bake keeps them). If we want them in Blender, an option to keep clips on the portable path is the follow-up.

title: fix(editor): export see-through glass as transmission glass in portable files
body:
Portable exports (Export GLB / USDZ, Send to Blender) wrote glass as a plain 30% alpha blend, because the viewer's glass is a fresnel-driven opacity node that glTF cannot carry. In Blender, Unity or Unreal that reads as a blue plastic film.

Untextured see-through materials under the viewer's own glass threshold (`transparent` with opacity < 0.6, the same rule as `maybeApplyGlassFresnel`) now export as `MeshPhysicalMaterial` with `transmission: 1`, `ior: 1.5` and roughness capped at 0.15 — `KHR_materials_transmission` + `KHR_materials_ior`, which every major consumer renders as real glass. The authored opacity becomes the tint strength (30% opacity keeps 30% of the tint).

The viewer bake (`purpose: 'viewer'`) is unchanged, so the hosted `/viewer` keeps its current look and avoids a transmission pass.

Test: `portable glass` in `glb-export.test.ts` covers the portable conversion, the tinted-plastic case above the threshold, and the untouched viewer path.

title: fix(editor): keep door and window clips in GLB downloads
body:
Since #831 the portable export path bakes no door/window open clips ("portable downloads are static"), so **Export GLB** and **Send to Blender** lost the clips every GLB carried before. Those clips are valid glTF and Blender imports them as actions, so for GLB the omission is a loss for nothing.

Clips become an explicit `animations: 'keep' | 'none'` export option:

- **GLB** keeps them by default (Export GLB, Send to Blender).
- **USDZ** passes `none`: it freezes geometry and USDPreviewSurface cannot play them.
- **STL / OBJ / print** are unchanged (static).
- **Viewer bake** is unchanged.

@adamnaili-pascal if #831 had another reason for dropping them on the portable path (beyond USDZ/print freezing), shout and I'll adjust.

Test: `portable clips` in `glb-export.test.ts` covers keep / none / the legacy default, and checks the clip's track targets a node that survives in the exported tree.

title: Browser scene creation returns 503 behind reverse proxy
body:
## Browser scene creation returns 503 on reverse-proxied self-hosted editor

### Reproduction

1. Deploy Pascal Editor behind a reverse proxy at `https://pascal.example.com`.
2. Set `PASCAL_SCENE_API_ORIGINS=https://pascal.example.com`.
3. Leave `PASCAL_SCENE_API_TOKEN` unset.
4. Open `/scenes` and click **Create new scene**.

The browser POST to `/api/scenes` fails with:

```json
{"error":"scene_api_token_required"}
```

The UI displays `Failed to create scene (503)`.

### Root cause

`scene-api-security.ts` correctly validates the configured browser origin, but `validateAuth()` then requires a token for every non-loopback request. A same-origin browser request arriving through the reverse proxy is not identified as loopback. The frontend does not send `Authorization` or `X-Pascal-Scene-Token`, so scene creation cannot work with the documented public-origin configuration.

### Expected behavior

A browser request from an origin listed in `PASCAL_SCENE_API_ORIGINS` should be accepted without an API token, while non-browser/API clients should continue to require token authentication.

### Environment

- Pascal Editor deployed with Docker/Openship
- Public origin configured with `PASCAL_SCENE_API_ORIGINS`
- Reverse proxy terminates TLS

title: Surface hosting protocol: any node that offers a surface can host any placeable asset
body:
## What

Hosting was the one layer of the editor that never became data-driven. Six declarations answered "who can host whom", two movers hardcoded the answer per kind, and the generic service in `core/src/services/hosting.ts` had five of its six functions with zero production callers. The visible symptoms were a procedural item that could not sit on a shelf, and a kitchen countertop that hosted nothing at all, for any asset type.

Surfaces are now first-class and addressable, with two providers. **Declared** surfaces come from nodes that know their own geometry: shelf boards, countertop spans, bar ledges, a recipe's named surfaces. **Hit-derived** surfaces come from the raycast for every other mesh, which is how a book still lands anywhere on a sofa armrest. Absence of a declaration means freeform and allowed, never unhostable.

## Behaviour

- **Shelves, countertops and islands hold things**, for catalog items and generated designs alike, through both movers. Counters elect no sub-surface, so you slide freely along them; the bar ledge is its own surface at its own height; sink and hob cutouts refuse; wall and tall units publish nothing so a kettle cannot land on a pantry.
- **A generated design holds things anywhere on it.** Where its recipe names a surface, the child stores the surface id and a surface-frame pose and survives the design being resized. Otherwise the surface comes from the pointer hit and the child stores a pose only.
- **Fit follows the world, not a rectangle.** Something stays hosted while its centre is on the surface, so overhang is free and it lets go only past halfway. Nothing is clamped or snapped back.
- **Hosted movement makes the same sound as the ground**, through one shared tick, without doubling when a grid event and a host event arrive together.
- **`hostable.parents` is gone as an eligibility gate**; the host's surface decides.

## Fixes found on the way

- **Procedural items were never a persisted node kind**, so the scene API used by agents rejected any scene containing one and collaborative projects refused the node outright.
- **A runtime import cycle** appeared when that was fixed, and is broken by extracting the pure footprint helper.
- **Recipes could not express whole-number division**, so every generated design using an indexed grid put a stray part outside its bounds; a four-legged table with a stated width of 450 mm measured 655 mm. Adds `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `abs` and `mod`.
- **A dragged mesh floated above its own preview box** whenever a host stood on a raised slab or was itself hosted; 52 combinations were wrong.
- **Editing a slab deleted everything standing on it.** Removing the host allowlists made slabs reachable as hosts, which released main does not allow, and a slab's schema has no `children` field so every update stripped the link. Slabs defer to floor placement again, and an update that omits `children` now carries them forward, closing the same hole for 24 other kinds.

## Checks

Editor 1032, core 2807, nodes 3110, viewer 341, host and preview matrices 406, frozen behaviour table 720. Root typecheck 12/12, Biome clean, zero skips in core and editor.

The frozen table records 717 cases across three adapters with per-adapter guards asserting both accepted and refused verdicts are represented, after a section once collapsed to a single verdict and hid two real defects.

Browser-verified on a live scene: a procedural item on a shelf board with row switching, gap stickiness, reload and undo; catalog items on counters with the countertop proven not to rebuild across ~14k sampled frames.

## Not in this PR

2D floor plan hosting (acquire, retain, cycle) and the remaining adapters for column tops and block faces. Tracked in `plans/editor-surface-hosting-protocol.md` in the private repo.

https://claude.ai/code/session_013LKpG6PpZe6Jb4dBBAKtBG

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes scene schema, save/load semantics, and placement/hosting paths across many node kinds; incorrect fit or child retention could drop or misplace hosted assets, though broad automated tests mitigate this.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a **data-driven surface hosting** layer (`surface-hosting`, `surface-region`, shelf board helpers) with centre-based fit rules (overhang allowed until the centre leaves the surface) and tests for declared vs hit-derived hosts. **`canAttach` no longer enforces `hostable.parents`**; eligibility moves to the host’s published surfaces.
> 
> **Procedural items become a first-class persisted `AnyNode` kind** (`ProceduralItemNode` in the discriminated union via `safeExtend`, level child typing, schema export). Host **`children` lists widen to arbitrary string ids** on shelf, cabinet, block, item, and column so catalog items, procedural designs, and plugin kinds can round-trip; a frozen corpus + load/save tests lock backward compatibility.
> 
> **Refactors** pull `getFloorPlacedFootprints` and `itemOverlapsPolygon` out of the spatial-grid stack into pure modules so schema/procedural code can bundle without pulling scene runtime (covered by a browser import test).
> 
> **Procedural recipes** gain `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `abs`, and `mod` so indexed grid layouts (e.g. 2×2 table legs) stay within nominal bounds; `query.ts` extends floor lift / world frames for shelves and cabinets and tightens attachment checks with `surfaceRegionContainsPoint`.
> 
> Registry types add optional **`surfaces.hosting`** and **`geometryChildTypes`** for surface providers and geometry invalidation from hosted children.

title: fix(viewer): preserve snapshot atmosphere and capture isolation
body:
## Summary

- render snapshot backdrops from the active `SceneAtmosphere` source, with the scene theme as the fallback
- keep the scene MRT transparent inside the nested Three.js r186 pass so preset captures retain alpha
- make preset isolation explicitly transparent while preserving the existing host scene-slot visibility policy
- pin Environment to `1aa0bc3`, adding its global visibility control, isolation-aware runtime, and Three.js 0.186 support

## Root cause

Three.js r186 resets renderer clear state inside `RTTNode` before the nested scene pass. The snapshot MRT therefore cleared empty sky to opaque alpha even when the outer capture requested transparency. Separately, the snapshot graph always synthesized the scene-theme backdrop, so active presentation skies never reached stored thumbnails.

## Verification

- `bunx tsgo --noEmit -p packages/editor/tsconfig.json`
- `bun run check-types` — 10/10 workspace tasks passed
- `bun run build` in `packages/viewer`
- `bun test packages/editor/src/components/editor/snapshot-capture.test.ts` — 19 passed
- `bunx biome check` on every changed source and manifest
- real editor smoke at Three.js 0.186: Environment master control rendered with the documented subtext; enabling it changed the live sky, disabling it restored the native background
- real WebGPU/Metal capture QA: native and Environment skies captured correctly; preset exterior remained transparent

Environment release verification:

- `bun test` — 347 passed
- `bun run check-types`
- lab `bun run check-types`

Environment commit: https://github.com/AxiomeCG/environment/commit/1aa0bc3cbed273dbf751e9af79e446f6de105c90

## Scope correction

The `viewerSceneSlot` gate is unchanged from upstream: `{!noEditing && viewerSceneSlot}`. Neither bundled editor mount supplies this optional host slot, and Environment uses `ViewerPresentations`, not the slot. Host-only Building Lab placeholders are outside this PR. After restoring the gate, `tsgo`, all 19 snapshot tests, and targeted Biome checks passed. Verified against freshly fetched `pascalorg/editor` main: the merge-base is `bcdf422a23580bf533893a73c2aba2192b05a762`. The entire `ViewerSceneContent` component matches that baseline byte-for-byte; the remaining `index.tsx` diff only changes preset isolation selection and transparency.

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core WebGPU snapshot rendering, per-frame isolation/fog handling, and a pinned third-party Environment plugin—high user-visible impact but scoped to capture and presentation paths with added tests.

> **Overview**
> **Snapshot and preset capture** now match what users see in the viewport: offscreen pipelines take an optional `useSceneAtmosphere()` source so thumbnails use the active presentation sky (native or Environment) instead of always compositing the scene-theme gradient. `createSnapshotPipeline` adds a custom scene pass that forces transparent clears inside Three.js r186 nested RTTs, fixing opaque skies on preset captures.

title: feat(wall): typed exact length during two-click wall drafting
body:
Closes #308.

## What

While drafting a wall in the two-click flow, typing an exact length (e.g. `3m`, `180cm`, `2500` in mm notation, `10'6"`) now locks the draft to that length along the current draft direction — the pointer keeps steering the direction only.

- **Enter** commits the wall at the typed length.
- **Escape** is two-stage: first press clears the typing buffer, second press cancels the draft (per the triage note on #308).
- **Backspace/Delete** edit the buffer.
- The HUD label shows the buffer while typing and falls back to the normal drafting label when empty.

## How

- New shared store `useWallDraftTyping` (`packages/editor/src/store/use-wall-draft-typing.ts`) holds the buffer so the 2D floor-plan draft and the 3D wall tool stay in lockstep per the 2D ↔ 3D parity rule in `wiki/architecture/tools.md`.
- 3D (`packages/nodes/src/wall/tool.tsx`): a `window` keydown listener mirrors the cabinet tool's `applyTypedDimension` pattern — `parseMeasurement` resolves the buffer with the same bare-unit defaults; `grid:move` projects the draft end onto the typed length; Enter synthesizes a `grid:click` at the projected endpoint so the normal commit pipeline (chain continuation, auto-close, support-slab election) runs unchanged.
- 2D (`floorplan-panel.tsx`): the same projection in the wall-draft pointer move, the same key handling in the window keydown effect, and the HUD label override.
- Angle snap / junction snap / magnetic alignment continue to work on untyped drafts; the typed commit intentionally bypasses endpoint snap so the typed length survives exactly (drafting direction is taken from the current snapped pointer, so snapped angles still steer it).

## Testing

- `packages/editor/src/store/use-wall-draft-typing.test.ts` — buffer lifecycle + accepted keys.
- `packages/nodes/src/wall/typed-length.test.ts` — the projection math shared by both views.
- Full `@pascal-app/editor` + `@pascal-app/nodes` suites pass (`turbo run test`: 3119 tests across 268 files, plus the editor suite).
- `tsgo --noEmit` clean for both packages; `biome check` clean on touched files.

Verified end-to-end on a self-hosted deployment (design.dekorproduct.com) in both the 2D plan and 3D views with metric-m and mm notations.

Thanks for the detailed triage spec on #308 — the interaction follows it point by point.

title: Typed coordinate entry for item placement (distance-from-wall + offset, AutoCAD-style)
body:
## Context

#308 added typed exact length while drafting walls (merged in #883). The next gap for precise placement: after a wall exists, placing items at exact distances still requires pixel-perfect mousing.

Cabinets already support typed **dimensions** (W/D/H) via the measurement pills + Tab cycling (#880-adjacent work in `packages/nodes/src/cabinet/tool.tsx`). What is missing is typed **position**: an AutoCAD-style two-field dynamic input where you type one axis, Tab to the second axis, then Enter to place.

## Proposal

While a placement tool is active and a snap point/reference exists:

1. Typing a number opens a two-field inline input (X = distance along reference, Y = offset from it), like AutoCAD's dynamic input.
2. **Tab** toggles focus between fields; the inactive field keeps its live pointer-tracked value.
3. **Enter** commits placement at the typed coordinates.
4. Values accept the full `parseMeasurement` grammar (m/cm/mm/ft-in), consistent with #883.
5. Escape clears the fields first, then cancels the tool (same two-stage pattern as #883).

## Implementation notes

- The typed-buffer store from #883 (`packages/editor/src/store/use-wall-draft-typing.ts`) is a proven base; generalize it to two fields with an active-field index.
- Same parity requirement as #883: 2D floorplan and 3D viewport must both get the behavior in one PR (`wiki/architecture/tools.md`).
- First candidates: cabinet/window/door placement against a wall.

## Out of scope (for the first cut)

- Polar coordinate entry (distance + angle) — could reuse the same store later.
- Absolute X/Y world coordinates — the from-wall reference is what designers expect.

Happy to implement this if maintainers agree on the interaction shape.

- 3D: coordinate entry rendered next to the preview via `Html`.

title: editor: keep GLB and USDZ exports from hanging
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the Export panel getting stuck on "Exporting GLB…" / "Preparing GLB file…" with nothing downloading (reported by a user of the open-source editor on a two-level, furnished scene). The panel's `try/catch/finally` is sound, so the only way to reach that state is an export promise that never settles, and the portable export path had two of those:

- **Per-texture GPU renderer.** Both the GLB and USDZ exporters used three's `WebGPUTextureUtils.decompress` for every compressed KTX2 texture. It constructs, initialises (adapter + device request, **no timeout**) and disposes a whole `WebGPURenderer` per texture; a furnished scene pays that dozens of times and a single stalled device request parks the export silently. Passing it a renderer is not an option: it resizes the renderer it is given (the live viewer's canvas) and, in r186, throws on the first call that supplies one (`_renderer` starts `undefined`, the cleanup checks `!== null`).
- **Unreportable exporter failures.** `GLTFExporter`'s binary path completes inside `FileReader.onloadend` callbacks with no error handler, after `writeAsync` has already resolved, and wraps `canvas.toBlob` in a promise that never rejects. A failed read calls neither `onDone` nor `onError`; the final read can hand `onDone` `null`, which `new Blob([null])` turned into a four-byte download.

Changes:

- `export-texture-utils.ts` (new): one bounded GPU decompressor per export, shared by preparation (normal-map baking) and serialisation, for GLB and USDZ. Built on the viewer's `initializeGpuRenderer`, so it gets the same adapter/init timeouts and WebGL fallback as the viewer, releases its device on dispose, and refuses work after dispose.
- `glb-export.ts`: every export runs under `withExportDeadline` (3 min default, `timeoutMs` option, `Infinity` disables). Covers plugin `bakeGeometryAsync` / presentation builders as well as the exporter. A `null` result rejects instead of resolving. `serializePreparedSceneToGlb` takes the shared `textureUtils`.
- `usdz-export.ts`: same decompressor and deadline.
- `bake-exporter.tsx`: passes `timeoutMs: Infinity`; the bake worker owns its deadline (`BAKE_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so headless bake behaviour is unchanged.
- Tests: `export-texture-utils.test.ts` (single renderer across textures, clamping, start-up failure, post-dispose guard) and `glb-export-serialize.test.ts` (drives the real `GLTFExporter` with a DOM stand-in: FileReader failure → deadline rejection, final-read `null` → "produced no data", compressed textures routed through the shared decompressor, never-settling plugin hook → deadline, preparation and serialisation share one decompressor).

Follow-ups deliberately left out (tracked privately): upstream three fix for `FileReader.onerror` in `GLTFExporter`, capping `maxTextureSize` / JPEG for opaque maps to shrink portable GLBs, `downloadBlob` revoke timing.

Refs #831 (introduced the portable export path), #867 (added the second `WebGPUTextureUtils` caller).

## How to test

1. `cd packages/editor && bun test src/lib/glb-export-serialize.test.ts src/lib/export-texture-utils.test.ts` — 14 tests, all exercising the real `GLTFExporter` / decompressor.
2. `bun test src` in `packages/editor` (1050 pass) and `bun run check-types` (clean).
3. In the editor with a scene using KTX2 finishes and furniture: Settings → Export GLB and Export USDZ. Expected: files download, button returns to "Export GLB", no error line. Textures in the GLB match the viewer (verified in headless Chromium against `public/material/leather/calf_leather/*.ktx2`: pixel-identical to the stock decompressor).
4. Regression guard for the hang: temporarily make a plugin's `bakeGeometryAsync` return a never-settling promise, export, wait 3 min → the panel shows "GLB export timed out after 180 s…" and the buttons re-enable.

Timing for eight decompress calls in headless Chromium, shared renderer vs stock per-texture renderer:

| Backend | Shared | Stock |
|---|---|---|
| SwiftShader | 18 ms | 359 ms |
| Metal | 40 ms | 501 ms |

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — non-visual change (export pipeline). The user's report screenshot shows the stuck state: "Exporting GLB…" button with "Preparing GLB file…" status and the sibling export buttons disabled.

title: fix(nodes): unmount inside act() in the hosted movement sfx test
body:
## Summary

`registry pending floor sound is cancelled on unmount` has failed on every `private-editor` CI run since #881 landed, keeping `main` red for two days. It is a **test race, not a product bug**.

The `unmount` case called `renderer.unmount()` *after* the `act()` block, while `commit` and `cancel` finish their interaction inside it:

```ts
await act(async () => {
  emitter.emit('grid:move', event as never)
  if (finish === 'commit') emitter.emit('grid:click', ...)
  else if (finish === 'cancel') emitter.emit('tool:cancel')
})
if (finish === 'unmount') await renderer.unmount()   // races the 0ms timer
```

`grid:move` schedules the floor cue on `setTimeout(flush, 0)` (`movement-tick.ts:22`), and async `act()` schedules a completion task before resolving (`timers.setImmediate`). On a loaded CI runner that yield is long enough for the cue to fire before unmount, so `sfx:grid-snap` leaks into a case that asserts `[]`. Cleanup *does* call `movementSfx.cancel()` (`move-registry-node-tool.tsx:1356`), but cancellation cannot undo an already-emitted event.

Moving the unmount inside `act()` makes cleanup run before that yield, matching how `commit` and `cancel` already work.

## Why the product code is fine

The trace under an injected delay shows the ordering plainly:

```
TRACE EMIT sfx:grid-snap   (tick ← pending ← flush)
TRACE UNMOUNT REQUEST
TRACE CLEAR                (cancel ← move-registry-node-tool.tsx:1356)
TRACE UNMOUNT COMPLETE
```

Cancellation runs; it is simply too late. Explicit `tool:cancel` cancels synchronously (`:1335`), which is why that case never flaked.

## Verification

The failure is timing-dependent and does not reproduce on an unloaded machine, so it was reproduced deterministically by delaying React's `act()` completion task (`timers.setImmediate`) by 10 ms:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 3 `pending floor sound` cases, 10 ms delay injected | **1 fail** (unmount), 2 pass | **3 pass** |

- `bun test src/shared/hosted-movement-sfx.test.tsx` — 54 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run test` (full `@pascal-app/nodes` suite) — 3118 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail
- `bunx biome check` on the changed file — clean

> **Overview**

> 
> The test now calls **`renderer.unmount()` inside the same `act()` block** as `grid:move` (alongside how commit/cancel already finish), instead of after `act()` resolves. That avoids racing a **0ms deferred floor snap cue**: async `act()` can yield long enough on loaded runners for `sfx:grid-snap` to emit before unmount/cancel runs, which broke the assertion that unmount should leave **`sounds` empty**. title: cli: start the web runtime this CLI was published with
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the CLI keeping an old web runtime after an upgrade. `startEditorUnlocked` launched whatever `~/.pascal/run/current-runtime.json` pointed at and only called `ensureWebRuntime` when nothing had ever been installed or `--runtime` was given. So `npx @pascal-app/cli@1.0.1 editor` printed "Editor runtime 1.0.0 ready", `pascal doctor` said "Installed web runtime 1.0.0", and the 1.0.1 runtime with the GLB export fix (#888) was never downloaded. The README already documented resolution as "the runtime installed for this CLI version".

- `editor-process.ts`: new `pinnedRuntimeVersion()` reads the version in `dist/runtime-source.json` (null with `--runtime`, `PASCAL_BUNDLED_RUNTIME_DIR`, or when the manifest is unreadable, e.g. running from source). Start provisions the runtime when the active one differs; `ensureWebRuntime` already reuses an installed copy or downloads and health-checks. When the editor is already running on another runtime, a new `runtime-outdated` progress event is emitted instead of restarting under the user.
- `bin/pascal.ts` + `terminal-progress.ts`: prints `! Editor runtime 1.0.0 is running; this CLI ships 1.0.1. Run "pascal restart" to switch.`
- `diagnostics.ts`: `doctor` warns with both versions when they differ.
- README: documents the upgrade behaviour.
- Tests: start switches to the pinned runtime (installed but inactive copy, no download), already-running older runtime is reported not restarted, unreadable manifest keeps the active runtime, doctor mismatch warning.

Reported by a user who upgraded to `@pascal-app/cli@1.0.1` and still could not export GLB. Their immediate workaround is `pascal update` (or `pascal update --version 1.0.1`), which already installs and activates the CLI's runtime.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/cli && bun test src` — 107 pass (4 new).
2. `bun run check-types` in `packages/cli`.
3. Manual: with a 1.0.0 runtime active (`~/.pascal/run/current-runtime.json`), run the built CLI's `pascal start`; expect a runtime download and "Editor runtime <pinned> installed". Start it again while running with a different pinned version: expect the `!` notice and `alreadyRunning`.

title: fix(hosting): stop objects vanishing on unrenderable hosts, correct 2D exits
body:
## Why
Follow-ups to the surface hosting protocol (#881), driven by three things found after it shipped:

1. **Objects vanished.** #881 removed the registry mover's host allowlist, so a generated design, a cabinet or a column could be parented onto about 36 kinds. About 20 of them never render a child (column, stairs, door, window, roof parts, vents), and the 2D plan threw `Unsupported host` for about 30. Production already had a column under a tree, a column under an elevator, and a cabinet plus a generated design under a grass field.
2. **2D exits floated.** Dragging a hosted object off its host in plan view kept the old host-local height on a level-parented node, with rotation and slab support unresolved.
3. **Two commit jumps in 3D**, both present on main: a generated design moved onto a 90°-rotated countertop turned 90° at commit, and a catalog item released over an occupied named surface jumped about 0.3 m after throwing.

## What changes
**Host eligibility (shared resolver, no kind list in the movers)**
- A host must retain the child id in its schema and mount children. Geometry-only definitions are inferred. Custom renderers stay permissive, as on main, and opt out with `rendersChildren: false`. Every built-in that does not mount children declares it, and a mounted sweep fails if a declaration disagrees with what is rendered.
- Ineligible hosts, and walls and ceilings in the registry mover, defer silently to floor support, the same path slabs use. No refusal label.
- `capabilities.surfacePlacement: 'floor-only'` on `cabinet`, `column`, `stair`, `elevator`, `fence`. They never rest on a surface. Structural parenting by their own tools is untouched.
- `nodeLevelFrame` composes any ancestor generically instead of throwing, so legacy slab-parented stacks and children of plugin nodes open, render and save unchanged.

**Plan view (owner decision: pro-CAD model)**
- 2D never acquires a host and has no cycling key. A hosted object keeps its host while its footprint centre is on the surface, re-validated against the live surface every tick and at commit.
- Leaving the host matches the 3D detach: level parent, floor datum, canonical `[0, yaw, 0]` for upright children, slab support re-elected, procedural attachment removed in the same transaction, block-face fields cleaned.
- The 3D mesh shows the pose that will be committed during a 2D drag and is restored on Escape, re-entry and unmount.
- Generated designs can be picked up in plan view. Moved subtrees are dirtied. Movement sound follows the preview pose.
- 2D rendering keeps main's resolver; the mover reuses it. Fifteen output pins pass on main's resolver too.

**Fixes to defects that exist on main**
- Registry mover: a batched floor excursion left a stale imperative transform when the pointer returned to the host with unchanged props. Accepted local position and rotation are reapplied.
- Occupied named surface: occupancy is checked before the placement is accepted, so the last valid preview stays and release is blocked, instead of throwing after the draft was mutated.
- `cloneNodesInto` remaps procedural `attachments` to the fresh ids.

## Tests
- Run from each package: core 2842, nodes 3269 (one existing skip), editor 1050, viewer 351. All pass.
- The 717 frozen resolver cases are byte-identical. Pre-existing tests changed only where they encoded the regression: unregistered hosts defer, ineligible-host diagnostics are silent, non-rendering provider hosts stay floor-parented, two procedural 2D exits expect Y 0.
- New: mounted production-registry sweep over every built-in kind in both movers and both native event orders; mounted 2D exit and rendered-pose suites; production plan pins; Table Lamp preview-equals-commit pin.
- Four rounds of independent review and four real-browser passes, including a side-by-side run against main that classified the two commit jumps as pre-existing.

## Not in this PR
Column tops, block faces as first-class providers and the end-to-end plugin mover proof (slice G). Until then a drop on a column goes to the floor.

body:
## What users get
- **No more blinking on block side faces.** A hosted child's preview override entered the block's geometry dependencies, so every pointer move rebuilt the block mesh, fired pointer leave and enter, and destroyed and recreated the draft: 100 rebuilds and 200 floor/face flips per 100 moves. Now 0 and 0. Block tops measured 0 before and after.
- **Column tops host.** A vase or a generated design can stand on a column, including an 80 cm pedestal or a column with a capital. It follows the column when it moves, rotates or changes height, survives undo, reload and duplicate, and keeps or leaves the column correctly in the plan view.
- **Generated designs on block tops behave like on any host.** They keep the block in 2D, and an L-shaped or notched block no longer accepts an object over empty space.
- **Block edits keep what stands on them.** Pushing or pulling a top carries the objects. A split keeps them in place. An edit that would remove or tilt the support under a generated design is refused before anything is written.

## How
- Column renderer mounts children; column becomes an eligible host and stays a floor-only child.
- The catalog coordinator gains one generic route for eligible hosts no specialised route owns. A rejected generic hit yields silently to the floor. Specialised refusals (sink cutout, occupied surface) keep ownership when the event bubbles to a generic ancestor. Cabinet modules leave their hits to the run, so countertop and bar placements commit byte-identical nodes to main, including nested corner runs and standalone modules.
- Shared frames apply slab lift once for any level-parented ancestor.
- 2D plan: main's resolver is kept verbatim for every chain main handled (480 differential cases against a fixture copy of main), and full-frame composition applies as soon as a column or generic host is in the chain, checked against the mounted 3D pose.
- Block face edits reuse the carry-or-refuse reconciliation extracted from the cabinet (behaviour-identical for cabinets). Catalog face children keep main's storage untouched. Face frames are cached per topology: editing an occupied 1,200-face block went from about 510 ms to under 2 ms.
- Childless blocks match main's writes, dirty calls and history steps. A refused numeric value keeps the operation open; releasing a drag after a refusal commits the last accepted preview with the display in sync.
- Duplicate takes the subtree for columns and blocks.

## Deliberately not changed
Floor collision around blocks stays main's bounding-box check. A polygon narrow phase was tried and reverted after review reproduced a rotated item passing through a block. A floor item still cannot stand inside the notch of an L-shaped block.

## Verification
- From each package: core 2842, nodes 3315 (one existing skip), editor 1061, viewer 351. Typechecks and Biome pass. The 717 frozen resolver cases and the 15 production plan pins are byte-identical.

title: fix(duplicate): carry what stands on a table, shelf or generated design
body:
## Problem
Duplicating an object that has other objects standing on it produced an empty copy: a table with a vase, a shelf with items, a generated design with things on it. The Duplicate action takes the whole subtree only for kinds that declare `duplicable.subtree` (cabinets, and since #895 columns and blocks). Every other kind goes through `prepareFreshPlacementRootDuplicate`, which sets `children = []`. That dates from April 2026. Presets were never affected because they clone through `cloneNodesInto`.

## Change
- `item`, `shelf` and `procedural-item` declare `duplicable: { subtree: 'with-children' }`. With hosted children they use the existing subtree path: fresh ids, links rewired, procedural `attachments` remapped, one draft, one undo step, same from the 2D menu. Without children they keep main's root-only path byte for byte (lifecycle fixtures captured from main's modules).
- A copied root that rests on a generated design's named surface keeps its external attachment from the first preview frame, added with the draft, removed on cancel, written with the commit.
- Every host-acquisition route rejects the draft itself and its descendants before reparenting, through one shared cycle predicate. Before this a copied shelf could become its own table's parent.
- History snapshots strip draft ids from procedural attachment maps, touching only maps that reference a draft.
- **Draft lifetime follows the move interaction, not a view.** A fresh subtree stays in the scene while the move is active, across pane teardown, direct 3D/2D replacement and Strict Mode replay; a mover that mounts later adopts it from the store.
- **Ownership is explicit.** Only factory-created subtrees adopted by the built-in movers (registry mover, item draft hook, 2D overlay) are registered, with gesture, creation and scene identity. Commit unregisters before finalising. The interaction-end cleanup deletes registered subtrees only and never reads metadata. Movers that keep `isNew` after a commit (fence, lean-to, the shipped pool plugin) are untouched.
- Side effect: main's ghost cabinet copy after an abandoned duplicate is gone.
- Escape differs from main only while a registered draft is active.

## Verification
- From each package: core 2843, nodes 3388 (one existing skip), editor 1061, viewer 351. Typechecks and Biome pass. Frozen resolver cases, plan pins and the 480-case 2D differential matrix untouched.
- A lifetime sweep: 43 built-in and 61 shipped-plugin duplicate/placement paths are committed through their real mover and must still exist after the scope ends.
- 72 ordinary-move traces (item, shelf, generated design, cabinet, column, plugin; both views; teardown, Escape, commit, unmount) equal main.
- Six independent review rounds. Round five reproduced data loss in an earlier design that inferred abandonment from `isNew` (duplicated fences, lean-tos and pool parts deleted after placement); that design was replaced by explicit registration, and round six found no path that deletes a committed node.
- Browser: table + Cactus, shelf + items, generated design + child, a root on a named surface, view switching during the gesture, Escape, tool switch, autosave and reload; fence, lean-to, pool stair and drain duplicates survive.

## Known and unchanged
Autosave can still persist an in-progress draft mid-gesture (logged in `plans/meta-todos.md`). Abandonment followed by autosave and reload leaves no copy for the registered kinds.

title: feat(editor): make wall drafting and attachments curve-aware
body:
## What does this PR do?

- **Curve-aware wall geometry and attachments**
  - Issue: Fixed curve sampling and straight-line remapping could make curved wall outlines, junctions, and hosted openings or items drift during topology changes.
  - Fixed: Wall geometry now uses exact arc-length and projection helpers with adaptive centerline sampling, while split and merge operations remap supported wall attachments along the resulting centerline.

- **Strict, migration-safe wall data**
  - Issue: Invalid dimensions, partial material migrations, and one-sided child ownership could leave saved walls in an inconsistent state.
  - Fixed: Wall dimensions and points are validated, legacy geometry and material fields are normalized on load, and bidirectional wall-child ownership accepts plugin-defined child kinds.

- **Exact wall drafting and shared drawing controls**
  - Issue: Wall lengths could only be set by pointer placement, and drawing tools implemented keyboard behavior independently.
  - Fixed: Wall drafts accept an exact typed length in 2D, 3D, and split views, and registered drawing tools share Enter, Backspace, and Escape behavior without duplicate commits.

- **Stable placement previews**
  - Issue: Ceiling elevation and door or opening previews could use stale geometry or write transient pointer state into the scene.
  - Fixed: Ceiling drafts resolve their level-aware height, while doors and opening affordances preview through live overrides and commit scene changes only once.

- **Plugin-owned editor extensions**
  - Issue: Core editor UI needed built-in knowledge of tool-specific overlays and drawing tools.
  - Fixed: Registered tools can provide drawing controls and overlays, and wall rendering accepts registered plugin children without adding plugin node kinds to core.

- **Provenance-safe PR descriptions**
  - Issue: Merge-imported or reverted work could be attributed to the feature branch when generating a PR description.
  - Fixed: OpenPR2 now audits first-parent commits, patch-equivalent commits, merge-only files, overlapping files, unexplained files, and reverted eligible files before writing PR metadata.

- **Editor integration maintenance**
  - Issue: Local package resolution and the environment plugin pin were out of sync with the current workspace.
  - Fixed: Turbopack aliases resolve from the monorepo root, the environment plugin pin is updated, and failed Next.js cache output is ignored.

## How to test

1. Draw walls in 2D, 3D, and split view; type a length and press Enter, then exercise Backspace and Escape.
   - The committed segment should keep the entered length, commit once, and preserve or cancel the active draft as indicated.

2. Create a curved wall with a hosted door, window, or wall item, then split or merge the wall.
   - The wall geometry should remain smooth and the supported attachment should remain mapped to the resulting wall centerline.

3. Place a ceiling and preview or resize a door/opening.
   - The ceiling should use the resolved level height, and preview movement should not mutate scene data until commit.

4. Run the focused provenance, wall, drawing, ceiling, door, opening, and slab tests:

   - All 76 tests should pass.

5. Run `bun run checks` and `bun run build`.

title: Send to Blender imports only default white cube — Pascal scene has 2 levels and hundreds of nodes
body: ### What happened? ## Description Hi, I'm currently blocked by what appears to be an issue with the Pascal → Blender workflow. I'm building an architectural house in Pascal using Pascal + Codex/Astra, with the goal of taking the completed architectural scene into Blender for high-quality/photorealistic rendering. The scene renders correctly inside Pascal and contains the complete house, including two levels, architecture, interior objects, exterior elements, etc. However, when I use **Send to Blender**, Blender does not receive the house. Pascal reports: `Send to Blender. Imported Pascal scene: 1 objects, 0 levels, lighting set up.` In Blender I only see the default white cube. There are no floors, walls, rooms, furniture, exterior objects, or other Pascal scene content. ## Expected behavior The complete Pascal scene should be transferred/imported into Blender, including the two levels and the authored architectural scene. ## Actual behavior Blender receives/imports: - 1 object - 0 levels The actual house is missing. ## Environment - macOS - Pascal CLI: 1.0.2 - Pascal web runtime: 1.0.2 - Node: 25.6.0 - Pascal editor health check: healthy - Pascal MCP: healthy - Pascal Blender extension installed - Local Pascal editor I originally had Pascal CLI 1.0.1, but updated to 1.0.2, restarted Pascal and Blender, and confirmed with `pascal doctor` that the CLI/runtime are current and healthy. The problem persists. ## Scene This is not an empty/test scene. It is a relatively large architectural project with two storeys and hundreds of authored nodes. Pascal scene ID: `0cf564b04807` The complete scene is visible and works inside the Pascal editor. ## Additional context My intended workflow is: `Pascal + AI agent → complete architectural environment → Blender → photorealistic rendering` So I would like to understand whether: 1. **Send to Blender** is expected to support a complete scene like this; 2. the current Send to Blender implementation expects GLB or Pascal scene JSON; 3. `1 objects, 0 levels` indicates that only an export/root object is being transmitted rather than the Pascal scene graph; 4. there is a recommended way to export/import the complete existing Pascal scene into Blender. ## Screenshots I can attach screenshots showing: 1. the complete house inside Pascal; 2. the Pascal `Send to Blender` result showing `1 objects, 0 levels`; 3. the resulting Blender scene containing only the white/default cube. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start the local Pascal editor. 2. Open the existing architectural scene. 3. Confirm that the complete two-storey house is visible in Pascal. 4. Start Blender with the Pascal extension installed. 5. Use **Send to Blender** from Pascal. 6. Pascal connects to Blender successfully. 7. The import completes, but reports: `1 objects, 0 levels` 8. Blender does not contain the Pascal house. ### Expected behavior The complete Pascal scene should be transferred/imported into Blender, including the two levels and the authored architectural scene. ### Browser & OS _No response_ ### Screenshots or screen recordings ### Additional context _No response_

title: Add "Mirror" option for stairs (Cut Back Stairs)

### Problem or motivation

Stairs can be rotated but not mirrored, so there's no way to get the opposite-handed version of a Cut Back staircase. I can't match my real floorplan, which has the turn going the other way.

### Proposed solution

A "Mirror" toggle in the stairs settings panel that flips the stair's handedness in place and keeps all other properties (dimensions, step count, riser height).

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

Left- and right-handed stair variants are common in real layouts, and mirroring is a natural companion to the existing rotation control.

## What does this PR do?

Completes the wall lifecycle — draw, split, merge — and fixes four `main` bugs found while testing it in the floor plan. Balconies and the plan workspace (calibrate / trace SVG plans) follow in separate PRs stacked on this one.

**Walls**
- **Rectangle walls:** `R` toggles line / rectangle inside the wall tool (HUD "Shape" chip cycles the same store). In 2D the rectangle drafts through the plan's own cursor, snapping, mitered footprints and measurement plates; in 3D it keeps the wall cursor and the line draft's look.
- **Split as a loop cut, driven by the HUD:** scrolling sets 1–32 cuts, one cut follows the pointer with the snapping modes (Shift cycles, Ctrl tap steps the grid, Alt frees), several divide the wall evenly, and a click commits them as one undo step (`planWallDivisions`). Openings re-host on their segment. The old floating panel is gone.
- **Merge adjoining walls:** select walls that continue each other → "Merge" next to Split (same component in 2D and 3D). `planWallMerge` keeps the wall with the most attachments and never turns it around; an absorbed wall read backwards mirrors its children's local frame (`side`, depth, yaw — hinges and swing hang off the yaw and stay as stored); every child is re-hosted at its world position, stale child ids are dropped, rooms follow; it refuses T/cross joints, walls out of line, different thickness / visible height / finish, or curved walls — the reason shows on hover.
- **Rectangle sides reuse existing walls:** a side drawn along an existing wall inserts only the uncovered remainder (`uncoveredWallSegments`); a side that T-joins or crosses a room wall keeps the room on the replacement walls.
- Openings keep their metadata when moved; transient previews never host walls; windows place through grid events on hidden walls.

**Behaviour changes on `main` that come with the shared planners** (worth knowing when reviewing):
- `planWallInsertion` — the line tool's planner too — now rewrites a room's `boundaryWallIds` when it splits one of that room's walls; before, the zone kept the removed wall's id.
- The delete heal's joining rule and attachment re-hosting (`resolveMergedWallEndpoints`, `buildMergedWallAttachmentUpdates`) moved from `node-actions.ts` into `systems/wall/wall-merge.ts`; at a start-to-start joint the heal no longer reverses the kept wall (which flipped its `frontSide` / `backSide` and hosted faces).

**Where it lives.** Split and merge are wall code, so they live in `packages/nodes/src/wall/` (`split-session.ts`, `split-store.ts`, `split-preview.ts`, `split-pointer.ts`, `split-tool.tsx`, `split-floorplan-layer.tsx`, `actions.tsx`). The editor only gains kind-agnostic seams, so the next kind-owned reshape needs no editor change:
- `ToolManager` mounts `def.affordanceTools[reshape]` for any `reshaping` scope without a dedicated arm (the split runs as `reshape: 'split'`, which also gives it the `polygon` snapping chip).
- `FloorplanRegisteredToolLayer` mounts the floorplan extension's `reshapeLayers[reshape]` while that scope runs.
- `HelperManager` renders `def.affordanceHints[reshape]` (the cut-count chip) like `toolHints`.
- `NodeActionMenu` renders the floorplan extension's `actionMenu.actions` for the selected kinds (Split / Merge come from the wall).
- Slab and ceiling declare `selectionCounterparts` on the same extension for the paired deselect below.

Known gap, left for a follow-up: the 3D rectangle draft has no alignment guides yet (the 2D one shares the line draft's).

**Fixes on `main` (each its own commit)**
- **WASD and orbit did nothing in 2D-only view** (the 3D canvas is paused there since #675, and a session opened straight into 2D never mounted the camera). The plan owns them in 2D-only view with the camera's key state, guards and speed (`lib/keyboard-pan.ts`) and publishes the pose to 3D when the move ends.
- **Drawing onto an existing wall in 2D selected it instead of placing the point:** registry entries now yield to the active tool in build mode, as 3D does; T-junctions draw in 2D.
- **Group selection box:** it measured world-space meshes (wrong under a rotated building, unbuilt in 2D-only view) and grew the selection to every connected wall. Group transforms now act on the selection (connected walls stretch at their shared ends), and the box is measured from plan data (`groupPlanBounds`); the 2D box, 3D rotate gizmo and keyboard R/T share its centre. This is a behaviour change: two walls of a room no longer move the whole room.
- **A room's slab and ceiling deselect together in the plan** (the ceiling is drawn as an unfilled outline a click can't reach; a marquee still picks it).

## How to test

1. `bun dev`, open a scene with a few rooms, switch to the **2D** view.
2. Wall tool: press `R` — the HUD shows *Shape: Rectangle*; click two opposite corners → four joined walls, mitered, with plates during the draft. Press `R` again → line mode; end a wall on the side of an existing wall → a T-junction, not a selection.
3. Select a wall → scissors (Split): scroll to change the cut count, `Shift` to cycle snapping, click to commit; undo once removes all cuts. Select the two halves → Merge (two arrows) → one wall again; hover a greyed Merge to read why.
   - Draw two walls toward each other (start-to-start), put a door on one, merge: the kept wall keeps its facing and the door keeps its hinge in the world. Draw a rectangle whose side runs along an existing wall and past its end: the overhang is added, not a doubled wall. Draw a rectangle whose side T-joins a room's wall: the room stays one zone.
4. In 2D-only view, hold WASD and use the orbit buttons: the plan moves / turns; switch to 3D — the camera is where the plan left it.
5. Marquee a room (walls + slab + ceiling): the dashed box hugs the room; Shift-click the slab → the ceiling leaves with it and the box hugs the walls. Rotate the building first to check the box stays on the walls.
6. `bun test` in `packages/{core,editor,nodes}` (all green), `bun check`.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Screen recording to be added by the author (2D rectangle draft, loop-cut split, merge).

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes wall topology, opening re-hosting, and zone boundary references; group-move behavior no longer drags entire connected wall components, which can surprise users but is localized to editor geometry.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **core wall planners** for rectangle drawing (`planWallRectangle` + `uncoveredWallSegments` to reuse collinear walls), explicit **split/division** (`planWallDivision` / `planWallDivisions`), and **merge** (`planWallMerge` in `wall-merge.ts`, shared with delete-heal). Merge/split paths re-host openings (including frame mirroring when a wall is read backwards), update zone `boundaryWallIds`, and validate collinearity, joints, and style.
> 
> **Editor integration:** registry seams for kind-owned reshapes (`reshapeLayers`, `affordanceHints`, `actionMenu.actions`), floorplan **rectangle wall** draft preview, and build-mode clicks that **yield to tools** instead of selecting walls underneath. **Group transforms** no longer auto-expand to every connected wall; the dashed box / gizmo pivot uses **level-frame plan bounds** (`groupPlanBounds` / `computeGroupPlanBox`). **2D-only view** drives WASD/orbit via shared `keyboard-pan` while the 3D camera is paused; slab/ceiling **deselect together** in the plan via `selectionCounterparts`.

title: fix(core): fill slab/ceiling hole fields on scene load
body:
## What

Fill `holes`, `holeMetadata` and (for slabs) `autoFromWalls` on slab and ceiling nodes when a scene is loaded, the same way doors and windows are already normalized in `setScene`.

## Why

The schema declares defaults for these fields, so a third-party writer (a scanning app, an IFC hand-off) can legitimately omit them. But the slab opening sync and the public viewer read them on the raw node. A scene whose slab has no `holes` therefore throws:

```
[viewer] ErrorBoundary caught (viewer-scene): TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
```

and the public viewer stays black, while the editor (which fills defaults on load) opens the same file fine.

Repro with a real export from A3 Atlas Scanner (69/69 nodes pass `AnyNode.safeParse`):

- drag `pascal.json` into a new project → editor renders it; open the project's public viewer → black screen, error above;
- same graph with `holes: []` added on the slab → viewer renders: https://editor.pascal.app/viewer/project_ej9qncUcEV7RX4lo

## How

`normalizeSurfaceHoleFields` in `use-scene.ts`, applied to `slab` and `ceiling` in the load migration. Only the three hole fields are touched: a full zod parse would also default `thickness`, which the vertical-model migration still needs to see as absent on legacy solids (three existing tests cover that).

## Tests

- New `use-scene-surface-holes-defaults.test.ts`: a slab and a ceiling written without holes load with empty arrays; existing holes and metadata are kept as written. Fails on `main`, passes with this change.
- `bun run test` in `packages/core`: 2125 pass; the one failure and one module-resolution error are pre-existing on `main`.
- `bun check`: clean.

Context: this is the scanning-app hand-off discussed in #720 / #737.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow load-time normalization for slab/ceiling hole fields only; behavior matches schema defaults and is covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Scene load now **backfills missing hole-related fields** on `slab` and `ceiling` nodes so third-party exports that omit `holes` / `holeMetadata` (and `autoFromWalls` on slabs) no longer crash the public viewer with `undefined.map`.
> 
> `migrateNodes` in `use-scene.ts` calls new **`normalizeSurfaceHoleFields`**, which sets empty arrays and `autoFromWalls: false` when absent. It deliberately avoids a full Zod parse so legacy **`thickness`** stays undefined for the vertical-model migration.
> 
> New tests in **`use-scene-surface-holes-defaults.test.ts`** assert defaults on bare slabs/ceilings and that existing holes/metadata are unchanged.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3f9e9666cb1c57bc48ee0185d88dfdb3678d99d6. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(editor): make the settings panel readable and scrollable in dialogs
body:
## Summary
- The settings panel root is an `overflow-auto` + `overscroll-contain` scroll container sized for the sidebar. Hosted in the community settings dialog it was never height-bound, so it never scrolled itself yet still stopped the browser from chaining the wheel to the dialog. Options below the fold were unreachable without zooming the browser out.
- `SettingsPanel` now accepts a `className` so a host can lay it out as the sole scroller.
- Restructured into titled sections (`h3` + description, `aria-labelledby`), switch rows with labels wired to their switches, and two-column button grids via `@container` queries that collapse to one column in the 18rem sidebar and on phones.
- Shadows moved out of the cloud-only Visibility block into its own Viewer section (it is a rendering setting, now shown for every project).
- Sentence-case labels; scene graph trigger is now a button like its neighbours.

## Test plan
- [x] Reproduced with a real wheel event via Playwright at 1440x900 (scroll stayed at 0); after the host change in private-editor the panel scrolls to the bottom
- [x] Phone width collapses to one column and scrolls
- [x] `tsgo --noEmit` clean for `packages/editor`
- [ ] private-editor follow-up: flex-column dialog host + submodule bump

> **Overview**

title: walls: add configurable curtain wall systems
body:
## What does this PR do?

- Adds curtain walls as a configurable wall type with stick and unitized construction, capped and structural-glazing frame styles, adjustable grids, spandrels, per-panel glass/solid/empty overrides, glass appearance controls, and frame materials driven by the paint tool.
- Supports straight and curved curtain walls, transparent shadow geometry, floor-plan rendering, and rectangular, rounded, and arched door/window openings with adaptive perimeter frames.
- Keeps slider and handle edits on live mesh overrides until commit, constrains openings to their host, preserves undo/redo as one history step, and optimizes dense grids and resize-time geometry work.
- Keeps curtain-specific rendering in the built-in wall node while exposing generic viewer geometry and material adapters, with schema compatibility and curtain-wall documentation.
- Adds contextual help for selected doors and windows: holding Shift enables one-sided corner-radius adjustment, and the floating shortcut panel shows the Shift hint.

## How to test

1. Run `bun run checks` and `bun run build`; both should complete successfully.
2. Run `bun run dev`, open `http://localhost:3002`, create several walls, and switch their wall type to **Curtain wall**.
3. Exercise stick/unitized construction, every framing style, count/maximum-spacing/fixed-spacing grids, grid alignment, spandrels, panel overrides, glass tint, opacity, and roughness; the mesh should update smoothly and undo/redo should restore each committed edit.
4. Use the paint tool on curtain frames and verify the selected scene or library material appears on the frame without changing the glass.
5. Add doors and windows with rectangular, rounded, and arched openings, resize and move them, then test the same combinations on curved walls; the perimeter frame and glass cutout should follow the opening without seams or stale geometry.
6. Select a single door or window and verify the floating shortcut panel shows the Shift hint; hold Shift and adjust one side’s corner radius.
7. Test full-height and cutaway wall modes and orbit the camera; transparent panes should transmit light while mullions, spandrels, and solid panels cast shadows.

## Screenshots / screen recording

![Curtain wall variations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sudhir9297/editor/feat/curtain-walls/docs/images/curtain-wall-variations.png)

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)

- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large surface area across wall rendering, opening placement, and editor handle/drag behavior; regressions could affect standard walls, undo, or door/window sizing on non-curtain hosts if constraints leak.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **curtain walls** as a first-class wall type: schema (`wallType: 'curtain'`, `CurtainWallConfig`), panel UI, stick/unitized layout, materials/paint roles, 3D geometry (including curved walls and dense grids), floorplan shapes, and a viewer **wall geometry adapter** for openings, shadows, and live previews.
> 
> **Doors and windows** on curtain hosts get perimeter-aware sizing/placement (`constrainCurtainOpening`, arc-length wall math), shaped opening frames in the curtain mesh, and a shared **property preview** path so sliders/handles update live overrides and commit as a single undo step. **`SliderControl`** gains cancel/escape, optional preview-while-typing, and pointer-loss cleanup.
> 
> The editor adds a **`corner-radius` handle** type (Shift for per-corner radii on openings), wired into door/window definitions plus contextual **Shift** help. Minor tooling: ignore `.next-*`, Biome exclude, `lints` script. Door panel drops the documentation section and uses preview-based dimension sliders.

title: fix(nodes): wall split and rectangle feedback from the first QA round
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #902 with the fixes from its first QA round, which landed a minute after the squash merge.

- **One wheel notch is one cut.** The split's cut count stepped every 60 px of wheel travel, and a notched wheel on macOS (e.g. an MX Master in ratchet mode) reports only a few pixels per notch, so it took three or four notches to change the count. A wheel event that follows an 80 ms pause now steps at once, and line-mode events always do. A continuous trackpad stream still steps by travel (`packages/nodes/src/wall/split-pointer.ts`).
- **Split and merge make a sound.** Committing a split, and a merge, plays the wall-placement sound (`sfx:structure-build`).
- **The rectangle draft ticks like the line draft.** Moving the second corner plays `sfx:grid-snap` once per snapped position, and the first corner plays the line tool's start sound, in 3D and in 2D.
- **The wall tool keeps its last shape.** Leaving the wall tool used to reset Shape to Line; re-arming it after drawing rectangles now resumes Rectangle (for the session).

## How to test

1. `bun dev`, select a wall, click Split (scissors). Scroll with a notched mouse wheel: each notch changes the cut count by one. A trackpad swipe still changes it smoothly by distance.
2. Click to commit the split: the wall-placement sound plays. Select the two halves and Merge: same sound.
3. Wall tool, press `R` (Shape: Rectangle), click the first corner (start sound), then move the mouse: a tick at each new snapped point, as in line mode. Check in 3D and in the 2D plan.
4. With Shape: Rectangle, switch to select mode, then pick the wall tool again: it comes back in Rectangle.
5. `bun test` in `packages/nodes` (new tests cover notched-wheel and trackpad stepping), `bun check`.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Mostly feel and sound; a short recording of the notched wheel and the rectangle ticks will be added by the author if useful.

title: editor: stop a hidden Site from emptying exports and the 2D plan
body:
## What does this PR do?

A layout whose root Site is saved with `visible: false` came out empty from every export while the editor showed the full house. Three code paths walked the `parentId` chain and treated the Site like any other container, so its flag hid every building, level and node beneath it:

- `pruneHiddenSceneNodes` in `glb-export.ts`, which feeds GLB, USDZ, STL, OBJ, the print formats and the production bake. A 275-node house exported as a 184-byte GLB holding one empty node.
- `isVisibleInFloorplan` in the shared viewer's `FloorplanPreview`, which left the public viewer's 2D tab blank for the same layout (0 of 198 level nodes passed against the real file).
- `isFloorplanHierarchyVisible`, which gated site-scoped plugin kinds on the Site's flag in the PDF export and the live 2D view.

The viewer never applies that flag: the Site renderer ignores `visible`, and the Site row in the sidebar has no eye toggle, so the state only arrives through the CLI, MCP or a hand-authored layout.

One rule now lives in core, `hidesDescendants(node)`, false only for a Site: hiding a Site hides its own ground fill and boundary and nothing beneath it. The exporter, the plan preview and the 2D hierarchy gate all read it. The `declaredSiteParents` map, which existed solely to cascade Site visibility onto detached Environment children, is gone.

Because nothing told the author the flag was presentation-only, `validate_scene` now returns a `warnings` list (same `{ nodeId, path, message }` shape as `errors`) and flags a hidden Site with that note, and Load Build (`validateBuildJson`) emits a `site_hidden` warning. `wiki/architecture/node-schemas.md` documents the rule.

Hosts that implement `SceneBridge.validateScene` (the hosted MCP bridge in private-editor) need to return `warnings` too; that lands with the submodule bump.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/editor && bun test src/lib/glb-export.test.ts src/components/viewer/floorplan-preview-visibility.test.ts src/components/editor-2d/renderers/floorplan-registry-layer.test.ts src/lib/floorplan/floorplan-export.test.ts` — the new tests cover a hidden Site over a visible building/level/item for the exporter, the plan preview and the 2D gate, plus hidden buildings, levels and leaves still hiding.
2. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/tools/validate-scene.test.ts` — a hidden Site yields `valid: true` with one warning; `cd packages/core && bun test src/validation/validate-build-json.test.ts` — Load Build warns with `site_hidden`.
3. Full suites: core 2866, editor 1104, mcp 381 passing; `bun run build` in core and mcp; `tsgo --noEmit` in editor.
4. Load a project whose root Site has `visible: false` (through MCP `update_node` or the layout JSON), leave "Export visible nodes only" on, and click **Export GLB**: the file contains the building. Open the shared viewer's 2D tab: the plan draws. Run `validate_scene`: one warning names the Site.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — non-visual change in the export, plan-collection and validation paths.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

Not ticked: the in-app export and 2D tab were not exercised in a browser from this checkout; coverage is the unit suites above.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes visibility semantics across GLB/USDZ and floorplan export paths; behavior is centralized and heavily unit-tested but affects all visible-only exports.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Hiding a root Site with `visible: false` no longer cascades to buildings and levels.** Core now exports `hidesDescendants` (false only for `site`) and `HIDDEN_SITE_NOTE`, so a hidden Site affects only its own ground/boundary while children keep their own visibility flags.
> 
> **GLB export**, the shared viewer **floorplan preview**, and **live 2D / PDF floorplan** hierarchy checks all use that rule instead of walking `parentId` and treating Site like any other container. Export pruning drops non–scene-node children under a hidden Site (parcel geometry) but keeps hosted building content; the old `declaredSiteParents` Site-visibility map is removed.
> 
> **Validation surfaces the behavior:** Load Build emits a `site_hidden` warning, and MCP `validate_scene` adds a non-failing `warnings` array (same shape as errors) for hidden Sites. Wiki node-schema docs describe the Site exception.
>

title: viewer: honour node.visible on buildings, levels, zones and ceilings
body:
## What does this PR do?

The sidebar's Hide/Show eye on a building or level was honoured by selection, first-person collision, the 2D plan and every export, but not by the 3D viewport: `BuildingRenderer` and `LevelRenderer` rendered a bare `<group>`, and the level system overwrote `obj.visible` every frame from solo-mode state. Hide a building and it kept drawing but could no longer be clicked; hide a level and walkthrough fell through its floor. Zones and ceilings had the same gap (their `floorplan.ts` honour the flag, their renderers did not), and two zone systems forced the zone group visible every frame.

Now:

- Building, level, zone and ceiling renderers apply `visible={node.visible !== false}` on their root, the same way `parametric-node-renderer.tsx` does for parametric kinds.
- `resolveLevelVisibility` (new, in `level-utils.ts`) combines the author's flag with solo mode: solo behaviour is unchanged for visible levels, and a hidden level never enters the shadow-caster-only branch, so it stops shadowing the floor below. `snapLevelsToTruePositions` no longer forces hidden levels visible during capture, matching the export, which prunes them.
- `ZoneSystem` and `ViewerZoneSystem` drive the zone group and its `<Html>` label from the node flag instead of forcing the group visible.
- `SiteRenderer` hides its own ground fill, sculpted terrain and lot line when the Site is hidden, while everything standing on the site keeps its own flag and the horizon disc stays. This is the rule #907 gives the exporter and the 2D plan: the Site is the parcel reference, not a container.
- `wiki/architecture/renderers.md` states the rule for custom renderers.

Independent of #907 (no shared files); together they make `visible` mean the same thing in the viewport, the 2D plan, selection, collision and exports.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/viewer && bun test src/systems/level` — `resolveLevelVisibility` cases plus three `LevelSystem` cases: a hidden level outside solo, a hidden level excluded from the shadow-caster branch, a hidden level staying hidden through `snapLevelsToTruePositions`.
2. Full suites: `packages/nodes` 3422 pass, `packages/viewer` 362 pass, `packages/editor` 1099 pass. `tsc --build` clean in viewer and nodes, `tsgo --noEmit` clean in editor, Biome clean.
3. In the app: hide a building from the sidebar eye — it disappears from the viewport and comes back on Show. Hide a level in solo mode — it neither draws nor casts shadows. Hide a zone — its fill and label go. Set a Site to `visible: false` through MCP — the parcel fill and lot line disappear, the house stays.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — the change is what the sidebar eye already promised; no new UI.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)

title: ci: release every @pascal-app package at the same version
body:
## What does this PR do?

Every `@pascal-app` package now carries the same version. `release.yml` used to bump each package from its own version, one package or all at a time, which is how `cli` reached 1.0.2 while the other six stayed at 1.0.1. Now:

- The `package` input is gone. Every run releases all seven packages in dependency order.
- One version is computed from the highest version currently in the tree plus the bump, and applied to every package and every internal `@pascal-app/*` range. From today's tree, `patch` produces 1.0.3 across the board.
- `none` republishes the current version: packages already on npm at it are skipped (existing recovery logic), and only tags that do not exist yet are created and pushed, so a drifted or partial release can be recovered in place.
- The single-package "missing published dependency" check is removed as dead code; `cli-smoke` and the portable-runtime validation always run.
- Root `package.json` keeps `release`, `release:beta`, `release:minor`, `release:major` without the package flag; the per-package scripts are removed.

## How to test

1. YAML parses and both extracted scripts pass `bash -n`.
2. The bump logic was run locally against copies of the seven manifests: `patch` → 1.0.3 for all, `none` → 1.0.2 for all, `beta` → 2.0.0-beta.1 for all; `@pascal-app/editor` peers rewrite to the shared version and the external `@pascal-app/lingo` range is untouched.
3. After merge, `gh workflow run release.yml -f bump=patch -f dry-run=true` should report every package at 1.0.3 without publishing.
