title: Stop the draft attachment snapshot test leaning on a leaked rAF
body:
`draft-attachment-snapshot.test.ts` fails with a bare `ReferenceError: requestAnimationFrame is not defined` depending on the order bun happens to run the core test files in. It surfaced on a private-editor CI run, on a diff that touched nothing in the editor.

## Cause

`updateNode` batches its dirty-node flush through `requestAnimationFrame` (`store/actions/node-actions.ts:1465`), which bun's test runtime has no DOM to supply. Seven other core tests that reach this path stub the global themselves — `use-scene-dirty-tracking`, `node-update-children`, `wall-merge`, `host-children`, `procedural-persistence`, `procedural-items/mutations`, `use-scene-temporal-reconciliation`. This one never did, so it passed only when one of those ran first and leaked `globalThis.requestAnimationFrame` behind it. Run the file on its own and it fails every time, on `main` as much as anywhere:

```
bun test src/store/draft-attachment-snapshot.test.ts
ReferenceError: requestAnimationFrame is not defined
  at updateNodesActionImpl (src/store/actions/node-actions.ts:1465:18)
```

## Fix

Stub rAF for the duration of the test and restore it in the `finally` that's already there, matching the idiom in the neighbouring store tests.

## Testing

- `bun test src/store/draft-attachment-snapshot.test.ts` on its own: passes (failed before).
- `bun test src` in `packages/core`: 2865 pass, 0 fail.
- Audited every core test that calls `updateNode`/`updateNodes` without stubbing rAF — `registry/scene-api.test.ts` is the only other one, and it passes standalone because it doesn't reach the batched path. No further latent cases.

title: test: pin plugin API v1
body:
## What does this PR do?

Plan item **A-09** pins plugin API v1 with synthetic public plugins. It adds tests only: no source change, `apiVersion` stays `1`, and every capability stays optional. Each surface is tested once, at the level that owns it:

- **`packages/core/src/registry/plugin-v1-conformance.test.ts`** (12 tests, registry and scene store):
  - capability defaults for a minimal kind
  - plugin ports in the system graph and port connectivity
  - surfaces and `relations` cascades
  - create, update and delete with undo
  - save, validate and reload into a fresh registry
  - a scene loaded before its plugin registers
  - duplicate and project clone
  - no-install store semantics
- **`packages/viewer/src/components/viewer/plugin-dispatch.test.tsx`** (3 tests, dispatch):
  - `NodeRenderer`, `GeometrySystem` and `RegisteredSystems` render, build and run a plugin kind only once it is installed
  - a plugin that registers after mount still gets its system
  - the baked viewer restores `strip` nodes and mounts `bakeReplaceRenderer`, only while the plugin is installed
- **`packages/editor/src/lib/glb-export.test.ts`** (3 tests, real export path), sync and async:
  - `strip` drops the node
  - `replace` bakes the hook's snapshot, calling the hook once
  - `static` keeps the live clone and leaves the live tree untouched
  - an uninstalled plugin contributes nothing to the export

**Why:** the building-fidelity charter makes "existing plugins keep loading, working and publishing" a non-negotiable (R1). These tests turn it into a regression gate.

**Failing case (known v1 gap, not fixed here):** two `test.failing` cases cover project clone (`cloneSceneGraph`) and subtree duplicate (`cloneNodesInto`). Both copy plugin-owned node references (e.g. `shot.cameraIds`) verbatim, so the copies keep pointing at the source scene. v1 has no way for a plugin to declare which of its fields are node references. P-03 owns that hook. The wiki documents the gap for plugin authors.

The two bugs these tests found were split into their own PRs: #921 (atomic `loadPlugin`) and #922 (floor-plan PDF install gate).

**After review (`18b4b4853`):**
- **Typed fixtures.** Definitions are `NodeDefinition<typeof Schema>` values, so a contract change fails typecheck. The only remaining casts are documented helpers at two boundaries API v1 cannot type:
  - a typed `NodeDefinition<S>` does not widen to `AnyNodeDefinition`;
  - plugin nodes are outside the closed `AnyNode` union.

  Every shipped plugin casts at the first boundary too (`as unknown as AnyNodeDefinition`). That is a finding for the v1 contract, not changed here.
- **Undo of a creation.** The editing test creates a plugin node, then:
  - undo removes it and its id from `level.children`;
  - redo restores both;
  - update and delete each undo in one step.
- **New known gap, `test.failing`:** plugin nodes mounted before their plugin registers never render. `NodeRenderer` reads the registry at render time but doesn't subscribe to it, so a scene mounted before async plugin discovery keeps those kinds invisible and their geometry unbuilt. The fix ships separately, with a preview.

Test lines grew to about 858 from typing the fixtures.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/registry/plugin-v1-conformance.test.ts packages/viewer/src/components/viewer/plugin-dispatch.test.tsx packages/editor/src/lib/glb-export.test.ts` → all pass. The 2 clone `test.failing` cases fail as expected.
2. Mutation check: breaking each of these made at least one test fail:
   - renderer dispatch, geometry dispatch or the geometry build
   - system mounting, or the late-registration dependency
   - strip restore or the replace mount
   - each install gate
   - export strip exclusion, the export install gate, or the sync bake hook
3. Full package suites, local: core 2878 pass, viewer 368 pass, editor 1108 pass, 0 fail. `bun run check` is clean. The new test files typecheck.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A: tests and docs only.

## R1–R9

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | API v1, optional capabilities and portable bake hooks are pinned at registry, dispatch and export level. The clone-hook gap is recorded as `test.failing` (P-03) |
| R6 | Strip/replace pinned through export and the baked viewer's restore. Live tree untouched |
| R2 | Unaffected (tests only). Pins one undo step per create/update/delete and no build work while uninstalled |
| R3 | Unaffected. The clone cases record that plugin reference fields have no typed namespace |
| R4 | Unaffected (no zone or space detection change) |
| R5 | Unaffected (no edit tools). Pins surface hosting and port connectivity reads for plugin kinds |
| R7 | Unaffected (no definitions or recipes) |
| R8 | Unaffected (no tools, MCP or kernel) |
| R9 | Unaffected (no capture or import) |

title: fix(core): make loadPlugin atomic
body:
## What does this PR do?

`loadPlugin` now validates every definition in a plugin before it registers any of them. Previously it registered them one at a time, so a plugin could throw halfway through and leave its earlier kinds live. That half-loaded plugin's kinds would then render, save and publish even though the plugin never loaded.

The existing checks are pulled out into two helpers, `assertValidDefinition` and `duplicateKindError`, and `loadPlugin` runs them over the whole plugin first. Error messages are unchanged, dev HMR re-registration still replaces in place, and no API changes.

**Failing case, committed first as `test.failing` in `c90d50bf3`.** In production mode, load a plugin with `[unique, invalid]`. Every variant threw but left `partial:a` registered (`Expected: false, Received: true`). The invalid definition was:
- a kind that collides with one already loaded
- a repeat of one of the plugin's own kinds
- an invalid `schemaVersion`

**Fix, in `f29713d41`.** Nothing from the rejected plugin is left behind: no kinds, no plugin ids, no inspector extensions.

Found by the plugin API v1 conformance work (plan item A-09).

**Second round, after review.** Two failures could still happen after preflight had passed:
- A malformed `inspectorExtensions[].kinds` rejected after the plugin's kinds had registered.
- Per-kind notification ran listeners mid-load, so a throwing `onRegistryChange` listener rejected after the first kind registered but before its plugin id was set.

Both are recorded as `test.failing` in `89a81e727` (`Expected: false, Received: true` and `Received: undefined`). `1c3445d0a` changes `loadPlugin` to:
1. validate every definition and extension;
2. commit the kinds, plugin ids and extensions;
3. notify once.

A listener now only ever sees the whole plugin. Behaviour change: `loadPlugin` bumps the registry version once per plugin instead of once per kind. `registerNode` still notifies per call. The only consumers re-derive on any bump.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/registry` → 81 pass, 0 fail. Full suites: core 2871, viewer 365, editor 1105, nodes and the rest all pass
2. Revert `registry.ts` → the 3 new cases fail

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A: registry behaviour, no UI.

## R1–R9

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | API v1 unchanged. A plugin now loads completely or not at all |

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)

title: perf(viewer): expose history and selection on the ?perf probe

## What does this PR do?

This adds two read-only methods to the `?perf` scripted probe, `window.__pascalPerf`. The probe is mounted only when `?perf` is in the URL.

- **`history()`** returns `{ past, future, tracking, pauseDepth }`: undo and redo entry counts, whether scene history is recording, and the number of refcounted pause owners (`pauseSceneHistory` and leases). A direct `temporal.pause()` shows as `tracking: false` with `pauseDepth: 0`. That is the signature of the unbalanced item-move pause that building-fidelity A-12 fixes.
- **`selection()`** returns `{ buildingId, levelId, zoneId, selectedIds }`.

**Why:** the private gesture receipts measure undo entries per gesture and whether history stays paused while an item is carried. Today they can only read those through dev-only store handles, so they cannot run against `next start`. This hook lets them. The logic is in `lib/perf-probe-state.ts`, with unit tests.

Nothing changes for the house: this is measurement only.

title: fix(viewer): render plugin nodes whose kind registers after mount
body:
Render plugin nodes when their kind registers after the node mounts. Each node subscribes to its own kind's registry entry, so unrelated kind registrations do not redraw existing nodes.

title: fix(editor): item move and placement record one undo step; the carry pauses no history (A-12)
body:
Keep item placement and movement to one undo step while allowing separate edits made during a carry to remain independently undoable.

Core tracks carried drafts and gesture ownership. New drafts stay out of history snapshots; adopted drafts preserve committed values without hiding another writer's changes. Placement and draft lifecycle writes use these shared boundaries.

This is the base of the #926 → #927 → #933 stack. Use the complete stack before updating consuming applications; #933 completes the 2D and split-view handling.

Validation covers placement, movement, cancellation, concurrent edits, surface attachments and rejected-drop retries through core and mounted interaction tests. Other tools that pause history for their entire gesture remain outside scope.

title: fix(wall): make a 3D wall move one history step and detect rooms at commit (A-11)
body:
Make a wall move one undo step containing its linked walls, supports and derived room surfaces. Drag previews use live overrides; separate scene edits remain independently undoable and trigger room reconciliation.

The 3D surface follower binds existing automatic slabs and ceilings to their boundary walls without running room detection on each drag tick. It refreshes after scene changes. New, merged and split rooms are reconciled at drop.

Use with #926 and #933 as one stack. Validation covers linked corners, curved walls, bridge previews, foreign edits, cancellation and both split-view drop directions. Bridged auto-zone preview remains limited; unrelated tools are outside scope.

body:
## What does this PR do?

This fixes the `quality` failure that #923 introduced on `main` at `a9c1d4561`. The failure also reproduced on a rerun.

**Cause:** `reference-inventory.test.ts` walks every editor source file to find the metadata keys it uses. At the same time, `history.test.ts` creates and deletes `.turbo/history-*/probe.ts`. When a file the walk has already listed is deleted before it is stat'ed or read, the walk throws `ENOENT`.

title: feat(procedural-items): curved shapes, choreographed mechanisms, part lights; shared item controls and light pool
body:
## Summary

Procedural items get curved shapes, moving parts, lights and pro-grade choreography, and catalog GLB items (Ceiling Lamp, Ceiling fan) share the same controls and light pool.

**Recipe vocabulary (core)**
- `ellipsoid` primitive, cylinder `topScale` taper (cones, lampshades), `sin`/`cos` expressions for radial layouts.
- `part.motion`: `hinge` / `slide` (with `delay`, `duration`, `easing`) and `spin`. Pivots/amounts may use `index`; motion envelopes are validated against floor / wall / ceiling references; moving parts can't host.
- `part.light`: one point light per evaluated part instance (≤ 12 per item), optional `emissiveSlot`.
- `ProceduralMotionController`: one clock for open-all / close-all (reverse sequence), individual parts skip unrelated padding, mid-transition reversal, spin ramp with phase kept.
- No operating state is persisted: doors start shut, fans stopped in the editor, lamps follow the scene theme (on for twilight/night).

**Runtime (nodes / viewer / editor)**
- Renderer splits batches per motion group × slot and drives groups from the controller; emissive bulbs are per-instance clones, Paint owns surface, the light owns emission.
- Shared 12-slot item light pool now takes `LightSource` adapters (catalog + procedural), keeps all 12 PointLights visible (intensity 0 when idle — avoids WebGPU lighting-program rebuilds), yields to the baked pool, skips fresh placement drafts.
- Selection action bar: Play/Stop and light on/off buttons for catalog and procedural items (replaces the floating HTML controls in the editor; preview mode keeps them). E, both walkthrough reticles and the buttons share one code path.
- GLB export: per-part sampled clips padded to the item timeline, `proceduralMotion` extras with actual clip bindings and `activeWindow`, `slotId` preserved, emission exported ON, no punctual lights.
- Baked viewer: procedural clips time-driven on their own mixer, fans spin on load, E/click per part, procedural + multi-light catalog items in `GlbInteractive`, moving parts excluded from walkthrough colliders.

title: feat(viewer): forward scene render errors to the host with onRenderError
body:
<!-- A-07 editor companion: Viewer onRenderError -->
## What and why
`Viewer` takes `onRenderError`. The host hears about two kinds of failure:
- **Render errors:** a node renderer or system that throws while rendering, caught by the viewer-scene boundary (`SceneErrorBoundary`). In immersive sessions the host handler is composed with the session's own `onError`.
- **Frame errors (review round 1):** a registered system that throws inside `useFrame`, which runs outside React's error boundaries. `FrameLimiter` catches it around R3F's `advance`, reports the first failure through `onFrameError`, and keeps the loop running.

`composeRenderErrorHandlers` keeps notifying the other handlers when one throws (round 1).

The private bake page (pascalorg/private-editor A-07 9/10, #757) needs this to report `plugin_unavailable` instead of exporting a GLB without the plugin's nodes. Nothing changes for hosts that do not pass the prop.

## Failing cases first
- `29ffa6377`: **2 of 2 fail**.
- `8180b026c` (round 1): **3 of 3 fail**. The tests now render the boundary and the real `FrameLimiter` with a system that throws in a frame; the round-0 source-string check is gone.

## Round 1
| Finding | Answer |
|---|---|
| Frame errors not covered | Fixed in `FrameLimiter`, with a render test. |
| Source-string wiring test | Replaced by render tests. The full `Viewer` needs a WebGPU canvas that the test renderer cannot create, so the tests render the two pieces `Viewer` composes. |
| Fan-out stops on a throwing handler | Fixed. |

## Round 2
| Finding | Answer |
|---|---|
| Tests never mount `<Viewer onRenderError>` | `viewer-render-error.test.ts` now runs `__tests__/viewer-render-error.fixture.tsx` in its own process. The fixture mounts the real `Viewer`, with R3F's DOM `<Canvas>` swapped for its children through a module mock, so the test renderer's R3F root hosts the scene without a GPU. A node that throws while rendering and a system that throws in a frame each reach `onRenderError`. Checked by mutation: emptying `renderErrorHandlers={[onRenderError]}` fails the render test, and dropping `onFrameError={composeRenderErrorHandlers(onRenderError)}` fails the frame test. These tests cover wiring that already exists, so they have no failing-first commit; the mutation check stands in for it. |
| Globals not restored | `render-error.test.tsx` restores `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener`, and a following test checks it. The fixture saves and restores every global it stubs. Failing first: `950cd48c8` (1 of 4 fails). |
| XR/immersive frame errors | **Follow-up, not in this PR.** The immersive branch mounts no `FrameLimiter`: the XR session drives frames itself, so a system that throws inside `useFrame` during an immersive session reaches neither `immersive.onError` nor `onRenderError`. The bake page never runs immersive; the follow-up has to catch frame errors in the XR loop. |

## Proof
- `bun test` in `packages/viewer/src`: 390 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run check`: clean.
- `bun run build` in `packages/viewer`: exit 0.
- `bun run check-types`: the only errors are 6 in `apps/editor`, which cannot resolve `@webxr/plugin` in this worktree's `node_modules`. They are unrelated.

**House effect:** no change; there is no rendering change.

R1: a plugin failure in `/bake` reaches the host through the real `Viewer` wiring, now proven by a mounted test. R2–R9: unaffected. This only adds a callback.

> **Overview**
> Adds **`onRenderError`** on `Viewer` so hosts (e.g. headless bake) can react when scene rendering fails instead of continuing silently.

title: fix(mcp): refuse apply_patch creates of existing ids and id/type updates (NH-02a)
body:
<!-- NH-02a PR body -->
## What

`apply_patch` now runs identity and validation guards before any bridge applies a patch. They live in the shared tool layer (`tools/patch-guards.ts`, called by `tools/apply-patch.ts`), so the hosted bridge inherits them on the next SHA bump. The guards dry-run the patch against a working copy of the scene and refuse, failing the whole patch:

| Code | Refused |
|---|---|
| `node_exists` | a create whose id is already present. To replace a node, delete it earlier in the same patch. Creates are parsed like the store parses them, so default `children` lists exist for later ops. |
| `identity_change` | an update that changes `id` or `type`. Restating the current value passes. |
| `immutable_field` | an update that changes `object` or `children`. Restating the current value passes. |
| `invalid_parent` | an update whose `parentId` names a missing node, a node that holds no children, or `null`, or that the registered relations reject (`validateNodeRelations`, now exported from core) |
| `invalid_update` | an update whose merged node gains schema issues. Validated with the registered definition's schema or the core per-kind schema. Only kinds with neither (unregistered plugins) skip validation, so a core door with `leafCount: 5` is refused. |
| `regenerated_default` | an op, later in the same patch, on a default gutter or downspout that a delete regenerates, and any update of the roof segment holding them. Its `children` aren't known until the commit, so a restated pre-delete list would bring back obsolete ids. |
| not found | any op on a node an earlier delete in the patch removed |

Refusals are tool errors whose text is JSON `{ code, patchIndex, id, message }`; the SDK drops `McpError` data, so this is how clients get the fields.

Deletes in the dry run go through core's new `planNodeDeletion`, the delete action's own planner, extracted as a pure function. The guard makes one call per run of consecutive deletes, just as the bridge sends one `deleteNodes` call per run. Kind cascades and walls merged across a deleted junction are therefore seen exactly as the store will commit them.

The guard calls it with `{ mintDefaults: false }`. The default gutter refresh mints gutters, downspouts and outlets with random ids, and which existing default downspouts survive depends on those ids: equal-length gutters on a hip roof tie-break by id. So a preview skips the refresh and lists the existing defaults it would touch in `unsettledIds` and their roof segments in `regeneratedHostIds`. The preview is then deterministic and equals the commit for every other existing id, and those defaults are refused later in the same patch.

SceneBridge itself is unchanged from main.

## Why

A create with an existing id silently replaced the node and orphaned its children. On the converted /next house, `wall_ground-exterior-01` lost its 3 windows while `validate_scene` still said valid. Updates could rewrite `id` or `type`. On hosted MCP the same patches fail at commit and end the session (409); after the bump they become ordinary tool errors.

The Codex review and Cursor Bugbot found more ways to lose or refuse a node, all fixed here:

- `[update wall.children=[], delete wall, create a node with the former child's id]` silently overwrote the child.
- A dry-run cascade that missed wall merges let an update to the merged-away wall report success as a no-op.
- The dry run missed children created earlier in the patch, nodes reparented earlier in the patch, and hosts created without a `children` list, and it planned batched deletes one by one.

No caller needs an upsert: every internal create uses freshly generated ids. The explicit upsert op is Q-01b and is not in this PR.

## Failing case first

```
# first round (tool tests, before any fix)
(fail) apply_patch > refuses a create whose id already exists, keeping the hosted windows   Received: undefined
(fail) apply_patch > refuses an update that changes id or type                              Received: undefined
# review round (apply-patch-identity.test.ts on the previous head cd88b4ae0)
(fail) a children update cannot detach a node so a later create overwrites it    Expected true, Received false
(fail) the dry run sees walls the real delete merges away                        Expected true, Received false
(fail) updates cannot change object or children; echoing current values passes
(fail) an update that adds schema issues is refused; one on an already invalid node is not
# round 2 (on e78dc4984)
(fail) refusals reach the client as structured data                 JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "MCP"
(fail) an invalid value in a core union field is refused, not skipped as a plugin kind   Expected true, Received false
(fail) a reparent must name an existing parent that can hold children                    Expected true, Received false
(fail) default gutters a delete regenerates cannot be addressed later in the same patch   Expected true, Received false
# round 3 (on 2789c445c)
(fail) a host whose default children a delete regenerates cannot be updated in the same patch   Expected true, Received false
(fail, core, intermittent) planNodeDeletion preview: two previews of one hip-roof delete differed (a default downspout kept in one, replaced in the other)
```

On the house, re-creating `wall_ground-exterior-01`: before, children went 3 → 0 with 3 `verify_scene` "not listed in wall … children" issues; after, `node_exists`, and the wall keeps its 3 windows and its slots. The guard over 890 updates takes 46 ms, and over 50 cascading wall deletes 6 ms.

## Proof

- `bun run --cwd editor/packages/core test`: 2996 pass (rebased on main after #939). `plan-node-deletion.test.ts` shows the plan equals what `deleteNodes` commits, including a merged-away wall; the preview is deterministic across runs (8/8) and equals the commit outside `unsettledIds`.
- `bun test --cwd editor/packages/mcp`: 411 pass. `apply-patch-identity.test.ts` holds 18 cases driven through `createSceneOperations`, as hosted does.
- `bun run --cwd editor check`: clean. `bun run --cwd editor/packages/mcp build` and core `check-types`: clean. `apps/editor` check-types can't run inside the private checkout (`@webxr/plugin` missing there); CI covers it.

**House effect:** no change: agent tooling. The converter and the viewer never call `apply_patch`.

## Not in this PR

- Local atomic rollback for mixed batches (the bridge still makes one store call per run of same-type ops) and an explicit upsert op are Q-01b.
- The guard's cascade uses the core store's semantics. The hosted bridge has its own delete cascade (P-08 parity).

## Round 4: bridge-specific delete previews

- The guard previews deletes with the **active bridge's** planner. `SceneBridge.planDeletion(scene, ids)` returns core's `planNodeDeletion` preview, and `SceneOperations` forwards it when the bridge has one.
- A bridge without a planner, which is the hosted bridge today, gets a stricter rule: a create may not reuse any id present at the start of the patch. The hosted bridge doesn't merge walls, so `[delete spur, create existing wall_b]` would otherwise overwrite `wall_b`. A private follow-up can add `planDeletion` to `HostedMcpSceneBridge` with its own cascade.
- Updating a roof or roof segment makes the store refresh its default gutters, so such an update now marks them as regenerated, as a delete does (core `previewDefaultGutterRefresh`). Later ops on those gutters, and later updates of their segments, are refused in the same patch with `regenerated_default`.
- Failing before: `without a bridge deletion planner, a create of an id present at the start is refused` (Received undefined) and `an update of an auto-gutter roof segment unsettles its default gutters` (Expected true, Received false). After: mcp 413 pass, core 2996 pass, all editor packages 11/11.

## R1–R9

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R3 | Final-graph validity: writes that would orphan children, split a key from its id, or add schema issues are refused before they land. The delete preview is core's own planner. |
| R8 | No raw-write bypass: refusals sit in the shared tool layer, so local and (after the bump) hosted `apply_patch` behave the same. Typed codes, tool description and README updated. |
| R9 | Stable source ids: a converter id such as `wall_ground-exterior-01` can no longer be clobbered. |
| R1, R2, R4–R7 | Unaffected: `planNodeDeletion` is a behaviour-preserving extraction; no schema, geometry, renderer or bake change. |

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes agent-facing scene mutation validation and delete semantics for MCP dry-runs; core delete behavior is intended to be unchanged but the planner is now shared with patch preview logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`apply_patch`** now dry-runs the full batch through shared **`patch-guards`** before the bridge commits anything, and rejects the whole patch with structured tool errors (`{ code, patchIndex, id, message }`) instead of silently corrupting the graph.
> 
> Guards block creates when an id already exists (`node_exists`), updates that change **`id`/`type`** (`identity_change`) or **`object`/`children`** (`immutable_field`), bad reparents (`invalid_parent` + **`validateNodeRelations`**), updates that introduce new schema issues (`invalid_update`), and later ops on default gutters/downspouts or their roof segments when a delete or roof edit would regenerate them (`regenerated_default`). Consecutive deletes are planned together via core’s new **`planNodeDeletion`** (with **`mintDefaults: false`** on preview) so cascades and collinear wall merges match what **`deleteNodes`** commits.
> 
> Core refactors delete into the exported pure planner **`planNodeDeletion`** / **`previewDefaultGutterRefresh`**; **`SceneBridge.planDeletion`** wires that into MCP. Docs and tests cover the refusal matrix and planner parity with the store.
>

title: feat(mcp): find_nodes by import source id and every node kind (NH-02c)
body:
<!-- NH-02c PR body -->
## What

`find_nodes` can find nodes by import source id and filter every node kind.

- New filters **`sourceId`** (exact) and **`sourceIdPrefix`** match any entry of `node.metadata.sourceIds`, the ids an importer records for its source elements. They combine (AND) with `type`, `parentId`, `levelId` and `zoneId`.
- **`type`** accepts any node kind: a string checked against the core kinds, the registered plugin kinds and the kinds present in the scene, so a plugin kind such as `fixture:bench` works. An unknown kind is a tool error. (A first version derived a closed enum from `AnyNode`, which still excluded plugin kinds; Codex review.)
- **`zoneId`** keeps only nodes on the zone's level, and tests each node's plan point in its level's frame. Positioned nodes resolve through core's `nodeLevelFrame`, so a window sits where its wall puts it and a module where its cabinet puts it. Polygons use their area centroid (`measurementCentroid`); blocks and imported meshes use their vertex-bounds centre. Before, it tested host-local `position` as level coordinates and ignored levels (Codex review).
- Source filters match the input as given and percent-encoded (printable ASCII kept, the rest as UTF-8 `%XX`), the form typed provenance (#942) requires. Legacy raw ids and encoded ids are both found. Matching `provenance.refs[].id` follows in a commit once #942 merges.
- Zone filtering resolves **plan-only** frames (core `nodeLevelFrame(id, nodes, seen, { cache, planOnly })`, new in this PR) through one per-query cache. An all-kinds zone query on the house drops from ~4 s (the review measured 9–10 s) to 18 ms, with the same hits. Imported-mesh and block bounds are taken in 3D and transformed by the full frame before projecting to plan.
- `metadata.sourceIds[]` gets a row in the R3 metadata reference inventory (`core/src/contracts/reference-inventory.ts`): a `source` reference, frozen on delete and stripped on preset save. The metadata scanner requires it now that an editor source reads the key.

A filter on the existing read-only tool rather than a new tool: same annotations (`READ_ONLY_TOOL_ANNOTATIONS`), so the OpenAI annotation inventory is unchanged (`bun run skills:validate` passes).

## Why

885 of the 890 nodes of the converted /next house carry `metadata.sourceIds`. An agent could only find a node by source by fetching the whole scene (1.5 MB) and filtering it client-side. Worse, the unknown `sourceId` argument was silently stripped, so `find_nodes({ sourceId })` returned all 890 nodes.

## Failing case first

```
# first round (before any fix)
(fail) find_nodes > source ids > sourceId matches any entry of metadata.sourceIds exactly   Received + 7 (every node)
(fail) find_nodes > source ids > sourceIdPrefix matches every node with an entry starting with it
(fail) find_nodes > source ids > source filters combine with type and parentId
(fail) find_nodes > type filter accepts every node kind in the schema   rejected: elevator, unit, … (34 kinds)
# review round (on the previous head 228cb18ea)
(fail) find_nodes > type accepts a plugin kind present in the scene     Received isError: true
(fail) find_nodes > zoneId only returns nodes on the zone’s level        Received + the upper-level wall
(fail) find_nodes > zoneId places a hosted window where its wall puts it Received + the window at wall-local x 1 on a wall at x 20
# round 2 (on 8b2c7c226)
(fail) find_nodes > zoneId places an imported mesh by its fully rotated vertex bounds   Received + the tilted mesh
(fail) nodeLevelFrame resolves each host once per shared cache (core)                    Expected true, Received false
(fail) find_nodes > source ids outside printable ASCII match raw and percent-encoded entries   the encoded id was not found
```

On the converter house (`bench/next-house/out/scene.extended.json`, 890 nodes):

| Call | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `{ sourceId: 'primary-rear-window-1' }` | 890 nodes (filter ignored) | 1 (`window_primary-rear-window-1`) |
| `{ sourceIdPrefix: 'primary-rear-window' }` | 890 | 3 |
| `{ sourceIdPrefix: 'screen' }` | 890 | 35 |
| `{ type: 'imported-mesh' }` / `'block'` / `'cabinet-module'` / `'solar-panel'` | input validation error | 182 / 51 / 45 / 48 |

Zone filtering on the house, summed over its 38 zones:

| `type` | hits before (on another level) | hits after (on another level) |
|---|---|---|
| door | 40 (6) | 5 (0) |
| window | 24 (8) | 0 (0) |
| item | 19 (4) | 15 (0) |
| wall | 41 (32) | 9 (0) |

Openings sit on walls, which lie on zone boundaries, so after the fix they rarely fall inside a zone polygon. The hits before came from host-local coordinates.

## Proof

- `bun test --cwd editor/packages/mcp`: 391 pass, 0 fail (10 new tests: source-id filters on a small fixture of a wall, its window with two source ids, a block, a column and an untagged wall; every core kind and a plugin kind accepted by `type`; `zoneId` with columns, a block, imported meshes (including a tilted one), hosted windows and two levels; encoded source ids). Core: `level-frame-cache.test.ts` (cache reuse, plan-only placement); `bun run --cwd editor/packages/core test` 2981 pass.
- `bunx turbo run test --filter='!editor'` (every editor package): 11/11 tasks, 0 fail. The first push missed the core R3 inventory test (`sourceIds` unclassified); fixed in the second commit.
- `bun run --cwd editor check`: clean (6 pre-existing infos). `bun run --cwd editor skills:validate`: 69 pass.
- `bun run --cwd editor/packages/mcp build` (`tsc --build`): exit 0. `check-types` passes for every workspace except `apps/editor`, which cannot resolve `@webxr/plugin` inside the private-editor checkout (not installed there; untouched by this PR).

**House effect:** no change: agent tooling. Read-only query.

## R1–R9

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R5 | Agent parity: an MCP agent can address converted elements of every kind, core or plugin, not only the 17 listed before; zone queries use level-frame positions. |
| R8 | All-surface registration: the same `registerFindNodes` serves local and hosted MCP (hosted calls `bridge.findNodes` and filters in the tool), so both gain the filters. Read-only; no write path. |
| R2 | Bounded work: zone queries resolve each host once and skip height resolution (18 ms on the house). |
| R3 | Reference inventory: `metadata.sourceIds[]` classified as a source-namespace reference (no remaps). On the private SHA bump, `bench/next-house/design/existing-references.json` must be regenerated, and its private importer row for the same path becomes redundant. |
| R9 | Stable source ids are now queryable: an agent can go from a SketchUp/ledger id to the Pascal node without the id convention. |
| R1, R4, R6, R7 | Unaffected: read-only MCP query; no schema, geometry, renderer or bake change. |

title: fix(mcp): measure nodes in world space, for every kind (NH-02b)
body:
<!-- NH-02b PR body -->
## What

`measure` now measures between world-space points and works for every node kind. It returns the two points it used (`fromPoint`, `toPoint`) and, where a point is not where the viewer draws the node, an `approximate: [{ id, reason }]` entry.

`resolveNodeWorldPoint` (`packages/mcp/src/tools/node-world-point.ts`) follows the frames the viewer renders in:

- core's `nodeLevelFrame`: wall frames with slab support, ceilings, roof and block faces, cabinets, shelves, and the generic position/rotation walk;
- the stair-segment attachment chain;
- the level's stacked base Y (`getLevelElevations`) and its building transform;
- missing `parentId`s are filled from the parents' `children` arrays first, so children-linked records resolve too.

Each kind's reference point comes from its own geometry:

| Node | Reference point |
|---|---|
| Positioned node | origin in its host's frame (an item's base, a door's or window's centre in its wall) |
| Wall, fence | centreline midpoint (arc or spline) at its base |
| Slab, ceiling, zone, site | area centroid (`measurementCentroid`) on its own plane |
| Block, imported mesh | vertex-bounds centre |
| Distance or angle measurement, dimension | centre of its anchors |
| Area or perimeter measurement | area centroid of `measurement.base` |
| Volume measurement | base centroid plus half the extrusion |
| Level | plan centre of its content on its base plane |
| Other containers | centre of their children's points |

## What is flagged `approximate`, not guessed

- **`floor-lift-unresolved-headless`**: headless MCP doesn't load `@pascal-app/nodes`, so these keep their level-plane point:
  - built-in block, cabinet, column, duct terminal, HVAC equipment, spawn and stair;
  - unregistered plugin kinds;
  - nodes hosted on those, such as cabinet modules and stair segments;
  - fences.

  When a host registers the definitions, core's `nodeLevelFrame` lifts these nodes and no flag is raised. Items, shelves and procedural items are lifted without the registry. A source-scan test keeps the list in step with the definitions that declare `floorPlaced`.
- **`anchor-fallback`**: a measurement or dimension anchor that references a node is resolved through that kind's registered measurement contribution (the wall parameter `t`), as the viewer does. When the contribution or the node is missing, which is always the case headless, the stored fallback point is used and flagged.
- **`roof-surface`**: solar panels and skylights. The viewer seats them on the finished deck-and-shingle surface; the point is on the structural surface.
- Poses the renderer derives elsewhere:
  - a downspout (at its gutter outlet; measured at its gutter);
  - a gutter (eave height);
  - a ridge vent (the ridge);
  - openings on roof or dormer faces;
  - lean-tos on walls;
  - wall-side items.

On the house, 192 of 890 nodes carry a flag:

| Kind | Flagged | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| block | 51 | floor lift |
| cabinet-module | 45 | floor lift |
| solar-panel | 48 | roof surface |
| column | 19 | floor lift |
| cabinet | 14 | floor lift |
| fence | 5 | floor lift |
| stair-segment | 4 | floor lift |
| hvac-equipment | 3 | floor lift |
| item (wall-side) | 2 | wall face |
| stair | 1 | floor lift |

## Why

`getCentre` read a door's, window's or item's `position` as a level point, although it is local to its host: `measure(wall_ground-exterior-01, window_primary-rear-window-1)` returned 14.74 m for a window in that wall. It also threw "Cannot derive centre" for 38 of the 51 kinds.

An earlier revision was stacked on #941, which put built-in floor-placed capabilities into core. The review rejected that as breaking registry ownership, and #941 is closed. The alternative, a headless-safe `@pascal-app/nodes` entry, was scoped at ~450 non-test lines plus ~150 test lines. It would also make `@pascal-app/mcp` depend on `@pascal-app/nodes`, whose React, three, editor and viewer peers npm installs automatically. So those lifts are flagged instead.

## Failing case first

```
# first round
(fail) a window is measured where its wall hosts it      Expected: 1.2  Received: 10.071742649611338
(fail) derives a finite point for every node kind         38 kinds: "Cannot derive centre …"
# review round 1
(fail) polygons are measured at their area centroid      Expected: 1.357142857  Received: 1.6666666666666667
(fail) every kind resolves on its real host …            approximate expected [downspout, gutter, ridge-vent], received []
(fail) a curved railing …                                 y 0 instead of the deck height, not on the arc
# review round 2 (on 9f726559d)
(fail) a floor-placed block is flagged when its floor lift cannot be resolved headless
(fail) solar panels are flagged: the viewer seats them on the finished roof surface
(fail) a curved railing is measured on its arc, its deck height flagged
(fail) the floor-lift flag list matches the built-in definitions that declare floorPlaced
(fail) every kind resolves on its real host, with renderer-derived poses flagged
(fail) scenes linked only through children arrays still resolve upper levels
# review round 3 (on 1a34ace05)
(fail) area, perimeter and volume measurements are measured from their base    Expected: 11  Received: 0
(fail) semantic anchors resolve from the referenced node, or are flagged         no approximate entry
```

On the house: wall to its own window goes from 14.74 m to 2.03 m (1.40 m along the wall, 1.47 m up). Errors go from 421 nodes of 13 kinds to 0. All 64 hosted doors and windows land on their wall line (max plan offset 1.8e-15 m).

## Proof

- `bun test --cwd editor/packages/mcp`: 405 pass (rebased on main after #939). The every-kind test builds real hosts (wall, roof segment, cabinet, stair) and a 1 m deck, covers all 51 kinds, checks that core-lifted kinds stand on the deck, and asserts the exact `approximate` set.
- `bun run --cwd editor check`: clean. `bun run --cwd editor/packages/mcp build`: clean. `apps/editor` check-types can't run inside the private checkout (`@webxr/plugin` missing there); CI covers it.

**House effect:** no change: agent tooling. `measure` is read-only.

## R1–R9

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R5 | Measure parity: agents measure hosted nodes where they render, for every kind; what can't be resolved headless is flagged `approximate`, not silently wrong. |
| R8 | The same `registerMeasure` serves local and hosted MCP; core stays kind-agnostic, and floor lifts come only from registered definitions. |
| R1–R4, R6, R7, R9 | Unaffected: read-only query; no core, schema, renderer or bake change. |

title: fix(core): floor lift without a registered built-in plugin (NH-02d)
body:
<!-- NH-02d PR body -->
## What

Core's `nodeLevelFrame` now applies the floor lift for blocks, columns, stairs, spawns, HVAC equipment, floor duct terminals, cabinet runs and modules without a registered built-in plugin.

- These kinds' `floorPlaced` capabilities move into core (`lib/floor-placed-builtins.ts`). Their helpers move beside the schemas: `blockBounds`, `columnFootprintHalf`, and the stair floor stack (`git mv` from `nodes/src/stair/floor-stack.ts`).
- The built-in definitions in `@pascal-app/nodes` register those same objects, so browser behaviour is unchanged.
- `floorPlacedConfig(kind)` returns the registered capability, or the built-in one when the kind is not registered. `floorLift` and `nodeLevelFrame` use it.
- A nodes test pins that every built-in `floorPlaced` capability is the object core uses headless, so the two cannot drift.
- The fence lift resolver (`resolveFenceLiftElevation(ForNodes)`) moves from `nodes/src/fence/lift.ts` into `core/systems/fence/fence-lift.ts`, unchanged and with its test, so headless consumers can place a slab-hosted railing (third commit; Bugbot on #940). `packages/editor/src/lib/elevation-guides.ts` still keeps its own mirror of this function, whose comment says nodes can't be imported. It could now import core's version; I left it for a follow-up.
- Cabinet runs and modules, which core's `floorLift` already special-cases, fall back to their own width × depth box. That is the footprint the cabinet definition uses when it has no scene (second commit).

## Why

Headless runtimes (MCP, the hosted scene API, bench) never load the built-in plugin, so the registry is empty there. `nodeLevelFrame` found no capability and left these kinds on the level plane. From the Codex review of #940: a block on a 1 m deck resolved to y 1.2 instead of the rendered 2.2. #940 (`measure` in world space) is stacked on this PR and needs it to be right.

## Failing case first

`bun test src/procedural-items/floor-lift-headless.test.ts` (empty registry, a 1 m slab under each node):

```

       Expected: 1  Received: 0
 2 pass / 1 fail
```

After: 3 pass (cabinet run and module included).

On the converted /next house, the Y of all 197 floor-placed nodes from headless `nodeLevelFrame` equals the Y with `builtinPlugin` loaded (max difference 0). Non-floor-placed kinds (roof, ceiling-mounted duct terminal) keep their stored height, and a column off the slab stays on the level plane.

## Proof

- `bunx turbo run test --filter='!editor'`: 11/11 tasks, 0 fail (core 2994 tests, including the moved fence-lift test; nodes including `floor-stack.test.ts`, now importing from core, and the new drift test).
- `bun run --cwd editor check`: clean. `turbo run check-types --filter='!editor'`: 9/9. `bun run --cwd packages/nodes build` (tsc): clean. `apps/editor` check-types can't run inside the private checkout (`@webxr/plugin` not installed there); CI covers it.

**House effect:** no change: headless frames only. The viewer already used the same capabilities through the registry, and bakes and the harness render in the browser.

## R1–R9

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R5 | Measure and agent parity: headless consumers place floor-placed nodes where the viewer renders them. |
| R8 | One capability object for both the registered and the headless path, with an identity test in `@pascal-app/nodes`. |

title: feat(core): typed provenance on every node, dark (EC-I01)
body:
EC-I01 (element-fidelity programme, owner decision D5): typed source identity on every node, shipped dark.

## What
`BaseNode` gains an optional `provenance` field (`packages/core/src/schema/provenance.ts`):

```ts
provenance?: {
  refs: { ns?: string /* ≤48 B */, id: string /* ≤160 B, verbatim */, role?: 'primary' | 'piece' | 'absorbed' | 'alias' | 'derived' }[] // ≤32
  lineage?: { op: 'import' | 'split' | 'merge' | 'duplicate' | 'convert' | 'promote' | 'make-independent' | 'attach', fromIds: string[] /* ≤32 node ids, ≤128 B */ }  // all strings printable ASCII
}
```

Nothing in the editor writes it. Importers write it (the private /next converter in the `-H` companion), and every validated write carries it. Two new reference-inventory rows cover it.

## Why these choices
- **Name `provenance`, not `source`.** A hosted third-party plugin (`articraft:asset`) already declares a top-level `source` enum, and `.extend()` would replace the base field for that kind. Generic readers (the I-02 source index, the I-03 bake stamp) would then misread a string. `source` is also taken three times in core (item asset source, hole metadata, `PascalPartTag.source`). None of the 68 hosted plugin kinds declares `provenance`, and it does not match the collaboration guard's `/Ids?$/`.
- **Caps: 32 refs, 32 lineage ids.** The /next house's largest node, `window_roof-main-left-gable-louver`, carries 18 source ids (the next two carry 15), and its longest id is 72 characters. 32 refs and 160-character ids leave about 1.8× and 2.2× headroom. With ASCII ids a full value is at most about 12 KiB: half the 24 KiB F8 field cap. **Nothing truncates.** A node over a cap fails its schema at every validated writer (hosted save, collaboration, MCP), and load keeps a stored over-cap node verbatim (tested through `healSceneNodes` and `setScene`). The spill rule: a writer with more ids refuses, or keeps the rest off the node (sub-record `src`, the import artifact's alias table).
- **No lift of `metadata.sourceIds`.** It is a private converter convention, and a client-only migration would break the hosted authority's whole-node preconditions. No editor code reads it. The converter writes the typed field itself.
- **Inventory rows.** `provenance.refs[].id`: namespace `source`, role `content`, onDelete `freeze`, **onPreset `strip`**, so presets never claim source elements. `provenance.lineage.fromIds[]`: namespace `label`, role `internal`, onDelete `freeze`, onPreset `strip`. Lineage ids are node ids kept as history: they are compared, never dereferenced, and may name deleted nodes (the other walls of a merge). So a future `node` validator must not flag them as dangling (tested). The array is named `fromIds` so the A-02 discovery walk sees it (its `Ids` rule), rather than hiding a node-id list from the tripwire. All three clones keep both fields verbatim today (tested); I-04 re-roles copies.
- **Collaboration.** `provenance` is one top-level field with from/to preconditions, so a concurrent stale edit is refused. Its lineage ids carry no hierarchy or host invariant, so the lexical guard needs no special case. The `-H` companion tests the round trip.

**Plans.** This amends foundations F8 ("`sourceCategory` + one `src` ≤ 64 B") as DESIGN §3.3 records. The coordinator owns that amendment; this PR edits no plan.

## Proof
- `bun run --cwd editor/packages/core test`: 3043 pass, 0 fail (new: `schema/provenance.test.ts` 7, `store/use-scene-provenance.test.ts` 3, 3 inventory tests, 48 compiled-parser cases plus two invalid variants per kind).
- nodes 3503, mcp 381, viewer 390, editor 1111: all pass.
- `bun run --cwd editor check`: exit 0.
- `bun run --cwd editor check-types`: core, editor, cli, ui and the package builds pass. `apps/editor` fails only on the known missing local `@webxr/plugin`, which is unrelated.
- **Failing case first.** Without the field, `store/use-scene-provenance.test.ts` fails 2 of 3: an edit or undo through `updateNode` strips `provenance` (the parse drops unknown keys).
- **Perf (M5 lock, A/B in one process, median of 5 × 100k parses).** Interpreted parse +0.003 to +0.049 µs per node (0.7–3.8 %) on wall, window, item, slab, door and zone. Compiled parse −0.016 to +0.024 µs, within noise. Every kind still compiles.

**House effect:** no change. This is an optional field with no default and no editor writer: old scenes parse byte-identically, and the renderers and the GLB export never read it. The converter output is identical apart from the added field (receipt in `-H`).

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | Optional base field. Plugins that extend `BaseNode` inherit it, and the plugin API v1 conformance tests pass. `provenance` avoids the `articraft:asset` `source` collision. |
| R2 | No gesture code. Parse cost is at most 0.05 µs per node (above). |
| R3 | Two typed rows. The discovery, stale-row, clone-column and label tests pass. The clones keep both fields today, and the preset policy is `strip`. |
| R4, R5, R7 | Unaffected: the field is data only (I-02 and Q-02 add lookup). |
| R6 | Unaffected. `stampIdentity` whitelists its extras, so the field never reaches the GLB (I-03 decides the stamp). |
| R8 | MCP and patch writes validate it through `AnyNode`, with typed cap refusals. The tools come in Q-02 and Q-04. |
| R9 | The `cap:` namespace is reserved in the doc. P-10 writes it. |

Companion: `pascalorg/private-editor` branch `fidelity/ec-i01-provenance` (converter writes the field; hosted save and collaboration round trip; plugin schema snapshot regenerated). It opens after this merges.

## Review round 1 (Codex, `5abfbd6cc`)
- **Store refuses invalid provenance writes.** A create or update whose `provenance` fails its schema throws, and nothing applies. Before this, it went through the numeric sanitize fallback and was stored. An unrelated edit of a stored over-cap node still applies, with nothing truncated. MCP `apply_patch` inherits this: a 33-ref update is refused and stores nothing (`apply-patch-provenance.test.ts`). A mixed patch should be refused before any of its ops applies; that is #938's dry run (`patch-guards.ts`). Its test is gated on that file and passes with #938 applied locally (2/2). **MCP relies on #938 for atomic refusal.**
- **Preset strip is real.** `withoutSourceIdentity` (`registry/subtree.ts`) is the preset serialization. It drops `provenance` and every inventory `source` row with `onPreset: 'strip'`, so WL-01's layer `src` rows (#943) are covered as they land; an inventory test fails for any strip row it misses. Tested by saving an imported node as a preset and placing it again. The community capture paths call it in the `-H` companion.
- **Caps are UTF-8 bytes.** Provenance strings are printable ASCII (`^[\x20-\x7E]*$`), so each length cap is a byte cap. Importers percent-encode other characters, which keeps ids exactly recoverable. A maximal value with worst-case JSON escapes stays under the 24 KiB F8 field cap; before this change, a maximal CJK value was 33,562 bytes. A byte-counting refinement would break the hosted plugins' JSON Schema snapshot (68 kinds) and `z.compile`.
- **Lookups encode too.** An importer percent-encodes non-ASCII source ids, so any lookup by source id must apply the same encoding: `find_nodes` `sourceId` (#939) should encode its input before matching.
- **Failing cases first** (receipts in `scratch/EC-I01/failing-*.txt`):
  - the store stored a 33-ref update;
  - MCP `apply_patch` returned no error;
  - a preset copy kept `provenance`;
  - the CJK value was schema-valid at 33,562 bytes.
- **Tests:** core 3049, mcp 382, nodes 3503, editor 1111, viewer 390, all passing. `check` exits 0, and `check-types` fails only on the known `@webxr/plugin` error.

## Re-verify fix (Codex, `4212e2889`)
- **Plugin kinds are no longer bypassed.** A plain API-v1 plugin kind (no `strictMutations`) falls through the closed `AnyNode` union, so the store never saw the provenance issue and stored 33 refs. Every create, and every update that writes `provenance`, now checks the value against `Provenance` directly, whatever the kind. Tested on a registered `acme:widget` through `updateNode`, `updateNodes`, `applyNodeChanges` and `createNode`.
- **Strict plugin kinds carry provenance.** Cursor Bugbot flagged this, fixed in `4ac6ba698`. A `strictMutations` kind's own parse made a stored over-cap node uneditable, and a strict schema without the base field dropped a valid one. Strict kinds now parse without `provenance` and get it back verbatim. Tested with both strict schema shapes; receipt `failing-strict-kind.txt`.
- **Rebased on main with #939 and #944.** #939 declares `metadata.sourceIds[]` a `source` reference a preset strips, and the inventory-driven preset strip now drops it too (`146d39215` updates the test).
- **Mixed-patch atomicity stays #938's job.** The gated MCP test turns on when #938 merges; the gate is removed in a follow-up commit once both are merged.

## Failing-first receipts
All in `/private/tmp/fid/scratch/EC-I01/`:

| Receipt | What it shows before the fix |
|---|---|
| `failing-store-refusal.txt` | `updateNode` stored a 33-ref provenance |
| `failing-mcp.txt` | `apply_patch` returned no error for a 33-ref update |
| `failing-preset-strip.txt` | a preset copy kept `provenance` |
| `failing-cjk.txt` | a maximal CJK value was schema-valid at 33,562 bytes |
| `failing-plugin-kind.txt` | a plain plugin kind stored an over-cap value |

title: feat(core): F2 assembly layers contract, stack sets the body, dark (WL-01a)
body:
**WL-01 (part a of 2) · contract, dark.** Freezes F2 assembly layers (`editor-fidelity-foundations.md` §2.3) as the ONE layer model for walls and roofs (owner ruling 2026-09-27, option 2), rebased on main after #937 (WS5 `WallAssembly`) and #942 (typed provenance). Types, pure functions and tests only; nothing renders F2 yet.

Walls keep WS5's `WallAssembly` in this PR. **Part (b)** moves them onto F2 (load migration, all WS5 readers through the F2 resolver, the Architect plugins through accessors) and gets the owner preview.

### The types

```ts
// core/src/schema/assembly.ts
AssemblyLayer = {
  id: string            // [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,40}, unique in the host: the `#layer:<id>` address
  role: LayerRole       // finish | lining | substrate | sheathing | membrane | underlay | insulation
                        // | air | furring | structure | deck | covering | fill | shell | glazing
  thickness: number     // 0–5 m along the host's measure axis, as declared
  core?: true           // body only, at most one, role structure | deck | shell: the structural layer
  material?: string     // construction-material kind: stucco, osb, wood, cmu, drywall, …
  slot?: string         // key into the host's own slots; absent = `layer:<id>`, then the role default
  returns?; display?; inset?; bottom?; lift?   // inset/bottom/lift: backing only
  src?: SourceRefString // `<ns>:<id>[::<sub>]`, printable ASCII, ns ≤ 48 B, id ≤ 160 B (#942 caps)
}
Assembly = {
  layers: AssemblyLayer[0..12]           // from the reference face inward; empty only when backing carries it
  face?: 'front' | 'exterior'            // exterior = from the outside (frontSide/backSide, front fallback)
  backing?: AssemblyLayer[..8]; presetId?: string; cavityInsulation?: string
}
RoofNode.assembly?: Assembly; RoofNode.slots?: Record<string,string>   // optional, no default
capabilities.assembly?: { reference, measure, body(node) → stored thickness | null, backing? }
  // declared by each kind in nodes/src/<kind>/definition.ts; core ships none
resolveAssemblyStack(assembly, { body, backing? })
  → { layers: {id, role, depth, thickness, core, …}[], total, backing: {…, depth from the body's far face}[], diagnostics }
getWallLayerBands(wall, assembly, miters) → { …stack, bands: { layerId, back, front, polygons }[] }
```

**The stack sets the body** (the WS5 rule, now F2's): a host's thickness is Σ layers, and a writer that edits the layers writes that sum in the same patch. A stored thickness that disagrees is reported (`assembly.thickness-mismatch`) and draws no bands. No thickness is ever rescaled.

### Examples (`core/src/contracts/assembly.test.ts`)
- **Stucco wall, 185.7 mm:** drywall 12.7 · studs 139.7 (core) · OSB 11.1 · stucco 22.2. The stucco band is y ∈ [−0.09285, −0.07065]. With `face: 'exterior'`, the stucco follows the exterior when rooms are re-detected, and falls back to the front face.
- **Shingle roof, /next thicknesses:** covering 9 mm, underlay 1 mm, sheathing 15.875 mm. Total 25.875 mm; t / cos 40° of the vertical prism on a 40° facet.
- **Two measured /next walls (ids withheld, D5):**
  - Timber weather wall: each of its 7 bands lands on the source faces.
  - CMU wall widened to 254 mm (the CV-10 ruling): its block band is exactly today's wall body.
- **Band math:** 9 cases, including an L mitre, an acute 12° mitre, a three-way junction vertex, a 1 mm membrane, curved walls and a zero-length wall.
- **Backing:** a ceiling with no body and insulation backing resolves its backing intervals.
- **Presets:** saving a layered roof drops every layer `src` and its `provenance` through `withoutSourceIdentity`.

### Review history
- Codex round 1 is fixed with failing tests first, then rebased:
  - `src` grammar: `2e330c2e3` → `65363a294`, then `e5b14c668` → `2ce68dc33`.
  - Preset strip: moved to #942's helper in `e255ef6f6`.
  - Rescaling removed.
- Frozen rulings: CMU walls get widened by the converter; the layer-id charset stands; `assembly` sits on the roof; one model with the stack setting the body.

### Review round d (Codex `rev-943-d`), failing first `f4bc9e090` (5 fail), fix `3c45c162e`
- Backing resolves: `ResolvedAssembly.backing` has the backing intervals on a host that accepts backing, and a zero-body ceiling with insulation backing resolves (SU-S4 case).
- `core` is refused outside `structure`, `deck` and `shell`.
- `assembly.{layers,backing}[].slot` is inventoried (namespace `part`), and reference discovery now finds `slot` fields.
- `RoofNode` keeps `slots`, so a layer slot's paint override survives a parse.
- The wall and roof host configs moved out of core into their kinds' definitions.

### Proof
- Core tests: 3125 pass, 0 fail.
- Nodes, mcp, viewer and editor tests: 6/6 turbo tasks pass.
- Lint: `bun run check` exits 0.
- Types: `turbo check-types --filter='!editor'` passes 9/9.

**House effect:** no change. Nothing reads F2 and the converter writes none.

| R3 references | Inventory rows: `assembly.{layers,backing}[].src` are source/content/strip (stripped by `withoutSourceIdentity`); `…[].slot` are part keys into the host's slots; `…[].id` are keys; `presetId` is asset/keep. |

title: feat(core): freeze the cut-intent contract and drop capabilities.cuttable (DT-03a)
body:
**DT-03a · contract, dark.** This PR freezes F5b cut intents (`editor-fidelity-foundations.md` §2.2) and `capabilities.cuts`. `capabilities.cuttable`, which nothing ever read, stays in the v1 plugin contract as a deprecated, ignored alias. It adds types, executable examples and docs only. No host reads intents yet, so every wall, ceiling, slab and roof cut draws exactly as before.

### The types

```ts
// core/src/schema/cut.ts
CutIntent = {
  host: { nodeId: string; surfaceId: string; partKey?: PartKey }  // one face of the host
  shape: { kind: 'polygon'; ring: [u, v][] }                       // ≥ 3 points
       | { kind: 'circle'; center: [u, v]; radius: number }         // stays a circle in the face
  depth: 'through' | number   // metres along −normal from that face: a pocket keeps the backing
  taper?: number              // (−π/2, π/2) rad; positive narrows with depth (splayed reveal)
}
// core/src/registry/types.ts
capabilities.cuts?: (node: AnyNode, ctx: { nodes: Record<AnyNodeId, AnyNode> }) => CutIntent[]
/** @deprecated ignored; declare `cuts`. Kept for plugin API v1, removed in v2. */
capabilities.cuttable?: CuttableConfig
```

**Frames.** Every `shape` is drawn in its face's F0 surface chart: [u, v] in metres, with v = normal × u.

| Face | Chart |
|---|---|
| Wall `front` | wall-local (x, y), the frame door and window `position` already use |
| Wall `back` | u = length − x (the chart runs from `end`), so v stays up |
| Ceiling `underside` and slab `top` | plan [x, z] in the host's local plan, the space of its `polygon` and stored `holes` (the one exception to the chart: never the mirrored [x, −z]) |
| `facet:<id>:covering` | u along the eave, v up the slope, both in metres on the slope |

### Examples (`core/src/contracts/cut-intent.test.ts`)

1. **Through:** a 1.2 × 1.0 window. The front ring is `[[1.4,0.9],[2.6,0.9],[2.6,1.9],[1.4,1.9]]` with depth `through`. Published on the back face, it maps to the same wall-local rectangle. A 15° taper narrows it to 1.093 m at the back face.
2. **Niche that keeps its backing:** depth 0.12 on a 0.2 m wall removes z ∈ [−0.02, 0.1] and leaves 0.08 m of backing. DT-03b's rule, that a pocket leaves at least 5 mm, refuses a 0.198 m pocket.
3. **Ceiling hole:** a recessed downlight. `buildCeilingHole`'s rotated ring becomes the `underside` ring unchanged. A round fixture can publish a circle instead.
4. **Roof accessory:** a skylight on a 40° facet. The framed opening is 0.72 × 1.12 m in slope metres, and its plan footprint is 0.6177 m².

Plus a stored slab hole published unchanged on `top`, a plugin kind that declares `cuts` and reads its wall host from `ctx.nodes`, and a test that a `cuttable` declaration still type-checks while no source under `packages/*/src` reads it.

### How today's cut sources map (details in `wiki/architecture/node-definitions.md`)

| Source | Consumed today by | As an intent | Switches in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Door and window on a wall | `collectCutoutBrushes` → `createOpeningCutoutBrush` | wall `front` or `back`, the opening outline, `through` | DT-03b |
| Item with a `cutout` mesh | same loop, from the mesh's wall-local bounding rectangle | wall and side, the rectangle, `through` (a number for recessed items) | DT-03b |
| `roofAccessory.buildCut` (skylight, dormer) | roof merge: shin, deck and wall brushes | `facet:<id>:covering`, `through`, per segment | RL-02 |
| Door or window on a roof-segment wall (`cutScope: 'wall'`) | same, wall brush only | `face:<wall face>`, `through` | RL-02 |
| `ceilingCut.buildCeilingHole` | `CeilingSystem` holes | ceiling `underside`, same ring | DT-03b adapter |
| Stair and elevator openings | persisted `holes` + `holeMetadata` via the opening syncs | slab `top` or ceiling `underside`, `through`; the persisted holes stay | — |

`cuttable` has zero readers or declarers in `editor/`, the private repo's `apps/`, `packages/` and `bench/`, and all 11 installed plugins. It stays as a deprecated alias because removing an exported type and field breaks the additive-only v1 plugin contract; removal waits for API v2.

### What it unlocks

- DT-03b: wall pockets that keep the backing, then the 4 niches and the foyer pocket (CV-13, G5).
- RL-02: accessory cuts per segment on the direct shed path, so roof windows can be hosted on facets.
- P-03+: cutter discovery through the dependency index.
- B-01b: consuming `CutIntent`.
- Plugins that cut core walls, and details that cut their hosts.

### Review round 1 (Codex, `rev-944-b`), fixed with a failing test first

| Finding | Failing first (`e60311048`) | Fix (`72c4d4bec`) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 blocker: removing `cuttable` breaks plugin API v1 | `check-types`: TS2724 (no exported `CuttableConfig`), TS2353 (`cuttable` not in `Capabilities`) | `cuttable` and `CuttableConfig` restored with `@deprecated`; a test type-checks a declaration and asserts no source reads it |
| Contract choices frozen without review | — | Coordinator rulings below, written into `cut.ts`, the wiki and the examples |

**Frozen answers** (coordinator rulings, owner-delegated):
- The wall `back` face runs from `end` (u = length − x) so v stays up.
- A positive `taper` narrows with depth: a splayed reveal is widest at the named face.
- `ctx = { nodes }` is the whole publisher context for now; discovery is scene children now, the P-03 index later.
- Horizontal hosts (slab `top`, ceiling `underside`) take plan [x, z], like stored holes, never the chart's mirrored [x, −z].
- No `CuttableConfig` release note is needed: the type stays.

### Proof

- `bun test packages/core/src`: 2991 pass, 0 fail, including 12 cut-intent tests.
- `turbo run test` for nodes, mcp, viewer and editor: 6/6 tasks pass.
- `bun run check`: exit 0. `bun run skills:validate`: pass.
- `turbo run check-types --filter='!editor'`: 9/9 pass. `packages/core` check-types verifies the `@ts-expect-error`. Locally, the standalone app fails only on the missing `@webxr/plugin`, as it does on main.

**House effect:** no change. Nothing reads `capabilities.cuts`, and no kind publishes intents yet. The bench was not rerun for the same reason.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 plugins | `cuts` is optional and API v1 is unchanged: `cuttable` stays as a deprecated, ignored alias with a type-check test. A plugin cutter is exercised in the examples. |
| R5 parity | Doors, windows, items, accessories and ceiling fixtures keep today's cut paths until their consumers switch. |
| R8 agents | This is a contract only. Detail and cut tools follow in Q-03. |

title: feat(procedural-items): recipe version 2 and a design-level datum (AK-D1)
body:
## AK-D1: recipe version 2 and a design-level datum

**What.** Procedural recipes accept `version: 1 | 2`. Content only a new reader understands requires `version: 2`, so an older reader fails with a plain version error instead of a geometry error. This PR adds the first two v2 rules:
- **Ceiling designs hang from their top reference.** A v2 ceiling design is exempt from the design-space `y ≥ 0` check. The ceiling relation check in `query.ts` still bounds the design against the level floor.
- **Floor designs can declare a `base`**, an expression for the design-space height that rests on the host. Geometry and motion envelopes must stay at or above it. Evaluation then shifts every output (shapes, surfaces, lights, hinge and spin pivots, bounds) so the base sits at y = 0. Consumers such as placement, handles, footprints and the renderer read design space exactly as before.

v1 evaluation is byte-identical, and no zod defaults were added.

**Why.** In the expressivity trial, the `y = 0` rule broke two real /next elements' parameter sweeps: the E7 five-drop pendant (longer drops hang below 0) and the E8 stair guard (a shorter riser puts the first baluster below the newel base). This is the S alternative the CHALLENGE recommended to AK-05's Mount: a design-level datum, since `parseRecipe` has no instance to consult.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, `core/src/procedural-items/datum.test.ts` failed 5 of 6 tests: v2 was rejected and the sweeps failed.

**Proof.** Receipt: `scratch/AK-CORE/proofs/d1-trial-sweeps.ts`. It sweeps the trial's own recipe files.

| Recipe | Sweep before | Sweep after |
|---|---|---|
| E7 pendant, top fixed at the ceiling | 15/33 (v1) | **33/33** (v2) |
| E8 guard | 14/29 (v1, or v2 without a base) | **29/29** (v2, `base: min(0, riser − 0.194)`) |

- `bun test src/procedural-items` (core): 96 pass, 0 fail. `bun test src` (core): 2985 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test src/procedural-item` (nodes, against the rebuilt core dist): 47 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run check`: clean. `bun run check-types`: 10/11 packages pass; `apps/editor` fails only on the known local `@webxr/plugin` resolution.
- An invariant test raises four floor fixtures (shelf, the cabinet with hinge and slide, the desk fan with spin, the chandelier with lights) by 0.25 m and declares `base: 0.25`. The evaluation matches the original to 1e-9, with the same motion group ids.

**House effect:** no change. The /next converter emits no `procedural-item` nodes (0 of 671 native and 0 of 890 extended), and v1 evaluation is unchanged.

**Reader-first.** This release only *reads* v2. Studio (prompt v12 and the normaliser) and the converters keep writing v1. They start writing v2 one release after this one ships, in a private companion that also updates `wiki/ai/procedural-items.md`. **Rollback note:** once v2 content exists, a Community rollback to a v1-only reader blocks saves and collaboration for the affected projects. #930 carried the same exposure.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | No API v1 or plugin change. `RecipeSchema` stays strict; `version` widens to `1 \| 2` |
| R2 | No gesture change. Evaluation adds one expression and an O(shapes) shift, only when a base is declared |
| R3 | No new references |
| R5 | Placement, handles, footprints, surfaces, paint and 2D all read the same evaluated design space. The base invariant test covers shapes, surfaces, lights and pivots |
| R6 | Motion group ids and clip names are unchanged. Hinge and spin pivots shift with the geometry; a slide's pivot is its group origin, so it stays put |
| R7 | Inline recipe. v1 parses hash-stably, with no zod defaults |
| R8 | No new tool. `version` and `base` appear in the recipe schema that AK-02's schema resource will publish |
| R4, R9 | Not touched |

**For Wassim to review:**
1. The version-gate pattern (`requireVersion2`). Later AK PRs reuse it for every v2 field.
2. `base` as an expression plus an evaluation-time shift, rather than a pose offset in `proceduralLocalPose`.
3. Whether v2 **wall-side** designs should also be exempt. `validateProceduralRelations` already bounds them against the wall base, but I left them under `y ≥ 0` to keep this change to what the trial needed.

title: feat(procedural-items): recessed ceiling designs cut their ceiling (AK-D2)
body:
## AK-D2: recessed ceiling designs cut their ceiling

**Stacked on #945 (AK-D1).** Merge that first; this PR then retargets to `main`.

**What.** A v2 ceiling design can declare one cut, either `{ shape: 'rect', size }` or `{ shape: 'circle', diameter }`, with an optional `center`. The cut is drawn in the plane of the design's mounting reference.
- The design may rise above its reference into the plenum, but only inside the cut. Any part that rises above the reference outside the cut is refused, and a cut-less ceiling design still needs its reference at the top.
- `validateProceduralRelations` lets a recessed design sit above the ceiling, up to the level height.
- `procedural-item` declares `capabilities.ceilingCut` → `proceduralCeilingHole(node)`: the cut ring in ceiling-local `[x, z]`, with the same pose as `proceduralLocalPose`. `CeilingSystem`'s existing registry dispatch opens the hole, so the viewer needs no change.
- The renderer marks the host ceiling dirty whenever the committed cut can move: parent, position, rotation or parameters.
- `Evaluation` gains `cuts` (empty for v1).

**Why.** Recessed downlights (51 plus 9 sloped on /next), grilles and vents cannot be real openings today. A procedural design can only hang flush under the ceiling. The CHALLENGE's ceiling-only slice of AK-06: additive, with no effect on existing scenes.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, `core/src/procedural-items/ceiling-cut.test.ts` failed 6 of 6 tests (receipt `scratch/AK-CORE/d2-failing-before.txt`).

**Proof.**
- `bun test src/procedural-items` (core): 103 pass, 0 fail. The tests cover the rect and 32-gon rings, the reference rotation and center, the inside-the-cut rule, the v2 and ceiling-only gates, no cuts for v1, plenum fit within the level height, and the hole following the node's position and yaw.
- `bun test src/procedural-item` (nodes, rebuilt core dist): 48 pass, 0 fail, including dispatch through `nodeRegistry…ceilingCut.buildCeilingHole`.
- `bun run check`: clean. `bun run check-types`: 10/11 packages pass; `apps/editor` fails only on the known local `@webxr/plugin` resolution.

**House effect:** no change. The /next scenes carry no `procedural-item` nodes, and no v1 design declares cuts.

**Reader-first.** Studio and the converters do not write `cuts` yet. They will in the release after this one. Same rollback note as #945.

**Bugbot fixes** (second commit):
- A shape that rises above the reference is now tested by its rendered footprint (a cylinder's rim, a box's corners), so a round can fits a circle cut of its own diameter.
- Motion envelopes may rise inside the cut.
- The ceiling is re-marked when the recipe's `cuts` or `surfaces` change.

Each fix has a test.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | Reuses the existing `ceilingCut` capability; no viewer or plugin change. It maps 1:1 to DT-03a's frozen `CutIntent` (ceiling `underside` ring, `through`) |
| R2 | The hole follows at commit, like recessed catalog items. During a move drag, the original is hidden and the old hole stays until drop (see Known limits) |
| R3 | No new references |
| R5 | Placement, handles and surfaces are unchanged. Cut rings are data on the evaluation |
| R7 | Inline recipe, no zod defaults |
| R8 | No new tool. `cuts` appears in the recipe schema that AK-02 will publish |
| R4, R6, R9 | Not touched |

**For Wassim to review:**
1. Whether the cut should live in a top-level `cuts` array (`max(1)` for now, to line up with DT-03a's `capabilities.cuts`) or under `mounting`.
2. The "rise above the reference only inside the cut" rule. It uses shape AABBs, so it is conservative for rotated parts.
3. The renderer effect that re-marks the ceiling.

## Local preview
Shared setup for the whole stack: `previews/AK.md` (`preview.sh start AK-PV previews/AK/ak-after.json` serves on :3301).
Setup, scene and worktree are in `previews/AK.md`, which covers the whole stack.

### What you will notice
- The four square downlights on the ceiling now sit **in** the ceiling. There is a hole behind the trim, and you see the dark can walls and the glowing lens set back 4 cm. Before, a flush square sat on the ceiling surface.
- **Did not change:** hanging designs without a cut (the pendant), and every catalog item.

### Where to look
Level Ground, items "Downlight 1–4". Look up from the middle of the room (pose `2-ceiling`).

### Try this
1. Select a downlight and change **Aperture** in the panel. Expected: the ceiling hole resizes with it after the commit.
2. Move a downlight along the ceiling and drop it. Expected: the hole follows it at the drop.
3. Undo. Expected: the hole returns to where it was.
