title: feat(procedural-items): triangle budgets from evaluated counts, v2 part caps (AK-10a)
body:
## AK-10a: triangle budgets from evaluated counts, and v2 part caps

**Stacked on #946 (AK-D2) → #945 (AK-D1).** Review the top commit only.

**What.**
- `evaluateRecipe(...).triangles` now reports what three.js builds for each shape: box 12, rounded box **300** (it was charged 588), cylinder 96, cone **48** (charged 96), ellipsoid 720. The counts come from `shapeTriangles()`, an analytic function that matches the renderer's generators exactly.
- **v1 is gated by the old charges.** No v1 recipe is newly accepted or newly rejected, and a v1 recipe still can't carry more than 16 parts or 24 shapes per part. The error message for those cases now says "…requires recipe version 2".
- **v2 is gated by the real counts,** with `RECIPE_V2_LIMITS = { parts: 64, partShapes: 512, shapes: 512 }` in place of 16 × 24 and 256 expanded shapes.
- These limits are unchanged: the 100k-triangle budget, the 128 KiB byte cap, the 12,000-value structural budget, and the motion and light caps.
- `RECIPE_LIMITS` is untouched on purpose, because Studio's v12 prompt embeds it.

**Why.** The trial's real kitchen run (E3) failed the recipe caps twice before it could be written at all. The first attempt failed with `<=24` shapes and `<=16` parts. The second, repacked, failed with 323 > 256 expanded shapes. The only way to fit the caps was to merge the 185 backsplash tiles into one box. The rounded-box charge also capped a design at 170 rounded boxes, not ~333.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, `core/src/procedural-items/budget.test.ts` failed 5 of 5 tests (`scratch/AK-CORE/10a-failing-before.txt`).

**Proof.**
- **E3, direct converter output, tiles unmerged** (`scratch/AK-CORE/proofs/10a-e3.out`, from `trial/out/E3-recipe-direct.recipe.json`):
  - v1: refused, "More than 16 parts requires recipe version 2".
  - v2: **valid**, with 26 parts, 185 shapes in one part and 323 shapes. The sweep passes 23/23, and evaluated triangles equal built triangles: **3,876 = 3,876**, in 6 batches.
  - Its size is 37,946 bytes and 4,056 structural values.
- **Parity test** (nodes `geometry.test.ts`): `evaluation.triangles === buildProceduralGeometry().triangles` on all 9 core fixtures, the shelf, the bed, and a v2 design that uses every primitive, including a cone.
- `bun test src` (core): 2997 pass, 0 fail. `bun test src/procedural-item` (nodes): 49 pass, 0 fail. `bun run check`: clean.
- **Cost at the new ceiling.** Timing on this machine is unreliable right now (load average 27; a SwiftShader harness is running). An interleaved old/new run on 256 boxes shows no measurable regression, 2.4–3.6 ms against 2.6–9 ms, all of it noise. Evaluation is linear in expanded shapes, so the 512 ceiling doubles today's worst case per node parse. I will re-measure on a quiet machine before merge.

**House effect:** no change. The /next scenes have no `procedural-item` nodes.

**R7 caveat.** The E3 recipe is 37.9 KB, above R7's 24 KiB inline threshold. It still fits the 128 KiB byte cap and a 64 KiB hosted create, but a hosted *recipe edit* carries both `from` and `to`, so it would exceed 64 KiB. Parameter and slot edits are fine. Until AK-01/P-05 stores large designs by hash, converters should keep designs this large inline only for creates.

**Reader-first.** Studio's v12 prompt keeps writing v1 against `RECIPE_LIMITS`. Converters write v2 only after this release ships.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | No API change. `shapeTriangles` and `RECIPE_V2_LIMITS` are additive exports |
| R2 | Evaluation stays context-free. The worst case per node rises from 256 to 512 shapes (see Cost) |
| R7 | Byte cap unchanged. The E3 proof is above the 24 KiB threshold (see caveat) |
| R8 | No tool yet. AK-02's `validate_design` can report `evaluation.triangles` as the real count |
| R3–R6, R9 | Not touched |

**For Wassim and the owner:**
1. **AD-10 is the owner's call:** the new ceilings, 64 parts / 512 per part / 512 expanded. The PROPOSAL suggested 2,048 expanded; I kept 512 to protect per-op parse cost.
2. For Wassim: whether to gate v1 with the legacy charges (as here, for the safest rollback) or with the real counts. v1 recipes with 171–333 rounded boxes would then become valid, and an older reader would refuse them.

title: feat(procedural-items): design schema resource and read-only validate_design (AK-02 1/3)
body:
<!-- AK-02 1/3 (AK-TOOLS) PR body: editor validate_design -->
**Merge as one unit (coordinator ruling on the Codex R8 finding):** #948, #953 and the private AK-02 3/3 PR (chat tools and scene programs) merge the same day, so there is no window where MCP has design tools that chat and programs lack. The owner's AD-6 exception covers today's surfaces.

## What

Agents can now read the design contract and check a design before anything touches a scene. Nothing is written.

- **Core** (`@pascal-app/core/procedural-items`):
  - `describeDesignSchema()` returns the JSON Schema, `RECIPE_LIMITS`, the rules JSON Schema cannot express, and one valid example.
    - The schema is generated from `RecipeSchema` with `z.toJSONSchema`. The node's `recipe` field is an opaque `z.custom`, so generating from the node would give an empty schema.
    - It is about 7.3 KB, with one named recursive `$def` (`Expr`).
  - `validateDesign(design, { parameters? })` takes an object or a JSON string and never throws. It returns:
    - `valid`;
    - coded diagnostics with paths: `invalid_json`, `schema`, `rule`, `parameters`, `sweep`, plus the warnings `floating_component`, `unbalanced` and `behind_wall` (a wall-side design whose geometry passes behind the wall reference; Bugbot finding, fixed in 37b655b47). Rule and sweep errors carry a `hint` built from the submitted design (8a3788e91), after the AK-02 eval showed agents looping on bare rule messages: valid placements went from 1/6 to 6/6 runs;
    - the parameter-sweep result;
    - `measurements`: bounds, per-part bounds, instances and triangles, the triangles the renderer really builds next to the charged budget, draw groups per slot and motion group, datum contact and balance (floor at y = 0, the wall-side reference plane, or the ceiling reference), and connected components with their gaps.
  - Its output schema (`DesignValidationSchema`) lives next to it.
- **MCP**:
  - the resource `pascal://schema/design`;
  - the read-only tool `validate_design`, which wraps `validateDesign` unchanged;
  - a "Custom Designs" section in the agent guide;
  - the annotation inventory goes from 49 to 50 tools (policy map, justification packet, publishing case, validators).


**Codex review fixes** (failing cases 7ce90f5bc, fixes eaf8c7cec): datum contact now needs the shape to reach the plane, so geometry behind a wall no longer touches it; a `draw_budget` warning fires above 16 draw calls per instance; balance weighs tapered cylinders as frusta; `PRIMITIVE_TESSELLATION` and `shapeTriangles(primitive, topScale)` live in core's recipe module, and the nodes renderer builds with them (same signature as #947's `shapeTriangles`, so the two PRs meet on one function; whichever lands second takes the other's). The publishing evidence carries the date and suite it was checked with. The behind-wall and hint commits predate this process and have their tests in the same commit.

## Why

Owner decision **AD-6**: agent design tools ship now on today's surfaces, read-only and validate first.

**This is an explicit, owner-approved exception to charter R8**, which otherwise waits for the unified tool kernel (P-04). To keep the cost of re-hosting low, the work is kernel-shaped: one core function per capability (`describeDesignSchema`, `validateDesign`) with a zod output schema. MCP only adds transport, and P-04 can re-host the same functions. The chat lanes and scene programs wrap the same functions in the private PR (AK-02 3/3).

Failing case before this PR: agents had no way to discover or check a design.
- `resources/read pascal://schema/design` returns "resource not found".
- `tools/call validate_design` returns "tool not found".
- `apply_patch.node` is `record<string, unknown>`, and there were 0 procedural hits in `packages/mcp/src`.

## Proof

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun test src/procedural-items/design.test.ts` (core) | 17 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test src` (core) | 2995 pass, 0 fail (1 run of 4 hit one unnamed timing flake under load; not reproducible) |
| `bun test` (mcp) | 385 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test` (nodes) | 3505 tests, 0 fail, 1 skip |
| `bun test scripts/openai-tool-annotation-policy.test.ts`, `bun run skills:validate` | 5 pass; 69 pass |
| `bun run check` | clean (6 pre-existing infos) |
| `bun run check-types` | 10 of 11 tasks pass. `editor#check-types` (apps/editor) fails locally only because the GitHub dependency `@webxr/plugin` is not installed in this checkout. It is unrelated, and CI installs it |

The tests use the asset-kernel trial recipes, committed as fixtures under `__fixtures__/trial-*.json` with neutral names:
- E1 condenser, E2 air handler and E5 louver validate with no diagnostics. Their triangles (4032 / 7200 / 252), draw groups (5 / 4 / 1), expanded shapes and dimensions match the trial's real builds.
- The E8 stair guard fails its sweep in 15 of 29 cases with "below the ground", the same as in the trial.
- A nodes test pins `shapeTriangles` and the draw groups to `buildProceduralGeometry` for 11 recipes, including a cone.
- Floating-part detection flags real defects in existing library fixtures:
  - the chandelier's 6 bulbs sit 0.375 m from anything;
  - the cabinet's door handles are 7.5 mm off their panels;
  - the desk fan's blades are separated from each other.
- Cost: 25–35 ms for 139–256 shapes, most of it the existing sweep.

**House effect:** no change. The tool is read-only and agent-facing. The only runtime edit is extracting `shapeBounds` in `recipe.ts`, which gives the same bounds (all procedural tests pass), so no geometry, bake or scene output can change and no bench rerun is needed.

## Eval (AK-02 3/3, cap-design-louver)

**Latest run** (2026-09-28, on the review-fix heads #948 `eaf8c7cec` / #953 `96b80a3b6`, prompt with "place exactly one vent", MCP lane with `read_resource` and prompt `mcp-lane-v2`; records `bench/ai-chat/runs/eval-2026-09-28T04-35-16-586Z` direct, `…T04-44-47-852Z` mcp):

| mcp | **0/3** | 2/3 | Every run read `pascal://schema/design` first and placed within 27–87 s, but both placed louvers are 0.45–0.48 m deep instead of ~0.08 m; the third run never placed |

Net: the design tools work end to end on both lanes. Duplicate placement in chat and depth control via MCP are prompt and task findings for a follow-up, not tool defects.

| R1 | API v1 and node schemas unchanged; additive exports only |
| R3 | No writer: read-only tool and resource; no reference changes |
| R5 | Design validation reaches MCP now; chat and scene programs follow in AK-02 3/3 over the same functions |

title: feat(procedural-items): select, bool and choice parameters, and when (AK-10b)
body:
## AK-10b: select, bool and choice parameters, and `when`

**Stacked on #947 (AK-10a) → #946 → #945.** Review the top commit only.

**What.** Three additions, all v2-only. A v1 recipe that uses any of them gets "…requires recipe version 2".

- **`{ op: 'select', args: [i, v0, …, vn-1] }`**, a per-index table. It returns `v_i` for an integral `i` in `[0, n)`, and anything else is an error. Only the chosen branch is evaluated, so an unused branch can't fail. It takes up to 64 values, matching the repeat cap.
- **`unit: 'bool'` and `unit: 'choice'` parameters.**
  - bool: `min 0, max 1, step 1`, integral default.
  - choice: `options: string[]` (2–16 labels), with `max = options.length - 1`.
  - Neither can bind a handle axis. Instances must hold integral values.
- **`when: Expr` on parts and shapes.** A repeat or shape is built only where `when` evaluates to nonzero. A skipped repeat drops its named surfaces too, and the existing node check already refuses to drop a surface that hosts a child.
- **Inspector:** a bool parameter renders as a toggle, and a choice of up to 4 options as a segmented control. Larger choices fall back to a slider labelled with the option name.

**Why.** Trial blocker 3: E7's five different cord drops could only be written as `Σ drop_k · max(0, 1 − |index − k|)`, which took 5 parameters and about 60 expression nodes. The audit (limit #13) also found no way to express hinge side, "with drawers" or style options.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, `core/src/procedural-items/options.test.ts` failed 6 of 6 tests (`scratch/AK-CORE/10b-failing-before.txt`).

**Proof.**
- The trial's own E7 recipe with `select` (`scratch/AK-CORE/proofs/10b-e7.out`) evaluates identically: same shapes and lights.
  - The drop expression shrinks from 686 to **77 bytes**, and the whole recipe from 7,282 to **3,628 bytes** (943 → 379 structural values).
  - The sweep passes 33/33.
- Tests cover:
  - a "With drawer" toggle on the cabinet fixture: the drawer's shapes and motion disappear, and motion ids are unchanged when it is on;
  - a 3-option choice that picks a shape and a size;
  - alternate shelf repeats skipped, with the surviving surface IDs kept stable;
  - validation and v1 gates.
- `bun test src` (core): 3003 pass, 0 fail. `bun test src/procedural-item` (nodes): 49 pass, 0 fail.
- `turbo check-types` for core, nodes and editor: 4/4 pass. `bun run check`: clean.

**House effect:** no change. There are no `procedural-item` nodes on /next.

**Reader-first.** Studio's prompt v12 still documents only the v1 ops and units. It gains `select`, bool/choice and `when` one release after this one ships.

**Bugbot fix** (second commit): a repeat whose shapes are all skipped by `when` now builds no light, instead of failing the light-bounds check. Tested with the pendant fixture.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | Additive schema. The `Expr` type gains a `select` member, so TS consumers that exhaustively switch on `op` get a compile error. Studio's normaliser only lower-cases `op` |
| R2 | `select` evaluation is lazy. `when` costs one expression per repeat or shape |
| R5 | Toggle and segmented controls go through the same `change()` path, validation and undo as sliders |
| R6 | A part skipped by `when` has no motion group. Kept parts keep the same group ids and clip names |
| R8 | No tool yet. These show up in AK-02's schema resource |
| R3, R4, R7, R9 | Not touched |

**Local preview:** only visible for v2 designs, which nothing writes yet. The inspector toggle and segmented control are in the batch preview card `previews/AK-10b.md`.

**For Wassim to review:**
1. `select` versus a comparison op (`eq`). I kept one op; choices use `select(style, …)`.
2. `when` semantics for repeats: evaluated per index, and a skipped repeat keeps later repeats' indices, so IDs stay stable.
3. The inspector controls.

## Local preview
Shared setup for the whole stack: `previews/AK.md` (`preview.sh start AK-PV previews/AK/ak-after.json` serves on :3301).
Setup is in `previews/AK.md`.

### What you will notice
- The **Side table with options** (front-left corner) shows a **With drawer** toggle and a **Legs: Square / Tapered** segmented control in its panel, instead of sliders.

### Try this
1. Select the side table. Turn **With drawer** off. Expected: the drawer and its pull disappear, and E on the table does nothing. Turn it back on and the drawer returns.
2. Switch Legs to **Tapered**. Expected: the four square legs become tapered round legs.
3. Undo each change. Expected: one undo step per change.

**Checked by me:** the static renders at the listed poses (captured from :3100 and :3301). I did not click through the interactive steps in a browser; unit tests cover them.

### Known limits
- Choices with more than 4 options still use a slider, labelled with the option name.
- `select` and `when` have no Studio UI yet; Studio does not write them.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core recipe parsing and evaluation (geometry, motion, lights, surfaces); editor parameter UI is extended but uses the same validation path as sliders.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **recipe version 2** capabilities for procedural items: per-index **`select`** expressions, **`bool` / `choice`** parameters, and optional **`when`** on parts and shapes. All of these require `version: 2`; v1 recipes that use them fail validation.
> 
> **`select`** picks one branch by integral index and evaluates only that branch (lazy), replacing encodings like delta-sums for per-repeat values. **`when`** skips whole repeats or individual shapes when the expression is zero; skipped repeats do not emit surfaces, motion groups, or lights, and gated motion keeps stable group IDs. **`bool`** and **`choice`** parameters are validated (integral 0/1 or option index) and drive recipes via `when` / `select`.

>

title: feat(procedural-items): cylinder segments, open, inner and arc (AK-03a)
body:
## AK-03a: cylinder segments, open, inner and arc

**Stacked on #949 (AK-10b) → #947 → #946 → #945.** Review the top commit only. This is part 1 of AK-03 (profile shapes). Extrude (03b) and revolve (03c) follow.

**What.** v2 cylinders take four new fields:

| Field | Meaning | When absent |
|---|---|---|
| `segments` | 3–64 sides | 24 sides, as today |
| `open` | no end caps; the wall draws both faces | caps drawn |
| `inner` | a hollow wall; the inner radius as a fraction of the outer, in (0, 1) | solid |
| `arc` | a partial sweep in radians, (0, 2π], from local +Z toward +X; closed by flat wedge sides unless `open` | full circle |

- All four are v2-only and cylinder-only. `inner` and `arc` cannot sit on a support shape. The evaluated shape carries a field only when it was set, so v1 evaluations are unchanged.
- **Builder** (`nodes/procedural-item/geometry.ts`, `cylinderSource`):
  - With no options, it is still exactly `new CylinderGeometry(top, 0.5, 1, 24, 1)`.
  - Otherwise it builds an open or closed `CylinderGeometry` with `thetaLength`, then adds a flipped inner wall, ring caps and wedge sides.
- **Open solids are two-sided.** Materials are front-sided because WebGPU MRT forces `DoubleSide` to `FrontSide`, so an open cylinder without `inner` also draws the back of its wall (second commit).
- **Triangles are analytic.** `shapeTriangles(shape)` returns `walls·n·ends + caps + 4 wedge triangles`, where:
  - `ends` is 1 for a cone and 2 otherwise;
  - `walls` is 2 for a tube or an open solid, and 1 otherwise;
  - the caps are rings for a tube.

  A test checks each shape's built triangle count against it.

title: feat(procedural-items): extrude shapes with F1 sections, holes and bevel (AK-03b)
body:
## AK-03b: extrude shapes with F1 sections, holes and bevel

**Stacked on #950 (AK-03a) → … → #945.** Review the top commit only. This is part 2 of AK-03.

**What.** A v2 `extrude` shape: `{ primitive: 'extrude', section, length, bevel?, position, rotation?, slot }`.

- **`section`** is an F1 `SectionProfile` whose numbers may be expressions:
  - `rectangle { width, depth, corner? }`;
  - `round { radius, wall? }`;
  - `oval { width, depth }`;
  - `polygon { outer, holes? }`, with 3–64 points per ring and up to 16 holes.

  Evaluation resolves it to the frozen numeric **`ResolvedSectionProfile`**, so no `ref` is allowed and recipes stay self-contained, as the CHALLENGE required.
- **Geometry.** The section lies in local x/y and is extruded along local z over `length`, centred. The evaluated shape is re-centred in its box, which gives three things:
  - bounds, handles, the base shift, cut checks and surfaces keep reading every shape as an oriented box;
  - `size` is derived;
  - `section` is carried on the evaluation.
- **`core/procedural-items/section.ts`** holds two helpers:
  - `sectionRings(profile)`: turns a resolved section into rings. Rounds and ovals use 24 sides, rounded corners use 4 segments per quarter, repeated points are dropped, a ring needs an area, and holes must sit inside the outline. **This is the seam for B-05's sweep**, which will consume the same rings along a path. Sweep is not in this PR.
  - `extrusionTriangles()`: analytic. Earcut caps give `V + 2H − 2` triangles each, and the side walls give 2 per edge per layer. The count is exact for rings without collinear points and an upper bound otherwise.
- **Builder.** three's `ExtrudeGeometry` (MIT, already bundled). A bevel uses `bevelOffset = −bevel`, so the outline shrinks and bevels back out and the box never grows. Bevel is at most min(length, width, depth)/4 and at most 5 cm.
- **Other rules.** `extrude` is v2-only and takes no `size`. Every other primitive now needs `size`; the schema made it optional only so `extrude` can omit it. An extrude cannot be a support shape.

**Why.** Audit limit #1. On /next, 525 elements (7.3 %) need extrusion: fascia and soffits (45/84), stair stringers and nosings (40/101), louvers (39/143), countertops and mouldings. It is also stage 1 of holes (limit #3): counters with a sink cut-out, grilles, frames.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, `core/src/procedural-items/extrude.test.ts` failed 5 of 5 tests (`scratch/AK-CORE/03b-failing-before.txt`).

**Proof.**
- **E6 fascia return** (trial element `cabana-roof-east-end-closure`). The sloped-top return was a box; now it is a polygon extrude of its four measured corners. Scored with the trial's `compare.py` against the /next source mesh, inside the return's box (`scratch/AK-CORE/trial-proof/e6-return.out`):

  | Return | R@2 | P@2 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Box (before) | 0.952 | 0.930 |
  | Extrude (after) | **1.000** | **1.000** |

  Both have 48 triangles. Over the whole element, R@2 goes from 0.9995 to 0.9998 (the return is small next to the cap).
- **Parity and fit.** nodes `geometry.test.ts` covers rectangle, rounded rectangle, fully rounded ends, round, round tube, oval, a countertop with a sink hole, and both of those with a bevel. For each, the built triangles equal `shapeTriangles`, and the built bounding box equals the evaluated box to 1e-5.
- **Expressions and pose.** Core tests confirm that a `width` parameter moves polygon vertices and that the re-centred position is correct.
- `bun test src` (core): 3012 pass. `bun test src/procedural-item` (nodes): 52 pass. `turbo check-types` for core, nodes and editor: pass. `bun run check`: clean.

**House effect:** no change. The /next scenes have no `procedural-item` nodes; the E6 gain lands when converters write v2.

**R7 size note.** Each polygon vertex costs 2 values of the 12,000-value structural budget. A 64-point ring with 16 holes of 64 points is about 2,200 values. Hole *patterns* such as grilles should use a repeated part with a `count` rather than listing many holes (CHALLENGE AK-03 fix).

**Bugbot fix** (second commit): a bevel is now capped by the section's **thinnest wall**, not only by its box. The thinnest wall is the least distance from a vertex to any edge it does not touch, across the outline and holes; `bevel ≤ wall / 2.5`, and a bevelled section may have at most 256 points. Tested on the counter (its slot is 5 mm from the edge, so 2 mm is OK and 2.5 mm is refused) and on an L-section.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | Additive. `size` is optional in the TS type only because extrude omits it; every other primitive still requires it at parse |
| R2 | ExtrudeGeometry runs once per (recipe, params) and is cached, at 0.25–2.7 ms per generator (CHALLENGE lpb bench) |
| R5 | Oriented-box invariant, so handles, bounds, paint and surfaces are unchanged. No support surfaces on extrusions |
| R7 | Sections are inline and resolved (no `ref`) |
| R3, R4, R6, R8, R9 | Not touched |

## Local preview
Shared setup for the whole stack: `previews/AK.md` (`preview.sh start AK-PV previews/AK/ak-after.json` serves on :3301).
Setup is in `previews/AK.md`.

### What you will notice
- The counter's stone top is an extruded section with a round **sink cut-out** and a 3 mm bevelled edge. Before, it was a plain slab.

### Where to look
Pose `3-counter-cylinders`, the counter on the left.

### Before / after
`previews/AK/before-3-counter-cylinders.png` / `after-3-counter-cylinders.png`.

**Checked by me:** the static renders at the listed poses (captured from :3100 and :3301). I did not click through the interactive steps in a browser; unit tests cover them.

### Known limits
- The bevel may be at most 2/5 of the section's thinnest wall.
- Sweep along a path is deferred to B-05.

**For Wassim to review:**
1. The `section` field name (F1's own), with `length` rather than `depth`, which collides with F1 `rectangle.depth`.
2. The re-centring invariant for profile shapes.
3. The polygonisation constants (24 sides for rounds, 4 segments per rounded corner).

> Touches recipe schema, evaluation, and mesh generation with new validation paths; v2-only and additive, but incorrect section/bevel rules could reject valid designs or mis-size bounds.

> **Overview**
> Adds a **version-2-only** `extrude` shape to procedural recipes: `{ primitive: 'extrude', section, length, bevel?, … }` instead of `size`. Recipe shapes are now a **discriminated union** on `primitive` (`solidShape` vs `extrudeShape`), with `solidFields()` so existing box/cylinder validation stays on sized primitives only.
> 
> **Core evaluation** resolves expression-driven F1 sections (rectangle, round, oval, polygon with holes, structural I/C/L/T/Z/rect-tube), builds rings via new **`section.ts`** (`sectionRings`, `extrusionTriangles`, `sectionThickness`), derives **`size` and re-centred `position`** from section bounds so extrusions still behave like oriented boxes for bounds/handles. Bevel is capped by length, 5 cm, and **thinnest wall / 2.5**. Polygon validation rejects crossing edges, nested holes, and invalid structural webs.
>

>

<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

## Codex review round (rev-951-a)

Failing test first: `test(... AK-03b, failing)`, then the fix.
- R1 public API: shapes are a discriminated union on `primitive`. Non-extrude shapes keep a required `size`. v1 key order is kept so parsed v1 recipes serialize byte for byte (there is a byte-pin test).
- UVs are face-frame and world-scale on extrude caps and walls.
- Section checks reject hole edges that cross the outer ring or each other. Sections allow at most 256 points.
- Structural sections (I, C, L, T, Z, rect-tube) are validated.
- A bevel is capped by the thinnest wall.

## Required change in the private bump PR

When private-editor bumps the `editor/` pin past this PR, fix `packages/ai/src/studio/procedural-normalize.ts` (~lines 199–212) in that same bump PR, or the private typecheck fails.

- The rounding clamp reads `shape.radius` and `shape.size`, then assigns `.radius` on the probe shape and on `target`.
- `RecipeShape` is now a union: extrude shapes (this PR) and revolve shapes (#952) have neither `radius` nor `size`.
- Fix: skip any shape whose `primitive` is `'extrude'` or `'revolve'` before the clamp. Those shapes can't carry rounding anyway.

title: feat(procedural-items): revolve shapes (AK-03c)
body:
## AK-03c: revolve shapes

**Stacked on #951 (AK-03b) → … → #945.** Review the top commit only. This is part 3 of AK-03; sweep is deferred to B-05 (see Seam).

**What.** A v2 `revolve` shape: `{ primitive: 'revolve', profile: [[radius, height], …], segments?, arc?, position, rotation?, slot }`.

- **Profile.** 2–64 points, and each coordinate may be an expression. The profile turns about local Y, starting from +Z toward +X like the cylinder. `segments` (default 24) and `arc` (default 2π) are the cylinder fields.
- **Closed or open.**
  - The shape is a **closed solid** when the profile meets the axis at both ends over a full turn. The builder orients the profile so the solid's normals face outward.
  - Otherwise it is an **open surface**, such as a lamp shade, and it also draws its back face. Materials are front-sided because WebGPU MRT forces `DoubleSide` to `FrontSide`.
  - The same rule is added to #950: an open solid cylinder now draws both wall faces (separate commit on that branch).
- **Evaluation.**
  - Points that collapse onto the previous one are dropped, so a `select`-driven feature can shrink to zero length.
  - The profile is re-centred vertically in its box, which keeps the oriented-box invariant.
  - `revolveIsClosed()` is exported for the builder and the tests.
- **Triangles are analytic:** `2 · segments · (points − 1)`, doubled for open surfaces, which matches `LatheGeometry`'s index.

**Why.** Audit limit #1: +3.5 % of /next (256 elements) needs lathe: pool details, openings, devices, pendants, balusters. It is also trial blocker 6: an ellipsoid only approximates E7's bell shade, and E8's turned balusters had to be boxes.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, `core/src/procedural-items/revolve.test.ts` failed 5 of 5 tests (`scratch/AK-CORE/03c-failing-before.txt`).

**Proof.** The trial's own recipes are built with this builder and scored with the trial's `compare.py` against the /next source meshes (`scratch/AK-CORE/proofs/e7-e8.out`, `e8-balusters.out`).

| Element | Candidate | R@2 mm | R@5 mm | R@2 cm | P@2 cm | Triangles |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **E7 five-drop pendant** (whole element) | ellipsoid shades (before) | 0.444 | 0.689 | 0.895 | 0.914 | 8,172 |
| | **revolved measured bell** | **0.795** | **1.000** | **1.000** | **1.000** | 7,932 |
| **E8 turned balusters** (baluster region) | boxes (before) | 0.190 | 0.287 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 192 |
| | **revolve, 12 segments** | **0.434** | **0.775** | 1.00 | 1.00 | 4,932 |

- **E8 authoring.** Each baluster is one revolve: a foot, two beads and the shaft. Each baluster's foot, bead offsets and length come from `select(index, …)` over values read from the source occurrences (`e8-baluster-params.json`), the way a converter would read them. At 2 cm both E8 candidates are already perfect, so the gain shows only at 2–5 mm.
- **Tests.**
  - nodes `geometry.test.ts`: closed baluster, reversed baluster, open shade, half-turn shade, quarter-turn solid. Built triangles equal the evaluated count, the height matches the box, and every side-wall normal on a closed solid points outward.
  - core: box and centring, open versus closed counts, expression points, collapse, validation.
- `bun test src` (core): 3017 pass. `bun test src/procedural-item` (nodes): 53 pass. `turbo check-types` for core, nodes and editor: pass. `bun run check`: clean.

**Seam for B-05 (sweep, deferred).** `core/procedural-items/section.ts` (#951) turns any resolved F1 section into rings. A future `sweep` shape takes `{ section, path: [Vec3], ends?: [SweepEndSpec, SweepEndSpec] }`, evaluates the section exactly as `extrude` does, and emits the same rings along the path. Its triangle count follows from `rings × path edges`. Nothing in this PR constrains that shape.

**House effect:** no change. The /next scenes have no `procedural-item` nodes; the E7 and E8 gains land when converters write v2.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | Additive primitive. `segments` and `arc` now also apply to revolve |
| R2 | `LatheGeometry` runs once per (recipe, params) and is cached (0.25 ms at 64×40, CHALLENGE lpb) |
| R5 | Oriented-box invariant, so handles, bounds, paint and surfaces are unchanged |
| R3, R4, R6–R9 | Not touched |

## Local preview
Shared setup for the whole stack: `previews/AK.md` (`preview.sh start AK-PV previews/AK/ak-after.json` serves on :3301).
Setup is in `previews/AK.md`.

### What you will notice
- The **balusters** are turned, with a foot, two beads and a shaft. Before, they were square boxes.
- The **pendant** shades are bell shapes revolved from the measured /next profile. Before, they were ellipsoids.
- The counter's steel **basin** is revolved.

### Where to look
Pose `5-balusters`; poses `1-overview` and `2-ceiling` for the pendant.

### Before / after
`previews/AK/before-5-balusters.png` / `after-5-balusters.png`, and `before-1-overview.png` / `after-1-overview.png`.

**Checked by me:** the static renders at the listed poses (captured from :3100 and :3301). I did not click through the interactive steps in a browser; unit tests cover them.

### Known limits
- A revolve that does not close on its axis draws both faces; materials are front-sided.

**For Wassim to review:**
1. The closed-versus-open rule and back faces.
2. Dropping coincident points rather than refusing them.
3. `[radius, height]` point order: radius first, like three's `Vector2(x = r, y)`.

title: feat(mcp): place_design creates a validated design on today's hosts (AK-02 2/3)
body:
<!-- AK-02 2/3 (AK-TOOLS) PR body: editor place_design -->
**Merge as one unit (coordinator ruling on the Codex R8 finding):** #948, #953 and the private AK-02 3/3 PR (chat tools and scene programs) merge the same day, so there is no window where MCP has design tools that chat and programs lack. The owner's AD-6 exception covers today's surfaces.

**Stacked on #948 (AK-02 1/3).** Until #948 merges, this diff also shows its commit; the change here is commits dde17bfe7, 20363052b and 30de13679 (rebased onto editor main with #938 merged, 5e7e128cf), plus the review fixes.

## What

Agents can now create a design they validated on today's hosts, with typed refusals.

- **Core**: `planDesignPlacement(nodes, request)`.
  1. It validates the design with `validateDesign`, the same authority as `validate_design`. The design can be an object or a JSON string.
  2. It picks the host from the design's `mounting`, using today's hosting fields only:
     - floor designs go on a level, or on a slab or zone of it (the level becomes the parent). They can also go on a named surface of a placed design (`attachments[childId] = surfaceId`);
     - wall-side designs go on a straight wall face (`wallId`/`side`, with position = along, height and offset of the reference);
     - ceiling designs go under a ceiling (plan x/z).
  3. It builds the node and runs `validateProceduralRelations` directly. The mount checks therefore hold without the node registry: before this, the trial saw ceiling and wall designs accepted as level children when `builtinPlugin` was not loaded.
  4. It returns `{ node, parentId, hostUpdate? }` or throws `DesignPlacementError`. The codes are `invalid_design` (with diagnostics), `invalid_placement`, `host_not_found`, `wrong_host`, `unknown_surface` and `does_not_fit`, plus the apply_patch guard codes. A wall misfit says where the reference fits, for example "fits along 0.317–3.683 m and at height 0.47–2.23 m on this wall".
- **MCP**: `place_design` wraps it and only creates.
  - The node, plus the host's attachment update for a surface, goes through `applyPatch`.
  - A refusal is a tool error whose JSON text is `{ code, message, diagnostics? }`; the message starts with the code.
  - It adds one line to the agent guide and one README row. The annotation inventory goes from 50 to 51 tools (additive).


**Codex review fixes** (failing cases in the commit before 96b80a3b6): `SceneBridge.applyPatch` commits a whole patch as one history step, so a design-surface placement undoes in one step; designs above 24 KiB are refused with `design_too_large` (R7, as #947); an explicit existing id is refused with `node_exists` before the surface host's shadow graph is built. The known limit about two undo steps no longer applies.

## Why

Owner decision **AD-6**: agent design tools ship now on today's surfaces. **This is an explicit, owner-approved exception to charter R8**, which otherwise waits for the P-04 tool kernel. It is kernel-shaped: one core function, and the MCP adapter adds only transport. Following the CHALLENGE correction, it uses v1 inline recipes and today's hosting fields; pin and `Mount` arguments wait for AK-01/P-05 and the Mount decision.

**Create-only goes through #938's patch guards.** `place_design` runs `assertPatchKeepsIdentity` over its create (and a surface host's attachment update) before `applyPatch`, so an explicit existing `id` is refused with apply_patch's own `node_exists` code and message; `planDesignPlacement` no longer carries its own check (30de13679). Refusals are tool errors with JSON `{ code, message, diagnostics? }`, like apply_patch's, because an McpError keeps only its message.

Failing case before this PR: no tool placed a design.
- `tools/call place_design` returns "tool not found".
- Through `apply_patch`, an agent had to hand-write the node, and without `builtinPlugin` a wall-side or ceiling design was accepted as a level child (trial.md, "mount relations are enforced only when the process has loaded builtinPlugin").

## Proof

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun test src/procedural-items/design-placement.test.ts` (core) | 18 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test src` (core) | 3012 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test` (mcp) | 388 pass, 0 fail |
| `bun test scripts/openai-tool-annotation-policy.test.ts`, `bun run skills:validate` | 5 pass; 69 pass |
| `bun run check`, core `check-types`, mcp `tsgo --noEmit` | clean (6 pre-existing infos) |

The tests use the trial fixtures:
- the E5 louver on both faces of a wall, and refused when too high, with the fit range;
- the E2 air handler under a ceiling, and refused outside its polygon;
- the example table on a level and on a slab, then a vase on its support surface: the attachment is written, an overlapping second vase is refused, and an unknown surface lists the valid ones;
- 11 refusal cases, each asserting the code prefix, plus node refusals that name the field (`invalid_placement: node: Unknown slot paint`);

title: feat(procedural-items): part trees and joints evaluate to nested motions (AK-04a)
body:
## AK-04a: part trees and joints evaluate to nested motions

**Stacked on #952 (AK-03c) → … → #945.** Review the top commit only. This is part 1 of AK-04. **Ship it with AK-04b** (render, bake, controls), which is the next PR and draws what this one evaluates.

**What (v2 only).**
- **`parts[].parent`**: the part moves with its parent part. The child must repeat exactly as often as its parent: both once, or equal counts bound by index. Chains are acyclic and at most 8 deep. A skipped parent repeat skips its children.
- **`parts[].frame { position, rotation? }`**: the part's shapes, light and joint are authored in this frame, which is relative to the parent.
- **`joints[]`**: `{ child, kind: fixed | revolute | continuous | prismatic, origin, axis (any vector), open?, rest?, range?, speed?, delay?, duration?, easing? }`, at most one per part.
  - **Id and kinds.** The joint id **is** the child part id. revolute, prismatic and continuous map to `hinge`, `slide` and `spin`. Values are radians, metres, or radians per second for `speed`, with #930's limits and timing rules.
  - **Rest pose.** `rest` is baked into the evaluated shapes, and the motion amount is `open − rest`.
- **Same motion records as flat motion.** Joints evaluate to the same `EvaluatedMotion` records as flat `part.motion`. Group ids stay `${part}` / `${part}~i` and kinds stay hinge/slide/spin, so the controller, clip names and baked extras keep their contract. Three optional fields are added:
  - `parent`: the group this one rides in;
  - `direction`: only for off-principal axes; `axis` stays the nearest letter;
  - `range`: relative to rest.
- **Equivalence (tested):** a root joint on a principal axis compiles to **exactly** the flat motion it replaces. The shapes and motions are identical to the cabinet fixture's flat drawer.
- **`part.motion` stays a valid, permanent input.** On one part it excludes a joint, and it stays outside part trees. Nothing is migrated.
- **Motion envelopes for joints** use per-joint interval bounds. Each group's box grows by its children's reach, then is swept over its own travel and range: exact arc extremes of the box corners for hinges and spins, the segment for slides. There is no product sampling. Floor, wall and ceiling rules are unchanged. Flat motions keep today's sampling byte for byte.
- **Math.** `spatial.ts` gains poses, Euler↔matrix (three's XYZ convention, round-trip tested) and swept-arc bounds.

**Why.** Audit limit #11 and AK-04. Articraft has nested movable chains in 51.9 % of 9,996 records. Doors with knobs, drawers with pulls and off-axis hinges could not be expressed.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, `core/src/procedural-items/joints.test.ts` failed 6 of 6 tests (`scratch/AK-CORE/04a-failing-before.txt`).

**Proof.**
- core `joints.test.ts` covers:
  - two nested chains (door → knob, drawer → pull): groups, parents, pivots, kinds, and the controller's per-part timeline;
  - principal-axis equivalence;
  - off-axis `direction`;
  - `rest`: an ajar door carrying its knob;
  - index-bound repeats: `knob~1` rides `door~1`;
  - envelopes: a bail pull swinging through the floor is refused, and one stopping at horizontal is accepted;
  - 10 validation cases.
- `bun test src` (core): 3023 pass, 0 fail. nodes procedural tests: 53 pass. `turbo check-types` for core, nodes and editor: pass. `bun run check`: clean.

**House effect:** no change. There are no `procedural-item` nodes on /next.

**Follow-up commit:** a jointed part of a recessed design may move inside its ceiling cut. The joint reach box is tested against the cut, matching #946's rule for flat motion.

**Bugbot fix** (later commit): a joint's `range` flips with the stored amount when its axis is negative. Tests: the stored range, and a flipped range that swings a pull through the floor, which is refused.

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | Additive: optional schema sections and optional `EvaluatedMotion` fields. `ProceduralMotionController` is unchanged and exported |
| R2 | Evaluation stays context-free: O(joints × depth) poses plus one box sweep per group. No sampling products |
| R6 | Joint id = child part id. Clip names, group ids, kinds and extras are unchanged. The rest pose is baked into shapes |
| R7 | Inline recipe, no zod defaults, v1 byte-identical |
| R3, R4, R5, R8, R9 | Not touched here; R5/R6 rendering is in AK-04b |

**For Wassim to review:**
1. Joint `origin` and `axis` are in the part's own frame (after `frame`, before the joint), so they share coordinates with its shapes.
2. The count-binding rule. It is stricter than the brief's "count-1 parts": a single child on a repeated parent is refused, not attached to repeat 0.
3. `rest` is baked into the shapes, so bounds, surfaces and exports show the authored "left open" pose.
4. The motion caps (8 moving parts, 32 groups) now count joints too.

## Local preview
Shared setup for the whole stack: `previews/AK.md` (`preview.sh start AK-PV previews/AK/ak-after.json` serves on :3301).
Setup is in `previews/AK.md`.

### What you will notice
The blue cabinet, back-left, has two nested mechanisms:
- the **door** swings open while its **knob** turns;
- the **drawer** slides out while its **bail pull** lifts.

Before, the knob and pull were fixed in place, so they were left behind in the air when the door and drawer moved.

### Where to look
Pose `4-cabinet`, "Cabinet".

### Try this
1. Select the cabinet and press **Play** (or E). Expected: the door opens with the knob riding on it and turning; the drawer slides out with the pull riding on it and swinging up. Press again and everything closes.
2. In walkthrough, aim at the knob or the pull and press E. Expected: only that part toggles. Aiming at the door leaf toggles the door, and the knob still rides on it.
3. Bake or export and play the clips in /viewer. Expected: the same nested motion, with clips named `<node>:door|knob|drawer|pull: open`.

### Before / after
`previews/AK/before-4-cabinet.png` / `after-4-cabinet.png` show the cabinet at rest; the change is in motion.

**Checked by me:** the static renders at the listed poses (captured from :3100 and :3301). I did not click through the interactive steps in a browser; unit tests cover them.

### Known limits
- Colliders still skip moving parts while they move.
- Studio and Articraft do not write joints yet.

title: feat(procedural-items): render, bake and operate joint trees (AK-04b)
body:
## AK-04b: render, bake and operate joint trees

**Stacked on #956 (AK-04a) → … → #945.** Review the top commit only. This is part 2 of AK-04; ship it together with #956.

**What.**
- **Renderer** (`nodes/procedural-item/renderer.tsx`).
  - Joint groups nest by `parent`. Each sits at its pivot less its parent's (`motionRestOffset`).
  - Off-axis joints turn by quaternion about `direction`. Slides move from their rest offset along `motionAxis`.
  - Flat designs keep the same group names, the same positions and no extra node.
- **Idle rest pose merged per slot.** This is the CHALLENGE fix for draw fan-out.
  - For part-tree designs, `buildProceduralGeometry` also returns `rest`: the whole rest pose merged per slot, with ranges.
  - The renderer draws that one mesh per slot while nothing moves.
  - It switches to the joint groups while a joint moves or is left open, and back when everything is closed. The switch is an imperative visibility toggle in `useFrame`, with no React re-render.
- **Bake.** Clips keep their `<node>:<part>: open|loop` names and `extras.proceduralMotion` keeps its shape.
  - Nested groups are posed at their rest offsets, and tracks use each joint's own axis.
  - `bakeProceduralAnimationClips` keeps the joint groups on the export clone and drops the merged rest pose, so the GLB animates.
  - The baked viewer (`glb-scene.tsx`) already plays nested clips, since tracks bind by uuid.
- **Operation.** Every consumer that listed moving parts from `part.motion` now reads `operableParts(recipe)`, which also counts non-fixed joints. The consumers are:
  - E and the action bar (`item-interactions`, `definition` keyboard action);
  - the first-person E prompt;
  - interactive controls;
  - the baked viewer's light-only check.

  Continuous joints default to running, like spins.

**Why.** AK-04. Nested chains must render, animate, bake and be operable. The CHALLENGE required the merged idle pose so joint trees don't multiply draws.

**Failing case first.** Before the fix, nodes `procedural-item/joints.test.ts` failed 3 of 3 tests (`scratch/AK-CORE/04b-failing-before.txt`).

**Proof.**
- **nodes `joints.test.ts`** uses a new fixture, `joint_cabinet.json`: a door with a turning knob and a drawer with a swinging bail pull.
  - The merged rest has one batch per slot, with the same triangles as the split batches. Flat designs build no rest.
  - Baked clips come out as `door`, `knob`, `drawer` and `pull`.
  - The knob group is nested in the door group at its rest offset.
  - The drawer's position track starts at its offset and ends at +0.3 m.
  - The pull ends at −1.2 rad about +X.
  - The export clone drops the rest container and shows the joint groups.
  - An off-axis knob ends exactly at its axis-angle quaternion.
- **viewer.** `procedural-controls.test.ts` checks that revolute and continuous joints get controls (continuous on by default) and fixed joints do not. `glb-interactive.test.ts` passes.
- **Suites.**
  - nodes: 3511 pass. The 1 fail is `lean-to roof-corner`, a load timeout at 6.3 s; it passes alone (24/24).
  - viewer interactive: 5 pass. core: 3023 pass.
  - `tsc --noEmit` on nodes and viewer: clean. `turbo check-types` for core and editor: pass. `bun run check`: clean.

**House effect:** no change. There are no `procedural-item` nodes on /next.

**Bugbot fix** (later commit): while idle, first-person E resolves the aimed part from the merged mesh's face ranges through `operablePartFor` (the part or its nearest operable ancestor).

| Rule | Check |
|---|---|
| R1 | No API change for plugins. `proceduralControlDescriptors` now takes the recipe (`{ parts, joints }`); its callers are internal |
| R2 | The idle/moving switch is imperative in `useFrame`, with no commits and no re-render. Rest and split geometry are cached per (recipe, params) |
| R5 | Paint, emission and slot lookups traverse both mesh sets. Selection stays bbox |
| R6 | Clips, names and extras are unchanged. The export uses the joint groups, and its rest pose is the evaluated rest |
| R3, R4, R7–R9 | Not touched |

**Known limits.**
- First-person colliders still skip moving groups. While idle, the merged rest mesh carries no motion tag, so a closed door is solid; while open, it is walk-through, as before.
- Articraft conversion (AK-17) and the Studio prompt (v13) come later, reader-first.

## Local preview
Shared setup for the whole stack: `previews/AK.md` (`preview.sh start AK-PV previews/AK/ak-after.json` serves on :3301).
Setup is in `previews/AK.md`.

### What you will notice

- the **door** swings open while its **knob** turns;
- the **drawer** slides out while its **bail pull** lifts.

Before, the knob and pull were fixed in place, so they were left behind in the air when the door and drawer moved.

### Where to look

### Try this

title: fix(viewer): clear floor-elevation dirty marks at priority 2 so moved columns leave their batch
body:
<!-- AK-B0 PR body (building-fidelity, found while building AK-B1) -->
## What

`FloorElevationSystem` still applies the slab lift at priority 1, but it now clears the dirty marks it owns (floor-placed kinds with no geometry builder or system: columns, procedural items) at priority 2, like every other consumer.

## Why

The node batch snapshots dirty marks at priority 1 to release changed members. `FloorElevationSystem` also runs at priority 1 and subscribes first (it mounts in the viewer before the lazily registered node batch), so it cleared a column's mark before the batch saw it. A batched column moved by undo, an MCP or scene-program write, or a collaborator's commit kept drawing its stale batched copy at the old place until something else released it (selection, hover, a re-sew). AK-B1 opts procedural items into batching, which have the same shape, so it must merge after this.

## Failing case first

`bun test src/shared/node-batch/source-systems.test.ts -t "floor-elevation"` (first commit): the real `FloorElevationSystem` and `NodeBatchSystem` frame callbacks in mount order, a batched column moved by a store write plus a dirty mark:

```
AssertionError: the moved column must draw itself, not its stale batch copy
(fail) a column whose dirty mark the floor-elevation pass consumes first still leaves its batch
```

After: pass; the column draws itself, then rejoins at its new place after the settle window.

## Proof

- `bun run --cwd packages/nodes test` → 3,508 pass, 0 fail (combined with the AK stack); node-batch 32 pass
- `bun run --cwd packages/viewer test` → 463 pass, 0 fail

body:
<!-- AK-B1 PR body -->
## What
`capabilities.batchable` (`BatchableConfig`) replaces the hard-coded `BATCH_KINDS` set and its `node.type` arms in node-batch (candidates, tint, wall cascade, wall-wait deferral). Its fields: `scope` (`'level'` children or `'wall'`-hosted openings that follow their wall), `excluded(node)`, `settled(userData)`, `batchKey(node, meshIndex)` (becomes the allocation key for geometry rebuilt in place) and `waitsForWalls`. The six existing kinds declare exactly their previous behaviour (`nodes/src/shared/node-batch/batchable.ts`).

New opt-ins, in the existing `NodeBatchStore` (no InstancedMesh, no second batcher):
- **procedural-item** while static: a playing motion releases the item (small `release.ts` signal from the renderer's motion frame) and keeps it out until it settles; recipes with part lights (per-node emissive clones) draw themselves; slot paint previews release as before; mounted/hosted items stay excluded (level scope).
- **imported-mesh**: per-node allocation key; primitives of one colour/opacity now share a cached material (`__pascalCachedMaterial`, cleared with the viewer cache) so they can share a batch. Transparent primitives still draw themselves.
- **block**: per-node allocation key. Only single-slot blocks batch (a single material, from #960); multi-slot blocks keep a material array and draw themselves.

Stacked on #958 (AK-B0); block batching needs #960: procedural items rely on marks surviving to the batch snapshot.

## Why
AK-08 recast per the challenge: extend the existing BatchedMesh batcher through a capability instead of a kind list. On /next extended, 196 of 281 imported primitives fall into 17 level×material buckets of ≥3, and 38 of 51 blocks into 7 (with AK-12a).

title: fix(nodes,core): ceilings above grade may hang below their level floor, down to grade
body:
## EC-CEIL: ceilings on a level above grade may hang below that level's floor, down to grade

**What:** a ceiling's lowest allowed height is now `-(world base Y of its level)` on a level above grade, so it may hang below its level's floor down to grade but never below it. title: feat(core): plugin install changes in scene operation patches
body:
## Summary

Hosted collaboration needs to share the installed plugin list. Today an install on an organization project stays local: the operation protocol only carries nodes and materials, and a joining peer re-adds its own default plugins over the shared list.

- `SceneOperationPatch.pluginChanges` (`{ id, installed }[]`): applied with the rest of a host patch, the list becomes explicit so hosts do not re-add their defaults on top of it. Duplicate ids in one patch are refused. Plugin-gated nodes get their dirty state updated with the list.
- `applySceneSnapshot(snapshot, { explicitPluginInstallState: true })`: a collaborative snapshot's plugin list is a decision the team made, not a default.
- Exports `ScenePluginInstallPatch`.

Consumer: the private community host (plugin install sync + splitting oversized Architect commits).

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test packages/core/src/store/use-scene-plugins.test.ts` (2 new tests: host patch install/uninstall with dirty state and commit origin, explicit snapshot list)
- [x] `tsgo --build packages/core`, biome
- [x] Verified end to end in the community host on two browsers: install survives reload and shows for the peer, install/uninstall sync both ways

**Pre-release review** (three Opus reviews plus Codex, fixed in 727ad66e9 and earlier)

title: feat(viewer,editor): studio hero look for worker thumbnails
body:
Community cards show the worker-rendered thumbnail (`/bake/:id?capture=thumbnail`). Those shots were framed too far out, shot from too low, and lit flat. This PR changes only the worker thumbnail capture; editor snapshots, studio renders and auto-save thumbnails keep their current defaults.

## Why the old shots looked wrong
- **Too far away.** The camera was fitted symmetrically around the centre of the union box, so about 40% of the frame was empty. The 60° lens exaggerated the perspective, and intentional site plates were included in the framing.
- **Too low.** At 13° elevation, roofless projects (most of them) showed their wall exteriors instead of the rooms.
- **Flat light.** The studio key light points along (10,10,10). With the camera at a 45° azimuth, the light sat roughly behind the camera, so shadows fell out of view.
- **Clipped roofs.** Roofs build their merged mesh a few frames after the scene reports ready, so the pose was computed against a roof that was too short.

## Changes
- **`hero-pose.ts`: new `tightFit` option on `heroCameraPose`.** It fits the projected silhouette and moves the aim off-centre. `computeHeroFraming` gets a `sitePlates` switch and returns detached items. Both default off.
- **`snapshot-pipeline.ts`: optional `studioBackdrop`.** It composites a radial gradient in exact sRGB: only the scene gets tone mapping, and the backdrop hexes land as authored. Without the option, the pipeline builds the same graph as before.
- **`key-light-override.ts` + `lights.tsx`: camera-relative key light override.** No-op when unset.
- **`materials.ts` / `wall-materials.ts`: slot default overrides.** They swap declared defaults only (drywall → plaster); painted refs always win.
- **`bake-thumbnail.tsx`: the look, as named constants.** It uses fov 40, padding 1.12, elevation 35° roofless / 24° roofed, and a key light 30° / 45° off the camera. The backdrop is #FAFAFA → #E4E4E4. The capture also:
  - waits for the framing bounds to settle (fixes roof clipping),
  - hides site surfaces and detached items,
  - adds a shadow catcher and per-wall contact shade.

  `prepareBakeThumbnailLook()` sets the look up before the scene builds and restores it on cleanup.

## Verification
- tsgo error lists for viewer, editor and community are identical to baseline.
- Tests: viewer 410/410, editor components 195/195, nodes roof + wall 304/304.
- Rendered 16 recent real prod publishes on Metal against the local stack. All clean: no roof clipping, backdrop corner/centre pixel-sampled at exactly #E4E4E4 / #FAFAFA.
- Editor snapshot path: every new option is opt-in and only the bake thumbnail page enables it. A pixel-statistics comparison with the old build is within run-to-run renderer noise.

## Test checklist
- [ ] Private-editor PR (submodule bump) renders `/bake/<id>?capture=thumbnail` with the new look
- [ ] Editor snapshot / studio render look unchanged

title: apply_patch can create and persist a schema-valid cyclic Site hierarchy
body:
### What happened?

apply_patch currently allows parentId updates that can create a cycle in the scene hierarchy.

A minimal case is two Site nodes:

Site_A.parentId = Site_B
Site_B.parentId = Site_A

The store also mirrors these relationships into the corresponding children arrays, producing:

Site_A
└── Site_B
    └── Site_A
        └── ...

This state remains locally schema-valid:

BaseNode.parentId accepts a string or null.

SiteNode.children accepts string[].

validate_scene validates nodes individually with their Zod schemas and does not appear to perform a global acyclicity check.

The generic reparent guard checks that the new parent exists and can hold children, but I could not find a check that prevents moving a node beneath itself or beneath one of its descendants.

This means a globally invalid cyclic scene graph can pass node-level validation.

On an active scene, apply_patch subsequently calls the live-sync persistence path, so the invalid graph can also proceed toward draft persistence before any global cycle check is performed.

I checked this against current main:

64fc7d8b6809ea1df253e17ec9da84391582da06

### Steps to reproduce

Starting from a scene containing a normal Site_A:

Create a second Site as a root node:

{
  "op": "create",
  "node": {
    "id": "site_b",
    "object": "node",
    "type": "site",
    "parentId": null,
    "children": []
  }
}

Reparent the original Site under the new Site:

{
  "op": "update",
  "id": "<site_a_id>",
  "data": {
    "parentId": "site_b"
  }
}

Reparent site_b under the original Site:

{
  "op": "update",
  "id": "site_b",
  "data": {
    "parentId": "<site_a_id>"
  }
}

Inspect the resulting graph.

The resulting relationships are conceptually:

Site_A.parentId = Site_B
Site_B.parentId = Site_A

Site_A.children includes Site_B
Site_B.children includes Site_A

Run validate_scene.

Both Site nodes are individually schema-valid, so the hierarchy cycle is not detected by node-local schema validation.

### Expected behavior

Any hierarchy mutation should reject a reparent operation that would create a cycle.

For example, changing parentId should fail if the proposed parent is:

the node itself; or

any descendant of the node.

A cyclic graph should also be rejected by scene-level validation before it can be persisted.

Conceptually:

node
└── descendant

node.parentId = descendant
→ reject with invalid_parent / cyclic_hierarchy

### Browser & OS

N/A

### Screenshots or screen recordings

N/A

### Additional context

Suggested fix

The primary fix should be at the hierarchy mutation boundary, rather than only adding guards to individual consumers.

Before accepting any parentId change, verify that the proposed parent is not the node itself and is not reachable from that node through the existing hierarchy.

A small helper could look conceptually like this:

function wouldCreateHierarchyCycle(
  nodeId: AnyNodeId,
  newParentId: AnyNodeId | null,
  nodes: Record<AnyNodeId, AnyNode>,
): boolean {
  if (!newParentId) return false
  if (newParentId === nodeId) return true

  const seen = new Set<AnyNodeId>()
  let currentId: AnyNodeId | null = newParentId

  while (currentId) {
    if (currentId === nodeId) return true
    if (seen.has(currentId)) return true

    seen.add(currentId)

    const current = nodes[currentId]
    if (!current) return false

    currentId = (current.parentId as AnyNodeId | null) ?? null
  }

  return false
}

Then the generic reparent path can reject the mutation before updating either side of the relationship:

if (
  'parentId' in data &&
  data.parentId !== current.parentId
) {
  const newParentId =
    typeof data.parentId === 'string'
      ? (data.parentId as AnyNodeId)
      : null

  if (
    newParentId &&
    wouldCreateHierarchyCycle(
      current.id as AnyNodeId,
      newParentId,
      scene.nodes,
    )
  ) {
    throw new PatchRefusedError(
      'invalid_parent',
      index,
      current.id,
      `reparenting "${current.id}" under "${newParentId}" would create a hierarchy cycle`,
    )
  }

  // existing reparent logic...
}

Ideally the same invariant should live in a shared core hierarchy helper so it is reused by:

apply_patch
updateNode / updateNodes
createNode / createNodes
any future reparent API

rather than being enforced only in the MCP layer.

Scene-level validation

It would also be useful for scene validation to verify global hierarchy properties that per-node Zod validation cannot prove.

At minimum:

- every non-null parentId resolves to an existing node
- child.parentId and parent.children are mutually consistent
- hierarchy traversal is acyclic
- a root node does not also have a structural parent

A simple DFS/parent-chain pass with a visiting/visited set would be enough to detect cycles.

For example:

function validateHierarchyAcyclic(
  nodes: Record<AnyNodeId, AnyNode>,
): string[] {
  const visiting = new Set<AnyNodeId>()
  const visited = new Set<AnyNodeId>()
  const issues: string[] = []

  const visit = (id: AnyNodeId) => {
    if (visiting.has(id)) {
      issues.push(`hierarchy cycle detected at "${id}"`)
      return
    }

    if (visited.has(id)) return

    visiting.add(id)

    const parentId =
      (nodes[id]?.parentId as AnyNodeId | null | undefined) ?? null

    if (parentId && nodes[parentId]) {
      visit(parentId)
    }

    visiting.delete(id)
    visited.add(id)
  }

  for (const id of Object.keys(nodes) as AnyNodeId[]) {
    visit(id)
  }

  return issues
}

This would complement, rather than replace, mutation-time prevention.

Defensive traversal guards

Even after the mutation path is fixed, some consumers should probably remain defensive because scenes can also enter through:

persisted older files;

imports;

migrations;

plugins;

external tooling.

In particular, resolveLevelId() could use the same pattern already present in findLevelAncestorId():

const seen = new Set<AnyNodeId>()

while (current) {
  if (seen.has(current.id as AnyNodeId)) {
    return 'default'
  }

  seen.add(current.id as AnyNodeId)

  if (current.type === 'level') {
    return current.id
  }

  current = current.parentId
    ? nodes[current.parentId]
    : undefined
}

Likewise, recursive render/traversal utilities could optionally keep an ancestor set and stop on repeated node IDs rather than relying on the hierarchy always being well-formed.

These defensive checks should be secondary safeguards; the main fix should still prevent invalid hierarchy mutations from committing in the first place.

Regression tests

A regression test for the mutation boundary could use a minimal scene:

Site_A
Site_B

Then attempt:

Site_A.parentId = Site_B
Site_B.parentId = Site_A

Expected:

second mutation → invalid_parent

and assert that the failed operation does not partially modify:

Site_A.parentId
Site_B.parentId
Site_A.children
Site_B.children
rootNodeIds

It would also be useful to cover a deeper descendant case:

A
└── B
    └── C

Attempt:

A.parentId = C

Expected:

reject

Finally, a scene-level validation test could construct a cyclic graph directly and verify that the validator reports it even though every individual node still passes its own schema.

Additional context

Relevant paths on current main:

packages/mcp/src/tools/patch-guards.ts
packages/mcp/src/bridge/scene-bridge.ts
packages/core/src/store/actions/node-actions.ts
packages/core/src/hooks/spatial-grid/spatial-grid-sync.ts
packages/core/src/utils/heal-scene-graph.ts

A few details make this potentially more than a malformed-state-only issue:

apply_patch permits parentId changes when the target exists and exposes children, but there is no apparent generic ancestor/descendant cycle check.

validate_scene is node-local and therefore does not establish that the scene hierarchy is globally acyclic.

publishLiveSceneSnapshot() runs after a successful apply_patch; when a scene is bound, the current graph is exported and saved as a draft.

The existing scene healer repairs stale child links and missing reverse parent links, but a symmetric cycle such as:

A.parentId = B
B.children contains A

B.parentId = A
A.children contains B

does not look locally inconsistent and is therefore not naturally removed by those repairs.

There are consumers that assume the parent chain terminates. In particular, the core resolveLevelId() walks parentId using an unbounded while (current) loop. The adjacent findLevelAncestorId() already has a 16-step loop guard explicitly intended to prevent a corrupt parent-chain cycle from hanging a frame loop.

The rendering hierarchy is also recursively driven through children using NodeRenderer, so a reachable child cycle is worth guarding even if mutation-time prevention is added.

I have not claimed an observed browser hang or stack overflow here; the concrete issue is that the mutation path can admit a schema-valid cyclic hierarchy and allow it to proceed into downstream scene consumers/persistence.

The safest repair seems to be:

mutation-time acyclicity enforcement
        +
scene-level hierarchy validation
        +
defensive traversal guards

with the first item treated as the primary correctness boundary.

title: Room-first structure foundations
body:
## Summary

Rooms now own their floor, wall and ceiling intent. Floors, walls and ceilings are derived from the rooms by one server-safe reconciler. The editor, the scene API and the MCP bridge all share that reconciler. Existing projects load and render the same as on main. The branch is one commit, rebased onto `main` (5e05c8b8).

## What users will see

- **Room tools:** draw a room as a rectangle or a polygon. Each room brings its own walls, floor and ceiling. The room panel has Divide, Delete room and return-to-room selection.
- **Raised and sunken rooms:** a room can be raised or sunk. Doorways between rooms at different heights get derived steps. Terraces and mezzanines are supported.
- **Floor & foundation:** each footprint has one base plate. Its panel sets the slab thickness, the height above ground, the edge band and the foundation (solid or none, plus a material). A garden shed on the same level can differ from the house.
- **Separate floors:** a floor picker puts a room on its own base plate. Rooms without a pick keep the shared floor.
- **Floor openings:** openings are real nodes (Edit floor, then Cut opening). Stair voids use the same path. Legacy holes are adopted.
- **Paint:** walls are painted per face (a/b) and support paint regions. Each doorway step can be painted, and paint carries through an open door.
- **Tutorial:** now starts with a Rectangle room and "Name your room".
- **Unknown outside:** when no room tells which side of a wall is outside, the exterior layers go on side B in both the 2D layer lines and the 3D cladding. Before, 2D used side A and 3D used side B.

## Legacy compatibility

Load migrations cover room zones, floor plates, openings and floor datums. They are idempotent and write parent links atomically with deterministic ids.

**Parity gate.** `bench/structure-migration/world-gate.ts run --set golden` (private repo) measures each scene with this branch's core and with the pinned main core (d36538b5), then compares them in world space. It checks floors, walls, ceilings, finish surfaces and exterior thresholds. It runs four legs: client load, hosted normalization, save→reload, and editor.

| Set | Scenes | Differ from main |
|---|---:|---:|
| aymeric | 60 | 0 |
| wassim | 33 | 0 |
| featured | 18 | 0 |
| top-viewed | 3 | 0 |
| structure tests | 11 | 0 |
| Wawa House | 1 | 0 |
| **Total** | **126** | **0 blocking, 0 documented exceptions, 0 crash-only** |

Main's changes after d36538b5 (wall assemblies, curtain walls, …) produced no findings. Those features sit outside what the gate measures, so they are covered by the merged unit suites. The anonymised fixtures in `core/src/lib/__fixtures__/plate-corpus/**` pin the legacy cases in the public suites: one fixture per case, geometry kept, labels and assets removed.

## MCP (65 tools)

- 14 new tools:
  - rooms: `move_zone`, `rotate_zone`, `duplicate_zone`, `divide_zone`, `merge_zones`, `delete_zone`, `set_zone_intent`;
  - floors: `set_room_floor_construction`, `set_floor_foundation`, `rebase_floor_reference`, `create_mezzanine`;
  - openings: `cut_floor_opening`, `remove_floor_opening`;
  - walls: `lock_outside_faces`.
- `create_room` and `create_story_shell` write only walls and room intent; the floor and ceiling are derived. With a `namePrefix`, walls are named "<namePrefix> Wall N", as on main.
- `apply_patch` refuses writes to derived nodes with a structured error. Deleting and recreating the same id in one patch still works.

## Merged with main

- Main's 2D move overlay is kept.
- Ceiling brackets appear only in Edit ceiling.
- Main's history-during-drag is kept.
- Main's wall follower is replaced by our live kernel preview.
- The reference inventory now lists the new reference fields and metadata keys. The whole-graph clone remaps every node id, so plugin-owned references now follow a project clone, and that conformance test passes as a normal test.

## Verification

- `bun test`:
  - core: 4228 pass;
  - nodes: 3834 pass, 1 skip;
  - viewer: 465 pass;
  - editor: 1906 pass;
  - mcp: 485 pass;
  - ifc-converter: 45 pass;
  - cli: 107 pass;
  - `apps/editor` lib: 51 pass;
  - skills scripts: 69 pass.
- `tsgo --noEmit` is clean in every package (plus core's contracts config).
- `biome check .` shows no errors.
- `bun scripts/validate-skills.ts` passes.
- Browser smoke on the local hosted editor: a Wawa House copy and structure test 11 (2D and 3D) load with no console errors.

## Local test checklist

- [ ] Open a legacy project. It renders the same as on main, with nothing moved or lost.
- [ ] Draw a room with Rectangle and with Polygon.
- [ ] Raise a room, then sink one. Check the doorway steps.
- [ ] Floor & foundation: change the slab thickness, the height above ground and the foundation (solid, none, material).
- [ ] Separate-floor picker: put a room on its own floor, then back on the shared floor.
- [ ] Per-doorway step paint.
- [ ] Paint through an open door.
- [ ] Floor openings: cut one, move it, remove it. Check a stair void.
- [ ] Tutorial: run it from the start.

The private-editor bump PR follows.

title: Expose pending item model loads by loading manager
body:
Expose the number of outstanding ItemGLTFLoader transactions for each Three loading manager, including retry waits. Consumers can distinguish item downloads from other work on the same manager, even when URLs are shared; completion, failure and cancellation balance the count once.

Validation: 12 loader tests (54 assertions), covering shared URLs, retries, cancellation, separate managers and synchronous failure/callback cleanup; core, viewer, editor and nodes builds pass. Independent architecture review found no blocker.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to item GLTF loading bookkeeping and exports; behavior is covered by expanded loader tests with no changes to load success/failure semantics for normal paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`getPendingItemModelLoadCount(manager?)`** so callers can see how many active **ItemGLTFLoader** transactions remain on a given Three.js `LoadingManager` (defaulting to `DefaultLoadingManager`), including time spent in retry backoff. The count is tracked per manager in a `WeakMap`, increments when a load starts, and decrements exactly once on success, failure, or cancellation.
> 
> **ItemGLTFLoader** now routes all `itemStart`/`itemEnd` balancing through a shared **`end()`** helper, with extra guards for synchronous `super.load` throws, `itemStart` failures, and throwing host/consumer callbacks so pending state cannot leak or double-end. Concurrent loads of the same URL each contribute to the count; custom vs default managers stay isolated.
> 
> The function is re-exported from `@pascal-app/nodes` (`item` barrel and package index). Loader tests were extended to assert pending counts across retries, shared URLs, cancellation, and error paths.

title: fix(viewer): keep offset door hit targets reachable from both sides
body:
A door positioned away from its host wall can leave its invisible opening hit target behind the wall collision surface. Clicking from that side then selects the wall despite the visible opening.

Resolve the hit target from the host wall's zero-offset opening placement and express its horizontal correction in the door's rotated coordinates. This follows straight, curved and justified walls, including effective wall thickness. Visible frames, panels and the resolved floor height retain their authored placement. Unhosted and roof-hosted doors retain their existing behavior; reused targets reset after offset or parent changes. Frameless opening outlines follow the corrected opening position.

Validation: 119 focused tests / 1,456 assertions pass across eleven files, including actual wall collision rays from both sides, positive and negative offsets, flipped doors, rotated and curved walls, both wall justifications, compound rotations and mounted mesh reuse. The curved-wall follow-up reproduces eight failures before correction. Current-main legacy-load and zone-deletion controls also pass. Core/viewer TypeScript builds, formatting checks and both CI jobs pass. Independent architecture and regression reviews found no blocker.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes invisible selection raycast geometry for wall-hosted doors with Z offset; behavior is heavily tested but affects core picking/interaction paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes selection when a door is offset from its host wall: the invisible **cutout** raycast proxy now stays centered on the wall opening (zero Z offset) while frames and panels keep their authored offset.
> 
> `resolveOpeningCutoutProxyDepth` becomes **`resolveOpeningCutoutProxy`**, returning depth plus an optional placement center from `getOpeningWallPlacement` with Z cleared; `syncDoorCutout` applies that correction in the door mesh’s local space (including compound rotation). Unhosted doors, roof segments, and zero offset are unchanged; the proxy resets when offset or parent changes.
> 
> Adds **`door-cutout-proxy.test.ts`** with raycast, curved/justified wall, `DoorSystem` live-update, mesh reuse, and sliding-door visual bounds coverage.
