title: fix(core): legacy scenes with raw nodes load without crashing
body:
## Cause

The load migrations added by #976 read stored nodes as if they had been schema-parsed. The oldest stored scenes don't have every field the schema defaults. The private CI fixture `legacy-parent-links.test.ts > documentationZone` shows it: its walls have no `children`, and its doors and windows are placed by a legacy `offset` with no `position`. Two crashes followed:

- `plateLevelContext` read `wall.children.flatMap` (`lib/plate-surface.ts`), reached from `migrateExteriorThresholds` inside `reconcileStructureOnLoad`.
- `isFloorAnchoredOpening` read `opening.position[1]` (`lib/floor-opening-footprints.ts`), reached from `migrateFloorPlates`.

Both the hosted authority (`normalize-authority-scene`) and the client `setScene` threw, so any such project failed to open. Prod isn't affected yet because private hasn't bumped to #976.

## Fix

One mechanism, applied to every exported load migration: `loadMigration` / `loadMapMigration` in `core/src/utils/load-migration.ts`.

- **Read view.** Each migration reads the stored nodes with their *container* schema defaults filled in: arrays such as `children`, `holes`, `holeMetadata`, `position`, `rotation`, `boundaryWallIds`, and empty objects such as `metadata`. Scalars stay absent, because migrations read their absence as meaningful: slab `thickness`/`elevation`, level `height`, `floorThresholdVersion`. A missing container means exactly its default, since the reload after `materializeNodeDefaults` sees it filled and must migrate the same way.
- **No writes from the view.** If a migration carries a fill through untouched (same instance, same content), it's stripped from the output, so no stored node is rewritten by it. When nothing else changed, the stored map identity comes back, so the authority's no-op detection and idempotence still hold. Anything the migration wrote itself, or grew in place, stays.
- **Safety net.** If a migration still throws, it's reported (`[scene load] <name> failed…`) and skipped. The scene then loads as main loaded it, instead of failing. `migrateFloorPlates` keeps its per-level guard inside this.

Wrapped: legacy material slots, vertical, room zones, ceiling room links, legacy auto openings, floor plates (including piece adoption), slab slots, stair/elevator openings, wall face keys, wall face bands, floor openings, owned floor openings, and structure reconcile on load (including exterior thresholds, legacy wall datums, and footprint following). The legacy map passed to `reconcileStructureOnLoad` goes through the same view. `materializeNodeDefaults`, `normalizeLegacyStructure`, `healSceneNodes` and `removeRetiredDrawingSheetNodes` already tolerate raw nodes.

Legacy door `offset`: main never converted it. The client parsed the door with its schema default `position: [0, 0, 0]` and left `offset` in place, and the authority stored neither. That behaviour is unchanged.

## Also: Bugbot finding on #976

`deleteZone`'s `levelPose` placed a wall-hosted item with the curve frame, but took the yaw from the wall chord. Items kept from a **curved** wall therefore got the wrong rotation when their room was deleted. It now uses the curve tangent at the item's station, the same way `opening-floor-datum.ts` does.

## Tests

- `utils/raw-legacy-load.test.ts`
  - Regression: a minimal raw legacy scene shaped like the private fixture (walls without `children`, door and window with `offset` only, a `vertices` slab, a documentation-only zone, a level without `height`). It loads through the authority's migration sequence and through `setScene` without throwing and without any migration falling back. Every stored node is retained, the source isn't mutated, and a second load is idempotent. The door stays as main left it: client `position: [0, 0, 0]` with `offset: 1`, and the authority writes no `position`.
  - Gate: a seeded fuzz over 6 corpus fixtures plus that scene. It strips every schema-optional field at rates 1 / 0.5 / 0.25, loads through both pipelines, and asserts no throw and no fallback.
  - The whole file fails on main (9/9) and passes with the fix.
- `utils/load-migration.test.ts`: view fills, restore semantics (carried-through fill vs written value vs value grown in place), and the fallback.
- `commands/structure/delete-zone.test.ts`: an item kept from a curved wall faces along the tangent. It fails before the fix.

## Verification

- Suites: core 4243, nodes 5208, viewer 465, editor 1906, mcp 485, all passing.
- `tsgo --noEmit` clean for core (plus contracts), nodes, viewer, editor and mcp. Manual tsgo dist build of core, nodes, viewer and mcp.
- World gate (private bench): `--set golden` 126 scenes, 0 blocking. `--set broad` 496 scenes, 0 crashes. Both were also run once with the fallback turned into a rethrow, and neither changed, so no migration falls back on any of the 622 real scenes.
- Private `legacy-parent-links.test.ts` against these dists: 2/2 pass (documentationZone failed before). The whole private `collaboration/__tests__` directory passes: 286.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the full scene load migration pipeline and persistence shape restoration; failures are swallowed per migration but incorrect restore logic could change stored graphs or skip migrations silently.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Legacy scene load safety** is the main theme: new `loadMigration` / `loadNodeView` in `load-migration.ts` runs each structure load migration on a *view* with container schema defaults (`children`, `holes`, `position`, etc.) filled in, while scalars stay absent so migrations can still read “missing” fields. Untouched view-only fills are stripped on output so stored JSON is not rewritten for no-op paths; thrown migrations log `[scene load] … failed` and the pipeline continues with the original nodes.
> 
> **Wrapped migrations** include floor plates, room zones, vertical model, material slots, wall faces, floor/opening reconcile, and related helpers—same public exports, safer behavior on raw stored nodes.
> 
> **`deleteZone` / `levelPose`** now subtracts yaw from the wall **curve tangent** at the item’s station (not the straight chord), so items kept when a room is deleted stay correctly oriented on curved walls.
> 
> **Tests** add `load-migration.test.ts`, end-to-end `raw-legacy-load.test.ts` (authority + client, optional-field fuzz), and a curved-wall keep-item case in `delete-zone.test.ts`.

title: fix: prevent cyclic scene hierarchies
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #975 
Prevents 'parentId' updates from creating cyclic scene hierarchies.

- rejects reparenting a node beneath itself or one of its descendents.
- applies the guard in both 'apply-patch' and core scene mutation paths.
- adds global parent chain cycle detection to 'validate-scene' for imported or legacy scenes.

title: Export a bounded IFC4 subset from a Pascal scene
body:
### Problem or motivation

Pascal imports IFC through `@pascal-app/ifc-converter` (`convertIfcToPascal`). There is no writer in the other direction. A search of this repository finds no `exportIfc`, `toIfc`, or other Pascal-to-IFC export. The MCP tools export JSON and GLB (`export_json`, `export_glb`).

#219 (".ifc bim format support") was closed on 2026-07-19 after import landed. A model that can be read into Pascal still cannot be written back out as IFC.

### Proposed solution

Add a writer for a bounded IFC4 subset, in metres:

- site, building, and storey
- wall centreline, thickness, and height
- door and window, carried by `IfcRelVoidsElement` and `IfcRelFillsElement` (overall width and height only; no separate opening mesh)
- space

Curtain-wall configuration stays a recorded loss. Import already leaves curtain entities as `imported-mesh`, and a written wall should not pretend to restore `wall.curtainWall`.

The plan mapping has to match the contract already pinned on `main` by `packages/ifc-converter/tests/handedness.test.ts`, from #931 (merged 2026-09-29):

> Pascal is Y-up and right-handed; IFC is Z-up and right-handed. Seen from above, IFC north (+Y) is Pascal -Z, so an IFC plan point (X, Y) is the Pascal plan point (x, z) = (X, -Y). Mapping +Y to +Z mirrors the model.

`worldToScene` uses `planDepthSign = -1` when `swapYZ` is on, so a writer for current `main` stores IFC Y as −Pascal z.

`@pascal-app/ifc-converter@1.0.3` (published 2026-09-24) copies IFC Y without that negation. A writer aimed at 1.0.3 mirrors on current `main`. This request targets `main`. It is not a report that #931 is wrong.

If this subset is what you want, I will re-run a small synthetic room against current `main` and then open a pull request in `packages/ifc-converter`, with a bun test that writes the room and reads it back through `convertIfcToPascal`, using the same `(x, z) = (X, -Y)` helper as `handedness.test.ts` and the existing `packages/ifc-converter/tests/fixtures/handedness.ifc` fixture on the import side.

### Alternatives considered

- A raw STEP writer aimed at npm 1.0.3. That sign is the opposite of `main`.
- A plugin. Plugins add node kinds and sidebar panels. An exporter does not fit that contract.
- Treating the existing JSON or GLB export as the IFC path. Those are already there, and they are not IFC.

### Additional context

The room I would use for the test, in Pascal plan metres `[x, z]`:

- storey at elevation 0, wall height 2.8 m except the extra wall below
- south (0, 0) → (6, 0), east (6, 0) → (6, 4), north (6, 4) → (0, 4), west (0, 4) → (0, 0), thickness 0.2 m
- one extra wall (0, −1.5) → (3, −1.5), thickness 0.15 m, height 3 m, marked curtain; the curtain configuration is the expected loss
- door on the south wall, 0.9 m wide, 2.1 m high, sill 0, starting 2 m along the wall
- window on the east wall, 1.2 m wide, 1.1 m high, sill 0.9 m, starting 1.5 m along the wall
- one space from (0.1, 0.1) to (5.9, 3.9), ceiling 2.8 m

On 1.0.3, that room round-trips centreline, thickness, height, opening size, sill, and the space polygon when IFC Y is written equal to Pascal z. The same file with IFC Y = −Pascal z mirrors. I have not re-run it on `main` (`ec0dcea440`) yet. That re-run happens before any pull request.

## What does this PR do?

1. **No selection outlines during walkthrough (live scenes).** The default `SelectionManager` kept routing hover and click through building → level → zone while walking. title: IFC import on the room-first model + Export IFC
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Import: IFC now lands in the room-first structure model.** The importer predated the rooms/plates/ceilings epic, so imported rooms rarely closed, floors were 5 cm thick at the wrong height, and there were no ceilings.

- Wall ends join onto neighbour centrelines (IfcRelConnectsPathElements + geometric fallback). Revit axes stop at the neighbour's face, so rooms never closed before. Justification is read from IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage, and hosted doors/windows keep their plan position.
- Slabs keep their real top, thickness and holes. A structural floor that fully covers rooms becomes a room floor plate; anything else (terraces, footpaths, partial floors) stays a manual slab and the room points at it.
- Finish floors and IfcCovering FLOORING become room floor finishes/regions. IfcCovering CEILING becomes room ceilings, with holes kept; sloped coverings stay meshes.
- IfcSpace zones get seeds, and separators split open-plan spaces. Doors/windows get the current threshold model. The site polygon covers the model.
- A Pascal-authored IFC keeps its node ids and skips cleanup merges. Node ids are seeded from the file bytes, so an import is reproducible (random ids made room adoption flaky).

| Test file | IFC spaces adopted (before → after) | Duplicate "Room N" overlapping a space |
|---|---|---|
| 01-duplex | 9/21 → 21/21 | 8 → 0 |
| 05-paris | 21/29 → 28/29 | 3 → 0 |
| 10-sample-house | 2/4 → 3/4 | 0 → 0 |

**Export: Settings → Export → "Export IFC".**

- New `@pascal-app/ifc-converter/export` subpath: a pure TypeScript STEP writer for IFC4. No web-ifc at runtime.
- Parametric elements: walls (stepped bases follow the renderer's supports), doors and windows with voiding openings, slabs (normalised voids), IfcSpace rooms, IfcCovering ceilings, columns, and units (IfcZone).
- Tessellated with colour: roofs, stairs, items, fences (IfcRailing) and vegetation (IfcGeographicElement).
- GlobalIds are derived from node ids, and every element carries a `Pascal` property set so a re-import keeps identity.
- Export now waits, with a bound, for collectively rendered plants to mount their export geometry. This also fixes plants missing from GLB/USDZ exports.

Known gaps: roofs re-import as empty roof nodes; Paris "ENTREE LOGEMENTS" stays merged with its neighbour; some core slab/ceiling helpers the exporter reuses are superlinear on very large scenes; BakeExporter still uses the old two-frame wait.

Publishing note: `@pascal-app/editor` now depends on `@pascal-app/ifc-converter`, so npm needs an ifc-converter release that includes `./export`.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/ifc-converter && bun test tests`: 88 pass. New tests: room-first load on 4 real files, 7 review regressions from generated IFCs, export round-trip, element and review tests, determinism.
2. `cd packages/editor && bun test src/lib/ifc-export.test.ts src/lib/export-geometry-wait.test.ts src/lib/glb-export*`: 65 pass.
3. In the app, import `apps/ifc-converter/public/test-ifc-files/01-duplex.ifc` and check its rooms, floors and ceilings. Then open any project, go to Settings → Export → Export IFC, and open the file in Revit/ArchiCAD/Bonsai.

Verified with headless browser passes on community :3005 (before/after imports of duplex, Paris, sample house and open house, plus an Export IFC round trip on a real project): no console errors. Exported files validate with IfcOpenShell (schema + rules; every element builds geometry).

title: CI: git hooks, bun run ci, turbo cache, cli-smoke heap cap
body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops the push → red CI → fix → push loop on editor PRs. Of the last 10 failed CI runs:
- at least 5 were type errors or failing tests that were never run locally (the repo had no git hooks)
- 3 were the cli-smoke build running out of Node heap on the 7 GB macOS runner
- 2 were type errors from git-installed plugin packages

**Git hooks (`.githooks/`, wired by `postinstall` via `core.hooksPath`)**
- pre-commit runs Biome on staged files, fixes what it can and blocks on the rest.
- pre-push:
  1. checks `bun.lock` is in sync, when a package.json or the lockfile changed
  2. runs lint (`bun run check`)
  3. runs `check-types` and tests for the packages the branch changes and their dependents

  The worst case is a `core` change, about 33 s. Skip once with `--no-verify`.
- The hooks are plain bash (runs on macOS's bash 3.2) and call `bun run` scripts, so they also work when editor is a submodule of pascalorg/private-editor. The private repo's install points the submodule at `.githooks`.
- `postinstall` does nothing in CI or when there is no `.git` (Docker).

**`bun run ci`** runs exactly what the quality job runs: check, skills:validate, check-types, test, build. CONTRIBUTING now points to it.

**CI**
- Turbo remote cache backed by the Actions cache (`rharkor/caching-for-turbo`, SHA-pinned) in both jobs. Unchanged packages replay instead of rerunning.
- `setup-bun` reads `packageManager` instead of a second hard-coded pin.
- cli-smoke: `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=5120`. Recent runs hit "Reached heap limit" and exit 137.

## How to test

1. `bun install`, then `git config core.hooksPath` prints `.githooks`.
2. Stage a file with a lint error and commit: the commit is blocked. Unsorted imports get fixed and restaged.
3. `bun run ci` passes. Validated from a clean worktree with `CI=1 bun install --frozen-lockfile` in 4.2 min: lint, skills, types 11/11, tests 13/13, build 8/8.
4. This push went through the new pre-push hook.

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)

## What does this PR do?

First slice of the DX curation pass (PR CI under 5 min, no dependents cascade in hooks).

- `cli-smoke` (macOS, ~5 min on every PR) runs only when something that ships in the packed runtime changed — docs, `wiki/`, `.agents/`, `plugin-evals/`, tests and fixtures skip it.

- `.githooks/pre-push` typechecks the directly changed packages only; `...[$base]` pulled in every dependent, so a core edit typechecked and tested the whole graph before each push. CI owns that parity. The hook-only `ci:changed` script goes.

1. `bun install` (reinstalls `core.hooksPath`), stage a `.ts` change with a lint error, `git commit` → blocked with the `check:fix` hint; nothing re-staged.

title: refactor(agent): one set of agent tools for the chat and the MCP — shared contracts and operations
body:
## What does this PR do?

Defines ten agent tools **once**, for both of Pascal's agent surfaces — this repo's MCP server and the hosted AI chat — instead of twice. No new tool: these are the tools both surfaces already had, each implemented separately and drifting apart.

The tools: `list_levels`, `get_node`, `get_walls`, `get_zones`, `get_level_summary`, `verify_scene`, `duplicate_level`, `delete_node`, `add_door`, `add_window`.

- **One contract per tool** — name, description, input schema — in `@pascal-app/core/agent-tools`. Zod only, so the hosted chat's sandbox can load it (`contracts-purity.test.ts`).
- **One implementation** — a pure function over the scene — in `@pascal-app/core/agent-operations`. Doors and windows go through `planWallOpening` in `@pascal-app/core/building`, which applies the editor tool's own rules (`clampDoorToWall`, `clampWindowToWall`, `findWallChildOverlap`): what a person can do by hand is what an agent may do.
- **One refusal shape** — `AgentRefusal(code, message, details)`, returned by both surfaces as `{ error, code, …details }`, with a message that says what would work.
- **The MCP registers these tools from the contracts** (`shared-tools.ts`, `room-tools.ts`); its own copies are deleted (`get-node.ts`, `delete-node.ts`, `duplicate-level.ts`, `scene-query.ts`, `geometry.ts`). Door and layout clearance move to core. Level duplication moves from the editor package to core so the Duplicate dialog and the agents share it.
- **The rule, written down:** `wiki/architecture/agent-surfaces.md` — same contract on both surfaces, operations live once, rules live in the operation, the editor is the reference.

**What changes for MCP clients**, because both surfaces now run one implementation:

- `get_node` returns `{ node }`; doors and windows include `resolvedOpening` (floor datum and anchor).
- `get_level_summary` is compact: zone polygons come from `get_zones`.
- `verify_scene` returns issues as `{ type, message }` objects instead of strings.
- `delete_node` deletes the node and everything under it, as the editor does (the `cascade` flag is gone).
- `duplicate_level` follows the editor's Duplicate and reports what it copied and skipped.
- `add_door` / `add_window` clamp and refuse like the editor tool, accept lengths with units (`"36 in"`), and overlap an existing opening only with `force` — which the contract reserves for when the person asked for the overlap (the editor's Alt).

**One fix found while testing this PR through the hosted MCP:** `create_room` and `create_story_shell` grouped their edits with `runAsSingleSceneHistoryStep(useScene, …)` — the editor's global store. The hosted MCP keeps its scene and undo history in its own bridge, and in the Next server bundle that store has no history, so both tools failed there with *"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getState')"* (on `main` too). They now use `bridge.runAsSingleHistoryStep`, like `structure-tools.ts`.

The hosted chat's side lives in the private repo: it switches the chat to these contracts and operations, and adds a test that starts this MCP server and fails if any shared tool's name, description or input schema differs between the two surfaces.

## How to test

1. `bun install`, then `bun run check-types` and `bun run check` — clean.
2. `cd packages/core && bun test` (3,607 pass) and `cd packages/mcp && bun test` (532 pass), on this branch merged with today's `main`. Each tool's edge cases are one table — `packages/core/src/agent-operations/__fixtures__/cases.ts` and `packages/core/src/building/__fixtures__/wall-opening-cases.ts` — run against the core operation and the MCP tool through a real client.
3. In the editor (`bun dev`): duplicate a level from the floating level selector (level height menu → Duplicate level) and from the Site panel (Duplicate level / Duplicate level with options → Structure only). The copy lands above with what the option says; one undo removes it.
4. With an MCP client on this server: add a wall, `add_door` at its middle, `add_door` again at the same spot → refused with `opening_overlap` and a message saying how to proceed; `delete_node` on the wall removes its door too; `get_level_summary` has no zone polygons and `get_zones` does.

Also driven end to end through the hosted MCP (an MCP client on a local server: doors, overlap refusal with `opening_overlap`, reads, `verify_scene`, duplicate, delete, `create_room` and `create_story_shell`) and through the hosted chat (Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, local): doors and windows placed, overlap refused or asked about rather than forced, units, reads, scene check (incl. a door blocked by a sofa), duplicate, delete, and one-step undo — all as described above.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — no visual change. The Duplicate level dialog and buttons are unchanged; they call the same duplication code from its new home in core.

title: Authored geometry: agents build objects, windows and doors in three.js
body:
## What this changes

Agents build what Pascal's recipes cannot reproduce faithfully (a porch, lanterns, vaulted and tray ceilings, a fan-grille window, a carved door) by writing plain three.js. Pascal keeps the result as a node with a script `source`: an `item`, or a `window` / `door` whose fill comes from the script. Design: `wiki/architecture/authored-objects.md`.

- **`@pascal-app/geometry-script` (new):** compiles a module to a GLB + manifest read from naming conventions (`slot_<id>` paint slots, typed `part:<id>` parts, lights, `cutout`, `anchor:<id>`, `collider`, clips). Derives resting surfaces and undersides, merges meshes per part and material, samples clips into TRS tracks held at their last pose. Ships a self-contained sandbox bundle (`/sandbox`).
- **Sandbox:** the editor compiles in a worker inside a hidden `sandbox="allow-scripts"` iframe (opaque origin) with a CSP allowing only its own scripts and blob workers: no network, fonts, images or frames (verified: the same fetch succeeds without the CSP and fails with it). The editor hashes the returned GLB and code itself.
- **core:** `source` on `item`, `window`, `door` (script hash, params, GLB hash, inline manifest ≤ 24 KiB); code is a separate `text/javascript` artifact, never in the scene. `artifact://` resolved through a host `ArtifactStore`. Surface/underside helpers, `resettledPosition`, `flushMountRotation`, `scriptedSize`, `scriptInteractive`.
- **Agent tools (shared contracts, one operation each):**
  - `add_object` — create or rebuild (by `nodeId`) a scripted object; children re-settle after a rebuild.
  - `add_window` / `add_door` — now take the native outline (rectangle / rounded / arch), type and panes, plus optional `code` / `params`; with `nodeId` they rebuild an opening (operation `rescriptOpening`).
  - `get_source` — the module and params of any scripted node. `find_by_type` — nodes and typed parts of one type.
  - `place_item` lands on an object's real surfaces, hangs ceiling items from its undersides.
- **viewer / nodes / editor:** scripted openings render through the item's model path; the wall cuts the script's `cutout` mesh (real shape); the window/door systems keep hitbox and placement; panels show the script's params; handles only for declared `width` / `height` params; the Open control plays the `open` clip; GLB export bakes their clips; the selection toolbar sits on what renders. title: fix(editor): use direct scene operations and normalize loopback on sc…
body:
fix(editor): read scenes directly on the scene pages, behind the scene API guard

## Description

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #876. On Windows, `/scenes` and `/scene/<id>` returned 500: the server-rendered pages loaded scenes by fetching their own `/api/scenes` endpoint over HTTP, and on Windows the `pascal.localhost` host in that URL does not resolve.

- Both pages now call `getSceneOperations().listScenes()` / `.loadStoredScene()` directly. The API route uses that same singleton, so the HTTP round trip added nothing. There is no fallback and no `localhost` → `127.0.0.1` rewrite, so a storage error reaches the Next error page and isn't hidden.
- Reading the store directly also bypassed the API's guard, so the pages now run the same check. The new `apps/editor/lib/scene-page-guard.ts` rebuilds a `Request` from `next/headers` and calls the existing `guardSceneApiRequest`. That applies the origin allow-list, auth (loopback, or `PASCAL_SCENE_API_TOKEN` as `Authorization: Bearer` / `x-pascal-scene-token`) and the per-IP rate limit, exactly as `GET /api/scenes` does. A denied request gets `notFound()` (HTTP 404). Server components cannot return a 401 without enabling Next's experimental `authInterrupts`, and a 404 doesn't reveal whether scenes exist.
- `SETUP.md`: replaced the paragraph saying the Docker port must stay at 3000 (that limit only existed because the page fetched its own API). It now documents the guard.

What doesn't change: on `localhost`, `*.localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` with no token configured (the local dev / CLI setup), both pages work as before. A missing scene still renders the in-page "Scene not found" card.

Behaviour change: a page opened through a LAN IP or a public host with no `PASCAL_SCENE_API_TOKEN` configured now gets a 404. Before this PR it got an empty list or a 500, because its internal API fetch was refused (503) for the same reason.

## How to test

1. `bun test apps/editor/lib` (`scene-page-guard.test.ts` covers loopback hosts, a non-loopback host with no token (503), a required or wrong token (401), bearer and `x-pascal-scene-token`, an unlisted origin (403), the rate limit (429) and a missing host).
2. `bun dev`, then open `http://localhost:3002/scenes` and a saved `/scene/<id>`. Both load. On Windows, also check `http://pascal.localhost:3002/scenes`.
3. Open the same URLs through the machine's LAN IP. You get a 404. With `PASCAL_SCENE_API_TOKEN=secret` and a client that sends `Authorization: Bearer secret` (for example `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer secret' http://<ip>:3002/scenes`), the page renders.

## Screenshots / screen recording

None. Apart from the 404 for unauthorized hosts, there's no visual change.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (not run here: this checkout lacks the private plugin packages the app imports; unit tests and type checks only)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

## Replies to bot review threads

(The GitHub API for pascalorg/editor wasn't reachable from this session, so these are keyed by topic. Paste each under the matching thread.)

- **pascal Bot / Cursor Bugbot — HTTP fallback or `resolveBaseUrl` / loopback rewrite (catch hides errors, duplicated helper):** Removed: both pages call `getSceneOperations()` directly with no fallback, so storage errors surface, and both `resolveBaseUrl` copies are gone.
- **Any thread about the pages serving scenes without auth:** Fixed: both pages now run `guardSceneApiRequest` (origin, loopback-or-token auth, rate limit) through `lib/scene-page-guard.ts` and return 404 when it refuses. Tests are in `scene-page-guard.test.ts`.
- **Any thread about `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` / the Docker port note in SETUP.md:** The page no longer fetches its own API, so the port constraint is gone and SETUP.md now documents the guard instead.

## Description

## What does this PR do?

Applies E-008 ("dimension fields carry no arbitrary caps", `wiki/architecture/inspector-field-limits.md`) to the reference (scan/guide) inspector:

- Removes the `min={-50}` / `max={50}` bounds from the X/Y/Z position fields. A reference can sit anywhere in the scene, so a scan of a large site can be placed beyond ±50 m.
- Raises the uniform scale field's cap from 10 to 1000 and keeps `min={0.01}` (scale must stay positive). A guide image or scan imported at the wrong unit, such as millimetres or centimetres, can now be scaled up to match the scene.

2. In the reference panel, type a position of `120` in X. It is accepted, not clamped to 50.
3. Type a scale of `100`. The reference scales to it, not clamped to 10. A scale of `0` or below is still rejected.

title: feat(mezzanine): support internal stair placement and auto deck cutou…
body:
feat(mezzanine): add stairs inside a mezzanine, cutting its own deck

## Description

## What does this PR do?

"Add stairs" on a mezzanine now offers **Outside** (the existing behaviour) and **Inside**. An inside stair starts at an open edge of the deck, climbs under it, and arrives through an opening cut in the deck. This branch is rebuilt on `main`, on the stair-opening model from #1000 (headroom-clearance openings via `stairClearanceOpening`, `createSizedStairFlight` sizing).

**Planner (`planMezzanineStair(nodes, zoneId, placement = 'outside')`)**
- `outside`: unchanged. The flight stands on free host floor and arrives flush with an edge.
- `inside`: the flight's bottom step is on an edge with at least a stair-width strip of free host floor in front of it. The run plus a top landing (depth ≥ stair width) must fit inside the deck. The free area for this check is the deck minus `mezzanineHostClearance` (walls), other mezzanines, free-standing items and existing stairs, the same as for outside runs. The run is the preferred run, shortened down to the minimum going if the deck is shallow, so there is always deck to step onto at the top.
- Candidates store the edge point and walking direction. Position and rotation are computed once `run` is known.
- The stair is created with `deckSlabId` and `slabOpeningMode: 'destination'` (inside) or `'none'` (outside).

**Openings (`stair-opening-sync`)** keep `main`'s clearance geometry. They add a per-slab filter, `shouldApplyStairToSlab(stair, slab, …)`:
- A **deck stair** (`deckSlabId`) cuts only its own deck, and only when its cutout is on. It never cuts the floors above.
- `shouldApplyStairToCeiling` returns false for deck stairs, so an inside stair never cuts the host room's ceiling.
- Other stairs keep the level rule. They also consider open-supported decks (`support: 'open'`) on their source level, and the clearance opening decides whether and where to cut. There are no separate height heuristics, and every surface uses the same reference height.
- Intermediate landings of ordinary L/U stairs are never cut out of a source-level deck they meet. A landing standing at or above the deck top is walked on, not climbed through, and is removed from that deck's cut. Destination-floor openings are unchanged.

**UI**
- Inside / Outside appear in both the room panel's Stairs row and the room action pill (shared by 2D and 3D), as "Add stairs outside" and "Add stairs inside".
- For a stair attached to a deck, the stair panel shows a **Cut Through Deck** toggle (plus Opening Offset). Before this, the cutout control was hidden for deck stairs.
- The `slabOpeningMode` schema description and the `getStairDestinationUpdates` doc comment describe the new rule. Attaching to a deck still turns the cutout off by default, because a stair attached from beside the deck lands on its edge.

## How to test

1. `bun dev`, draw a room and add a mezzanine large enough for a flight plus a landing (about 5 m deep), with one edge away from the walls.
2. Select the mezzanine. In the room panel (or the action pill), choose **Inside**. A straight flight starts at the free edge and climbs under the deck. The deck gets an opening over the flight, with at least a stair width of deck beyond the top step. The opening's edges should get the deck's guard, open where you arrive (existing `stairArrivalOpening` railing logic; not checked visually in this revision). The host room's ceiling is not cut.
3. Choose **Outside** on another mezzanine. The result is the same as before this PR, and the deck is not cut.
4. On a mezzanine too shallow for flight + landing, or whose only deep edge faces a wall, **Inside** shows "No room for stairs" and writes nothing.
5. Select an inside stair and toggle **Cut Through Deck** off and on. The deck opening disappears and comes back.
6. Tests: `bun test packages/core/src/commands/structure/mezzanine-transform.test.ts packages/core/src/systems/stair/stair-opening-sync.test.ts` and `cd packages/editor && bun test src/lib/mezzanine-actions.test.ts`

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not captured for this revision. The behaviour is covered by planner, opening-sync and editor-level tests (see below). Screenshots or a recording of the Inside flow should be added before review.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`. Not done for this revision; verified through core and editor tests only.
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable). `slabOpeningMode` schema description and the destination doc comment.
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

Tests added:
- Planner: an inside stair leaves a top landing within the deck; a shallow deck shortens the run to keep the landing; a wall under the deck blocks the inside run (refusal, no writes); outside is the default and leaves the deck uncut.
- Opening sync: a deck stair cuts only its own deck, ending at the top step; it never cuts the host ceiling or the floor above, even within headroom (without the deck link the same flight cuts both); the cutout off cuts nothing; an L stair keeps its intermediate landing on a source-level deck it meets, while the storey above still opens over the landing for headroom.
- Editor: Inside via `addMezzanineStairs` places one stair with `deckSlabId`/`destination`, selects it, takes one undo step, and cuts only the deck. Both placements refuse with no writes when there is no room.

---

## Replies to review threads

**Cursor Bugbot: "Landings cut destination floors"**
> Fixed by the rebuild on #1000's model. The landing and intermediate-flight slicing heuristics this thread flagged are gone; destination floors use `main`'s `stairClearanceOpening` unchanged. Separately, an intermediate landing of an ordinary L/U stair is never cut out of a source-level deck it meets (landings at or above the deck top are subtracted from that deck's cut). Test: "an L stair keeps its intermediate landing on a deck it meets, and cuts only its stairwell above".

**Cursor Bugbot: "Inside stairs cut host ceilings"**
> Fixed: `shouldApplyStairToCeiling` returns false whenever `stair.deckSlabId` is set, and `shouldApplyStairToSlab` limits a deck stair to its own deck. Test: "a deck stair never cuts the host ceiling or the floor above, even within headroom". It uses a 4 m storey, where 2.5 m deck + 2 m headroom would otherwise reach both, and checks that the unlinked stair does cut them.

**Cursor Bugbot (earlier, resolved): inside candidates' position/rotation pairing**
> Still resolved after the rebuild. Candidates store only the edge point and walking direction; position and rotation are derived after `run`. The unused reversed (`rotB`) candidate is removed.

**Cursor Bugbot (earlier, resolved): deck stairs falling through to inter-level slab cutouts**
> Still resolved. A deck stair returns from the slab filter before any level rule, so it can only ever cut its own deck.

**pascal Bot**
> Thanks. The branch is rebuilt on current `main` (#1000's clearance openings and sizing). The unused `'auto'` placement is dropped (`'outside' | 'inside'` only, both wired to the UI). The open-deck rule is simplified to "source-level open decks are candidates; clearance decides". The `slabOpeningMode` description and the destination doc comment are updated, and both entry points (room panel and action pill) offer Inside/Outside.

title: editor: integrate local plugins, surface stairs and deck railings
body:
## What does this PR do?

- Integrate Bath Space, Landscape, Pool, Streetscape and WebXR through plugin discovery and host panels, with immutable GitHub package revisions and portable bundler configuration. Installs use the published GitHub packages and require no sibling checkout.
- Add registered surface snapping for straight stair placement and movement in 2D and 3D, live flight previews, inspector controls and curved-boundary transitions. Keep stair authoring in the node definition and respect visible snapping modes.
- Draw fences as deck railings with inward edge/corner snapping, deck-top elevation and active-floor tracking. Remap support references when cloning, strip preset host references, and clear deleted hosts.
- Preserve wall-mounted object grab offsets and face placement, support alpha-cutout selection outlines, repair GLB export cloning, and integrate Pool controls and plugin styling.
- Add documented connected-move hooks, inspector extension composition and room-boundary opt-outs. Increase the portable runtime size budget for the integrated catalogs.
- Pin the published Bath Space guided UI package. Widen the editor sidebar to 360 px and collapse secondary tool hints under More shortcuts.
- Prevent autosave SSE echoes from resetting active tools and selection. Accept namespaced attachment slot IDs at the API boundary while continuing to validate asset URLs.

Includes the maintainer fixes for Streetscape identity, stair elevation and fence drawing sessions, retaining the project dashboard and navbar.

- Publish the Bath Space card picker in subtree `70cffa9a6878122acf6e3fdbde5725db4908f737`: shared mounting cards and attached style panels in Guided and Catalog, sharp top pointers, responsive style grids, and one active category/style at a time. Clicking a category selects its first style; switching categories clears the previous selection.

Removed the local Bath Space symlink and bundler override. The installed package now comes from the published subtree commit above. Frozen installation, editor lint and all 13 workspace typecheck tasks passed after this cleanup. The installed package source matches the local Bath Space source.

## How to test

1. Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in a clean checkout. No sibling plugin checkout is required.
2. Start the standalone editor on port 3004, open a saved project from the dashboard, and check Bath Space Guided/Catalog, Pool, Landscape, Streetscape and WebXR panels. Switch between 2D and 3D. Catalog thumbnails should load.
3. Open a bathroom containing a wall-mounted tap, edit it and reload. Autosave should succeed with a generated `wall-point:<node-id>` slot ID, and save echoes should preserve tools and selection.
4. Draw a fence on a raised deck on the active floor. Check inward edge/corner snaps and deck-top elevation, then change floors and verify the old drawing chain clears.
5. Place and move a straight stair against a supported surface in 2D and 3D. Check the snapped high end, rise and flight dimensions, mode-driven snapping, and a single undo step per move.
6. Duplicate a level containing a surface and its fence/stair, then check copied host references. Delete and undo a host, and check wall-mounted movement and alpha-cutout selection outlines.
7. Expand and collapse More shortcuts. Confirm the primary action and active hints remain visible when collapsed.

Current review-fix verification:

- `bun install --frozen-lockfile --dry-run`, `bun run check`, `bun run skills:validate`, and all 13 workspace typecheck tasks passed.
- The editor package passed 2,543 tests and the node package passed 4,850 tests. Core passed 4,948 tests, viewer 684, MCP 1,127, IFC converter 92, geometry script 36, and app library tests 67.
- New regression coverage exercises railing inset/corner/floor behavior, support-reference cloning, wall grab tracking, cutout masks, plugin LOD cloning, pending save echoes, surface-parented stairs and legacy stair field migration.
- Landscape attachment/irrigation suites passed 102 tests; its additional raised-source attachment/detachment test and typecheck passed.
- The portable production build, runtime staging and packed CLI smoke passed, including digest validation and a scene round-trip between MCP and the CLI. Browser checks loaded Bath Space, Landscape and the canonical Streetscape panel and verified its layout styles.
- `PASCAL_PORTABLE_BUILD=1 bun run ci` now passes end to end: check, skills validation, all 13 typecheck tasks, all 15 test tasks and all 9 build tasks. The CLI passes 107 tests, including activation, rollback and stopped-editor updates. A published-layout regression test reproduces the pin override on the previous code and passes with the fix.

## Review follow-up

- Shared distribution authoring moved to `@pascal-app/editor/distribution`; builtin consumers and the published Landscape plugin use that entry. External plugins no longer need `@pascal-app/nodes` for these tools.
- Stairs now use `destinationSurfaceId` / `autoSurfaceSnap`, with migration of the former fields. Curved transitions read the registered boundary rather than Landscape's private shape. Surface-parented snapping uses a common level frame. Raised-source previews and Landscape reparenting preserve the source elevation.
- Inspector subscriptions select the node type and primary extension ID. Move cleanup clears previews without rewriting a committed pose, eliminating `sameStairMoveStillActive`. The temporary fence alias migration was removed. Public `DEFAULT_STAIR_*` exports are restored through core-owned constants.
- The four open bug findings are addressed: reject unsafe URL schemes in attachment slot IDs, scan the canonical Streetscape styles, preserve raised stair bases, and reject explicit fence hosts on another level.
- E-017 and the plugin authoring guide document connected movement, primary inspectors, independent child frames, preserved elevation, surface boundaries and room topology opt-outs.
- Landscape is pinned to `d60ee247334dad037e02a432a50bed9264193402` on the stable `packages/landscape` publishing branch. Bath Space is now pinned to `357338ddb7e042498fca7b6e6ee2054edbeb70b7`, published on `packages/bath-space`; its 370 tests and two thumbnail checks pass. Streetscape remains the maintainer's org pin.
- Explicit runtime activation and rollback now boot their selected runtime directly. Previously startup replaced that selection with the CLI package pin and attempted an unrelated download, causing the lifecycle hangs after staging a release.
- The portable archive is reduced from 184.22 MiB to 125.84 MiB, about 32% smaller. Bath Space thumbnails fit within 512 × 512 pixels at WebP quality 90 with preserved transparency. All 198 catalog thumbnails remain; the plugin image payload falls from 70.64 MiB to 3.65 MiB. All 767 previously recorded model/public assets are byte-for-byte unchanged. Static media still includes all 561 WebPs and 40 GLBs. The archive ceiling is now 140 MiB.
- The expanded packed smoke test fetches and byte-compares all 601 WebP/GLB assets from the installed archive. Digest/tamper checks and MCP/CLI scene round-tripping also pass. Browser checks confirm the optimized thumbnails load in Guided and Catalog without broken images.

feat(stair): add Mirror action for stair handedness (Cut Back stairs)

## Description

## What does this PR do?

Adds a **Mirror** action to the stair panel. It flips a stair's handedness in place without moving it or changing its dimensions. Closes #901.

`getStairMirrorUpdates` (core, `systems/stair/stair-mirror.ts`) computes the patch:

- **Straight / segment stairs** (Cut Back, L, U): child segment `attachmentSide` left ↔ right, and winder `turn` left ↔ right (`StairSegmentNode.winder` from #1000). Other winder settings (inner gap, walking-line offset, division) are kept.
- **Curved / spiral stairs**: `sweepAngle` changes sign. On these stairs Mirror does the same thing as switching the existing **Clockwise / Counterclockwise** control in Geometry. It is still offered so that Mirror behaves the same on every stair type.
- **Guards and handrails**: one-sided `railingMode` and `handrail.mode` (#1000) flip left ↔ right. `both` and `none` stay as they are.

`hasStairMirrorUpdates` reports whether a mirror would change anything. The panel has a single Mirror button, in **Actions** next to Move / Duplicate / Delete. It is disabled when there is nothing to mirror (for example a single straight flight with symmetric or no railings). The rotate sound plays only when the mirror applies. The edit is one undo step (`runAsSingleSceneHistoryStep`). With four buttons, the Actions row uses a two-column grid, as the parametric inspector already does for extra actions, so Delete is no longer clipped.

The branch is brought up to date by merging `main` (no force-push). The conflicts were only in `packages/core/src/index.ts` exports and the `panel.tsx` imports.

## How to test

1. `bun dev`, add a stair, apply **Layout → U turn** (Landing). In the stair panel, click **Actions → Mirror**. The second flight moves to the other side of the landing, and a Left guard becomes Right. Undo restores it in one step.
2. Apply **Layout → L turn** with **Winder**, then Mirror. The winder turns the other way in both the 2D plan and 3D. Enable **Separate handrail** with mode Left, Mirror, and check that it becomes Right.
3. On a Curved/Spiral stair, Mirror toggles the **Clockwise / Counterclockwise** control.
4. On a single straight flight with railing None or Both, Mirror is disabled and silent.
5. `bun test packages/core/src/systems/stair/stair-mirror.test.ts`

- L winder (left turn): `1002-winder-before.png` → `1002-winder-after.png`. The winder and upper flight turn right.

title: fix(core): core stability (plugin duplicate ids, WebGPU disposal, error surfacing)
body:
fix(editor): stop mid-drag GPU disposal in the drag box and surface guide-image errors

## Description

## What does this PR do?

Two stability fixes in the editor:

1. **`DragBoundingBox` no longer creates and disposes GPU resources every frame.** It previously rebuilt its `BoxGeometry`/`PlaneGeometry` on every size change and disposed the old ones in an effect cleanup. During a resize drag that happens once per frame, and WebGPU can still be executing a command buffer that references the destroyed buffers, so it drops the whole frame ("Vertex buffer slot … was not set"). The box now uses module-level unit geometry scaled through the mesh transform, plus materials cached by colour.
2. **Guide-image upload errors show the reason.** Both guide-image upload paths (action-menu upload button and site panel) used a bare `catch {}`. They now log the error and show `Could not add that guide image: <reason>`, built by one shared `guideImageErrorMessage` helper in `lib/local-guide-image.ts`.

The earlier description also mentioned a plugin duplicate-id change and an insecure-context (`crypto.randomUUID`) fix. Both are out of this PR: the first only affects third-party plugin kinds, and upstream asset ids already come from nanoid.

The branch is merged with the current `main`.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/editor/src/lib/local-guide-image.test.ts`.
2. `bun dev` on a WebGPU browser: resize-drag an item or a cabinet with the bounding box showing. No frames blank out, and the box follows the size live.
3. Make a guide-image upload fail (for example by blocking IndexedDB / storage). The error message now includes the reason.

## Screenshots / screen recording

<!-- A short clip of a resize drag (before: frame flashes on WebGPU; after: steady) would help. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) (none needed)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

## Replies to bot review threads

- **Cursor Bugbot — shared module-level geometry/material disposed on unmount (needs `dispose={null}`):** Checked against the versions in use; it does not occur. In @react-three/fiber 9.6.1, unmounting calls `dispose()` on the removed object only, and three 0.186's `Object3D.dispose()` only fires its `dispose` event, which lets the WebGPU renderer drop the per-object RenderObject. The shared `UNIT_EDGES`/`UNIT_PLANE` geometry and the cached materials are never disposed. `dispose={null}` would also skip that per-object cleanup, so it is left out.
- **pascal Bot / any thread that says the described plugin duplicate-id fix is missing:** That change was taken out of this PR; it only affects third-party plugin kinds whose id prefix contains an underscore, which Pascal's own nodes never have. Title and description are updated.
- **Any thread on the stale "secure-context TypeError" comment:** Removed.
- **Any thread on the duplicated error formatting in the two catch blocks:** Moved into `guideImageErrorMessage` in `lib/local-guide-image.ts`, with a test.

title: feat(nodes): support slanted (tilted) walls
body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR brings a highly requested architectural capability to the wall generation system: Slanted (Leaning) Walls.

1. **Schema Update:** Adds `tilt` (in radians) to the `WallNode` schema, defaulting to 0 for standard vertical walls.
2. **True Shear Transform:** Instead of merely rotating the extrusion (which would lift the wall off the ground or distort its footprint), this PR injects a pure **Shear Matrix** directly into the `wallWorldMatrix` and the wall's `Mesh` transform. This allows the wall to lean off the vertical Y-axis while keeping its base perfectly planted on the `slabElevation`.
3. **Seamless CSG & Openings:** Because the shear is applied globally to the wall's `Mesh`, any child nodes (doors, windows, wall-mounted items) naturally inherit the sheared transform. The `generateExtrudedWall` lifecycle leverages this inverse transform, meaning boolean cutouts perfectly follow the wall's new leaning angle without requiring manual math corrections on every window cutout!
4. **Editor Integration:** Added an `Angle` slider under the **Dimensions** property panel for walls, allowing precise leaning between -45Â° and +45Â°.

## How to test

1. Draw a wall in the editor.
2. Select it, and in the right properties panel under "Dimensions", find the new "Tilt (EÄŸim)" slider.
3. Slide it back and forth. The wall will dynamically lean forward and backward.

title: core, mcp: the shared tools foundation, one definition per agent tool
body:
## Reviewer guide: the shared tools foundation

**Frozen for testing (2026-10-06):** this PR's content is fixed. Any later foundation commit goes to a follow-up PR (`slice/s1b-…`, stacked on this one), not here. The foundation and its s1b follow-up merge together.

**Merge order:** this PR first, then pascalorg/private-editor#843, which points its submodule here.

**On upstream main (2026-10-06):** this branch merges main twice: 0f1878309 (#915 fences, #1000 stairs) in 478bdeb27, then a860e197e (#996, optional hosted service tools) in bb6dd80ac. Its diff against main is only the foundation. #996 merged as a union: main's optional service tools register beside the foundation's asset catalog. Where both solved the same thing, main's version wins:
- `create_stair` sizes its flight with main's `planStairCreation`, as the editor's stair tool does (risers of at most 18 cm, a run from the design targets).
- Main's `measure_stair` and `fit_stair` sit beside it in the shared contracts.
- `create_stair_between_levels` stays removed: its options live on `create_stair`.
- The tool-count line main dropped from `read-tool-annotations.test.ts` stays dropped.

**What changes for a user** (an agent on the MCP or in the chat):
- The MCP's write tools take the chat's names: `create_wall` → `add_wall`, `create_level` → `add_level`, `place_item` → `place_items`, `create_stair_between_levels` → `create_stair`. `cut_opening` is gone: `add_door` / `add_window` cover it, and `add_door` with `openingKind: 'opening'` makes a passage with no leaf.
- `save_scene` never writes a session's scene over a project it wasn't loaded from; with no `id` or `projectId` it saves to the project the session is bound to.
- A write that would silently do nothing is refused, naming the field. For example, `apply_patch` with `material.color` names `material.properties.color`; it also refuses an unknown material, naming the nearest, and a material a preset hides.
- `place_items` hangs items on walls, ceilings and other items, and `create_stair` keeps the railing, preset, name and opening options of the tool it replaces.
- Duplicate level (an agent's, and the editor's Duplicate) fills a freed floor instead of pushing every floor up.
- A wall behind a porch or a terrace (a room with no ceiling that opens to the outside) is exterior on that face: the front door faces the porch, and finishes and facades follow. A kitchen open to a terrace, or a courtyard walled on every side, stays inside.
- A door on an outside wall faces out, for agents and by hand: `add_door` turns it out, and the editor's door tool places it facing out whichever face is hovered (R still flips it). A garage door's track runs inside, a front door opens into the hall.
- `place_items` refuses a floor item standing where a door needs space (`blocks_door`, naming the door and a spot that clears every door) or that its room can't hold in any turn (`too_large_for_room`, with both sizes). Overlaps stay allowed: a chair under its table.
- A new level is born with the storey height (2.5 m): in the editor's store, the hosted MCP's default scene and a new project.
- Divide, merge, delete and an outdoor room's outline name a room boundary with no wall as the editor labels it: "a separator (the editor's Separator: a room boundary with no wall)". The agent then says what the person finds in the Scene panel, not "an open divider".

**How to test:**
1. `bun install && bun run ci` on this branch.
2. Build and connect the MCP ([packages/mcp/README.md](https://github.com/AxiomeCG/editor/blob/slice/s1-one-contract/packages/mcp/README.md)), then follow steps 2–8 of "How to test" below.
3. With [pascalorg/private-editor#843](https://github.com/pascalorg/private-editor/pull/843), follow its QA in the chat.

**Known flaky on main:** the `quality` check can fail on one timing test, core's `space-detection.test.ts` "stays near-linear on 2,000 isolated walls" (a ratio under 40). Main failed it today too ([run 37464791592](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/actions/runs/37464791592), 40.3); here it read 47.8, then 41.8, and passes locally. This PR doesn't touch space detection.

**Manual parity** (every agent capability this PR adds or brings to a new surface, and how a person does the same in the editor):

| Agent | By hand | |
|--|--|--|
| `divide_zone` | Room pill **Divide room** | ✓ |
| `merge_zones` | Select the separator between two rooms, Delete | ✓ |
| `move_zone`, `rotate_zone`, `duplicate_zone` | Room pill **Move**, **Rotate**, **Duplicate** (by hand: 45° steps about the room) | ✓ |
| `delete_zone` | Room pill, room panel or site tree trash, Delete key | ✓ |
| `set_zone_intent` | Room panel (name, built-on, floor height, floor/ceiling on-off) and paint (finishes, regions, wall material) | ✓ |
| `lock_outside_faces` | Room panel **Keep outside dimensions** (one room at a time) | ✓ |
| `cut_floor_opening` | Room panel **Cut opening** | partial: no multi-level shaft, no level-only rectangle, `cutsPrimary` not settable |
| `remove_floor_opening` | Floor-opening panel delete | ✓ |
| `set_floor_foundation` | Base plate panel (thickness, on the ground / raised, foundation height and finish) | ✓ |
| `set_room_floor_construction` | Room panel floor thickness, floor-height drag | ✓ |
| `rebase_floor_reference` | — | **missing** (no editor path writes the plate's reference elevation) |
| `create_mezzanine` | Room panel **+ Add mezzanine** | ✓ |
| `add_door` with `openingKind: 'opening'` | Door panel Type: Door / **Opening** / Garage | ✓ |
| `add_door` facing out on an outside wall | The door tool places it facing out whichever face is hovered (R flips) | ✓ |
| `place_items` on a wall, a ceiling, an item | The item tool's wall, ceiling and on-item placement | ✓ |
| `place_items` refusing a floor item in a door's way or too large for its room | — | **missing**: the editor checks collisions only, no door or room-fit check |
| `create_stair` options | Stair panel: railing, auto cutout, opening offset; rename in the tree; paint | partial: opening width/length/centre/rotation, cutting only one of floor/ceiling, and the destination slab are agent-only |
| `duplicate_level` filling a freed floor | Site panel or level selector **Duplicate level** (same builder) | ✓ (copying below, and naming at creation, are agent-only) |
| `add_object` (a scripted object, with a reason) | — | **missing** to create one by hand; an existing one's parameters are editable |

Missing or partial before this PR: `rebase_floor_reference`, `cut_floor_opening`'s shaft, `create_stair`'s opening controls and `add_object` already existed on main's MCP; this PR brings them to the chat too. New in this PR: the `place_items` door and room-fit refusals. Decided (2026-10-06): the `place_items` door and room-fit check gets its manual half in the s1b follow-up that ships with this PR: the item tool warns "blocks the door" or "too large for the room" while placing, from the same core check. | Before (MCP) | Now (MCP and chat) |
|--|--|
| `create_wall` | `add_wall` |

- every `__fixtures__/` and `*.test.ts`;
- `wiki/`, `skills/`, the MCP README and examples;
- 714c4ea0f, comment-only: comments keep the failure that motivated the code, without internal run names, codes or dates.

---

## What does this PR do?

One contract per agent tool: each tool is defined once in `@pascal-app/core/agent-tools`, runs one core operation, and is registered by the MCP and by the hosted chat from the same object.

- **Shared tools:** `add_wall`, `add_level`, `create_stair`, `place_items`, `create_room`, `furnish_room`, `search_assets` and the fourteen room and floor tools (`divide_zone`, `merge_zones`, `move_zone`, `rotate_zone`, `duplicate_zone`, `delete_zone`, `set_zone_intent`, `lock_outside_faces`, `cut_floor_opening`, `remove_floor_opening`, `set_floor_foundation`, `set_room_floor_construction`, `rebase_floor_reference`, `create_mezzanine`). `create_roof` keeps its MCP definition for now.
- **Breaking for MCP clients:** `create_wall` → `add_wall`, `create_level` → `add_level`, `place_item` → `place_items`, `create_stair_between_levels` → `create_stair`, and `cut_opening` is removed (`add_door` / `add_window`).
- **Writes say what happened:** a mutating shared tool returns `achieved` (created, updated, deleted, read against a copy taken before the call) and where the write went (`writeTarget`). `add_door` and `add_window` return one declared result.
- **`add_object` requires a `reason`:** what the object stands in for, checked before its script runs. `verify_scene` lists authored objects with their reason, and a plain wall-sized box or floor plate is refused (`use_walls`, `use_slab`).
- **Honest patches:** `apply_patch` refuses an update the node would drop or change (`unknown_field`), a material the library lacks, naming the nearest of the target's kind (`unknown_material`), and a material a set preset hides (`shadowed_field`). `null` clears a field.
- **Fixes:**
  - the room and floor tools run without the editor's scene store (a regression test; main already fixed the crash);
  - no listed input schema holds a tuple, so Claude Code keeps every tool;
  - `find_by_type` refuses a missing level;
  - `add_level` on an empty scene starts a site, building and level;
  - `create_project` saves its first draft;
  - Duplicate level (agent and editor) fills a freed floor instead of pushing every floor up;
  - `duplicate_level` lists at most 40 new ids and counts the rest (`newNodeIdsOmitted`): a floor copy is hundreds of ids the model reads back on every call;
  - `save_scene` with no `id` or `projectId` saves to the project the session is bound to, where it was refused "Call create_project first".
- **Also:**
  - `add_door` takes `openingKind: 'opening'` for a passage with no leaf;
  - `apply_patch`'s checks register from the module that owns what they protect (`patch-guards.ts`, `honest-patch-guard.ts`); the honest-update check answers as before;
  - its description and `add_window`'s say that glass strips and carved panels go in `code`;
  - the MCP takes the host's item library for `search_assets`, `place_items` and `furnish_room`.

No schema change, so old scenes load as before.

- **Nothing the old tools did is lost:**
  - `place_items` takes a `targetNodeId` per item: a wall face (with `y`, the height of its bottom), a ceiling (hung flush), another item or an authored object, or a room, slab or level floor. Per-item refusals: `height_required`, `item_too_tall`, `unsupported_host`, `host_not_found`, `host_not_on_level`. An unknown catalog id is refused (`asset_not_found`), where `place_item` placed a 0.5 m placeholder.
  - `create_stair` takes `create_stair_between_levels`' `railingMode`, `materialPreset`, `name` and every opening control, under the same names. With none given, it cuts the editor tool's own opening. With any given, the opening follows the climb (main centred it at z + length/2 even on a turned flight). New refusals: `slab_not_found` and `ceiling_not_found`.
- **Refusals name no tool S1 doesn't ship:** an unknown material points to a flat colour (`library:preset-…`).

**Draft:** it stays a draft until the slice is verified (live checks and your QA).

## How to test

1. `bun install && bun run ci`: lint, skills validation, type checks, tests and build pass.
2. Build the MCP (`bun run --cwd packages/mcp build`) and connect a client to `node packages/mcp/dist/bin/pascal-mcp.js`. `tools/list` lists `add_wall`, `add_level`, `place_items` and `create_stair` and all fourteen room and floor tools, and lists none of `create_wall`, `create_level`, `place_item`, `create_stair_between_levels` or `cut_opening`.
3. Draw a room and call `divide_zone` on it: two rooms, one undo step. Call `set_floor_foundation`: the slab rises.
4. `add_wall {start:[0,0], end:[5,0]}` returns `achieved: { created: { wall: 1 } }`.
5. `add_object` without `reason` returns `reason_required` and nothing is compiled.
6. `add_door` with `openingKind: 'opening'` on a wall builds a door node with no leaf.
6b. `place_items` with a wall as `targetNodeId` and a `y` hangs the item on the face; with an unknown asset id it returns `asset_not_found`. `create_stair` with `railingMode: 'none'` and an `openingWidth` builds a stair without railings, owning an opening of that width.
7. `apply_patch` updating a door with `material: { color: '#343b3c' }` returns `unknown_field` naming `material.color`; `{ material: { properties: { color: '#343b3c' } } }` applies.
8. In the editor, with three levels, delete the middle one and Duplicate the ground floor: the copy takes the freed floor and the top level keeps its index.
9. Build a room and, in front of it, a porch room with no ceiling that opens to the outside; add a door on the wall between them: its outside faces the porch, and the porch side of that wall takes the outside finish.
10. `place_items` a 2.3 m bathtub into a 1.5 m bathroom: refused `too_large_for_room` with both sizes. Place a cabinet in front of the bathroom door: refused `blocks_door`, naming the door and a spot that clears it.

title: core: modern and half-louvered doors have a leaf
body:
## What does this PR do?

Modern and half-louvered doors have a leaf again.
- **Modern:** the preset was a single `empty` segment, which the door system draws as no leaf, so every modern door rendered as an open frame. It is now a flush panel over the whole leaf.
- **Half-louvered:** the preset built its slats from empty rows, leaving a hole over its top half. The slats are now ten raised bars (about 7 cm tall, 2.2 cm proud, 2.8 cm apart), deep and narrow enough to read.
- **Panels on both faces:** a panel segment's raised inner panel was drawn on the front face only, so a door seen from the hall was flat. It is now mirrored on the back face, for every panelled style (the shaped-top path is unchanged).

- **The same styles by hand:** a person picks the same styles from the panel or while placing; the agent and the panel write the same fields. The door and window panels gain a **Style** row under **Type** (it shows the style a door or window reads back as, or Custom when its leaf or panes match none), and the standalone editor's door and window tools gain the chips **[O] Type** and **[L] Style**, which the placed door or window takes. The door panel's Type logic moves into core (`doorTypeFields`, `doorTypeChange`), so the row, the chips and agents write the same fields; a style the person chose survives a type change.

- **Type and style:** Changing a door's Type keeps a Style the person chose (a modern door made sliding stays modern); a door still on its type's own leaf takes the new type's (hinged → French gets the French glazing).
- **Renamed export (npm consumers of `@pascal-app/core/building`):** `getDoorStyleOverrides(style)` is replaced by `doorStyleLook(style)`, which returns the whole look (`segments` and `contentPadding`) where the old function returned only the fields a style changed (`{}` for panel). A door parsed from either is the same for every style. Its one caller in the hosted app moves in pascalorg/private-editor#846.

New viewer tests check that every door style's closed leaf covers its opening, and that six-panel, shaker and half-louvered doors show their panels on both faces.

## How to test

0. **By hand:** place a door, select it, and set its Style to **Modern** in the door panel: a closed flush leaf. Set **Half-louvered**: ten slats on top, a panel below; orbit to the other side: the panels show there too. In the standalone editor's door tool, **L** cycles styles and **O** types before placing.
1. `bun test packages/viewer/src/systems/door/door-styles.test.ts`: 13 pass. Without this change, the modern and half-louvered leaf cases fail, and the three both-faces cases fail on the one-sided panels.
2. Over the MCP (or in a chat using these tools), ask for a modern door: `add_door` with `style: 'modern'` builds a flat leaf, not an open frame. Then a half-louvered door: ten slats on top, a panel below, no hole. Orbit to the other side: the panels show there too.
3. `bun run ci` is green.

**Merge:** merge this PR with a merge commit (not squash), so pascalorg/private-editor#846's submodule pin stays reachable; then #846.

## Reviewer guide: the agent's vision

**Merge order:** after pascalorg/editor#1007 (the shared tools foundation), which this branch is stacked on. Until #1007 merges, this PR's diff also shows #1007's commits: **review only the commits after `8f8bb72ce`**. Then [pascalorg/private-editor#847](https://github.com/pascalorg/private-editor/pull/847), which points its submodule here.

**What changes for a user** (an agent on the MCP or in the hosted chat):
- `view_scene`: the agent looks at what it built from a viewpoint it picks (a compass side, a height, a street-level eye, an orthographic face, a photo's own camera) and gets the picture back, to compare with a reference before it fixes anything.
- A door, a window or an item frames at detail scale; given a photo and a region, the photo's crop of the same element comes back beside the view.
- Every view comes with the same note on both surfaces: a picture to compare, not a measure.
- The editor can capture a frame for a caller without storing anything (no project snapshot, no thumbnail), and a capture waits for the roofs it shows.
- A host can add its own lines to what an MCP client reads at connect.

**How to test:**
1. `bun install && bun run ci` on this branch.
2. Over the MCP with no view host (the plain server): `view_scene` is refused `view_unavailable`. The hosted MCP renders it in the user's editor tab (the private PR).
3. With pascalorg/private-editor#847, follow its QA: a view in the chat, then one over the hosted MCP with the editor tab open, in the background, and closed.

**What to read:**
- `packages/core/src/agent-operations/scene-view.ts`: where the eye goes (the pose), the size, the photo crop request, and the note. Pure, shared by both surfaces.
- `packages/core/src/agent-tools/view-scene.ts`: the contract.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/view-scene.ts`: the MCP tool, which asks its host (`SceneViewHost`) for the picture and the crop.
- `packages/editor/src/components/editor/snapshot-capture.ts`: the ephemeral capture.

**What to skim:**
- `packages/viewer/src/systems/roof/roof-system.tsx` and `viewer/index.tsx`: a capture waits for roofs still building, and only for roofs on screen;
- `packages/mcp/src/server.ts`: `sceneViews` and `instructions` options; the registration and annotation lists.

**What to ignore:** `*.test.ts`, `plugin-evals/tool-annotation-justifications.json`, `scripts/openai-tool-annotation-policy.ts`.

**Not in this pack:** the photo tools (locating and straightening a facade photo), cropping an uploaded photo (it arrives with Plans in), and an inventory of what a reference shows (Checks).

---

## What does this PR do?

`view_scene` on both agent surfaces, from one contract and one planner in core:

- **Core** plans the view: the target (a building, level, wall, zone, door, window, item, stair, column, fence or slab, or the whole scene; a level with no walls framed by what it holds), the side and elevation or an exact eye, perspective or orthographic, or a photo's camera at the photo's aspect. A refused view (`target_not_found`, `nothing_to_view`, `photo_region_invalid`) refuses before any render is asked.
- **The photo crop (L51):** `photo { source, region }` returns the photo's crop of the element beside the view, sized by one rule on both hosts (`photoCropSize`: a small crop enlarged to 512 px, a large one capped).
- **The MCP** registers `view_scene` and asks its `SceneViewHost` for the picture; without one it refuses `view_unavailable`, without a crop host a photo is refused `photo_crop_unavailable`.
- **The editor** captures ephemeral frames (`ephemeral: true` on the thumbnail request; the frame comes back on `snapshot:captured`, stored nowhere). The viewer holds a capture for roofs on screen whose merged shell is still to build.
- **`createPascalMcpServer({ instructions })`:** the host's lines for what a client reads at connect.

No schema change; old scenes load as before.

**Draft:** it stays a draft until the slice is verified (the live checks and your QA).

2. `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/scene-view.test.ts packages/mcp/src/tools/view-scene.test.ts packages/mcp/src/server.test.ts`.

title: viewer: give bake replace renderers the published graph
body:
## What does this PR do?

**For a user:** in a published project's baked viewer, ground that a plugin draws from its site (painted surface, grass) now shows up. Before, the lot was an empty grey plane in the baked viewer, while the editor showed the grass.

**Why it was missing:** a kind with `bake: 'replace'` has its baked mesh hidden by `GlbScene`, and is re-rendered live through its `bakeReplaceRenderer`. That renderer only received `{ nodes }`. The baked viewer never loads the scene graph into `useScene`, so a renderer that builds from its parent (a ground surface needs its site's polygon and terrain) found no parent and drew an empty group.

**What changes:**
- `BakeReplaceRenderer`'s component takes an optional `resolve`, with the same signature as `GeometryContext.resolve`.
- `GlbScene` takes `sceneNodes` (the graph the artifact was baked from), builds one stable resolver, and `GlbReplaceInstances` passes it to every replace renderer. It's stable because `GlbReplaceInstances` is memoized.
- `wiki/architecture/node-definitions.md` → Bake policy documents the prop.

**Compatibility:** no schema change, so saved scenes and existing bakes load as before (E-003). A renderer that ignores `resolve` behaves exactly as today, and a host without the graph just omits it. Plugins keep loading (E-010).

**Test (T-001):** one repro in the existing `plugin-dispatch.test.tsx`. It mounts a replace renderer with an empty `useScene` and checks that it resolves its parent through `resolve`.

## How to test

How to see it, once a host passes `sceneNodes` and the plugin reads `resolve` (merge order below):
1. Publish a project whose site has a painted ground surface and ground cover (Environment plugin), and let it bake.
2. Open it in the baked viewer (the `lod0.glb` path): the grass is drawn. Before this change, only the lot outline showed, on grey.
3. Open the same project in the editor: unchanged. Grass shows there before and after.

Checks run on this branch:
- `bun test packages/viewer/src/components/viewer/plugin-dispatch.test.tsx`: 6 pass. Full viewer suite (`bun test src` in `packages/viewer`): 510 pass.

title: mcp: clear_scene, an agent empties a project on purpose
body:
## Reviewer guide: clearing a project on purpose

**Merge order:** this PR first, then pascalorg/private-editor#848, which points its submodule here.

**On editor main (2026-10-06):** d92eb5a5a merges main a860e197e (#915, #1000, #996). The tool lists follow main's: `read-tool-annotations.test.ts` compares names with the policy lists, and the policy count is main's 73 plus `clear_scene`. fa483f1ef is comment-only.

**What changes for a user** (an agent on the MCP or in the hosted chat):
- `clear_scene` empties the project on purpose, back to the default scaffold: a site, a building and one level of the standard storey height. The agent calls it when the person asked to start over, and says what they asked in `reason`.
- A store may refuse a write that would leave a populated project empty, which is far more often an accident (a client that never finished loading, a deletion of everything) than an intent. The hosted store does. The MCP now answers that refusal as `scene_wipe_blocked` with its code, instead of a generic failure, and **the session goes back to the project as stored**: before, it kept the refused write, so deleting the only room was refused yet the room was gone from the agent's session, and its next writes built on a scene the project didn't hold. The message fits a deliberate deletion as well as an accident: "This write would leave the project empty, so it was blocked and nothing changed. To empty the project on purpose, call clear_scene. To remove only part of it, such as its only room, build what replaces it first, then remove it."
- A store with no such guard (the local SQLite store) saves as before; `clear_scene` works there too.

**How to test:**
1. `bun install && bun run ci` on this branch.
2. `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/clear-scene.test.ts`: `clear_scene` empties a house and the next `create_wall` lands on the scaffold; an `apply_patch` deleting the site is refused `scene_wipe_blocked`, nothing is saved and the session keeps the house; `delete_zone` on a one-room project's room is refused, the session keeps the room, and the next `create_wall` leaves the store and the session equal.
3. With pascalorg/private-editor#848: the hosted MCP and the chat, by hand and by agent (its QA).

**What to read:**
- `packages/core/src/agent-tools/clear-scene.ts`: the contract;
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/clear-scene.ts`: the tool;
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/live-sync.ts`: `allowSceneWipe` passed to the store; on `SceneWipeBlockedError` the stored scene is loaded back into the session, then the refusal is answered. Other refused live-sync writes (a version conflict, a store failure) keep their behaviour.

**What to skim:** `packages/mcp/src/storage/types.ts` (`allowSceneWipe`, `SceneWipeBlockedError`, a `SceneInvalidError` so callers that know only that keep working), `apply-patch.ts` (a store's refusal returned with its code), the tool list and README row.

**What to ignore:** the tests, `plugin-evals/tool-annotation-justifications.json` and `scripts/openai-tool-annotation-policy*` (the new tool's annotations).

---

## What does this PR do?

Adds `clear_scene`, one shared agent tool (core contract, in `AGENT_TOOL_CONTRACTS`), the only way for an agent to empty a project on purpose:

- The MCP tool resets the scene to the host's default scaffold (`setScene({}, [])` then `loadDefault()`) and persists it through live sync with the new `SceneSaveOptions.allowSceneWipe`. It answers `{ cleared: { removed }, version, graphHash }` with the usual live-sync fields. Destructive annotation.
- `SceneWipeBlockedError` (a `SceneInvalidError`) is what a store throws when it refuses an emptying write without `allowSceneWipe`. Live sync loads the stored scene back into the session (as `load_scene` does), then answers the refusal `scene_wipe_blocked` with `mutationApplied: false`; when the stored scene can't be read back, it says to call `load_scene` before writing again. `apply_patch` returns that refusal with its code, as the shared tools return theirs.
- The local SQLite store has no wipe guard; nothing changes there.

No schema change; old scenes load as before.

## How to test

1. `bun install && bun run ci`: lint, skills validation, type checks, tests and build pass.
2. `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/clear-scene.test.ts packages/mcp/src/tools/read-tool-annotations.test.ts`.
3. Build the MCP and connect a client: `tools/list` has `clear_scene` with `destructiveHint: true`; on a project with walls, `clear_scene { reason: "start over" }` leaves the site, building and level.
