title: editor: warn when a floor item blocks a door or can't fit its room
body:
## Reviewer guide: a floor item in a door's way is warned by hand too

**Stacked on #1007** (the shared tools foundation). This PR targets `main`, so GitHub lists #1007's commits as well. **Review only the top commit:** [the comparison against #1007](https://github.com/AxiomeCG/editor/compare/slice/s1-one-contract...slice/s1b-floor-item-fit). The foundation and this follow-up merge together.

**Merge order** (in pairs, each editor PR then its private PR): #1007, then pascalorg/private-editor#843, then this PR, then pascalorg/private-editor#852, which points its submodule here.

**Why:** with #1007, `place_items` refuses a floor item standing in the space a door needs (`blocks_door`), or one its room can't hold in any turn (`too_large_for_room`). The editor's item tool checked only collisions, so a person could do by hand what an agent is refused, with nothing said. This PR is the manual counterpart: one check in core, read by both.

**What changes for a user:**
- **By hand:** while a floor item is placed from the catalog or moved, the HUD's "!" row warns when it stands in a door's way ("Blocks the door to Bath") or its room can't hold it in any turn ("Too large for Bath"). It's a warning, not a block: the item still places. Once it's placed, the selected item's panel shows the same warning at the top, with the item's and the room's sizes when the room is too small.
- **Agents:** `place_items` refuses the same cases with the same words as in #1007. The check now lives in core (`floorItemFit`), and the editor reads the same function.
- **Floor items only:** an item on a table, a shelf or a wall isn't checked. Overlapping items aren't a misfit either: a chair under its table is fine.

**How to test:**
1. `bun install && bun run ci` on this branch.
2. Run the standalone editor (`bun dev`). Draw a room about 3.1 × 2.2 m, name it Bath, and put a door in one wall.
3. From the catalog, take the bathtub (2.34 m long) and move it across the door before placing it. The HUD's "!" row reads "Blocks the door to Bath". Place it anyway: it places. Select it: the panel's top shows the warning.
4. Move the tub clear of the door: the warning goes. Draw a second room of about 2.2 × 1.9 m named Bath 2 and move the tub into it: "Too large for Bath 2", and the panel adds both sizes.
5. A sink that fits shows nothing. Neither does an item set on a table.
6. Over the MCP: `place_items` with the tub across the door is refused `blocks_door`, naming the door and a spot that clears it.

**What to read:**
- `packages/core/src/building/floor-item-fit.ts`: `floorItemFit`, the check, and `floorItemWarning`, the sentence a person reads;
- `packages/editor/src/hooks/use-floor-item-warning.ts`: the warning read at the item's live pose while it's placed or moved.

**What to skim:**
- `packages/core/src/agent-operations/place-items.ts`: now calls `floorItemFit`, with its refusal words unchanged;
- `helper-manager.tsx`, `item-helper.tsx`, `registered-tool-helper.tsx` and `contextual-helper-panel.tsx`: the "!" row (`notice`), placed after main's fence-placement card;
- `packages/nodes/src/item/panel.tsx`: the warning at the panel's top.

**What to ignore:** `floor-item-fit.test.ts`.

---

## What does this PR do?

The manual counterpart of `place_items`'s door-clearance and room-size refusals:

- `floorItemFit` (core, `building/`) decides whether a floor item fits where it stands: one its room can't hold in any turn, or one in a door's keepout as `verify_scene`'s blocked-door check sees it, doesn't fit. For a door, it suggests a spot in the room that clears every door.
- `place_items` refuses with it, and its words are unchanged.
- `floorItemWarning` turns a misfit into the sentence a person reads. The editor shows it in the HUD's "!" row while the item is placed or moved, and at the top of the selected item's panel.

No schema change; old scenes load as before.

## How to test

1. `bun install && bun run ci`.
2. `bun test packages/core/src/building/floor-item-fit.test.ts packages/core/src/agent-operations`: the editor and `place_items` agree on the same spot; an item that fits gets no warning; an item on a table or a wall isn't treated as on the floor; a room with no name still reads as a sentence.
3. By hand, steps 2–5 of the guide above.

title: Sync bundle: the shared tools foundation, vision, the floor-item warning and the doors fix
body:
## How to merge

**Merge this PR with a merge commit** (not squash: pascalorg/private-editor's sync bundle pins its submodule to this branch's head, which must stay reachable). Then merge the private bundle, pascalorg/private-editor#853.

This PR brings everything the user tested into one merge, so there's nothing to rebase. It replaces the small PRs listed below, which remain the review map: each section links its original PR, where the reviewer guide and per-commit history live. They'll be closed with a link here once this merges.

## What's in it

### 1. The shared tools foundation (from #1007)
**What a person sees:** in the hosted chat and over the MCP, an agent has one set of building tools, with the same names, inputs and refusals on both surfaces.
- The MCP's write tools take the chat's names (`add_wall`, `add_level`, `place_items`, `create_stair`). `add_door` with `openingKind: 'opening'` makes a passage with no leaf.
- The room and floor tools reach the chat: divide, merge, move, rotate or delete a room, raise a floor, cut a floor opening, add a mezzanine.
- `place_items` hangs items on walls, ceilings and other items.
- A wall behind a porch faces out, and so does its front door.
- A new level is born with the storey height (2.5 m).
- An agent that writes something that would do nothing is refused, with the field named.

Each tool has one contract in `@pascal-app/core/agent-tools` and one operation in core. Every agent capability has its by-hand counterpart in the editor (table in #1007).

**Checked:** the user tested it on a dev server (a room divided with one Undo, an opening with Type Opening, a wall light at 1.8 m, the porch door facing the porch). The Bugbot findings since are fixed with failing-first tests and touch no visible behaviour:
- add_object's hints name only registered tools;
- create_stair reports the slab and ceiling its opening is in, refuses another storey's ids, and claims a slab hole only when the slab above is cut;
- create_project keeps an unbound session's work.

### 2. The floor-item warning by hand (from #1013)
**What a person sees:** placing or moving a floor item in a door's way, or one too large for its room, shows a warning in the HUD's "!" row ("Blocks the door to Bath", "Too large for Bath") and at the top of the item's panel. It's a warning, not a block. It's the same check `place_items` refuses with.

**Checked:** the user tested it by hand (the bathtub across the door). The private bundle's E2E (`floor-item-fit.spec.ts`) passed on a dev server.

### 3. The agent's vision (from #1010)
**What a person sees:** `view_scene` lets an agent look at what it built from a viewpoint it picks (a compass side, a height, a street-level eye, an orthographic face, a photo's own camera) and get the picture back. Given a photo and a region, it also gets the photo's crop of the same element. On the hosted MCP the picture is rendered by the person's open editor tab.

**Checked:** the user tested it on a dev server.

### 4. The doors fix (from #1009)
**What a person sees:**
- Modern and half-louvered doors have a leaf again, and panels show on both faces.
- The door and window panels have a **Style** row, and the standalone editor's tools have **[O] Type** and **[L] Style** chips, writing the same fields as `add_door` / `add_window`.
- Since the user's first test:
  - a window placed with the tool after cycling the type past Bay or Bow keeps its sill;
  - a window style shapes only a Fixed window's panes, so the Style row and the tool's L chip show only on Fixed windows, and `add_window` refuses a style on another type (`style_needs_fixed_window`);
  - each look is offered once: Picture is Single, and `picture` stays an agent alias.

**Renamed export:** `getDoorStyleOverrides(style)` is now `doorStyleLook(style)`, which returns the whole look.

**Checked:** the user tested the doors. The sill fix is in the user's final checklist.

## Review fixes (Bugbot, all in this PR's own code)

- **create_room:** a declared door on a new outside wall faces out (60d181f0f); a zone conflict carries its own code (fd46f7a3e).
- **view_scene:** frames an item hosted on a wall, a ceiling or another item (eecc996ad).
- **Captures:** a capture waits for a roof's first shell (347a060b1); an ephemeral capture is never stored (c6cfe4c3e).
- **Earlier rounds:** add_object's hints name only registered tools; create_stair reports the surfaces its opening is in and refuses another storey's; create_project keeps unbound work.

## Architecture review (review-architecture skill)

Run on this PR by package (core / mcp / skills; viewer / editor; nodes):
- **Blocker, fixed in 5e83f1a8a.** The floor-item warning lived in the editor and branched on the item kind. It's now an optional `NodeDefinition.placementNotice`, which the item kind implements with core's `floorItemFit`. The person-facing wording moved out of core into the item kind, and one generic editor hook (`usePlacementNotice`) asks the definition, subscribing to the scene only while a node is in hand.
- **Nit, fixed in 6405ce4c6:** a single `windowTakesStyle` in core.
- **CI flake that this PR made worse, fixed in 9dc78b705:** the near-linear wall timing runs in its own process. The extra core tests had made the in-suite measurement slower; the code itself runs at ~26, the same as main.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The editor finds a tool's draft by scanning for transient metadata; the placement coordinator should publish the draft id.
- The viewer's scene-ready count imports the roof system's pending-merge count; systems should register their own pending-work counters.
- The floor plan's off-wall door and window ghost ignores the tool's O/L chips (3D follows them).
- The MCP README tool table omits several tools (older than this PR).

## Merged with main

Main's clear_scene (#1012) and the foundation overlapped. Resolved as unions:
- the shared contract list holds both;
- live sync keeps the foundation's `{ status, project }` answer and main's deliberate-wipe path, with the session restored on a refused wipe;
- `apply_patch` answers a store's refusal with its code;
- the annotation inventory is computed from the policy, which lists clear_scene.

## Docs

The docs match the code (96de5d317, cc928be1f, 251dfcdec). For every tool added, renamed or changed and every changed behaviour, the docs were searched for the old name or behaviour.

**Retired names:** none left anywhere in wiki/, skills/, the READMEs, DECISIONS.md or AGENTS.md (create_wall, create_level, place_item, cut_opening, create_stair_between_levels, place_on_surface, getDoorStyleOverrides).

**Fixed:**
- **`wiki/architecture/agent-surfaces.md`:**
  - the agent-first rule: a by-hand alternative where possible, never blocking a tool;
  - a step-by-step "Adding a tool to both surfaces";
  - the stair table: the chat already has measure_stair and fit_stair;
  - new `view_scene` and `clear_scene` sections (rendering hosts, refusals, `allowSceneWipe`).
- **`wiki/architecture/tools.md`:** the door and window O/L chips, the Bay/Bow sill rule, and the floor-item fit warning.
- **`skills/pascal-3d`** (SKILL.md, references/tool-workflows.md) and **`skills/furniture-fit`:** create_stair's sizing and refusals, view_scene, clear_scene, and place_items' blocks_door / too_large_for_room.
- **`packages/mcp/README.md`:** a view_scene row. The create_room, add_door, add_window, furnish_room and place_items rows were out of date and now match the contracts.
- **Agent-facing text that contradicted the code:**
  - create_stair's `length` said "default 3.0 m"; the run comes from the design targets;
  - place_items' description now lists its floor-fit refusals;
  - the MCP agent guide gains view_scene and clear_scene.

**Known gap, older than this PR:** the MCP README's tool table still omits most lifecycle, room, collection and unit tools.

## Checks

- `bun run ci` on cc928be1f: check, skills:validate, check-types 13/13, test 15/15, build 9/9.
- Every small PR's own checks and the user's tests (see each section). A local server on the two bundle heads is up for the user's final 10-minute check.

title: Rooms, open wall ends, scripted objects and a look-up camera
body:
## What does this PR do?

A fix pass on rooms, levels, scripted (AI-authored) objects and the 3D camera.

**Rooms and levels**
- Duplicate level: one floor plate per footprint (derived plates regenerate instead of being copied), upper copies stack on the walls below with no foundation and no gap, links (ceiling lights, support/deck slabs) follow the regenerated surfaces, and copies are named by position like added levels.
- Room hover (purple) follows the click from any phase; clicking a room on the Furnish tab selects it and stays on Furnish.
- Open wall ends: `findOpenWallEnds` / `planJoinOpenWallEnd` find walls that look joined but aren't (gap, overshoot, parallel, refused), with markers, a dashed line and gap label in 2D and 3D, a level hint, and a one-click **Join walls** (one undo) that squares near-90°/45° corners. An overshoot past a wall now counts as a junction when the stub beyond it ends free. Whole-wall moves rejoin their moved ends. `verify_scene` reports `wall_open_end`.

**Editing**
- Eyedropper: a pick click no longer paints the surface behind.
- Items land on the shelf of a scripted object under the cursor, not its top.
- Glass surfaces on items (incl. scripted and procedural) stop casting shadows.

**Scripted objects**
- Slots are matched to Pascal library materials after a build (one matcher shared with procedural items; user paint never overwritten).
- Reset parameters per row and for the whole group (one undo).

title: viewer: nothing passes through a roof
body:
## What does this PR do?

Walls, posts and other meshes ignore the roof today: a full-storey wall under a low roof (eaves below the storey height) pokes through the roof and its overhang, and so do posts, furniture or a pipe placed under it. This PR makes a roof cut everything in its building at its underside (the bottom of the deck):

- **Walls** get one extra CSG subtraction of a heightfield solid above the roof underside (`wall-roof-fit.ts`), kept separate from the opening union, so the wall top follows the slope with a closed, flat-shaded top. Walls never grow towards a roof.
- **Every other mesh of a level** — posts, furniture, fences, pipes, ceilings — is clipped geometrically against convex prisms above the underside (`roof-clip.ts`), whatever its material or loader. The cut face sits against the deck underside and is not visible. Roofs and the nodes they host (chimneys, skylights) are left alone; skinned and instanced meshes are skipped.
- **Columns** under a roof reach its underside, measured from their slab lift (`getFloorStackedPosition`), so posts of a terrace or porch meet the roof.

The underside planes come from the same faces the roof renders: the `getVol` closure in `getRoofSegmentBrushes` is extracted as `getRoofSegmentVolumeFaces`, and `getRoofSegmentUndersidePolygons` returns the deck-bottom faces clipped by the segment trim (`roof-underside.ts`). Only 3D geometry changes: plans, stored heights, the spatial grid and the roof elevation that follows wall tops keep reading the storey height. A roof edit rebuilds only the walls whose roof cover changed; a mesh is re-clipped only when its geometry, placement or the building's roofs change.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/viewer/src/systems/wall/wall-roof-fit.test.ts packages/viewer/src/systems/roof/roof-clip.test.ts` — walls cut by a low roof (full-height, partition and half walls), walls outside a roof untouched, roof edit marks only affected walls, posts reach the underside up or down and from a slab, mesh clipping keeps material groups.
2. `bun dev`, draw a room with full-height walls, add a shed roof whose eave is below the storey height: the walls follow the roof slope instead of poking through.
3. Put a column and an item under the roof: the column reaches the roof underside; anything taller than the underside is cut at it.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Before/after screenshots will be added in a comment (tested on a real house plan with a split-level shed roof).

title: One building mode, light room labels and a unified viewer
body:
## What does this PR do?

Simplifies how the editor and viewers handle levels, rooms and selection.

**One building mode.** The editor phase was Site / Structure / Furnish, but clicks switched it to the clicked node's home, so the tab followed the last click, 2D and 3D disagreed, and some handles only existed on Structure. Phase is now `site | building`:
- No click changes it, except entering the building from Site. In 2D or 3D, a click on the house from Site selects the building.
- Everything on the active level is clickable in 2D and 3D: rooms first, then drill down.
- Outline editors and 2D opening placement depend only on select mode.
- Keys: `1` = Site, `2` = building, F opens the catalog; B/P/M/Z just arm their tools.
- A stored structure/furnish preference reads back as building.
- `resolveNodeSelectionTarget`, `emitCanvasNodeSelection` and the `selection:canvas-node-click` event are removed.

**One rooms list, light room labels.** The Elements | Rooms layer split (`structureLayer`) is removed.
- The Scene panel lists Units, then Rooms, then Elements.
- Rooms on the active level show a small pill (colour dot, name, area in the active unit) in 2D and 3D when nothing but the site, building or level is selected.
- Pills float 1.25 m above the floor, declutter when they overlap, and fade in and out. Hover and click go through the canvas's zone rule.
- Tinted zone volumes remain only for unit-membership painting. Drawn zones look like rooms.
- The zone toolbar button is gone; Z still works.

**Room colours.** A colour is picked once at creation from the room's id (`zoneColorForSeed`, `newZone`) and stored; existing rooms are never recoloured.

**Viewers.** The public viewer (baked and parametric), embeds and the editor's Preview share one rules module (`viewer-selection`) with two hit sources and one header:
- Floor or wall click → room; second click → element. An empty click clears but keeps the floor.
- Breadcrumb Building › Floor › Room › Item, with framing on crumb, sidebar and pill clicks (`camera-controls:frame`).
- Sidebar Units / Rooms / Zones, and a hover-name pill.
- The editor's pills replace tinted volumes.
- Preview saves and restores the editor's selection, focused unit, tool and camera.

**Editor app.** Streetscape is pinned to a one-line fix (drop `setPhase('structure')` / `setStructureLayer`); upstream sudhir9297/streetscape-pascal-plugin#1.

## How to test

1. Click a sofa, a wall, then stairs in 3D and 2D → the mode stays Building.
2. From Site, click the house in 2D or 3D → the building is selected and you're inside.
3. With nothing selected → room pills with distinct colours. Select a wall → pills fade out. Hover a pill → the room highlights; click it → the room is selected.
4. Draw a zone → it gets a pill like a room, with no tint.
5. Preview → click a floor (selects the room), an item (breadcrumb shows the room), a sidebar room (camera frames it) → exit → the editor is exactly as before.

Automated: editor, nodes, core, viewer and mcp suites pass locally.

title: Room pills move aside instead of vanishing; saves skip placement drafts
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Room pills move aside instead of vanishing, and sit under the UI.**
- **Why they overlapped:** pill sizes were measured once, so fonts arriving, renames or unit changes left some pills overlapping while the declutter hid others.
- **Sizes:** pill sizes are now observed.
- **Placement**, larger room first:
  - keep the pill on its room;
  - else nudge it to the nearest free slot within one pill height;
  - else collapse it to its colour dot (which also shifts, and expands on hover);
  - hide it only as a last resort.
- **When it runs:** placement is applied at camera rest with eased style writes, so nothing jitters while orbiting.
- **Stacking:** 3D pills render in an isolated layer inside the canvas and the 2D pane inside the plan, so panels and toolbars always sit above them, in the editor and the viewers.

**Saves never include a placement draft.**
- **The bug:** clicking a preset tile clones it into the level before any click, and the window/door tools keep a hover draft in the store. Every save read the raw store, so an unplaced window could be autosaved and survive a reload.
- **The fix:** saves now go through `getSavedSceneDocument`. It leaves out drafts an interaction owns (`beginSceneHistoryDraft`, the active move-tool scope) and keeps moved nodes at their pre-move state.
- **Exports:** GLB and JSON exports use it too.
- **Not filtered by `isNew`:** placed nodes can keep that flag.

## How to test

1. Dense project, oblique 3D view, nothing selected → no overlapping pills; crowded rooms show as nudged pills or dots; hover a dot → its full pill.
2. Pan so pills pass under the left panel → the panel stays on top.
3. Arm the Window tool, hover a wall, wait for autosave, reload → no window was saved; place one → exactly one window, one undo step.

Automated: editor, core and nodes suites pass locally.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes what gets written on autosave/export and how history snapshots omit drafts—high user impact if draft ownership is wrong—but behavior is heavily covered by new tests across core, editor, and nodes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Saves and exports now read a “document” view of the scene** instead of the live store, so in-progress placement never persists. Core adds **`getSceneDocument`** (and editor **`getSavedSceneDocument`**) built from **`withoutDraftSubtrees`**: it strips only **explicit** carry drafts (`beginSceneHistoryDraft`, active move-tool scope) and still treats **`metadata.isNew`** fresh placements as non-document for undo snapshots—but **does not** drop committed nodes just because they still have `isNew`. Autosave, JSON export, and GLB/USDX/etc. paths use this; GLB prep also skips registry meshes whose nodes are absent from the saved graph.
> 
> **Room labels** replace distance-based **hide-on-overlap** with **placement**: larger rooms first, then vertical nudges, collapse to a **hover-expand dot**, hide only when needed. Pills **re-place when the camera rests** (not while orbiting), sizes track **ResizeObserver** / fonts, and 3D/2D pills render in **isolated layers** under editor UI. Hidden zones no longer get pills.
> 
> **Door/window** draw and move tools register placement/move drafts via **`beginSceneHistoryDraft`** / **`runSceneHistoryDraftWrite`** so live drags stay out of history and saved document until commit.
>

title: editor: views — 3D, 2D and plugin views in one or two panes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Turns the 3D / 2D / Split switch into **views**. The stage is one or two panes, each showing a view; Split is its own control, so any two views can sit side by side.

- **View registry.** `registerEditorHostView` / `EditorHostView` sit beside `registerEditorHostPanel`; a plugin can register several views, gated by `pluginId` and `workspaces`. `openEditorView(id, { beside })` opens one. 3D and 2D are built in. Documented in `plugin-authoring.md`.
- **Per-workspace layouts.** `viewLayouts` replaces `viewMode` / `floorplanPaneRatio` / `splitOrientation`.
  - Old preferences migrate; split keeps the plan on the left.
  - Capture and first person show 3D alone without touching the layout.
  - Studio no longer forces 3D.
- **`viewMode` / `setViewMode` stay as `@deprecated` aliases** so plugins written before views keep working (the WebXR plugin forces 3D for its session): `viewMode` mirrors `visibleScene`, `setViewMode(m)` sets `sceneLayout(m)`. Kept on purpose despite the no-shims rule, at the owner's request.
- **No remounts.** Panes are grid cells in a fixed DOM order, so swaps never remount the 3D canvas (its WebGL context survives) or the plan.
- **View bar.** A row above the stage, one bar per pane:
  - pinned views, the current view, and a "More views" menu
  - Split and swap at the right of the last pane; `\` toggles split in every workspace
- **Scene chrome.** The level selector, tool dock, host toolbar and the new `sceneOverlay` span 3D + 2D together, and follow the scene pane beside any other view.
  - With the plan in the right pane, its compass and Floor plan / Site plan switch mirror to the bottom-right.
- **Input hand-off.** Readers use `visibleScene` / `isViewVisible`, so a plan beside another view owns input exactly as a plan alone did.
- **Plugins directory.** The rail's plugins entry (new puzzle icon) opens the directory as a full view and stays lit.
  - Layout: categories, search, an Installed / Available filter, cards, and a detail drawer with Install, Uninstall, Open and Undo.
  - Fed by new optional panel fields `category` / `summary` / `access` and by `setPluginDirectoryContext`.

## How to test

1. Open a project. The view bar sits above the canvas: **3D | 2D | ⋯**, with **Split** at the right.
2. Click **Split** (or press `\`). Expect plan on the left and 3D on the right, as before. **⇄** swaps them; the 3D view does not reload.
3. With the plan on the right, the compass and Floor plan / Site plan switch sit at the bottom-right corner.
4. Click the puzzle icon in the rail. The Plugins directory opens in the focused pane, the rail entry stays lit and the sidebar panel closes. Click **Build**: the directory closes and 3D returns.
5. In the directory, pick a plugin to see its detail, then change category: the detail closes. On an installed plugin, **Open <plugin>** shows its panel.
6. Close and reload the page: the layout comes back. A layout saved before this change opens the same as before.

Ran locally:

title: feat: Bundle 2 editing, interior captures and native materials
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Bundle 2, editor half.** Point and ask, building feedback that follows the work, steadier keyboard and audio, sturdier walls, slabs, ceilings and roofs, interior captures, persistent native materials, and the shared tool contracts that the hosted chat and the MCP server both use.

**Ready for review.** The owner marked it ready after testing the bundle on a server built from the PR heads, and is testing these exact heads on that server now; Wassim merges. The hosted half is pascalorg/private-editor#877, whose `editor` gitlink pins this PR's head (`cad1839f`).

**Only bundle 2 is in this PR.** A bundle PR contains only the features selected for that bundle (the 29 on the delivery board). Everything else stays in the lab (R&D) branch for a later bundle. The lab families that had been carried here by default were taken out on 13 October; they are listed below under "Not part of bundle 2".

**Size:** 66 commits plus 6 merge commits, on top of upstream `main` (80d7a2f2, #1033, as last fetched; re-check before merging): 400 files, +40,358 / −920 lines. About 18,000 of the added lines are tests and fixtures. (Figures as of `cad1839f`; before the scope trim the PR stood at 489 files, +59,777.) Upstream `main` is merged in twice, never rebased: 86f8e833 (#1026) earlier on 12 October and 80d7a2f2 (#1033, Blender bpy modules) that night, so this PR merges cleanly with `main` as of then.

### What a person gets

- **Point and ask (the editor's half).** Point at an element or region, ask for a change, compare before and after (hold to compare, and a before view in 3D), ask for more, Undo/Redo. The card closes when the pointer is on neither it nor the pin. Room suggestions come from what the room contains. A host can say "Pascal is working", and an ask sent meanwhile is handed to the chat, which queues it. A pin that never heard its turn end is settled when the chat goes idle, and a turn's changes go only to the pin of the ask that is running. A scene preview shows another state of the document without writing it, and autosave stands still while one is held. The standalone editor gains no hosted chat; the host provides the handler.
- **Follow Pascal and construction feedback.** The camera follows the build onto the target floor and keeps the target in sight; a manual camera move pauses it. When Follow ends it puts back the cutaway, the floor and the hidden floors it had changed. Construction reveal, reverse playback on Undo and animated updates to existing pieces, including changes from a hosted MCP agent.
- **Keyboard and audio.** Group, editor, move and draft shortcuts stay out of text fields; editable keys survive group rotation. Construction sounds respect the calm and playful controls.
- **Walls, slabs and ceilings.** A wall authored at storey height binds to the covering slab's datum, and scene verification reports wall contacts with covering slabs. Ceiling-mounted scripted objects are anchored at the top; their bounds are checked above attachments and inside slabs. Floor underlays and authored footprint bounds are honoured. `verify_scene` also reports an object that is wholly or partly inside its wall (`item_wall_body_overlap`), one that goes through the wall (`item_through_wall`) and one that faces the wall (`item_faces_wall`); a new back-side wall object with no rotation now defaults to a half-turn yaw (the old zero default turned it to face the wall, which z-fought the cinema screen).
- **Furniture.** Wall-hosted furniture stays planar to its wall face. A new advisory lists wall-bound pieces standing away from every wall. Finishes of a room and its walls can be read back.
- **Windows and rooms.** Windows are centred when no sill is given; corner windows place, snap and merge; storey heights are coherent; named rooms get no duplicate zones and are not silently renamed.
- **Interior captures.** `view_scene` can show the inside of a chosen storey. It waits for the scene to finish building and sets aside nodes no system will settle, then restores the normal view.
- **Persistent native materials.** Create a named material, apply it to supported native surfaces, reuse and read it back, save/reload, Undo/Redo. Ceiling paint keeps existing properties; identical paint reports zero changes; an invalid target fails with no partial paint and no orphan material. No generated textures.
- **Doors and windows.** A door or window that carries clips draws its own leaves instead of a static batch instance, the walkthrough operates a door or window built from a script through its mechanism, and an open scripted door can be walked through (upstream `main` causes, fixed here).
- **Roofs.** A roof segment's fascia takes a height, a depth and its own finish. A roof outline's sharp corner is bevelled past a mitre limit instead of reaching out without bound (`857016ea`, from Bugbot).
- **Blender (bpy) modules, from `main` (#1033).** Merged in. The compile refusals of this PR sit in the shared `finishBuild`, so a bpy build gets the same non-finite-transform refusal and "no visible meshes". `add_object`'s `unmeasurable_object`, scripted-door clips and walk-through, and the wall-object observations read the manifest and the loaded model, not the language. A test commit (`6be2b6d9`) pins this for bpy builds. Where `main`'s tool text gave a method order ("read it first with get_source", "fields first; code only beyond them"), this PR keeps its factual wording and adds `main`'s facts about bpy.
- **Smaller repairs.** `add_object` refuses an object it cannot measure (`unmeasurable_object`) before building its asset; the geometry script's compile fails on a mesh at a non-finite position and names the mesh; the room labels' timers are called as functions, not as methods of the placer (an upstream `main` bug, kept as its own commit `9a1375c5` because it was asked for in review). Plugin nodes are validated and respect vertical collision bounds; the geometry script compiles consecutive imports on one line; scene-tool evidence and batching are optional in core.

### Not part of bundle 2 (kept in R&D)

Removed from this PR on 13 October, one commit per family, because they are not among bundle 2's selected features. They stay in the lab branch for a later bundle. Anything already on upstream `main` stays.

- **Photo location** (`locate_photo`), `4cc6ee74`. The photo tool `straighten_facade_photo` stays.
- **The scene coherence checker** (`dispute_coherence_item` and the checker behind it), `60b78690`. `verify_scene`, `validate_scene` and `validate_design` are `main`'s and stay; new checkpoints record no checker issues.
- **Site works** (`add_site_surface`, `add_steps`, this PR's `add_fence`), `dc015331`. `add_fence` is `main`'s again.
- **Apartments, units and circulation** (`propose_unit_layouts`, `apply_unit_layout`, `name_units`, `create_stairs_and_lifts`, circulation and reachability), `56b7b1b9`. `main`'s unit tools stay.
- **Plan reading and reference construction** (plan reference import, calibration, survey, matching, correction, reference elements, vectorising, furnish-from-plan, and the plans guide), `bbb4e1b6`.
- **`request_upload`**: its hints and the resolver type, `95813f7a`.
- **Visual reference search contracts**, `00c76f05`.
- **Modules nothing imports** after the above, `cad1839f`.
- **The facade family**, removed earlier (`e9a36f6a`): its nodes, schemas, tools and prompts. `straighten_facade_photo` stays.

**Tests trimmed (`da081b46`).** Two independent audits read every test this PR adds. Where both named the same blocks as pinning implementation details rather than behaviour (animation feel, copied constants, pixel placement, copy text), those blocks went: 11 files, −666 lines. No test that guards a fix made on 12 October was dropped.

### Bugbot, round 1

- **Roof outline mitre can explode**: real, fixed in `857016ea` (see Roofs), with tests in `create-roof.test.ts`.
- **Short landing still builds the stair**: real, but the tool has left this PR with the apartments and circulation family; the fix is written and tested separately for when that family ships.

### Tests and checks on this head (`cad1839f`)

Run on 13 October on `cad1839f`, from the hosted PR worktree, with the editor built.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| root `bun run check-types` (turbo) | 13 of 13 tasks green |
| core tests | 4268 pass, 0 fail |
| geometry-script tests | 49 pass, 0 fail (includes `main`'s Blender tests) |
| nodes tests | 4791 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail |
| viewer tests | 665 pass, 0 fail |
| mcp tests | 777 pass, 0 fail |
| editor package tests | 2419 pass on the tracked test files (the one failure in the local run is an untracked file that is not part of this PR) |
| `bun run skills:validate` | 69 pass (run on `00c76f05`; `cad1839f` only removes modules nothing imports) |

Carried from `c9f54660`, not re-run on this head: cli 107, ifc-converter 92 and editor app 51 pass; `bun run check` (biome) exit 0 with warnings only. Not run for this description: `turbo run build`, browser/e2e tests, GPU capture checks.

**The viewer test "pins the vendored closure to the installed R3F version"** (`packages/viewer/src/lib/pointer-events.test.ts`) passes here, where `@react-three/fiber` resolves to 9.8.1. It used to be red in the hosted repo (and on hosted `main`), whose lock resolved 9.6.1; #877 now pins 9.8.1 with a root override, and it passes there too.

### Seen, not in this PR

Upstream `main` issues found while testing this branch. They are not fixed here; they are listed so they are not lost.

- **`view_scene` timeout contract.** The hosted tool call gives up after 60 s without cancelling the capture, the view tool waits 75 s for its snapshot, and the capture's own budgets allow 120 s, so late capture work outlives the error. One deadline and real cancellation would fix it.
- **Capture pipeline lifetime.** In `thumbnail-generator.tsx`, a capture can run on a pipeline that was cleaned up while it awaited; a version check right before each capture closes that gap. Possibly linked to an "uncaptured WebGPU error: destroyed texture used in a submit" seen in the browser; not proven.
- **Shared studio HDR.** The hosted item preview, thumbnail modal and auto-thumbnail share one HDR, and drei's `Environment` disposes it on unmount, which can leave the live scene with a destroyed `PMREM.cubeUv` texture. The hosted `procedural-items/preview.tsx` already clones and disposes its own copy; the others could do the same.
- **Pool plugin dirty mark.** The pool plugin never clears its dirty mark, so a capture waited for the scene to finish building for ever. This PR's capture no longer waits on nodes no system will settle; the plugin-side patch is with Sudhir.

### Not in yet

- The lab families above (kept in R&D) and facades.
- A wall readback that gives the finish actually visible on each face, including a room's override of that face, is written and tested but held for the next bundle.
- Nothing else is known to be pending on the editor side. Nothing in this PR needs a migration, a credential or a paid service.

### Before merging

- Bugbot's threads resolved on the exact PR head, and CI green on it.
- Re-check that this PR still merges cleanly with `main`.
- Carried over from the earlier description and not re-checked at this head: transient corner-placement HUD state should not live in Core.
- If this PR is squashed, update the hosted PR's gitlink to the resulting public commit before that PR merges.

## How to test

Use a disposable scene. Chat scenarios run in a compatible host and may use normal model credits.

| Scenario | What should happen |
| --- | --- |
| **Edit a window or room** | Place or merge a corner window, then Undo. An explicit sill wins over centering. Creating a room over existing walls adds no duplicate zone and does not rename a person's room. |
| **Ask for a local change** | Point at an object or region, ask for a small change, compare, Undo/Redo, Change more. The request keeps its intended scope. |
| **Watch a build, then reverse it** | The camera follows the build; Undo plays it back. Typing in a field is not taken by shortcuts. |
| **Walls against slabs** | Author a storey-height wall on a slab; it binds to the slab datum and the scene check reports the contact. |
| **Open a scripted door** | A door built by the agent with an `open` clip slides open from the action menu or E, and in the walkthrough; an open one can be walked through, a closed one blocks. |
| **Follow Pascal ends** | After a build Follow had shown in cutaway, on another floor, the view, the floor and the hidden floors come back as the person had them. |
| **A screen on the back of a wall** | Add a wall-side object on the back of a wall with no rotation: it faces into the room, and `verify_scene` stays quiet. Push an object into its wall: the check names it. |
| **A roof on a sharp corner** | Roof a footprint with a very sharp point: the roof stays within about a wall's width of the corner. |
| **Look inside a storey** | Capture the interior of a two-storey scene with a roof, then an ordinary view; normal presentation returns. |
| **Create and reuse a finish** | Apply one named native material to two surfaces, save/reload, Undo/Redo. Repainting identically adds no change; an invalid target leaves nothing behind. |
| **Only bundle 2's tools** | The agent's tool list has no plan-reading, unit-layout, coherence-dispute, site-works, upload or visual-reference tool, and a full build completes without asking for one. |

## Screenshots / screen recording

A recording of the final pair is still needed.

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (the owner is testing these exact heads on a local dev server)
- [ ] My code follows the existing code style (`bun check` exited 0 on `c9f54660`; tick once it passes on the final head)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [ ] This PR targets the `main` branch

No merge, deployment, migration, credential change or paid model run is part of this PR.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core scene mutation, placement, and refusal paths used by chat and MCP; behaviour is heavily fixture-tested but regressions could affect everyday editing and agent writes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Expands shared agent-tool behaviour and the declarative fixture tables** that keep core, MCP, and chat aligned: corner windows, merging windows, roof creation, room-over-walls adoption, finish readback, and batch execution.
> 
> **Scripted geometry is guarded before build.** Compiles whose manifest bounds are non-finite (NaN in-process or `null` after JSON) now refuse with `unmeasurable_object` on `add_object`, `add_column`, and door/window paths instead of surfacing raw schema errors. Wall-side objects default **back** mounts to π yaw so they face into the room; `add_object`’s **reason** copy emphasises design intent.
> 
> **Rooms and openings.** `create_room` renames or refuses when walls already enclose a person-named zone (`room_named_by_person`, `rename: true`), and fixture expectations shift windows to **centred on the wall** at storey height. New **`create_roof`** derives footprint from bridged wall loops, bevels sharp mitres, and picks/reuses roof levels via `roofHost`.
> 
> **Layout and verification.** Plan footprints honour scripted bounds and asset corrective pose; collisions can separate vertically; floor rugs/underlays stop blocking placement; **`item_mid_room`** flags wall-bound furniture away from walls. Ceiling- and wall-hosted observation helpers feed **`verify_scene`** (body overlap, through-wall, facing). **`run_batch`** merges ordered tool calls into one undo step; **`applySceneChanges`** drops patch fields set to `undefined`; outcomes can **`keep`** session checkpoints. Levels created without height get **`fillLevelHeights`** to match editor derivation.

> **Tests/fixtures** add large case tables (`CORNER_WINDOW`, `MERGE_WINDOWS`, `FINISH_READBACK`, native-material oracle, cinema wall-screen JSON) plus focused unit tests for roofs, mid-room layout, and unmeasurable openings.

title: Add IFC import and export editor plugin
body:
## Summary
- Add a Pascal host panel for importing IFC files and exporting the current scene as IFC4.
- Preserve the open scene by inserting remapped nodes through one undoable scene operation patch.
- Copy web-ifc WASM assets into the editor public directory during dev/build.

## Verification
- `git diff --check` passed.
- TypeScript syntax transpilation passed for the plugin sources.
- Targeted importer checks passed for fresh IDs, hierarchy, orphan retention, and reference remapping.
- Full Bun/Next checks could not run in this Alpine VM because Bun’s Linux binary requires glibc.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Import applies large undoable scene-graph patches and depends on correct WASM hosting; export piggybacks on existing model export, but bad IFC input or converter edge cases could still corrupt or bloat the scene.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`@pascal-app/plugin-ifc`**, an editor host panel for **importing `.ifc` models** and **exporting the open scene as IFC4**, and wires it into the editor app like other first-party plugins.
> 
> **Import** dynamically loads `@pascal-app/ifc-converter` / `web-ifc` (WASM served from `/`), converts the file to a Pascal scene graph, then **`createIfcImportOperations`** remaps node/collection IDs and applies a single **undoable** `applySceneOperationPatch` so the current scene is preserved. After import it can set building/level selection, **fit the camera** via newly exported **`computeSceneBoundsXZ`**, and remap cross-references in the graph.
> 
> **Export** reuses the editor’s existing **`modelExport('ifc', …)`** hook and downloads the STEP blob from the panel UI.
> 
> **Host setup:** editor `bootstrap` registers the plugin/panel; **`predev` / `prebuild`** run **`copy-web-ifc-wasm.mjs`** to copy `web-ifc` WASM into `public/`; Next **`transpilePackages`** includes the new packages and `web-ifc`.

title: Plugin agent tools: contracts, chat extension types, MCP runner
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a plugin ship its own agent tools without changing the `Plugin` manifest (E-014). They come as separate exports, the same way panels and views do. This PR adds the shapes and the MCP runner. It adds no registries.

- **`@pascal-app/core/agent-tools`**: adds `AgentToolContract`, the `{ name, title, description, input }` shape every shared tool already had, now named, with optional `annotations`. Also adds `AgentToolAnnotations` and the plugin-side `PluginAgentTools` / `PluginAgentTool` / `PluginSkill`. A plugin tool says where it runs: `'operation'` is pure over the scene's nodes, and `'editor'` needs the live editor. `PluginAgentTools.version` is the plugin's contract revision, so a host can pin the contracts a run was offered. The module is types only and sits inside the zod-only purity walk. `AGENT_TOOL_CONTRACTS` now `satisfies readonly AgentToolContract[]`.
- **`@pascal-app/core/agent-operations`**: adds `AgentOperations`, the by-name map a plugin's `./agent-operations` export provides. `AGENT_OPERATIONS` now `satisfies` it.
- **`@pascal-app/editor`**: adds the browser-side types `PluginChatExtension` (in-tab executor, lazy cards, `/` actions, accepted file types), `ChatToolOutput` and `ChatToolCardProps`.
- **`@pascal-app/mcp`**: the runner that `registerSharedTools` used inline is now exported as `registerOperationTool(server, operations, tool, catalog?)` from `@pascal-app/mcp/tools/shared-tools`. It parses, plans, applies in one history step, and answers with `achieved`, the persistence envelope and refusals. The shared tools register through it unchanged. The host passes the annotations a tool advertises; they are never read from the contract.
- **Docs**: adds "Agent tools and chat extensions" to `plugin-authoring.md`, "Plugin tools" to `agent-surfaces.md`, and **E-016 Plugins own their agent tools** to `DECISIONS.md`. Annotations are hints, not authorization. The host decides which tools are offered, to whom and with what authority. Contracts are versioned. These are reviewed, trusted contributions, not a sandbox.

## How to test

1. `bun --cwd packages/mcp run test`: the "a plugin's operation tools over MCP" block registers synthetic `acme:signage` tools from a `PluginAgentTools` contract and an `AgentOperations` map, then drives them through a real MCP client. It covers the listing (the host's annotations win over a wrong `readOnlyHint` in the contract), an applied write (`achieved.updated: 1`), a refusal (`level_not_found`, scene untouched), input the contract rejects, and collection-only, mixed (nodes + collections) and reconcile-only outcomes, each one undo step. Every existing shared-tool case still passes.
2. `bun --cwd packages/core run test`: `contracts-purity.test.ts` still passes with `contract.ts` in the walk.
3. `bun --cwd packages/core run build`, `bun --cwd packages/mcp run build` and `tsgo --noEmit` in `packages/editor`: the `satisfies` clauses hold for every core contract and operation, and the new exports typecheck.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — non-visual change.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> MCP `registerOperationTool` changes when mutating calls run (collections and reconcile-only outcomes), affecting all shared operation tools; plugin tools are designed as trusted host-reviewed code with scene write access once registered.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **E-016**: plugins ship agent tools via separate `./agent-tools`, `./agent-operations`, and browser `PluginChatExtension` exports without extending the `Plugin` manifest.
> 
> **Core** names the contract shape (`AgentToolContract`, `PluginAgentTools` / `PluginAgentTool` with `runsIn: 'operation' | 'editor'`, versioned contracts, optional skills) and the operations map type (`AgentOperations`); existing `AGENT_TOOL_CONTRACTS` and `AGENT_OPERATIONS` now `satisfies` those types.
> 
> **Editor** adds chat types for plugin tool output, lazy cards, `/` actions, and in-tab execution of `runsIn: 'editor'` tools.
> 
> **MCP** factors shared registration into exported `registerOperationTool`, so hosts can register plugin operation tools the same way as core tools. The runner also applies **collection** writes and runs **`afterReconcile`** outcomes in a single history step when there are no node patches first. Host-supplied tool annotations win over hints on the contract.

title: Detached scene runtime: compute on a copy, apply with dependency checks
body: ## What does this PR do? Adds an instance-scoped, detached scene runtime, so an agent tool can compute on its own copy of the scene while the person keeps editing, then apply the result as a field-level patch only if nothing it read has changed. Decision **E-017**; architecture page `wiki/architecture/scene-runtime.md`. - **`@pascal-app/core/runtime`** (new export): `openDetachedScene(doc, { base, context, ids })` loads a canonical snapshot (no second migration) into an isolated store. - The store owns its history, commit bus, gesture drafts and hydration. - It records what a tool reads (fields, query membership, ordered children, materials, plugins, missing lookups) through a `DocumentReader`. - It allocates deterministic ids (`effectIds` / `withIdAllocator`) and produces a complete field-level `patch()`. - `dispose()` makes every later read or write throw. - **`applyPatchWithDependencies`** checks the recorded dependencies against the live store and either applies the patch in one undo step or returns a conflict saying what changed. - **`reconcileDocument`**: one synchronous pass for every system that writes saved fields (room structure, stair rises, stair and elevator openings, roof elevation), shared by the live editor systems and detached scenes. Its support index is built once per store and updated incrementally. Room detection and roof recomputation are scoped to the levels and buildings an edit can affect. - Shared operations select what they read through queries. A Biome rule keeps whole-map reads out of `agent-operations/`. - **MCP:** `new SceneBridge({ runtime })`. Handlers run in the scene's scope, so ids are deterministic, including `add_door`, `add_window`, `add_object` and `add_column` across their awaits. The bridge now settles stair rises and roofs as the editor does. `SceneOperations.runInScene` is optional; the README says when a host should provide it. - `compileAndStoreGeometryScript(input, { nodes, artifacts })` reads the scene and allocates its id before the first await. ## Behaviour and performance - **Editing by hand** (wall, stair, roof, slab edits and undo) is unchanged from `main` within noise, on generated scenes of ~0.5k, 2.9k and 10k nodes. - **Agent-host edits** are now at or below `main`. For example, a 10k-node wall edit runs at p50 429 ms against 732 ms on main. - Drag previews do no reconciliation. - **MCP slab and roof edits cost more:** about 2.0 s against 1.4 s for a 10k-node slab. The bridge now settles everything the edit owes, which it previously skipped. One MCP test changed for that reason: its stair now reaches the upper floor. ## How to test 1. `bun --cwd packages/core run test`: the runtime suites cover isolation, disposal, deterministic ids, the recorder and the conflict table (stair reorder conflicts; independent same-level inserts and cross-building edits merge; collection rename + recolour merge; two renames conflict). Parity: every agent-operation fixture yields an identical complete patch detached and live, then no deferred write; scoped and full reconciliation match. 2. `bun --cwd packages/mcp run test`: derived changes ship in one commit (raise a wall, its roof moves in the same commit), and handler ids are deterministic. 3. title: roof: draw a roof by outline — shed/gable over any outline, canopies, overhangs, roof paint roles
body:
Continues #1018 ("viewer: nothing passes through a roof"). This branch contains that change as well (with follow-up fixes to the roof clip), so it can either land after #1018 or replace it.

## What
- **Outline tool for roofs.** Draw a roof segment as a polygon. Points snap to the building's outer contour: outer wall corners and faces of this storey and the one below, slab corners, posts. Partitions are ignored.
- **Shed and gable over any outline.** The slope planes cover the drawn polygon, not just its bounding rectangle.
- **Per-side pitch and ridge step on gables.** Each side can have its own pitch, and the ridge can step (split-level). Ridge height, ridge position and per-side attic walls are edited from a new "Ridge" section in the panel and from plan handles, measured against the house walls.
- **Canopies.** Pull any edge of a segment's covering outwards. The covering continues in the slope's plane while the walls stay on the house. The sides narrow only the added part. Canopy edges snap to the building contour.
- **Overhang drawn on every edge** of the outline (eaves and rakes), with fascia and soffit, set by the single Overhang value.
- **Separate roof paint roles**: gables, fascia, inside, covering, soffit. Each has its own material slot (`ROOF_SLOT_ROLES`) and is paintable separately on roofs and segments, including the paint preview.
- **Walls and posts meet the roof.** Walls under a roof are cut to its underside, and rise to it when the roof sits above the storey height. Posts end at the underside.
- **Roof clip fixes** (on top of #1018):
  - a storey above a lower roof stays intact;
  - removing a roof restores the clipped geometry;
  - clip planes are normalised before they are moved into mesh space;
  - clip planes face inwards whatever the outline winding.
- **Print solids** follow the new shapes: per-side pitches, the gable back and the per-pitch deck overhang.
- **No mouse-wheel edits in panel fields.** Metric and slider controls no longer change value on wheel, so scrolling the panel can't edit a value by accident.

## Why
Real roofs rarely sit on a rectangle. L-shaped and irregular footprints, porches and terraces under an extended slope, and gables with unequal pitches or a stepped ridge were impossible or needed several hand-aligned segments. Walls poked through the roof or stopped short of it. Fascia and soffit could not be painted apart from the covering.

## How tested
- `bun check`: no new diagnostics (same warning count as `main`).
- `bun run check-types` for core, nodes, viewer, editor; `tsc --noEmit` in each package.
- `bun run test` in core (4017 pass), nodes (4775), viewer (604), editor (2070). All green; `main` is green as well.
- New tests: outline snapping, outline tool, canopy snapping, gable ridge editing and handles, per-side pitches, ridge steps, canopies, abutments, footprint clipping, CSG robustness, paint slots and paint roles, wall fit to the roof, roof clip frame.
- `wall-progressive-budget.test.ts`: its `@react-three/fiber` mock gains `addAfterEffect`/`invalidate` stubs, because the wall system now reaches `lib/materials.ts` through the roof underside.
- The same changes run in our product's editor, where they were checked by hand on a real house plan. The full app build and e2e of this repository were not run here.

title: nodes: add wall and slab niches and bumps
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds rectangular niches and bumps to straight solid walls and the top surface of slabs, including niches nested inside bumps.

- Adds scene schemas, shared placement validation, CSG geometry, inherited finishes, paint slots, and feature surfaces for hosted objects.
- Adds actions, 2D/3D placement and movement tools, single-arrow resize handles, and inspectors using shared dropdowns. Finishes are managed through the paint tool.
- Preserves feature ownership and attachments through duplication and deletion; wall split, merge, and reversal remap feature coordinates and refuse splits through a feature.
- Uses translucent previews with outer borders, protects previews during view handoff, and makes slab outline/hole drags save once with one undo step. Caches live slab ancestor frames across features.
- Fixes hosted-object rotation pivots and patches Drei HTML root cleanup to avoid synchronous unmount during React rendering.
- Adds plugin-owned create/update agent contracts and operations for both feature kinds; wall tools are registered in MCP with project installation gating. Slab tools are exported for hosts to register.
- Adds public documentation, regression tests, and wall/slab feature runtime benchmarks. Ordinary slab item drops retain level ownership and floor support.

Remaining scope: interactive acceptance for picking/batching, finishes, hosted objects, transformations, split view, reload and exported geometry; hosted-chat registration; slab host registration; semantic IFC mappings; complete UI-frame and boolean-rebuild performance checks. Curved walls, slab underside features, arbitrary overlapping stacks, automatic trim wrapping, and emissive niche strips are follow-up work. See `docs/wall-features-checklist.md` and `docs/slab-features.md`.

## How to test

1. Run the editor with `bun dev`. On a straight solid wall, use **Add niche** or **Add bump** on either face. On a slab, add a niche or bump on the top surface. Add a niche inside either kind of bump. Verify valid geometry and clear refusals for invalid bounds, overlaps, openings, or insufficient backing.
2. Move and resize features using the single-arrow handles and inspector in 3D and the floor plan. Switch views during movement, cancel, undo, and redo. Verify previews have translucent fills and outer borders, no diagonal lines, and each gesture produces one undo step.
3. Drag slab boundary and hole vertices/edges. Confirm features remain contained, invalid edits retain the last valid preview, and cancellation leaves the document unchanged.
4. Paint feature surfaces and place/rotate objects on a niche floor/shelf or bump top. Duplicate and transform the host, save/reload, and check finishes, rotation pivots, attachment positions, and hierarchy. Confirm ordinary drops on a slab stay level-parented with floor support.

Automated checks run: `bun run ci` (formatting, skills validation, types, all package tests, production builds), a fresh `bun run check-types`, 212 targeted slab/wall-feature tests, and feature runtime benchmarks.

The slab benchmark measures 100 features across 120 frames with an unchanged live slab override: both 1,000-node and 10,000-node scenes require one construction-lift scene scan. This measures frame resolution, not complete UI-frame time or boolean rebuild cost.

title: nodes: let hosts set the wall materials resolver
body:
`WallCutout` already accepts a `materialResolver`, but `WallSystems` hard-wires `getCurtainAwareWallMaterials`, so a host cannot restyle cut-away walls without forking the wall kind (plugins cannot re-register `wall`).

This adds `setWallMaterialsResolver(resolver | null)`, read by `WallSystems` through `useSyncExternalStore` (`null` restores the default), and exports `getCurtainAwareWallMaterials` so a host can wrap the default and replace one variant — for example a low stub in place of the translucent film for cut walls.

No behaviour change by default.

- `bun run check-types --filter=@pascal-app/nodes`: passes
- Biome on the three files: clean

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Default behavior is unchanged; changes are an optional host hook plus batch invalidation when the resolver changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hosts can now override how **WallCutout** picks wall material variants (visible, cut-away, translucent, delete) without forking the wall node kind.
> 
> **`setWallMaterialsResolver(resolver | null)`** registers a global **`WallMaterialsResolver`** (default unchanged: **`getCurtainAwareWallMaterials`**). **`WallSystems`** subscribes via **`useSyncExternalStore`** and passes the active resolver into **`WallCutout`**. **`getCurtainAwareWallMaterials`** is exported so hosts can wrap the default and tweak one variant (e.g. cut-away styling).
> 
> **`WallBatchSystem`** treats a resolver swap like other appearance inputs (themes, textures, material library), so merged per-level wall batches **re-sew** instead of keeping stale materials. A new test covers that re-sew path.

title: editor: Docker-ready self-hosting (image, runtime URL, admin password)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes the open-source editor deployable as a managed service, then finishes the standalone app so it reads as a product. Elestio reviewed it for their catalogue and listed three blockers; each is addressed inside `apps/editor`, the Dockerfile and the workflows. No package changes.

**Self-hosting (commit 1)**

- **Official image.** `ghcr.io/pascalorg/pascal-editor:<version>` (plus `latest` / `beta`), published by `release.yml` after the npm packages, built per architecture on native runners and merged into one manifest. Two-stage Dockerfile: bun build stage, then `node:22-alpine` holding the same portable runtime `stage-runtime` packs for the CLI. `docker-compose.yml` pulls the image. `docker.yml` builds and drives the image on PRs that touch what shapes it.
- **Public URL at runtime.** Server pages read the store directly instead of fetching their own HTTP API, so `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and the Vercel-era `BASE_URL` are gone. `PASCAL_PUBLIC_URL`, read per request with a forwarded-headers fallback, replaces `MINT_PASCAL_HOST_ORIGIN`; the CLI sets it from the instance URL.
- **Single-admin auth.** `PASCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD` gates every page behind `/login` (`proxy.ts`) and the scene API behind session-or-bearer (`PASCAL_SCENE_API_TOKEN` keeps working for agents). Sessions are HMAC tokens keyed by a digest of the password. A network host with nothing configured serves `/setup` only; `PASCAL_AUTH=proxy` defers to a reverse proxy; loopback stays open. Signed-in saves stamp `owner_id = admin`.

**Standalone app pass (commit 2)**

- **Home at `/`**: the scenes grid, dark like the editor chrome, with "New scene", a gear to `/settings`, and a card menu for rename and delete. `/scenes` redirects. The unsaved localStorage scratch canvas is gone; its Items tab and WebXR button move into the scene editor.
- **Editor navbar** via `navbarSlot`: Pascal logo back to home, inline rename (PATCH with If-Match, version kept in step with autosave), Preview. The floating "Light preview / All scenes" buttons are gone; `?disable=postFx` still works without UI.
- **`/settings`**: instance (public URL, version, data directory), connect an agent (scene API endpoint, token configured or not), sign out, source and docs links.
- **Thumbnails are real**: `POST/GET /api/scenes/[id]/thumbnail` stores a webp under the data directory; list and get fill `thumbnailUrl` from the file with no column write; a 30 s dirty-gated trigger in the app requests the capture after edits (armed only after hydration). The hosted product keeps its own trigger and storage; the editor package is untouched.
- **Hygiene**: `/privacy`, `/terms`, `vercel.json` removed; `Community…` toolbar components renamed.
- **Projects, not scenes** (commit 3): `/project/<id>` (old routes redirect), "New project" names `Project #n`, view-bar radius on the text buttons.
- **Public embeds** (commit 4): a Share button after Preview with a "Public link" switch (off by default), the link and an iframe snippet. The flag is a per-project file under the data directory; `GET /api/scenes/<id>/public` is the one unauthenticated scene read (plus the artifacts a shared scene references); `/embed/<id>` is the editor's Preview stage read-only (header, controls bar with walkthrough, 3D/2D/Split, compass, rooms, hover labels) opening on a fitted view, with `frame-ancestors *` and `noindex` and a "Made with Pascal" mark; `?ui=0` (the panel's "Hide controls" switch) keeps only the canvas.

One behaviour change: a dev server opened from another LAN device now shows the setup page instead of the editor. That flow already failed on save; `SETUP.md` documents the one-line fix.

## How to test

1. `docker build -t pascal-editor:local .` then `docker run -d -p 3000:3000 -v pascal-data:/data -e PASCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD=secret -e PASCAL_PUBLIC_URL=http://pascal.test:3000 pascal-editor:local`.
2. With a `Host: pascal.test:3000` header: `/api/health` is 200 without a session; `/` redirects to `/login`; `GET /api/scenes` is 401.
3. Sign in with `secret`: the home lists scenes; create one, rename it from the card menu and from the navbar, build something, wait ~35 s, go back home: the card shows the capture. Delete it from the card menu.
4. Click Share, turn on Public link, open the link in a private window: the project renders read-only with the name and the Pascal mark; turn it off and the same URL is 404.
5. `/settings` shows the public URL, the scene API endpoint and sign out. Sign out lands on `/login`.
6. `docker restart` the container and sign in again: scenes and thumbnails survive (volume).
7. Run the image with no `PASCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD`: a non-loopback `Host` lands on `/setup`; `http://127.0.0.1:3000/` on loopback is open.
8. `bun dev` on `localhost:3002` shows no login. `npx @pascal-app/cli editor` is unchanged apart from the renamed variable.
9. Automated and run: `bun test` in `apps/editor` (72 pass) and `packages/cli` (`runtime.test.ts`, 19 pass), `next typegen && tsc --noEmit` in `apps/editor`, `biome check`, the local docker build plus steps 2 to 6, and a Playwright drive of the thumbnail loop (edit → capture → stored webp → card).

title: Blender (bpy) modules as a second geometry-script language
body:
## What does this PR do?

An authored object, window, door or column can now be built from a Blender `bpy` module as well as a three.js one.

- **Schema:** `source.language` widens from `three` to `three | bpy` (old scenes still read as `three`). The module text is stored as `text/x-python` (`GEOMETRY_SCRIPT_MIME_TYPES`, `isGeometryScriptMimeType` replace the single mime constant).
- **Agent tools:** `add_object`, `add_window`, `add_door` and `add_column` take an optional `language`; on an edit it defaults to the object's own (`editedScriptLanguage`). `get_source` reports the language. The `add_object` description gains a short bpy section (module shape, the conventions in Blender terms).
- **`@pascal-app/geometry-script`:**
  - `bpy/runner.py` runs the module in an empty scene and exports a GLB.
  - `compileBlenderBuild` (`./blender`) loads that GLB into the same `finishBuild` a three.js build goes through (split out of `compileGeometryScript`), so the manifest, limits and conventions stay one implementation. It runs no model code and re-checks the params Blender resolved.
  - `runBlenderLocally` (`./blender-local`) runs a local Blender binary.
  - Tests are no longer emitted into `dist`.
- **Editor:** bpy builds go through a host-provided `BlenderScriptBuilder` (`configureBlenderScriptBuilder`); without one they are refused. The Parameters panel says "Rebuilding in Blender…". Nothing the sandbox worker reports sets the language.
- **MCP:** `GeometryScriptHost.compile`/`build` receive the language; local MCP runs bpy in the binary `PASCAL_BLENDER` names (opt-in, unsandboxed, like `PASCAL_SERVER_SCRIPT_COMPILE`).
- **Docs:** `wiki/architecture/authored-objects.md` (new "Blender modules" section), MCP README, `pascal-3d` skill.

Blender-specific handling, found by running Blender 5.2:
- GLTFLoader strips `:` from names. The reader restores them from `userData.name` after rebinding clip tracks to uuids.
- A material's viewport `diffuse_color` is carried to its shader when the shader still has the default colour.
- Blender light watts don't map onto Pascal's lights, so brightness is an `intensity` custom property (default 2).
- One action assigned to several objects becomes one clip.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/geometry-script && bun test`: `blender.test.ts` reads a committed Blender-exported fixture (cabinet: 3 parts, 2 slots, an anchor, a light, a two-door `open` clip). With Blender installed (`PASCAL_BLENDER` or the macOS default path), two more tests run the real binary.
2. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/tools/scripted-metadata.test.ts`: all four kinds store `text/x-python` for a bpy build and keep the language on an edit.
3. `cd packages/core && bun test src/agent-operations/geometry-metadata.test.ts`: the language rule, and old sources still parse as `three`.
4. End to end (done in the hosted app against Blender on Modal):
   - MCP `add_object` with `language: 'bpy'` built the cabinet in 3.5 s.
   - `get_source` returned the Python.
   - A params-only rebuild resized it.
   - A failing module returned `ValueError: … (line 3)`.
   - In the editor, the object rendered, the Parameters panel rebuilt it through Blender, and the ▷ control swung both doors.
