title: Interior views in view_scene, paint and search_materials with native scene materials
body:
## What

The E2 set from Adam's #1024, curated onto main. Two capabilities:

- `view_scene` can look inside a floor.
- `paint` and `search_materials` are shared agent tools, with native scene materials.

**Interior views (`view_scene`)**
- Contract (`core/agent-tools/view-scene.ts`): new input `interior: { levelId }`. The description only covers what main does; #1024's `request_upload` wording is gone.
- Plan (`core/agent-operations/scene-view.ts`): `sceneViewInterior(nodes, levelId)` returns the floor's box, a cut at 0.65 of the storey, and the ids to hide (the other floors, plus this floor's roofs and ceilings).
  - With no target, eye or camera, the view looks down into the floor from 55°.
  - It refuses:
    - `interior_level_invalid`: not a level, or a level holding only roofs and ceilings.
    - `interior_hidden`: the level or a parent is hidden. A hidden site doesn't count, because it only hides its own ground.
    - `interior_transform_unsupported`: a tilted building.
    - `interior_target_elsewhere`: a target on another floor, or one of this floor's roofs or ceilings.
  - The contract says what is cut: everything on the floor (walls, openings, furniture) at 0.65 of the storey height.
- Editor capture (`thumbnail-generator.tsx`): `interiorCutaway` runs inside the capture's existing set-up and restore cycle, for one render.
  - It hides those ids and clips the level at the cut height. Shadows are clipped too, so light gets into the rooms.
  - Walls are drawn whole whatever the user's wall mode, and the user's solo and isolation on that floor are lifted (`temporarilyShowPresentation`, new in the viewer).
  - The live view doesn't change.
- Whole walls for a capture now come from the viewer's `WallCutout`. An authored pose or an interior view emits `thumbnail:before-capture` with `{ wholeWalls: true }`, and `wallsForCapture` swaps each wall's palette using the resolver the renderer mounted, so a curtain wall keeps its glass. This replaces the capture's own swap, which used the plain wall palette.
- A capture that asks for its own perspective view (as `view_scene` does) stays perspective when the user's camera is orthographic (`capturesOrthographically`).
- MCP (`view-scene.ts`): passes `interior` on to its `SceneViewHost`.
- Two framing fixes from the same file in #1024:
  - A building that is moved or rotated on its site is framed where it actually stands.
  - A roof, or a roof level holding only roofs, now frames instead of being refused with `nothing_to_view`.

**`paint` and `search_materials`**
- `planWallPaint` and `plannedWallIds` move unchanged from `nodes/src/wall/paint-plan.ts` to `core/src/systems/wall/wall-paint-plan.ts`. The editor's hand paint and the agent's `paint` share one plan instead of #1024's copy.
- `paint` gives one finish to walls, columns, slabs, ceilings, fences, doors, windows and roofs. The finish is one of:
  - a colour (the nearest library colour, reported with how near it is);
  - a `library:` or `scene:` ref;
  - a native material;
  - erase.

  `role` picks the surface: a slot, a wall's `exterior` or `interior` face (worked out from the rooms on each side), or a roof's `top`, `edge` or `wall`.
  - A wall face is painted whole, the same way the editor's Paint writes a click on each part: the face's slot, plus an override in each room whose wall finish would otherwise show over it.
  - Painted parts (regions) keep their own finish, and the result's `note` names them.
  - An unknown target, role or material refuses the whole call. So does `exterior` or `interior` on a curtain wall. `shadowed_field` refuses a roof role that a segment's own finish would hide.
- Native materials are reused when the scene already holds one the material schema reads as equal; otherwise they become a new scene material through `SceneChanges.materials`. A host that can't store scene materials refuses them (`materials_unavailable`) but still paints refs and colours.
- `search_materials` finds library refs by words (timber is wood, render is stucco), by shade and by surface, and names the words nothing matched.
  - Words match whole words, or the start of a word from four letters (`tile` matches `tiles`).
  - Short and common words are dropped.
  - A flat colour passes every `surface` filter.
- Other core changes:
  - `AgentContext.materials` is new.
  - `requireMaterialRef` checks scene refs against the scene's materials, and its refusal now points to `search_materials`.
  - `get_node` returns the scene materials a node's finishes use.
  - `mergeSceneChanges` carries materials through.
- MCP:
  - `SceneBridge` takes `upsert_material` patches, written before the nodes in the same history step. This is an internal op, not part of `apply_patch`'s schema.
  - `supportsMaterialUpserts` and `getMaterials` are added on `SceneOperations`.
  - `paint` is registered as destructive and `search_materials` as read-only.
  - Updated to match: the annotation policy and justifications, the MCP README, the agent guide, the pascal-3d skill and `wiki/architecture/agent-surfaces.md`.

Not ported, on purpose:
- #1024's read-only capture transaction: per-node commit tracking in NodeRenderer, a frame-loop freeze, snapshots of camera controls and object state, and refusals on pending or failed assets. It also dropped the loader hooks that only fed it (`model-loader` resource failures, `ktx2-loader` load state). Interior views stay on the snapshot path `view_scene` already uses, which waits for the scene to build and holds the viewport's last frame. The asset-readiness and scene-revision gaps are on that path for every `view_scene` picture today (see Review).
- `material-swatches.ts` (only the facade elevation reads it; facades are held back).
- `sceneViewFacing` (Follow Pascal).
- The `run_batch` and plan-reference hooks.

## Why

From the owner's feedback (plan `plans/scene-agent/ai-architect-chat-feedback.md`, slice E-materials):

> **C14** "let's look at the latest PRs from Adam (AxiomeCG) and Steven Tibbs to bring them in: I also added images in the reference folder with commentary on some Steven's feature for generative UI and DXF import."

> **G2** "we need to compile and harmonize tools developped by Wassim, Adam (AxiomeCG), and Steven Tibbs from the AI capabilities to avoid conflicts, explosation in complexity, and increase reliability and consistency of outputs."

Adam's interior views and native materials come in as shared tools: one contract and one operation in core, so the chat and the MCP get the same `paint`, `search_materials` and `view_scene`. The editor's hand paint and the agent's paint now share one wall paint plan.

## How to test

From a checkout that has this branch as its `editor/` submodule (the commands run from the repo root):

```sh
bun test editor/packages/core/src/agent-operations/paint.test.ts editor/packages/core/src/agent-operations/search-materials.test.ts editor/packages/core/src/agent-operations/scene-view.test.ts
bun test editor/packages/mcp/src/tools/paint.test.ts editor/packages/mcp/src/tools/view-scene.test.ts editor/packages/mcp/src/tools/read-tool-annotations.test.ts
bun test editor/packages/viewer/src/lib/scene-visibility.test.ts editor/packages/viewer/src/systems/wall/wall-cutout-cache.test.ts editor/packages/editor/src/components/editor/thumbnail-generator.test.ts
bun test editor/packages/nodes/src/wall   # the hand paint on the moved plan: preview equals commit, room scope, erase
```

Results on this branch (head b5663692):
- core: 4061 pass.
- mcp: 704 pass.
- nodes: 4753 pass.
- viewer: 527 pass.
- editor: 2054 pass.
- check-types (`--force`): clean.
- biome: clean on the changed files.
- skills:validate and its policy tests: pass.

Viewer and editor show only the failures that happen without this branch too: the R3F version pin, and the `history.test.ts` subprocess stderr. Both come from the hosted install, not editor CI.

Checked in the running app on a two-storey test scene. The chat doesn't pass `interior` until the hosted bump, so this used a local hook that calls the chat's `executeViewScene` directly.
- First pass (before review):
  - Interior views of the ground floor, the upper floor and one room all came back. Each showed no other floor, no ceilings, walls cut low and light in the rooms.
  - A normal south-west view still shows the whole house.
  - `interior_target_elsewhere` and `interior_level_invalid` came back as refusals.
  - The live viewport was pixel-identical before and after the six calls.
- After review, on the same scene with its east ground-floor wall turned into a curtain wall:
  - The interior view of the ground floor shows the curtain wall's frame and glass, and so does a view from the east.
  - With the user's camera switched to orthographic, the interior view came back perspective from 55°. It was byte-identical to the same call made in perspective mode.
  - The live viewport matched before and after the calls: no pixel moved by more than 12/765.

## Deployment notes

- Merge this before the hosted H-roofs PR. That PR bumps the editor and wires `paint`, `search_materials` and `interior` into the chat and the hosted MCP. Until then the hosted app doesn't offer them.
- With this branch pinned, hosted's inventory tests fail until H-roofs registers the tools: `agent-surface-parity`, `hosted-mcp-tool-effects` and the hosted MCP tool count. That's expected.
- This branch is rebased on main 80d7a2f2. That includes #1033, whose geometry-script API change (`GEOMETRY_SCRIPT_MIME_TYPE`, `language`) breaks hosted typecheck on its own. Any hosted bump past #1033 needs that adaptation as well.
- This PR edits the same tool index files as the E-foundations editor PR (`agent-tools/index.ts`, `agent-operations/index.ts`, `mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.ts`). Whichever lands second rebases.
- For H-roofs and H-catalogue (G2), with this bump:
  - Pro's in-tab toolset calls `registerSharedTools` on a `SceneBridge`, so it gets `paint` and `search_materials`, with native materials. That puts them next to the Architect plugin's `set_material` and `list_materials`, which have different semantics: slots named interior/exterior, missing targets skipped. One of each pair has to be retired or routed to the other with the bump.
  - `search_materials` searches the built-in catalog only. Community and workspace materials (`library:mtl_…`, or registered at runtime) still need an owner before `list_materials` retires.
  - Nothing yet checks that `interior` reaches the capture on either host: the chat's `executeViewScene` and the hosted `SceneViewHost` both drop it today. Test it on both surfaces.
- `thumbnail:before-capture` now takes an optional `{ wholeWalls }` payload. Existing listeners that ignore it are unaffected.
- Env vars: none. Migrations: none.

## Review

Both reviews (Claude adversarial, GPT-6 Astra) were checked against the code.

Fixed:
- **paint on a room-finished wall.** It wrote a face slot that the room's wall finish hides, and still reported the paint. It now paints the face whole (see What). Tests check what the renderer resolves along the face after paint and after erase.
- **search_materials matched substrings.** `for` matched `forest`, `red` matched `prepared`, and `a` matched everything. It now matches whole words and drops short and common ones. A universal flat colour now passes a `surface` filter.
  - Surface words still only count materials made for that surface. Counting flat colours too flooded "light oak floor" with presets.
- **Roofs on an interior view.** An interior of a roof-only level, or a roof or ceiling target, framed something the picture leaves out. Both are now refused.
- **Hidden site.** A hidden site blocked interior views, but it only hides its own ground. It no longer counts.
- **Contract wording.** It said only walls are cut; everything on the floor is cut at 0.65. Fixed in the contract, README, agent guide, skill and wiki.
- **Orthographic live camera.** It replaced `view_scene`'s requested perspective camera.
- **Curtain walls in captures.** An interior or authored-pose capture lost their glass. Whole walls now come from `WallCutout`'s own resolver.
- **Curtain wall faces.** `exterior` and `interior` on a curtain wall wrote unused face slots. They are now refused.

Not changed:
- **Asset readiness, and camera vs. cutaway revision** (Astra).
  - Every `view_scene` and sheet capture already waits for the scene to build, then renders. The interior view adds no new path.
  - #1024's capture transaction, which gated on asset readiness, is held back from this PR on purpose.
  - A pending or failed-asset refusal for `view_scene` as a whole is a follow-up.
- **`library:mtl_…` refs pass without a check** (Astra). That is main's behaviour, unchanged here: the host checks community refs against its catalog. Scene refs are now checked whenever the host lends its materials.
- **MCP receipts under `readOnly`** (Astra). This is in the shared runner and affects every mutating shared tool, not just `paint`, so it is out of scope for this PR.
- **Other buildings' floors are hidden in an interior view** (Bugbot). This is intended: the picture shows one floor, and a neighbouring building's floors, uncut, would block the look down into it.
- **A fourth "equal scene material" matcher** (Claude nit). Follow-up: make hand paint's three `findMatchingSceneMaterial` copies use core's normalising matcher, so agent-made materials aren't duplicated by hand paint.

## Supersedes

Supersedes in part #1024 by Adam NAILI (@AxiomeCG): its E2 set (interior captures and native materials). Adam is co-author on every commit that ports his work. The rest of #1024's curated set (E1) comes in a separate PR. Plan reference, vectorize, facades, unit layouts, photo tools, coherence, batch/checkpoints, visual references and `request_upload` are held back.

title: editor: the rail panel and preferences survive a reload
body:
## What

The editor's UI preferences now survive a reload, including the open rail panel.

- **Fix: a write before rehydrate no longer overwrites the stored preferences.** `useEditor` and `useSidebarStore` persist through a new `hydrationGatedStorage` (`lib/hydration-gated-storage.ts`), which drops writes until the store has rehydrated. The cause: zustand `persist` saves the whole state on every `set`, hydrated or not. The editor rehydrates in a mount effect, and a host's own mount effects run before it (Community calls `setCanFindNode` first). So since `skipHydration` (#461), every reload saved the defaults over the stored blob and then read them back. That reset the rail panel, phase, view layouts, pinned views, snapping, grid step and reference floor.
- **Each workspace remembers its own rail panel.** The stored blob keeps `sidebarPanels` (the last panel picked per workspace) in place of `activeSidebarPanel`. `setActiveSidebarPanel` records the pick and `setWorkspaceMode` reopens that workspace's panel. A reload opens Edit on Edit's last panel; the workspace itself is not restored.
- **The rail no longer resets the pick.** The desktop and mobile layouts used to write the first tab over a stored panel the rail did not have yet: a plugin panel registers once the scene's plugins load, and Studio swaps the tabs. The new `useShownSidebarPanel` (`lib/sidebar-panel.ts`) shows the first panel until the stored one arrives and leaves the pick alone. A workspace with nothing picked yet adopts the tab it shows.
- **Mobile:** tapping Items arms the item tool. An Items tab restored on load opens in select mode.
- `wiki/architecture/plugin-authoring.md` now describes the rail memory and the rule for hosts: a write to a persisted field before the editor mounts has to wait for `useEditor.persist.onFinishHydration`.

## Why

From the owner's feedback on the hosted editor (plan row D1, quoted verbatim):

> D1: "Editor active sidebar menu or open menu should remain in state and survive page reload (like if user is on chat it should remember where when reload or navigated to another part of the web app)"

The decision on workspaces: a reload lands in Edit, on the last panel used in Edit.

## How to test

1. Open a project and pick a rail panel other than the first (e.g. Chat or Scene). Reload: the same panel is open.
2. Collapse the panel by clicking its rail icon again, then reload: the panel stays collapsed. Click any icon and it expands.
3. Split the stage (2D | 3D) or change the phase, then reload: both come back.
4. In a host with a second workspace (Community's Studio), open a panel in each workspace, then switch back and forth: each workspace reopens its own panel. A reload opens Edit on Edit's panel.
5. Open a plugin's rail panel and reload. The first panel shows until the plugin registers, then the plugin panel opens. If the plugin is gone, the first panel stays.
6. Mobile (390 px): tap Items and the item tool arms. Reload: Items is the active tab and select mode is on.

Automated, run from the private-editor worktree root against this branch:
- `bun test editor/packages/editor/src/store/opens-in-select-mode.test.ts`: 9 pass. The new repro fails without the storage gate (Expected "ai", Received "build").
- `bunx turbo run check-types --filter='./editor/packages/*'`: 9/9.
- `biome check` on the changed files with this repo's config: clean.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added here. The behaviour was checked in the running Community app at 1440x900 and 390x844; screenshots are listed in the hosted PR.

## Deployment notes

- **Merge order:** merge this PR first. The hosted PR (pascalorg/private-editor) bumps the gitlink to this branch, and the landing step re-bumps it to this PR's merge commit.
- **Stored preferences:** in `pascal-editor-ui-preferences`, `sidebarPanels` replaces `activeSidebarPanel`, and the old field is ignored. A user's first load after deploy opens on the first panel, which is what the bug did on every load anyway.
- Env vars: none. Migrations: none.

## Supersedes

Nothing.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (tested through the Community dev server, not this repo's `bun dev`)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) (`biome check` on the changed files)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)

title: Docker: OCI labels, hermetic build context, README self-host section
body:
## What does this PR do?

Prepares the first GHCR publish of `ghcr.io/pascalorg/pascal-editor` after #1032.

- **OCI labels** on the runtime image: title, description, `source` (links the GHCR package to this repository, so the package page shows the README and inherits access), `documentation`, `url`, `vendor`, `licenses: MIT`. The release job also stamps `version` and `revision`.
- **Hermetic build context**: `.dockerignore` now drops `*.tsbuildinfo`. A stale host file copied into the context made `tsc --build` trust it and skip emitting core's new `geometry-metadata` module (#1033), so `docker build` on main failed with "Cannot resolve extensionless ESM import ./geometry-metadata". CI never saw it because runners start clean.
- **README**: a "Self-host it" section with the one-line `docker run` and a link to SETUP.md.

1. `docker build -t pascal-editor:labels .` on this branch succeeds (it fails on main from a checkout that has built locally).

title: Editing foundations: roofs on the building's roof level, add_fence shared, corner-window editing and review fixes
body:
## What does this PR do?

One rule for where a roof lives, by hand and by agent, on top of Bundle 2's tools (#1024, now on `main`), plus `add_fence` as a shared tool, the corner-window editing that Bundle 2 left out, and the review fixes to the editing code both branches shipped.

- **Roofs live on the building's roof level.** One core service, `services/roof-level.ts`: a roof lives on the level directly above the storey whose walls carry it; over the top storey that is the building's roof level (`metadata.role: 'roof'`, named Roof), kept above every storey, so exploded and solo views lift the roof off the plan.
  - `planRoofLevel`: a storey built anywhere above takes a lower wing's roof on the storey directly above; else the roof level above every level still to be built and every support level; else the empty level directly above when it is the only one, declared; else a new Roof level on top. A support level is never declared the roof level.
  - Bundle 2's shared `create_roof` keeps its footprint (the walls' outline with gaps bridged, else floor plates, else rooms), the mitre limit and the fascia, and seats its roof through `planRoofLevel`, on the storey's wall tops; a roof level it makes is as tall as the roof rises over it, the eave's lift included, and its answer carries `ok: true`. It refuses `roof_exists`, `storey_above`, `building_required` (several buildings, none named) and `storey_without_building`. Overlapping floor plates are one footprint. The result names `coveredLevelId`; no `referenceLevelId` metadata is written, since the rule derives it.
  - `servesAsRoofLevel` is the one test of a level's role (a declared support level stays one, roofs on it or not): `levelRole` (so `list_levels` and `verify_scene`), the agents' `roof_level` refusals and `storeyInsertIndex` read it. A declared roof level someone walled stays the roof level everywhere.
  - Which storey a roof covers is derived (`coveredStoreyId`, `roofsOver`), so a porch roof on the upper storey does not stop `create_roof` capping it. A lower wing's roof that follows walls follows the walls below only (the upper storey's wall along its edge lifted it to that storey's eaves).
  - `add_level` and the editor's "add a floor" (level selector, Settings, site tree, command palette) put a new storey under the roof level, which moves up one in the same undo step. The level selector's top "+" reads "Add a floor under the roof" when a roof level tops the stack, inserts between two levels in one step, and refuses a drag that puts a roof level under a storey.
  - The hand Roof tool follows the rule: a room footprint, a rectangle drawn on a walled storey and a cone over a curved wall go on the level above the walls, standing on them; the ghost shows where the roof lands, and the roof's level is selected with it so it stays in view.
  - `verify_scene` reports `roof_level_not_on_top` (replacing Bundle 2's `roof_level_below_reference`), counting an empty storey above; `roof_mixed_in_storey` only for a roof covering its own storey. Existing scenes are not migrated.
  - Unpainted gables on a roof level take the cladding of the storey below. The site plan draws the roof line from every level and does not count the roof level as a storey.
- **`add_fence` is one shared contract and operation**: a fence through points, one per side, `closed` for a lot's boundary, privacy by default; it refuses a side under 10 cm and a roof level, and runs in `run_batch` like `add_wall`. Bundle 2 kept the hosted chat's own one-segment `add_fence`; this replaces it (pascalorg/private-editor#903 registers it in the chat).
- **Corner-window editing Bundle 2 left out.** The plan draws a corner pair through its corner (mitred, not a wall post) and outlines a waiting window on hover; a window dragged in the plan joins a corner as in 3D; a preset placed at a corner in the plan stays joined; Merge windows says why in the editor's words and units; the HUD's note at a free wall end is a "!" row; an edit a pair shares is one undo step. The corner-snap HUD state moves from core to the editor store (#1024's own list asked for it).
- **Review fixes on the corner windows, rooms and storey heights** (Bundle 2's code and this branch's):
  - A corner pair holds only while both sides reach their corner end, on walls of one level meeting there at 10°–170°. Deleting one side, dragging it off its corner or copying it alone leaves the other plain; a duplicated level, or both walls pasted together, keep the copies joined. A frame built for a pair that broke is rebuilt.
  - `add_corner_window` reads the walls of one level (`levelId`, default the floor in view): stacked storeys share corner points, so a two-storey house was refused or joined across floors.
  - Only a fixed window's glass fuses (`corner_not_fused`); the panel offers Fused glass / Corner post for a fixed window only. A side resized to its whole wall keeps its pair. A same-wall merge keeps the union. Wrap the corner refuses a flat or folded angle. A waiting window the join would refuse is a "!" row ("Another opening is in the way at the corner", "The window waiting there is taller than this wall"). Two windows that already wrap their corner get Unwrap the corner.
  - Corner snapping follows the snapping mode, releasing Alt brings it back without moving the pointer, and the window tools' keys (Alt included) ignore typing targets. The panel no longer plans a wrap on every scene update; its Corner buttons have a focus ring and press state.
  - `set_zone` over a walled room is that room (a retry is a no-op; a room a person named otherwise is refused). A level created in a patch gets the height its outer `parentId` gives. `achieved` counts each node once, and only when it changed. `verify_scene`'s `corner_unjoined` and `corner_partner_missing` are notes pointing at `merge_windows`.
- Comments say why, without bench runs, ticket ids or dates.

## Reconciled with Bundle 2

Rebuilt on editor `main` (`c69d1d33`: #1024, then #1042, #1043 and #1041) instead of carrying the two merges of `main`. The one conflict, #1041's light hover on the Corner buttons, takes this branch's token classes, which work in both themes.

- **Dropped, already on `main`:** the port of sill centring, named rooms, storey heights, and corner/merged windows (contracts, operations, snap, fuse, the viewer's corner cut); the MCP's single `create_roof` registration; the lines that only existed because the old base lacked Bundle 2's additions.
- **Kept:** the roof-level service and every user of it (above), with Bundle 2's `create_roof` rebuilt on it rather than replaced: `roofHost` gives way to `planRoofLevel`, and Bundle 2's footprint, mitre limit, fascia and tests stay; `add_fence`; the corner editing above; the HUD state moved to the editor; this branch's fixes to Bundle 2's corner code (labels, token hover, `writeWindowChanges`, `corner_unjoined` as a note).
- **Changed against Bundle 2's decisions, for the owner:** `add_fence` becomes shared (Bundle 2 kept the chat's own); an empty level directly above the storey, alone at the top, becomes the roof level (Bundle 2 roofed above it, leaving the roof a storey up from its walls); `roof_level_below_reference` becomes `roof_level_not_on_top`; the result field is `coveredLevelId`, not `referenceLevelId`.

## Why

The owner's feedback (2026-10-12):

- **G1** "in ai chat often the architect create a roof on the same level as the ground floor, preventing exploded view or obstructing the layout entirely."
- **C19** "…every time we build with an LLM, it actually places the roof system on the same level as its supporting walls. That's not what we have intended for exploded view or obstructions… There should be a roof or a level dedicated for the roof system so we can appropriately see the floor plan without having the roof segments obstructing our view inside the home."
- **G2** "we need to compile and harmonize tools developped by Wassim, Adam (AxiomeCG), and Steven Tibbs from the AI capabilities to avoid conflicts, explosation in complexity, and increase reliability and consistency of outputs."

Decision (plan §3): "Roofs: one rule by hand and by agent — a roof lives on the level directly above the storey whose walls carry it; over the top storey that is the building's 'Roof' level. Existing projects are not migrated; `verify_scene` reports them."

## How to test

1. One-storey house: Roof tool, "Room" footprint, click inside the room → a **Roof** level appears above Ground floor and is selected with the roof, which stays in view (3D and 2D); exploded view lifts the roof; solo Ground floor shows no roof. Undo removes both. Site plan: the dashed roof line, "1-STORY RESIDENCE".
2. Level selector "+" on that house (it reads "Add a floor under the roof") → the new storey goes under Roof; Roof moves up with the roof. One undo removes the floor and moves Roof back. Dragging Roof under a storey snaps back.
3. Two-storey house, ground-floor wing beside the upper volume: Roof tool on the ground floor, "Room" on the wing → the roof goes on First floor at the wing's eaves, not the upper storey's.
4. Window tool near a wall end where another window waits → the ghost snaps, the waiting window is outlined, the HUD reads "Join as a corner window"; click → one corner window. Alt, or snapping Off → plain. Drag a window in the plan to that corner → joined. Delete one side → the other is a plain window, framed at the corner.
5. Two windows selected → Merge windows, or the reason in words and the project's units; a joined pair → Unwrap the corner.
6. MCP: `create_roof` on a one-storey scene → roof on a new Roof level; again → `roof_exists`; `add_level` → `shiftedLevelIds` names the roof level; `add_fence` with five points and `closed: true` → five fences. `add_corner_window` on a two-storey house with `levelId` → both sides on that floor.

Ran, from the hosted worktree with this head pinned (pascalorg/private-editor#903 on hosted `main` `734519e74`):
- `bunx turbo run check-types --filter='./editor/packages/*'` (9/9) and the dists' build.
- `bun test` by package: core 4,389, MCP 812, nodes 4,805 and viewer 667 pass; editor 2,444 pass, with the 19 `lib/history.test.ts` subprocess tests failing on THREE's CJS deprecation warning in stderr, as on the base.
- `biome check` (editor config) on every changed file.
- The hosted typecheck, suite (25/25), `bun check` and `ci:contracts` with this pin.

Earlier rounds checked steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 in the running app, in both themes (screenshots on #903 and `/tmp/feedback-work/foundations/shots`); this round changes no UI beyond the "+" title, the Corner section's fixed-only post choice and the Unwrap action.

## Screenshots / screen recording

From the verify round, in dark and a light preview: the Room footprint preview and the roof on its Roof level; the ground floor's plan with the roof level above; exploded view; "+" inserting Floor 1 under Roof; the corner snap; the corner window; the Corner section; the merge note; the HUD's "!" row; the plan's mitred corner.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

## Deployment notes

- The hosted app follows with the SHA bump in pascalorg/private-editor#903: its chat registers `add_fence` from the shared contract and drops its own; its MCP inventory classifies `add_fence` (the package's 82nd tool). A bare bump fails its parity test, so #903 is the bump. pascalorg/private-editor#915 (the bare bump) is closed.
- Scene format: one optional field, `window.corner`, already on `main` from #1024. No new fields.
- Env vars: none. Migrations: none.

## Review

Reviewed with #903 by an adversarial review and GPT-6 Astra, on the pre-Bundle-2 head `591efd5f`; every finding was checked again against this head.

Fixed: stale `corner` links after delete, drag and copy; `add_corner_window` across storeys and its `widths`; roof-only ground levels in `storeyInsertIndex`; `fuseAtCorner` swallowing every error and the HUD promising a join that would be refused; the "+" title under a roof level; the two definitions of a roof level; the panel's per-update wrap plan; `add_fence`'s `search_materials` and `raised` descriptions; unused corner exports; the Corner buttons' focus ring; incident stories in `roof-footprint.ts`; the README's `create_roof` row; patch heights ignoring an outer `parentId`; a lower-wing roof counted over the upper storey; a lower-wing roof lifted onto the upper storey's walls; a drawn rectangle not following its walls; level and clipboard copies breaking pairs; pairs surviving moved walls; disagreeing corner validity across paths; fused glass offered to framed types; a side resized to its wall breaking its pair; a declared roof level reused under a storey; `building_required` skipped on empty buildings; `set_zone` stacking a second zone on a retry; same-wall merges shrinking the union; `achieved` counting repeats and no-ops; snapping ignoring the snap mode and Alt release; typing targets in the window tools' handlers. The Corner section's segmented control in light mode is fixed on `main` by #1041 (light classes, `aria-pressed`); the Corner buttons use tokens.

Bugbot on this head, fixed: the roof level `create_roof` makes was not tall enough for a lifted eave; `create_roof` had no `ok`; a declared support level holding a roof was read as the roof level. Bugbot, not changed: "placement still promises refused corner joins" (the window tool always passes its draft as `ignoreId`, so the preflight runs on placement too); "corner snap swallows other merge refusals" (after the angle, pair and reach checks before it, `mergeWindows` can only refuse `height_exceeds_wall` or `opening_overlap` there, both mapped); "fascia material skips library check" (`main`'s `create_roof` already validates it).

Not fixed, and why:
- **The terrace over a walled numbered room becomes that room** instead of being refused. That is `main`'s behaviour (Bundle 2) and the intent: a walled courtyard drawn as a terrace is the outdoor room. It is now documented in `terrace-draft.ts` and `space-detection.md`.
- **The level selector's refused drop has no message.** The selector has no invalid-drop feedback to reuse; the level returns to its place.
- **`achieved` over the MCP counts the planned changes, not the bridge's settled state.** That is Bundle 2's design for every shared tool; reading the settled state is a change to the MCP's apply path, not this PR's.
- **The agent can't roof a lower wing** (`storey_above`); the hand tool can, and now seats it on the wing's walls. Where a lower-wing roof shows in solo views is the owner's call.
- **No repair for existing scenes.** Plan §3: not migrated; `verify_scene` reports them.

## Builds on

Adam's #1024 (Bundle 2), now on `main`; co-authored by Adam NAILI (@AxiomeCG).

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core scene semantics (roof placement, level stacking, corner-window pairing) across agents, MCP, and editor; incorrect edge cases could corrupt multi-storey or multi-building scenes, though fixture tests cover many paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> Unifies **where roofs live** in a shared `roof-level` service (`planRoofLevel`, `roofsOver`, `storeyInsertIndex`, `isRoofLevel` / `servesAsRoofLevel`). **`create_roof`** now places roofs on the building’s roof level above the capped storey, seats them on wall tops via elevation resolution, refuses duplicate roofs and non-top storeys, unions overlapping slabs for footprint, and can require `building_required` on multi-building sites. **`add_level`** inserts new storeys under the roof level and shifts roof levels up.
> 
> Adds shared **`add_fence`** (agent operation + tool + fixture cases). **Corner windows** gain per-level targeting (`targetLevel`), casement vs fused-glass rules (`fusesAtCorner`, `corner_not_fused`), stale partner link cleanup in merge/wrap/snap, and informational `verify_scene` hints pointing at **`merge_windows`**. **Same-wall merge** uses the union of spans (nested windows) and clears broken corner links.
> 
> **`achievedChanges`** counts each node at most once and treats no-op updates as unchanged. **`level-height-fill`** respects create `parentId` when deriving heights. **`levelRole`** defers roof classification to `servesAsRoofLevel`. **`verify_scene`** adds `roof_level_not_on_top` and narrows `roof_mixed_in_storey` via `roofsOver`. Extensive declarative **agent fixture tables** (`CREATE_ROOF`, `ADD_FENCE`, corner/merge cases) wire into the shared case runner.

title: editor: host select/frame/unit exports; the plan frames a node alone and lights what a chat points at
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a host surface select and show a scene node the way the editor's own lists do. The plan frames a node when it is the only view on screen, and it lights what a host's chat points at.

- `selectZoneOrRoom`, `frameViewerNode`, `enterUnitFocus` and `PLUGINS_VIEW_ID` are exported from `@pascal-app/editor`.
  - `selectZoneOrRoom` selects a zone by the Rooms list's rule: an enclosed room as the room, anything else as the zone.
  - `frameViewerNode` is the navigation's framing (the node's saved view, else its box in the scene).
  - `enterUnitFocus` focuses a unit as the site panel does.
  - `PLUGINS_VIEW_ID` is the plugin directory's view, for `openEditorView`.
- `FloorplanPanel` answers `camera-controls:frame` itself while no 3D view is visible.
  - The request waits for the selection it came with to render, so a node on another floor or in another building is placed with that building's transform, after the floor change has reset the view.
  - After a floor change the glide starts from the new floor's view, so the plan never shows the whole floor for a frame and then snaps.
  - It fits the node's box to the pane at the current turn and aspect: the box's rotated corners against both dimensions, plus the plan's usual 2 m padding.
  - A saved view with no box centres on its target at the current zoom.
  - With a 3D view on screen nothing changes: the plan keeps following the framed camera's pose.
- A frame request now carries the node's box as well as its saved view. The 3D camera still frames the saved view; the plan frames the box.
- Under reduced motion, framing jumps to its pose in 3D and in the plan (`framingAnimates`).
- What a host's chat points at (`useViewer.pointedIds`, Bundle 2's slot for chat chips) now lights beyond the 3D outline.
  - The plan's registry entries draw a pointed node as they draw a hovered one: an entry lights when its own node is pointed, or its hover target (the selection proxy, the building in the site phase).
  - A single pointed zone shows the room outline a hovered zone does (`room-highlight.tsx`). With zones hidden a zone draws nothing of its own, so the point outline had nothing to trace.
  - A pointed zone shows over a room kept selected, as the editor's own hover does. The kept room returns when the pointing ends.
- `wiki/architecture/selection-managers.md` and `point-and-ask.md` describe all of it.

## Why

The hosted Architect chat now draws the nodes a reply names as references (pascalorg/private-editor#900, slice H-entities). Hover lights the node, and a click selects and frames it. The owner's feedback of 2026-10-12, verbatim:

> C10: "introduce rich message text with interactive and icon rich highlighted entities (see image examples): tool calls, scene graph node mentions, project version mentions, and more"
>
> S5: "rich clickable icon highlighted text intead of unreadable low contrast inline code"
>
> C23: "here are renders example of interactive highlighted mentions, we should make the right abstractions so we can change the style over time if we need." (renders: tooltip "Highlight & focus camera"; footnote "Click an entity to highlight it and focus the camera.")

Each export closes a gap the running app showed:
- Without `selectZoneOrRoom`, a host could only set `selection.zoneId`, which opened a room as a bare zone.
- A box a host computes from the graph misses saved views and a moved or turned building. `frameViewerNode` has neither problem.
- A unit is not selectable on its own; without `enterUnitFocus` a host put its id in `selectedIds`, where no selection manager acts on it.
- The plugin directory is a view, not a sidebar panel. Setting the sidebar to `plugins` showed nothing.

The plan change is the 2D half of the same click (E-006). Before it, a node clicked in a list while only the plan was on screen stayed wherever it was, often off screen. This applies to `camera-controls:frame` only: the scene tree's double-click focuses through `camera-controls:focus`, which the plan does not answer, so it keeps its current behaviour.

The `pointedIds` change is the 2D half of a chat's hover. The host now lights every chat chip through that one slot (references, Point and ask's elements, step cards), so they never fight the editor's own `hoveredId`. Before this, a pointed node lit only in 3D, and a pointed room not at all.

## How to test

1. Open a project with a few rooms and show the plan alone (2D, no split).
2. Zoom into a corner, then select a far room from a host surface that frames (the hosted chat's reference, or `frameViewerNode(id, source)`). The plan glides to the room and fits it, at the same rotation.
3. Do the same for a door: the plan centres on it with about 2 m around it.
4. Turn on the OS's reduced motion and repeat: the plan and the 3D camera jump instead of gliding.
5. Split 2D + 3D and repeat. The 3D camera frames the node and the plan follows it, as before.
6. Hover a wall's reference in the hosted chat with the plan on screen: the wall is stroked in the plan. Hover a room's reference in 3D: its outline shows.

Checks run (from the hosted worktree root, at `111612ee`):
- `bunx turbo run check-types --filter='./editor/packages/*'`: 9/9.
- Biome on the changed files, with the editor's config.

title: editor: light chrome that follows the host's theme
body:
## What

The editor no longer forces its chrome dark. It sets no theme of its own and follows the host's `.dark` class, so a host can offer a light editor.

- **No forced dark.** The `document.body.classList.add('dark')` mount effect is gone, and so is `dark` on the v1, v2 and mobile layout roots, the app sidebar, the mobile panel sheet and the riser diagram panel.
- **Light counterparts, dark unchanged.** About 75 editor and nodes files: every dark-only chrome literal gets a light base, and the original value stays under `dark:`. For example, `bg-[#2C2C2E]` becomes `bg-black/4 dark:bg-[#2C2C2E]`, white tints become black tints, and pale inks become -700/-800 in light. The riser diagram's waste and vent colours are CSS variables with a darker light value.
- **Caller overrides still win.**
  - `ActionButton` (controls) runs its fill through custom properties, so a caller's `bg-*` or `hover:bg-*` (red delete hovers, `bg-primary` buttons) replaces it in both themes.
  - Ghost-variant dock buttons leave the dark hover to the variant, as before.
  - Where a caller resets a state under `disabled:hover:`, the reset is repeated under `dark:disabled:hover:`, because `dark:hover:*` ties with it and is emitted later.
- **Rail selection.** The selected and hover states use `bg-sidebar-accent`. It equals `accent` in dark and shows on the light sidebar.
- **What stays dark in either theme:**
  - the Preview stage, the walkthrough HUD and the viewer scene header;
  - the controls bar and the stage switcher;
  - the controls bar's dropdown menus and tooltips, which portal to `<body>` (the action-menu `ActionButton` takes a `tooltipClassName` for this);
  - the snapshot viewfinder, including its level picker;
  - the scene-graph viewer dialog, which draws its own dark viewer;
  - the Point and ask layer over the canvas, which draws its own dark colours.
- **Interface theme row.** `InterfaceThemeRow` (`{ value, onChange }`) is the System / Light / Dark "Interface theme" row, exported with `InterfaceTheme` like `SettingsSwitchRow`. A host that owns the setting passes it through `SettingsPanel`'s `preferences` slot; a host that passes nothing gets no row. `SegmentedControl` buttons report `aria-pressed`.
- **Bundle 2's new controls.** The Point and ask button, the Follow Pascal toggle and its "Resume following" pill, and the window inspector's Wrap / Unwrap corner buttons get light values, with their dark values kept under `dark:`. Follow Pascal also sits in the Preview controls bar, so it takes a `tooltipClassName` and the bar passes `dark`.
- **"Scene theme".** The viewer's Display submenu now reads "Scene theme", so it isn't confused with the interface theme.
- **The open-source app keeps its look.** `SceneLoader` is the one page that mounts the editor. Its root carries `dark` from the first paint, and it adds `dark` to `<body>` while mounted for the menus the editor portals there, as the editor used to do itself. The home, login, settings and setup pages keep their own theme.
- **Test hygiene.** `lib/sfx-player.test.ts` sets the real audio store's state instead of mocking `../store/use-audio` for the whole process.
- **Wiki:** `wiki/architecture/materials-and-themes.md`.

## Why

Owner feedback of 2026-10-12, row D2 (verbatim):

> D2 · "introduce light mode for the editor (default system sync, allow override reuse theme config from the main app nav pages)"

This is slice E-theme of the feedback plan: "The host owns the theme: no forced `dark`, light counterparts for every dark-only literal (dark stays pixel-identical), an "Interface theme" row in Settings". It follows the plan's decision "Light mode: Studio stays dark; presentation HUDs stay dark; the 3D scene keeps its own theme."

## How to test

1. Open a project in a host that sets no `.dark` class: the chrome is light. That covers the navbar slot, rail, panels, inspectors, action dock and its popovers, level selector, view bar, split view, helper HUD and dialogs. With `dark` on `<html>` or `<body>`, it renders as before.
2. In dark, check these computed values:
   - an inspector `ActionButton` is `rgb(44, 44, 46)` and hovers to `rgb(62, 62, 62)`;
   - its Delete variant hovers red (`red-500/20`);
   - the slab and ceiling `bg-primary` buttons stay primary;
   - a disabled segment has no hover tint;
   - a block's disabled slot delete stays muted on hover;
   - the dock's camera buttons hover to `accent/50`, as before.
3. In light, select an elevator. Turn on Service and Disabled for a level and look at the current Destination tile: every label reads. The storey heights in the level selector read too.
4. In light, take a snapshot (⌘K → "Take Snapshot") on a building with two levels: "Levels in the shot" is dark, like the rest of the viewfinder. In Preview, the controls' tooltips look the same in both themes.
5. Pass `<InterfaceThemeRow value=… onChange=… />` through `SettingsPanel`'s `preferences`: Preferences shows the row with the current value pressed, after the construction animation. Without it there is no row.
6. In light, with a host that answers Point and ask: the Point and ask button (C) and Follow Pascal show a lavender or violet tint with a deep ink when on, and a readable ink on hover when off. In dark they look as on main.
7. Open-source app: open `/project/<id>`. The editor and its menus are dark; `/` and `/settings` are not.

Checks run on this head (beef29fb, on editor main 35a49051), from the hosted worktree root (the editor is its submodule):
- `bunx turbo run check-types --filter='./editor/packages/*'`: 9/9 passed.
- Biome with the editor's config on the 47 changed files: clean.
- `bun test editor/packages/nodes/src`: 4797 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test editor/packages/editor/src`: 2432 pass, 19 fail. All 19 are `lib/history.test.ts` subprocess checks: run from the host root, their stderr carries three's `THREE_CJS_DEPRECATED` warning. This branch touches no history code.
- `bun test editor/packages/editor/src/components/ui/sidebar/panels/settings-panel`: 7 pass.

**Visual QA.** I ran the hosted app with this branch in light and dark, at 1440 px and 390 px. The first pass covered every surface in step 1, plus the profile menu, command palette, Studio and Preview. The review round (below) found more editor defects, now fixed and re-checked in the running app:
- elevator access and destination states;
- tile surfaces and storey heights;
- the snapshot viewfinder's level picker;
- Preview tooltips;
- the "Scene theme" label.

The riser diagram can't be opened from the hosted UI, so its colour variables were checked by computed style: light `rgb(3, 105, 161)` and `rgb(147, 51, 234)`; dark `#0ea5e9` and `#a855f7` as before. Dark crops of the sidebar, level selector, navbar and dock are pixel-identical to the screenshots taken before the fixes.

After the rebase on Bundle 2 I re-checked the new controls in the running hosted app, in both themes: the dock with Point and ask on and Follow Pascal on, off and hovered, and Settings → Preferences with the construction animation, the theme row and the host's rows. Computed values: Point and ask on is `rgb(93, 73, 223)` on `#a99bff` at 20% in light and `rgb(201, 193, 255)` in dark, as on main; hovered it takes the ghost variant's `accent` fill and ink in both themes, as on main.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Local QA screenshots for both themes are listed in pascalorg/private-editor#901.

## Review

Reviewed adversarially by Claude and GPT-6 Astra.

Fixed:
- **Elevator selected states** kept their dark-only -100 inks and were invisible in light. Each now has a -700 or -800 light ink.
- **The block slot's disabled delete** turned red on hover in dark. It now has a `dark:disabled:hover:` reset.
- **Warning and accent inks** (solar panel, cabinet, item, floor plan notice, measurement, panel extensions, property line) are -700 in light. At -600 they fell below 4.5:1.
- **The snapshot viewfinder** carries `dark`, so the level picker matches it. The picker's light variant is dropped.
- **Viewer tooltips** in Preview get `dark` through `tooltipClassName`.
- **The riser diagram's** waste and vent colours have darker light values.
- **Tiles** (build tools, item categories, tool options) get a light surface.
- **Storey heights** read in light.
- **"Scene theme".** The viewer's Display submenu is renamed.
- **The SFX player test** no longer leaks its audio-store mock.
- **The endpoint drag pill**, found while checking the elevator, reads in light.
- **No light flash in the open-source app** (Cursor Bugbot): the editor page's root carries `dark`, so its first paint is dark.

Not changed:
- The rail's selected fill: it keeps `bg-sidebar-accent`. The active tab already changes its icon from grey to full colour and adds a shadow, so selection does not depend on the tint.

## Deployment notes

- **Merge this first.** pascalorg/private-editor#901 is re-bumped to this PR's merge commit when it lands.
- **Hosted pin.** Hosted main now pins editor main (35a49051), so #901 pins this branch's head (beef29fb) directly. The old `feedback/interface-theme-pin` branch is no longer used.
- **Hosts.** A host that renders the editor and wants it dark must put `dark` on an ancestor of both the editor and its portals (`<body>` or `<html>`). A host that sets nothing now gets light chrome.
- Env vars: none. Migrations: none.

## Reconciled with Bundle 2

Rebased on editor main 35a49051: #1024 ("Bundle 2 editing, interior captures and native materials") and #1042 (room labels), which merge without conflicts beyond the one below.
- **Dropped:** the `interfaceTheme` prop on `SettingsPanel`. Bundle 2 added a host slot for Preferences (`preferences`, with an exported `SettingsSwitchRow`), so the theme row became an exported `InterfaceThemeRow` that hosts pass through that slot. That leaves one extension point. The Preferences description stays Bundle 2's, since the open-source app shows no theme row.
- **Kept:** everything else. Bundle 2 ships no light chrome, so no forced dark, the light counterparts, the `ActionButton` custom properties, the dark scopes and the open-source app's dark editor page are all still this PR's.
- **Added:** a light pass over the chrome Bundle 2 brought in (Point and ask, Follow Pascal and its pill, the window corner buttons). The dark-only literal sweep over editor main found nothing else: the Point and ask layer is a self-contained dark overlay, like the HUDs, and the other hits are 3D materials and fixtures.
- **Test fixes from the merge:** the theme row test now reads the row's own pressed value, because Bundle 2's construction animation control is a `SegmentedControl` that also reports `aria-pressed`. Bundle 2's new muted-startup SFX test sets the real audio store's state, like the rest of that file.

## Verified in the hosted app after merge

I checked this on private-editor main c5741f613, which pins c69d1d33, in light and dark. Screenshots are in `/tmp/feedback-work/theme/reconciled/`:

- Point and ask, Follow Pascal (off, on and hovered) and the dark Preview bar (`06-*` to `09-*`).
- The window inspector's Wrap / Unwrap buttons (`10-*`) and the multi-selection Merge windows block (`11-*`).
- The Settings → Preferences row order (`03-*`).
- The inspector's dark values, which are unchanged (`21-*`).

One defect, in the command palette rather than in this PR's code: a search left groups in the order they were registered, so `theme` listed the theme commands fifth. The fix is pascalorg/editor#1052.

## Supersedes

Nothing.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (not run for the open-source app; QA ran in the hosted app)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (Biome with the editor's config on the changed files)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: Room labels never pile up: fit their rooms, open on hover
body:
## What

Room label pills no longer overlap, and every room's whole label opens on hover or keyboard focus, in 3D, 2D and the read-only viewer. Two commits on editor main: the feature and the review round.

- **The overlap bug is already fixed on main** by #1024. `PillPlacer` kept `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` as default fields and called them as `this.schedule(...)`. Chrome throws "Illegal invocation" the first time a pill has to hide, so `apply` stopped halfway: every pill after it kept its stale place, and the hidden one never left. This branch keeps that fix: its `startTimer` / `stopTimer` wrappers call the timers as plain functions, for the placer and the new reveal alike. Its repro test, strict fake timers on a manual clock that throw for the wrong receiver the way Chrome does, replaces #1024's test of the same bug.
- **A label has to fit its room.** At rest, each pill takes the first slot whose rectangle lies inside its room's outline on screen (holes included, via Liang–Barsky against each edge), inside the pane, and 4 px clear of the pills already placed. In 3D the outline is first cut to the part in front of the camera, so a room running behind it still holds its pill. A zone drawn inside a room is a hole in that room, so the room's label keeps off it. Each pill tries name and area, then the name alone (cut at 160 px), then its 16 px dot, then nothing. Zooming changes how big rooms are on screen, so the detail follows the zoom. Largest rooms go first, as before. A re-placement tries the anchor, then the side the pill was nudged to last time.
- **Hover is the room under the pointer** (the owner's "ray-traced Voronoi"). In 3D the pointer's ray is met with each room's floor plane: the floor it reaches first wins, then the smallest room on that floor. In 2D the point goes through the inverse CTM and the smallest room holding it wins. The mesh in the way doesn't matter: furniture, a roof on the walls' level, or nothing at all in the viewer, where zone meshes aren't mounted.
- **One read-only chip.** The room under the pointer opens a chip with its whole label after 80 ms of rest. The chip stays 120 ms after the pointer leaves. Moving to the next room moves the same chip there without fading it out and in. A pill under the pointer, or a keyboard-focused pill, opens it at once; when both are set, whichever moved last wins.
  - The chip opens with its colour dot on the pill's dot; a hidden room's chip opens centred on its anchor. It wraps a long name to stay 8 px inside the pane.
  - It takes no pointer: the rooms under it open as the pointer moves over them, and a click there goes to the canvas or plan. The pills it covers fade out and nothing moves. The open room's own pill fades too but stays the control under the chip.
  - In 3D the chip has a layer of its own above the canvas's flags and below the editor's chrome. Escape closes it until the pointer or focus moves on to another room.
- **Pending pills.** A pill that is mounted but not yet measured, or whose anchor is off screen, now waits hidden and out of the tab order. Before, it could show outside the collision pass. A moved anchor (`RoomAnchors`) triggers a re-place.
- **Pills are `<button>`s** named "Kitchen, 27.3 m²". Keyboard focus opens the chip with a two-tone ring (a white outline on a dark halo, so it reads on the 3D scene and on the light plan). Enter or Space selects like a click; Space no longer reaches the canvas's and plan's pan handlers from a pill. Touch never opens the chip: a tap selects as today. The CSS `:hover` expansion of dots is gone, because the chip replaces it.
- `bench:room-labels` (`__bench__/room-label-placement.bench.ts`) times a placement pass and a pick.

## Why

Plan `scene-agent/ai-architect-chat-feedback.md`, row C20:

> "Another issue in this is the label of the different rooms and the zones. They are kind of overlapping and crowded, making it almost unreadable. We need to figure out, based on different patterns (such as the zoom level), how we detect overlapping. Can we use some kind of ray-traced Voronoi to make it dynamic when we mouse over it? All those things have to be figured out in order to provide a good user experience" (screenshots: overlapping room label pills — "Pool Vestibule", "Bedroom 4 Closet", "Pool Bath", "Storage" stacked on each other; "Master Bath" under "Master Vestibule")

Departures from the design (`labels/design.md`):
- It said to try the previous nudge first. Here the anchor (dy 0) still comes first, then the previous nudge. With the previous nudge first, a pill once pushed aside stayed off its anchor forever, even after the neighbour had gone.
- Suppressed pills fade out over 150 ms but come back on the pill's usual 180 ms, not 100 ms. A third duration would need a second flag.
- It ruled out Escape on the chip. The review showed why it is needed (the chip covers other labels, WCAG 1.4.13), so Escape closes it.

## How to test

- `bun test editor/packages/editor/src/components/editor/room-labels.test.ts` (41 tests, run from the hosted root). They cover:
  - the timer repro;
  - placement: detail by zoom, a 45° corridor that only takes a dot, a hole, the pane edge, keeping a side, and a 40-room no-overlap and inside-the-room property;
  - a zone drawn inside a room, and a corridor running behind the camera;
  - the pick: nearest floor, then the smallest room, and a hole;
  - the reveal on a manual clock: dwell, grace, handoff, pointer against focus, Escape, and focus after the view rests;
  - suppression with the open pill, and the pending state.
- `bun --preload ./editor/scripts/bun-preload-three.ts editor/packages/editor/src/components/editor/__bench__/room-label-placement.bench.ts`: median placement 0.04, 0.07 and 0.19 ms for 31, 60 and 120 rooms; a pick 0.004, 0.006 and 0.013 ms.
- In the app. Checked on the hosted dev server with headless Chromium and the Metal GPU. The house is `bench/fixtures/next-house` (31 ground-floor rooms), plus two copies: one with its 8 roofs moved to the ground level, one with a 73-character room name.
  - **Overlaps.** None at five zoom levels in 3D and four in 2D, measured as overlapping pill rects. In 2D, every visible pill's centre and both ends hit its own zone in `elementsFromPoint`. The default 3D view shows 5 full pills, 5 names and 13 dots; the farthest zoom shows dots only.
  - **Hover.** The chip starts showing 120–150 ms after the pointer arrives (80 ms of that is the dwell). A direct pill hover opens it in about 30 ms. A handoff between two rooms always had exactly one chip open. With "Primary bathroom" open, moving the pointer over the chip's far half opened "Primary bedroom" in 3D; in 2D, "Great room" opened under "Primary water closet".
  - **Keyboard.** Tab reaches only the visible pills (22 of the 31 mounted in 2D). Focus opens the chip with the ring. Pointing at another pill moves the chip there, and the next Tab brings it to the focused pill. Space on a focused pill selects its room in 3D and 2D. Escape closes the chip, and it stays closed while the pointer stays in that room.
  - **Drag.** A right-button drag released over a room, with the pointer then held still, opens that room once the view rests.
  - **Roofs and furniture.** With the roofs on the ground level covering the rooms, 57 of 99 grid points open their room. Hovering a sink vanity opens "Bedroom 3", and a kitchen cabinet opens "Kitchen".
  - **Long name.** In a 400 px pane, the 73-character name wraps to two lines and stays inside the pane (8–392 px). In 3D the chip shows above the wall flags and below the level switcher.
  - **Two storeys.** With the upper storey selected, only its 3 pills show: none of the ground floor's ids.
  - **Viewer.** `/viewer/<id>` with the ground floor selected shows dots, and hover opens the room's chip.
  - **Frame time.** Medians at rest, while the pointer moves and while zooming: 16.9, 20.3 and 18.3 ms. The first round measured 17.3, 18.9 and 18.9 ms in the same headless setup. A placement pass (`?perf`, `room-labels` track) takes 0.3 ms median and 2.9 ms at most.
  - **Themes.** The editor stays dark in both themes until E-theme lands, so the light screenshots match the dark ones. The pills keep their dark palette on purpose, and the focus ring was checked on the light 2D plan.

## Reconciled with Bundle 2

Rebased onto editor main 18eb6392 (#1024, Bundle 2).
- **Dropped:** the first commit (098e5d02, the timer fix). #1024 shipped the same fix in the same file. #1024's repro test went too, so the file has one timer repro: this branch's, which also checks that the pills after the hidden one are still placed.
- **Kept:** everything else, unchanged. `room-labels.tsx`, `room-labels.test.ts`, `viewer-rooms.tsx`, the bench and the wiki page are byte for byte what was reviewed at 4fdb9c8c. #1024 touched nothing else of the labels.
- **Re-checked on the new base**, from the hosted root: `check-types` for the editor packages (9/9), the 41 room-label tests, Biome on the touched files, and in the browser on next-house: no overlaps at five 3D and four 2D zooms, every 2D pill inside its zone, the chip opening, closing and handing over in 3D, and no console errors. `bun test editor/packages/editor/src` has 19 failures, all in `lib/history.test.ts`: its child-process probe prints three's `require("three")` deprecation warning on stderr. That file and its imports are untouched here, and it fails the same way when run alone.

## Deployment notes

None: editor package only, no schema, no agent tool. Hosted picks it up with the SHA bump.

## Stack

Base `main`. Hosted bump: pascalorg/private-editor#905, merged with the gitlink on this PR's merge commit 35a49051. C19 (roofs on their own level) is a separate slice.

## Review

Round 1: an adversarial review and GPT-6 Astra (`gpt-6-astra`, high). Every finding was checked against the code first.

**Fixed** (commit 1df038d4, 4fdb9c8c before the rebase):
- **The chip took the pointer** and counted as a direct hover, so rooms under it couldn't be reached (adversarial, medium). The chip is now read-only, `labelAt` no longer matches it, and the open room's pill keeps its hit area (`data-room-label-open` fades it without `pointer-events-none`).
- **Stale suppression**, and a chip left behind by a re-placement (adversarial; Astra 1). `RoomLabelDetail` clears its rect on unmount, and `place()` moves an open chip to its pill's new place. The viewer's layer is keyed by level.
- **The focus ring** never rendered (`outline-none` set `--tw-outline-style: none`), and white at 70% read at about 1:1 on the light plan (adversarial; Astra critique 4). It is now a two-tone ring on the pill and the chip. `clear()` keeps focus, so a focused pill reopens once the camera rests.
- **The chip sat under the wall flags** in 3D (adversarial; Astra critique 2). It has its own `z-30` layer beside the pill layer: above the flags (z-index 25 at most), below the chrome. In 2D it was already above the plan's SVG flags.
- **Nested rooms** (adversarial). A smaller entry whose interior point lies inside a larger one becomes a hole of it. next-house has one: the understairs closet inside the stair hall.
- **The 3D chip got stuck invisible** after opening behind the camera (adversarial; Astra 2). Its drei `Html` now has no position and a no-op `onOcclude`, so drei never sets `display: none`. Astra suggested a plain DOM portal, but react-dom portals can't be used inside the R3F tree; drei's `Html` is the existing bridge.
- **Outlines crossing behind the camera** lost the fit check (Astra 3). Rings are clipped at w = 1e-3 (Sutherland–Hodgman in level coordinates) before projection.
- **The 3D pick chose by area over depth** (Astra 4). `roomAt` now takes the distance along the ray: nearest floor first, then the smallest room within 1 mm of it.
- **Space didn't press a pill** (Astra 5). The host stops Space keydown and keyup from a pill, so the camera's and plan's pan handlers never see it.
- **A resting mouse beat keyboard focus** (Astra 6). Whichever moved last now wins.
- **Long names were clipped**, and the chip's rect went stale on a reflow (Astra 7). The chip is capped at the pane width minus 16 px, the name wraps, and a `ResizeObserver` re-places the chip.
- **No Escape** (Astra 8). Escape closes the chip until the pointer or focus moves to another room. The key isn't consumed: the editor's own Escape still runs, and it keeps the labels shown.
- **A drag ending under a still pointer** didn't reopen the chip (Astra 9). `pointerup` now updates the pointer like a move.
- **Simplifications** (adversarial). Liang–Barsky keeps its state local. The read-only chip is its own component (`RoomPillDetail`), so the viewer no longer passes `detail={!elements}`.
- **Motion** (Astra critique 5). One chip element serves every room: no `key` remount, so no re-entrance on a handoff. The easing is `ease-[cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)]`, because the editor package has no `--ease-smooth-out` token and hosted's `ease-out` is the weak CSS keyword.
- **Hidden pills in the tab order** (Astra critique 4). Hidden pills become `visibility: hidden` once faded.
- **The roof and furniture claim was untested** (adversarial). It is checked now; see How to test.
- **Found while checking.** The 3D chip appeared and closed about 100 ms after its state changed: an R3F render, then drei's root render. It now subscribes inside the drei root, so Escape closes it in the same task.

**Not taken:**
- **Pills under the floating chrome still count as placed** (adversarial, first half of that finding). The chrome is spread over several editor and Community components, each with its own visibility, so marking it as obstacles is a change of its own. Logged in hosted `plans/meta-todos.md`.
- **Tests through `ViewerRooms` or `Editor`** (Astra 10). Rendering them needs a WebGL canvas, which Bun tests don't have; the browser checks above cover the DOM paths. The tests import the module, as the file did on main and as most editor tests do. New behaviour is tested through its exports with an injected clock, and `candidates3D` is exported to test the projection.
- **"The light screenshots prove nothing"** (adversarial note). That is true until E-theme; it is now said in How to test.
- **Anonymous dots in the default plan** (Astra critique 1: a "Rooms (31)" list, 4–6 overview callouts, "Fit floor"). This goes beyond C20. The plan opens framed on the whole site, which is what turns next-house into dots. Logged in meta-todos.
- **An outline and leader for the open chip** (Astra critique 3). Logged in meta-todos, together with the canvas's room-first hover lighting next-house's leftover "Room 1" while the chip names the bathroom inside it.
- **Reading the live dot rect when the chip opens** (Astra critique 5). The placed rect is where the pill lands; the live rect is mid-ease for 180 ms.
- **The PR claims.** They are reworded: "exact for any room shape" and "GPU-bound" are gone, and the farthest zoom shows dots.
- **A 1,024-vertex-ring pick at 4.19 ms** (Astra's perf note). Not a case the editor produces; the bench keeps houses of 31 to 120 rooms.

## Verified after landing

Re-checked after landing, on hosted #905's final head (b2f646446, which pins this PR's merge commit 35a49051, the same tree as 1df038d4), on the hosted dev server: a feedback account, headless Chromium with the Metal GPU, `bench/fixtures/next-house` (31 ground-floor rooms) and its two copies (roofs on the ground level, a 73-character room name). The screenshots are local, in `/tmp/feedback-work/labels/reconciled/` on the machine that ran the checks; each item names its files.
- **No overlaps** at five 3D zooms and four 2D zooms, and every visible 2D pill lies on its own zone (`vr-3d-*`, `vr-2d-*`). The default 3D view shows 5 full pills, 5 names and 13 dots.
- **Hover** (`vr-h-*`). A room's chip starts showing about 135 ms after the pointer arrives in 3D (80 ms of dwell) and 95 ms in 2D. A pill under the pointer opens it in 43 ms (3D) and 18 ms (2D). Leaving closes it after the grace and the faded pills come back. A handoff to the next room always had exactly one chip open.
- **Under the chip, Escape, keyboard, drag** (`vr-r-*`). The rooms under a wide chip open through it. Escape closes it, and it stays closed on that room. Tab reaches only the visible pills (23 of 23 in 3D, 22 of the 31 mounted in 2D) and shows the ring, on the light plan too. Space selects the room and Bundle 2's room panel opens on it. A drag released over a room opens it once the view rests.
- **Two storeys** (`k-3d-level-2-*`). The upper storey shows only its 3 pills. Its rooms open on hover, the ground floor under it doesn't.
- **Viewer** (`vr-viewer-*`): dots, and hover opens the room. **Roofs on the walls' level**: 57 grid points open their room. **Furniture** (`furniture-*`): a vanity opens Bedroom 3, a kitchen cabinet opens Kitchen. **Long name** (`long-name-chip`): the chip stays 8 px inside the pane.
- **390 px phone, touch** (`phone-*`): no overlaps, and a tap on a pill selects its room (the room panel opens) without opening the chip.
- **Next to Bundle 2:**
  - Point and ask (C): the pills step aside while pointing, come back after, and the room chip opens again (`pointask-*`).
  - Rooms built by an Architect · Low turn get their pills as they appear: pending until placed, then Study, Walk-in closet and Hall, with no overlaps, in 3D and 2D (`agent-*`).
  - The wall-end flags stay under the open chip (`vr-r-3d-chip`).
- **Themes.** The editor stays dark in both until E-theme lands, so the light shots match the dark ones.
- `bun test editor/packages/editor/src/components/editor/room-labels.test.ts`: 41 pass.

Seen, not caused here:
- At 390 and 760 px, pills and the open chip can sit under the floating chrome (level switcher, controls hint). That is the follow-up already in `plans/meta-todos.md`.
- In dev, React warns "Attempted to synchronously unmount a root while React was already rendering" once per drei `Html` when the editor remounts while a project loads (33 times on next-house). Main already mounts one `Html` per pill; this change adds the chip's.

title: editor: a plugin's start screen in a host chat; IconRefGlyph exported
body:
## What

- `PluginChatExtension.start`: a lazy component a host's chat shows while its thread is empty. It acts only through the new `ChatStartProps`:
  - `send(text, images?)` sends a message now, its pictures by reference;
  - `attach(files)` puts files on the next message, in the composer;
  - both run at the level that runs the plugin's tools;
  - `requirePro()` only asks whether the person's plan includes that level. It answers `false` after the host offered the upgrade, and changes nothing in the chat. The doc says "Pro" is the hosted product's name for that level.
- `ChatStartProps`, `IconRefGlyph` and `IconRefImage` are exported from `@pascal-app/editor`, so a host renders registry icons the way the editor does.
- `wiki/architecture/plugin-authoring.md` documents the start screen.

Types and exports only: no runtime change in the editor.

## Reconciled with Bundle 2

Rebased onto editor main 18eb6392 (#1024, Bundle 2), cleanly. Bundle 2 added exports next to these in `packages/editor/src/index.tsx` and a section next to this one in `plugin-authoring.md`. Nothing is dropped: Bundle 2 has no start-screen contract, and `IconRefGlyph` / `IconRefImage` were not exported yet.

## Why

Owner feedback (2026-10-12), slice E-start of the Architect chat feedback plan:

- C14: "let's look at the latest PRs from Adam (AxiomeCG) and Steven Tibbs to bring them in: I also added images in the reference folder with commentary on some Steven's feature for generative UI and DXF import."
- C10: "introduce rich message text with interactive and icon rich highlighted entities (see image examples): tool calls, scene graph node mentions, project version mentions, and more"

Steven's Architect plugin had its own start screen (story photographs, 37 styles, build from plans) inside its own panel. The hosted chat has one empty state for every engine. This contract lets a plugin contribute its start screen there without importing the host. `IconRefGlyph` is the icon a host needs for plugin and entity rows.

## How to test

1. From a host checkout with this branch: `bunx turbo run check-types --filter='./editor/packages/*'` passes (I ran it on this head, 9/9).
2. In a plugin's chat extension, add `start: () => import('./chat-start')` where the default export takes `ChatStartProps`. It type-checks, and `import { IconRefGlyph } from '@pascal-app/editor'` resolves.
3. The hosted Community chat mounts Architect's start through this contract (pascalorg/private-editor#909). I checked it in the running app at a 288 px panel and a 390 px phone, in both themes. "Start building" and "Build from plans" run at Pro. On the Free plan every one of them opens the upgrade and keeps the brief. Opening the design studio leaves the effort where it was.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A: no visual change in the editor (types and exports). The host's start screen is shown in its own PR.

## Deployment notes

- Hosted #909 pins this branch's head (c3481011, editor main plus these two commits) and is re-bumped to this PR's merge commit when it lands. Hosted #908 no longer needs an editor change: #1017 is on editor main.
- Env vars: none. Migrations: none.

## Review

Fixed:
- `requirePro()` moved the chat to Pro as a side effect, so a step that only needs the plan (opening Architect's picture studio) changed the effort the next message ran at. It now only asks; `send` and `attach` are what run at the plugin's level.
- The doc says that "Pro" is the hosted name for that level, so a self-hosted host maps it onto its own.

Rejected: none.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (checked through the hosted Community dev server, not the editor's `bun dev`)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (Biome on the changed files)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
