title: core: the site comes first — get_site, place_building, one setback envelope
body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR places a house on its lot by moving the building node, never its walls. The model's coordinates stay as written. Every path places the house the same way: a layout program, a hand trace, a DXF import, the lot drop-in.

It is rebased on editor main (`cc978fe8`: Bundle 2's #1024, then #1039, #1040, #1041, #1043).

- **One envelope, in core.**
  - The edge roles, `setbackEnvelope` (with #1017's straight-front rule) and the oriented yards move from `editor/.../site-plan/geometry.ts` to `core/src/lib/setback-envelope.ts`.
  - The building footprint (`levelFootprintLoops`, `footprintOutline`, `siteFrame`, `levelFrame`) moves to `core/src/lib/building-footprint.ts`.
  - The site plan, the lot code and the 3D site import them from core. The 3D copy in `nodes/src/site/setbacks.ts` is deleted, so the 2D and 3D envelopes can't drift apart. Its ribbon tests are now `line-ribbon.test.ts`.
  - `siteFrontEdge(site)` and `siteSetbackEnvelope(site)` are the one recipe the site plan, the 3D site and the agents use. The front edge is the recorded front edge, else the first street edge, else the north-facing guess.
- **`core/src/lib/site-placement.ts`** (also exported as `@pascal-app/core/site-placement`):
  - `siteBrief` reads the site in the building's level frame:
    - the lot, and the buildable area with its state (`lot` / `setbacks` / `none` / `advisory`) and centre. Setbacks of zero exclude nothing.
    - the street side and the `squareRotationDeg` that squares the house to it
    - north, the address, APN and zoning, and the new-project `placeholder` flag
    - the footprint's fit, yards and overhang. Fit is judged by area; the overhang counts a piece's middle, so a house across a notch reports how far it reaches.
  - `placeBuildingPose` centres a footprint in the buildable area. The footprint is an outline about to be drawn, or the walls already standing. It tries the centroid first, then the most interior point.
    - It can place by the yards given (one of front/rear, one of left/right). These are solved together at the rotation asked, so a lot askew to the house still meets both, and a pose that misses them is refused.
    - A house with no walls yet is turned square to the street. A standing house keeps its rotation unless asked.
    - It never resizes the lot.
    - Its inputs don't depend on the current pose, so a repeated call changes nothing.
  - `describeSiteBrief` writes the same facts as a few lines. The hosted chat prints them at the top of its scene snapshot. The street line names a rotation only for a standing house that is askew.
- **Two shared tools, on both surfaces:**
  - `get_site` (read).
  - `place_building` (writes only the building node). Refusals: `needs_footprint`, `other_building_on_site`, `no_street`, `yards_conflict`, `yards_infeasible`.
  - Both get annotations, justifications, the README table, and an MCP agent-guide line: "the site comes first, before the first wall".
- **Reported where the agent looks:**
  - `verify_scene` reports `footprint_outside_site`, `footprint_outside_setbacks` and `buildable_area_none`. Off-centre is never an issue.
  - `create_room` and `add_wall` return `site: { fit: 'outside', overhangM, sides }` when the walls they raise, mitred and curved, cross the lot line. Only the lot is read to do it.
- **Lot drop-in:** a house the new lot leaves outside is re-centred through `placeBuildingPose`, keeping its facing. `buildingRecentreOffset` is gone.
- **The site's facts move apart from the node schema:** `SiteAddress`, `SiteParcel`, `SiteSetbacks` and `migrateSiteMetadata` now live in `schema/nodes/site-facts.ts`. This lets the site brief run inside a workflow, whose bundle refuses anything that reaches nanoid.

## Reconciled with Bundle 2

Bundle 2 (#1024) and the editor PRs that landed after it touched the same registration and test files. Nothing in this PR was already there: Bundle 2 has no site placement.
- **Dropped:** nothing.
- **Kept, both sides:**
  - `verify_scene`: Bundle 2's description, with "a house past its lot line or in its required yards" added to its list. The three site codes sit after Bundle 2's new item and wall codes.
  - The case tables: the site cases next to Bundle 2's corner-window and merge-windows cases and #1039's `ADD_FENCE_CASES`.
  - The MCP registrations: `get_site` and `place_building` between Bundle 2's `place_in_room` and `search_assets`, whose `catalog: true` is unchanged.
  - `create_room`: Bundle 2's room-name import beside `lotOverhang` and `levelFootprintLoops`. `add_wall`: #1039's `isRoofLevel` beside them.
  - The site plan: #1039's roof rings over every storey (`aboveGradeLevels`) and its roof-level storey count, with the footprint now read from core.
- **Not added:** `get_site` and `place_building` are not in `run_batch`'s list (`BATCHABLE_TOOLS`). That list belongs to Bundle 2, and both tools work on their own.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations`. The tables in `__fixtures__/site-cases.ts` also run on the MCP (`packages/mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.test.ts`) and in the hosted chat. They cover get_site, place_building, the lot-line flags and the verify_scene issues:
   - a corner-traced house that lands centred
   - an outline on an empty building, and on a turned parcel, where it stands square to the street inside the setbacks
   - a replay that moves nothing
   - a parcel turned 20° off the origin; a yaw of 0.7 rad kept
   - yards, conflicts and infeasible yards, yards with a new rotation and its replay, and front and side yards on a lot askew to the house
   - two buildings; a fenced house; an oversize house centred without the lot being resized
   - the pole winning on a lot whose centroid is too near its edge
   - a U lot whose notch a house bridges with every corner on the lot, and how far it reaches past it
   - zero setbacks; a street edge with no front edge
   - a room drawn to the lot line, and a curved wall whose chord stays on the lot
2. Draw a lot with setbacks in the site plan. The 2D and 3D dashed envelopes match.
3. Drop in a lot by address on a project whose house falls outside the new lot. The house is re-centred and still faces the same way.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Verified end to end through the hosted app in pascalorg/private-editor#910, which has the screenshots. Those runs used this code before the rebase; the hosted PR now pins this branch's head:
- An Architect Low turn on a turned parcel stood the house square to the street, centred 0.00 m off the buildable centre, inside its setbacks, in one program.
- An Architect Pro turn on a blueprint PDF read `get_site` and called `place_building` with the outline before its first wall. The house was centred on the lot when its walls first went up.

## Review

The pascalorg/private-editor#910 reviews covered this code. On the editor side:

**Fixed**
- **Squaring.** A house about to rise on a turned lot now stands square to the street.
- **Yards.** Yards given with a new rotation are read at that rotation, and front and side yards on a lot askew to the house are solved together.
- **Front edge.** The setbacks and the street use one front edge, and the 3D renderer now goes through `siteSetbackEnvelope` like the site plan.
- **Zero setbacks** no longer read as "nothing buildable".
- **Notch.** The overhang of a house across a notch counts the piece's middle.
- **`create_room` / `add_wall`** measure their walls' mitred, curved bands, reading only the lot.

**Rejected**
- **`which_building` for the tools' ambiguous case.** The tools resolve the building through `targetBuilding`, the helper every building-targeted tool shares, which refuses `building_required`. Renaming it would give one case two names.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (through the hosted app's dev server, before the Bundle 2 rebase)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

Checks run on this branch (rebased on editor main `cc978fe8`), from the hosted worktree:
- `check-types` for every editor package: 9 of 9.
- `bun test` for core, mcp, the editor's site-plan and lot code, nodes' site code and the tool-annotation policy: 5475 pass, 0 fail. The `metadata references (R3)` failure is gone; #1045 fixed it on main.
- Biome on the touched files.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> **Overview**

>

> 
> **Surfaces lot compliance** in `verify_scene` (`footprint_outside_site`, `footprint_outside_setbacks`, `buildable_area_none`) and in `create_room` / `add_wall` via `lotOverhang` on mitred wall bands. Lot drop-in re-centres with `placeBuildingPose` when the footprint is outside the new lot.

title: editor: the panel on screen is the store's, and a collapsed sidebar opens onto the one picked
body:
## What

Follow-up to #1036 (the rail panel and preferences survive a reload). It fixes what the review of that work found.

- **`activeSidebarPanel` is the panel on screen.** When the rail lacks the panel picked in a workspace, the layout shows its first panel. Two cases: a plugin panel joins only once the scene's plugins load, or the plugin is gone. Until now the store kept the missing id, so host code that reads it disagreed with the screen. Examples in Community: the getting-started guide could keep asking for the Build panel while Build was open, and on mobile the navbar hid Share for an Item builder the screen no longer showed. `useShownSidebarPanel` (`lib/sidebar-panel.ts`) now writes the panel it shows into `activeSidebarPanel` and leaves the pick in `sidebarPanels`, so the pick still comes back once the rail has it. This removes the old "adopt the shown tab" effect, and with it the stale-closure path from the Bugbot thread on #1036.
- **A collapsed sidebar opens onto the panel picked.** Both the rail click and `openSidebarPanel` expanded first and switched panels second. For a moment, the panel left open was the open one. Community arms the paint brush when Paint opens, so reopening a sidebar collapsed on Paint onto Chat armed Paint on the way: that cleared the selection, replaced the paint material and left the Site phase. The new `showSidebarPanel(id)` picks first, then expands at a usable width. The rail click and `openSidebarPanel` use it, and it is exported for hosts' own entry points.
- **B and F open their panel before they arm their tool** (`hooks/use-keyboard.ts`). A host may drop the armed tool when the panel changes (Community does), so B or F pressed from any other panel opened Build or Items in select mode. Since the rail now reopens on the panel left open, that is the first thing a reload offers.
- **Preferences storage** (`lib/hydration-gated-storage.ts`):
  - A blob that fails to parse now counts as none. Before, hydration failed and `hasHydrated()` stayed false for the session, so nothing was saved again and the bad blob was never replaced.
  - A save of the blob the tab already holds is skipped. `persist` writes the whole state on every `set`, so a second tab's next update, even one that changed no preference, replaced the panel picked in the first.
- `wiki/architecture/plugin-authoring.md`: `activeSidebarPanel` is the panel on screen, `showSidebarPanel`, and a tab saves its preferences only when they change.

## Why

From the owner's feedback (plan row D1, verbatim):

title: core: move old roofs to the roof level, by hand or by agent
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Rebuilt on main after #1039 (and #1044) landed.** It is now four commits on editor `main` `f9bcb0c5` (#1052, the editor commit hosted `main` pins): `0b3a6c4d`, the move, then `d4460ebd`, `4e440fa3` and `b7b7ec60`, three fixes from Bugbot's review (below). Everything #1039 already had is gone from the diff: its roof-level rule (`planRoofLevel`, `coveredStoreyId`, `roofsOver`, `servesAsRoofLevel`) stays exactly as `main` has it. This PR adds only the move, by hand and by agent.

A roof written onto the storey whose walls carry it can be moved to the level the roof rule gives it, without changing how it looks. Existing projects need this: roofs built before the roof level, and by tools that ignored it, still cover their storey's plan in solo and exploded level views.

- **`services/roof-move.ts`** (new):
  - `isRoofOnStoreyWalls(nodes, roofId)` names a roof held by the storey whose wall tops it bears on, within 0.15 m. A porch roof on its beam bears lower, so it is not one. A lower wing's roof on the storey above bears on the walls below, so it is not one either.
  - `planRoofsOffStorey(nodes, storeyId)` moves only those roofs. Each goes to `planRoofLevel`'s level: the roof level over the top storey (created or declared in the same changes), otherwise the storey above. A roof level it creates is as tall as the roofs rise over its floor, the eaves' lift included, as `create_roof` makes one. Each roof group drops by the storey's offset, so it stands where it stood. A roof that follows walls switches to a fixed height where the walls on its new level would lift it, or where the follow would not see the storey's walls (a support level or an empty level between them). A second move leaves a lower wing's roof that the first move put on the storey above.
  - `roofsKeptOverStorey(before, after)`: a roof group above the storey it covers (`coveredStoreyId`), at a fixed height (`support` level: moved roofs, the agents' and the auto roof's), keeps its height over that storey when the storey, or a support level or empty level between them, is made taller or shorter. A level put in, taken out or reordered between them carries the roof with its level, as #1039 decided for "+ level". The roof elevation sync applies it without an undo step of its own, as it already does for a roof that follows walls. A roof standing on its own level's walls is left alone.
- **`roof-level.ts`**: `planRoofLevel` returns `storeyOffset` (the storey's floor from the target level's floor), for the roof writers that measure heights from the storey. `roofLevelAbove` reads where `planRoofLevel` would put a roof without planning a level, so the panel can ask on every store change. `coveredStoreyId` and `servesAsRoofLevel` are exported for the plugins.
- **"Move to the roof level" on a roof's panel**, in 2D and 3D.
  - It shows only for a roof on its own storey's walls, and says why: "On First Floor with its walls, so it hides that floor's plan in solo and exploded views". When several roofs move, it adds "The floor's 2 roofs move together".
  - Under an upper storey the button reads "Move to Second Floor".
  - The move is one undo step, and the selection follows the roof to its new level. The button is filled (`bg-foreground/[0.08]`, `rounded-full`).
- **`move_roofs_to_roof_level`**: the panel's move for agents. One contract (`agent-tools/roofs.ts`), one core operation (`agent-operations/move-roofs.ts`), with its case table. It is registered on the MCP with its annotation policy (destructive: it re-parents existing roofs), and listed in the README's tool table and the agent guide. Refusals: `level_not_found`, `no_roof_on_walls`.
- **`verify_scene`'s `roof_mixed_in_storey` keeps `main`'s reports** (a roof on a storey that covers it, with walls, rooms or a stair there). It also reports a roof standing on its storey's own walls that `main` read as a lower wing's roof, and for those it names `move_roofs_to_roof_level`, the panel action, and "never delete and rebuild them". A porch roof on its beam is still reported, without the move. A roof level holding a plugin's roof planes is no longer reported as `roof_level_no_roof`.
- `systems/roof/roof-elevation.ts` splits out the footprint test it already ran (`wallsUnderRoof`, `roofWallTop`), so the move reads the same walls the elevation sync does. `main`'s rule that a lower wing's roof follows the walls below only is kept.
- `wiki/architecture/vertical-model.md` (Roof levels) describes the move.

Resolved against `main`: `storeyCoveredBy`, the bearing-based coverage reader of the earlier branch, is dropped for `main`'s `coveredStoreyId`. The roof-level tests are `main`'s, with `storeyOffset` added and the move's cases appended. The MCP guide test lists `roof_mixed_in_storey` as a code the guide may name.

## How to test

1. Make a one-storey house whose roof is on the storey, as older projects have it. For example: four walls 2.7 m tall on a 2.5 m storey, and a hip roof parented to that storey with `support: 'walls'` at y = 2.7.
2. Select the roof and open its panel. A **Level** section says it hides the floor's plan and offers **Move to the roof level**.
3. Click it. A level named **Roof** appears above the storey and is selected. The roof looks the same: same eave height, still "Follows walls".
4. Select the storey: its plan shows with no roof over it. In Preview, Exploded lifts the roof off the plan, and Solo on the storey shows the plan alone.
5. Undo: the roof is back on the storey and the Roof level is gone, in one step.
6. A two-storey house: a large First Floor (16 × 10 m) under a small Second Floor (8 × 10 m over its west half), with Architect-style hip roofs on each storey at its wall tops.
   - Select the wing's roof. The panel reads **Move to Second Floor**. Click it: the roof is on Second Floor at y = −2.7 m, its eave still at 2.7 m, and its panel has no Level section.
   - Select Second Floor's roof: **Move to the roof level** moves only it.
7. Make First Floor taller (10 ft, its walls still 2.7 m). The wing's roof stays on the 2.7 m walls (y = −3.048 m). Undo puts both back.
8. Repeat steps 2–5 in the 2D view.
9. Agents: `move_roofs_to_roof_level { levelId }` does what the button does. A second call answers `no_roof_on_walls`.

Ran on `b7b7ec60`, from the hosted root (pascalorg/private-editor#913's worktree):
- `bunx turbo run check-types --filter='./editor/packages/*'` (9/9), Biome on the changed files.
- `bun test editor/packages/core editor/packages/mcp/src editor/packages/nodes/src/roof`: 5369 pass, 0 fail. On `0b3a6c4d`, with `editor/packages/editor/src/components/ui/command-palette` added: 5366 pass.
- The hosted side: `agent-surface-parity`, `agent-tool-table` and `hosted-mcp-tool-effects` pass with the tool on both surfaces.

In the browser, in the hosted app (pascalorg/private-editor#913), on `0292ac09`: that is this commit before its rebase onto #1052, which touches only the command palette.
- Steps 1–5 and 8, in 3D and 2D, dark and light, on a house with two hip roofs on First Floor (one following walls, one at a fixed height). The button moved both to a new Roof level at the same world heights. Preview's Building view was pixel-identical before and after. Exploded lifted both roofs, First Floor selected showed its plan, and one undo put both roofs back and removed the Roof level.
- Step 9's first call, from a real Architect · Low chat turn on a fresh copy of that house: one `move_roofs_to_roof_level` step ("Moved roofs to the roof level") gave the same result, and undo restored it.
- Steps 6–7 (two storeys) and the second call were not re-run in the browser. The core tests cover them.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

## Review

Two reviews of the earlier branch and its hosted half (pascalorg/private-editor#913): an adversarial review, and GPT-6 Astra.

Fixed here:
- **A wall-following roof moved over a level between kept a follow that could not see its storey** (Bugbot on `4e440fa3`, medium). The follow reads only the roof level's walls and those directly under it, so the roof rose with the roof level when the storey grew. Fixed in `b7b7ec60`: such a roof keeps its height, and `roofsKeptOverStorey` keeps it on the storey's walls. The new case fails on `4e440fa3`.
- **A roof level made for the move was short of the roofs** (Bugbot on `d4460ebd`, medium). It was sized by the roofs' rise alone, so with walls taller than their storey the roofs stood above it. Fixed in `4e440fa3`: it is as tall as the roofs rise over its floor, as `create_roof` makes one. pascalorg/private-editor#913 sizes the hosted writers' roof level the same way.
- **A moved roof rose off its walls over a support level or an empty level** (Bugbot on `0b3a6c4d`, medium). `roofsKeptOverStorey` took the level directly under the roof level as the storey it covers. With a support level or a level still to be built between them, it kept nothing, so a fixed-height roof standing on the storey's walls rose when the storey grew. Fixed in `d4460ebd`, which reads the storey from `coveredStoreyId`. With levels between, it keeps only a roof bearing on that storey's walls, so a roof that "+ level" lifted stays on top of the new level. The new tests fail on `0b3a6c4d`.
- **The move counted roofs the rule itself had placed** (adversarial, high). A lower wing's roof moved onto the storey above was offered again, and a second click took it two levels above its walls. Only roofs on their own storey's walls are offered and moved. Tests cover a second move and a lower roof on the storey above.
- **No agent counterpart to the move** (both reviews, high). `move_roofs_to_roof_level` is the lossless move, and `verify_scene` names it.
- **A fixed-height roof group above its storey floated when the storey grew** (both reviews). The roof elevation sync keeps it over its storey.
- **The button read as plain text; the panel planned a roof level on every store change** (adversarial, low). The button is filled; the label comes from `roofLevelAbove`.
- **A plane-only roof level was reported roofless** (Astra).

Not changed, with the reason:
- **A level inserted, deleted or reordered under a roof** (Astra). The roof moves with its level, as #1039 decided for "+ level".
- **One click moves every roof on the storey's walls** (Astra). The storey's plan stays hidden while any of them stands there, so the move takes all of them and the panel says how many.

> **Medium Risk**
> Re-parents roof nodes and can create or declare roof levels; scene graph and elevation sync behavior change for migrated roofs, though geometry is intended to stay fixed.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **lossless migration path** for legacy roofs parented to occupied storeys: new **`move_roofs_to_roof_level`** agent tool and roof panel **"Move to the roof level"** both run **`planRoofsOffStorey`**, re-parenting only roofs that **bear on that storey's wall tops** (porch beams and lower-wing roofs on the storey above are excluded) onto the target from **`planRoofLevel`**, preserving world position, ids, and segments.

title: release: fail before publishing when a package was never published to npm
body:
## What does this PR do?

Explains and prevents the two release failures (#65 on 2026-09-24, #66 on 2026-10-12). Both ended in `ENEEDAUTH` after npm's OIDC token exchange answered `package not found`: in September for `@pascal-app/nodes` (trusted publisher not yet configured), yesterday for `@pascal-app/geometry-script`, which has never been published to npm, so there is nothing to attach a trusted publisher to. Because packages publish one after another, `core@1.0.4` is now on the registry with no tag or commit; the existing "already published; continuing release recovery" branches make the rerun safe.

- A preflight step right after the version bump checks that every package in the release list exists on npm and fails with the one-time instructions when one does not. No build, no publish, no half release.
- `wiki/npm-release.md`: an "Adding a package" section, and the package count is eight.

The unblock itself cannot come from CI: a maintainer publishes `@pascal-app/geometry-script@1.0.3` once by hand (with the 2FA browser approval), adds the trusted publisher (GitHub Actions, `pascalorg` / `editor` / `release.yml` / environment `npm`), then reruns Release with `bump: patch`.

## How to test

1. Rerun Release with `dry-run: true` on this branch: the new step passes once `geometry-script` is on npm, and until then fails at that step with the instructions (and nothing else runs).
2. After the manual first publish and trusted publisher: Release with `bump: patch` publishes 1.0.4 for every package (core skipped as already published), tags, uploads the runtime and builds the image.

title: release: push the release commit and tags with a deploy key that bypasses the main ruleset
body:
## What does this PR do?

Release #67 (2026-10-13) got further than any run since 1.0.3: every package published at 1.0.4. It then died on the last push, `GH013: Repository rule violations`: the `main` ruleset requires pull requests and the `quality` status check, and its only bypass is the repository-admin role. The workflow pushes with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is neither, so the release commit and the eight tags were rejected and the docker jobs never ran.

The release job now checks out with `secrets.RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY`: a deploy key with write access, listed in the ruleset's bypass actors. `actions/checkout` configures the remote for SSH with that key, so the existing `git push --atomic origin HEAD:main <tags>` goes through an identity the ruleset allows. Nothing else changes. The wiki documents the key and its rotation.

One-time setup (admin), before rerunning:

1. `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -C "pascalorg/editor release" -f release-deploy-key`
2. Settings → Deploy keys → Add: title `release`, the `.pub` contents, "Allow write access".
3. Settings → Rules → Rulesets → `main` → Bypass list → Add bypass → Deploy keys.
4. Settings → Environments → `npm` → Add secret `RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY` with the private key file contents. Delete the local files.

Then Release with `bump: patch` again: every 1.0.4 package is skipped as already published, the commit and tags land, the runtime asset uploads, the image builds.

## How to test

1. After the setup above, run Release with `dry-run: true`: the checkout step shows the SSH remote; nothing is published.
2. Run Release with `bump: patch`: the "Commit version bumps & tag" step pushes, the tags exist on GitHub, the docker jobs run.

title: core: view_scene pictures at 1920 × 1200
body:
## What does this PR do?

Raises `VIEW_SIZE`, the size every `view_scene` picture is planned at, from 1280 × 800 to 1920 × 1200, the most of each side. At 1280 a shelf's books and a door's handles did not read. Photo crops follow, since their longest side is the view's width. Both hosts get the change through the shared contract: the hosted chat and the MCP.

Vision models scale a picture down past about 1568 px on its long side, so this is the useful ceiling. The hosted chat now encodes views as WebP, and moves them out of its requests as links, so the larger size costs no request weight there (pascalorg/private-editor, `fix/ai-stop-payload`).

## How to test

1. In an editor tab, have an agent call `view_scene` on a project with walls.
2. The returned picture is 1920 × 1200, or 1920 wide at a camera's own aspect.
3. A `view_scene` with a photo region returns a crop at most 1920 px long.

title: editor: a palette search lists the best-matching group first
body:
## What does this PR do?

A command palette search now lists the group with the best match first.

cmdk 1.1.1 ranks the items inside a group but never moves the groups: its group sort looks each group up by an internal id that the DOM doesn't carry, so the lookup finds nothing. The palette therefore listed groups in the order they were registered, and a strong match could sit below a screen of weak fuzzy ones. In the hosted editor, typing "theme" put the theme commands fifth, under Generate, Sheets, Units and Viewer Controls. Typing "light" and pressing Enter ran the first group's weak match, not "Use light theme".

- `rankedGroups(actions, search)` groups the registered actions and, while a search is typed, orders the groups by their best `defaultFilter` score (cmdk's own scorer). With no search, the groups keep the registered order. Ties keep it too.
- cmdk scrolls to the selection before the list re-renders it. Once the groups move, it would scroll to wherever the previously selected item went, and the new first match could end up above the fold. `TopOnFirstItem` scrolls the list back to the top when a search has selected its first item. It leaves keyboard and pointer moves alone.

Found while verifying the interface theme (#1041) in the hosted app.

## How to test

1. Open the editor with a few plugins installed, so the palette has several groups. Switch the theme once, which re-registers the theme commands at the end.
2. Press Cmd+K and type `theme`. The theme commands' group is first, its first enabled item is selected, and the list is scrolled to the top.
3. Type `solid` instead. Viewer Controls comes first with "Switch to Solid" selected.
4. Arrow down past the fold and back up. The list scrolls with the selection as before.
5. `bun test packages/editor/src/components/ui/command-palette` (run from the host repo root: 2 pass).

## Screenshots / screen recording

Local captures (hosted dev server, light and dark):
- Before, at the pin: `/tmp/feedback-work/theme/reconciled/04-palette-theme-light.png`. Theme commands are below the fold.
- After: `/tmp/feedback-work/theme/reconciled/22-palette-theme-fixed-light.png` and `…-dark.png`.

- [ ] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify). `components/ui` is excluded from the editor's Biome config, so `bun check` skips these files. Biome lint passed on copies of both files placed outside the excluded path.

The hosted `e2e/community/editor-theme.spec.ts` now types `light` and `dark` in the palette and presses Enter. It fails without this change, because Enter runs another group's command, and passes with it.

title: editor: keys typed into any field stay out of the tools
body:
## What does this PR do?

Twenty-two tool and camera key handlers counted only an `<input>` or a `<textarea>` as typing. They now ask `isTypingTarget`, the rule the room, fence, window and slab tools already follow, so a key typed into a contenteditable field (or a textbox, combobox or dialog) belongs to that field.

Read from the handlers, in a contenteditable field:
- R and T rotated the item, stair, elevator, wall, roof, building or HVAC piece being placed or moved; the item placement coordinator also called `preventDefault`, so the letters never reached the field;
- M (duct terminal mount) and F (liquid line follow) were taken by their tools and never typed;
- Enter took a snapshot in capture mode;
- walk mode swallowed its movement keys;
- Escape cancelled a duct or pipe run.

The hosted Architect chat's composer becomes a Lexical (contenteditable) editor in pascalorg/private-editor (the M2 slice of `@` mentions), which is why this lands first.

Files: `editor/src/components/{editor/first-person-controls,editor/snapshot-capture-overlay,tools/elevator/*,tools/item/use-placement-coordinator,tools/stair/stair-tool}.tsx` and `nodes/src/{building/move-tool,cabinet/tool,duct-fitting/*,duct-terminal/tool,fence/move-endpoint-tool,hvac-equipment/tool,lineset/tool,liquid-line/tool,pipe-fitting/*,pipe-trap/tool,shared/distribution-run-tool,shared/move-roof-tool,wall/move-endpoint-tool,wall/move-tool}.tsx`. The distribution run keeps its exceptions: a button still blocks it, and its own length field still drives it.

## How to test

1. Arm the duct terminal tool, click into any contenteditable field (the hosted chat's composer on the private-editor PR that pins this) and type "mm": both letters are typed and the mount does not cycle.
2. Place an item, keep its ghost on the canvas, click into the same field and type "rotate the tray": every letter is typed and the ghost does not turn.
3. With focus on the canvas, R, T, M and F still act on their tools as before.

Not reproduced live: my one try in the hosted app (Items picked, then the Chat tab, then typing "rotate the tray, then the table") found the editor back in select mode, so the text came through whole and proves nothing either way. The failure list above is read from the handlers.

title: editor: a placed item stays selected through the click after its drop
body:
## What does this PR do?

A catalog item dropped on the ground of a new project is placed but left unselected, so its inspector never opens (hosted E2E `preset-capture-transparency` and `project-snapshot-sky` fail on it since the #1024 pin).

Why: a surface `:click` is synthesized on pointer-up (`use-node-events`). A placement that commits there (a floor drop whose ray lands on the site mesh, a wall, an item host) still has the browser's own `click` to come. Since #1024 the editor is back in select mode by the time that click arrives, and `useGridEvents` → `SelectionManager.onGridClick` takes it for a click on empty ground and calls `handleDeselect`. Traced in a local probe: `finishCommittedPlacement` selects `item_…` from `commitFloorOnSurfaceClick` (node:click), then the same press's DOM click deselects it from `SelectionManager.onGridClick`. Bisected on the hosted pins: editor `f88b020e` keeps the selection, `18eb6392` (#1024) and every pin since drop it.

The coordinator now eats that click when a non-repeating drop lands between a pointer-up and its click, the way the press-drag release already did (`swallowNextClick`, hoisted so both paths share it). A drop made by the click itself (`grid:click`) leaves the next click alone.

## How to test

1. Open a new project, Items → Sofa, click the ground in the 3D view.
2. Expected: the sofa is placed, selected (outline), and its inspector ("Sofa") opens. Before: placed, unselected, no inspector.
3. `bun test packages/editor/src/components/tools/item/placement-history.test.tsx` (from the repo root here): the new "item placement selection" case fails without the coordinator change and passes with it.

## Screenshots / screen recording

title: Add barrel roofs and glazed roof construction

## What does this PR do?

Adds barrel roofs in standard and glazed construction, and glazed construction for gable and straight shed roofs. The roof inspector exposes supported construction choices, arch rise and divisions, glazing grids, framing, glass appearance, end infill and individual panel overrides. Frame, glass and solid panels have independent paint slots. The geometry fixes overlapping corner faces, preserves barrel rise consistently during 2D and 3D resizing, respects wall-only accessory cuts, and follows palette and debug display settings. Roof creation and glazing paint use shared agent contracts and operations; floor plans, accessory hosting, shadows and printable solids follow the new roof geometry. Existing scenes retain standard construction by default.

## How to test

1. Run `bun dev`, open a project, create a roof and choose Barrel. Switch between Standard and Glazed. Adjust rise and arch divisions; inspect the end-wall corners for overlapping faces. Resize the span in both 2D and 3D: the rise stays fixed until a smaller span requires clamping it to half the span.
2. Try Glazed on gable and straight shed roofs. Inspect unsupported roof shapes: Glazed should be visibly disabled. Adjust glazing grids, framing and glass controls; change individual panels to solid or empty. Cancel a preview and undo a committed edit. Paint frame and glass separately, then change palette, texture and debug display settings.
3. Add skylights and roof-wall openings: skylights cut the covering, while wall openings leave it intact. Exercise `create_roof` with `roofSystem: "glazed"` and barrel parameters, then `paint` with `glazing-frame`, `glazing-glass` or `glazing-solid`. Invalid shapes and excessive barrel rise should refuse without creating nodes.

title: editor: agent-turn cues (done, failed, needs input) and a per-tab mute
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds three sounds a host can play when an agent's turn ends, and makes the mute each tab's own.

- **Three cues.** The SFX map gains `turnDone`, `turnFailed` and `turnNeedsInput`, with the bus events `sfx:turn-done`, `sfx:turn-failed` and `sfx:turn-needs-input`. They go through `playSFX`, so mute and the master and effects volumes apply as for every other sound. They are tonal, so they have no rate or volume jitter, and they have no throttle of their own: the host plays each one once per turn. Each is two struck notes, 600 ms, mono, at -20 LUFS momentary as played (level with `item_place`, under `success`):
  - done: a rising major third, G5 to B5
  - failed: a falling minor third, C5 to A4, slower and darker
  - needs input: one D6 twice, short and dry, 220 ms apart
- **`scripts/synth-turn-cues.ts`** renders the three files from sine partials with ffmpeg. With ffmpeg 8.1.2 and LAME 3.100 it gives the same bytes on every run, so changing a cue means editing the script and running it again.
- **Mute is per tab.** Someone working in two projects in two tabs can mute one and keep hearing the other.
  - `useAudio` keeps this tab's mute in `sessionStorage['pascal-audio-muted']`, so it survives the tab's reloads.
  - The last choice made in any tab goes in `localStorage['pascal-audio-muted']`, and a new tab starts from it. Open tabs keep their own.
  - The volumes stay in `pascal-audio-settings`, every tab's, now saved without `muted`. They reach open tabs at once: a `storage` listener takes another tab's volumes and autoplay, never its mute or whether its radio plays. So a later save of a tab carries them instead of writing older ones back.
  - No version bump, so the previous build still reads the settings (it keeps the volumes and only loses the mute). `merge` takes a mute the settings still carry as the last choice, unless a choice was made since, so someone who had muted stays muted. The next save drops it.
  - A save that changes no shared setting (a mute) is skipped.
  - `setMuted` joins `toggleMute`.
- **The audio settings dialog** says what is shared and what is the tab's. Its button reads "Mute this tab" / "Unmute this tab", its sliders stay usable in a muted tab (the volumes are every tab's), and its labels are in sentence case.

The hosted chat plays the cues and adds "Mute this tab" to its sound popover in the PR that pins this commit (pascalorg/private-editor#959).

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/editor/src/store/use-audio.test.ts packages/editor/src/lib/sfx-player.test.ts` passes. It covers:
   - a tab's mute survives its reload, and a new tab starts from the last choice
   - another tab's choice leaves an open tab alone
   - a volume another tab sets reaches this one at once, and this tab's saves carry it, also when its radio pauses
   - an old mute carries over in settings the old build still reads, and a newer choice wins over it
   - the three cues play at master × effects volume, and not in a muted tab
2. In the app, open Settings → Audio settings and press "Mute this tab". Open a second tab: it starts muted. Unmute it there and reload the first tab: the first tab is still muted. Move a slider in one tab: the other tab's dialog shows it.
3. With ffmpeg 8.1.2 (LAME 3.100), `bun scripts/synth-turn-cues.ts /tmp/cues` gives files byte-identical to `apps/editor/public/audios/sfx/turn_*.mp3`.

Checks I ran from the private-editor worktree that pins this branch: the two test files above; `check-types` for every editor package; Biome on the changed files with this repo's config; the synth script (output identical to the committed files). After rebasing on main (`559db739`), the two test files, `check-types` and Biome again, with no change to this PR's content. In the hosted app, against its dev server with a Web Audio spy, because I can't listen:
- done, failed and needs-input each played once, and a reload played nothing
- muting one tab left another unmuted, and a new tab started muted
- a muted tab's sliders stayed usable, and a volume set there showed in an open tab without a reload
- settings saved with `muted: true` loaded muted and stayed version 0

I did not run this repo's own `bun dev`.

## Review

Findings from the review of the hosted PR that land here:
- **Taken: the version bump was not rollback-safe** (a version-1 blob made the previous build reset everyone's volumes). The settings keep version 0, and `merge` moves an old mute out.
- **Taken: "volumes apply to every tab" was not live**, and a stale tab's save could undo another tab's volume. Fixed with the `storage` listener, which leaves the mute and the radio alone.
- **Taken: the sliders were disabled in a muted tab.** They stay enabled.
- **Taken: Title Case labels.** They are now "Master volume", "Radio volume" and "Sound effects".
- **Taken: the cue level.** At -23 the cues sat 3.6 LU under `item_place`; they are re-rendered at -20.

## Screenshots / screen recording

The only visible change here is the dialog's copy and its labels. I checked the hosted popover that uses the new mute in light and dark.

title: core: every roof writer seats roofs on the level above their walls
body:
## What does this PR do?

The owner's rule (G1/C19): "every time we build with an LLM, it actually places the roof system on the same level as its supporting walls ... There should be a roof or a level dedicated for the roof system so we can appropriately see the floor plan without having the roof segments obstructing our view inside the home."

So: a roof lives on the level directly above the storey whose walls carry it. Over the top storey, that is the building's roof level. A porch or portico roof bearing on beams or posts stays on its storey. Legacy projects are not migrated: `verify_scene` reports them and `move_roofs_to_roof_level` repairs them.

Until now only `create_roof` and the hand roof tool followed the rule. This PR puts it in one core seam and runs every editor-side writer through it. pascalorg/private-editor#962 pins this branch's head (`a56e3c42`, which merges editor main at `b1031a51`, the commit hosted main pins) and runs the hosted writers through the same seam.

### Causes (the 29 audited gaps, grouped)

| Cause | What was wrong |
|---|---|
| C1 | Generic agent writers (`apply_patch`, `save_scene`'s graph) checked ids and schemas only, so they could put a roof on its walls' storey or walls on a roof level. |
| C2/C6 | "On the walls" was a footprint-height test. It misread generated gable porches as bearing on the house and missed a garage mass on lower walls. |
| C4 | Copy and placement writers (paste, Duplicate, the level duplicate, a fresh placement) carried a roof onto whatever level they targeted. |
| C5 | Storey-content guards tested the declared role only, or nothing. |
| C7 | The roof level did not stay on top: reorders and new levels could put it under a storey. |

### The seam

- **Bearing** (`services/roof-bearing.ts`, the Architect's edge test moved into core). A segment bears on the walls along its edges that have open air past them; a cone bears on a curved wall under its sector. `isRoofOnStoreyWalls` and `verify_scene` read it, so every roof verify reports is one the repair moves, and porches are neither.
- **Seat** (`seatRoofs`, `planRoofSeats`). A roof that a write makes, moves, turns or reshapes onto its walls' storey goes where the repair would put it, in the write's own store call. A legacy roof the write only edits stays where it is.
- **Agent writes** (`seatWrittenRoofs`, the `roof-levels` patch guard). The seat is appended as ops with a note per roof, and refusals keep the model's `patchIndex`.
- **The roof level** (`servesAsRoofLevel`). A level is the roof level if it is declared, or, in a building that declares none, if it is one of the roof-only levels at the top of the stack. It is never the lowest level. A roof-only level under a storey is a storey still to be built.
- **One lift and one order check.** `liftRoofLevels` and `roofLevelOrderBreach` serve every writer that adds or reorders levels.

### Per writer

| Writer | Now | Test |
|---|---|---|
| `apply_patch` (every MCP bridge, the in-page Architect) | Seats with notes. Refuses `roof_level`, `roof_level_holds_storey` and `roof_level_on_top`. A new storey lifts only the roof levels at the top of the stack. | `roof-writes.test.ts`, `apply-patch.test.ts` |
| `save_scene` graph | Judged against the scene it is saved over: the session's scene when the save goes to it, else the stored scene `id` names. A graph with no scene under it is saved as it is. | `save-scene.test.ts` |
| `create_story_shell`, `set_zone`, `place_items`, `add_wall`/`add_fence`/`create_stair` | `roof_level` refusal on any level that serves as the roof level, naming the storey it covers | construction-tools, set-zone, place-items tests |
| `add_object` | Refuses when given no host while the roof level is in view. An object named onto the roof level goes up with the roof (the Architect's gable louvres and chimney caps). | `add-object-cases.ts` (core, MCP and chat) |
| `duplicate_level`, the level selector's and site panel's duplicate | Seats the copy's roofs. A walled copy of a roof level loses the role. | `duplicate-level.test.ts`, `roof-writes.test.ts` |
| `verify_scene` | `roof_mixed_in_storey` exactly for the roofs the repair moves | `roof-level.test.ts` |
| Paste, cut and paste, Duplicate | Seats roofs in one history step. A paste lands on one level: onto a roof level, one carrying anything a storey holds goes to the storey it covers, whole. | `scene-clipboard.test.ts` |
| Tool manager | A storey-content tool armed on a roof level switches to the storey it covers. Storey content includes every `floorPlaced` kind (cabinets, shelves, columns, …). | |
| Move tool, plan drag/resize/cone/turn handles, roof and segment inspectors, a segment drawn into the selected roof | Commit through the seat. The selection follows a roof the seat moved. | `floorplan-affordances.test.ts`, `fresh-planar-placement.test.ts` |
| Hand roof tool (rectangle, cone) | Re-plans to the level above only when the drawn roof stands over the storey (`standsOverStorey`: an edge bears on its walls, or it covers a room they enclose). A portico over posts stays. | `tool.test.ts` |
| Level selector drag | `roofLevelOrderBreach`: refuses only an order that puts the roof level under a storey it stood over | `roof-level.test.ts` |
| Stair tool | Climbs to a storey, never into the roof level. A new upper floor goes under the roof level, which moves up. | `stair-levels.test.ts` |

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/services/roof-level.test.ts`. Bearing table (18 scenes, porches included), roof-level role table (10 stacks), lift and order check, seat table.
2. `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/roof-writes.test.ts packages/core/src/agent-operations/add-object.test.ts`. Refusals and seat for ordered writes, a second pass and a basement leaving a seated middle level alone, walls redrawn under the roof level not refused, and every core writer on six roof shapes.

Ran after merging editor main: `check-types` on all editor packages (9/9) and `biome check` on the changed files. Suites: core 4546, mcp 866 and nodes 4806 pass. Editor: 2460 pass. Its 19 failures are all in `lib/history.test.ts` and fail here only because, in this worktree's install, a spawned probe prints a `require("three")` deprecation to stderr.

Seat cost on a 9.6k-node scene with 50 roofs and 450 segments: 869 ms before the per-snapshot bearing memo, 95 ms after.

The live check is in the hosted PR (#962): real Low and Pro chat turns on this branch's build. The garage roofs went on the upper storey, the main roofs on a Roof level, and the porches stayed on Ground floor. Solo Ground floor and First floor views show open plans.

Two reviews (a gap walk, and GPT-6 Astra's adversarial pass) raised 19 findings. Editor-side resolutions:

- **save_scene judged a graph against whatever scene the session held** (high). Fixed: it is judged against the scene it is saved over, and a graph with no scene under it is saved as it is.
- **The lift moved middle roof-only levels and was not idempotent.** Fixed: `servesAsRoofLevel` reads the top run, and `liftRoofLevels` lifts only that run and roof levels the write declares.

- **Six copies of "the roof level stays on top".** Fixed: `roofLevelOrderBreach` in the selector and the guard here, and in chat and the capture REST in the hosted PR.
- **Bearing rebuilt wall spans per segment.** Fixed: identity-keyed per-level plan.
- **`add_object` wrote onto the roof level in view.** Fixed for the implicit target. Kept: an explicit roof-level parent, because the Architect hangs roof-borne objects there by design (`storeys.test.ts`).
- **The stair tool climbed into the Roof level.** Fixed.
- **Bugbot: a lone declared roof level was never lifted.** Fixed (`2cb5aa1c`).

title: A scripted ceiling item hangs from its top when placed from the library
body:
## What
The geometry-script compiler origins a ceiling-mounted script at its **top**; `add_object` places it at the ceiling plane accordingly. Library placement and the move tool (`ceilingStrategy` enter/move) dropped every non-recessed ceiling item by its full height, which is right for catalog GLBs (origined at their bottom) but hung a scripted one a full height too low: the catalog forge's island hood sat 0.5 m off the floor.

`ceilingSeatY` (core) now says where a ceiling item's origin sits in the ceiling's frame: recessed → flush, scripted → from its bounds' top, catalog model → its full height. Both ceiling strategy paths use it.

## How to test
1. Library → "Island hood" → place on a ceiling: the chimney top meets the ceiling, canopy ~1 m below.
2. Move it elsewhere on the ceiling: same height.
3. Place a catalog "Ceiling Lamp": still hangs just below the ceiling (unchanged).
4. `bun test src/components/tools/item/placement-strategies.test.ts` (packages/editor): two new ceiling cases pass.

Verified in the local editor (headless Chromium): fresh island hood top at the ceiling (2.48), bottom 1.48; after a move unchanged; catalog lamp unchanged; no console errors.

title: editor: upgrade pdfkit to 0.20 and register its standard fonts
body: ## What does this PR do? Upgrades `pdfkit` from ^0.19.1 to ^0.20.2 in `packages/editor` and adapts the floor-plan PDF export to it. Major upgrade (0.x minor), so no auto-merge. **Breaking changes ([v0.20.0](https://github.com/foliojs/pdfkit/releases/tag/v0.20.0), [v0.20.1](https://github.com/foliojs/pdfkit/releases/tag/v0.20.1), [v0.20.2](https://github.com/foliojs/pdfkit/releases/tag/v0.20.2))** - The package now has an `exports` map, so deep imports such as `pdfkit/js/pdfkit.standalone` no longer resolve. The browser entry is the `default` condition of `pdfkit`. - Standard fonts use pre-parsed metrics. In the browser build, each standard font must be imported from `pdfkit/standard-fonts/*` and registered with `registerStdFonts()`. Node still loads them lazily. - The virtual file system (`pdfkit/virtual-fs`) is removed in favour of `registerFile(path, Uint8Array)`. `Buffer` is no longer used internally. - Named exports are added (`PDFDocument`, `LineWrapper`, `registerFile`). AcroForm options are restricted to the documented mappings, annotation option keys are no longer uppercased automatically, and `addNamedEmbeddedFile` throws when no ref is given. - New experimental `toBytes`/`toBlob` helpers are available in `pdfkit/output`. **Code changes** - `createFloorplanPdfDocument` imports `pdfkit` instead of `pdfkit/js/pdfkit.standalone`, and registers the four standard faces the export falls back to (Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold, Courier, Courier-Bold). This is required: the `PDFDocument` constructor sets Helvetica, so the browser build throws `Standard font "Helvetica" is not registered` on `new PDFDocument()` without it. The Node build has no `registerStdFonts` and loads its own metrics, so the call is optional-chained. - Adds `pdfkit-standard-fonts.d.ts`, because 0.20 ships the `standard-fonts/*` entry points untyped and `@types/pdfkit` 0.17.6 (the latest) predates them. ## How to test 1. `bun install && bun run ci` 2. In `bun dev`, export a floor plan to PDF, then block the `pdf-fonts/*.ttf` requests and export again. The second export exercises the standard-font fallback. ## Screenshots / screen recording Not added yet. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Local results: `check`, `skills:validate`, `check-types` and `build` pass, with only the local-only test failures that `main` also has. A script against pdfkit 0.20's browser build confirmed two things: an unregistered `new PDFDocument()` throws, and after registering the four faces it renders all of them to a valid PDF. The full browser export flow has not been clicked through.

title: editor: let hosts supply the scene loading surface
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an optional `loadingSlot` to `Editor`, so a host can supply its loading surface in either layout and across the 2D and 3D views. The editor still owns readiness and `onLoaderChange`; a failed load always shows the existing error and retry screen. Omitting the slot or passing `null` keeps the default loader.

## How to test

1. Supply a visible `loadingSlot` and hold `onLoad` pending: the custom surface should cover the editor in both `v1` and `v2` layouts.
2. Let the scene become ready in 2D and 3D: the surface should disappear with the existing `onLoaderChange(false)` notification.
3. Reject `onLoad`: the existing failure message and **Try again** button should replace the custom surface. Omit the slot or pass `null` to verify the default loader remains available.

Validation: editor package typecheck and its dependency builds passed (`bunx turbo run check-types --filter=@pascal-app/editor`). The 21 existing `use-auto-save.integration.test.tsx` cases passed. Biome passed for the changed file.

Browser validation in an isolated Next.js host using the actual `Editor`: held loads showed the custom slot, 2D and 3D readiness dismissed it, failures and successful retries worked in both layouts, and passing `null` restored the default loader. The upstream quality and CLI smoke CI jobs passed.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — the default appearance is unchanged; the optional surface is supplied by the host.

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)

title: deps: land nine major upgrades with one lockfile
body: ## What does this PR do? Combines the changes of nine major-upgrade PRs into one branch off `main` (after #1058), with a single regenerated `bun.lock`, so they don't conflict with each other in the lockfile. **Supersedes #1060, #1062, #1063, #1064, #1065, #1066, #1067, #1068 and #1069.** Those PRs are left open, and their descriptions hold the full breaking-change notes. #1061 (`@types/three` 0.186) is not included; it's still blocked on the pool plugin. | Superseded PR | Upgrade | Source changes carried over | |---|---|---| | #1060 | typescript 6.0.3 → 7.0.2 | the metadata scanner and the ESM import fixer use the 6.0 API from `@typescript/typescript6`; `eslint-config` keeps typescript 6.0.3 | | #1062 | @types/node 22 → 26 | none | | #1063 | nanoid 5 → 6 | root `engines.node` goes to `>=22`, and `SETUP.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` say Node.js 22+ | | #1064 | motion 12 → 14 | none | | #1065 | eslint-plugin-react-hooks 5 → 7 | none (React Compiler rules are now on in `recommended`) | | #1066 | eslint 9 → 10, @eslint/js 9 → 10 | shared configs pin `settings.react.version: '19.3'`, because eslint-plugin-react's `'detect'` calls the removed `context.getFilename()` | | #1067 | globals 16 → 17 | none | | #1068 | pdfkit 0.19 → 0.20 | the floor-plan export imports `pdfkit` and registers the standard fonts the browser build requires; adds `pdfkit-standard-fonts.d.ts` | | #1069 | react-grab 0.1.50 → 0.2.0 | none | **One change not in any of the individual PRs.** Combining TypeScript 7 with ESLint showed that `typescript-eslint`, which is hoisted to the root, aborts with "typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0". #1060 had this latent problem too, but CI doesn't run ESLint. Every workspace still declares `typescript` 7.0.2, gets its own nested copy, and compiles with TS 7 (`bunx tsc --version` in a package prints 7.0.2). ## How to test 1. `bun install` (the lockfile should stay unchanged) 2. `bun run ci` 3. `cd packages/ui && bun run lint`. Expect it to be clean. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Local results: `check`, `skills:validate`, `check-types`, `build` and `packages/ui` lint all pass. `turbo run test --continue` has no failures beyond the ones a clean `main` checkout shows in this environment (GitHub CI for `main` is green). title: editor: keep loading and retry inside canvas panes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Opening a scene no longer covers the editor's navigation and sidebar. Loading and retry surfaces live inside the 2D and 3D canvas panes in both layouts, with separate readiness: the plan can appear when its data arrives while 3D finishes preparing. Split panes keep their own loading surface, and other host views remain accessible.

The loading lifecycle holds a scene read-only lease so exposed controls cannot edit an unloaded graph. The lease is released before successful hydration, retained on failure, and cleaned up on retry or unmount without releasing another owner's lock. Autosave and existing readiness notifications keep their lifecycle. The default loader remains available when the optional loading slot is omitted.

## How to test

1. Hold a scene load pending. Use the navbar and sidebar, switch between 2D/3D, and split the views: only the canvas panes should be covered. Scene edits must be rejected until data arrives.
2. Resolve the data while 3D rendering is still preparing. The 2D pane should be available immediately; the 3D pane keeps its loader until ready.
3. Reject the scene load, then retry. The error stays inside the canvas, navigation remains usable, and a successful retry removes the error and loading surfaces.
4. Repeat in both layouts and at a mobile viewport. Omit the loading slot to check the default loader. Unmount during a pending or failed load to check that its read-only lease is released.

Validation: editor typecheck and dependency builds passed; all 21 existing autosave/loading integration tests passed. Browser checks used the actual Editor in an isolated Next.js host: usable chrome during a held load, canvas bounds, independent 2D readiness with 3D frames paused, failure/retry, split panes, unique SVG IDs, default loader, mobile layout, and read-only lease cleanup/composition.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches scene load/hydration timing, autosave gating, and edit blocking via read-only leases; UX regressions could allow edits during load or leave the graph locked incorrectly.
> 
> **Overview**
> Scene loading no longer blocks the whole editor with a fixed full-screen overlay. **Loading and error/retry UI** now render inside the 2D floorplan pane, 3D viewer pane, and preview stage via a shared `loadingOverlay` (custom `loadingSlot` or default `SceneLoader`; failures still use `SceneLoadFailed`).
> 
> **2D and 3D readiness are split:** `isSceneDataLoading` covers fetch/hydration and drives the 2D overlay; `showLoader` also waits on viewer scene readiness for 3D, so the plan can become usable while WebGL is still warming up. Panes get `aria-busy` and `data-scene-loading` for accessibility and host instrumentation; `onLoaderChange` still reflects when a loader is shown in preview-aware cases.
> 
> While a scene is loading, the editor **holds a scene read-only lease** so chrome stays interactive but edits cannot touch an unloaded graph—the lease is released before successful `applySceneGraphToEditor`, re-held on load failure, and cleaned up on retry/unmount.
>

title: core: create_stair builds L and U stairs, railings and a flight to no level
body:
## What does this PR do?

One stair tool for every agent. `create_stair` now builds everything the hosted Architect plugin's `add_stair` built, so `add_stair` can retire (the hosted PR that follows does that):

- **L and U layouts.** `layout: 'l' | 'u'`, `turn: 'left' | 'right'` (the climber's side) and `lowerSteps` (the first flight's risers). The flights and landings are laid out as `fit_stair` lays them out (`planStairPreset`): a landing as deep as the stair is wide, and a U's second landing across. `planStairPreset` now takes a riser count, a run and the first flight's risers. `fit_stair` passes none of them and behaves as before.
- **Railings.** `railingStyle` (balusters, post-and-rail, cable, boards, glass, metal) and `railingMaterial` (a library id, refused when unknown), beside `railingMode`. The railing enums move to a dependency-free `schema/nodes/stair-types.ts`, so the contract can use them (the contracts may only import zod and dependency-free files).
- **A flight to no level.** `toLevelId: null` builds porch or deck steps. The flight rises `height` (by default the storey's floor-to-floor height), keeps that rise, cuts no opening and makes no level. An opening option on such a flight is refused (`no_level_above`).
- **One origin.** (x, z) is described once, as the middle of the bottom riser where the first flight starts. Before this PR, `create_stair` called it "the back-centre of the first step" and `add_stair` called it "the centre of the bottom riser", and both wrote the same point. The case table checks the description against the stair's own footprint geometry at all four climbs.
- **The result** now gives `segmentIds` (an L or U has several segments; nothing read `segmentId`), `layout`, `rise`, the run, the whole `footprint` and the `arrival` point where the top step lands.
- **Openings as given on an L or U.** An opening cut as given defaults to the stair's footprint in its own frame (for a straight flight this is the same opening as before). Its owner pose now keeps that footprint box, and the live opening sync (`owned-floor-openings.ts`) maps the opening from the old box to the new one, so refitting an L (`fit_stair fitRun`) keeps its landing and turned flight under the hole; while the stair's segments are hidden or missing it keeps the box it last had. An opening cut before keeps the width and first-run scaling it was made with, and no metadata changes on load. The slab and ceiling it cuts are the ones covering most of the flights and landings, not the one under the footprint's middle (for an L, that falls in its empty inside corner).
- **Refusals with a code:** `stair_layout_required` (`turn` or `lowerSteps` without an L or U), `stair_layout` (a split the risers cannot take, or "An L stair needs at least 4 risers") and `no_level_above`.
- `steps` now accepts 2, the stair sizing's own minimum, so two steps up to a porch can be asked for.
- **A `@pascal-app/core/stair-footprint` subpath and `stairSegmentFootprints`**, each visible segment's plan outline (a flight with its nosing, a landing, a winder's own outline); the straight stair's bounding box is now read from it. A host can then read an L or U stair's footprint and top step (`stairArrivalOpening`) as core draws them, without loading the core root and its store. The hosted chat's program checks (`scene.check()`) and room blueprint use both.
- **One rule for a way upstairs: `stairReachesStoreyAbove`** (beside `resolveStairTotalRise`, and on a `@pascal-app/core/stair-rise-query` subpath). A flight onto a deck or to no level (a `fromLevelId` and no `toLevelId`, as `toLevelId: null` writes) reaches nothing, whatever its rise. One naming a level above reaches it. One following its storey reaches the storey above when there is one. One with its own `totalRise` and no level named (an Architect `add_stair` flight, an older stair given a custom rise) reaches it when that rise is within a riser of the floor-to-floor height, above or below. A declared roof level is no storey. `stairClimbsToNoStorey` (porch or deck steps) is exported beside it. `verify_scene` now counts only these for `missing_stair`, so a two-storey house whose only stair is porch steps is reported, and it no longer reports porch or deck steps as standing off the floor slab. The hosted `scene.check()`, the chat's missing-stair nudge and the bench graders read the same predicate.

Docs: the `pascal-3d` skill, the MCP README row, `agent-surfaces.md` and the vertical model's helper table.

## The case table

`agent-operations/__fixtures__/add-stair-cases.ts` holds every call `add_stair` served, each beside the `create_stair` call that covers it. The sources are the host's stored threads (their coordinates moved into the fixture's hall), the calls the Architect's skills teach, and `add_stair`'s own sizing. The core, MCP and chat runners all run it without a model. Each check confirms the stair `add_stair` would have built in everything but its sizing: the first flight running from (x, z) along the climb, the flights and landings in order, landing depth = width, the railings, the levels joined, and the opening cut (or none). The risers and run are `create_stair`'s own sizing (risers of at most 18 cm on 28 cm goings: 16 risers for the 2.8 m storey, where `add_stair` built 15 on 10-1/2 in treads), except in the two rows that pass `add_stair`'s sizing as `steps` and `length`, which build its risers and run. The case names say which.

| `add_stair` call | `create_stair` call that covers it |
|---|---|
| `climb: 'north', width: 0.95, railing: 'right', toLevelId` (stored threads) | `rotation: 180, width: 0.95, railingMode: 'right', toLevelId` |
| `climb: 'south', width: 1, railing: 'both', name` (stored threads) | `railingMode: 'both', name` (rotation 0) |
| defaults, `climb: 'east'` (3'-6", handrail left) | `rotation: 90, width: 1.067, railingMode: 'left'` |
| `climb: 'west', railing: 'right'` | `rotation: 270, railingMode: 'right'` |
| `shape: 'L-left', lowerRisers: 7` | `layout: 'l', turn: 'left', lowerSteps: 7` → at `create_stair`'s sizing, flight 7, landing, flight 9 left |
| `shape: 'L-right'` (risers halved) | `layout: 'l', turn: 'right'` → at `create_stair`'s sizing, flight 8, landing, flight 8 right |
| `shape: 'U-left', lowerRisers: 8` | `layout: 'u', turn: 'left', lowerSteps: 8` → flight, landing, landing left, flight left |
| `shape: 'U-right'` | `layout: 'u', turn: 'right'` |
| `railingStyle: 'cable', railingMaterial: 'black'` | `railingStyle: 'cable', railingMaterial: 'library:preset-nearblack'` |
| `railingStyle: 'post-and-rail', railingMaterial: 'wood-plank'` | `railingMode: 'left', railingStyle: 'post-and-rail', railingMaterial: 'library:wood-woodplank19'` |
| `railing: 'right', railingStyle: 'boards', railingMaterial: 'steel'` | `railingStyle: 'boards', railingMaterial: 'library:metal-steel'` |
| `railingStyle: 'balusters', railingMaterial: 'wood-woodfine1'` | `railingMaterial: 'wood-woodfine1'` → `library:wood-woodfine1` |
| `railing: 'none'` | `railingMode: 'none'` |
| no `toLevelId` (rises the storey's height) | `toLevelId: null` → rise 2.8 m, no opening |
| no `toLevelId`, `totalRise: 1.2, width: 1.83` (porch, 6 ft) | `toLevelId: null, height: 1.2, width: 1.83` → 7 risers, no opening |
| no `toLevelId`, `totalRise: 0.38` (two steps) | `toLevelId: null, height: 0.38, steps: 2` |
| `totalRise: 3.05, toLevelId` | `height: 3.05` → 17 risers, opening cut |
| its own sizing (risers ≤ 7-3/4 in, 10-1/2 in treads) | `steps: 15, length: '157.5 in'` → 15 risers, run 4.0005 m, as `add_stair` built |
| `shape: 'L-right', lowerRisers: 7` at its sizing | `layout: 'l', turn: 'right', lowerSteps: 7, steps: 15, length: '157.5 in'` → flight 7, landing, flight 8 right, as `add_stair` built |

The compass maps to rotation as south 0, east 90, north 180, west 270. `add_stair`'s railing names are library ids. For the default split, `add_stair` rounded half down and `create_stair` rounds half up, so an odd count passes `lowerSteps`. The hosted retired answer tells a model how to keep `add_stair`'s sizing (`steps` and `length`) and its defaults (`width: 1.067`, `railingMode: 'left'`).

Two calls are not covered, on purpose. Both are below `create_stair`'s fewest risers, which are the editor's own (two for a straight flight, four for an L or U):
- `add_stair` with a rise of one riser or less (≤ 7-3/4 in) built a one-riser "flight", a single step.
- `add_stair` with an L or U of three risers (a rise ≤ 23-1/4 in) built flight 1, landing, flight 2. `create_stair` builds such a rise with four risers, and refuses `steps: 3` on an L or U.

None of the stored calls did either.

`structure-cases.ts` adds `create_stair`'s new edge cases: a U's opening as given defaults to the footprint, an L's opening as given goes through the slab over its flights when another slab lies under its middle, the three new refusals, a flight to no level from the top storey makes no level, and an unknown railing material is refused. `owned-floor-openings.test.ts` refits an L with a floor-only opening and checks the opening still holds every segment, also after its segments were hidden and shown again, and that missing segments write nothing. `verify-scene-cases.ts` adds porch steps and a full-height flight to no level under a storey (`missing_stair`), an older stair naming no level at its storey's rise (connects), at twice it (does not) and on the top storey under the roof level (does not), and porch steps off the slab (no `stair_outside_slab`).

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/operations.test.ts -t create_stair`: 46 cases (27 of `create_stair`'s own, 19 of `add_stair`'s); `-t verify_scene`: 46.
2. `bun test packages/core/src/systems/owned-floor-openings.test.ts`.
3. `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.test.ts -t create_stair`: the same tables over a real MCP client (45; one case is core and chat only).
4. `bun run check-types`.

Run for this PR, rebased on main (#1076): `check-types` (9 packages), the core tests (4632 pass), the MCP tests (943 pass) and Biome over the changed files. The S1 origin check was mutation-tested: shifting the stair's position by 5 cm fails all the `add_stair` cases. The L opening test fails with the footprint mapping turned off. In the private host the chat runner (`shared-tools.test.ts -t create_stair`, 46 pass) runs the same tables.

## Review findings

From the review of the hosted PR (pascalorg/private-editor#1013), the ones in this repo, all fixed:
- `verify_scene` counted porch steps as connecting the storeys: `stairReachesStoreyAbove`, above.
- The riser-minimum refusal read "A l stair needs at least 4 risers": now "An L stair…".
- An L's opening as given stopped matching after a resize: the pose keeps the footprint box, above.
- The slab to cut was picked by the opening's middle, which for an L lies in its inside corner: picked by overlap with the flights and landings, above.
- The case table claimed `add_stair`'s sizing where it checked `create_stair`'s: relabelled, above.
- `add_stair`'s three-riser L or U was not listed: listed as the second exclusion, above.

A GPT-6 Astra pass over these fixes found two more here, both fixed: the predicate took a declared roof level for the storey above, and an as-given opening dropped its footprint box (for good) while its stair's segments were hidden or missing.

## Bench (main vs this PR, one server after the other on one port)

The case table without a model, against each server's hosted MCP (`/api/mcp`), one fresh project per case (run before the review fixes):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `create_stair`'s own cases | 18/25 | 25/25 |
| `add_stair`'s cases, as `create_stair` calls | 0/19 | 19/19 |
| median call | 76 ms | 40 ms |

On main the 26 failures are the new inputs (`layout`, `turn`, `lowerSteps`, `railingStyle`, `railingMaterial`, `toLevelId: null`, `steps: 2`) being dropped or refused, and the result lacking `footprint`. The model lanes (GPT-6 Astra, Low, 3 reps) are in the hosted PR: no stair call failed on either arm, and no lane regressed.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A: no editor UI changes. The hosted PR has the chat screenshots of one real Low turn building a U stair with black cable railings and porch steps to no level.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (in the private host, which runs these packages)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: A click anywhere on a leaf row of the scene tree selects it
body:
## What

In the scene tree, every row kept a 16 px fold button before its icon, also on rows with nothing to fold. On a leaf row (a window, a door, an item) the button was empty: it stopped the click's propagation and called a no-op `onToggle`. A click in that 16 px, just left of the icon, selected nothing.

`TreeNodeWrapper` now renders the fold button only on a row with children. A leaf row keeps the same space as a plain `span`, so a click there reaches the row and selects it.

## Why now

The hosted nightly's `window-merge.spec.ts` failed every time, locally and on CI: two windows clicked in the tree, then no inspector and no Merge windows button. Rows now sit one level deeper under "Elements", which put a window row's empty fold button at 48–64 px from the row's left edge. That is exactly where the spec clicks (x = 60), so neither click selected anything.

Reproduced by hand with a feedback account's seeded corner-window project:
- A click at x = 60 of the "Corner window" row changes no selection (a selection-store subscription logged nothing).
- A click on the label selects it.
- A Cmd-click on the second window gives `selectedIds: ["window_cwsquare", "window_cwbay"]` and the inspector.

Multi-select from the tree and the merge action work. Only the dead spot was wrong.

## Checks

- `check-types` for `@pascal-app/editor`, run from the hosted worktree (`bunx turbo run check-types --filter=@pascal-app/editor`).
- Biome ignores `components/ui` in this repo.
- The hosted bump PR carries the browser proof: `window-merge.spec.ts` in a nightly dispatch on a throwaway branch pinned to this commit.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized UI hit-target change in the site panel tree; no auth, data, or API impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Leaf rows in the scene tree now select when you click the fold-column area**, fixing a dead zone where an empty fold control swallowed clicks.
> 
> `TreeNodeWrapper` only renders the chevron **fold button** when `hasChildren` is true. Rows without children keep the same **16×16 px** gutter via a non-interactive `span`, so layout stays aligned but clicks reach the row’s `onClick` (selection, Cmd-click multi-select, etc.). Parent rows still use a button that `stopPropagation` and calls `onToggle`.
