title: core: view_scene takes a front photo's sides, the person's view, a light and a size
body:
## What does this PR do?

`view_scene` becomes the one tool an agent looks at the house with (the owner's G2, slice V of the agent tool catalogue). It now covers every view the Architect plugin's `screenshot_3d` took, so the hosted PR that pins this one (pascalorg/private-editor#1023) retires that tool.

- **Sides as a front photo names them.** `from` also takes `street`, `street-left`, `street-right`, `left`, `right`, `back`, `back-left` and `back-right`, as seen standing in the street facing the house.
  - They turn with the house's street, core's new `buildingStreet`: the street edge its site records (its `frontEdge`, else its first `streetEdges` entry), else the house's own front, its −z turned by its yaw (the way a generated house faces).
  - The hosted Architect's `street_order`, plan labels, `compare_to_reference` and `design_check` read the same function, so a street side never disagrees with them. This replaces the `no_street` refusal of the first round: on Pro's placeholder lot, which records no street, every street side was refused while `street_order` described a street.
  - The street is read from the framed building: the target's, an interior view's floor's, or the scene's. Buildings on several sites with neither are refused (`which_building`).
  - Corners are at 45°, like the compass corners. Compass sides and `above` are unchanged.
- **`camera: 'current'`** looks through the person's own view. The host passes it to `sceneViewPlan` as `currentCamera`: position, target, projection, fov or view width, and the canvas aspect.
  - A host with no person's view refuses it with `no_current_camera` (the MCP; on the hosted chat a sandbox, a walk in first person, a layout showing the plan alone).
  - Asked together with a viewpoint of the agent's own, it is refused with `camera_and_viewpoint`.
- **`lighting`** (`day`, `overcast`, `sunset`, `dusk`, `night`, or `current`) comes back from `sceneViewPlan`, and the MCP passes it to `SceneViewHost.capture`. The host renders in that light.
- **`maxPx`** makes the picture smaller on its longest side (64 to 1920). No view is longer than 1920 px, the default included: the person's view on a portrait canvas or a narrow photo camera is scaled to fit.
- **Every storey and the roof are framed.** A view of a building, or of the whole scene, frames its roofs up to the peak with its storeys. Before, a roof on a roof level of its own was cut off at the top storey. A plugin's node on a level (Architect's roof planes) frames up to its storey's top, as `screenshot_3d` framed it.
- **Capture sessions are counted once, in core.** `camera-controls:capture-session` is a typed event on core's bus, and `events/capture-sessions.ts` counts its owners from the moment core loads (`isCaptureSessionOn`, `subscribeCaptureSessions`). The editor's finished presentation follows that count (`presentWhileCapturing`): the first session presents the finished house and the last puts the person's view back, however a sheet's pictures and an agent's view overlap. The hosted Bones plugin reads the same count to draw its X-ray finished, so a renderer mounted mid-session knows it at once.
- **The description says each thing once.** The street sides are explained in `from`, and the MCP's refusal of the person's view in `camera`. The definition grows from 4,602 to about 5,760 characters for the new sides, lights and sizes. The hosted chat defers it behind `discover_pascal_tools`, so a turn that never looks doesn't pay for it.
- MCP README, agent guide and CHANGELOG updated.

### Review findings

All resolved here or in the hosted PR:
- **Street sides on a lot with no recorded street** (Pro's street tools disagreed with `view_scene`): one rule, `buildingStreet`, for both; see above. Rows for a streetEdges-only lot, no street, a turned house and no site.
- **An interior view with a street side** names its building through the floor: `{ interior: { levelId }, from: 'street' }` on two lots no longer asks for a target. Row added.
- **The default size was not capped**: `sized()` caps at `VIEW_MAX_PX`. Row added: the person's view at aspect 0.6 is 1152 × 1920, not 1920 × 3200.
- **`siteStreet` returned an unused `edge`**: `buildingStreet` returns the direction only.
- **Two capture-session trackers** (the editor's and Bones'): one, in core; the editor's `captureSessions` goes.
- **`maxPx` bounds**: rows for 64, 1920 and 2048 (refused `invalid_input` by the contract's schema; the core runner now checks every row's input against it).
- **Row 1's `was`** claimed `screenshot_3d {}`; it now says it is `view_scene`'s own default and that `{}` was `street-left` (the next row).

### The case table

`packages/core/src/agent-operations/__fixtures__/view-scene-cases.ts` lists every view `screenshot_3d` was asked for (its `view`, `lighting` and `maxPx` values, and the calls stored Pro threads made), each mapped to the `view_scene` call that covers it. Three runners execute it without a model: core (`scene-view.test.ts`, 39 rows), the MCP (`view-scene.test.ts`, 36 rows) and the hosted chat (pascalorg/private-editor, `lib/ai/__tests__/scene-view.test.ts`, 38 rows). The MCP skips the three rows that need a person's view and the schema row; core and the chat skip the MCP's refusal; the chat skips the schema row, which its model API refuses.

The house is two storeys of 12 × 8 m with a 30° hip roof on its own roof level, on a 30 m lot whose recorded front is its east line. A row passes when the eye stands within 2° of the side worked out by hand, every corner of the house and the roof is in the frame, and the size and light are the ones asked for.

title: One finish tool: paint reaches every part with surfaces, search_materials browses the library
body:
## What

Catalogue slice F (G2): one finish tool. The Architect plugin's `set_material` and `list_materials` retire into core's shared `paint` and `search_materials` in the hosted PR that follows. This PR grows the two shared tools until they cover every case the retiring tools served, and proves it with a case table that runs without a model on the core, MCP and chat runners.

- **`paint` reaches every part with surfaces.** It reads core's slot declarations (`nodeSlotDeclarations`), so blocks, stairs and their flights, cabinets, shelves, elevators, roof accessories and the rest take a finish, not just walls, slabs, ceilings, fences, doors, windows and columns. A block's body, and any part with one surface, is painted without a role. A stair flight's slots are now declared in core (`stairSegmentSlots`), shared with its node definition.
- **A roof shows one finish per surface.** A roof-segment target paints its roof (the note says so). A roof's finish takes the same role off its segments, and a segment's catch-all finish from an older paint stays on its other roles. Before, `paint` refused a roof whose segment had a finish of its own (`shadowed_field`). This is what Architect's `set_material` did through `paintRoof` and what its `settleRoofPaint` repaired after every write, which the hosted PR deletes (W1).
- **A roof's fascia is its own role** (`fascia`), written on every segment of the roof, since each segment holds it. A fascia band's finish (`create_roof`'s `fasciaMaterialPreset`) used to hide role `wall`.
- **A wall's `exterior` and `interior`** read its rooms, else its stored sides (`frontSide`/`backSide`, as a generator writes them). A partition, with a room on each face, is interior on both. Before, a wall with rooms on both sides or none was refused. A wall whose sides nothing says, or a face that rooms stand on for only part of its length (`roomFaceCover`, measured along the wall so a curve's ends count), is refused `side_unknown`, naming the face to paint whole.
- **An item's surfaces** come from its model's `slot_<id>` materials, which a headless host can't read: `paint` writes the role named, as the editor's Paint writes the one clicked, and its note says paint can't check it. Without a role it asks, naming the roles already painted. On an item, and on any kind but a wall, `exterior` and `interior` are slot names.
- **A bare community id** (`mtl_…`) is written as `library:<id>`, as a built-in id is (I1). A malformed one (`library:mtl_missing.`) is refused; a well-formed one is the host's to check (the hosted MCP checks its database before the call), by the same `isCommunityMaterialId`.
- **`search_materials` browses and reads the whole library.** A query without words lists a kind (new `kind` filter), a surface or the whole library, by name, 150 at a time; a search lists its best 12 at a time; `more` and `next` page the rest of either. A query whose words are all too short or too common (`tv`, `for the`) finds nothing and says so under `missing`, rather than browsing. It reads the materials the host registered (community, mine, workspace), with Pascal's own winning an id collision. A search also matches a piece of an id (`plank48`, `48`, and three letters no word answers, `cco`), as `list_materials`' substring did. The kinds and surfaces live in `material-kinds.ts`, so the contract names them without a copy (`@pascal-app/core/material-library` still exports them).
- **The roof segment renderer** resolves a fascia ref as it resolves the other roles, so a native material (`scene:`) or a colour on the boards shows.
- **The case table**: `packages/core/src/agent-operations/__fixtures__/finish-cases.ts`, in `AGENT_TOOL_CASES`, so the core, MCP and chat runners all run it.

## Why

The owner, verbatim (G2): "we need to compile and harmonize tools developped by Wassim, Adam (AxiomeCG), and Steven Tibbs from the AI capabilities to avoid conflicts, explosation in complexity, and increase reliability and consistency of outputs."

A finish had three tools at Pro (`paint`, `set_material`, `list_materials` + `material_guide`) with different ids (`library:<id>` against bare ids and PlanCrafters keys), different roof rules (refuse a shadowed roof against write the roof) and different refusals (an error with a code against a successful text). The catalogue rule is that a tool retires only when its replacement covers every case it served, proved by a case table run without a model in the editor PR. The rows are in `wiki/ai/tool-catalogue.md` (hosted).

## The case table

Each case is a call the retiring tool served: its contract, the Architect skills that told the model to call it, the stored Pro threads (`local-08`, `-09`, `-17`, `-30`) and the Pro bench runs of 2026-10-11. Each runs as the replacement call through the core operation, the MCP server (a real client) and the hosted chat's executor (the hosted PR's `shared-tools.test.ts`). The main column is the same table run against `main`'s core.

| # | What the retired tool served, and how the replacement answers | The replacement call | main | PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | set_material slot 'exterior' on a run of walls (a stored Pro call): paint role exterior, the face turned out of the rooms | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_s","wall_e"],"role":"exterior","material":"library:siding-lap-white"}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |
| 2 | set_material slot 'interior' with a flat colour (a stored Pro call): paint role interior | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_n","wall_w"],"role":"interior","material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |
| 3 | set_material 'interior' on a partition painted one face; paint paints both, a room on each | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_mid"],"role":"interior","material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 4 | set_material 'exterior' on a partition painted a face inside the house; paint refuses: it has none | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_mid"],"role":"exterior","material":"library:siding-lap-white"}` (refuses `side_unknown`) | pass | pass |
| 5 | set_material 'exterior' on a wall no room touches: paint reads its stored sides, as set_material did | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_garden"],"role":"exterior","material":"library:siding-lap-white"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 6 | set_material with no slot on a wall painted both faces: paint with no role does too | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_e"],"material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |

| 9 | set_material on a roof, slot 'top' (its default): paint's default role on a roof is top | `paint` `{"targets":["roof_finish"],"material":"library:roof-greyshingles"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |

| 12 | set_material on a roof segment painted its roof: so does paint, and says so | `paint` `{"targets":["rseg_plain"],"material":"library:roof-greyshingles"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 13 | set_material slot 'gable' (also 'edge', 'trim'): paint role edge, the gable ends and trim band | `paint` `{"targets":["roof_finish"],"role":"edge","material":"library:preset-nearblack"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 14 | set_material slot 'soffit' (also 'fascia', 'deck', 'wall'): paint role wall, the fascia and soffit | `paint` `{"targets":["rseg_own"],"role":"wall","material":"library:siding-lap-cedar"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 15 | a fascia band with a finish of its own keeps it under role wall; role fascia paints the boards on every segment | `paint` `{"targets":["rseg_own"],"role":"fascia","material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 16 | roof_soffit's fascia on a segment with a catch-all finish (Architect's own writer, settleRoofPaint gone): role wall shows on it | `paint` `{"targets":["roof_finish"],"role":"wall","material":"library:preset-nearblack"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 17 | set_material's standing seam (ROOFING metal_black, a metal colour): paint a native metal material | `paint` `{"targets":["roof_finish"],"material":{"preset":"metal","properties":{"color":"#2b2e32","roughness":0.55,"metalness":0.45}},"materialName…` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 18 | set_material on a slab, a terrace (its 'surface' default): paint's default on a slab is its surface | `paint` `{"targets":["slab_finish"],"material":"library:wood-floorplank1"}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |
| 19 | set_material on a ceiling: paint its surface | `paint` `{"targets":["ceiling_finish"],"material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |
| 20 | set_material's window and door frames ('frame', preset-nearblack): paint role frame | `paint` `{"targets":["window_finish","door_finish"],"role":"frame","material":"library:preset-nearblack"}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |
| 21 | set_material on a block ('body'): paint's default on a block is its body | `paint` `{"targets":["block_pier"],"material":"library:flooring-wallstone1"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 22 | set_material on a stair and its flight ('treads'): paint role treads on both | `paint` `{"targets":["stair_finish","sseg_finish"],"role":"treads","material":"library:wood-woodplank48"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 23 | set_material on a cabinet ('front'): paint role front | `paint` `{"targets":["cabinet_finish"],"role":"front","material":"library:preset-navy"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 24 | set_material wrote any slot asked ('surface' on a stair, which has none); paint names the stair's | `paint` `{"targets":["stair_finish"],"role":"surface","material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (refuses `unknown_role`) | fail | pass |
| 25 | set_material on a catalog item's slot ('body', its model's slot_body): paint role body writes it, as the editor's Paint does | `paint` `{"targets":["item_vase"],"role":"body","material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 26 | set_material with no slot on an item wrote a 'surface' it may lack; paint asks for the role, naming those painted | `paint` `{"targets":["item_vase"],"material":"library:preset-softwhite"}` (refuses `unknown_role`) | fail | pass |
| 27 | set_material took a bare community id ('mtl_…'): paint writes it as library:<id> | `paint` `{"targets":["block_pier"],"material":"mtl_terrazzo_green"}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 28 | set_material skipped an id not in the scene and painted the rest; paint refuses the call, painting nothing | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_s","wall_gone"],"role":"exterior","material":"library:siding-lap-white"}` (refuses `target_not_found`) | pass | pass |
| 29 | set_material answered an unknown id with a plain text; paint refuses it with the library's nearest | `paint` `{"targets":["wall_s"],"role":"exterior","material":"library:siding-vinyl-beige"}` (refuses `unknown_material`) | pass | pass |
| 30 | list_materials with no filter listed the library: a browse with no words lists all of it by name | `search_materials` `{"queries":[{}]}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 31 | list_materials by surface ({surface: 'floor'}, a stored Pro call): a browse of the floor | `search_materials` `{"queries":[{"surface":"floor"}]}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 32 | list_materials by category ('roofing'): a browse of a kind | `search_materials` `{"queries":[{"kind":"roofing"}]}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 33 | list_materials by category 'paint' (a stored Pro call; no such category, so nothing listed): a browse of the flat colours | `search_materials` `{"queries":[{"kind":"colors"}]}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 34 | list_materials by a word ('stucco'): search the word | `search_materials` `{"queries":[{"query":"stucco"}]}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |
| 35 | list_materials matched any piece of an id ('plank48', '48'): so does a search | `search_materials` `{"queries":[{"query":"plank48"},{"query":"48"}]}` (writes / lists it) | fail | pass |
| 36 | list_materials matched a word inside an id ('lap'): a search matches an id's words | `search_materials` `{"queries":[{"query":"lap","surface":"wall"}]}` (writes / lists it) | pass | pass |

36 cases: 23 fail on `main`, all 36 pass here on all three runners.

**Added in review** (all pass on the three runners; the `main` column above was not re-run for them):

| # | What the retired tool served, and how the replacement answers | The replacement call |
|---|---|---|
| 37 | set_material 'exterior' on a wall no room touches and no side stored painted face b (its guess); paint asks for the face | `paint` on `wall_free`, role exterior (refuses `side_unknown`) |
| 38 | set_material 'interior' on a wall with rooms along all of one face and part of the other painted its stored side; paint asks for the face | `paint` on a T-junction's `wall_long`, role interior (refuses `side_unknown`, naming face b) |
| 39 | the same wall, 'exterior' | role exterior (refuses `side_unknown`) |
| 40 | a native material on the fascia boards is kept as a scene material each segment shows | `paint` role fascia, a native material |
| 41 | set_material on an item's slot named 'exterior' (its model's slot_exterior) | `paint` on `item_vase`, role exterior (writes `slots.exterior`) |
| 42 | list_materials listed every match of a word ('wood', 23 then): a search lists 12 at a time, with `more` and `next` | `search_materials` `wood`, then offset 12 |
| 43 | list_materials matched nothing for 'tv' or 'for the': a search lists none, never the whole library | `search_materials` `tv`, `for the` |
| 44 | list_materials matched three letters inside an id ('cco' of concrete-stucco) | `search_materials` `cco` |

Where the replacement deliberately differs (each one is a case above):
- `set_material` skipped an id that wasn't in the scene and painted the rest. `paint` refuses the whole call, as it always has.
- An unknown material was a successful text ("no material …"). `paint` refuses it with `unknown_material` and the library's nearest (R1).
- `set_material` wrote any slot it was asked for (`surface` on a stair, which has none). `paint` refuses with the stair's slots.
- `list_materials`' `category` was a substring. `kind` is the library's enum, and a stored call's `category: 'paint'` (no such category) becomes the flat colours (`kind: 'colors'`).
- `set_material` guessed a face for a wall with no room and no stored side (exterior b, interior a), and painted a wall's stored side whatever its rooms. `paint` asks for the face, a or b, when its sides are unknown or rooms stand on only part of a face.

## Bench

Since then the branch has been rebased onto `604fd4725`, with no change to the slice. Two check commits were added (`802b826c0`, `1f10adea3`), and every run below was re-graded with them, at no model cost. gpt-6-astra at low effort, 3 reps per lane, signed in as a feedback account.

**The case table without a model** (core runner, the PR's `finish-cases.ts` against each core): 36 cases. On `main` (`c6637b31`), 13 pass and 23 fail. On this PR, all 36 pass.

| PR | fidelity (4 tasks) | mcp | 12 | 69/93 | 10 | 101 | 12 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 171.6k | 47.9 s |

What the numbers say:
- **No regression.** Every task scores the same on both arms, lane by lane. The fidelity tasks match one for one (create-design 9/15, fit-wall 12/18, mount-device 18/21 direct and 9/21 MCP, stretch-room 36/39 direct and 38 → 39/39 MCP). None of the fidelity tool errors involve `paint` or `search_materials`. They come from `discover_pascal_tools`, the fit-wall `update_node`/`apply_patch` refusals and `add_object`'s geometry script, and they appear on both arms.
- **The workflow lane stops after its first segment on both arms.** Since the executor protocol landed, `persistAiWorkflowInput` refuses a continuation that does not carry the tab's executor identity, and the bench harness has none. A turn therefore ends at its first client tool, here `search_materials`, which happens on `main` too. So `cap-finishes` also ran on `--lane direct` (the same chat route, prompt and tools, with the harness running the client tools) and `--lane mcp`.
- **cap-finishes, direct:** every finish check passes on all 6 runs. The one check that fails, on both arms, is "tool calls without errors": the model's first call is `discover_pascal_tools`, which the direct harness does not serve.
- **cap-finishes, MCP:** every finish check passes. "Called paint" fails on both arms because the MCP model puts its `paint` calls inside `run_batch`.
- **Inline colour vs library colour.** On this PR the model painted the inside walls soft white as a native material (`#F5F3EE`, "Soft white wall paint") on 3 of 3 runs. On `main` it did so on 1 of 3 runs and used `library:preset-softwhite` on the other 2. Both render soft white. The `finish` check now reads a scene material as the library flat colour nearest it, the way `paint` answers a colour. The interior check asks for `preset-(soft)?white`, so white siding inside does not pass it. Every run above is graded with that check.
- **Retired-name calls: 0.** Low and the MCP never offered `set_material`. Pro is not benched per slice: the plan runs Pro at the milestone after F and N1.
- **The killed run.** `main`'s first direct `cap-finishes` run was killed after 2 reps by another session's `pkill -f "eval/run.ts --tasks"`. Those 2 reps scored the same as the rerun (6/7). The table uses 3 fresh reps.

The numbers come from the hosted PR, which runs these tasks; pascalorg/private-editor#1024 has the live check.

## How to test

- In this repo: `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations` (the core runner, `paint.test.ts`, `search-materials.test.ts`) and `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.test.ts` (the MCP runner).
- Hosted: `apps/community/features/community/lib/ai/__tests__/shared-tools.test.ts` (the chat runner).
- Results on this branch (rebased onto `bed2a9f4`): editor `check-types` 9/9; core, MCP and the wall and roof-segment nodes tests 5854 pass; Biome clean. Hosted, on its PR: typecheck 26/26, tests 25/25, contracts.
- A seeded roof whose fascia boards were painted a native red (`paint` role fascia) renders a red band in the editor (local screenshot `/tmp/feedback-work/g2-f/fascia2/fascia-native.png`).

## Review

GPT-6 Astra reviewed both PRs adversarially. Fixed in the second commit: item slots by name, the fascia role, the bare community id, id pieces in a search and a paged browse. A stronger whole-library case and `roof_soffit` through core's paint are in the hosted PR. Kept as is: `kind` is an exact enum rather than `list_materials`' category substring, because the schema names the kinds and a word query matches the kind too (`roof` finds roofing).

Hosted PR: pascalorg/private-editor#1024, which pins this branch's head. The retiring tools are Steven's, and `paint` and `search_materials` are Adam's. Neither can be added as a reviewer on this repo, so their reviews are requested on the hosted PR.

**Second round** (the orchestrator's review findings, then GPT-6 Astra on the fixes). Each is fixed here or in the hosted PR, which lists them all:
- A wall face that rooms cover in part (a T-junction, a wall running on into the garden) was painted whole as interior; it is refused, naming the face. Coverage is measured along the wall, an arc's station found exactly (Astra: a half circle's end hid 0.785 m behind 0.06 m of chord, and sampling the arc still read 15 cm as 7 cm).
- A freestanding wall with unknown sides is refused, and the table says set_material guessed face b.
- `paint` role fascia with a native material showed nothing: the renderer now resolves it.
- An item slot named `exterior` or `interior` is paintable.
- `search_materials`: a short or stop-word query browsed the whole library; a search cut at 12 with no `more`; three-letter pieces. All fixed, with cases.
- The contract's kinds were a hand copy: now one constant, and the published subpath still exports it (Astra).
- Declined: checking a community id against the host's registered materials once it has any. The registry can hold only the scene's materials (the Pro sandbox executor), so a valid id would be refused (Astra). A malformed id is refused instead, and a material catalog the host passes per call is parked in the hosted `plans/meta-todos.md`.

title: Moving the paint brush off a surface clears its preview
body:
## What

In paint mode, moving the brush off a surface left that surface previewed. Its paint preview and warm outline stayed, and the HUD kept saying "Paint: Face" while the brush was over the ground.

Why: `onLeave` in `selection-manager.tsx` re-resolved the paint interaction from the leave event, then returned early when that came back empty. A leave event's ray no longer meets the node it left, so the resolver (role, opening and pass-through checks) always came back empty. Every leave was ignored.

`onLeave` now goes by the node that left. When it is the hovered node, the hover ends: HUD, outline, preview, `hoveredId` and highlight mode. A surface behind the hovered one leaving is still ignored, as before. Every paint interaction hovers `event.node.id`, the roof and roof-segment arms included, so the id is the same thing the old check compared.

## Evidence

A probe in the hosted app (nine batched walls, paint mode, a new material, the brush moved onto a wall face and then onto the ground). It logged each leave and counted the outline's warm pixels:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Brush on the ground, before any hover | 0, "Hover a surface to paint" | 0, "Hover a surface to paint" |
| Brush on the wall face | 1734 to 2426, "Paint: Face" | 1776 to 2411, "Paint: Face" |
| Brush back on the ground, 1 s and 4 s later | 1910 to 2506, "Paint: Face" | 0, "Hover a surface to paint" |

Every leave event logged `interaction: NULL`, including the hovered wall's own. A click on the ground did not paint the stale wall either before or after this change.

The hosted nightly's `wall-hover-outline.spec.ts` measures exactly this. Its paint baseline is taken with the brush parked on the ground, so the stale outline was already in the baseline, and the hover added nothing (-788, -414, -314, 1 warm px). With this fix it passed 3 of 3 locally (2036, 2207, 2434 warm px).

## Checks

- `bunx turbo run check-types --filter=@pascal-app/editor` and Biome on the file, run from the hosted worktree.
- The hosted bump PR carries the browser proof: `wall-hover-outline.spec.ts` in the nightly dispatch.

> Small, localized fix to paint-mode pointer leave handling with no data or auth impact; behavior change is clearing stale UI state users already expect.
> 
> **Overview**

title: editor: vertex-colored meshes over 65k faces export instead of failing
body:
## What does this PR do?

A GLB/USDZ export (and the saved-viewer bake) failed on any vertex-colored mesh with more than 65,536 faces: `Vertex-color atlas requires 4096px, exceeding the 2048px export limit`. The export paints each face into an 8 px tile of one atlas, capped at 2048 px.

Such a mesh now spreads its faces over as many 2048 px atlas pages as it needs, at the same tile resolution. Each page gets its own copy of the mesh's materials, and the geometry groups are cut at page boundaries. A mesh that fits in one atlas exports exactly as before.

Found when Pascal's bake worker refused a scene the Architect built from a floor-plan photo (bake job failed 4 times with the error above).

## How to test

1. `cd packages/editor && bun test src/lib/portable-export.test.ts`: the new test normalizes a 65,538-face vertex-colored mesh. On `main` it fails with the error above; here it gets two atlases, two materials and two groups, and the last faces read back blue from the second atlas.
2. `bun run ci` passes locally.

Not yet checked on the real scene: that happens once this reaches the bake worker through a private-editor bump.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A: non-visual change.

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)

>

Single-page meshes behave as before.

title: One notation: roofPitch(), and every length and angle of the shared tools through measurement() (G2, N1)
body:
## What

Catalogue slice N1 (G2): one notation. Every length, angle and roof pitch a shared tool takes goes through `measurement()` or the new `roofPitch()`. A bare number keeps the unit its field states, text in any unit is converted, and no field is renamed. The hosted PR that follows does the same for every Architect tool, which imports these two helpers from `@pascal-app/core/agent-tools`.

- **`roofPitch('deg' | 'twelfths')`** reads a pitch either way it is said: degrees (`26.6`, `"26.6°"`, `"0.46 rad"`) or rise over run (`"6:12"`, `"6/12"`, `"6 in 12"`, `"6-in-12"`, `"6 on 12"`, `"6:12 pitch"`). A bare number is in the field's unit. `create_roof`'s `pitch` takes it. On `main`, `"6/12"` was read by the unit parser as a fraction and built a 0.5° roof; `"6:12"` was refused. Minutes and seconds are refused (`'6"'`, `"4'"`, `"6 arcmin"`): their marks are a builder's inches and feet, and `'6"'` read as 6 arcseconds built a flat roof. "pitch" after a ratio needs a run of 12: a carpenter's `"1/4 pitch"` is rise over span (6:12), so it is refused, not read as 3:12.
- **`measurement()` reads inches, feet and millimetres too** (the units Architect's fields are in). It drops conversion float noise (`"6"` in an inches field is 6, not 5.999999999999999), and it shares one bounds check with `roofPitch()`.
- **A default is shown to the model.** Both take a `default` option, which applies it and states it in the description ("Default 18 in.", "Default 6:12."). The JSON Schema the AI SDK and the MCP show a model drops `default` from a field that converts, so a `.default()` after `measurement()` was invisible.
- **`create_roof`'s eaves reach as asked.** Its `overhang` is the eaves' reach past the walls in plan, as its description said and as Architect's `overhangIn` reads; the segment stores it along the slope (divided by the cosine of the pitch, the reach the viewer draws). On `main`, `"18 in"` at 6:12 stored 0.4572 m along the slope and reached 16.1 in, and the default 0.3 m reached 0.23 m at 40°.
- **One inventory** (`agent-tools/notation-inventory.ts`): `fieldSchema()`, `bareNumberPaths()` and `unshownDefaultPaths()`. Core's notation test and Architect's (the hosted PR) enforce the rule through them.
- **Core's remaining bare lengths and angles** go through `measurement()` in the unit their field already had:
  - `measure_stair.available`, and `fit_stair`'s width, landing depth, inner gap, walking-line offset and design targets;
  - the room tools: slab thickness, foundation height and floor height (`set_floor_foundation`, `set_room_floor_construction`), the reference elevation, the mezzanine's elevation and thickness, an opening's width and depth, `rotate_zone`'s grid step, and `move_zone` / `duplicate_zone` rotation (radians);
  - `set_zone_intent`'s floor thickness and elevation;
  - lengths and angles the catalogue's U1 did not list, which the inventory test below found: `place_in_room`'s yaw, offset and inset, `view_scene`'s elevation, eye height and fields of view, and `straighten_facade_photo`'s heights, distances and focal length (mm).
- **`fit_stair`'s targets change only the targets given.** The partial schema used to fill every target left out with its default, so `{ targetGoing: 0.29 }` reset a stair's own riser height and minimum going.
- **The unit note is half as long.** Every `measurement()` field carried "Accepts a number (meters) or a natural-language string; other units are converted. e.g. 0.9, "6 ft", "180cm", "2 ft 3 in"." It now says "In metres, or text with a unit ("6 ft")." The unit still comes first, so a bare number is read in it. With every N1 field converted, the shared contracts are 1.7k characters shorter than on `main` (113,940 against 115,624 on editor `main` `5fb915f0`, every contract's name, description and input schema).
- **The stale note** in `measurement.ts` that called the MCP's and the chat's copies "intentionally duplicated" is gone: both re-export this one.
- Docs: `agent-surfaces.md`'s "Adding a tool" states the rule; the MCP README's `create_roof` row says a pitch can be rise over run.

## Why

The owner, verbatim (G2): "we need to compile and harmonize tools developped by Wassim, Adam (AxiomeCG), and Steven Tibbs from the AI capabilities to avoid conflicts, explosation in complexity, and increase reliability and consistency of outputs."

The catalogue's rule 4 is one convention per quantity (`wiki/ai/tool-catalogue.md`, conflicts U1 to U3). Core took most lengths through `measurement()` but left some bare, and core said pitch in degrees while Architect said it in twelfths with no way to write either in the other's terms. A model that wrote `"18 in"` for one field and `"18 in"` for its neighbour got a number for one and a refusal for the other.

## The case table

N1 retires no tool, so its cases are the values each converted field served: the bare number calls gave it, which must keep its meaning, and text in other units, which it now reads.

- **`notation-cases.ts`**: 36 fields and 79 readings, each read through the tool's own contract, the one the MCP, the chat and Pro register (`agent-tools/notation.test.ts`).
- **The same test is an inventory.** Every other number a shared tool takes by name must be a coordinate, a fraction or a ratio listed in `NOT_LENGTHS`. A length or an angle added as a bare number fails it, and so does a stale entry. A defaulted field whose default the model is not shown fails it too.
- **Operation rows** in the tables beside it run a call written in other units on the core, MCP and chat runners: a 6:12 roof with 18-inch eaves, a roof with the default eaves, a 42 in flight, a target in inches, a target given alone, a slab in feet, a datum in inches, and a half turn in degrees.

Since the runs, both PRs have been rebased onto slices S and V, with no change to what the runs measured; the fourth review changed `create_roof`'s overhang (below). gpt-6-astra at low effort, 3 reps per lane, signed in as a feedback account (`BENCH_DEV_EMAIL`).

**The case tables without a model:**
- Core (`notation-cases.ts`): 79 readings. 38 pass on `main`, all 79 on this PR.
- Operation rows: all 8 fail on `main` and pass here.
- Architect (`notation.test.ts`): 159 readings. The 77 bare ones pass on `main` and the 82 in text are refused; all 159 pass on this PR.

**Model runs**

| arm | task | lane | runs | checks | all checks pass | complete | tool calls | tool errors | retired-name calls | create_roof calls | tokens (median) | time to complete (median) |
|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| main | cap-units | workflow | 3 | 12/18 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 34.7k | 8.4 s |
| PR | cap-units | workflow | 3 | 12/18 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 33.6k | 5.8 s |
| main | cap-units | direct | 3 | 15/18 | 0 | 3 | 9 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 26.2k | 10.0 s |
| PR | cap-units | direct | 3 | 15/18 | 0 | 3 | 9 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 25.7k | 11.1 s |
| main | cap-units | mcp | 3 | 18/18 | 3 | 3 | 9 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 110.2k | 18.0 s |
| PR | cap-units | mcp | 3 | 18/18 | 3 | 3 | 9 | 0 | 0 | 3 | 105.1k | 20.4 s |
| main | fidelity (4 tasks) | direct | 12 | 75/93 | 0 | 9 | 141 | 30 | 0 | 0 | 78.8k | 23.7 s |
| PR | fidelity (4 tasks) | direct | 12 | 75/93 | 0 | 9 | 131 | 28 | 0 | 0 | 76.9k | 28.2 s |
| main | fidelity (4 tasks) | mcp | 12 | 69/93 | 3 | 10 | 100 | 21 | 0 | 0 | 206.4k | 35.6 s |
| PR | fidelity (4 tasks) | mcp | 12 | 69/93 | 3 | 11 | 100 | 11 | 0 | 0 | 183.0k | 41.0 s |

What the numbers say:
- **No check regresses.** Every task scores the same on both arms, lane by lane and task by task:
  - fidelity on direct: stretch-room 12/13, fit-wall 4/6, mount-device 6/7 and create-design 3/5, every rep;
  - fidelity on MCP: 13/13, 4/6, 3/7 and 3/5;
  - `cap-units` on MCP: 6/6 on every rep.
- **Fewer tool errors and tokens.**
  - Fidelity on MCP drops from 21 to 11 tool errors (fewer `apply_patch` refusals), on direct from 30 to 28. The errors on both arms come from `discover_pascal_tools`, which the direct harness does not serve, from `add_object` scripts, and from the fit-wall `update_node` and `apply_patch` refusals. None is a unit refusal.
  - Median tokens are lower on every lane, since the shared contracts are shorter.
- **The model now writes the notation as said.** On MCP, `main`'s model converted the pitch itself and sent `pitch: 26.565…`. This PR's model sent `pitch: "6:12"` on every rep, and the roof came out 26.565° with 0.4572 m eaves.
- **The workflow lane stops after its first client tool on both arms.** The bench harness has no executor identity, as slice F found, so `cap-units` there ends at `list_levels`. It also ran on direct and MCP.
- **`cap-units` on direct** misses one check on both arms: "tool calls without errors", from the unserved `discover_pascal_tools`.
- **Time.** Fidelity's median time to complete rose by 4.5 s on direct and 5.4 s on MCP. That is time to the first node: 12.6 → 15.9 s and 22.5 → 32.9 s, which is the model's first call, before any contract is read. Time after the first node fell on direct (12.1 → 9.5 s) and rose on MCP (7.1 → 9.5 s).

- **A timing re-run** of fidelity on MCP, both arms on current `main`, was cut short at 22:00: the local Docker daemon stopped, and dev sign-in then answered 503 "local database unavailable". The 5 runs `main` finished show how much the time varies at the same code: stretch-room 21.7, 24.4 and 130.2 s, fit-wall 79.2 and 76.9 s. In the first run, `main` took 18.8 to 20.9 s and 21.3 to 93.2 s on those tasks, and this PR 22.9 to 41.6 s and 23.2 to 40.4 s. Their checks matched the first runs (13/13 and 4/6).
- **Retired-name calls: 0** on every run. N1 retires nothing. Pro is not benched per slice: the plan runs Pro at the milestone after F and N1.
- **Not re-run after the fourth review.** The local Docker daemon is down, and with it the local Supabase that dev sign-in needs. The `cap-units` rows above graded the overhang a segment stores, along the slope, on a `create_roof` that stored what it was given. `roof_shape` now grades the reach past the walls in plan and the roof type, and `create_roof` now reaches what it is asked, so those runs' roofs (18 in along the slope, 16.1 in in plan) would now fail it on both arms. The hosted PR's `checks.test.ts` grades `create_roof`'s own output instead: `"18 in"` at 6:12 passes, 18 in along the slope and a hip fail.

## Live check

One real Low turn on a fresh project (`feedback-g2-n1-units-3`), signed in as the feedback account, on this branch. The prompt: "Make a 5 m by 4 m studio from (0, 0) to (5, 4), then put a 6:12 gable roof on it with 18-inch eaves."

- It worked for 31 s in 2 steps: "Build a room · Studio" and "Build a roof". Each reads as a sentence in the chat, with "Saved as Version 1".
- Opened, the roof step's input is `{ "roofType": "gable", "pitch": "6:12", "overhang": "18 in" }`, as the person said it.
- Reading the scene back: the segment is pitched 26.5650511771° with a 0.4572 m overhang, on a level named Roof (role `roof`).

Screenshots (local, `/tmp/feedback-work/g2-n1/live/`):
- `units-low-dark.png`, `units-low-light.png`: the turn and the roofed studio.
- `units-low-steps-dark.png`, `units-low-steps-light.png`: the two steps.
- `units-low-roof-input-dark.png`: the roof step's input.

## Review

GPT-6 Astra reviewed both PRs adversarially in three rounds, a fourth review (Claude, with Astra's findings verified) found eight more, and Astra reviewed those fixes. Each defect in N1 is fixed, with a case:
- **Text missed the rise-over-run pattern** and the unit parser read it as degrees: `"+6/12"` and `"６／１２"` built a 0.5° roof, and `"6,0"` and `"6e0"` read wrongly in a twelfths field. A pitch's text now needs an angle unit unless it is a plain number or rise over run.
- **Unicode folding** turned `"26¼°"` into 65.25° and `"6²:12"` into 62:12. Only full-width forms are folded now. A super- or subscript digit is refused in every length and angle.
- **A rise and a run near 1e308** overflowed before the division. The ratio is divided first now.
- **On the hosted side**, the Architect panel's schema adapter dropped the string alternative (fixed in the hosted PR).
- **Round 4**, all fixed:
  - Inch and foot marks in a pitch read as arcseconds and arcminutes (`'6"'` built a 0.000349-twelfths roof). Refused now.
  - `"1/4 pitch"` read as 3:12 (a carpenter's quarter pitch is 6:12). Refused unless the run is 12.
  - A rise and run past the largest number (`"1e309:2e309"`) divided as 45°. Refused.
  - `create_roof` stored the overhang along the slope, so 18-inch eaves reached 16.1 in while Architect's reached 18 in. Converted now (above).
  - The model no longer saw the defaults of 29 Architect fields (the JSON Schema drops `default` on a converting field). The `default` option states them.
  - Architect's notation test copied core's inventory machinery. One implementation now, exported from core.
  - In the hosted PR: `cap-units` did not check the roof type, and `pdf_page_vectors.minLength` was listed as a place, not a length in PDF points.
- **Astra on round 4.** Fixed: the inventory missed a default under `.optional()` or another wrapper, took "Default 18 in." for a default of 8, and missed numbers in discriminated unions and in the objects a list holds; `fieldSchema()` took the first union option with the first step of a path; `measurement()` refused a `MeasurementOptions` variable; and Architect read a flat roof's eaves through the 40° pitch core leaves on it, so `roof_list` said 14 in for 18 and `roof_segment_update` grew it to 0.597 m (now level, as the viewer draws it). Two it found are older than N1 and left for their own change:
  - The eave edge stands about 7 cm past the reach asked: `create_roof`'s segments start at the walls' outer faces, and the deck adds half the segment's wall thickness and the covering's projection. Architect's roofs carry the same extensions; `roof_shape` and `roof_list` read the overhang's share, `overhang × cos pitch`.
  - Bones' rake framing places barge rafters at the stored overhang, along the slope, as if it were the horizontal reach, so they sit outside a steep roof's rake. It does so for any roof; `create_roof`'s now larger stored value at a given reach moves them further.

## Tests

- The core and MCP tests from the hosted root: all of core (4,768) and the MCP suite pass, the case tables over a real MCP client included.
- The hosted chat runner (`shared-tools.test.ts` in the hosted PR) runs the operation rows too.
- `check-types` 9/9; `biome check` on the editor is clean.

title: core: get_site reads the lot's frontage and depth, each edge as a front, the ground and the footprint range
body:
## What changed and why

G2, slice G of the tool catalogue (private `plans/scene-agent/ai-architect-chat-feedback.md`, H-catalogue): one site read. The hosted Architect plugin's `lot_info` (Pro only, written by Steven) read the lot, its buildable envelope and the ground in feet; the shared `get_site` read the same site in metres but lacked part of it. This PR extends `get_site` (core's site brief, `lib/site-placement.ts`) until it covers every case `lot_info` served, proved by a case table run without a model; the hosted PR then retires `lot_info`.

`get_site` now also gives:

- **The street's frontage and depth on the lot:** `street.frontage`, `street.depth`.
- **The buildable area as fronts:** `buildable.areaM2`; `buildable.edges`, every edge of the envelope as `{ edge, frontage, depth }` (the depth square to the edge, inward by the ring's winding, so an L or a U measures right); `buildable.frontEdge`, the edge the front setback is measured from: behind the street, or, while no street is recorded (`street` null), behind the lot edge facing most nearly north, which the summary calls a guess until the street is set. It is null when no edge of the buildable area faces the street (side setbacks wider than a narrow frontage leave it a point there), and the summary says so.
- **The footprint a house usually covers:** `lot.footprintRangeM2`, 30 to 45% of the lot. The summary gives it on a real lot only: the new-project placeholder is no lot, and a share of it says nothing of the house (the chat's snapshot prints the summary every step).
- **The ground:** `ground.state` `sloped` (the site has terrain; `reliefM` is its fall across the lot, exact on the field's triangles: the lot's corners, every crossing of a lot line with a grid line or a diagonal, and the samples inside), `flat` (the lot drop-in read the ground and found it flat; `reliefM` is the read's own figure over the grid it sampled) or `unread`.
- **A site by its id** (`site`, new input), read for the building viewed when it stands there, else the first on it; and **a lot with no building yet**, read in site coordinates instead of refused. An id no node has, a node that is not a site, or a building on another site, is refused (`site_not_found`, `not_a_site`, `building_not_on_site`).

One shared fix rides along: **`envelopeFrontEdge` took the longest envelope edge parallel to the lot's front either way round**, so on a lot widening away from its street (10 m on the street, 100 m at the back) it named the rear, and failing that it took the edge whose midpoint was nearest the front's, a diagonal side on a lot whose side setbacks take the whole frontage. It now takes an edge facing the way the front does, and returns null when none does (the site plan drawing's `meta.envelopeFrontEdge` is `number | null`). Instrumented, no test or case in core, the floorplan site plan, plugin-generate, plugin-procedural or plugin-architect reached the old fallback. The site plan, the generator's placement and `get_site` read it.

The summary says each in words ("· 300 m² · 15 m along the street, 20 m deep (its edge 0)", "lot edge 0, 18 m of frontage, 32 m deep", "a house usually covers 30–45%: 173–259 m²", "ground: not read, flat until it is"). The chat's scene snapshot prints the same brief each turn (563 → 728 characters on the turned parcel). `edgeFronts` is exported for the hosted generator, whose own copy of the arithmetic now delegates to it. The contract's description, the MCP README and the agent guide say what `get_site` gives.

## The case table

`agent-operations/__fixtures__/lot-info-cases.ts`, 15 cases, run on the core, MCP and chat runners with every other case (`cases.ts`). `lot_info` took no input, so each case is a lot it read, with `lot_info`'s answer in its own units (feet, square feet, its words) beside the `get_site` call that covers it. Every answer is the one the real `lot_info` gave on hosted main over the same scene (worked by hand too where the envelope is a plain inset). Each case's check finds every fact of `lot_info`'s answer in `get_site`'s, in metres (±0.05 ft, ±2 sq ft; a missing or NaN number fails), and its `result` states `get_site`'s own numbers.

| Lot `lot_info` read | `lot_info` answered | `get_site` answers |
|---|---|---|
| The new-project placeholder (its stored calls, local-08 and local-17) | 9688 sq ft, terrain not read, setbacks "defaults", "no envelope", footprint 2906–4359 sq ft | 900 m², placeholder, buildable the whole lot, `ground` unread, 270–405 m² (in the answer; the summary leaves it out) |
| 20 × 40 m, setbacks 6 / 1.5 / 7.5 m, street north, an address | 8611 sq ft, envelope 55.774 × 86.942 ft on edge 0, 4849 sq ft, four edges, 2583–3875 sq ft | street 20 × 40 m, buildable 450.5 m², 17 × 26.5 m on edge 0, four edges, 240–360 m², the address |
| The same lot turned 20°, off the origin, the building moved | 6200 sq ft, envelope 49.213 × 65.617 ft, 3229 sq ft | street 18 × 32 m, buildable 300 m², 15 × 20 m on edge 0 |
| Setbacks, no street recorded | the north-facing edge as the front: 55.774 × 86.942 ft | `street` null, `frontEdge` 0, "along its edge facing north (the setbacks take it as the front until the street is set)" |
| The same, north a quarter turn round | front edge 1, 121.391 × 21.325 ft, 2589 sq ft | `frontEdge` 1, 37 × 6.5 m, 240.5 m² |
| A corner lot, a 40 ft sight triangle | envelope front edge 4, 73.187 × 59.057 ft, six edges with a 0.436 ft sliver | `frontEdge` 4, the six edges |
| A U-shaped lot, 1 m setbacks | the first six of 18 traced edges | all 18; the arms 8 m deep |
| A round lot (64 sides), 1 m setbacks | front edge 0, an arc chord 2.903 ft long, the first six | `frontEdge` 0, all 64 edges |
| Setbacks that leave nothing | "no envelope", 1076 sq ft | buildable `none`, 0 m², no edges |
| A sloped lot (terrain wider than the lot) | "sloped: 8.202 ft of relief across the lot", the drop-in's figure over its wider grid | `ground` sloped, 2 m: the fall across the lot itself |
| Ground read flat | "read flat" | `ground` flat, the read's 0.06 m |
| No building on the lot | the lot read | the lot, in site coordinates |
| Two buildings | the lot read | the lot, for the building named (`building`) |
| Two sites, the house on the second | the first site read, whichever the house stood on | the first site read by its id (`site`) |
| No site | "no lot in the scene" | refused `no_site` |

Where they differ, `get_site` is the honest one: it lists every edge, not the first six; it says whether the street is recorded; it gives the terrain's fall across the lot rather than over the drop-in's wider grid; it reads the site the house stands on, or the one named. `get_site`'s own cases add a peak on a lot line between terrain samples (9 m, where the samples alone gave 1 m), a terrain field far off the lot with samples 10 nm apart (read at once: the crossings are clamped to the field's own lines), a field finer than the coordinates can hold (its fall is what `heightAt` shows, 0 m, not its raw 5 m sample), a lot widening away from its street (front edge 0, where `lot_info` named the 297 ft rear), a 2 m frontage the 5 m side setbacks take whole (`frontEdge` null, "no edge of it faces the street"), a named site read for the building viewed, and the three new refusals.

## Review

GPT-6 Astra reviewed the change twice, adversarially. Fixed: the terrain's fall missed a peak on a lot line between samples; a length filter on the edges emptied a round lot's list and left its `frontEdge` dangling (every edge is listed now); the front setback's edge was dropped with no street recorded (named, and called a guess); a NaN passed the numeric checks; a vacant site could not be read when another site held the house (`site`); the envelope's front could be the rear on a lot widening away from its street; a terrain one sample wide read a fall `heightAt` never shows; a ground read flat was described as the fall across the lot. Rejected, with Astra agreeing on the second pass: setbacks missing `side` or `rear` read as leaving nothing, but `SiteSetbacks` requires all three and such a site fails the schema (slice K's `verify_scene` reports it); and keeping `lot_info`'s terrain figure, which measured the drop-in's wider grid, not the lot.

Third review (findings on the PR as it stood, all fixed here, one in part): `get_site {site}` ignored the viewed building and read the first on the site; the placeholder's summary gave a footprint range of a lot that is not one; `site_not_found` was missing from the README and the cases; `PlaceBuildingInput` carried `site`; the per-site ground cache was a second cache with no measured gain (gone); `terrainFall` walked every crossing between the lot and a field far off it, so a schema-valid field (origin 1e16, or spacing 1e-8) hung the read, and with it `verify_scene` and the chat's per-turn snapshot (now clamped to the field's lines, `heightAt` holding the edge past them); and with no envelope edge facing the street, `envelopeFrontEdge` named a diagonal side and the summary called it "along the street" (now null, and said). Rejected in part: the reviewer asked the callers to orient by the street direction instead. The site plan's `meta.envelopeFrontEdge` is null there, but the hosted generator stands every house on an envelope edge, so it takes the edge whose midpoint is nearest the street's, the one this fallback took (a version that tried every edge opened refaces whose bands were never checked); standing it square to the street, set back until the envelope is wide enough, is its own change, in the hosted repo's meta-todos.

Astra then reviewed that round and found one more here: with a spacing finer than the coordinates can hold, the fall counted samples no point of the lot reaches (5 m on a field at 1e16 whose ground reads flat). The samples inside the lot are now read through `heightAt` at their place, the same plane the lot's lines are read on. Over 320 ordinary fields and 8.6 million dense samples it found no fall under the dense reading, and over 500 ordinary fields the change moved the fall by at most 1.5e-8 m. Rejected: on a field whose spacing is below the coordinates' resolution in both directions (origin 1e8, spacing 2.2e-8) the fall can still miss a peak `heightAt` reaches between rounded sample places; such a field cannot be drawn either, and the read now terminates on it.

## Tests

- `bun test packages/core` (4793 pass), `bun test packages/mcp` (1010 pass); the 32 `get_site` cases on the core and chat runners, 31 on MCP (the viewed-building case has no viewed level there); the floorplan site-plan tests (164 pass).
- `check-types` on every editor package; biome on the changed files.
- A site brief on a 257 × 257 terrain under a 64-sided lot takes about 1 ms after the first read.

The hosted PR: pascalorg/private-editor#1039.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: One scene check: verify_scene lists every schema error and the rooms the walls leave open, validate_scene retires
body:
## What does this PR do?

One scene check for every agent (G2, slice K of the hosted tool catalogue). `verify_scene` now covers every case the MCP's `validate_scene` and the hosted Architect's `check_rooms` served, so both retire: `validate_scene` here (the MCP's first retirement), `check_rooms` in the hosted PR that follows.

- **Every schema error, by node and path.** `verify_scene` listed five `schema_invalid` messages and a count of the rest. Each field a node's schema rejects is now its own `schema_invalid` issue with `nodeId`, `path` and the message, every one, as `validate_scene` listed them; `valid` is unchanged. A hidden Site, `validate_scene`'s warning, is the info issue `site_hidden`, read as stored (a malformed one still warns). The schemas are checked first, and the checks that measure read each node with the defaults its schema fills (a level stored with no `children` threw), the stored node itself when it lacks none (the editor's rendered-mesh evidence finds the store's node by identity). A malformed node of a known kind is listed and left out of them: a zone with no polygon or a wall with no start made `verify_scene` throw where `validate_scene` answered. Its level lists it as `unread` and gets no finding read around it (a room open for the wall left out, its door off its wall, the level with no door); the checks across levels (openings, furniture, wall and ceiling objects, registered checks) read the scene without that level, and its building gets no stair finding (a malformed storey or slab would change the stair count and arrival). A node of a kind no schema here knows (a plugin's, where the plugin is not loaded) is no error: one `schema_unknown_kind` issue (info) per kind gives its count and five ids, where each such node was a ~880-byte `schema_invalid` listing every core kind.
- **The host's own node schema.** `validate_scene` checked nodes by the bridge's own schema. A bridge may now lend one per kind (`nodeSchema(kind)`, read by `SceneOperations` and passed as `AgentContext.nodeSchema`), and `verify_scene` checks each node of a kind the host checks by it; any other by the registered kind's schema, else core's, else it is an unknown kind. The hosted MCP lends its schema for the kinds its write boundaries check, its plugin checks on or dark.
- **The rooms against the spaces the walls enclose** (`roomFindings`, `agent-operations/room-findings.ts`). Each level entry gives `spaces`, the count of spaces its walls and separators enclose (the editor's detected spaces). A space no zone covers by half is `space_no_room` (its walls, area in m², a point inside). A space with several zones lying in it past half and no wall between them is `space_many_rooms` (with their `zoneIds`): the reconciler's "Room N" beside a zone drawn over it, or a plan's rooms split by lines no wall draws, which `check_rooms` listed as "space … : Room 1 + Kitchen + Dining"; a mezzanine (`floor.support: 'open'`) stands over its room and does not count. A room the walls and separators cover by less than half is `room_not_enclosed`: a room is a zone with `spaceRole: 'room'`; an automatic room the reconciler marked open when its walls stopped closing it counts, a room a person declared open does not. A generic zone walls of a room's height (2 m and up) bound along most of its outline is a room too and gets the same finding as info: it may be a room drawn before its last wall (no reconcile could adopt it) or a courtyard the house wraps; one garden walls bound, or none (an analysis area), is no room and splits no space. A room named nothing, "Room" or "Zone" is `room_unnamed` (info). A terrace closes with separators, so it is enclosed; a zone no walls bound (a garden, a site or analysis area) needs neither walls nor a name. Each space and room is joined only with the shapes whose boxes meet it. A store numbers a room for every enclosed space when it loads a scene and after each edit, so `space_no_room` reads a graph as stored or a level mid-edit.
- **`validate_scene` retires.** Its registration goes. Core's `RETIRED_MCP_TOOLS` (`@pascal-app/core/agent-tools`, zod-free data) names its replacement and how to use it, and every MCP server answers a call to a retired name at `tools/call` with `{ error, code: 'tool_retired', replacement }` (`answerRetiredTools`, `tools/retired-tools.ts`, which takes a host's own map too), where the SDK would answer an unknown name. An unknown name still gets the SDK's error.
- **The MCP's `verify_scene` output schema** takes an issue's own fields (`z.looseObject`, the new fields declared): a check registered with `verify_scene` that added fields (the wall- and ceiling-object observations) failed a client that had listed the tools.
- Every mention moves to `verify_scene`: the agent guide and prompts, the `pascal-3d` and `furniture-fit` skills, the MCP README (with a note on retired tools), the examples, the smoke script, the OpenAI annotation policy and its packet, `agent-surfaces.md` (a section on `verify_scene` and one paragraph on retiring a tool) and `node-schemas.md`. `PLAN.md` and `PR_DESCRIPTION.md` stay as the history they are.

## The case table

`agent-operations/__fixtures__/scene-check-cases.ts`: each case names the retiring tool's call and what it answered, then the `verify_scene` call that covers it. The core, MCP and chat runners run it without a model (33 cases: 15 for `validate_scene`, 18 for `check_rooms`; the two on a space with no zone run on core only, see above).

| Retiring call and its answer | `verify_scene` covers it with |
|---|---|
| `validate_scene {}` on a valid scene: `{ valid: true, errors: [], warnings: [] }` | `valid: true`, no `schema_invalid`, no `site_hidden` |
| `validate_scene {}` with a hidden site: valid, a warning on the site's `visible` | `valid: true`, `site_hidden` (info) on the site, mentions "stay visible", `hasIssues: false` |
| `validate_scene {}` with a field its schema rejects: `valid: false`, `{ nodeId, path, message }` | `valid: false`, `schema_invalid` with `nodeId: 'zone_bad'`, `path: 'color'` |

| `validate_scene {}` with a node of no known kind: an error on its type | `schema_unknown_kind` (info) with its kind, count 1 and the node; `valid: true` |
| `validate_scene {}` with 300 nodes of a plugin's kind: 300 errors, each listing every kind | one `schema_unknown_kind` with `count: 300` and five ids; the whole answer under 8 KB |

| `check_rooms` on a room a new wall split, its zone over one half | one `space_no_room`, on the uncovered half |
| `check_rooms`: zone "… walls do not close around it" | `room_not_enclosed` with `levelId`, `zoneId` |

Not covered, on purpose: a terrace closed by separators and a room a person declared open, which `check_rooms` called open, and a zone no walls bound (a garden, a yard along one house wall, a site or analysis area), which it called open or unnamed. Six cases pin this: those two, a mezzanine over its room and zones no room inside a room (no `space_many_rooms`), a courtyard the house's rooms wrap on three sides (`room_not_enclosed` info, `hasIssues: false`) and a courtyard behind 0.6 m garden walls (nothing).

Run without a model on main and on this PR, in process (round 1's fixtures, each checkout's code; the cases the second review added run on the three runners in this PR):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| core: `verify_scene`'s own cases | 42/42 | 42/42 |
| core: `validate_scene`'s cases | 1/7 | 7/7 |
| core: `check_rooms`' cases | 2/12 | 12/12 |
| MCP: `verify_scene`'s own cases | 35/35 | 35/35 |
| MCP: `validate_scene`'s cases | 1/7 | 7/7 |
| MCP: `check_rooms`' cases | 2/10 | 10/10 |
| MCP: a call to `validate_scene` | answered `{ valid: true, … }` | `tool_retired`, `replacement: 'verify_scene'` |

Each case was also run against the hosted MCP of a dev server, main's and then this PR's: see the hosted PR (pascalorg/private-editor#1043).

`verify_scene` on one level of many 4 × 3 m rooms, each walled and zoned: 400 rooms 309 ms on main, 533 ms here; 1,024 rooms 1.7 s and 3.2 s (the second space detection; a house is a few dozen rooms).

## Review findings

A GPT-6 Astra pass found these here, all fixed with a test each: a malformed node made `verify_scene` throw; an automatic room the reconciler opened was exempt as if a person had declared it open; a zone three walls bound that no room adopted lost both room findings; joining every zone for every space was quadratic (3.9 s for 500 rooms in its probe); and the in-page server of the hosted Architect panel had no retired answer of its own (`answerRetiredTools` now takes a host's map).

## Review findings, round 2

A second review found these; each is fixed with a case in the table:
1. Removing the cap made a scene with many plugin nodes cost ~1 KB per node per check (448 KB for 500 `bones:*` nodes), `valid` false on a scene the Architect's method calls fine: `schema_unknown_kind`, once per kind, info. The hosted bridge lends its schema whatever the flag (hosted PR).
2. A space carrying several zones had no finding: `space_many_rooms`.
3. A malformed wall produced false `room_not_enclosed`, `opening_not_on_wall` and `walls_no_doors` around it: its level is `unread` and waits for the fix.
4. Nodes were measured raw, so a level stored with no `children` (valid) threw: each node is measured as parsed, its keys kept.
5. Courtyards walls bound on three sides (the house's U, low garden walls) got a warning that failed the bench's `verify_clean`: info on a generic zone, nothing on an open-air one.
6. A hidden site its schema rejects lost its warning: `site_hidden` reads the scene as stored.
7. The `pascal-3d` skill's "Validate and persist" steps read 1, 2, 4, 5: renumbered.

A GPT-6 Astra pass on those fixes found five more, fixed with a case each: a lent schema made a kind autosave stores while the hosted checks are dark (`environment:pond`) an error that hid its level's findings (the host now lends its schema per kind); an analysis zone inside a room read as a second room; a sofa read as mid-room around an unread wall; a malformed storey dropped out before the stair guard (`missing_stair`); a malformed destination slab gave `stair_arrival_mismatch`. It also found a node with an empty type passing as an unknown kind (now `schema_invalid`). Editor CI found that measuring copies broke the rendered-mesh evidence's identity check (`wall-object-observations.test.ts` in nodes): a node is copied only when its schema fills a default it lacks. And the MCP store writes `hasFloor: false` on the zones of a level with no slab, so "no floor or no ceiling" is no outdoor mark: the wall height is.

Left as is: a wall stored with no `children` key lists no door, which `opening_not_listed` reports as the graph stores it (main's `verify_scene` said the same); the stores relink children from `parentId` on load.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/operations.test.ts -t verify_scene`, `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/room-findings.test.ts` and `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.test.ts -t verify_scene`.
2. `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/retired-tools.test.ts packages/mcp/src/tools/verify-scene.test.ts`.
3. `bun run check-types`.

Run for this PR, rebased on main (#1080): `check-types` (9 packages), the core, MCP, nodes and geometry-script tests (10704 pass), Biome over the changed files. In the private host the chat runner (`shared-tools.test.ts -t verify_scene`) runs the same table.

title: core: a roof segment takes its own gable overhang, so the hip and gable planes can retire (G2, R)
body:
## What does this PR do?

A roof segment's gable ends can now reach their own distance past the end walls, apart from its eaves. With this, the hosted Architect plugin's `hip_roof_planes` and `gable_roof_planes` can retire into `roof_segment_add` (catalogue slice R). The hosted PR that follows, pascalorg/private-editor#1049, retires them.

- **`gableOverhang` on the roof-segment node.** It is how far a gable's or gambrel's ends (a shed's sides) reach past the end walls' outside faces, in plan metres. When it is absent, the ends reach as far as the eaves, as they always did, so saved scenes draw the same and need no migration. A hip, a flat roof and the other forms have no gable end, so the field does nothing there.
- **One rule for the deck's reach: `getRoofSegmentDeckReach`.** It gives how far a segment's deck reaches past its wall centre lines along its ridge (x) and across it (z): half the wall's thickness, then the eaves' overhang (stored along the slope), or at the rakes `gableOverhang`. `roofTypeHasRakes` names the forms that have gable ends. Before, five places each computed `wallThickness / 2 + overhang · cos(pitch)` themselves, and four more used the overhang along the slope as a plan distance. All of them now read the rule:
  - core: the visible top bounds (the roof plan, ridge vents, ridge snaps and trim handles read these) and `RoofShape.reach`, now `{ x, z }`.
  - viewer: the deck, the covering and the fascia's rake boards; the skylight surface frame; the trim cutters' margin.
  - editor: the print solids, the site plan's roof outline, and the roof selection.
  - nodes: the shared roof surface (solar panels, skylights, vents) and the segment hit test.
- **`getRoofSegmentEndReach`** gives how far a segment's ends along its width reach past the wall centre lines, for the readers that measure its eaves by the stored `overhang`: gutters (an eave gutter now runs out to the rakes), lean-to attachments and the hosted sheets. A gable's, gambrel's or shed's ends are rakes, at the deck's edge (`getRoofSegmentDeckReach`), whether or not the segment sets its own gable overhang; a hip's ends are eaves like its sides.
- **Changing `gableOverhang` regenerates the automatic ridge vents and gutters**, as changing `overhang` does, and so does changing `wallThickness` for the gutters, since the rakes reach half a wall past the centre lines.
- **A "Gable overhang" slider** for gable, gambrel and shed segments, in the panel and the parametrics, so a person can edit what an agent set. The "Eave overhang" slider above it now shows and takes the eaves' reach in plan past the walls' faces too (the node keeps it along the slope), so the two read in one convention.

Why: the owner's G2 asks for one canonical tool per capability. At Pro, a hip or gable roof over a rectangle could be made two ways, as a segment or as a set of planes, and each took different terms. The planes took the walls' outside faces, a thickness and their own gable overhang. A segment had no gable overhang of its own, so it could not build what the planes built.

editor#1028 (roof by outline) adds per-side pitch, a placed or stepped ridge and outline footprints. This slice takes none of them: every roof the plane tools made is a rectangle with one pitch and a centred ridge, which a segment already draws. What a segment lacked was a gable overhang separate from its eaves. When #1028 lands, its rakes should draw `gableOverhang` too. The fields don't clash.

## The case table

`viewer/src/systems/roof/__fixtures__/roof-plane-cases.ts` has 13 rows: every kind of roof the two plane tools built, each beside the `roof_segment_add` call that covers it and the segment that call writes. No stored thread called either tool (the local store and the archived bench runs were searched). So the rows come from the tools' own contracts and from the plugin's own call, a hip at the walls' 2.6 m tops.

`roof-plane-cases.test.ts` draws each segment through the viewer's roof geometry and compares it with the planes' own geometry, without a model:
- the covering's outline matches the planes' outline within 1.5 cm (the shingles lap about 1 cm past the deck);
- the top surface matches at 63 points over the roof, within 5 mm;
- the slab's depth square to the slope matches, over the house.

| Plane call | `roof_segment_add` call | Same roof? |
|---|---|---|
| `hip_roof_planes` defaults (0.457 m eaves, 0.29 m thick, 6:12), surface where a roof on the 2.6 m plate has it | `roofType: 'hip', rect, rectAt: 'outside', pitchTwelfths: 6, overhangIn: '0.457 m', thicknessIn: '0.29 m'` | yes |
| `hip_roof_planes` at the walls' tops, `eaveHeight: 2.6` (the plugin's own call) | the same | lifted 0.283 m onto the walls |
| hip deeper than wide, 5:12, 0.6 m eaves, 0.2 m thick | `ridgeAxis: 'z'`, `overhangIn: '0.6 m'`, `thicknessIn: '0.2 m'` | yes |
| hip over a square (a pyramid), 8:12, 0.3 m eaves | `overhangIn: '0.3 m'` | yes |
| hip flush with the walls, 4:12 | `overhangIn: '0 m'` | yes |
| hip on a plate 0.3 m over the walls | `eaveHeight: 2.9` | yes |
| `gable_roof_planes` defaults, ridge east-west (0.457 m eaves, 0.305 m at the gable ends) | `roofType: 'gable', ridgeAxis: 'x', gableOverhangIn: '0.305 m'` | yes |
| gable at the walls' tops | the same | lifted 0.283 m onto the walls |
| gable, ridge north-south over a deep house, 8:12 | `ridgeAxis: 'z'` | yes |
| gable, ridge north-south across a wide house, 4:12 | `ridgeAxis: 'z'` | yes |
| gable ends past the eaves: 0.9 m rakes, 0.3 m eaves, 3:12, 0.25 m thick | `gableOverhangIn: '0.9 m'`, `overhangIn: '0.3 m'` | yes |
| gable with flush ends | `gableOverhangIn: '0 m'` | yes |
| gable over a porch on posts, eave on the beam | `eaveHeight: 2.4` | yes |

On `main`, the 6 hip rows pass and all 7 gable rows fail: without `gableOverhang`, a gable's ends cannot reach their own distance. On this PR, all 13 pass.

Two calls are not reproduced, on purpose. No stored call made either.
- **A plane call at the walls' tops sank its roof into them.** A plane call's `eaveHeight` was the roof's surface at the outside wall face; a segment's is the plate it bears on, by default its walls' tops. Called with the walls' tops (the plugin's own call, and the likeliest one), the planes' slab stood `thickness / cos(pitch)` under the plate at the wall face. A segment is never sunk under the walls it sits on (`eave_under_walls`). So the replacement leaves the eave out, and the roof sits on the walls with the same outline, pitch and thickness, its surface 0.283 m higher at 6:12. The two rows above say so.
- **Planes over a storey with another storey over it stood inside that storey.** A segment refuses that (`into_storey_above`). The hosted table checks the refusal.
- **One slope edited on its own.** The plane tools answered each plane's id, so one slope could be edited or painted alone (`update_roof_plane`). A segment's slopes change together; one slope on its own stays `create_roof_plane`'s, and the retired tools' answer says so.

Under the eaves, a segment draws its deck boxed level, 5 cm under its edge, with the fascia covering that edge. A plane's slab kept its slope all the way to the edge. So the depth check runs over the house, 1 m in from the walls.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/viewer/src/systems/roof/roof-plane-cases.test.ts`: 14 tests (13 rows and the coverage check).
2. The new unit tests:
   - `bun test packages/core/src/schema/nodes/roof-segment-deck-reach.test.ts`: the reach rule;
   - `packages/viewer/src/systems/roof/roof-fascia.test.ts`: the rake boards at the gable overhang;
   - `packages/editor/src/lib/print-roof-solids.test.ts`: the print shell;
   - `packages/core/src/schema/nodes/gutter-defaults.test.ts`: the eave gutters out to the rakes;
   - `packages/core/src/store/actions/ridge-vent-update.test.ts`: the vents regenerate.
3. `bun run check-types`.

Run for this PR, from the private host's worktree, on editor main (#1083):
- `check-types`: every editor package.
- Tests: core, viewer, nodes, mcp and editor, 9640 passing; after the fourth round, core's schema, store and agent-tools, the viewer's roof systems and the lean-to, 2214 passing.
- Biome over the changed files.
- In `editor`, 19 tests in `lib/history.test.ts` fail in that worktree because a spawned child prints three's CJS deprecation warning on stderr. They fail the same way without this change.

## Review

GPT-6 Astra reviewed the slice adversarially three times, across both PRs.

Fixed here:
- Gutters and lean-to attachments sized a roof's ends by the eave overhang.
- Changing `gableOverhang` did not regenerate the automatic ridge vents and gutters.
- The trim cutters' margin had changed for segments without the field: it is the old formula again, plus the gable overhang when one is set.

The third pass found no material issue. It checked that, against `main`, segments without `gableOverhang` give byte-identical outputs:

| Output | Identical |
|---|--:|
| Viewer, untrimmed | 32/32 |
| Viewer, trimmed | 64/64 |
| Gutters | 96/96 (before the fourth round, below) |

The fourth round (a review and Astra) found, and this PR fixes:
- `getRoofSegmentRakeReach` measured in two frames: the deck's reach with `gableOverhang`, the slope `overhang` without one, so setting the field to the eaves' own reach moved the gutter ends by 4.7 cm. It is now `getRoofSegmentEndReach`, one rule: a gable's ends are at the deck's edge either way. So, on purpose, the eave gutters and lean-to ends of an existing gable move to the deck's edge they belong at, by `wallThickness / 2 − overhang · (1 − cos pitch)`: 2 cm in on the default segment (0.1 m walls, 0.3 m at 40°), 3 cm out on an Architect one (6.5 in walls, 18 in at 6:12). The gutter tests say so.
- A wall-thickness change left the default eave gutters at their old length.
- The panel's "Overhang" (along the slope) and "Gable overhang" (in plan) sat side by side in two conventions.

Left as they are:
- The print shell of a plate-seated segment (`wallHeight` 0), which is older than this slice.
- The eave boxing described above.
