title: An MCP host lends the floor its person views, and the shared tools default to it (G2, N2)
body:
## Description

**An MCP host lends the floor its person views, and the shared tools default to it.** `createSceneOperations` takes the host's `activeLevelId`, a function. The shared operation tools, `add_object`, `add_column` and the rescripted openings read it as their `AgentContext.activeLevelId`. Before, the MCP always passed `null`. A host with no view, the remote MCP, lends none and still reads the lowest storey.

**Why.** The hosted Architect runs an MCP server in the page, with core's shared tools beside its own. For a call that names no level, its own reads took the floor the person views, and core's took the lowest storey. So in one turn, `get_walls {}` and Architect's `design_check {}` could read two different floors, and a model checking one floor got another floor's wall ids. This came up in the review of the hosted PR for G2's slices N2 and N3 (pascalorg/private-editor#1047, the catalogue's L1). The owner, G2: "we need to compile and harmonize tools developped by Wassim, Adam (AxiomeCG), and Steven Tibbs from the AI capabilities to avoid conflicts, explosation in complexity, and increase reliability and consistency of outputs."

- `packages/mcp/src/operations/scene-operations.ts`: the `activeLevelId` option and field.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.ts`, `add-object.ts`, `add-column.ts`, `room-tools.ts`: each reads `bridge.activeLevelId?.() ?? null` where it passed `null`.
- `wiki/architecture/agent-surfaces.md`: the executor's surface context names it.

## The case tables

The MCP runners of the shared tools and of `add_object` now run each case with its own viewed floor (`context.activeLevelId`), passed through `createSceneOperations`. Twelve cases were limited to core and the chat only because the MCP had no viewed floor. They now run on the MCP as well:
- `list_levels`, `get_walls`, `duplicate_level`, `verify_scene`;
- `create_room`, `add_wall`, `create_roof`, `add_level`, `create_stair`;
- `place_items`, `get_site`, `add_corner_window`;
- `add_object`'s roof-level case.

The cases with no viewed floor still check the lowest storey on every surface.

## PR Review Checklist

- [x] `bunx turbo run check-types --filter='./editor/packages/*'` (9/9), from the hosted root
- [x] Biome on the changed files (the editor's config)
- [x] `bun test editor/packages/mcp/src`: 1,055 pass. `bun test editor/packages/core/src/agent-operations`: 801 pass.
- [x] The hosted PR pins this change and passes its own case tables. They include `get_walls {}` and Architect's reads defaulting to one floor, with a level picked and after the Architect shows the building.

title: One finder and one node read: find_by_type takes find_nodes' filters, get_node what describe_node added
body:
## What does this PR do?

One finder and one node read for every agent (G2, slice Q of the hosted tool catalogue). `find_by_type` now covers every case the MCP's `find_nodes` served, and `get_node` every case `describe_node` served, so both MCP tools retire.

- **`find_by_type` takes `find_nodes`' filters.** Beside a type it filters by `levelId`, `parentId`, `zoneId` (on the zone's level, a node's plan point inside the polygon by the spatial grid's ray cast, as `find_nodes` placed it: a wall's midpoint, a polygon's centroid, a window where its wall puts it, a block or mesh by the middle of its geometry, turned in 3D first), `sourceId` and `sourceIdPrefix` (an importer's ids, typed `provenance.refs[].id` or legacy `metadata.sourceIds`, raw or percent-encoded). Without a type it finds every node the filters match. It still finds item categories, lights and typed parts. A kind is matched as asked, any case; a word without a namespace also in the singular ("walls"), a plugin's kind (`bones:studs`) never. Each result gives the node's id, name, kind, level and now its `parentId`, `metadata` and `provenance` (Architect's method reads `metadata.flatwork` off each slab), a record over 1 KB named in `omitted` instead, so an IFC property set does not flood a search. A level, parent or zone that is not there is refused (`level_not_found`, `node_not_found`, `zone_not_found`, `not_a_zone`), where `find_nodes` answered nothing found; a type that names nothing (no core or registered plugin kind, and no kind, item category or part type in the scene) is refused `unknown_type` with the scene's kinds, as `find_nodes` refused it, while a real kind that is absent still answers `count: 0`. The zone is read only for what matched, so an unrelated malformed node no longer breaks a search; a part with bounds stands in a zone by their middle, and a zone's holes are out of it. It lists 200 results unless `limit` asks for more: `count` stays the number that match, and `truncated` with a hint says some are left out, so a typeless call on a converted house no longer hands a chat model the whole scene.
- **`get_node` takes what `describe_node` added.** Beside the node as stored: a wall's or a ceiling's `resolvedHeight` and `heightIsExplicit`, a wall's `resolvedThickness`, a door's or window's `resolvedOpening` (as before), a level's or floor plate's `displayName` (the name the editor shows), and `ancestorIds`, parent first (`describe_node`'s `ancestryIds`); a container's node lists its `children` as stored (`childrenIds`), and `missingChildIds` the ones that name no node, which `childrenIds` left out. The resolved fields are read from the node as its schema parses it, so a stored node that omits a default reads; a node its schema rejects, or one whose neighbours do not read, comes back as stored with `unresolved` saying why, where `get_node` threw. `describe_node`'s sentence ("Wall from (0,0) to (5,0), thickness 0.10m, height 2.75m") is the node's own fields.
- **`find_nodes` and `describe_node` retire.** Their registrations and files go. Core's `RETIRED_MCP_TOOLS` names each replacement and how to use it, and every MCP server answers a call to them `tool_retired`.
- **One link repair for every loader.** `healSceneNodes`' reverse link repair is its own function, `repairHostChildLinks`, which also rebuilds a level stored without `children` in scene order (the editor's order), so the hosted MCP's load, which runs only the parent repair today, can run the same one (hosted PR). Both stores link parents and children on load, so `get_node` follows `parentId`.
- Every mention moves: the `pascal-3d` skill and its tool workflows, the MCP README (the two rows replaced, the retired-tools note), the changelog, the examples (`embed-in-agent.ts` reads `find_by_type`'s `results`), the OpenAI annotation policy and its packet, the reference inventory's note. `PLAN.md`, `PR_DESCRIPTION.md` and `CROSS_CUTTING.md` stay as the history they are. The furniture-fit journey (`packages/mcp/scripts/furniture-fit-journey.ts`) hashed the deleted `find-nodes` and `validate-scene` sources and four compiled tools that moved into core, so it threw before its first case; its lists now name files that exist.

|---|---|---|

Each case was also run against the hosted MCP of a dev server, main's and then this PR's: see the hosted PR.

## Review findings

GPT-6 Astra reviewed this three times, and a fourth pass confirmed the last fixes (the healer before and after the move matched on 20,000 generated graphs); every finding is fixed with a case:
1. A zone drawn closed (its first corner repeated) held every node: the boundary-inclusive test counted a zero-length edge. The zone test is the spatial grid's ray cast `find_nodes` used.
2. A plural plugin kind matched its singular too, and a kind written with a capital matched nothing: a kind is matched as asked, any case; only a word without a namespace is also read in the singular.
3. Geometry was read before the kind, so a block stored without its topology broke a wall search; an authored item whose manifest lists no parts broke every typed search; a lights search read `effects` a stored interactive part may omit (from before the slice).
4. Every result carried its metadata whole (10 MB for 1,000 walls with 10 KB each): a record over 1 KB is named in `omitted`.
5. `get_node` threw on a wall stored without its start, a door stored without its position (its schema's default) and a wall beside a slab with no polygon: the resolved fields come from the parsed node, and `unresolved` says why when they cannot be read.
6. `describe_node` found ancestors and children through either link; the stores link both on load (the hosted MCP's load now too, hosted PR), and the cases run on the MCP and chat runners. The two loaders also rebuilt a level stored without children in different orders: one repair now does it, in scene order.
7. `get_node` scanned the whole scene at the root for a parent: it follows `parentId`.

A fourth review (two adversarial passes) found:
1. A typeless call, or one by level, had no bound: on the converted /next house (1,544 nodes) `find_by_type {}` answered 589 KB. Fixed: 200 results unless `limit` asks for more, `count` of all, `truncated` and a hint (cases: 254 nodes, `limit: 1000`, `limit: 3`).
2. A type that names nothing answered `count: 0` where `find_nodes` refused it. Fixed: `unknown_type` with the scene's kinds (cases: `not-a-type`, `windw`, `bones:studs` beside only a `bones:stud`; a real absent kind and a part type held elsewhere still answer `count: 0`).
3. The furniture-fit journey hashed deleted files and threw before its first case. Fixed: its lists name files that exist. It now runs to its first save, which `save_scene` refuses because `create_project` already made that id; that is older than this PR and logged in the hosted repo's `plans/meta-todos.md`.
4. With `zoneId`, a typed part was placed at its object's plan point, so a porch column 20 m outside the zone was found. Fixed: a part with bounds stands at their middle (case: the porch).
5. `get_node` listed a stored child that names no node with nothing to say so, where `describe_node`'s `childrenIds` left it out. Fixed: `missingChildIds` (case: a wall listing `door_gone`).
6. The retired `find_nodes` text did not say an unknown type now answers `count: 0`. Superseded by 2: it is refused again, and the text says so.
7. The zone test ignored a zone's `holes` (from `find_nodes`). Fixed: a point in a hole is out (case: a wall in a courtyard).
8. Schema-refused arguments answer `invalid_input` in the chat but the SDK's uncoded `-32602` text on the MCP. Not changed here: it holds for every MCP tool, so it is its own change, logged in the hosted repo's `plans/meta-todos.md`.

GPT-6 Astra then reviewed these fixes (158 probes) and found:
1. On the hosted MCP a plugin kind the host checks but core's registry does not hold (`spielberg:camera` on a scene with none) was refused `unknown_type`. Fixed: the type check also asks the host's `nodeSchema` (a hosted test in the private PR).
2. A part's zone test used the yaw-only level bounds, so a part of an object tipped about X was misplaced. Fixed: a part stands at the middle of its bounds taken through its node's whole frame and hosts (case: a tipped porch).
3. Coverage: a limit across a node and parts, a limit equal to the count (no `truncated`), and a whole wall with no `missingChildIds`. Added.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/operations.test.ts -t "find_by_type|get_node"` and `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.test.ts -t "find_by_type|get_node"`.
2. `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/retired-tools.test.ts packages/core/src/utils/heal-scene-graph.test.ts`.
3. `bun run check-types`.

Run for this PR, merged with main (#1082): `check-types` (9 packages), the core and MCP tests (6,022 pass) and the nodes tests, Biome over the changed files. In the private host the chat runner (`shared-tools.test.ts -t "find_by_type|get_node"`) runs the same table.

title: Add kitchen catalog, magnetic placement, and refined cabinet models
body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes kitchen items discoverable through a searchable catalog with Add and Find-in-project actions, three-column cards, and isometric WebP thumbnails that show color on hover. Cabinet controls expose common settings first, with advanced construction options collapsed.

- Adds magnetic ghost placement, adjacent-run joining, and add-beside/replace workflows with fit feedback.
- Refines cabinet and appliance models while reducing geometry; fixes padding and wrapping in shared panel controls.
- Adds run alignment, wall fillers, continuous toe-kicks, and advisory opening-clearance warnings during placement, movement, and inspection. Clearance checks account for host transforms and elevation; curved walls and wall openings remain outside the advisory calculation.
- Shares finishing operations between inspectors and exported agent tools, with opt-in MCP registration and behavioral coverage. Existing scenes retain their default cabinet behavior.

## How to test

1. Start the editor with `bun dev`, open a project, and choose Build → Kitchen. Verify three-column cards, readable labels, gray thumbnails with color on hover, search, and Find-in-project selection.
2. Place cabinets and appliances near a wall and an existing run. Verify the ghost snaps magnetically, add-beside and replace actions preview the result, and undo restores the previous run.
3. Select a run and exercise alignment and wall fillers. Check toe-kicks and end finishes, then move a cabinet near an obstruction and verify the same clearance warning during placement, movement, and inspection. Inspect cabinet and appliance geometry in 3D.
4. For agent integration, follow the nodes README to register the exported operation tools. Verify `kitchen_finish_run` applies the same run changes and `kitchen_check_clearance` returns the shared advisory notice.
5. Automated validation completed: `bun run check-types`; `bun run check` (existing warnings remain); `bun run skills:validate`; and `bunx turbo run test --filter=@pascal-app/nodes --filter=@pascal-app/editor --filter=@pascal-app/mcp --concurrency=1` (8,385 passed, one skipped). Public agent entry points were also smoke-tested in plain Node, and the tool contracts were bundled for a browser target.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> Changes cabinet scene graph (fillers, alignment, hosted-item guards) and adds agent/MCP operations; heavily tested but touches core placement and kitchen run logic.

> Replaces the standalone editor’s single **Modular Cabinet** tile with a full **Kitchen** flow: searchable build tools, a dedicated `KitchenBrowser` catalog (`KitchenCollection`, preset placement via `beginKitchenPlacement`), and **Find in this project** when searching. Command-palette commands register add/find kitchen actions via `KitchenCommands` in `scene-loader`.
> 
> Adds **run finishing** and **advisory clearance**: new `wall-filler` `moduleKind`, align/fill planners (`finishKitchenRun`, `fitCabinetWallFillers`, `alignCabinetRun`), shared `cabinetPlacementNotice`, and headless **`kitchen_finish_run`** / **`kitchen_check_clearance`** agent contracts plus MCP registration docs and integration tests.

> **Editor UX/engine:** `usePlacementNotice` can read ephemeral placement previews without inserting a draft; `BuildToolTile` gains a neutral active tone; action/segmented controls wrap long labels. **Cabinet geometry** is refined (panels, appliances, hoods, sinks, drawers, lower tessellation) with continuous toe-kicks, wall-filler solids, and neighbor placement/finishing covered by new tests.

title: core: furnish_room keeps a sofa, a bed and a TV against their wall, inside the room
body:
## What does this PR do?

`furnish_room` and `verify_scene` disagreed. In the G2 milestone's live Pro turn (a two-bedroom cottage), core's `furnish_room` placed the sofa 0.6 m and the TV stand 0.8 m off their walls, and core's own `verify_scene` then reported both as `item_mid_room`. The placement stepped a piece up to 0.75 m into the room before trying the next spot along its wall, while `verify_scene` reads a wall-bound piece (`furnitureKind` `wall`) more than 0.4 m off every wall face as standing mid-room. A bathroom under 6.5 m² also got its shower at the room's centre, which `verify_scene` reads the same way.

- **A wall-bound piece stays against a wall that stands.** It slides along its wall, between the wall's ends (a short stretch of wall still tries the spot nearest the piece's own), and steps off it only as far as `verify_scene` still reads it against the wall. A spot with no wall within that distance (a polygon edge with no wall on it) is not taken; the piece is skipped with "no wall to stand against there". A level with no walls yet is furnished by its outline, as before; `verify_scene` judges no piece there.
- **A group moves together.** The coffee table and the TV move along their walls as far as the sofa did, and the bedside tables with the bed, so a sofa that slides off a door keeps its table and TV across from it.
- **A small bathroom's shower stands against the side wall**, as the tub does in a larger one.
- **Nothing lands outside the room.** Every spot must lie inside the room's outline: the piece's middle inside, and no outline edge through its turned footprint (a millimetre of overlap allowed, never a piece's whole thickness). Main tested only the outline's bounding box, so it placed a bed in the corner an L-shaped room leaves out, and a long table across a U's notch. This PR skips those pieces as "outside the room".
- **A skip names what is in the way of the spot it is about**: the first spot with a wall, not a spot that had none.
- **`pointOnSegment` on a segment of no length.** It read every point as lying on it, so an outline drawn closed (its first corner repeated) held every point on its boundary, and `pointInPolygon` answered `includeBoundary` for every point. It is now that one point.

Left as on main, logged as its own follow-up: `edgeFrame` (used by `furnish_room` and `place_in_room`) reads an edge's inside from the bounding box's centre, so a non-convex room's inner edges face out. `furnish_room` now skips a piece there instead of placing it outside.

## The case table

`agent-operations/__fixtures__/build-room-cases.ts` runs on the core, MCP and chat runners without a model. Its `furnished` check now also fails on a piece `verify_scene` reads as mid-room and on a piece whose turned footprint leaves the room. The footprint test clips the piece against the outline, independent of the operation's own test.

| Case | main | PR |
|---|---|---|
| A door in the sofa wall and in the TV wall (7 × 4.5 m): the sofa slides along its wall, the table and the TV with it, nothing into the room | fail (sofa mid-room) | pass |
| A wall-bound piece where no wall stands is skipped, and says so: the TV of a living room open to the south | fail | pass |
| An L-shaped bedroom: nothing lands in the corner the L leaves out | fail (bed and tables outside) | pass |
| An outline drawn closed (its first corner repeated): the closet stands against its far wall | pass | pass |
| A U-shaped room: nothing stands in the notch between its arms, though its corners touch the outline | fail (table across the notch) | pass |
| A room turned 45°: the closet stands inside it, against a wall | pass | pass |
| A bathroom under 6.5 m², which takes a shower and no tub: the shower stands against a wall, not in the middle | fail (shower skipped) | pass |
| The 12 cases already there | pass | pass |

Live, on the hosted dev server with this build: the milestone's cottage with its living room emptied, a Medium turn "Furnish the living room (furnish_room), then check the scene with verify_scene". The sofa, table and chair were placed, the TV stand skipped for a door, and `verify_scene` came back valid with no issues. On main, the same room gave two `item_mid_room`.

## Review

GPT-6 Astra reviewed five rounds:

- Round 1: slides past the wall's ends, and edges with no wall.
- Round 2: a U's notch, the bounding box of a turned piece, opposite-winding lobes, and the reason ordering.
- Round 3: the edge probe, the area slack, the clip's rounding, the door named in a skip, and `lateralSteps`' bounds.
- Round 4: a slide range between two steps, a piece under 2 mm thick, and the fixture's corner order.

Each finding is either fixed, with a case or a scratch reproduction, or out of scope: `edgeFrame` is main's again. Round 4 also traced every core caller of `pointInPolygon` through the `pointOnSegment` change, with an outline drawn closed. Each caller now answers as it does for the same outline drawn open: `place_items`, `place_in_room`, `findItemsMidRoom`, `floorItemFit`, the roof's `wallsUnder`, `verify_scene`'s stair checks and `place_building`.

Round 5 confirmed the round 4 fixes and found no P1 or P2 in the whole diff.

## How to test

```sh
bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/operations.test.ts -t furnish
bun test packages/core/src packages/mcp/src
```

title: deps: upgrade ultracite to 8 (major, needs review)
body:
## What does this PR do? Upgrades `ultracite` from ^7.8.2 to ^8.0.1 in the root `package.json`, with `bun.lock` regenerated. It also raises the root `engines.node` from `>=22` to `>=22.18` to match Ultracite 8's own requirement, and updates the Node prerequisite in `SETUP.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` to 22.18+. The CLI package's `>=22.13.0` engines field and the "CLI-managed editor" note in `SETUP.md` are unchanged, because they describe end users of the published `@pascal-app/cli`, not contributors. Ultracite 8 peer-requires `@biomejs/biome ^2.5.0`, which #1087 (now merged) provided. `main` has been merged into this branch, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes on the merged lockfile. **How it was done:** I ran `ultracite upgrade --pm bun`. It reported "Configuration files are already in this release's format", and the only extra change it made was pinning `@biomejs/biome` to an exact `2.5.15`. I reverted that pin to keep the repo's `^` ranges; otherwise the result is identical to a manual bump. I did not run `ultracite init`, because it would rewrite `biome.jsonc` and `AGENTS.md`. **Important context:** Ultracite is effectively unused in this repo. `biome.jsonc` doesn't extend `ultracite/biome/core` (`ultracite doctor` warns about exactly that), no script or hook calls `ultracite`, and `AGENTS.md` has no Ultracite rules block. No Oxlint, ESLint, Stylelint or Prettier configs exist, so there's no whitespace-only diff from the Oxlint preset. Reviewers may prefer to **drop `ultracite` entirely** rather than carry a major-version upgrade of an unused dependency. ### Ultracite 8.0.0 / 8.0.1 breaking changes, checked against this repo | Breaking change | Effect here | |---|---| | Every agent reads Ultracite rules from `AGENTS.md`; `init` migrates old `CLAUDE.md`/`GEMINI.md`/`.firebender` blocks | None. `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` are symlinks to `AGENTS.md`, there is no Ultracite block anywhere, and `init` was not run. | | Biome core preset sets `noSuspiciousSemicolonInJsx`, `noDuplicateJsxProps`, `noVoidElementsWithChildren` to `error` | None. `biome.jsonc` doesn't extend the preset. Adopting it later would turn these on. | | ESLint core preset makes `compat/compat` an error (needs browserslist targets) | None. ESLint presets aren't used (`packages/eslint-config` doesn't reference ultracite). | | Cypress and Storybook rules moved to opt-in presets | None. They aren't used. | | ESLint/Stylelint no longer run Prettier as a rule | None. They aren't used through Ultracite. | | Type-aware ESLint rules are now opt-in | None. | | `ultracite fix --hook` exits 2 when problems remain | None. `.githooks/pre-commit` calls `bun run check` (Biome directly), not `ultracite fix --hook`. | | Pre-commit hooks fix only staged files | None. The repo's own hook is check-only. | | `init`/`upgrade` install `oxlint`/`oxfmt`/`oxlint-tsgolint` within caret ranges | `upgrade` installed none of them, since Biome is the detected linter. They show up only as optional peers in `bun.lock`. | | Requires Node 22.18+ | Root `engines.node` is now `>=22.18`, and the contributor docs say Node.js 22.18+. CI's `node-version: 22` already resolves to a newer 22.x. | ## How to test 1. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` 2. `bunx ultracite doctor` should show "4 passed, 1 warnings" (the warning is the non-extended `biome.jsonc`). 3. `bun run ci` should pass. CI is green. Locally (Node 22.21.1, Bun 1.4.2), `bun run ci` passes except for `packages/viewer/src/components/viewer/perf-monitor.test.tsx`. That test passes in isolation and in CI. It fails locally only when `render-error.test.tsx` runs first: that test's `finally` restores `window`, `requestAnimationFrame` and `cancelAnimationFrame` with `Object.assign`, which leaves them as own keys set to `undefined` instead of deleting them. This predates this PR and is left for a separate fix. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: Open project file tabs and retain exported deliverables
body:
## What does this PR do?

Let hosts open project files in closable tabs alongside 2D and 3D, rename those tabs, and remove their layout state when closed. Document panes keep copy, delete, and editing shortcuts away from the scene until a scene pane is focused.

Retain requested PDF, JSON, model, and imported-file deliverables through a host-provided project file sink before reporting a successful download. Capture that sink at export start so switching projects cannot send the output to another project. A hosted build import also stops with a visible error if its source cannot be retained; this enforces the requirement that every imported source reaches project files before it changes the scene. Hosts without a sink retain their existing import behavior. Add shared project-file contracts and operations, with authenticated host execution over MCP; Community registers the same contracts for chat and supplies the catalog and file viewers. The by-hand alternative is the Files panel and existing export controls.

This branch starts at Community's current editor pin. After merging with a merge commit, Community will pin this branch head, which is reachable on upstream main, to keep unrelated later editor changes out of this release.

## How to test

1. `PATH=/Users/aymeric/.bun/bin:$PATH bun run ci` passed locally using the pinned Bun 1.4.2: lint, skill validation, typechecks, unit tests, and production builds.
2. In a host with document views, open a file beside the scene, rename it, close it, and switch workspaces. Its tab should update and closing should remove its slots from both layouts.
3. Focus a document pane and copy text or press Delete; the scene must remain unchanged. Focus the scene to resume scene shortcuts.
4. Supply a file sink and export a drawing or model. The sink receives the completed bytes before the download; a rejected sink surfaces an export failure.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet. Community owns the file browser and viewers; its integration is verified separately.

title: [Bugs] viewer: room-wide paint preview no longer leaves walls unraycastable
body:
## What does this PR do? Fixes Sentry MONOREPO-EDITOR-ZT / ZV / ZW: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'side')` on `/editor/:projectId`. That is about 4.5k events from more than 100 users since Sep 30, the day after #976 shipped wall finish palettes, paint previews that regroup wall faces, and `wallHitInOpening`. ### Root cause I matched the minified production chunks to source (the same column offsets appear across releases): - **ZT (pointer move) and ZV (pointer leave):** the selection manager's paint hover runs `resolvePaintInteraction`, which calls `wallHitInOpening` (`packages/editor/src/lib/paint-pass-through.ts`). That function calls `THREE.Mesh.prototype.raycast.call(drawnWallMesh, …)` directly, which bypasses the `hasMaterialsForGroups` guard that only the R3F collector in `pointer-events.ts` applies. - **ZW (pointer down):** `ElevatorInteractionSystem`'s capture-phase canvas listener runs `intersectObjects(scene.children, true)` on every click. Any mesh in the scene with a group that has no material throws. Each of these is just a raycaster that reaches the broken mesh. The broken state comes from the paint preview: - With the **room** or **all matching** scope, the paint preview calls `applyWallPreview` on every wall in the spread. - On each of those walls, `applyWallPreview` regroups the faces onto indices into its own longer, copied material array. - `WallCutoutCache` only treats the **hovered** wall as a preview's owner. When the cache re-applies another wall in the spread, it puts that wall's shorter palette back over the preview's groups. - That wall now has groups pointing past the end of its material array. Its faces vanish, and every raycast over it throws until the hovered wall's preview restores the groups. - The common sequence: the hover moves from wall B to wall A of the same room. B is released and re-applied while it wears A's spread preview. The paint hover path makes this loop. It never stops propagation, so the nearer broken wall resolves first, throws before it can restore anything, and throws again on every move. That fits the roughly 27 events per user. The hypothesis that geometry is rebuilt before materials are swapped describes a related case that was already handled: `handleRebuilt` swaps the palette in the same synchronous call as the geometry swap. The actual tear is the opposite one: the material is swapped while a preview owns the groups. ### Fix 1. **`WallCutoutCache.apply` (root cause):** the cache no longer assigns a palette that can't draw the mesh's current groups when the material the mesh already wears can draw them. Those groups belong to a live preview. The assignment is deferred and retried every frame, and it goes on once the preview's restore gives the groups back. When neither array covers the groups, the cache assigns as before, so a rebuild's new palette still wins. `hasMaterialsForGroups` gains an optional `material` argument so the cache can ask that question about a candidate array. 2. **Paint hover, defense in depth:** `wallHitInOpening` and the curtain-wall branch of `resolveWallRole` skip a mesh they can't raycast. The wall hit stands for that move, matching how the R3F collector already skips that mesh. 3. **Elevator clicks:** only elevator-button subtrees are raycast. The handler already picks any button hit along the ray, regardless of occlusion, so the result is the same. It also stops raycasting the whole scene on every click. ### Regression risk - **Hover and selection highlighting:** palettes and highlight variants always have the same length for a given geometry, so the new check only ever defers when a foreign array owns regrouped faces, which is a live paint preview. Existing cutout-cache tests pass unchanged, including the preview-preservation, preview-gives-way-on-rebuild and same-facing repair tests. - **A wall in a spread whose variant changes while it is deferred** (for example, selected during the hover) shows that variant one frame after the preview restores, instead of immediately. - **Paint pass-through:** while a mesh is torn, a paint hover over a wall opening resolves to the wall for that move instead of passing through. Before this PR, that move threw. - **Door and window placement:** no code on that path changed. The R3F collector and the wall handlers are untouched. - **Elevator buttons:** the result is the same set of hits, filtered as before. Button objects are found by `userData.elevatorButton`, the same key the existing lookup walks up to. ## How to test 1. Open a project with a closed room. Arm a paint material and set the paint scope to **Room**. 2. Hover one wall of the room, then move to another wall of the same room. Use an elevated orbit view where the far wall shows over the near wall's top, and move from the far wall down onto the near one. 3. Expected: before this PR, the first wall's faces can disappear and the console throws `reading 'side'` on every move. After it, the preview spreads across the room and there's no error. 4. Click to paint, then click an elevator button if the scene has one. No errors, and the elevator responds. Automated tests I ran: - `bun test` in `packages/viewer`, `packages/editor` and `packages/nodes/src/wall`. One failure in viewer (the `?perf` probe test) and one in editor (`Upper-floor height drag release`) fail identically on `main` without this branch. - `turbo run check-types` for viewer, editor and nodes. - `biome check` on the changed files. - New tests: - `wall-cutout-cache.test.ts`: a room-wide preview keeps its groups on a wall that isn't hovered. This test fails on `main`. - `paint-pass-through.test.ts`: a torn mesh doesn't throw. Without the guard it fails with the production message `material.side`. - `elevator-interaction-system.test.ts`: a button behind a torn mesh is still found, and the old whole-scene raycast throws. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A. This is a crash fix and I didn't run the app locally. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches wall material assignment timing and multiple raycast paths (paint hover, curtain walls, elevators); deferral can delay palette updates by one frame after preview ends. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 191bbc3615ebabe559d3ce3fbb6fc7f202a2bcd7. title: feat: Let users dock the action menu to any edge
body:
#995 let the host pick where the action menu docks, but thats a default for everyone and users cant change it themselves. Not everyone wants the same, for example on an ultrawide monitor you probably dont want to waste viewport height and would rather have it on the sides, and others (like me) prefer everything in the top so we regain precious viewport space in the lower part.

This adds a dock picker at the end of the action menu itself with Bottom, Top, Left and Right, so the very user chooses where the menu goes. The pick is saved per browser and wins over the host's `actionMenuPlacement`, which stays as the default until the user picks something. Left and right dock it as a vertical rail (the inspector steps inwards when its on the right), and mobile keeps the bottom rail as always.

title: Framing build animation: a lazy nested reveal, an animation speed, and a level that follows the project
body:
# Framing build animation: a lazy nested reveal at the Framing level, one pace, an animation speed, a level that follows the project, walls that keep their finish through the rise, and a reveal that follows edits, deletions and the person's display

Base: `pascalorg/editor` main (`bb7d014c0`, #1001), merged in, not rebased. Head: branch `feat/framing-build-animation-20261015` (`faa6e27c3`), from the AxiomeCG fork. 47 commits; squash-merge.
Pairs with the private-editor PR "Framing build animation: Bones builds each wall in its preroll". That PR pins this head and must be re-pinned to the squash commit once this one merges.

## What is in it (read this first)

- **Framing gets its own schedule** in the construction reveal (it was treated as Full): floors, rooms and pieces staggered, roofs after the walls, furniture last, at one pace (`FRAMING_PACE` 1.75) and with a cap that grows with the build. Full, Simple and Off keep their tables (a test pins them).
- **Animation speed** setting, ×0.5 to ×2, read when a plan is made.
- **The level follows the project**: Framing where the framing plugin is installed, Full where it is not; the Framing option is greyed with a tip and wears the Pro badge when it is not available.
- **Walls keep their finish while they rise** (texture scale per metre, preset re-skin). Full gains it too.
- **The animation follows what happens**: a build always shows (even on a hidden level), an edit replays its reveal, a deletion plays the creation backwards, deleting a room or a floor takes it apart, a roof's covering is laid from the eave to the ridge, the cutaway never hides what plays, Follow Pascal pulls back to the whole house and looks at an outside edit from outside.
- **Plugin hooks** for staging members in a preroll (`setRevealPreroll`, `getRevealTurn`, `revealClockMs`, `getRevealPlanSpeed`, `emitRevealPuff`, `commitRevealCandidates`, `planLazyReveal`).
- Core gains four optional registry fields (`derivedWrites` on a commit; `revealOnEdit`, `exterior` and `revealLayout` on a kind). No schema, no migration, no mcp or app change.

## What changes for a person

The Construction animation setting already offers **Framing**, described as "Full, plus the framing members dropping in first, where the framing plugin draws them". Today the viewer treats Framing exactly as Full and nothing reads it. This PR gives Framing its own schedule in the construction reveal and two settings around it.

### The Framing schedule

- floors a beat apart, the rooms of a floor a beat apart, the pieces of a room one by one around it, every start jittered;
- roofs once every floor is up, then furniture room by room;
- a big build takes proportionally longer instead of being squeezed (cap 70 s at the Framing pace);
- the whole Framing timeline runs at one pace, `FRAMING_PACE` = 1.75: a build that took 20 s now takes about 35 s, and a smaller or larger one scales the same;
- a rise, scale or settle overshoots and settles (back.out), gentler for a rising wall (about 2 % past its top, so it does not push into the slab over it while floors build side by side);
- a new node whose kind declares no reveal, added where its host was already there, comes in on a default reveal instead of popping (under a host still coming in, it comes in with it).

**Full, Simple and Off keep their schedules.** Full reads `REVEAL_TIMING` / `RETRACT_TIMING` and a test pins their tables as literals.

### Animation speed

Settings, Preferences, under Construction animation: **Animation speed** ×0.5, ×0.75, ×1, ×1.5, ×2 (default ×1). Every time of a schedule is divided by the speed, caps included: Full, Framing (at its pace) and the undo's rewind. ×1 returns the shipped tables themselves. The speed is read when a plan is made: what is already moving keeps its own durations, so a change applies to the next build and never moves one that is playing. Persisted with the level under the same key (`pascal-construction-reveal`); a person saved before it is at ×1.

### The level follows the project

The level that plays is the person's choice, or, with none of their own, **Framing where the project has the plugin that draws the framing and Full where it has not**. Nothing is stored for the default; it is read per project.

| Case | Level that plays | Framing option |
|---|---|---|
| no choice, framing plugin available | Framing | enabled |
| no choice, plugin absent | Full | greyed, tip "Framing needs the Architect plugin." |
| chose Full / Simple / Off | the choice | per plugin |
| chose Framing, plugin removed | Full (the choice is kept) | greyed; Framing returns with the plugin |
| level saved before this change | that level, as a choice | per plugin |

"Available" is one read: the kind `bones:framing` is registered and `isNodeKindEnabled` says its plugin is installed in the project. The editor never names a plugin id (on main it resolves to `pascal:procedural`). Hosts read `useConstructionRevealLevel()` / `getConstructionRevealLevel()` instead of the saved `level`. A `SegmentedControl` option can be `disabled` (greyed, stays hoverable so a tooltip can say why).

### Walls keep their finish through the rise

A wall rises by scaling in Y, which squashed its textures while it moved and let a preset finish go stale. Now:

- while a wall rises its UVs are counter-scaled along the vertical, so a texture keeps its tiles per metre (`reveal-texture-scale.ts`: the mesh draws a clone of its geometry, shared materials and cached geometry untouched; the clone goes when the reveal ends);
- a wall face whose finish comes from a material preset (a slot, the assembly's cladding, a preset ref) re-skins when the library's materials change, and curtain-wall materials resolve preset refs: the wall batch watches the library version and the face signature carries the preset.

This is the same rise Full plays, so Full gains it too.

### The animation follows what is built, edited and removed

- **A build always shows.** The level a reveal plays on shows while it plays, whatever the level display hides (`levelsRevealing`); the reveal publishes the levels it works on. An undo plays back the kinds that came in with a default reveal.
- **Follow Pascal shows the whole house.** It pulls back to the finished house with the floors above shown, and the person's display (cutaway, floor, hidden floors) comes back when it ends.
- **An edit replays its reveal, quickly.** Each kind lists the fields that make its picture (`revealOnEdit`); a commit that changes one replays the node's reveal. What the structure reconciler writes as a consequence of an edit (`derivedWrites`) is not an edit and does not replay. Many edits begin spread over one second (the cap spread over the pieces), not piled on its last frame.
- **A deletion plays the creation backwards**, from a snapshot of the node, through the reveal's `deletes` prop.
- **A roof is covered, not dropped.** At the Framing level a roof keeps its frame (Bones' frame falls in a preroll of its own) and its covering is laid over it in place, from the eave to the ridge: the node holds still and its meshes wear a world-height mask whose level moves with every frame from the lowest edge to the highest (an ease in and out, no steps; a flat roof sweeps along its longer plan side), in a time that follows its size: 450 ms for each metre of sweep at pace 1, never under 1.4 s nor over 4.2 s (at the Framing pace 0.79 s a metre, 2.45 s to 7.35 s); its parts are not staged on their own. Undo and a deletion lift the covering off from the ridge, the same sweep backwards in 0.6 of that time. The speed setting scales all of it. Full, Simple and Off are unchanged.
- **Deleting a room or a floor takes it apart.** At the Framing level a deletion (and an undo) plays the build's own plan read from its end: the furniture lifts out first, then the roof's covering, the openings, the walls and the slabs last, the floors from the top down, each room as it went up, with the prerolls a plugin asked kept after each piece's going. A deleted floor's pictures stand in their building, so they outlive the floor's own object. A derived plate or ceiling goes with its room (the reconciler derives them; a plate it merely derives anew is not a deletion). Capped at 14 s however many pieces it takes back. Full keeps its rewind.
- **The cutaway never hides what plays.** The reveal publishes the nodes playing (moving in, going out, carried, an edit replaying: `nodesRevealing`); in cutaway the wall cutout cache keeps a wall visible for as long as it, an opening it hosts or a node it stands under plays, and goes back to what the view wants after. The person's wall mode is never written; walls down stays their choice. A deleted wall plays its deletion in its own picture (the wall's visible variant, as a capture draws it), not under the cutaway, unless that palette cannot draw the groups the copy carries (a room-wide paint preview was live): then the copy keeps what it wears.
- **Follow looks at an outside edit from outside.** An exterior wall bent, a window or door moved along one, a roof or the ground edited is an outside step: Follow sets the walls up for it and frames the exterior face (it would have fallen back to the cutaway, which hides the wall that plays), and puts the presentation back. A commit that changes one such piece takes the outside view for all of it; a build keeps its single cutaway and never writes the walls up in between; a mode the person picks meanwhile is theirs. A window or door moved along its wall replays (`position` joins `revealOnEdit`); a wall moved does not replay its windows. `sceneViewFacing` answers for an exterior wall (the way its exterior side faces).
- **What stands above a deleted floor waits for it.** Deleting a storey re-stacks the levels above it at once (a roof level drops by the storey's height), while the floor still comes apart for seconds. The levels above a deleted floor now keep their place while its pictures remain, then come down onto what is below in one eased move, in the rewind's own drop time at the level and speed (`systems/level/level-hold.ts`, read by `LevelSystem` ahead of the stacked elevation; presentation only, no scene write). Everything a held level holds goes with it (the roof, its Bones frame). A load, a capture, an export, the reveal stopping and an undo release the hold at once. A level object that has just mounted (a restored floor, a new storey, a load) now cuts every level to its height in the same frame instead of sliding about 250 ms, so an undo never runs a floor and its roof through each other.
- **A guard test** (`reveal-coverage.test.ts`): every built-in kind an agent can create is staged by the reveal, on a level and on a roof, at the Full and Framing levels; a kind that declares `revealOnEdit` lists only fields its schema has.

### Framing wears the Pro badge

The plugin that draws the framing is a Pro one on main (the Architect plugin pulls it in), so the Framing option wears the mark the plugin manager shows next to a plugin that needs a plan. The manager's `Badge` becomes a shared primitive used by both.

## For plugins

The reveal exposes what a plugin needs to stage its own members at the Framing level:

- `setRevealPreroll` asks for a preroll before nodes of the lazy schedule move in; the schedule leaves the time and the node starts after it;
- `getRevealTurn` and `revealClockMs` give each node's turn on the reveal's clock (a preroll already playing keeps its turn when the plan is made again);
- `getRevealPlanSpeed` tells a plugin which speed the plan in force was made at;
- `emitRevealPuff` lends the reveal's dust;
- `commitRevealCandidates`, `planLazyReveal`, `LAZY_REVEAL_BASE_TIMING`, `LAZY_REVEAL_TIMING`, `pacedLazyTiming`, `FRAMING_PACE` are exported from `@pascal-app/viewer`.

Candidates carry their room (`cluster`): the room a node stands in (for a node on a line, the room on either side of its middle), else runs of the lines that meet end to end. What is a room and what is a line is declared by the kind (`capabilities.revealLayout`: the zone and the wall declare it), so a plugin kind that declares the same is laid out the same way.

## Scope

`packages/viewer` (reveal schedule, candidates, pose, texture scale, wall material signature, construction-reveal system, level system, exports), `packages/editor` (the construction-reveal store, the two settings, the Pro badge, `SegmentedControl`'s per-option `disabled`, Follow Pascal), `packages/core` (`derivedWrites`, `revealOnEdit`, `exterior`, `revealLayout`), and `packages/nodes` (the wall batch's library-version watch, curtain-wall preset refs, each kind's `revealOnEdit` list, `exterior` and `revealLayout` declarations, the coverage guard). 99 files, +8,587 / -330, of which 1,090 lines are one JSON test fixture and ~3,800 are tests and fixtures. Core gains four optional registry fields (`derivedWrites` on a commit; `revealOnEdit`, `exterior` and `revealLayout` on a kind), nothing else; no mcp or app change. No schema, no migration.

## How to test

1. Settings, Construction animation: **Framing** (needs a project where the framing plugin is installed; otherwise it is greyed with its tip "Framing needs the Architect plugin.").
2. Ask the agent for a multi-room, two-storey build (any commit that creates many walls).
3. Watch: slabs first, floors offset, rooms side by side, roof after the walls; nothing pops.
4. Settings, Animation speed: ×2 and ×0.5; the next build plays in half and double the time.
5. Watch a textured or painted wall rise: its texture keeps its scale and its finish is the one it settles in.
6. Switch to **Full** and repeat: the schedule is as before (it gains the wall finish fix).
7. Edit a built piece (change a wall's height, move a door): it replays its reveal in a moment; a stair's or a roof's structure follow-up writes do not.
8. Delete a piece (select, Delete): it plays its creation backwards; undo plays it in again.
9. At Framing, ask for a build with a roof: the roof's frame falls and stays, then the covering closes over it continuously from the eave to the ridge, a small roof in about 2.5 s and a large one in at most about 7 s (it is not dropped whole); delete the roof and the covering lifts off from the ridge.
10. At Framing, delete a room, then a whole floor: furniture lifts out, the roof covering and openings go, then the walls and the slabs, the top floor first and each room as it went up; undo plays it back in. At Full the rewind is as before.
11. With the cutaway on, ask for a build: nothing that plays is hidden by the cutaway while it plays (a wall a window is being added to stays up for it); delete a wall: it plays in its own picture, not stippled.
12. Turn Follow Pascal on, bend an exterior wall or move a window along it: the camera looks at it from outside with the walls up, then your display comes back. Turn Follow Pascal on and ask for a build: the camera pulls back to the whole house, floors above shown; when it ends the display you had comes back.

## Architecture review (16 Oct)

A read-only architecture review (the editor's `review-architecture` skill) found two blockers, both the same rule broken (`DECISIONS.md` E-002: no kind-specific branching keyed on `node.type` in `packages/viewer` or `packages/editor`; the behaviour belongs on the kind's definition). Both are fixed in this PR; the review's suggestions and nits are not part of this change.

- **Follow Pascal's "seen from outside" (editor).** `follow-pascal-exterior.ts` held a hand-kept set of 22 kind names and `node.type` branches for wall, door, window, slab and the storey kinds. It now asks the registry: the new optional `capabilities.exterior?: boolean | ((node, nodes) => boolean | undefined)`. `true` for the roof, roof segment, every roof accessory, the fence and its gates, the site; `false` for level, building and zone; a function for the wall (an exterior face) and for the door and the window (in a roof segment, or in such a wall). The helper keeps its walk up the parents (a `true` kind outdoors, up to the first `false` one) and its "stands in no storey" fallback. Six of the names were not kinds on main (`ramp`, `rock`, `terrain-tile`, `terrain-break`, `facade`, and `fence-feature`, whose real kinds are `fence-gate` and `fence-opening`) and a slab's `terrainMode` is a field no schema has: they are gone, and no real node's answer changes. A plugin kind now says it stands outdoors the same way.
- **The reveal's host, rooms and lines (viewer).** (1) A node hosted on a roof defaulted to a drop through `parent.type === 'roof'`: it is now any ancestor whose `capabilities.reveal.style` is `assemble` (only the roof declares it, so the result is the same). (2) The deletion ghost of a wall the cutaway was hiding was dressed through a `node.type === 'wall'` check and the wall's own palette builder: the wall cutout (`WallCutoutCache`) now keeps the wall's visible palette on the mesh it cuts away (`visibleMaterialsOf`), and the ghost wears it, with the `hasMaterialsForGroups` guard kept; the reveal names no wall kind. (3) The room-by-room layout needed "this node outlines a room" and "this node stands on a line": the new optional `capabilities.revealLayout?: { room?, line? }`, set by the zone (`room`: its polygon) and the wall (`line`: its two ends). The `as unknown as { start; end }` casts are gone, and the plates and ceilings a deleted room or wall takes with it are those of any kind that declares a `revealLayout`.
- Both fields are documented in `wiki/architecture/node-definitions.md` (capability reference) with their doc comments in `packages/core/src/registry/types.ts`.
- New tests: a plugin-style kind that declares the fields is treated as the built-in it imitates: outdoors for Follow (always, by a field, by what holds it); staged on an assembled host; laid out in its room and run along the lines it meets; taking a derived plate with it when it goes (`reveal-declared-kinds.test.ts`, `follow-pascal-exterior.test.ts`); what the built-in kinds declare (`exterior-declarations.test.ts`); the cutout keeps the visible palette (`wall-cutout-cache.test.ts`).

## Bugbot (16 Oct)

- **Stale derived writes skip later reveals** (`history-control.ts`): real. A derived write that set a value the node already had, deleted a node that was not there, or cancelled out inside a history step left its note in the module map, and the next real commit inherited it; `applyNodeChangesActionImpl` never noted `changes.delete`. Notes are now taken only for the fields whose value changes and the nodes that exist, after the last early return; a no-op commit or transaction clears the map; deletes through `applyNodeChanges` are noted as the whole node. Six tests in `derived-commit-nodes.test.ts` (they fail before the fix).
- **Bugbot round 2 (16 Oct), three findings, all real** (each reproduced by a test that failed before the fix):
  - *Loose wall runs ignore outline order* (`reveal-candidates.ts`): `layoutRuns` walked an outline breadth-first, so a run of six was two stretches; it walks depth-first from a free end (open chain) or the first wall (closed outline), so a run is one stretch. New `reveal-candidates-runs.test.ts` (3 tests).
  - *Follow outdoor latch raises walls mid-build* (`follow-pascal.tsx`): `outsideBuild` was read from the global edit queue at every word and kept for the session, so an exterior edit queued by another commit, or an exterior commit just before an interior one, took a build outdoors and wrote the walls up between its steps. Only an edit's own words (`changed`) read the queue now, a build or a deletion clears the latch, and the first edit after the reveal said `complete` starts from false. Two tests in `follow-pascal.test.tsx`.
  - *Deletion ghosts omitted from `nodesRevealing`* (`construction-reveal.tsx`): a ghost is out of the scene, so the cutaway could not find the wall a departing opening stood in. Each ghost keeps its host (the nearest node the commit leaves in the scene that is not a storey, building or site; `CONTAINERS` is exported from `reveal-candidates.ts`) and `nodesAtPlay` publishes it. Test "the wall an opening is leaving stays in play for as long as its picture plays".
- **Bugbot round 3 (16 Oct), one finding, real** (reproduced by a test that failed before the fix):
  - *Fallback Full click erases Framing* (`construction-animation-setting.tsx`, `use-construction-reveal.ts`): the control shows the level that plays, so a saved Framing shows as Full while the plugin is gone, and a click on that pressed Full wrote `chosen: true, level: 'full'` over the kept Framing. `chooseConstructionLevel` now ignores a click on the level that plays when the person has already chosen (the kept choice comes back with the plugin); any other level, or a click with no choice yet, is a choice as before. Tests: "clicking the level that plays" (3).

## Merged with main again on 16 Oct (#1001)

`upstream/main` moved to `bb7d014c0` (#1001: local plugins, surface stairs and deck railings) and merged in (`ba4cc7323`). Two content conflicts, in `nodes/src/fence/definition.ts` and `nodes/src/stair/definition.ts`: main added `hostRefFields` beside this PR's `revealOnEdit` in the same `capabilities` block; both are kept. Every suite green after it (viewer 805, editor 2587, core 4955, nodes 4960, plugin-bones 1404, hosted 2682, typecheck 26/26; load timeouts green when rerun alone).

## Merged with main on 16 Oct

`upstream/main` moved to `3dd378b8e` (#1085 kitchen catalog and magnetic placement, #1061 `@types/three` 0.186, #1091 room-wide paint preview keeps walls raycastable) and merged in (`d7e00a05a`, a merge commit, no rebase). One content conflict, in `packages/viewer/src/systems/wall/wall-cutout-cache.ts`:

- Both sides edited `update()` at the same spot: this PR's in-play stamps (`wallsInPlay`, `playChanged`) and main's loop that re-applies the walls a paint preview deferred. Both are kept. The in-play block runs first, so `this.inPlay` is current when main's loop calls `apply`, which now reads it for `hidden`; then main's deferred loop; `playChanged` still joins `invalidated` and the per-wall `apply` condition. In `apply` the branch's `hidden` expression and main's `mayAssign` guard around `wall.mesh.material = …` are both kept.
- A wall deferred by the preview is still applied, and a wall in play is still stamped. New test in `wall-cutout-cache.test.ts` ("a wall in play while a room-wide preview holds its groups is stamped now and given its palette when the preview lets go"): the play starts under a preview that holds the wall's groups (stamp visible at once, preview kept), the preview lets go while it still plays (visible palette), the play ends (hidden palette and stamp). It fails if main's loop or `playChanged` is dropped.
- The deletion ghost (`construction-reveal/ghost-dress.ts`) assigned the wall's visible palette to its copy without main's guard. It now assigns it only when `hasMaterialsForGroups(copy, palette)` holds, so a deletion during a room-wide preview cannot leave a copy with a group and no material (a raycast over it would throw on `material.side`). Test in `ghost-dress.test.ts`; two tests that used a six-group box with a three-entry palette now give the mesh the one group a wall's geometry has (`ghost-dress.test.ts`, `construction-reveal.test.tsx`).
- `@types/three` 0.186 raised no type error in this PR's code.

## Merge with main (15 Oct)

Main was merged in twice (`upstream/main` `683ce0c22` then `dcd304a30`); the Framing work is unchanged by it except for what is listed here.

- `SegmentedControl`: main added a per-option `disabled` at the same time. Main's version is kept (`isDisabled`, `opacity-40`); the one difference is that the native `disabled` attribute stays the control's own, so a greyed option keeps `aria-disabled`, ignores its click and stays hoverable for its tooltip.
- `roof-segment/definition.ts`: main added `paint` and `slots`, this PR `revealOnEdit`; both are kept. The list also gains `barrelRise`, `barrelSegments`, `roofSystem` and `glazing` (the fields main's barrel roofs and glazed roofs added), with a test.
- `node-batch.test.ts` and `follow-pascal.test.tsx`: main's Biome 2.5 reformatted the tests this PR also edits; main's layout is taken and the PR's cases (`revealing`, the floors-above-shown assertion, the 1.5 s build) are kept. Three other test files are reformatted with Biome 2.5.
- A type annotation in `follow-pascal.test.tsx` (main's `toEqual` is stricter).

## How it was checked

Run on the head (`f936603cd`), with the dists rebuilt first (turbo build of the editor packages, 7 of 7 tasks), `bun install --frozen-lockfile` on the merged lockfile:

- `packages/viewer`: `bun test src` 803 pass, 0 fail, Ran 803 tests across 90 files (with the held levels above a deleted floor: Full, Framing, speed, Off, undo mid-dismantle and after).
- `packages/editor`: `bun test src` 2534 pass, 0 fail.
- `packages/core`: `bun test src` 4939 pass, 0 fail.
- `packages/nodes`: `bun test` 4997 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail; the rise test mounts real walls (solid and rendered shading), drives a construction reveal and checks each frame that the faces keep their materials and metre-scale UVs, then that the settled batch has the same UVs.
- `reveal-add-volume.test.ts` runs a frozen two-storey, three-room commit (`__fixtures__/add-volume-commit.json`): every wall, slab, room and roof goes through the timeline; walls are grouped by room; slabs first; at most two starts in a 60 fps frame; the build is never a pulse.
- New tests: each speed step scales Full, Framing and the rewind by exactly 1/speed; ×1 equals today's tables; caps scale; raising the speed mid-wall leaves its progress per frame at the old rate and the next build plans at the new one; persistence and reload; the default, the greyed option, its tooltip, the fall back and the saved choice (store and drawn control); a wall in play under a room-wide paint preview; a deletion ghost under one.
- `turbo run check-types --continue`: 11 of 13 tasks pass. Two fail, both main's: `editor#check-types` (8 `TS2307` for `react-scan`, `geist/font/pixel` and `@webxr/plugin`, not installed in the test tree; the same 8 as on a clean `upstream/main`) and `@pascal-app/editor#check-types` (`ceiling-bracket-batch.test.ts` TS2578 and TS2352 on main's `three/src/renderers/common/Attributes.js` cast from #1061; the file is not touched here, and a clean `upstream/main` checkout gives the same two errors and no other).
- Biome on the 88 source and config files this branch changes against main: 0 errors (4 pre-existing plugin warnings in `node-batch.test.ts`, from main).
- Not run: e2e, any browser or GPU check. The animation itself was not watched in this pass.

## Limits

- The cap is 70 s at the Framing pace (before the speed): a very large commit is pulled together past it.
- The Framing schedule applies to what an agent commits (the host's `reveals` policy); a person's own edits stay instant.
- Not scaled by the speed: the roof lifts and glides of a moved piece (not build animations).
- A kind that declares only a default reveal replays nothing on an edit.
- Follow looks at an edited piece, not at a deleted one.
- An undo of a deleted floor is a cut, not a play (an undo plays nothing in this code base): the floor and the levels above appear at their heights in the same frame.
- The undo of a turn that created a storey (retract, then history restore) is not held: a roof that existed before the turn still settles by the old lerp when that storey goes.
- A person's delete plays for every local commit, so a tool that deletes and recreates a node shows both.
- Main does not clamp a window or door to its wall when the wall is shortened (the window stays at 6 m on a 4 m wall): shortening a wall replays the wall only, and the window plays nothing. That is main's behaviour; R&D's clamp is not part of this PR.
- The deconstruction plays the build's order read backwards, capped at 14 s: a very large deletion is compressed past it.
- The covering sweep is a mask over the roof's meshes: a node with nothing drawn has an empty sweep and plays nothing.
- Terrain tiles and breaks are not staged by this PR (main has none).

title: editor: run tool names no kind; duct and pipe specifics back in nodes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #1001. To let node packs share the run-drawing tool without importing the built-in plugin, #1001 moved it to `@pascal-app/editor/distribution`. Some details that belong only to the built-in duct and pipe kinds moved along with it. This PR keeps the tool in the editor but makes it kind-agnostic:

- **Trade-specific pieces move back to `nodes`.** The port systems (duct supply/return, DWV waste/vent, refrigerant) and the nominal-inch section size `runSectionHalfSizeM` now live in `packages/nodes/src/shared/port-systems.ts`. The duct, pipe, lineset and liquid-line tools import them from there.
- **No hidden duct default.** `findNearestRunBodyXZ`, `findNearestRunBody3D`, `findRunBodyCrossingXZ` and `findRunBodyCrossingSurface` used to fall back to `'duct-segment'` when no kinds were given. `kinds` is now required, so a node pack's runs are never treated as ducts by accident. 1. Draw a duct run in 3D, ending on the side of an existing duct. It should tap the trunk exactly as before.

3. Draw a DWV pipe and a lineset and connect them to fittings. Each should snap only to ports of its own system, as before.

title: @pascal-app/cli 1.0.4: `pascal start` fails, runtime archive digest does not match the value pinned in the npm package
body:
## What happens

`npm install --global @pascal-app/cli` installs 1.0.4. Running `pascal start` downloads

https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/releases/download/@pascal-app/cli@1.0.4/pascal-web-runtime-1.0.4.tar.gz

and then fails with:

```
The Pascal web runtime archive does not match the digest published with this CLI.
```

Verified 2026-10-16 on macOS (Darwin 24.3.0), Node 25.6.1.

## Expected vs actual digest

| Source | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| Pinned in the npm package (`dist/runtime-source.json`) | `0b0e9c56d615e341634dadce6b40928e5809216de80c469cebeaaefcac67373e` |
| Actual archive (two separate downloads) | `d101720c4bf76e634b282a40ab7ec50788804e4aab6fe62c45097986130e3a0d` |
| GitHub asset digest from `gh release view` | `d101720c4bf76e634b282a40ab7ec50788804e4aab6fe62c45097986130e3a0d` |
| `pascal-web-runtime-1.0.4.tar.gz.sha256` asset on the release | `d101720c4bf76e634b282a40ab7ec50788804e4aab6fe62c45097986130e3a0d` |

The archive on the release is self-consistent, so the stale value is the one baked into the npm package.

## Timing

- npm `@pascal-app/cli@1.0.4` published: 2026-10-13T11:37:35Z
- Release asset `pascal-web-runtime-1.0.4.tar.gz` uploaded: 2026-10-13T12:11:53Z

The asset was uploaded 34 minutes after the npm package, which suggests the runtime archive was rebuilt after the digest was pinned in the CLI.

## Workaround

```
npm install --global @pascal-app/cli@1.0.3
```

1.0.3 installs and `pascal start` runs cleanly.

title: editor: click-to-move holds the item; new items face the camera
body:
## What does this PR do?

Three placement fixes:

- **Click-to-move no longer drops the item instantly.** Clicking an already-selected item picks it up, but the move tool mounted before the browser's trailing `click` of that same press, which committed the item where it stood (pick sound, then place sound, no movement). The pick-up now swallows that one click, like the Cmd-drag path already does.
- **New floor items start facing the camera.** `cameraFacingYaw()` (exported) turns the item's front (+Z) toward the view the placement starts from, snapped to 90° in the active building's frame; it falls back to the plan azimuth when the camera looks straight down. Used for the initial floor draft of the item tool. Wall/ceiling strategies keep their own rotation, and R/T plus repeat placement behave as before.
- **`alwaysPinned` views.** A host view can stay in the view bar for good: no pin/unpin control in "More views", and a stale stored unpin is ignored.

## How to test

1. Select a placed item, click it again: it follows the cursor; the next click drops it at the new spot.
2. Arm a catalog item from two camera angles 90° apart: the facing arrow points at you each time.
3. Register a view with `alwaysPinned: true`: it shows in the bar and has no pin button in the "More views" menu.

title: Underground: the ground steps aside over a basement, the world turns to earth below it, a ground line in the levels, and a foundation under every house
body:
Base: `pascalorg/editor` `main` (`82153a03c`). Head: branch `feat/underground-20261016` (`cee68cf36`). 44 commits; squash-merge.
Pairs with the private-editor PR "Underground: the chat and hosted MCP serve set_ground_level, Bones draws its foundation under the ground, the scene program reads grade". That PR pins this head and must be re-pinned to the squash commit once this one merges.

## What a person can now do

- **See a basement from above.** With a level below grade shown, the ground over it is a veil with a hole in it: the hole's edge is a clean section cut over earth walls, and a deep level reads as a pit with strata. Several levels below grade work: the hole follows the level shown and those between it and grade.
- **Dive under the ground.** The orbit may go under any building, down to a floor 3 m under the lowest ground. Under the ground the world turns to a dark earth (soil sky, fog past the shown level, a vignette, a light from the eye); crossing the ground is a 0.4 s fade. Reduced motion or an animation setting of Off makes it instant.
- **Set the ground floor.** The levels panel has **Set as ground floor**; the building names the level at grade (`groundLevelId`; absent = the lowest level not under the datum). One undo step. Adding a basement goes under the lowest floor and leaves the building where it stands.
- **See the foundation.** Every building gets a generic foundation under its exterior walls (a concrete footing and a stem, derived from the walls), drawn under the ground and visible when diving. A plugin that draws its own foundation (Bones) takes that level out of the generic one (`drawsFoundation`).
- **Build a basement wall that is a foundation wall.** A wall against the ground on a level below grade defaults to the building's regional construction: 8 in CMU with 2x4 treated furring laid flat inside (United States and where nothing is known), 25 cm cast concrete insulated and waterproofed outside (Europe). The ground floor is seated 8 in over grade, the top of the foundation. A partition inside the outline is an ordinary wall; a wall given a thickness or an assembly keeps it; existing walls are never rewritten.
- **View bar:** a Ground toggle, Auto / Solid.
- **Agents (MCP):** `set_ground_level`; `list_levels` answers `groundLevels` and, per level, `gradeStanding` and `isGroundLevel`; `verify_scene` says `basement_at_grade` and `ground_level_unseated`; the MCP guide names the ground line.

## What is in it

- `core`: `groundLevelId` on a building, the ground line (`ground-level`, `grade-standing`, subpath exports), `buildGroundLevelChanges`, `buildLevelBelowChanges`, `belowGradeFloorY`, the generic foundation and `FOUNDATION_STANDARD`, `foundationReadingOf` / construction by region (block, cast concrete), `set_ground_level` contract and operation, `drawsFoundation` on a node definition, the hole's box that follows the level shown.
- `viewer`: the ground veil and ground window, the underground ambiance, the eye's fill, `undergroundLook`.
- `nodes/site`: the hole, its edges, the pit, the generic foundation renderer.
- `editor`: orbit dive and its clearance, view bar toggle, levels panel, `addStoreyBelow`.
- `mcp`: `set_ground_level` and README/guide rows. Docs: `wiki/architecture/{layers,materials-and-themes,vertical-model}.md`, the pascal-3d skill's tool workflows.
- No schema migration: `groundLevelId` is an optional field on the building node.

## What stays on R&D

- The other edge looks (`noise`, `quiet`, `section`) and the noise transition: still in the code as `EDGE_LOOKS` rows and a uniform, **unexposed**. The shipped look is `DEFAULT_UNDERGROUND_LOOK = { edge: 'section-earth', transition: 'fade' }`.
- The roof veil; insert a storey between under the ground line (needs the porch roofs); stone construction and the facade-style choice of the foundation (read facade nodes); `create_story_shell` foundation walls (MCP-only on main); storey facts on `list_levels`; the grade-aware core checks (`room-light`, enclosure, unroofed storey, facade columns, circulation) and the Flow grade part.
- Not here, by design: design brief, catalog, Flow fixes, facade work, terrain shaping tools, +0.20 seating of new houses.

Main wins duplicates: Wassim's floor foundations (#976), editing foundations (#1039) and `recessed-slab-ground-holes.ts` are untouched; the generic foundation is derived and independent of `set_floor_foundation`.

title: Let open briefs become fully designed spaces, with shared catalog references and creation tools
body:
Companion of the private PR "Give normal Architect and model turns room to design beyond the minimum". Review the two as one change: the chat side lives there, the contracts and shared operations here.

**Head** `4ac2e8ad1`, 24 commits and the merge of upstream main, on `599727dc3` (70 files, +5,985 / −355). The private PR pins this head last; it is re-pinned to the merged SHA once this one lands.

## What changes for a person using the chat

An open request leaves the agent room to design the space rather than stop at a stock furniture set. What the request states still binds the work: a request for one bedroom is one bedroom, and "add a lamp next to the sofa" is one designed lamp, not a redecoration. Named pieces are a minimum unless the person says otherwise. The agent can look at catalog items as references, create several objects in one batch, place procedural designs and look across a room from a person's height. A rug on a living room's floor is accepted as furniture instead of being refused as a floor plate.

## In this PR

- **The brief by axes.** `design_brief` reads the request axis by axis: action, size, pieces, openings, style, materials, dressing, and the source. Each axis is bounded by the person's own words (a quote and a short reading; `pieces` as a minimum or exact) or open with a design statement. The server judges no taste and checks facts only: an absent axis, an open axis with no design, a quote that is not in the person's message (in the chat), a source that is not named. Six of the eight dressing layers must name pieces only when the dressing axis is open; the named pieces are a minimum and cannot bound the dressing (`dressing_bounded_by_minimum`). Open-source `asIs` accepts only technical equipment viewed first. Briefs stored in the earlier shape still read.
- **Shared tools and gate.** `view_assets` (catalog pictures, sizes, paintable surface names; paint's surface lookup uses the catalog's URL, never a URL from scene nodes). `add_object` inside `run_batch`: up to three host compiles at once, per-object receipts, independent failures; other batch refusals stay atomic. `view_scene({ interior: { zoneId } })`: a shared room-interior camera plan. The existing MCP procedural placement and validation (`place_design`, `validate_design`) extracted into shared operations so the chat can offer them; main's design-version semantics stay authoritative.
- **A flat object is a floor plate only where no floor is under it.** `add_object` still refuses `use_slab` for a plate of at least 2 m, at most 0.35 m thick, on the floor, but not when at least half of its footprint lies over a slab of its level (a room's floor plate, a drawn slab, a deck; holes left out). The scene decides, not the name or category. `use_walls` is unchanged.
- Fact and glossary wording in the MCP guide and the shared tool descriptions, without a compulsory building recipe.
- The shared case tables run on core, MCP and chat: 23 `design_brief` cases (the bedroom, "add a lamp" in English and French, "only a bed and a lamp", the guard), nine rug cases, the batch and gate cases.

Creation tools are `add_object` and `place_design`, not a furniture-template tool, and no capability is MCP-only. By hand, the existing item and design placement, catalog, source editor and camera controls remain; there is no manual design-brief step.

## Not in this PR

`add_furniture` and the parametric furniture kind, window dressing, underground work, facade and terrain work, catalog step B, paid material generation, broad tool consolidation, stalled-turn and watchdog features. Facts that name unavailable tools are adapted, not backed by importing those features. Main's newer chat presentation is left alone. This PR does not change billing.

## Tests

Whole suites of the editor packages, run in the private repo's CI configuration (hoisted install, `CI=true`, `bun run test --concurrency=4`, no editor filter), with the private PR's head pinning this one. Real lines:

| Suite | New head | Main (same bases) |
|---|---|---|
| `@pascal-app/core` | `Ran 5131 tests across 316 files.` `0 fail` | 4,955 pass, 0 fail |
| `@pascal-app/mcp` | `Ran 1213 tests across 74 files.` `0 fail` | 1,128 pass, 0 fail |
| `@pascal-app/viewer` | `Ran 811 tests across 92 files.` `0 fail` | 811 pass, 0 fail |
| `@pascal-app/nodes` | `Ran 4962 tests across 388 files.` `0 fail` | 4,961 pass, 1 skip |
| `@pascal-app/editor` | `Ran 2598 tests across 285 files.` `0 fail` | 2,598 pass, 0 fail |
| Whole turbo `test` | ` Tasks:    33 successful, 33 total` | |
| Editor `check-types` | ` Tasks:    10 successful, 11 total`, two errors | the same two |

The two `check-types` errors are `ceiling-bracket-batch.test.ts(13,1): error TS2578` (unused `@ts-expect-error`) and `(33,20): error TS2352`. They are on main; this PR does not touch that file. Biome on the changed files: clean (the fixtures directory is ignored by its config).

## Not proven

No model was called: the tests establish contracts, operations and host requests, not that a model produces a better design from the axes. No live browser or GPU render: the room view and the rug were exercised on tests and shared cases, not on screen. The pushed heads are being tested by hand. The guard compares quote containment only (a dressing quote that contains the pieces quote is not caught); over MCP an axis quote is required but compared with no message.

> **High Risk**
> Changes core agent furnishing workflow, batch atomicity rules, and session-gated catalog placement—mistakes would block or mis-route normal design turns.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces a **`design_brief` gate** so furnishing (`place_items`, `furnish_room`, `place_in_room`, `place_design`, and gated batches) only runs after a recorded brief. The brief reads the request **axis by axis** (bounded quotes vs open design statements), validates **dressing** (`beyond` layers), and routes **source** (open → create; catalog/brand → place). title: editor: FIX - door and window placement works in 2D-only view
body:
## What does this PR do?

In 2D-only view the hidden 3D pane had `display: none`, so its canvas had no size and the scene never mounted, and with it the door and window tools. The 2D plan sends its `wall:*` events to those tools, so placing a door or window in 2D-only view just showed the cursor chip and the click placed nothing, until 3D was opened at least once. The hidden pane now keeps its size (`visibility: hidden`, no pointer events, render still paused), so the tools are there from the first hover.

Side effect worth knowing: since the 3D camera now mounts in 2D-only view too, the plan opens aligned to the camera like it already did after visiting 3D once.

## How to test

1. Reload a project with walls straight into 2D-only view (dont open 3D or Split)
2. Pick Door and hover a wall: the door draws on the wall with its gap and swing
3. Click: the door is placed where it was drawn. Same for Window
