title: IFC export drops wall assembly layers; floorplan PDF fills rooms with the wall colour
body:
### What happened?

Two export bugs found while testing layered walls (the `Exterior 2x6 — stucco` preset) on the two-bedroom template:

1. **IFC: wall assemblies are lost.** Every wall is written as one `Core` IfcMaterialLayer of the total thickness (`Wall 186 mm`), even when `wall.assembly` holds stucco / OSB / 2x6 framing / drywall layers. Tools that read IfcMaterialLayerSet (Revit, Archicad) can't recover the wall type.
2. **PDF: rooms print as solid dark blocks.** In floorplan and sheet PDF exports every room comes out filled in the wall colour (#374151). `paintStyledGeometry` builds a path for zone outlines whose fill and stroke are both `none` but never ends it, so the next filled shape (a wall) paints that path too.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Load the two-bedroom template and give the walls an assembly preset (e.g. Exterior 2x6 — stucco).
2. Export IFC and read the walls' IfcMaterialLayerSet (IfcOpenShell or web-ifc): one `Core` layer per wall.
3. Export the floorplan PDF (or call `exportSheetsToPdf`): rooms are filled dark grey.

### Expected behavior

- IFC: one IfcMaterialLayer per assembly layer, with its material and thickness, and the exterior finish on the exterior side.
- PDF: a shape with no fill and no stroke draws nothing.

### Browser & OS

Reproduced headless with the packages at 599727d (Bun 1.4.2, Linux)

### Screenshots or screen recordings

_No response_

### Additional context

I'll open a PR with fixes and tests for both.

title: [Bugs] ifc-converter, editor: export wall assembly layers to IFC; unpainted PDF shapes no longer filled
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #1103. Related: #981 (IFC4 export).

**IFC — wall assembly layers** (`packages/ifc-converter/src/export/scene-to-ifc.ts`)
- A wall with an `assembly` now exports one `IfcMaterialLayer` per layer: an `IfcMaterial` named after the layer's material (falling back to its role), the layer thickness, the layer id as Name, the role as Description, and the IFC4 category (`LoadBearing` for the core, `Insulation`, `Finish`). `air` layers are marked ventilated.
- Layers run from the front face (+n), where the existing `AXIS2`/`POSITIVE` usage at `-faces.a` starts. A stack with `face: 'exterior'` whose exterior is the back face is reversed, so the exterior finish stays outward whichever way the wall was drawn.
- The layer set takes the preset label (e.g. `Exterior 2x6 — stucco`).
- Walls without an assembly, or whose layers don't sum to the body thickness, keep today's single `Core` layer. Usages are still shared per thickness/offset/stack.

**PDF — unpainted shapes** (`packages/editor/src/lib/floorplan/floorplan-pdfkit-renderer.ts`)
- `paintStyledGeometry` built a path for geometry with neither fill nor stroke (zone outlines) and never ended it, so the next fill (the walls) painted it as well and every room printed as a dark block. The path is now ended with `n`.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/ifc-converter/tests/export-wall-assembly.test.ts`: 3 new tests (layer stack and set name, one wall reversed so both orientations are covered, no-assembly fallback). Two of them fail on `main`.
2. `bun test packages/editor/src/lib/floorplan/floorplan-pdfkit-renderer.test.ts`: the new test fails on `main`.
3. The full `ifc-converter` suite passes (95 tests). I also opened the exported IFC (two-bedroom template with the `exterior-2x6-stucco` and `interior-2x4-drywall` presets) in IfcOpenShell 0.9: 0 schema issues, 4 and 3 layers per wall, and a geometric check that the stucco is on the outside of every exterior wall, with one wall reversed as well.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not a UI change. Before the PDF fix, a floorplan sheet of the two-bedroom template printed every room as a solid #374151 block; after it, rooms are blank with walls, dimensions and marks drawn as usual.

title: Elevations and sections in sheets, for residential construction documents
body:
### Problem or motivation

We're starting a residential architecture firm (custom homes) and evaluating Pascal for both design and documentation.

Pascal already covers a lot of a permit set: floor, foundation, reflected ceiling, roof and site plans, automatic dimension strings, door/window/room schedules, wall assemblies with layer poché, and multi-sheet PDF export with title blocks. What's missing for a residential construction set is **exterior/interior elevations and building/wall sections**. Every permit set we produce needs them, so today we'd have to export IFC and redraw those views in Revit or Archicad, which splits the documentation across two tools.

### Proposed solution

- New drawing types alongside `ConstructionDrawingType`: `exterior-elevation`, `interior-elevation`, `building-section`, `wall-section`.
- Views generated from the 3D model: a cut plane (sections) or view direction (elevations) with a depth range, cut elements drawn heavy with poché from their assembly layers, beyond elements drawn light.
- Level/datum lines with heights, opening marks matching the plan and schedules, material callouts taken from the assemblies (stucco, OSB, studs, drywall…).
- Section and elevation markers on plans that reference the sheet and view they land on.
- Placeable as sheet viewports at standard scales (1/4", 1/8", 3/4" = 1'-0" for wall sections). The `sheets` workspace mode is defined in the editor store but not used yet in the open-source editor; a sheet layout UI there would make this end to end.

### Alternatives considered

- IFC export, then elevations and sections in Revit, Archicad or Bonsai. It works for the model but means maintaining documents in a second tool.
- Screenshots of the 3D cut view. They aren't to scale and have no annotation, so they don't meet permit requirements.

### Additional context

Two smaller gaps we hit in the same test, in case they're useful:
- Room name/number tags don't appear on plan sheets; rooms only show up in the room schedule.
- No DXF/DWG export for structural and MEP consultants.

title: mcp + core: author_scene converts a whole three.js design into native, editable nodes
body:
## What does this PR do?

A frontier model writes a whole design as free three.js, richer than tool-by-tool building; `author_scene` then turns it into native, editable Pascal nodes in one MCP call. The agent reads its own module any way it likes and sends a payload: levels, walls as centerlines with openings (type, style, hinge, exact colours, or a module for a non-standard one), rooms with a seed point and a floor finish, slabs, columns, railings, every piece of furniture as an authored object with its own module, lights. Pascal compiles and stores the modules, derives rooms, floors and ceilings, paints, runs its checks and answers a gate report: `defects` by the agent's own ids, `warnings`, `defaults` (what Pascal filled in), `snapped` wall ends, an `ids` map, `verify_scene`. The module and the agent's adapter are kept with the scene. `replace: true` writes over a previous conversion with fresh ids.

Pascal fixes that came out of eight fresh-agent conversions (GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus, flats, a bedroom, a two-storey house, a living room from a photo):

- Finish scripts: a room's floor and a wall face can carry a module built for exactly that polygon or face, cut by Pascal to the region and its openings, rebuilt by the structure reconcile when the room or wall changes, and measured: the report warns when a finish leaves part of the floor or face bare. The native wall skirting is exposed in the payload.
- The compiler bakes the back face of double-sided materials (the viewer draws front faces only), so a curtain built as a plane shows.
- A new door's handle hangs opposite its hinges (`add_door` too); a slab lying on a wall's top is its cap, never its support; a wall's room side is read from the plan; a room-edge push keeps a painted wall's finishes and children.
- `verify_scene` reads hosted items through their host, lets stacked things stack, and keeps a door's keep-out to its swing side.
- An authored object's glass stays Pascal's glass; exact slot colours keep the module's roughness and metalness; a light with no fixture becomes a ceiling point in its room; a wall-hosted item keeps its distance from the face.
- A preview colour for every textured library material.

The tool is MCP-first: it is not in `AGENT_TOOL_CONTRACTS` until the chat can run it; the private app registers it with the hosted effects.

## How to test

1. `bun test` in `packages/core`, `packages/mcp`, `packages/geometry-script`, `packages/nodes`, `packages/editor` and `packages/viewer/src/systems/wall`: all green on this branch.
2. `packages/mcp/src/tools/author-scene.test.ts` runs the whole thing through a real MCP client and the real compiler: a bedroom payload with a scripted window, a glass door, a baseboard on a wall, a plank floor module laid past the room edge, a tile face module laid over a window, sage on one wall face; it reads the nodes back with `get_node` and `get_source`. Expect the room written, the floor and face builds cut to their regions, the glass slot on `library:preset-glass`, and a `finish_gaps` warning on the floor module that leaves a strip bare.
3. Against a running server (the private app with `PASCAL_SERVER_SCRIPT_COMPILE=1`, or a local editor with a script host): call `author_scene` with `bench`-style payload of four walls, a door, a window, a `floorCode` and a `wallCode`; open the project; expect walls, openings, a room with the scripted floor, tiled faces, skirting; move a wall and expect the floor and face scripts to rebuild. The eight converted projects on the owner's :3008 are the reference.
4. `bun run check-types`: two errors remain in `packages/editor/src/components/systems/ceiling/ceiling-bracket-batch.test.ts`, unchanged since the base commit (deps refresh #1037), not from this branch.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet. (Pictures of the converted scenes beside the raw three.js renders are in the private repo's `bench/author-scene/briefs/`.)

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` (through the private community app on :3008 against these packages, eight agent conversions end to end)
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> **Medium Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`author_scene`**, a one-shot path from an agent’s three.js design payload to native scene nodes: walls (join snapping, openings, skirting, paint), rooms/zones, slabs, items, lights, materials, structure reconcile, and a detailed report (`defects`, `warnings`, `defaults`, stable `ids`). title: Preserve authored scenes through conversion and level verification
body:
## What does this PR do?

Combine the author_scene converter from #1107 with the retained-design and level exploration work. Re-conversion now keeps stable node IDs, preserves unrelated/manual changes and rejects overlapping edits. All scripted geometry and room finishes compile before one scene commit, shared by MCP and chat hosts.

Preserve room cameras alongside explicit Solo and Exploded presentation so roof separation and interior verification remain observable. Hosts using the evidence-led design workflow own their brief policy; existing MCP sessions retain their brief behavior.

## How to test

1. Convert a fixture, move one authored item manually, add another, and convert again. The manual changes survive; a conflicting authored move is refused without a scene mutation.
2. Repeat conversion and verify node IDs and room boundaries remain stable. A populated scene with no conversion baseline is refused.
3. Capture Solo and Exploded views, including a room camera.

Validation: 82 targeted converter/MCP/view tests pass; core, geometry-script, MCP and editor TypeScript builds pass. Full upstream CI runs on this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Targeted tests and package TypeScript builds pass
- [x] This PR targets main
- [ ] Full upstream CI passes

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large changes to destructive `author_scene` merging and scene commits, plus roof-level and view-capture behavior; mitigated by conflict refusal and extensive tests but still core agent editing paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`author_scene` is now an incremental, building-scoped conversion** instead of wiping and reminting levels. Stable payload-keyed node IDs and `authorSceneState` on the building support **`replace: true` deltas** that merge against the last candidate via **`authoredSceneChanges`**, keeping manual moves/adds/deletes and refusing overlapping edits; first-time conversion refuses buildings that already have native work without a baseline, and copied buildings cannot hijack another building’s conversion.
> 
> **Hosts share one compile-then-commit path**: `@pascal-app/geometry-script/author-scene`’s **`compileAuthorScene`** builds the full candidate (items, openings, floor/wall finishes) before **`finalizeAuthorScene`** applies a single patch set; MCP adds **abort/`assertActive`**, a **scene-changed** guard, optional **`buildingId`**, and re-registers **`author_scene`** in the tool list.
> 
> **Retained authored roof/ceiling items** (`metadata.role`) are treated as geometry for roof-level rules, verification counts, interior/view hiding, clipboard paste, and capture framing—not ordinary storey furniture.
> 
> **`view_scene`** gains optional **stacked / exploded / solo** presentation (with renderer confirmation), editor capture applies it, and bounds framing respects exploded vertical gap.
> 
> **Site** can persist **`presentation`** (lighting, exposure, edges, etc.) and **`showGround`**; ceilings and imported GLTF items keep authored PBR/unlit appearance more faithfully; **`authorSceneTool`** is exported for MCP.

title: [Discovery] Sync agent integration versions + add MCP Registry server.json
body:
## What does this PR do? Agent integrations now take their versions from the package versions instead of hardcoding them, and `server.json` is ready for the official MCP Registry under a reverse-DNS name. Nothing publishes automatically. - **One source of truth.** `scripts/sync-agent-versions.ts` rewrites every `@pascal-app/cli@` quote (both Cursor `mcp.json` configs and the three setup docs) from `packages/cli/package.json`, and the `server.json` version from `packages/mcp/package.json`. `--check` runs in `bun run skills:validate`, so CI fails on drift. `scripts/cursor-plugin-policy.ts` reads the expected pin from the CLI package instead of hardcoding `1.0.0`. The pin moves from `1.0.0` to the published `1.0.4`. - **Betas keep the last stable version.** A `beta` release commits to `main`, so a naive sync would pin Cursor marketplace installs and `server.json` to a prerelease. While the packages are on a prerelease, the sync leaves integrations alone, and the Cursor policy and the registry workflow accept the last stable pin, which must still be an exact stable version. - **`server.json`** (schema `2025-12-11`, the current one) is renamed from `io.github.pascalorg/editor` to `app.pascal/editor`. It lists the npm package `@pascal-app/mcp` (stdio, `npx`) next to the remote `https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp` (`streamable-http`), and its version is the package version, `1.0.4`. I removed the remote's required `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_…` header: the endpoint advertises OAuth through its 401 `WWW-Authenticate: … resource_metadata=…` challenge, and the Cursor plugin already uses OAuth only. API keys still work as a bearer token. `packages/mcp/package.json` gains `"mcpName": "app.pascal/editor"`, which the registry needs to verify npm ownership. - **Release/CI.** In the bump step, `release.yml` runs the sync after `bun install` (before any publish), so the release commit's `git add -A` carries the new pin and manifest. It then runs `mcp-publisher validate`. There is no registry publish step. On PRs, `mcp-registry.yml` also checks `server.json` against `packages/mcp/package.json` (version, `mcpName`, package entry) and checks that the endpoint returns the OAuth challenge. The live API-catalog and server-card checks are in a separate `hosted-matches-manifest` job gated on `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'`, so it is skipped on PRs and pushes and cannot block PR CI. It is the gate to run by hand before publishing. - **Docs.** `wiki/npm-release.md` has a new MCP Registry section with the manual publish steps (DNS or HTTP auth for `pascal.app`, `mcp-publisher publish`). `README.md` and `skills/README.md` are updated to match. ### Publishing audit Only `release.yml` publishes (npm, GitHub release asset, GHCR image), and it is `workflow_dispatch`-only, as before. `ci.yml`, `mcp-ci.yml`, `docker.yml` (builds without pushing) and `mcp-registry.yml` publish nothing. Nothing in this repo runs `mcp-publisher publish`. ### Outside this repo - **Hosted card and catalog (`pascalorg/private-editor`).** Done in private-editor #1119 and deployed. `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` reports `serverInfo.version: "1.0.4"`, and `/.well-known/api-catalog` reports `app.pascal/editor` `1.0.4`. title: Resolve hosted roof support and refuse ambiguous conversion identities
body:
A hosted `create_roof` call failed because roof elevation read the browser scene store through the spatial-grid singleton. Resolve wall support and wall tops from the supplied scene graph so the same operation works on the server and in the editor, including raised slabs and support offsets.

A conversion that reused source identifiers across floors could overwrite its candidate nodes and fail with a missing-parent patch. Reject duplicate wall, item, opening and generated mapping keys before any compilation or scene change, with the conflicting ID in the refusal.

Validation: 71 focused core conversion/roof tests and the MCP author_scene/construction suites passed; the core, geometry-script and MCP packages rebuilt. Regression cases cover an unavailable browser store, repeated storey IDs and collisions with generated source mappings. The by-hand alternative remains normal roof placement and scene-tree editing.

title: [Discovery] CLI: pascal architect run/status/cancel
body:
## What does this PR do? Adds three commands to `@pascal-app/cli`. Together they form a thin client over Pascal's hosted OpenAI-compatible Responses API (`https://editor.pascal.app/api/v1/responses`), authenticated with the agent's `PASCAL_API_KEY`: - `pascal architect run ""` creates a background run (`background: true`, `store: true`) and streams it over SSE while you stay attached. Text deltas go to stdout and progress goes to stderr. Ctrl+C detaches without cancelling (exit 130). `--detach` queues the run and returns its ID straight away. - `--effort low|medium|high|pro` selects the `architect-` model. Without it, the run uses `architect`. - `--project ` is sent as `metadata.project_id`. - `--max-credits ` is sent as `metadata.pascal_max_credits`. - `--json` prints a stable run object (`schemaVersion: 1`). - `pascal architect status ` calls `GET /responses/{id}`. - `pascal architect cancel ` calls `POST /responses/{id}/cancel`. **Errors.** A `503` with `executor_unavailable`, sent either as an HTTP error or as an SSE `error` event, becomes `architect_executor_unavailable`, with a message saying no run was started. That error exits with `75` (EX_TEMPFAIL); so do 429 and other 503s, so scripts can tell when retrying will help. `401` and `403` point you to `pascal agent status`. The CLI never echoes the key or the server's HTTP error bodies, and it strips control sequences from server text before printing it. **Shared code.** `agent-account.ts` now exports `requireAgentApiKey`, used by both the agent and architect commands. **Docs.** Only the CLI README changed, per the docs owner. It says the commands ship in the next `@pascal-app/cli` release after 1.0.5 and gives no credit estimates. ## How to test 1. `cd packages/cli && bun test src` should report 137 passing tests, including the new `architect.test.ts` and the CLI process tests in `cli.test.ts`. 2. `bun run build`, then `node dist/bin/pascal.js architect --help` should print the architect usage. 3. `node dist/bin/pascal.js architect run "x" --effort max` should fail with `invalid_option` and exit 2. 4. `PASCAL_API_KEY=sk_test_fake node dist/bin/pascal.js architect status resp_probe --json` should return `architect_unauthorized` (HTTP 401) from the live endpoint. 5. With a real agent key: `pascal architect run "A small cabin" --effort low` should stream output; press Ctrl+C, then `pascal architect status `. Ran after rebasing onto main (CLI 1.0.5): `bun run check-types` and `bun run build` in `packages/cli`, `bun test src` (137 pass), and the repo-level `bun run check` (passes with warnings only). Step 3 was run by hand. Step 5 was **not** run, because no real agent key was available. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: Fix node dragging and refine pillars, elevators, and roofs
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes node placement, movement, and resize interactions and refines pillar, elevator, and roof editing on this branch:

- Keeps handle previews in live overrides and fixes hosted opening/accessory movement, snapping, and selection cleanup.
- Adds lower-polygon pillar geometry, consistent bounds and floor-plan representation, paint coverage, property previews, and a single thumbnail preset gallery with a white default material.
- Routes elevator placement and movement through the registry, hardens service/runtime and opening synchronization, adds inspection controls, and recesses sliding doors behind stationary entrance surrounds so they no longer overlap the buttons.
- Corrects roof surface queries and accessory cache invalidation, aligns editing limits, moves trim editing into transient interaction scope, and preserves the previous mesh when geometry rebuilding fails with an explicit retry action.
- Adds WebP preset thumbnails, a four-column roof menu with grayscale-to-color hover, and ghosts matching all nine roof forms. Roof thumbnails are bundled with nodes; geometry failures use a generic viewer API, and Escape in text fields preserves trim mode.

The elevator movement review finding is addressed through the optional registry
`movable.resolvePosition` hook: the 3D and 2D movers resolve landing height after
snapping and again at commit. Regression coverage checks an elevator crossing a
raised slab in both directions and a mounted mover whose support changes between
preview and drop. One undo still restores the gesture.

## How to test

1. Run the editor locally. Place pillars from several presets, change their shape and dimensions, paint their surfaces, and switch between 2D and 3D. Confirm the preset matches its preview, the default material is white, and movement/resizing can be undone without flicker.
2. Place an elevator across multiple levels. Request stops, disable a stop, adjust dimensions, and open/close its doors. Confirm openings follow the shaft and door panels remain recessed behind the entrance surround and buttons.
3. Choose each roof type and draw it. Confirm the ghost matches the selected form, all nine thumbnails render, and the left menu has four columns with grayscale images that regain color on hover.
4. Select a roof segment, enter footprint trimming, and adjust it. Press Escape inside a numeric field: the field cancels without exiting trim mode. Press Escape over the canvas: trim mode exits. Check undo/redo and dimensions in both views.
5. Automated checks run on the final branch: `bun run check-types` (13 tasks passed), `bun run check` (passed with warnings), and `bun test packages/editor/src/components/systems/roof/roof-edit-system.test.tsx packages/nodes/src/roof-segment/renderer.test.tsx packages/nodes/src/roof/type-thumbnail.test.tsx` (4 tests passed). title: core, mcp: Studio renders — view ids, quotes, previews
body:
## What does this PR do?

The shared contracts that let an agent render images and videos of the project through Pascal's Studio, from the hosted chat and over the MCP, quoted before it spends credits.

- **`view_scene` names its frame.** `SceneViewCapture.viewId` (optional): a host that keeps the picture it captured answers its id, these exact pixels, so a later call can name that frame instead of taking the view again. The tool stays read-only.
- **`generate_studio_media` quotes first.** `pluginId` is optional (omitted: the person in Pascal's own Studio). A call without `quoteToken` answers a quote (model, settings, sources, exact credits) and charges nothing; the same input with the quote's `quoteToken` submits, and `confirm: false` submits at once within `maxCredits`. Sources take a view (`{ type: 'view', id: viewId }`). `generationKey` makes a retry return the render already created. `idempotentHint` is now true.
- **`get_studio_generation includePreview`.** A finished image's WebP preview comes back inline; the MCP registration turns it into an image block beside the job's JSON.

The host implementations (storage, pricing, quotes, spending rules) live in the hosted app.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/view-scene.test.ts packages/mcp/src/tools/hosted-services.test.ts` → 49 pass: a host's `viewId` reaches the answer; a quote is text alone; a submission carries its key and token; a render's preview becomes an image block and leaves the JSON.
2. Hosted end to end (with the private host): a chat turn looks at a room with `view_scene`, quotes `generate_studio_media` with its `viewId`, and a click submits it; over the MCP with an API key, `list_pascal_services` → quote → submit → `get_studio_generation { includePreview: true }` returns the image.

title: Add connected duct and pipe editing with shared build controls
body:
## What does this PR do?

Add remembered duct and pipe build settings for profiles, materials, routing elevations and crossing behavior, with nonblocking connection feedback shared by 2D and 3D. Duct editing supports connected resizing, transitions, offsets and registered equipment/terminal collars. Pipe editing adds grade and downhill flow, grade-preserving endpoint edits, connected resizing with reducers, offsets and registered fixture/trap collars.

The same edit operations power the inspectors and five agent tools, with atomic undo and refusals for incompatible connections or insufficient fitting space. Profile math is separated from rendering so agent operations remain headless; agent contracts advance to revision 1.1.0, and inspector drafts refresh after committed edits or undo. Offsets are geometric routing and do not validate obstacle clearance or drainage compliance. Catalog objects need authored ports to connect.

## How to test

1. Draw ducts and pipes in both 2D and 3D. Change profile/material settings, horizontal or vertical routing, and elevations; switch tools and confirm settings persist. Compare connect versus cross-without-joining on same-height crossings, and confirm different-height crossings stay separate.
2. Resize connected duct and pipe branches, add offsets, and connect registered collars. Confirm reducers/transitions join the boundary collars, occupied or incompatible collars refuse cleanly, and undo restores the entire edit.
3. Set pipe grade and downhill flow, then move endpoints in both views. Confirm grades and connected collars remain preserved. Edit or undo the selected run and confirm its inspector fields refresh.
4. Automated validation completed: `bun test packages/nodes/src` (5,082 passed, one skipped), `bun run check-types` (13 tasks successful), Biome checks on all 38 review-fix files, and `git diff --check`. The pre-push hook also passed repository-wide lint with warnings and repeated the type checks. The earlier shared-distribution run tests also passed. A headless bundle regression test rejects editor/viewer dependencies in agent operations.

Manual checks covered connection and crossing cases in both views, including tees, size transitions, vertical equipment collars, undo, occupied collars and invalid-connection refusals.

title: [Bugs] viewer, nodes: pointer moves no longer throw on a wall mid paint preview
body:
## What does this PR do? Fixes MONOREPO-EDITOR-131 and MONOREPO-EDITOR-132 (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'side')` from `pointer-events.js:368` on pointer move). Both Sentry stacks crash on the **stock fallback** branch of the vendored pointer manager (`layer.raycaster.intersectObject(obj, true)`), not the cached collector. #1091 guarded the elevator click raycast and the cached collector, but once an event falls back to three's own recursion (any untagged custom raycast in the scene), a wall whose geometry groups point past its material array still throws. - **Source (`nodes`)**: `applyWallPreview` regrouped the geometry and swapped the material through two independent restores. A rebuild during the preview put the older, shorter palette back over the new geometry's groups. `swapPreviewMaterial` now takes the groups along with the material and swaps them as one pair. On undo it puts back only what is still the preview's, and restores the original material only over groups it can draw. The other paint previews (material-only) get the same "never restore a palette over groups it can't draw" rule. - **Guard (`viewer`)**: the stock path now uses `intersectDrawable`, which mirrors three's recursive `intersectObject` but skips meshes `hasMaterialsForGroups` rejects (their children are still tested). Raycasters with their own `intersectObject` are still asked directly. - **Breadcrumb**: every skip (cached or stock) is reported once per mesh and material as a `raycast_invalid_material` breadcrumb `{ category, message, level: 'warning', data: { nodeType, nodeId, objectName } }`. It reaches the host through the new `` prop, forwarded as ``. The public packages carry no Sentry SDK, so the hosted app needs to wire it, e.g. `onViewerBreadcrumb={(b) => Sentry.addBreadcrumb(b)}`. - **Test**: the #1091 elevator regression test now drives real pointer moves through `createPascalPointerEvents` over the same torn wall, on both the cached and stock paths. It asserts no throw, that the hover target behind the wall still gets `onPointerMove`, and that exactly one breadcrumb is recorded with `nodeType: 'wall'` and the node id. With the old stock call put back, the stock case fails with `material.side`. ## How to test 1. `bun test packages/viewer/src/systems/elevator packages/viewer/src/lib/pointer-events.test.ts` (after `bun run build`): all pass. 2. `bun test packages/nodes/src/shared/swap-preview-material.test.ts`: the groups and material undo as a pair, and a rebuilt geometry keeps the preview palette instead of getting the shorter original. 3. In the editor, open the paint tool and hover a room-wide wall finish across several walls while clicking to commit. Moving the pointer no longer throws. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A: non-visual change. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Deps] mcp: MCP SDK v2 (2.2.0); stdio serves protocol 2026-07-28
body:
## What does this PR do? Moves `@pascal-app/mcp`, `@pascal-app/cli` and `@pascal-app/nodes` (tests only) from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` ^1.32.1 to the v2 SDK line at [2.2.0](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/v2.2.0). The stdio server now answers clients on protocol 2026-07-28 as well as 2025 clients. v2 has no `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 2.x: the package is split. So the manifests now declare the split packages. | Package | Where | Locked | |---|---|---| | `@modelcontextprotocol/server` | mcp (dep), cli (dep), nodes (dev) | 2.2.0 | | `@modelcontextprotocol/client` | cli (dep), mcp (dev), nodes (dev) | 2.2.0 | | `@modelcontextprotocol/node` (Node Streamable HTTP transport) | mcp (dep) | 2.1.0, the release paired with 2.2.0. 2.1.1 requires server ^2.3.0 | The ranges are `^2.2.0` / `^2.1.0` and `bun.lock` pins 2.2.0. 2.3.1 is out; the full mcp suite also passes on 2.3.1. Upgrading to it is left to a later bump. ### v1 behaviour against a 2026-07-28 client (tested before the upgrade) I built `main`'s server (SDK 1.32.1) and spawned `dist/bin/pascal-mcp.js --stdio`. Then I connected `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.2.0 over real stdio: | Client | v1 server (before) | This PR | |---|---|---| | Default (2025 `initialize`) | ✅ legacy, 2025-11-25, 86 tools | ✅ legacy, 2025-11-25, 86 tools | | `versionNegotiation: { mode: 'auto' }` | ⚠️ falls back to legacy, 2025-11-25 | ✅ **modern, 2026-07-28** | | `versionNegotiation: { mode: { pin: '2026-07-28' } }` | ❌ `SdkError ERA_NEGOTIATION_FAILED`: "the server did not offer pinned protocol version 2026-07-28 via server/discover (no fallback in pin mode)" | ✅ **modern, 2026-07-28** | | Raw `server/discover` carrying the 2026-07-28 `_meta` envelope | ❌ `{"code":-32601,"message":"Method not found"}` | ✅ `DiscoverResult` with `supportedVersions: ["2026-07-28"]` | So on v1, a 2026-07-28-only client could not use Pascal at all. A negotiating client fell back to 2025. ### Changes - **stdio → `serveStdio(createServer)`.** `connectStdio` takes the server factory and hands it to `serveStdio` from `@modelcontextprotocol/server/stdio`. This follows the corrected quickstart ([modelcontextprotocol@3778656](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/commit/3778656b2e0ba6725035e816fe3085374cbaa736)). The bin passes its existing `createServer`, which builds a fresh bridge and server each call. That matters because the factory is called twice on a probe followed by a fallback. - **HTTP: Node transport rename only; it still serves the 2025 sessionful protocol.** `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` becomes `NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport` (`@modelcontextprotocol/node`). On HTTP, the SDK serves 2026-07-28 through `createMcpHandler`, which builds one server per *request*. Every Pascal server owns its own `SceneBridge`, so a 2026-07-28 HTTP client would lose its scene between calls. Over HTTP, a negotiating client falls back to 2025 and a pinned client is refused; both cases are now tested and documented in `http.ts`. The CLI's `pascal mcp connect` pipes stdio into this HTTP service, so it has the same reach. - **`expectedIssuer`: nothing to set.** No code here constructs `ClientCredentialsProvider`, `PrivateKeyJwtProvider`, `StaticPrivateKeyJwtProvider`, `CrossAppAccessProvider` or any `OAuthClientProvider`. The CLI connector sends a static bearer token header. - **Codemod plus manual fixes.** I used the official `@modelcontextprotocol/codemod@2.2.0 v1-to-v2`, then fixed what it marked: - Raw Zod shapes are wrapped in `z.object()` from our own zod. - `McpError`/`ErrorCode` become `ProtocolError`/`ProtocolErrorCode`, with no alias kept. - Tool callbacks read `ctx.mcpReq.signal`. - The wrapper for `McpServer.tool()` is dropped, because v2 removed `tool()`. - The dead strip of the `MCP error -N:` prefix is removed; v2 messages don't carry it. - The private `tools/list` and `tools/call` handler hooks are checked against v2's `Protocol` (same `_requestHandlers` map, same `(request, ctx)` signature). ### Breaking-change notes - **Dependencies:** consumers that imported SDK classes alongside `@pascal-app/mcp` need `@modelcontextprotocol/server` / `@modelcontextprotocol/client` instead of `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. v1 and v2 classes don't cross: `instanceof` fails between them. The README and `examples/embed-in-agent.ts` now import `Client`/`InMemoryTransport` from `@modelcontextprotocol/client`. - **Node 20+ and zod ≥ 4.2** are required by v2. The repo already declares Node ≥ 22 and zod `>=4.6.7 <4.7`. - **Unknown tool name:** `tools/call` for a name no server has is now a JSON-RPC `-32602` error ("Tool X not found"), not an `isError: true` result. Retired tool names still answer `tool_retired` as before. - **`tools/list` wire output, compared byte for byte against v1** (2025 handshake, raw JSON-RPC): - Unchanged: names, order, titles, descriptions, **annotations**, capabilities, instructions, resources, resource templates and prompts. - Every `inputSchema` is semantically identical; only `$schema`/`type` key order changed. - `execution: {"taskSupport":"forbidden"}` is no longer emitted, because v2 removed the experimental tasks feature. - `measure_stair` and `fit_stair` output schemas use `$defs` instead of `definitions`, the 2020-12 keyword matching the `$schema` they already declare. - On a 2026-07-28 connection, the tool names, titles, descriptions and annotation values are the same. - **Not touched:** tool annotations and the registry `server.json`. The annotations are neither in the diff nor different on the wire. `server.json` declares no protocol version and needs no change. - Internal `connectStdio(server)` is now `connectStdio(createServer)` and returns the SDK's `StdioServerHandle`. `transports/*` is not in the package `exports`. ## How to test 1. `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run --cwd packages/mcp test`: 1264 pass. The new handshake tests are in `src/transports/stdio.test.ts`: - In process, through `connectStdio` with an injected transport: an older client, an auto-negotiating client and a client pinned to 2026-07-28 all list and call tools. A 2026-07-28 connection keeps one scene across calls. A server wired to the transport by hand fails the pinned client. - Over real stdio: the same three clients connect to `bun src/bin/pascal-mcp.ts --stdio`. 2. `src/transports/http.test.ts` pins the HTTP behaviour: a negotiating client falls back to 2025, and a pinned client gets `ERA_NEGOTIATION_FAILED`. 3. Optional manual check: `bun run --cwd packages/mcp build`, then `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli node packages/mcp/dist/bin/pascal-mcp.js --method tools/list`, with and without a modern-era client. Run locally on the rebased head (after #1117), with bun 1.4.2: - Passed: `bun run check`, `bun run skills:validate`, `bun run check-types` (13/13), `bun run build`, `smoke:node`, the cli-smoke job's steps (editor portable build, stage-runtime, smoke-runtime: "Packed CLI smoke passed (1.8 MB compressed …)"), the mcp tests and the cli tests. - `@pascal-app/nodes` has 22 local failures (column, registry-move and plan tests). The identical set fails on `main` in this environment, and `kitchen-tools.test.ts`, the nodes test that uses the SDK, passes. CI on this PR is the reference. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A: non-visual change. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches the MCP wire protocol, stdio negotiation, and broad tool-server wiring; regressions could break CLI/MCP clients or tool calls even though tests and smoke paths were updated. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9fb8ecc1c203bd3fb48ad4dedf2947042c05690e. title: [Deps] mcp: MCP SDK 2.3.1 and @hono/node-server 1.19.17 (security)
body:
## What does this PR do? Security dependency fix. [#1118](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1118) moved to MCP SDK v2 at 2.2.0, which is inside the affected range `>=2.0.0 <2.3.0` of these advisories (all fixed in 2.3.0): | Advisory | Severity | Package | |---|---|---| | [GHSA-jm63-cq47-j5jp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jm63-cq47-j5jp): shared transport/server instances delivered one HTTP client's messages to another | high | `@modelcontextprotocol/server` | | [GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453) | high | `@modelcontextprotocol/server` | | [GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq): bearer auth | moderate | `@modelcontextprotocol/server` | | [GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw) | moderate | `@modelcontextprotocol/client` | | [GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9) (fixed in 1.19.15) | — | `@hono/node-server` (via `@modelcontextprotocol/node`) | Changes: - `@modelcontextprotocol/server` and `@modelcontextprotocol/client` `^2.2.0` → `^2.3.1` in `packages/cli`, `packages/mcp` and `packages/nodes`. The lock now resolves server, client and core at **2.3.1**. - `@modelcontextprotocol/node` `^2.1.0` → `^2.1.1` in `packages/mcp`, to match its `server ^2.3.0` peer. - Root `overrides`: `"@hono/node-server": "^1.19.15"`. The lock now resolves **1.19.17**. `@modelcontextprotocol/node` 2.1.1 still declares `^1.19.9`, so the override is what keeps the floor above the vulnerable range. It sits next to the existing `hono` override. - `bun.lock` refreshed. No other packages moved. After the refresh, the lock no longer contains `@modelcontextprotocol/{server,client,core}@2.2.x` or `@hono/node-server@1.19.14`. No app code changes were needed. The breaking change in 2.3.0 is that one `Server`/`McpServer` now serves one connection, and a stateless HTTP transport serves one request. Pascal already meets that rule: - `connectHttp` builds a new server and a sessionful transport for each session. - stdio uses `serveStdio(factory)`. - Each test builds its own server on in-memory transports. The 2.3.0 change to client redirects (same-origin only) doesn't affect `pascal`'s `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` connector, which talks to a fixed URL. ## How to test 1. `bun install`, then `rg '@modelcontextprotocol/(server|client|core)@|@hono/node-server@' bun.lock`. You should see 2.3.1 and 1.19.17 only. 2. `bun run --filter @pascal-app/mcp test` and `bun run --filter @pascal-app/cli test`. These include the HTTP transport tests with two concurrent sessions and the stdio transport tests. Run locally: `bun run check`, `skills:validate`, `check-types` and `build` all pass. The `mcp` suite passes 1264/0, `cli` 107/0 and `core` 5414/0. The `nodes` suite fails 22 viewer/selection tests in this environment, and it fails the same 22 on `main` with the old 2.2.0 lock, so those failures were already there. Separately, `main`'s own CI has been red since [#903](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/903), with 5 `verify_scene` / scene-verification failures in `core`. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Bugs] core, nodes: tests no longer leak registry and store state across files
body:
## What does this PR do? Fixes the `quality` job on `main`, which has been red since #903. It also fixes 22 order-dependent `nodes` tests. **Root cause on CI (core, 5 `verify_scene` tests).** Bun runs all of a package's test files in one process, in filesystem enumeration order. That order differs between machines and changes when a file is added. `verify_scene` looks up a kind's schema in the node registry before falling back to core's own schemas. `services/drag-session.test.ts` and `services/alignment-anchors.test.ts` register a stub `wall` kind with schema `z.object({ type: z.literal('wall') })` and never restore the registry. So when those files run before `agent-operations/operations.test.ts`, malformed walls pass validation: `start: null`, or a pool retyped as `wall`. On the last green run, `hosting.test.ts` happened to run in between, and its `beforeEach` wiped the registry by accident. #903 changed no logic involved here. It only added a test file, which reordered the runner's file list so nothing cleaned up before `operations.test.ts`. Running core in CI's exact 336-file order reproduces exactly those 5 failures locally. **Changes** - **core:** add a test preload (`packages/core/test-setup.ts`) that snapshots `nodeRegistry` before each test and restores it after. Preload hooks wrap each file's own hooks, so registrations made inside a test or its `beforeEach` (including after a `_reset()`) end with that test. Stub registrations made at file scope (top level or `beforeAll`), which a per-test hook can't reach, now restore in `afterAll`: `validate-dwv`, `system-graph`, `port-connectivity`, `stair-surface-snap` and `procedural-items/mutations`. - **nodes, the 22 failures:** `wall-batch-system.test.ts` set `useViewer`'s `selection.selectedIds` and `previewSelectedIds` to `Set`s. The store holds arrays. It never restored them, so later stair, column and floor-plan tests threw on `.includes`. The test now uses arrays and restores the viewer state it started with. - **nodes, leaks found while verifying:** - The stair paint test now loads the built-in plugin itself instead of relying on an earlier test in its file. - `cabinet/hosting` and `shelf-hosting` start a mounted move session that writes the placement preview and alignment guides, and never commit or cancel it. They now clear both in `afterEach`. Leftover guides made a later stair tool mount render DOM labels. - Six hosting tests restored `document` by assignment, which left an own `document: undefined` property instead of removing it. They now restore by property descriptor, the way they already restore `window`. - **nodes guardrail:** a test preload (`packages/nodes/test-setup.ts`) snapshots and restores, around every test, the node registry and the `useScene`, `useLiveNodeOverrides`, `useLiveTransforms`, `useViewer`, `useEditor`, `usePlacementPreview` and `useAlignmentGuides` stores (the built `@pascal-app/*` instances). No timeouts were raised and no tests were skipped. **Not done: a random-order CI step.** `bun test --randomize` still finds a few latent dependencies unrelated to these fixes, so as a required gate it would flake today: - a test-to-test dependency inside `core/src/lib/structure-kernel.test.ts` (seed 12); - the core `spatialGridManager` singleton in nodes `frame-pipeline.test.tsx` (seed 6). The per-test reset preloads are the guardrail in this PR. ## How to test 1. `bunx turbo run build --filter=@pascal-app/nodes...`, so core's and nodes' self-imports resolve to `dist`. 2. In `packages/core`, run `bun test ./src/services/drag-session.test.ts ./src/agent-operations/operations.test.ts`. On `main` this reports the same 5 failures as CI; on this branch it reports 0 failures. 3. In `packages/core`, run `bun test src`. Expected: 5414 pass, 0 fail. Under `--randomize`, seeds 1, 2, 3, 11, 13 and 14 also pass. 4. In `packages/nodes`, run `bun test`. On `main`: 22 failures. On this branch: 5021 pass, 0 fail. Under `--randomize`, seeds 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 also pass. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change (tests only). ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Bugs] mcp, editor: harden image URL fetching and login redirect
body:
## What does this PR do? Two security hardening fixes. **`mcp`: `safeFetch` (used by `analyze_floorplan_image`, `analyze_room_photo`, `photo_to_scene`)** - Resolves the host of every hop (initial URL and each redirect) with `dns.lookup({ all: true })` and requires every resolved address to be public. - Classifies addresses after normalising all IPv4/IPv6 text forms, judging IPv6 forms that embed an IPv4 address by the embedded address. The blocked set now also covers CGNAT `100.64.0.0/10`, NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96`, and a few other special-use ranges. - Connects only to the addresses that were checked, through a pinned socket `lookup`. Requests go through `node:http`/`node:https` instead of global `fetch`, which works the same under Node and Bun. - Logs a `[pascal-mcp] safe_fetch_blocked {...}` line to stderr whenever a fetch is refused by policy (scheme, host/address, or origin allowlist). - The network boundary (`resolve`, `request`) is an optional third argument so tests can cover redirects and DNS changes without real network access. Callers are unchanged. **`apps/editor`: post-login `next` redirect** - `safeNextPath` moved to `lib/safe-next-path.ts`. It now parses `next` against the app's public origin, requires the same origin, and returns the normalised path, falling back to `/` otherwise. ## How to test 1. `bun test packages/mcp/src/lib/safe-fetch.test.ts`: covers the address classifier for every range and encoding, DNS answers containing any private address, rechecks on redirects, connection pinning (including one real socket test), size caps, and the block log. 2. `cd apps/editor && bun test lib/safe-next-path.test.ts`: same-origin paths are kept and anything else falls back to `/`. 3. `bun run ci` passes locally. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A, non-visual change. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: Refine roof accessories, build search, and HVAC connections
body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes build tools searchable by common names, strengthens HVAC port compatibility and connected movement, and refines roof-accessory models, inspectors, and placement. Covers box/ridge/turbine/eyebrow vents, cupolas, chimneys, solar panels, skylights, dormers, gutters, downspouts, and canopies. Adds small WebP style thumbnails and documents their generation prompts.

Placement validates roof footprints and preserves host relationships; related geometry and placement tests cover the changed behavior. Architecture follow-ups isolate accessory previews on the editor layer, stabilize box-vent inspector callbacks, and inject the scene API into the rewritten placement tools.

The visual follow-up adds theme-aware rendered finishes, smooth shading across shallow curved facets, and refined solar cell artwork without increasing triangle counts. Paint now works independently on skylight glass/frame, solar face/frame, HVAC parts, and refrigerant lines; ridge-vent slot paint also survives reload. Existing dimensions and placements remain unchanged. Optional material slots are written only when painting previously unsupported kinds.

title: [Discovery] Add workflow to deprecate legacy io.github.pascalorg/editor registry entry
body:
## What does this PR do? Adds `.github/workflows/mcp-registry-deprecate-legacy.yml`, which can only be run manually (`workflow_dispatch`). It installs `mcp-publisher` v1.8.1, checks its SHA-256 against the release's published `registry_1.8.1_checksums.txt` (the same pin `mcp-registry.yml` uses), and logs in with `github-oidc`. It then runs: ``` mcp-publisher status --status --message "Superseded by app.pascal/editor" --all-versions --yes io.github.pascalorg/editor ``` The goal is to free the remote URL `https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp` so that `app.pascal/editor` can be published. The `status` input can be `deleted` (the default) or `deprecated`. Upstream's duplicate-remote-URL check (`validateNoDuplicateRemoteURLs` with `status != 'deleted'` in `internal/database/postgres.go`) only skips deleted entries, so only `deleted` frees the URL. The command uses `--all-versions` instead of pinning `0.6.1`, and `--yes` because bulk updates prompt for confirmation. ## How to test 1. After merge, run the workflow from the Actions tab with `status: deleted`. 2. Check that https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=io.github.pascalorg/editor no longer lists the entry, and that publishing `app.pascal/editor` with the same remote URL succeeds. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [ ] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: editor: download snapshots and complete capture feedback
body: ## What does this PR do? In the standalone editor, clicking the snapshot shutter captured an image but only uploaded it as the project's thumbnail. The host never emitted `snapshot:saved`, leaving the overlay on “Capturing…” without exporting a file. Download user snapshots with a project-based filename and the image's actual extension, then acknowledge completion so the overlay shows “Saved” and exits. Keep automatic thumbnail uploads on their existing path. Correlate shutter requests with save/failure events so unrelated captures cannot complete the overlay, and show capture/download failures while enabling retry. **Host integration:** the overlay now supplies a `cameraData.requestId`; hosts must process manual captures before skipping background request IDs and echo the exact ID on `snapshot:saved`. Return/reject the capture callback promise so failures can reach the overlay. See the package README's Snapshot completion section. **URL lifetime:** the standalone download's blob URL remains valid for 60 seconds, then is revoked. It is a temporary download URL, not persistent image storage. A regression test covers deferred cleanup. **Thumbnail behavior:** intentionally, a manual snapshot downloads without replacing the project's thumbnail. Background thumbnail captures continue to upload as before. ## How to test 1. Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun dev --filter=editor --ui=stream`, then open a saved project. 2. Open Command+K → Take Snapshot, select Standard 16:9, and press the shutter. A 1920 × 1080 WebP should download; the overlay should show “Saved” and exit. 3. Repeat with Standard 9:16. Verify a 1080 × 1920 image downloads. Choose the desired levels explicitly; Whole building includes the roof. 4. Check that ordinary background thumbnail saves do not download files. Capture/download failures should display an error and enable another attempt. Validation completed: - `bun run check` (passes with existing repository warnings) - `bun run check-types` (all 13 tasks passed) - `bun run build --filter=editor^...` (all six dependency builds passed) - `bun test apps/editor/lib/snapshot-download.test.ts packages/editor/src/components/editor/snapshot-capture.test.ts packages/editor/src/components/editor/thumbnail-generator.test.ts` (47 tests passed) - Browser verification: 16:9 and 9:16 downloads decoded at the expected dimensions, capture mode exited, and the browser console had no errors. ## Screenshots / screen recording Generic demo room; no private house plan is shown. ### 16:9 capture completed ### Error feedback and retry Optional: attach `snapshot-review-export.webp`, the actual downloaded 1920 × 1080 demo image. ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes the snapshot completion contract (required requestId correlation) and host thumbnail handlers; incorrect integration can leave the overlay stuck on “Capturing…”. > > **Overview** > Manual snapshot shutter presses now get a **`requestId`**, and the overlay only shows “Saved” or errors when **`snapshot:saved`** / **`snapshot:capture-failed`** match that ID and project—not when background thumbnail jobs finish. > > The standalone app routes **`captureMode`** captures through a new **`downloadSnapshot`** helper: file download with a sanitized project-based filename, **`snapshot:saved`** after the download starts, and a **60s** blob URL lifetime. Background thumbnail uploads are unchanged and still skip captures that carry a **`requestId`**. > > **`isOverlaySnapshotSave`** now requires an exact **`requestId`** match (legacy “no requestId” behavior is gone), and the package README documents the updated host **`onThumbnailCapture`** contract. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7cd149e2fcd891bf7d1877581e0d72d4d1c3819c. title: [Discovery] Publish to the MCP Registry after each stable release
body:
## What does this PR do? **Root cause:** no workflow in this repo has ever published `server.json` to the MCP Registry. `mcp-registry.yml` only validates the manifest, and publishing was a manual owner step (`wiki/npm-release.md`). The green run after the 1.0.6 release ([run 39880562788](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/actions/runs/39880562788)) was just the `push` trigger's `validate` job, so a green result said nothing about the registry. Changes: - **`mcp-registry.yml`** also runs as a reusable workflow (`workflow_call`) and by manual dispatch, with `version` and `publish` inputs. `version` is required for dispatch, so every publish run is tied to a release tag. - The server name `app.pascal/editor`, package `@pascal-app/mcp` and remote `https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp` are hard-coded. The version check and the full manifest check are defined once at workflow level, and both jobs run them. - **`validate`** checks the version input before any checkout. The version must be a stable `X.Y.Z` (anchored regex, no CR or LF). It then checks out the `@pascal-app/mcp@` tag, resolves the tag to its commit, and outputs that commit SHA. It also runs the full manifest check. - **`publish`** (needs `validate`, environment `mcp-registry`, concurrency group `mcp-registry-publish` without cancel-in-progress): 1. checks the version input, and that validate reported a 40-hex commit, before any checkout; 2. checks out that exact commit, not the tag name. It fails if HEAD differs or the tag no longer points at that commit; 3. repeats the full check before login, and fails on any mismatch: - `server.json`: name, version, exactly one package entry (registry type, registry base URL, identifier, version, runtime hint, transport) and exactly the one remote URL; - `packages/mcp/package.json`: name, `mcpName` and version. Later steps get the version only from this step's output, and nothing goes to `$GITHUB_ENV`; 4. waits up to 10 minutes for `npm view --registry https://registry.npmjs.org @pascal-app/mcp@ mcpName` to return `app.pascal/editor`, run from outside the checkout; 5. skips the publish if the registry already lists the version. Otherwise it runs `mcp-publisher login dns --domain pascal.app` and `mcp-publisher publish`; 6. deletes `~/.config/mcp-publisher/token.json` (and `~/.mcpregistry_registry_token` as a fallback) in an `if: always()` step; 7. **fails** unless `/v0/servers/app.pascal%2Feditor/versions` then lists the version. - The concurrency group keeps one running and one waiting run, so a third queued run replaces the waiting one. That is accepted: a replaced run can be dispatched again, and an already listed version is skipped. - `hosted-matches-manifest` runs only when the `check-hosted` dispatch input is set, and it doesn't gate the publish. - Unchanged: the triggers, `contents: read` permissions, checkout SHA pin and `mcp-publisher` sha256 check. - **`release.yml`**: a new `mcp-registry` job runs after `release` for non-dry-run `latest` releases. It runs only when the released `@pascal-app/mcp` version, taken from `packages/mcp/package.json` as a new `mcp-version` output, contains no `-`, so a `bump=none` rerun after a beta doesn't publish. It passes only `MCP_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY`, through the declared `workflow_call.secrets`, instead of `secrets: inherit`. GitHub needs that pass-through even though the secret lives only in the environment. - **Docs** (`wiki/npm-release.md`, README): the automated flow, the CI-only signing key and the `mcp-registry` environment, key rotation, publish queueing, and recovering a missed version. **Version sourcing:** this was already in place. `scripts/sync-agent-versions.ts` rewrites `server.json` from `packages/mcp/package.json`, and `skills:validate` fails on drift. This PR doesn't change it. **Server card:** it is served by the hosted deployment, not this repo. Top-level `"version": "1.0"` is the card's format version. `serverInfo.version` and the API catalog follow whatever `@pascal-app/mcp` the deployment runs, so fixing them is a hosted-deployment change. `hosted-matches-manifest` flags the mismatch when dispatched. ## Maintainer action needed (repository admin) The `mcp-registry` environment exists, limited to `main`, with no required reviewer. 1. Generate a fresh, CI-only Ed25519 keypair and add its own `pascal.app` TXT record (`v=MCPv1; k=ed25519; p=`). Neither of the two existing `v=MCPv1` records on `pascal.app` is CI's. Record CI's public key in `wiki/npm-release.md#the-ci-signing-key`. 2. Store the hex private key as `MCP_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY` in the `mcp-registry` environment only. It must never be a repository secret or a secret of another environment. 3. A tag ruleset that limits who can create `@pascal-app/mcp@*` tags is recommended. Setting it up needs a repository admin. This PR adds no secrets and changes no environments or rulesets. Until the secret exists, the `publish` job fails with an error naming it. 1.0.6 is already in the registry, so no manual publish is needed after merge. ## How to test 1. With shellcheck 0.11.0 installed, `actionlint .github/workflows/mcp-registry.yml` (actionlint 1.7.7) reports nothing, and shellcheck is clean on the two shared check scripts. `release.yml` passes plain actionlint; its only shellcheck findings are in lines this PR doesn't touch. 2. Local harness: it takes the version check, the full manifest check and both commit steps straight from the workflow YAML and runs them against fixtures. - **Version input:** `1.0.6` passes. These fail before checkout: - `1.0.6-beta.1`, `v1.0.6`, `01.0.6` or an empty value - a value containing LF or CR - a validated commit that isn't a SHA - **Manifest:** a valid manifest passes and outputs only `version=1.0.6`, and so do the real `@pascal-app/mcp@1.0.6` files. Each of the following fails and writes no output: - `server.json` name, version, or a multi-line version - package registry type, base URL, identifier, version, transport or runtime hint - an extra package entry - the remote URL, or an extra remote - `package.json` name, `mcpName` or version - **Commit hand-off:** run against a local git origin. `validate` resolves the tag and outputs its commit. `publish` passes when it is handed that commit, and refuses when it is handed a different commit, when the checkout differs from the commit it was handed, or when the tag is moved after validation. The commit check also passes against the live `@pascal-app/mcp@1.0.6` tag. 3. On this PR, `MCP Registry` runs `validate` only. `publish` and `hosted-matches-manifest` are skipped. I did not run a registry publish. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Introduces automated registry publishing with a DNS signing secret and strict tag/commit pinning; misconfiguration or key issues could block releases or publish wrong manifests until admins complete environment setup. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d2e96ca069ce4c2b373104284b9244d186b2b9ab. title: [Deps] Bump MCP TypeScript SDK to 2.4.0
body:
## What does this PR do? Bumps the MCP TypeScript SDK in every workspace that depends on it. Only `package.json` ranges and `bun.lock` change. No source code changes were needed. | Package | From | To | Workspaces | |---|---|---|---| | `@modelcontextprotocol/server` | ^2.3.1 | ^2.4.0 | `packages/mcp`, `packages/cli`, `packages/nodes` (dev) | | `@modelcontextprotocol/node` | ^2.1.1 | ^2.1.2 | `packages/mcp` | | `@modelcontextprotocol/client` | ^2.3.1 | ^2.4.0 | `packages/mcp` (dev), `packages/cli`, `packages/nodes` (dev) | - **Why the client moves too:** it ships in lockstep with the server. `server@2.4.0` pins `core@2.4.0` exactly, and `client@2.3.1` pins `core@2.3.1`, so leaving the client behind would install two copies of `core`. The lockfile now resolves one `core@2.4.0`. - **`node@2.1.2` peer dependency:** it requires `server ^2.4.0`, so the two have to move together. - **`@hono/node-server`:** stays on 1.19.17. That satisfies both our direct `^1.19.15` and the SDK's widened `^1.19.9 || ^2.1.3`. - **`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (v1):** not used by any workspace, so there was nothing to bump to 1.32.2. It is only mentioned in the historical `packages/mcp/PLAN.md`. **Provenance:** every version was checked on npm (`latest` dist-tag) and on the official [modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk releases](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/v2.4.0), all published 2026-10-23. ### Changelog summary ([v2.4.0](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/v2.4.0), [node@2.1.2](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/%40modelcontextprotocol%2Fnode%402.1.2)) - **New:** a Skills over MCP extension (SEP-2640) under new `ext/skills` subpaths; package root exports are unchanged. Also an opt-in `scopeForRefresh` for OAuth token refresh, and `ServerEvent` now takes optional `params`. - **Fixes:** - `update({ title })` changes now show up in resource list responses. - A per-request transport at a modern protocol revision now binds that revision instead of answering `-32022`. - `createMcpHandler` sends `Allow: POST` on every `405`. - `@modelcontextprotocol/node` accepts `@hono/node-server` 1.x or 2.x. - **Upgrade notes:** the three behaviour changes below. ### How each upgrade note was checked To check all three notes, a throwaway script (not committed) connected a real `Client` to `createPascalMcpServer` over `InMemoryTransport`. It listed every tool and scanned every `inputSchema` and `outputSchema`, and it captured the SDK's `console.warn` output. The same script ran on SDK 2.3.1 (main's lockfile) and on 2.4.0. On both versions, all 77 tools list on a 2025-11-25 connection, and 53 of them have an `outputSchema`. The `tools/list` output is **byte-identical** between the two versions. 1. **`x-mcp-header` on a `number` parameter is rejected.** Not affected. - No schema in the repo declares `x-mcp-header`: no source match, and no hit in the advertised schemas. - The SDK warning for invalid `x-mcp-header` declarations never fired. - Our server does not offer protocol revision 2026-07-28: a client pinned to it is refused at `server/discover` on both versions. So the client-side exclusion of such tools could not apply anyway. 2. **`outputSchema` from `z.object().meta({ id })` is no longer wrapped in `{ result }` on 2025-11-25.** Not affected. - No advertised `outputSchema` has a root `$ref`, which is what `.meta({ id })` produces. - No `outputSchema` is the single-`result` wrapper. - No code or test reads `structuredContent.result`. - `output-schema-contract.test.ts` already calls tools through a client that lists first, and it passes. 3. **Bundled Ajv (fast-uri 3.1.8) rejects `$id`/`$ref` with an invalid URI scheme.** Not affected. - No advertised schema contains a `$id`, or a `$ref` other than a `#…` fragment. - `normalizeToolSchemaDialect` only retargets `$schema` and flattens tuples; it never writes `$id` or `$ref`. ## How to test 1. `bun install`: the lockfile is unchanged after install. 2. `bun run ci` (Biome check, skills:validate, check-types, test, build): passes locally, with 0 failures. Test counts: mcp 1,295, nodes 5,022, core 6,095, editor 2,646, viewer 875, cli 137, ifc-converter 97, geometry-script 41, app 74. 3. Optional: `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/output-schema-contract.test.ts packages/mcp/src/tools/schema-dialect.test.ts` covers the listed-client output validation and the advertised schema dialect. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

body:
## What does this PR do? Bumps the transitive dependency `fast-uri` from 3.1.2 to 3.1.9 in `bun.lock`. 3.1.9 fixes GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg (moderate, scheme spoofing), GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h (low) and GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp (low). `fast-uri` reaches the tree through `ajv-formats/ajv` and `conf/ajv` (both `ajv@8.20.0`, which asks for `fast-uri: ^3.0.1`). - **Lockfile change:** one line. Only the hoisted `fast-uri` entry changed: the version moved to 3.1.9 and the integrity hash was replaced with the registry's `sha512` for 3.1.9. 3.1.9 is inside ajv's `^3.0.1` range, so no override was needed. The lockfile format is unchanged (`lockfileVersion: 1`, `configVersion: 0`), and no other package was re-resolved. title: [Deps] Security: patched Node in Docker build and engines floor
body:
## What does this PR do? Picks up the [October 21, 2026 Node.js security release](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases) (22.23.4 / 24.22.1 / 26.12.1, all flagged `security: true` in https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json). It covers several high-severity CVEs: the Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write CVE-2026-111497, the dns.resolve NUL truncation CVE-2026-105482, and the TLS hostname bypasses CVE-2026-105483 and CVE-2026-106069. - **`Dockerfile` build stage.** `oven/bun:1.4.4-alpine` is Alpine 3.24.3, checked from the image's rootfs layer. Alpine v3.24/main ships `nodejs 24.22.1-r0` (built 2026-10-23) for both x86_64 and aarch64, per [pkgs.alpinelinux.org](https://pkgs.alpinelinux.org/packages?name=nodejs&branch=v3.24) and the APKINDEX, and 24.22.1 is the patched 24.x release. The stage now installs `'nodejs>=24.22.1-r0'`. That's a minimum rather than an exact pin, so later Alpine rebuilds still install, but a stale or unpatched index fails the build. Bun stays at 1.4.4. - **Runtime stage.** Already on `node:22.23.4-alpine`, the patched release. Unchanged. - **`engines.node`.** Raised to `>=22.23.4` in the root `package.json` (was `>=22.18`) and `packages/cli/package.json` (was `>=22.13.0`). No other package declares `engines`. **Impact on `@pascal-app/cli` users.** `engines` is advisory. npm prints an `EBADENGINE` warning but still installs and runs the package unless the user has turned on `engine-strict`. The repo's own `.npmrc` is empty. Nothing in the repo reads `engines`. The runtime check in `pascal doctor` (`packages/cli/src/diagnostics.ts`) still accepts 22.13+, and the README/skills docs still say "Node.js 22.13 or newer". Both are left alone to keep this PR free of app-code changes. No functional break below 22.23.4, only the warning. ## How to test 1. `docker buildx build --load -t pascal-editor:test .` should succeed. The build log shows `Installing nodejs (24.22.1-r0)` in `build 3/7`, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes. 2. `docker run --rm oven/bun:1.4.4-alpine sh -c "apk add --no-cache 'nodejs>=24.22.1-r0' && node --version && bun --version"` should print `v24.22.1` and `1.4.4`. 3. `docker run -p 3999:3000 pascal-editor:test`: `GET /api/health` and `GET /` both return 200, and `node --version` in the container prints `v22.23.4`. All three were run locally on amd64. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [ ] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch
