title: [Maintainer] i18n: locale registry, formatting and first locales
body:
## What does this PR do? Links #621 and delivers the first maintainable localization slice: - uses Lingui 6 core behind Pascal’s experimental registry facade, preserving owner namespaces, ordered host/plugin overrides (including English), locale fallback, dev-only missing-message warnings, and isolated request/editor scopes - retains client scopes only while their React provider is mounted, so SSR scopes are collectible and Strict Mode effect replay can safely detach and reattach them - uses plain `i18n._({ id, message, values })` runtime descriptors in published packages—no Lingui macros, compiler plugin, or host build step - registers the compiled English catalog synchronously from the published editor entry so production interpolation works for package consumers; hosts opt into the other bundled packs - replaces the custom message/plural engine and JSON catalogs with ICU MessageFormat, PO source catalogs, and committed Lingui-compiled English, zh-CN, fr, es, and ja catalogs for the existing 85 messages - resolves standalone/iframe `?lang=` on the server and hydrates with the same request-local locale; `` is also initialized before first render and runtime switching remains supported without catalog registration resetting the active locale - keeps locale-aware number/length formatting and decimal input parsing separate from the unit system, including scoped decimal parsing in sliders, stair/metric controls, floor-plan dimensions/reference scales/measurement extrusion, and cabinet placement dimensions - converts the viewer controls/header/floor-plan/stage surfaces plus the Build panel Rooms section and Advanced heading - routes missing/stale translation fill through lazily loaded Vercel AI SDK structured output with configurable OpenAI/Anthropic providers; ICU, IDs, placeholders, attributed/self-closing tags, plural categories, and glossary terms are validated, multiline review notes are escaped, and every AI result is written `fuzzy` with `Review: required` - treats defaults extracted from code as the canonical English source: `i18n:check` reports drifted IDs without writing files, while `i18n:extract` overwrites only English, preserves target translations, and marks changed targets fuzzy/review-required; stale entries are omitted from compiled target packs so runtime falls back to current English until review - keeps `i18n:check` key-free, read-only, and strict for PO/extraction/compiled drift, completeness, stale source hashes, placeholders, plurals, glossary rules, and human-review status; source line shifts do not alter PO files - rejects prototype-mutating catalog keys and builds registry accumulators without object prototypes - includes #1156’s self-host proxy matcher/exclusions unchanged, applies locale forwarding only after the auth gate, and checks the matcher against the real `public/` and `app/` top-level folders - runs the standalone i18n-tool and proxy regressions from the root CI test command - verifies scene serialization is identical across locales; exports, MCP/agent text, catalog content, and developer errors remain untranslated The design follows the proposals from @luis-caf and @volkankurt2. #1022 can rebase onto this registry and contribute its broader zh-CN surface coverage. ### Runtime dependency footprint `@pascal-app/core` adds only two direct Lingui runtime dependencies, both pinned to 6.10.1: - `@lingui/core` is the message runtime used for catalog activation, fallback, ICU interpolation, and plural selection. - `@lingui/message-utils` is loaded only when a host calls asynchronous `registerMessages` with raw ICU strings, so those packs can be validated and compiled atomically. Bundled packs use precompiled messages and do not load it on the rendering path. `@lingui/react` was removed: Pascal’s own context and `useSyncExternalStore` provider are sufficient for the published plain-runtime API. CLI, PO, AI SDK, provider, and Zod packages remain root development tooling; the AI modules load only for `i18n:translate`. ### Proxy / security scope This branch merges main at `5ec20e77` and preserves #1156’s matcher and static exclusion list exactly. Relative to main, `apps/editor/proxy.ts` only imports the locale helpers and replaces the successful-gate `NextResponse.next()` with a request-header copy that overwrites `x-pascal-locale` from canonicalized `?lang=`. `gateRequest(request)` still runs first and any redirect/error returns immediately. This forwarding is required because Next App Router layouts cannot read `searchParams`; without it, the root layout cannot choose the locale during SSR and the first paint would disagree with hydration. The change does not add an auth bypass, alter open paths, or trust a client-supplied locale header. The root test script executes `apps/editor/proxy.test.ts`, retaining #1156’s dotted-route and static-asset matcher cases alongside locale canonicalization. A filesystem-backed regression now requires every top-level `public/` folder to be excluded and every non-shadowed top-level `app/` folder to remain matched. ### Deferred follow-ups A follow-up issue should cover the intentionally deferred deeper placeholder/select validation, per-locale lazy entry points, inherited parent-catalog plural rules such as `pt` used by `pt-PT`, and client-side `?lang` navigation without a reload. None expands this first slice beyond its current 85 messages. ## How to test 1. Run `bun run i18n:check`; all bundled PO catalogs and compiled modules should be synchronized and complete without an API key, and the command must leave them unchanged. 2. Run `bun test scripts/i18n.test.ts packages/core/src/i18n packages/editor/src/i18n packages/editor/src/components/ui/controls/slider-control.test.tsx packages/editor/src/components/ui/controls/metric-control.test.ts packages/nodes/src/cabinet/__tests__/dimension-input.test.ts apps/editor/proxy.test.ts`. 3. Run `bun run check`, `bun run check-types`, and `bun run ci` for the complete gate. 4. Run `bun dev`, then compare the editor with no `lang`, `?lang=fr`, and `?lang=ja`. The selected locale should be present in the server-rendered first paint and remain unchanged through hydration and later pack registration. 5. In French, edit slider, metric/stair, floor-plan, and cabinet fields with comma decimals; they should parse in the provider’s locale while English comma behavior stays unchanged. In particular, ambiguous `1,000` means `1` in French and `1000` in English. 6. To exercise AI fill without credentials, run `bun test scripts/i18n.test.ts`; the provider path is mocked and validates that output remains flagged for human review. ## Screenshots / screen recording The screenshots are served from a dedicated non-merged asset branch so they are public to all contributors without adding binaries to `main`. ### English (default) ![Pascal editor in English](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/6fca014c251647c1ddf9eee3f7ab6735f8105ce6/pr-assets/1148/i18n-english.png) ### French ![Pascal editor in French](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/6fca014c251647c1ddf9eee3f7ab6735f8105ce6/pr-assets/1148/i18n-french.png) ### Japanese ![Pascal editor in Japanese](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/6fca014c251647c1ddf9eee3f7ab6735f8105ce6/pr-assets/1148/i18n-japanese.png) ### French decimal input verification ![Pascal editor accepting French decimal input](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/6fca014c251647c1ddf9eee3f7ab6735f8105ce6/pr-assets/1148/french-comma-decimal-test.webp) ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Credits: @luis-caf for the inventory and extensibility contract, and @volkankurt2 for the agreed four-point host design.

title: [Bugs] IFC: skip unreadable (NaN/Infinity) geometry instead of failing the import
body:
Upstream half of pascalorg/private-editor#1304. The IFC converter now skips mesh primitives whose positions contain NaN or Infinity, instead of throwing "Could not build imported mesh node at primitives.0.positions.0" and failing the whole import. A test reproduces the production error with one coordinate overflowed to Infinity: it fails before the fix and converts after.

This branch is cut from the commit private-editor currently pins, so the pin bump carries only this fix. Once this merges, #1304 moves its editor pin to the merge commit.

Opened by Bugs (cloud agent bc-30e07df3).

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core IFC mesh extraction and slab/level placement logic; incorrect skipping could hide elements or misplace storeys, but behavior is covered by new regression tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> IFC import no longer aborts when a file contains **NaN/Infinity** in mesh or placement data (the previous failure mode was schema errors like `Could not build imported mesh node at primitives.0.positions.0`). Conversion now **sanitizes geometry** (skip non-finite placement matrices, strip bad vertices/triangles via `keepValidTriangles`) and **falls back** on bad unit factor, site origin, or storey elevation, while accumulating an **`IfcConversionReport`**.
> 
> **`convertIfcToPascalWithReport`** returns `{ scene, report }`; **`convertIfcToPascal`** is unchanged for callers that only need the scene. Elements with no readable mesh are tracked and **omitted** (including avoiding slab rebuild for unreadable roofs). **`ConversionOptions.locateWasmFile`** lets hosts override web-ifc WASM URLs. The ifc-converter demo shows **amber warnings** when the report indicates skipped geometry or replaced placements. Tests cover overflow fixtures and WASM resolution.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ae7e363c9b3ca91766f6a8a66d729a8e37754bd3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

## Why `locateWasmFile` is here
#1304 needs it for one thing `wasmPath` can't express: retrying with a cache-busted URL. web-ifc builds the URL as `wasmPath + fileName`, so a prefix can version the path (`/web-ifc/0.0.78/`), but it can't add a query after the file name. After the 0.0.77 → 0.0.78 bump, prod served new JS against a stale cached `/web-ifc.wasm`, and every conversion failed with a LinkError on `__cxa_throw` (Oct 16–17). The fix in #1304 loads `/web-ifc-<version>.wasm` and, on a LinkError, retries once with `/web-ifc-<version>.wasm?v=<now>`, which a cache has never seen. That second URL needs the file-name-level hook.

title: [Bugs] safe-fetch: redact logged URLs, cap drained bodies, exact 192.0 ranges
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to [#1122](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1122). It fixes the open bot findings on `packages/mcp/src/lib/safe-fetch.ts`, the SSRF-safe fetch used by the hosted MCP photo and vision tools. There is one commit per fix: 1. **Redacted blocked-fetch logs.** `safe_fetch_blocked` log lines used to include the full URL. Now they record only the scheme, host and path (`loggableUrl`), so the query string (presigned image tokens), the userinfo and the fragment no longer reach hosted logs. The `ProtocolError` returned to the caller still has the full URL, which the caller supplied in the first place. 2. **No unbounded body reads.** Redirect and error responses used to be drained with `res.resume()`, which had no size cap. They are now `res.destroy()`ed, so zero bytes are read. With `agent: false` there's no keep-alive socket to preserve. The response is a Node `IncomingMessage`, so there's no `res.body` to cancel. 3. **Exact reserved ranges.** The `192.0.x.x` check blocked all of `192.0.0.0/16`. It now blocks only `192.0.0.0/24` (IETF protocol assignments) and `192.0.2.0/24` (TEST-NET-1). I also rechecked the other constants against the IANA IPv4/IPv6 special-purpose registries and added the entries that aren't globally reachable but were missing: `192.88.99.0/24`, `198.51.100.0/24`, `203.0.113.0/24`, `100:0:0:1::/64`, `2001:2::/48`, `2001:db8::/32`, `3fff::/20` and `5f00::/16`. Globally reachable entries (AS112, AMT and similar) stay allowed. Because `203.0.113.0/24` is now blocked, the test suite's public IPv4 fixture moved from `203.0.113.10` to `93.184.215.14`. ## How to test 1. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/lib/safe-fetch.test.ts`: all 34 tests pass. 2. New tests, each confirmed to fail against `main`'s `safe-fetch.ts`: - `logs blocked URLs without query, fragment or userinfo`: covers the host-blocked, scheme and origin-allowlist paths. The logged URL is `scheme://host/path`, with no token, password or fragment. - `never reads redirect or error bodies`: a 16 MB 302 body and a 16 MB 500 body are destroyed, and 0 bytes are pulled from either. - `allows public addresses` now includes `192.0.1.1`, `192.0.3.1` and `192.0.255.1`. The `blocks …` cases include `192.0.0.1`, `192.0.2.1` and the newly added ranges. 3. Ran locally: `bun run check`, `bun run skills:validate`, `bun run check-types` and `bun run test`. One unrelated `ifc-converter` timing test (`scaling > grows linearly…`) failed once under parallel load and passed when re-run. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Bugs] safe-fetch: IPv6 special ranges, DNS abort, log trimming
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to [#1154](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1154) for `packages/mcp/src/lib/safe-fetch.ts`, with one commit per finding: - **IPv6 `2001::/23`.** Blocks the whole IETF protocol assignments block. Before this, only Teredo (`2001::/32`) and benchmarking (`2001:2::/48`) were blocked. The entries IANA lists as globally reachable stay allowed: `2001:1::1`–`2001:1::3`, `2001:3::/32`, `2001:4:112::/48`, `2001:20::/28` and `2001:30::/28`. - **DNS abort.** The DNS lookup now races the fetch's abort signal, which the timeout fires. `dns.lookup` can't be cancelled, so before this a resolver that never answered kept the fetch open past `timeoutMs`. It now fails as `fetch_timeout` and never sends a request. - **Ports.** Only ports 80 and 443 (or the scheme's default port) are fetched, so a public host's other services can't be reached through the image fetch. An origin listed in `PASCAL_ALLOWED_ASSET_ORIGINS` may still name any port, since the operator has trusted it explicitly. The rejection reason is `url_port_not_allowed`. - **Log trimming.** `loggableUrl` caps the logged path at 128 characters. Blocked non-http(s) URLs such as `data:` and `javascript:` carry their payload in the path, so they now log only the scheme and host (for example `data:` or `ftp://a.example`). ## How to test 1. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/lib/safe-fetch.test.ts`: all 38 tests pass. 2. These tests fail against `main`'s `safe-fetch.ts`: - `blocks IETF protocol assignments 2001::/23` - `a DNS lookup that never answers still times out`: uses Bun fake timers with a resolver that never settles. - `only web ports are fetched unless the origin is allowlisted` - `truncates long logged paths and logs only scheme and host for other schemes` - the updated `logs blocked URLs without query, fragment or userinfo` 3. `allows public addresses` now also covers the `2001::/23` exceptions and `2001:200::1`, the first address past the block. 4. Ran locally: Biome on the changed files, plus `turbo run test check-types --filter=@pascal-app/mcp`. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Maintainer] i18n: fix scoped-locale and decimal Bugbot findings from #1148
body: ## What does this PR do? Follows up on #1148’s five remaining Bugbot findings: - **False positive — client locale reset:** `ClientBootstrap` subscribes with `defaultI18n.subscribeLocale`, which excludes catalog refresh notifications. Registering a later compiled pack therefore refreshes messages without applying the global English locale to the request scope. The regression now explicitly registers a compiled catalog while global `en` and request-local `fr` differ, and verifies no locale notification or reset occurs. - **False positive — slider scoped parsing:** `SliderControl` gets `locale` from `useLocale()` and calls `parseSliderBareValue(text, locale)`, which forwards it to `parseLocalizedNumber`. title: [Bugs] ifc-converter: keep geometry whose normal is NaN, recomputing the normal
body:
Only a non-finite position drops a vertex now. A NaN normal on a vertex that is kept gets recomputed from the faces of the surrounding kept triangles, or set to zero when those faces have no area. Until now, geometry with bad normals was dropped entirely.

Test: `imported-mesh-conversion.test.ts` runs `convertIfcToPascalWithReport` with web-ifc's `GetVertexArray` spied so every normal is NaN. It expects the same meshes and triangle counts as a clean conversion, with finite normals. Without the fix it fails with 1,002 vertices dropped. With the fix, all 103 converter tests pass.

title: [Bugs] safe-fetch/core: shared allowlist parser and hardening
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to [#1158](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1158). `PASCAL_ALLOWED_ASSET_ORIGINS` is now read one way by both consumers: the scene asset URL validator (`packages/core/src/schema/asset-url.ts`) and the MCP server's `safeFetch` (`packages/mcp/src/lib/safe-fetch.ts`). - **One shared parser in core.** `parseAllowedOrigins` and `allowedOriginsFrom` are exported from `@pascal-app/core/schema`. - Each entry is normalised to `new URL(entry).origin`, so a trailing slash, uppercase or `:443` no longer stops a scene asset URL on that CDN from validating. - The parsed list is cached per value, and each rejected entry warns once. - Unset or empty means no allowlist. A whitespace-only or all-invalid value is an allowlist with no valid entries, so it admits nothing in both places. Before, core treated a whitespace-only value as unset. - `safeFetch` drops its own parser and uses this one. `mcp` already depends on `@pascal-app/core/schema`, so there's no new dependency edge, and the release workflow bumps the `@pascal-app/core` peer range in lockstep. - **Malformed entries aren't logged raw.** Rejected entries are reported as `{ index, reason }`, with reason `not_a_url` or `scheme_not_allowed`, never by value. That way an entry like `user:secret@host` or `ftp://user:secret@host` can't put credentials in logs. - **Only `http:` and `https:` entries count.** Anything else is rejected with a warning. That includes `blob:https://…`, which would otherwise borrow an https origin. - **The two DNS tests now catch their regressions.** - The listener-cleanup test observes the abort listener at the moment `safeFetch` first reads each lookup's answer or error. It fails if the removal is missing or deferred to a later tick, as with the earlier `.finally` version. - The late-DNS test switches back to real timers and flushes a real event-loop turn before asserting there was no unhandled rejection, instead of counting microtasks. ## How to test 1. `cd packages/core && bun test src/schema/asset-url.test.ts`: 49 tests pass, including: - a `GuideNode` with a CDN URL validating under a `https://cdn.pascal.app/`, `HTTPS://CDN.PASCAL.APP` or `https://cdn.pascal.app:443` entry; - whitespace-only and all-invalid allowlists; - one test each for `blob:`, `ftp:` and `ws:` entries; - index-and-reason reporting for credential-bearing entries. 2. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/lib/safe-fetch.test.ts`: 46 tests pass. I also broke `untilAborted` in four ways locally: - removing the listener removal fails the listener test; - deferring the removal to a `.finally` fails the listener test; - rethrowing a DNS failure that arrives after the timeout fails the late-DNS test; - dropping the race against the abort signal fails the late-DNS and timeout tests. 3. Ran locally: `bun run check`, plus `turbo run test check-types` for `@pascal-app/core`, `@pascal-app/mcp` and `editor`. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Bugs] core: asset allowlist warnings, comment, docs and release note
body:
## What does this PR do? Small follow-up to [#1161](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1161) for the shared `PASCAL_ALLOWED_ASSET_ORIGINS` parser in `packages/core/src/schema/asset-url.ts`. - **Warning wording:** the no-valid-entry warning now reads `no origin is permitted`. The http-only warning notes that `safeFetch` still fetches the listed `http:` origins. - **Cache comment:** the comment on `allowedOriginsFrom` now says what the cache does. It holds only the most recent value, so warnings repeat when the value changes. - **New warning for http-only allowlists:** scene asset URLs accept only `https:` origins, so an allowlist of only `http:` entries rejects every one. That now logs a one-time `asset_allowlist_has_no_https_entries` warning. A mixed allowlist doesn't warn. - **Credentials in entries:** a full `https://user:secret@host` entry keeps its origin. The dropped credentials are reported as `asset_allowlist_entry_credentials_dropped {"index": N}`, by index only, never the entry. - **Wildcard entries:** a wildcard host (`https://*.example.com`) is skipped with reason `wildcard_not_supported`, instead of being kept as a literal origin that never matches. - **Late-DNS test:** the late answer is now `127.0.0.1`. The test checks that it's neither fetched nor even evaluated (no blocked-host log) once the timeout has fired. - **Docs:** `packages/mcp/CROSS_CUTTING.md` §5 describes the shared parser that `safeFetch` uses. - **Release note:** the root `CHANGELOG.md` "Unreleased > Breaking" entry covers: - a whitespace-only value now admitting nothing instead of meaning unset; - core normalising entries, so a trailing slash, uppercase, `:443`, a path or credentials now grant the origin; - only `http:` and `https:` entries counting, and wildcard hosts being skipped; - the log line rename from `safe_fetch_allowlist_entry_ignored {entry}` to `[pascal] asset_allowlist_entry_ignored {index, reason}`, so alerts on the old name need updating. ## How to test 1. `cd packages/core && bun test src/schema/asset-url.test.ts`: 53 tests pass. - The credentials and wildcard tests fail if those parser checks are removed. - The http-only test fails if its warning is removed. 2. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/lib/safe-fetch.test.ts`: 46 tests pass. The late-DNS test fails if the lookup and its address check keep running after the timeout; the late loopback answer then gets checked and logged. 3. Ran locally: `bun run check`, plus `turbo run test check-types` for `@pascal-app/core` and `@pascal-app/mcp`. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Bugs] ifc-converter: unit fallback normal, typed-array recompute, count recomputed normals
body:
Follow-up to #1160.

- A vertex whose adjacent faces have no area now gets the unit normal (0,0,1) instead of [0,0,0].
- The recompute sums into a `Float64Array`, with an `Int32Array` mapping vertices to slots. The new `bun run bench:normals` (a 1M-triangle grid with every normal NaN) runs in 169 ms vs 445 ms before.
- `report.replaced.normals` counts recomputed normals. It doesn't count as a conversion issue.

Tests in `imported-mesh-conversion.test.ts`: degenerate geometry gets (0,0,1) normals, and the all-NaN test checks the count and that recomputed normals match web-ifc's on flat faces. Both fail on the old code. All 104 converter tests pass.

title: [Bugs] ifc-converter: overflowed normals take the unit fallback; keep the bench unpublished
body:
Follow-up to #1165.

- The normal recompute also checks `Number.isFinite(length)`, so a summed normal that overflows to Infinity gets (0,0,1) instead of [0,0,0]. The test uses a triangle with coordinates around 1e155.
- New `tests/geometry-validity.test.ts`: on a four-vertex quad with two NaN normals, `replaced.normals` is exactly 2. A vertex with a NaN position isn't counted.
- `src/__bench__` is excluded from `tsconfig.json`, and `package.json` `files` has `!dist/__bench__`. `npm pack --dry-run` lists no bench file, and `bun run bench:normals` still runs.

All 106 converter tests pass.

title: [Maintainer] i18n: string-extraction codemod + CI literal guard
body:
## What does this PR do? Adds the tooling for the full localization migration (#621, after #1148 and #1162). It also migrates the viewer toolbar, so the new literal baseline starts lower than the scan rather than higher. - **Codemod.** `bun run i18n:literals -- convert [--apply] ` (`scripts/i18n-codemod.ts`) rewrites hardcoded JSX text, `aria-*`/`title`/`placeholder`/`alt`/`label`/`tooltip`… props, conditional and template-literal copy, and `toast`/`alert`/`confirm`/`setError` payloads into the existing runtime form, `i18n._({ id, message, values })`. It adds `usePascalI18n()` to the owning component (one-line bodies stay valid) and the import. Adjacent text and simple interpolations become one ICU message. - `--keys=… --vars=…` turns module data into lazy `/* i18n */` descriptors (`MessageDescriptor`, now re-exported by `@pascal-app/core`). - Copy is ICU-encoded so the compiled message renders exactly the original text. - Adjacent static pieces are encoded together. - No-break spaces are kept. - Text before a placeholder is encoded knowing a `{` follows. - Attribute entities are decoded. - Emitted strings escape CR and line separators. - Listed as `MANUAL` and never edited: - app modules and editor package entry exports without `'use client'`; - named `.map(function …)` callbacks (also parenthesized) and async functions; - complex interpolations, concatenations and string constants. - A second run, including a repeated `--vars` pass, changes nothing. - **CI literal guard** (inside `i18n:check`, already in `bun run ci`). `i18n/literal-baseline.json` lists each file's legacy copy **by text**: 2,884 candidates today. The baseline format is version 3, since fingerprints are now rendered text. - Per file: adding or swapping a string fails, and a new file must have none. - The baseline may only shrink, **measured across the repository**: each text it adds must consume an equal text removed elsewhere, duplicates counted. Copy that moves with a `git mv`, split or extraction passes after `update`. - The allowlist may not gain entries relative to the base either. One-off exemptions use `// i18n-ignore: `; a bare `i18n-ignore` exempts nothing. - Text is recorded as it renders: JSX whitespace rules, full HTML entity decoding (`entities`, attributes included) and `{' '}` joins, so equivalent spellings match. A no-break space is content. The allowlist applies to the whole joined text. - These count as copy: - hyphenated labels; - `const` strings rendered in JSX or inside a sentence (resolved through lexical scope); - copy built with `+`, constants included. Toast descriptions are counted once. - **Review policy.** Drafts ship as English until reviewed; regressions never ship. - CI accepts AI drafts only when they are flagged `fuzzy` + `Review: required`. They are never compiled into packs, so users see English. - `bun scripts/i18n.ts release-check` compares the committed catalogs with a base revision, never the working tree. - In CI the base is the PR base (part of `i18n:check`, depth-2 checkout). On push to `main` it is `github.event.before`, which covers every commit of the push. - In `release.yml` the base is the latest `@pascal-app/editor@` tag, since the editor package ships the catalogs. - When that tag predates the catalogs (true today: `@pascal-app/editor@1.0.6`), it falls back to `origin/main` when that is another commit with catalogs, then to the commit that introduced the catalogs, and otherwise fails loudly. - An explicit `--base` that cannot be resolved or read fails the job. - It fails when an entry reviewed at the base, with unchanged English, became a draft. - **Renames** are declared with a `renamed-from: ` descriptor comment. - `i18n:extract` carries the reviewed translation over when the English is unchanged. CI fails only if a declared rename arrives without it. - An undeclared new ID that shares English with a removed reviewed ID is reported as a possible rename (console and job summary), never an error. It may be an unrelated addition, and a missed carry-over just shows English. - No one has to mark `Review: human` themselves. - It also inspects the compiled packs themselves and fails if any draft msgstr is shipped. - Both jobs write the per-locale draft count, the base used and any rename warnings to the job summary. `check --reviewed` remains a manual sign-off command; it is not in any workflow. - `extract` never approves a newly filled translation by itself. - **Pseudo-locale.** `en-XA` (accented, ~30 % longer, bracketed) is compiled from English and checked for drift. `apps/editor/lib/dev-locales.ts` registers it only outside production, inside a `NODE_ENV` branch that the bundler drops. A local `next build` has no `en-XA` strings in `.next/static` or `.next/server`. - **Screenshot audit.** `bun run i18n:pseudo-audit` (playwright-core 1.64.1, matching the tree, with the system Chrome; a dev tool, not a CI job) opens each surface in `i18n/pseudo-surfaces.ts` and saves full-viewport screenshots. - It fails on visible text or accessible names with plain ASCII words, and on visible controls without an accessible name. - Allowlisted data is removed as whole words only, so the unit `in` no longer hides `Find` or `Pin`. - **Viewer toolbar.** Stack/Exploded/Solo, wall mode, the Display menu, Walkthrough, Preview and Enter/Exit VR are migrated. Scene theme names moved to a shared helper used by both toolbars. The Display menu is `w-max min-w-60 max-w-80`, so longer labels no longer wrap or truncate. - **Docs.** `i18n/README.md` covers the guard, codemod, review states, how to declare a rename, release behaviour (including which tag the release compares with) and the audit. It includes "Releases ship drafts as English until they are reviewed." `CONTRIBUTING.md` gets a short "User-visible text" section. ## How to test 1. `bun run i18n:check`: passes. It reports 2,884 legacy candidates and 64 drafts per locale awaiting review, and writes that table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in CI. 2. In `packages/editor/src/i18n/locales/fr/messages.po`, mark `editor.buildPanel.advanced` as `#, fuzzy` + `Review: required` and rerun: it fails with `fr: "editor.buildPanel.advanced" is reviewed on the base branch with the same English and must stay reviewed`. I ran this locally. 3. Rename the ID `editor.buildPanel.advanced` in `build-panel.tsx` to `editor.buildPanel.advancedSection`, with `comment: 'renamed-from: editor.buildPanel.advanced'`, then run `bun run i18n:extract`. The French entry arrives as `Avancé` with `Review: human`, and `i18n:check` passes. I ran this locally and reverted. 4. Add `

Hello there

` to a component, or change an existing literal's text: the check fails and names the file, line and text. Add `{/* i18n-ignore: demo */}` above it and the check passes; a bare `{/* i18n-ignore */}` does not. `

Pascal{' '}

` passes like `

Pascal

`. 5. `bun scripts/i18n.ts release-check` prints the base it compares with and passes; `--base nonexistent-ref` exits 1. - Three tests run the default lookup, without `--base-dir`, in a temporary git repository. It uses an `@pascal-app/editor@*` tag that has catalogs, ignoring `v*` tags. It falls back to the catalogs' first commit when the tag predates them. It fails loudly when no base exists. The first two exit 1 on a reviewed-to-draft change. - The job tests on temporary catalog copies exit 1 when French `Avancé` becomes a draft with the same English, and when a draft is injected into the compiled French pack. 6. `bun test ./scripts/i18n.test.ts ./scripts/i18n-literals.test.ts ./packages/editor/src/i18n`: 55 pass. The tests use fixtures, temp copies and temp repositories, never the real catalogs. They include: - the unrelated-addition (warning only) and declared-rename cases; - the git mv/split baseline test and the allowlist ratchet; - the release tag lookup; - codemod round trips for braces, no-break spaces, quoted placeholders, attribute entities and CR. 7. `bun dev`, then `bun run i18n:pseudo-audit -- --out .i18n-audit`: screenshots land in `.i18n-audit/`. ## Follow-ups (not in this PR) - Make pseudo-locale availability an explicit deployment flag (`NEXT_PUBLIC_PASCAL_PSEUDO_LOCALE`), so production-built Preview deployments can enable it. - Store error codes/descriptors instead of translated strings in component state, so cached text follows a later locale change. - Resolve the supported locale before setting `` (inherited from #1148). - Resolve React import aliases (`memo as reactMemo`) in the hook-owner check; aliased wrappers are currently refused conservatively. ## Screenshots / screen recording The editor in `en-XA` from the audit. The migrated top bar and toolbar are pseudo-localized; the tool tiles, tool dock and sidebar are later surface PRs: [Editor in en-XA](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-305ffe90-aea2-59de-99f1-557e81c16d7c/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fnavbar-display-menu-en-XA.png) ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: [Bugs] safe-fetch: redacted error data, refuse URL credentials, allowlist doc fixes
body:
Follow-ups to #1161, #1163 and #1166.

- **mcp/safe-fetch:** error data now carries only redacted URLs (`loggableUrl`) for every failure reason and for each redirect hop. `invalid_url` carries no URL. DNS and fetch failures report a system error code only. A table test checks every reason.
- **mcp/safe-fetch:** request URLs with userinfo are refused as `url_credentials_not_allowed`, before lookup and on redirect hops.
- **core:** `__resetAllowedOriginsCacheForTests()` added for the one-time warning cache, and the tests now use it.
- **docs:** an all-invalid or whitespace-only allowlist admits no `https:` origin. Local, blob, data-image and relative assets are still accepted. The CHANGELOG notes that safeFetch is unchanged there. Also fixes a comment line break in `asset-url.ts`.
- **ifc-converter:** `check-types` now type-checks `src/__bench__`.

Locally, lint, skills validation, check-types and all package tests pass.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes MCP SSRF fetch validation and what agents see in errors; operators relying on full URLs in `ProtocolError` data or URLs with embedded credentials will need to adjust.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens MCP **`safeFetch`** so failure paths no longer leak secrets in `ProtocolError` data or logs: URLs use **`loggableUrl`** (no query, fragment, or userinfo), **`invalid_url`** omits the URL entirely, redirect **`hops`** are redacted, HTTP failures use **`STATUS_CODES`** instead of the server reason phrase, and DNS/network errors expose only a validated **`code`** (not `Error.message`).
> 
> **`safeFetch`** now rejects any hop whose URL contains **userinfo** as **`url_credentials_not_allowed`** (before DNS), including redirect targets that embed credentials.
> 
> **Core** adds test-only **`__resetAllowedOriginsCacheForTests()`** so allowlist warning cache behavior is assertable; **CHANGELOG** / **CROSS_CUTTING** clarify that a whitespace-only **`PASCAL_ALLOWED_ASSET_ORIGINS`** blocks **`https:`** scene assets while non-allowlisted schemes still pass, and that **`safeFetch`** behavior there is unchanged.
> 
> **`@pascal-app/ifc-converter`** adds a **`check-types`** script targeting **`src/__bench__`** via **`tsconfig.bench.json`**.

title: [Maintainer] Reference scale: validate calibration input and harden label fallback
body:
## What does this PR do? A follow-up to [#1164](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1164). It adds input validation to reference-scale calibration and makes the legacy label parser more robust. - **Calibration rejects lengths over 1,000,000.** The "Set overlay scale" form used to check only that the length was above 0. The schema caps `displayLength` at `1e6`, so a larger value could be saved and then fail validation on import, paste or patch. The form now shows an inline message ("Length must be at most 1000000 m.", using the unit you picked) and disables Save Scale. `createGuideScaleReference` is the only code that writes `displayLength`. It now leaves out `displayLength`/`displayUnit` when the value is outside the schema range and keeps only the label, so whatever it returns always passes the schema. The guide move/resize path copies a reference that is already stored and doesn't set these fields. - **Label fallback no longer calls `String()` on arbitrary values.** If a scene was loaded without validation and a persisted `label` isn't a string, the label now renders as the number when it is a number and as an empty string otherwise. Odd values such as `{ toString: null }`, null-prototype objects or symbols can no longer throw. - **Legacy labels accept runs of whitespace between digit groups.** `'1 234,5 m'` parses again. The pattern is now `\s+` between digit groups; JavaScript's `\s` already covers NBSP and narrow NBSP. Whitespace and digit groups can't match the same characters, and the existing 64-character cap still applies before matching. **Deferred: a hand-typed `'1.234 m'` still reformats to `'1234 m'`.** Only hand-typed labels are affected. The editor never saved a label with a thousands separator or more than two decimals: it used `toFixed(2)` before [#1162](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1162), and the shared formatter has had grouping off since [#1148](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1148). The parser reads three digits after the last separator as grouping, which is what makes a hand-typed `'1,234 m'` read as 1234. Reading `'1.234 m'` as 1.234 instead would mean choosing a convention for dot versus comma in free text. That is out of scope for this PR, so behaviour is unchanged. ## How to test 1. Open a floor plan with a reference image and start **Set Scale**, then draw a line. 2. Enter `2000000` (meters). An inline error says the length must be at most 1000000 m, and **Save Scale** is disabled. 3. Enter `1000000`. The error goes away and saving works. 4. Automated: `bun test src/components/editor/floorplan-panel.test.ts` and the full `packages/editor` test suite (2669 pass), plus `turbo run check-types --filter=@pascal-app/editor`. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A: the only visible change is the inline validation message. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

body:
## What does this PR do? Localizes the left side of the editor: the icon rail, the layers (site) panel, the floating level selector and the level dialogs. Part of #621. - **Icon rail.** The app's tabs (Scene, Build, Paint, Items, Settings) become descriptors, translated once in `SceneEditor`. That covers the rail tooltips and aria-labels, the mobile tab bar and the panel headers. The editor's own Site, Settings and Plugins entries are translated too, and a crashed plugin panel shows translated fallback copy. - **Layers panel** (`site-panel`): - section headers, empty states, the level and building rows, units, rooms and zones, and the camera snapshot menus; - the upload button, as one ICU select per asset type; - the selection badge, as an ICU plural. - **Layer row names.** Unnamed rows used to show hard-coded English kind names ("Dormer", "Solar Panel", "Wall"…). They now use the existing `node..label` messages through `nodeLabelDescriptor`, so they share translations with the build tab. The registry fallback does the same with `presentation.label`. Generated names ("Room (12 m²)", "Roof (2 segments)", "Gable (4.0×6.0m)", "Flight / Landing") live in `site-panel/default-names.ts` as whole ICU messages, with plurals and a roof-type select. The drag preview uses the same names. - **Level names** in the tree, the unit rows, the duplicate dialog and the delete confirmation use `localizedLevelName`, so they read "Ground floor / Floor 1", not the core English helper's output. - **Level rename.** Both rename fields start empty when the level still has its generated default name, instead of prefilling the stored English. The localized default shows as the placeholder (`authoredLevelName`), and leaving the field unchanged writes nothing. - **Floating level selector.** Covers add, insert, reorder, the height popover, the row menu, ground-line labels and titles, unit focus, and the delete confirmation. A new `messageWithSlot` helper keeps that confirmation one translatable sentence around the bold level name. - **Duplicate level dialog.** The presets are lazy descriptors, and the description is a whole sentence with `{levelName}`. - **Zone and items panels.** Their copy (source chips, search, empty states) is converted while they're here. - **Accessibility.** Fixes the unnamed controls the audit flagged: - expand/collapse chevrons get labels and `aria-expanded`; - the rename pencil, the room-row delete button and the colour dots get names; - the level option buttons get "{levelName} options". - **Overflow.** The level menus in the selector and the tree now grow with their content (`w-max`, up to `max-w-72`) instead of wrapping longer translations. - **Codemod fix.** The codemod no longer adds a second `usePascalI18n` import when the file already imports it in another `@pascal-app/core` import (with a test). - **Server-component guard.** `site-panel/index.tsx` gets `'use client'`. It already called hooks 57 times, but the codemod's guard read it as a possible server component because the editor barrel re-exports it. - **Catalogs.** 152 new messages. zh-CN/fr/es/ja drafts are `fuzzy` + `Review: required` (`AI-Provider: cursor-agent`), so they show English until a fluent reviewer approves them. The literal baseline drops from 2,592 to 2,436. - **Audit surfaces.** New surfaces `icon-rail`, `layers-panel`, `level-selector`, `level-menu`, `duplicate-level-dialog` and `delete-level-dialog`. They run on a project seeded from the MCP `two-bedroom` template, so the tree and level list have rows. The template's room names are listed as `data`. ## How to test 1. `bun run i18n:check`: passes and reports the drafts per locale awaiting review. 2. `bun dev`, then open a furnished project with `?lang=en-XA`. The rail tooltips, the Scene panel tree (expand a level and walls), the level pill, its ⋮ menu and both level dialogs should all be bracketed and accented. Rename a level that still has its default name: the field starts empty with the localized name as placeholder. 3. `bun run i18n:pseudo-audit -- icon-rail layers-panel level-selector level-menu duplicate-level-dialog delete-level-dialog`: all six PASS, with no untranslated strings and no unnamed controls. I ran this, and the full audit: every surface from the earlier PRs still passes. Screenshots below. 4. Tests I ran: - `bun test src` in `packages/editor`: 2,670 pass. - After the merge with `main`: the `src/i18n` and sidebar tests (24 pass, including the new `authoredLevelName` test) and `bun test scripts/` (130 pass). - `bun test lib` in `apps/editor`: 74 pass. - Type checks for the editor and the app are clean, and `bun run check` reports no findings in the changed files. ## Still English after this PR - **Plugin rail entries** (Nature, Environment, WebXR, Pools, Landscape, Bath Space, Streetscape). External plugin packages register these labels, so they're listed as `data` on the `icon-rail` surface. - **Row names a definition's `tree.label` returns.** That is plugin and definition API, which returns English. - **Base-plate footprint names** ("Shared floor", "Kitchen floor"). These come from core `floorFootprintName`, which MCP also reads; #1174 adds the structured variant. - **Unit formatting:** - the "8 ft / 9 ft / 10 ft" height presets, which stay in the literal baseline; - the fixed `m` in roof and stair segment sizes; - `toFixed` in area and perimeter. These belong to the units and number-formatting PR. - **Other pages and surfaces:** the settings panel (its own surface PR), the home and settings pages, and the WebXR "Enter VR" button. These still fail the `home`, `settings` and whole-`editor` audit sweeps. ## Screenshots / screen recording `en-XA` (accented, about 30 % longer, bracketed), captured by `i18n:pseudo-audit` at 1440×900. body: ## What does this PR do? Localizes the properties and inspector panels: the shared panel shell, the editor's own panels, the auto inspector, the building-structure inspectors and the floor footprint names. Part of #621. `main` (23bdaf47) is merged in. ### Codex round 3 (at 585db60a): room-name edits, new design The reverse lookup across all translations is gone. - **Picks.** A suggestion pick still stores the English catalog name, numbered. - **Panel edit.** An edit stores English only when the room's stored name is a catalog name (optionally with " N") and the edit is that same entry's translated label with the number changed, added or removed. It uses the room's own entry, so in French "Salon 3" on a Lounge stores "Lounge 3" and "Bureau 2" on a Study stores "Study 2", even though Living room and Office share those labels. - **Free text.** Everything else is stored exactly as typed: a click on 'Use "…"', an exact translation such as "Cuisine", another room's translation ("Salon 2" on a Bedroom), and any other text. Surrounding spaces are kept as typed, as main keeps them ("Chambre 3 " stores "Bedroom 3 ", like "Bedroom 3 " in English), and an unchanged padded name writes nothing. - **'Use' row.** It is hidden again when the text exactly matches an English catalog name, as on main, so English offers only "Bedroom 2" next to a Bedroom. Enter on the typed row commits like blur; only a click uses the text literally. A label two names share is never treated as an exact match for Enter. - **Tests.** `room-name-storage.test.ts` drives the panel's own `commitRoomNameEdit` and `commitRoomNamePick` (moved out of `RoomName`, which calls them, unchanged-field guard included), and compares French with the same keystrokes in English. It covers Lounge/Salon and Study/Bureau, the 'Use' click, "Cuisine", trailing and surrounding spaces, and unchanged fields. - **Merge.** `main` at 23bdaf47 is merged in. `i18n:extract` and the literal baseline needed no changes. ### Verify round (Codex at 6e727bfd, Tooling) - **Partially translated packs.** Filtering matches the English name as well as the label, and an exact match becomes the active row (superseded in part by round 3 above). - **Viewer labels.** The breadcrumb, sidebar and hover label get the editor's i18n passed in (no global shim), and their memo keys include the locale and catalog version. The viewer still imports nothing from the editor. - **Prototype keys.** Catalog lookups use `Object.hasOwn`, so rooms named `constructor`, `toString`, `__proto__`, `hasOwnProperty` or `valueOf 3` are free text. Each has a test. - **Nits.** `formatFixed` rounds like `toFixed` and shows -0 as 0. Opening and hidden-panel counts are ungrouped ("1000 openings"). The pseudo-audit roof and stair row matches are anchored regexes. ### Review round (Codex audit and Tooling) - **Room names (P1).** Picking a suggestion now saves the English catalog name in every UI language, numbered against the level's rooms. In French, picking "Chambre" next to an existing Bedroom saves "Bedroom 2", exactly what English saves. Typed text is saved as written. - The combobox shows and searches translated labels. - `displayRoomName()` shows catalog names translated with their number ("Bedroom 2" → "Chambre 2") wherever a room is named: room panel title, field and kickers; layers rows; unit and zone lists; 2D/3D room pills; viewer breadcrumb, sidebar and hover; walkthrough HUD; node display; footprint names; floor-opening kicker; shared-wall notes; unit members; zone quantities. - Tests cover a French pick saving the same value as an English one, label search, typed text, and display. - **Stored data.** Scenes keep exactly the English names `main` writes today. Nothing migrates or rewrites existing scenes: - the layers rows' rename field still edits the stored name; - display paths never write; - floor-plan builders, exports and agent context keep the stored English; - the zone's own 3D label (a nodes renderer the standalone viewer also uses) keeps the stored name, so the viewer doesn't depend on the editor. - **Window-merge refusals (P2).** These now use an ICU select on the blocking node's type, with one whole sentence per kind. English reads "There is an item between them." again. - **Number formatting (P2).** Run lengths, hole areas, curtain-wall spacing and effective thickness use the locale formatter instead of `toFixed`. - **Room opening counts (P2).** These are one ICU plural, keeping "No openings". - **Nits.** "1 custom panel is outside this grid. It returns…"; an unnamed room reads "Opening · in Room" again. - **`formatList`.** English keeps the original comma list ("Kitchen, Hall"). Other locales use `Intl.ListFormat` for their own separators (Japanese 、, French "et"). The doc comment says so, with a test. - **Audit browser.** Pinned to UTC and en-GB, so the editor defaults to metric and accepted data such as areas match on every machine. I ran the audit with `TZ=America/New_York`. - **Merge with `main`.** `slab-tree-node.tsx` keeps both sides, and the audit manifest keeps both surface sets. Catalogs and the literal baseline are regenerated with `i18n:extract` and `i18n:literals update`, with #1173's drafts carried over by ID. ### Tooling follow-ups (from the first round) - **Node-messages check.** It skips a missing `packages/nodes/src/index.ts` only in the tests' temporary catalog projects (`I18N_ROOT`). In a real checkout it fails extract and check. Covered by a test. - **Roof-segment name: × kept.** The x only ever appeared in the roof row's default name; its drag preview already used ×, and so do the stair rows. See the screenshots below. ### Inspector migration - **Floor footprint names.** - `floorFootprintNaming` returns the name's parts. - `floorFootprintName` builds the same English from them, so MCP, agents and core messages don't change. - The editor words the parts in the UI language. - **Auto inspector (`def.parametrics`).** - Group and action labels, field names and enum options are translated at display time with shared `editor.inspector.*` IDs. - The definition-messages generator emits them for every built-in kind. - Plugin kinds keep their English. - **Editor panels.** Room, floor & foundation, floor opening, reference, multi-selection, multi-height, mobile sheet and selection bar, collections, the panel shell and node display names. English plural helpers are now ICU plurals, and split sentences use `messageWithSlot`. - **Node inspectors.** - Covered: wall and curtain wall, slab, ceiling, door, window, roof, roof segment and glazing, stair, stair segment with railing and construction controls, site, unit, item, zone quantities and system check. - Door and window style and type cards, wall reference options and stair diagnostics get display-time descriptors. Core's English stays for chips and agents. - **Accessibility and overflow.** The panel's back, reset and close buttons and the finish swatch are named, and the mezzanine shape row wraps. - **Catalogs.** zh-CN, fr, es and ja drafts are `fuzzy` with `Review: required`, so they show English until reviewed. - **Audit.** Nine inspector surfaces, opened from layers rows on a two-bedroom project seeded with a roof and a stair. ## How to test 1. `bun run i18n:check` passes and reports 2,523 entries per locale awaiting review, and 1,399 legacy literal candidates. 2. Run `bun dev` with `?lang=en-XA`. - Select rooms, walls, doors, windows, a roof, a roof segment, a stair and a flight from the Scene panel. Turn on a room's floor and open Sits on. Every inspector should be bracketed and accented. - Rename a room from its suggestions next to an existing Bedroom. The scene stores "Bedroom 2", and the UI shows the pseudo-localized "Bedroom" plus "2". Change the number in the field and blur: the scene stores "Bedroom 3". 3. Run `TZ=America/New_York bun run i18n:pseudo-audit`. Every migrated surface passes: navbar through MEP tools, the nine inspectors, and #1173's six left-panel surfaces. `home`, `settings` and the whole-`editor` sweep still fail on pages not migrated yet. I ran this. 4. Tests I ran: - `packages/editor`: 2,700 pass. - `packages/nodes`: 5,025 pass. - `packages/core`: 6,162 pass. - `apps/editor`: 74 pass. - `bun test scripts/`: 131 pass. - Type checks are clean. ## Still English after this PR - **Other inspectors.** Cabinets, column, chimney, elevator, construction dimension, block, vents, cupola, dormer, skylight, solar panel, fences and MEP. These are the next inspector PR. - **External plugins.** Inspector extensions from external plugins, such as landscape's "Retaining wall". - **Command messages.** Room-construction refusals and floor notices, for the toasts and errors pass. - **Room names in unmigrated English sentences.** The delete confirmation, item placement notices and point-ask chips still use stored names; each gets `displayRoomName` when its copy is migrated. - **Material names.** The catalog material names. - **Unit formatting.** "8 ft" presets and fixed m and mm suffixes, for the units PR. ## Screenshots `en-XA`, captured by `i18n:pseudo-audit` at 1440×900 (UTC, metric). title: author_scene runs the author's adapter; add_object makes pieces from words
body:
## What does this PR do?

The editor side of Pascal's one AI lane: `author_scene` becomes the way an agent turns a whole design written freely in three.js into native Pascal nodes, on the chat as on the MCP.

- **`author_scene` runs the author's adapter.** The agent writes its design as a three.js module plus an adapter, a small program that reads the module and returns the payload; Pascal runs the adapter in an isolated runner (`geometry-script/src/adapter.ts`, replacing the old design-graph reader) and writes the scene. Revisions send `edits` (`{ in, find, replace }`) instead of whole files; Pascal's own rebuilds no longer count as edits.
- **Pieces from words.** `add_object` takes a `piece` (what it is, its size and mount): Pascal's model writes its module in the background, many at a time, and `author_scene` items place it by id. A piece that fails comes back in the report.
- **What a conversion can express:** curved walls, double-height voids, glass fronts, arches, round columns, `faceOutside` finish modules, ceilings, rugs, paint by meaning, stairs with `lowerSteps`/`steps` where an L or U turns, storey heights, roofs on the roof level, default room lights, joined open-plan names, the floor between storeys (and the cladding under it). The report carries `checks` and `complete`.
- **Fixes along the way:** a room's floor script builds with y = 0 at the floor's surface; finishes stop 1 mm short of openings; openings no longer z-fight with wall finishes and reveals; an `InstancedMesh` in authored geometry is measured, cut and merged as its instances; `validate_design` answers every schema error with what was expected, the schema and an example.
- **E-018:** the eye placement `view_scene` uses for interior views selects stairs and items with `queryNodes` instead of enumerating the scene.
- **`design_brief`'s first sentence** now says it is bottom-up building's record before furnishing: read in a tool list as "the design brief of the request", agents writing a design freely recorded one too.

The private host (chat, hosted MCP) follows in pascalorg/private-editor, pinned to this branch until it merges.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core packages/mcp packages/geometry-script`: passes.
2. Over the MCP, call `author_scene` with a small module (two rooms, a door, a window) and an adapter returning its payload: the scene gets native walls, rooms and openings; the report's `checks` pass and `complete` is true.
3. Send a revision with `replace: true` and one `edits` entry changing a wall's colour: only that changes.
4. `add_object` with `piece: { description, size, mount }` answers at once with `status: pending`; an `author_scene` item naming that piece places it when its module lands.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Large changes to `author_scene`, scene merge, and `add_object` placement rules affect how agents write and revise entire buildings; mistakes could corrupt scenes or block legitimate edits.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`author_scene`** grows into a full design-to-native conversion path: curved walls and arc-aligned openings, curtain walls and passages, multi-storey plates and wall heights, stairs (with floor openings), double-height **voids** with railings, roofs on a dedicated roof level (`role: 'roof'` on items), open-plan room merging, default ceiling lights, `faceOutside` / inside-outside paint, ceiling-hung items, and rugs vs slabs. The conversion **report** adds counters (passages, stairs, voids, roof segments) and exports **`authorSceneChecks`**—deterministic pass/fail checks agents can iterate on.
> 
> **Revisions** are safer: **`authored-scene-merge`** treats reconciler-derived fields (outlines, holes, child order, compile artifacts) as non-edits so Pascal’s rebuilds between conversions don’t block the next payload; real person edits on scripts and manual holes still win or conflict explicitly.
> 
> **`add_object`** adds a **`piece`** contract (description, size, mount, optional id) and **`planPiece`** to validate the word-based create path before compile; roof-level placement skips storey wall/slab refusals via **`role: 'roof'`**.
> 
> Smaller follow-ons: **`view_scene`** interior eye placement avoids standing inside or behind tall floor items and stairs; **`verify_scene`** reports blocked stair arrivals; floor placement uses scripted room finish tops; docs/tool copy for pieces, `design_brief`, and `validate_design`.

title: author_scene: keep its bookkeeping in pieces live collaboration accepts
body:
## Problem

Hosted `author_scene` fails in production on collaborative (organization) projects with `live_sync_failed: Field "metadata" is not a supported persisted value`. The conversion wrote its bookkeeping into the building's metadata, and live collaboration carries at most 64 KB per change and only plain JSON:

- the revision baseline (`authorSceneState`: every node written plus source ids): 0.5–1.4 MB on multi-storey houses, holding `undefined` values;
- the stored conversion (`authorScene.payload` + `report`): 60–180 KB on large houses.

## Fix

- Baseline split so each piece rides with what it describes: building `authorSceneState = { version: 2, buildingId, seed }`; each authored level `authorSceneWritten = { ids, keys }`; each authored node `authorSceneBase` (itself as written, plain JSON), the base of the next revision's three-way merge.
- The stored payload is a script of the scene (`export default <payload>`, the one script type project files take); the building keeps its hash, as it does for the module and adapter. The report is no longer stored (the tool answers it). Everything written to metadata is plain JSON.

Revisions keep the exact merge semantics (person edits survive, deletions stay deleted, conflicts refused). Scenes with a v1 state still load; their next revision starts from the current scene as base. Reference inventory rows updated.

Two more limits on the community side are fixed in the private PR (more new materials than one change carries; the authority repairing a commit's half-built steps).

## Verification

- core 6160 tests, mcp 1338 tests pass; `tsgo` clean; Biome clean.
- New core test: a four-storey conversion writes only plain JSON values, none past 62 KB.
- Live, on a local collaborative organization project over hosted MCP (with the private PR): the 140-item two-storey villa bench payload converts (complete, green, 32 live changes, 236 nodes); after deleting the sofa, `author_scene {replace: true}` with no payload re-runs from the stored payload file, saves as one change, and the sofa stays deleted.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how conversion state is persisted and merged across revisions; behavior is covered by tests but affects collaboration saves and MCP re-convert flows.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes hosted **`author_scene`** failing live sync when conversion metadata exceeded the ~64 KB collaboration limit (whole-house baselines were 0.5–1.4 MB and could include values the sync layer rejects).
> 
> **Conversion bookkeeping is sharded across the scene graph** instead of one blob on the building: the building keeps a small **v2** `authorSceneState` (`seed` + `buildingId` only); each authored level gets `authorSceneWritten` (node ids + source-key map); each authored node gets `authorSceneBase` for the next revision’s three-way merge. `finalizeAuthorScene` attaches this metadata on creates/updates, strips bookkeeping when merging, and serializes values with **`plain()`** so every persisted chunk is JSON-safe. Prior revisions are reloaded via **`authoredBaseline()`** (v1 monolith is no longer read—first revision after upgrade uses the live scene as base).
> 
> **MCP `author_scene`** stops embedding the full payload and report in building metadata: the payload is stored as a **geometry script artifact** (`export default …`) and referenced by hash; stored conversions rehydrate through **`readStoredPayload`**.
> 
> **Reference inventory** documents the new metadata keys (`authorSceneWritten`, `authorSceneBase`) and drops `authorScene.report` from non-reference provenance.
> 
> A new **four-storey** core test asserts each create/update payload is plain JSON and under 62 KB, with building state minimal.
>

title: [Maintainer] i18n: room-name and count follow-ups
body:
## What does this PR do? Fixes the four P3 follow-ups from Tooling's review of #1174. Part of #621. Stored scene data is unchanged: in every UI language the scene stores exactly what `main` stores. - **(a) Shared labels on Enter.** Two catalog names can share a translation; in French, Living room and Lounge are both "Salon". `roomNameOptions` now takes the room's stored name. When the typed text matches a shared label, the room's own entry becomes the active row, so typing "Salon" on a Lounge and pressing Enter keeps Lounge. Any other room still falls back to the first suggestion. Tests: - `roomNameOptions`: the shared-label `active` row for a Lounge, a Lounge 2, a Living room, and another room. - `room-name-storage`: Enter on a shared label stores the same English in French as in English. - **(b) Exact English wins on Enter. This is a behaviour change from `main`, and it is kept.** Typing "Closet" (or "closet") and pressing Enter picks Closet. `main` picked Walk-in closet, the first name containing the text. A test covers it. - **(c) Ungrouped counts.** Lingui formats `#` with grouping (1,234), but `main` wrote these counts as 1234. The plural counts added in #1174 now use a plain `{number}` value inside the plural, the same pattern as the openings count. That covers: - hole points ("# pts"), walls and open sides, MEP runs (system check and the floating action menu), curtain-wall and glazing rows and columns, and "Lower/Raise all #". The existing drafts were rewritten with the same substitution, so no translation changed wording. - **(d) Layer-tree rename.** A new `RoomRenameInput` is used for room and zone rows. While you edit, it shows the name as `displayRoomName` does ("Chambre 1" for "Bedroom 1" in French). It commits through `commitRoomNameEdit`, via a new `commitTreeRoomRename`. That keeps the tree's own write path (`updateNode`, trimmed text, `undefined` when cleared), so "Salon 3" on a Lounge 2 stores "Lounge 3", free text is stored as typed, and an English UI writes exactly what `main` writes. A test checks renumbering, a padded name, free text and clearing in French against English. - **Accessibility found by the new surface:** - the inline rename input is named "Rename"; - the wall, ceiling and roof attachment badge icons in the layer tree and item catalog now have translated `alt` text. - **Audit.** New `layer-room-rename` surface: it expands the Scene panel and opens the rename field on "Bedroom 1". `openLayer` now shares the expansion step (`expandLayers`). - **Catalogs.** 3 new messages, 11 changed. zh-CN, fr, es and ja drafts are `fuzzy` with `Review: required`, so they show English until reviewed. ## How to test 1. `bun run i18n:check` passes, with 2,526 entries per locale awaiting review. 2. Run `bun dev` and open the two-bedroom project with `?lang=en-XA`. In the Scene panel, click the pencil on "Bedroom 1": the field shows the bracketed, accented name plus "1". Change the number and press Enter. The stored name, as seen in English or through MCP `get_zones`, is "Bedroom 3". 3. In a room's construction rows, "8 walls" stays ungrouped. The counts only differ from grouped output at 1,000 or more. 4. `bun run i18n:pseudo-audit -- layer-room-rename layers-panel room-panel floor-foundation-panel`: all four pass. I ran this. 5. ## What does this PR do? Localizes the cabinet inspectors: the module panel, the kitchen run panel, the compartment cards, item options, and the kitchen "Add beside / Replace with" dialog. Part of #621. `main` (87ec430e, with #1180) is merged in with a normal merge commit. Its conflicts were in the compiled en and en-XA catalogs, the literal baseline and `i18n/pseudo-surfaces.ts`. The catalogs and baseline were regenerated with `i18n:extract`, `i18n:literals update` and `i18n:compile`, and the surfaces file keeps both sides. Reviewed entries stay at 85 per locale, and `release-check` finds no draft compiled in. Stored scene data is unchanged. - **Option arrays** (front style, overlay, handles, handle position, cabinet tier, top finish, compartment types, fridge, cooktop, sink and rack styles, door types) become lazy descriptors, translated where the controls render. Labels that are numbers or units ("2", "60/40", "300 mm") stay as written. - **Whole messages:** - "This {width} item cannot fit…"; - "Finished height extends {overflow} mm above the ceiling.", now using `formatFixed` instead of `toFixed`; - "Inserts on the left/right of the selected item." as an ICU select; - each change line in the replace preview ("{name}: {before} → {after}", "{name}: moves {distance}"); - "Module {number}" and "Use {name} as array source"; - the array button title, as an ICU plural, which replaces the English `cop${y|ies}` logic. Its count is written ungrouped, as in #1179; - the equalize-widths titles; - the module summary ("{number} compartments", plus the compartment type). - **Preset names.** `CABINET_PRESETS` keep their English labels, because agents and MCP read them. The kitchen picker, the replace dialog and the module panel title use new display-time descriptors (`KITCHEN_ITEM_LABELS`, `KITCHEN_GROUP_TITLES`). - **Kitchen search.** It also matches the name the picker shows, through a new optional `label` argument on `kitchenItemMatches`, so a translated tile name finds its item. The English names and keywords still match. A test covers it. - **Module panel title.** A wall cabinet attached above a base module is now titled "Wall cabinet". `kitchenPresetForModule` reads it as a base cabinet, because its parent isn't a wall run, so the title now uses the panel's own wall-cabinet check. - **Accessibility.** The compartment move up/down/remove buttons, the stepper −/+ buttons ("Decrease/Increase {label}") and the module delete button ("Delete {name}") now have accessible names. - **Audit.** New `cabinet-module-panel` and `cabinet-run-panel` surfaces on the two-bedroom project with a seeded two-module kitchen run. Module names that presets write ("Base Cabinet", "Sink Base") are scene data and listed as `data`. - **Catalogs.** 240 new messages. zh-CN, fr, es and ja drafts are `fuzzy` with `Review: required`, so they show English until reviewed. The literal baseline drops by 230, from 1,369 on `main` to 1,139. ## Display changes from `main` - An upper cabinet attached to a module now shows as "Wall cabinet": in its panel title, in kitchen search and in the command palette. Before, it showed as "Base cabinet". - A single-compartment module summary in the run panel now shows a label (for example "Drawer" or "Gas cooktop") instead of the raw type (`drawer`, `cooktop-gas`). ## How to test 1. `bun run i18n:check` passes after the merge, with 2,804 entries per locale awaiting review. `bun scripts/i18n.ts release-check --base origin/main` passes too: no reviewed translation regressed, and no draft is compiled in. 2. The inspectors are bracketed and accented, and the upper cabinet's title is the localized "Wall cabinet". 3. `bun run i18n:pseudo-audit -- cabinet-module-panel cabinet-run-panel`: both pass. I ran this. The Next app loads `@pascal-app/nodes` from `dist`, so run `bunx turbo run build --filter=@pascal-app/nodes` first. 4. Tests I ran after the merge, with core and nodes rebuilt first: - `packages/nodes`: 5,027 pass, 1 skip. - `packages/editor` `bun test src`: 2,704 pass. - `apps/editor` `bun test lib`: 74 pass. - `bun test scripts/`: 131 pass. - The editor, nodes and app type checks are clean, and `bun run check` reports no errors. ## Still English after this PR - **Cabinet copy outside the inspectors:** - the 3D quick-action bar ("Left / L Left / Wall / Tall…"). It renders inside drei `Html` and can switch to `LocalizedHtml`, now on `main`, in a follow-up; - the placement HUD in `tool.tsx`; - the layer-tree label "Modular Cabinet (N modules)", which comes from definition API copy. - **Planning-check messages** (overlaps, gaps) from cabinet validation, which agents share. They're for the command-messages pass. - **Module names presets write** ("Base Cabinet"). These are stored scene data, like room names. - **Other inspectors:** column, chimney and elevator (#1182), dormer, skylight and solar panel (#1183), and vents, fences and MEP (#1185). Construction dimension and block also remain. ## Screenshots / screen recording `en-XA`, captured by `i18n:pseudo-audit` (UTC, metric). The images are served from the image-only branch `cursor/i18n-audit-screenshots-8160`, which is never merged. title: i18n: add Turkish (tr) as a bundled locale
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds Turkish (`tr`) as a bundled locale, following the "To bundle another language" steps in `i18n/README.md` and the community `tr` pack discussed in #621 and #1148.

- `lingui.config.ts` and `TARGET_LOCALES` in `scripts/i18n.ts` gain `tr`.
- `packages/editor/src/i18n/locales.ts` registers the `tr` pack.
- `i18n/glossary.json` gains Turkish terms: tavan, kat planı, kat, oda, 3B tarama, duvar, gezinti.
- `packages/editor/src/i18n/locales/tr/messages.po` has a draft for all 2,611 messages.

Every entry is an AI draft, marked `fuzzy` + `Review: required` (AI-Provider: claude-code). The drafts were not produced with `i18n:translate`; they were checked with the same `validateTranslation` rules (placeholders, tags, Turkish `one`/`other` plurals, glossary). Since only `Review: human` entries are compiled, the shipped `tr` pack stays empty and the UI shows English until a native speaker reviews entries. I'm a native speaker and will send reviewed batches as follow-ups, starting with the viewer, navbar, toolbar and Build panel copy.

1. `bun run i18n:check`: it passes and reports `tr 2611` awaiting review.

title: Agents: units in author_scene and shared unit tools; opening frames follow the wall
body:
## What does this PR do?

Two things the hosted AI agents needed (owner, 2026-10-27):

**Units for agents.** A condo, apartment building or hotel asked of the agent came back as rooms only: no chat tool could create a unit and `author_scene` had no way to name one.
- `author_scene`: a room takes `unit: "Apartment 2B"`, the payload an optional `units` list (kind, colour). One `UnitNode` per name under the building, members across levels (a duplex), defect `unit_split_room` when one open-plan room names two units, warning `unit_no_rooms`, check `rooms_in_units`, `report.units` and `report.ids['unit/<name>']`. Units ride the building's own `authorSceneWritten` list so a revision removes one the payload drops (the per-level baseline of #1178 never saw them).
- `create_unit`, `set_unit_members`, `list_units` become shared core contracts (`agent-tools/units.ts`) and operations (`agent-operations/units.ts`, 16-case table), registered on the MCP through `shared-tools.ts`; the MCP-only files are gone. `get_zones` answers each room's unit.
- The public `pascal-3d` skill says what a unit is, top-down (`unit` in the payload) and bottom-up (`create_unit` after the rooms exist).

**Opening frame depth follows the wall.** `frameDepth` on doors and windows was a fixed 0.07 m default while walls are 0.1–0.35 m, so the wall's cut faces showed around every frame. `frameDepth` is now optional: left out, the frame is the host wall's thickness plus a 1 cm lip on each face (`resolveOpeningFrameDepth`, core `lib/opening-frame-depth.ts`); a stored number stays explicit (E-003, nothing migrates). Every reader (viewer door/window systems, move tools, plan offset, documentation, schedules) goes through the resolver; the manual tools and `planWallOpening` stop writing it; the panels show "Depth (auto)" with an Auto reset; MCP templates drop their hardcoded value. Catalog entries for the new panel copy are drafts awaiting review.

## How to test

1. `bun run ci` (run on this branch in a clean clone: check, i18n, skills, types, tests, build all pass).
2. Editor: draw a 0.2 m wall, add a door and a window: the frames stand proud of both faces, no grey reveal. Select the door: Frame → "Depth (auto)" reads 0.22 m; drag it to 0.07 and the reveal appears; press Auto and it follows the wall again.
3. MCP or chat: `author_scene` with two rooms naming `unit: "Apartment A"` / `"Apartment B"` → two units under the building, the report counts `units: 2`; `list_units` reads them; `set_unit_members` moves a room.

title: core: author_scene revisions leave a derived surface's holes to the reconciler
body:
## What does this PR do?

A second `author_scene` call with `replace: true` was refused in production (Architect Medium on a plan photo, 2026-10-27):

```
Refusing to change holes on the derived ceiling ceiling_as4a66ada3. The structure reconciler owns it…
```

Cause: when a revision moves a room that sits inside another room, the conversion's own reconcile pass re-cuts the outer ceiling's `source: 'room'` hole, and `authoredSceneChanges` let a reconciler-owned field "follow the design where it changed", so the update carried the new `holes`. The host's `filterDerivedNodeWrites` strips `polygon` silently but lets `holes` through, `mergeRoomHoles` kept both holes, and the derived-node guard refused the whole write. The model then spent its turn working around it.

Fix in `authored-scene-merge.ts`: on a derived surface, `holes` / `holeMetadata` never follow the design; the update keeps the scene's current value and the host's reconciler re-cuts the room holes from the walls the revision did change (manual cut-outs are re-applied by the kernel). A person's manual cut-out still counts as their edit for the "cannot be removed by regeneration" check, compared metadata-aware on both sides. No schema or stored-shape change.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/core && bun test src/agent-operations/author-scene.test.ts src/store/derived-node-guard.test.ts` → 75 pass. The new case "a room moved inside another leaves the outer ceiling's re-cut hole to the reconciler" fails on main's merge code and passes here.
2. In the editor or over MCP: `author_scene` a plan with a closet inside a bedroom, then `author_scene` again with `replace: true` and an edit moving the closet's walls: the write succeeds and the bedroom's ceiling hole follows the closet.
