title: Agents: exact colours, column code, textured maps, slab surface scripts
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets `author_scene` and the MCP tools build more faithful finishes:

- **Columns in author_scene** take `code` (the add_column module contract, mount `floor`), `rotation`, and a `color` that is now applied, as an exact material on every native surface (it was stored in metadata and never applied).
- **Same gap on other kinds:** a slab's `railing` accepted a `height` but the slab renderer drew every run at 1.1 m in the slab's edge finish. Slab railings are now fences standing on the slab (`supportSlabId`) with their own `height` and a new `color`. Stairs now take `railing` (sides), `railingStyle`, `color` (flight), `treads` and `railingColor`.
- **`exact: true`** on `paint` (with `color`: that colour as a matte scene material, not the nearest library colour) and on `add_object` (the module's slot colours with their roughness/metalness, not their library matches; glass and emissive slots keep theirs). One shared helper (`exactColorMaterial` / `exactScriptSlots`) now backs author_scene's exact slots too.
- **Native textures** take `offset`, `normalMap`/`normalScale`, `bumpMap`/`bumpScale`; the viewer applies them (maps share the albedo's repeat and offset; normal/bump are non-colour, rendered shading only). New map URLs are inventoried as asset references; reference discovery now treats any `AssetUrl` field as a reference. `paint` documents the UV convention so an agent can line joints up (`offset = frac(−c × repeat)`).
- **Slab surface scripts:** a standalone slab (not a room's floor plate, `boundary !== 'auto'`) can carry `surfaceScript`, the same record as a room's `floor.script`: author_scene `surfaceCode`, `setSlabSurfaceScript`, refreshed by `refreshFinishScripts` when reshaped, drawn on the slab's top, owning the surface's colours (paint refused), items stand on its build, `get_source` reads it, clipboard carries its artifacts, the slab panel shows it (view / remove, like the room panel, via a shared `ScriptedFinishRow`).

Reviewer note: the slab kind now has a lazily loaded `renderer` (`ParametricNodeRenderer` + the script build beside the slab's group), like columns, doors and ceilings, instead of the default generic mount. `ParametricNodeRenderer` is exported from viewer for that.

Old scenes load unchanged: every new field is optional.

## How to test

1. `bun run ci` (run locally: green).
2. author_scene a payload with a slab `{ polygon, top: 0.3, surfaceCode: <decking module> }` and a column with `code` and another with `color`: the slab shows the decking on its top, the coded column its module, the coloured one that exact colour on shaft/base/capital.
3. `paint` a wall with `{ color: '#3a5f8c', exact: true }`: a scene material named `#3a5f8c` is created and reused on a second call.
4. `paint` a floor with a native material `{ texture: { url, repeat: [2, 2], offset: [0.5, 0], normalMap } }`: the pattern shifts half a tile and shows relief.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Checked locally in `apps/editor` (`next dev`): a payload sent through the MCP `author_scene` tool, with real compiles and the app's artifact store, then a textured `paint`. It renders the terrace's script-built decking on the slab top, cut to its outline; a 0.9 m red railing standing on it; a native column in its exact green, turned 30°; a scripted post in its module's exact blue; and a brick wall face with its normal map, offset half a tile. The slab kind's new renderer path also renders an existing project's slabs unchanged. No new console errors; the two "synchronously unmount a root" warnings also show without this change. No recording attached.

title: editor: walls, porches and decks, railings, stairs, roofs, openings
body:
## What does this PR do?

The editor side of the punch list (walls, rooms, porches and decks, railings, beams, posts, stairs, roofs, doors and windows), reworked in review. The **Addendum** at the end records every review decision and change; this section describes the branch as it is now.

### Walls
- Pushing or dragging a wall leaves no doubled walls; a wall drawn over another built differently takes over that stretch (its openings move onto the new wall). Drawing into a wall splits it, as on main.
- Exterior corners miter; interior walls meet the inside face and leave the outer wall whole.
- Pull to continue from a selected wall's end; line-up snap and arrow-key nudge (2D); Tab steps through stacked objects (2D); open wall ends select their wall.
- Temporary dimensions on selected walls (one or several): room widths and outside size, editable in 2D and 3D. The wall's length reads its faces (ID / OD), chosen in **Display → Dimensions → Measure walls**.
- Moving several walls pushes each along its own normal, parallel to where it was, with joined walls following and the same live dimensions as a single wall.
- Wall types live in the wall panel: Preset plus a menu to create, edit and duplicate project wall types; stud spacing on the framing layer. New walls are plain, as on main.

### Rooms, porches, decks and patios (on main's floor plates)
- Invisible walls (room dividers): they close rooms, never cut walls, stay joined when moved, push and drag at their ends.
- Room types Room, Porch, Deck and Patio. A room closed off outside the house steps down and takes its type's defaults; porches get automatic posts and a beam.
- Decks drawn as boards on their framing (ledger, joists, rims, beam, posts on piers); porch and patio slabs run down to the natural ground.
- All of it reads and writes main's floor plates. The plate of an outdoor room carries `metadata.floor` (`porch-slab` / `deck`) as a documented interop field for framing plugins; built-in code reads the room's `roomType`.

### Railings, beams, posts and stairs
- Railing as a wall type (style, post spacing and size, openings); rooms close on railings; a door on a railing is a gap (via a host-surface capability, not a kind check).
- Beam and Post tools with their panels and plan symbols.
- Stairs with wood stringers, concrete or steel, with code checks; square floor openings; a moved stair heals its old cutout at once.

### Roofs
- Roof plan with the eave outline and live updates; moved roofs and side arrows catch the wall lines; gable and heel walls match the walls below; roofs snap to porch, deck and invisible-wall edges.
- Roof layers (build-up) and ceiling layers; Display → Ceilings (solid tops).

title: mcp: author_scene payload by reference (payloadFile)
body:
## What does this PR do?

- `author_scene` takes `payloadFile`: the `fileId` of a JSON project file (from `upload_project_file`) holding the payload. It's for a payload too large for one call, like a whole house with its modules. The server reads it through a new host hook, `ProjectFileReader` (`readFile` on `createPascalMcpServer`). After that it is handled exactly like an inline payload: it is stored, so `replace: true` writes it again.
- Refusals:

  - a server without a reader answers `files_unavailable`.
- Paint's texture `url` description now says it can be `artifact://<sha256>` of an image stored with the project.

title: Spotlights, per-light shadows and lamp glows
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lights held by items can now be spotlights, cast shadows, and draw a glow at the lamp.

- **Scene graph:** the item `light` effect (and the authored-object manifest light) gains three optional fields. Old scenes load unchanged.
  - `spot { direction, angle, softness }`: `direction` is the aim in the item's frame, so it turns with the item; `angle` is the full cone in degrees; `softness` runs from 0 (hard edge) to 1 (fully feathered).
  - `shadows`: casts shadows.
  - `glow { size, strength = 1 }`: a soft additive halo at the lamp in the light's colour, nearly invisible in daylight and strongest at night (follows the sun's elevation, or the theme).
- **Modules:**
  - three.js: a `SpotLight` keeps its target, angle and penumbra. `castShadow` (or `userData.shadows`) and `userData.glow` carry over.
  - Blender: a spot keeps its cone and blend. The `shadows` and `glow` custom properties carry over.
- **author_scene:** `lights[]` takes `direction` or `target`, `angle`, `softness`, `shadows` and `glow`. A target is stored as a direction in the fixture's frame.
- **Viewer:** the editor and baked viewers share one pooled runtime (`PooledLights`): 12 point lights, 6 spots and 2 shadow slots.
  - Spots get the shadow slots before point lights, since a point shadow is six renders.
  - The spot and shadow pools mount the first time a scene needs them, so existing scenes keep today's light count and shaders.
  - Glows are one instanced sprite for every lit lamp, drawn their radius toward the camera so the fixture around the bulb doesn't hide them.
- **Fix:** the baked viewer and the in-scene controls now read an authored item's own `asset.interactive`, as the editor already did. Before, lights author_scene hung on a module fixture went dark once published. A rebuild of the object now keeps those lights after its new module's own.

## How to test

1. Build an object with `add_object` whose module adds a `THREE.SpotLight` named `light:wash` with `castShadow = true` and `userData.glow = { size: 0.2 }`. Its `manifest.lights[0]` has `spot`, `shadows: true` and `glow { size: 0.2, strength: 1 }`.
2. Switch the theme to Night. The cone lights the wall or floor with a soft edge, it casts shadows, and a soft halo shows at the lamp. In the Studio theme the halo almost disappears.
3. Run `author_scene` with a fixture light given `target`, `angle: 40` and `glow`. Rotate the fixture: the beam turns with it. Bake or publish the scene: the light is still there.
4. Ran locally: `bun test src` in core, viewer, geometry-script, mcp and nodes; `bun run check` (no errors).

title: viewer: light pools ranked by contribution; captures lit for their camera
body:
## What does this PR do?

Item lights get bigger pools ranked by what they add to the view, pictures are lit for their own camera, and glows no longer get outlined in captures.

- **Pools:** 16 point lights and 16 spots, all unshadowed, plus the 2 shadow slots. Unshadowed lights only lengthen the shaders' light loop: no extra pass, and the count is fixed at mount, so there are no recompiles. Touch devices get 6/6.
- **Ranking:** a light whose reach misses the view frustum gets no slot. Its reach is its `distance`, or, when it has none, where intensity ÷ d² falls under 0.01. The rest rank by intensity ÷ d², with a light on another storey than the edited one counting a quarter.
  - This replaces angle × 0.7 + distance/200 × 0.3, where distance barely counted: a ceiling can 15 m straight ahead beat a sconce 3 m off-axis.
  - The baked viewer's ground-floor preference and its `levelOrder` prop are gone with it.
- **Captures:** `itemLightsForCapture(scene, camera)` re-ranks the pools for the capture camera and sets every light straight to its strength, then gives the live view its lights back. The thumbnail generator calls it last in a capture's setup.
  - `view_scene` used to get the lights chosen for the tab's live view.
  - A theme switched for the picture (`lighting: 'night'`) no longer catches lamps mid-fade.
- **Glows:** the glow sprite writes nothing into the scene pass's normals and diffuse colour (`mrtNode`, as the dust), so the ink no longer outlines its quad.

## How to test

1. Open a house with exterior spots and many interior lights, and look at the facade from the street: every exterior beam facing the camera is lit.
2. Aim the tab's camera away from a room, then run `view_scene` on a lamp in it with `lighting: 'night'`. The lamp is lit at full strength, the same as with the tab aimed at it, and the same as a tab already in Night.
3. Run `view_scene` of a lit pendant at night with edges on: there is no square around its glow.
4. Ran locally: `bun test src` in viewer, editor and nodes; `bun run check` (no errors). Steps 2 and 3 were checked on a lamp close-up through `view_scene` over a local MCP. Step 1 was checked by the 9-exterior / 50-interior test.

title: viewer: draw a light's glow at its bulb, not over its fixture

## What does this PR do?

A light's glow is drawn at its bulb, depth-tested, instead of half its size nearer the camera. The pull put the glow over the fixture's own housing. title: Remove the generic foundation and the 8 in seat; terrain and skirts meet floors cleanly
body:
## What does this PR do?

This removes most of what #1097 drew automatically around a house's foundation and ground, and fixes two places where the ground and a building met badly.

- **The generic foundation is gone.** The viewer derived a concrete footing and an 8 in CMU stem under every building's exterior walls. They looked wrong, did not follow terrain, and spread to every shared floor plate. A foundation is now only what the person sets on a floor (`set_floor_foundation`, the floor construction).
  - Removed with it: the `drawsFoundation` capability, `useViewer.pluginFoundationLevelIds`, and the capture helper that hid its meshes.
  - `deepestDrawnY` is now the lowest floor's underside.
- **The ground floor sits on grade.** "Set as ground floor" and `set_ground_level` used to stand the floor 8 in (0.203 m) over grade, a gap the generic foundation filled. That seat is removed:
  - from the foundation constructions: `seatAboveGrade`, `seatBasis`, `stemThickness`;
  - from the ground seat: `aboveGrade`, `atFoundationTop`.
  - A seated floor is one on grade within 5 cm. A building seated 8 in up by the old rule now reads unseated and comes down when it is set as the ground floor again.
  - Basement walls against the earth keep their foundation construction (8 in CMU and furring, cast concrete in Europe).
- **The grade ring is gone.** This was the dark ribbon drawn along a basement's outline while the ground is veiled. It read as black wall tops, and the hole already shows where the ground is cut. `UNDERGROUND_RING` and `anyGroundVeiled`, which only the ring used, go with it.
- **Foundation skirts reach the drawn ground.** A flat site's fill lies 5 cm under the datum (`FLAT_GROUND_Y`). A base plate's solid foundation, a porch's concrete edge, and a plate filled to the terrain stopped at the datum, so the top of a basement wall showed in the 5 cm gap. They now go down to the ground as the site draws it.
- **Terrain never shows over a floor inside its own plate.** The ground was cut only where it stood more than 0.3 m (`BELOW_GRADE_TOLERANCE`) over a floor. On a hillside, the slope between the floor and 0.3 m over it showed as thin wedges inside a walk-out's rooms.
  - `terrainOverFloors` returns the part of every visible floor plate that the rendered terrain stands over, and the site cuts the ground there along with the cover under the house.
  - The tolerance still decides grade standing, the hole and the pit.

The private repo's Bones plugin drops its `drawsFoundation` capability and its `pluginFoundationLevelIds` claims in the matching bump.

## How to test

1. On a house with no foundation set, look from under the ground: no footing or block course is drawn under the floor plates.
2. Run "Set as ground floor" on a level: the building moves so that floor sits on grade, not 20 cm above it.
3. Show a basement level from above: there is no black band on its wall tops, and the hole and pit are unchanged.
4. On a floor over a basement with a solid foundation, there is no band between the foundation and the ground.
5. On a hillside walk-out, look inside the lower rooms near where the ground rises: no terrain wedges show over the floor.
6. Ran locally: `bun test src` in core, viewer, nodes, editor and mcp; `bun run check` (no errors). Steps 1–5 were checked by Wassim in the community app.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)

> 
> **Overview**
> Removes the **derived generic foundation** (footing + stem under exterior walls), the **`drawsFoundation`** plugin hook, and all viewer geometry for it. **`deepestDrawnY`** now stops at floor slab undersides, not footings.
> 
> **Ground seating** no longer lifts the ground floor to a region-specific height above grade (8 in block, 15 cm cast concrete, etc.). **`set_ground_level`** / the level panel seat the named floor **on grade** (within tolerance); **`GroundSeat`** drops `aboveGrade`, `atFoundationTop`, and foundation metadata from agent messages and MCP docs. Foundation **construction** data keeps wall assemblies only—no `seatAboveGrade` or stem thickness for seating.

title: verify_scene catches more of what is wrong in a built house, with fewer false alarms
body:
## At a glance

**What it brings.** `verify_scene` tells the agent much more of what is wrong in a house it built, with far fewer false alarms. This applies to the chat, Pro and the hosted MCP.
- 🚶 **Usage checks:** narrow passages, furniture pockets, clashes, door swings, narrow entries, bed and fixture clearance, blocked openings, a door over a stair.
  - They are off by default in this repository; the private PR turns them on.
  - They were trimmed after counting their findings on 42 saved final scenes: passage warnings 322 → 227, clash warnings 38 → 10.
- 🧱 **Rooms and walls:** a wet room left untiled, missing skirting, faces and floors left at the default finish, a room no walk from outside reaches, walls that nearly join or end short, two zones overlapping on one floor.
- 🪑 **Fewer false clearance alarms** on twelve stored final scenes, against main:
  - `door_blocked` 23 → 12;
  - `item_too_close` 34 → 11;
  - `item_overlap` 12 → 2.
- 📋 **The brief:** the catalog's tags decide what can be placed from the catalog under an open source (`asIs` is gone), and the brief can state the request's form, facade and rooms.
- 🧩 **Tools:**
  - a `run_batch` call is checked call by call;
  - `move_node` and `duplicate_node` become shared agent tools (MCP surface 87 → 89);
  - `author_scene`'s description states the output limit.

**On its own** this PR changes nothing a person sees until the private PR bumps the submodule and turns the checks on.

**How to review**
- About 40 % of the PR (9,549 of 23,568 added lines) is the usage-field checks under `packages/core/src/spatial/usage-field`, including generated furniture outlines kept as one line per polygon.
- Then:
  1. the room and wall checks in `agent-operations`;
  2. the brief;
  3. the batch;
  4. the two MCP tools.
- Per-area sizes, and what was moved to later PRs (with why), are in "Details" below.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Base and size.** Against `pascalorg/editor` main (`cf2ca56f8`, #1204) the branch is 41 commits, 149 files, +23,568 / −598 (code 15.9k lines, tests 6.5k, shared case tables and builders 1.1k). It contains a merge of main, so it needs no rebase.

The private PR (`pro/private-checks-20261102`) bumps the submodule to this one and turns the checks on in the chat, Pro and the hosted MCP. This PR changes the shared contract and the operations; on its own it changes nothing a person sees in the chat until that bump.

## Sizes

Added lines against main, by directory:

| Area | Code | Tests and fixtures | Added |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Usage-field checks (`core/src/spatial/usage-field`) | 6,115 | 3,434 | 9,549 |
| Operations: room, wall and zone checks, reachability, brief, batch, `verify_scene` (`core/src/agent-operations`) | 6,875 | 3,174 | 10,049 |
| Agent tools: descriptions, `design_brief`, `move_node`, `duplicate_node` (`core/src/agent-tools`) | 769 | 379 | 1,148 |
| Scripted objects: usage shape (`geometry-script`) | 750 | 220 | 970 |
| MCP package (`mcp`) | 88 | 333 | 421 |
| Rest of core (systems, building, hooks, coherence, registry) | 1,257 | 132 | 1,389 |
| Skills, wiki, plugin evals, other | 42 | 0 | 42 |
| **Total** | **15,896** | **7,672** | **23,568** |

## What changes for the user, by lane

All three lanes run the same shared tools and operations from this package; what differs is when the checks run and which host switches them on.

**Chat and Medium.** After this PR plus the private bump:
- `verify_scene` reports more of what is wrong with a built house: narrow passages, furniture pockets, clashes and door swings (usage checks, behind a flag the private PR turns on), rooms that owe tile, skirting, a floor or a finish on their faces, rooms no walk from outside reaches, walls that nearly join, two zones overlapping on one floor, and item and door clearances that now carry figures.
- `design_brief` reads the request on two more axes, form and facade, both optional (a brief that leaves them out is accepted); an open form states its massing and lists its rooms.
- Under an open source, technical equipment and plants are placed from the catalog by their tags; furniture is still made.
- A `run_batch` call is checked call by call.
- The usage checks were trimmed after their findings were counted on 42 saved final scenes: a doorway limited only by a standard door leaf is information (passage warnings 322 to 227, 95 now information); a whole-room pocket that `room_unreachable` already names is dropped; an approximate outline warns from 12 cm and a bed against a window sill or frame is no clash (clash warnings 38 to 10).
- `author_scene`'s description and the pascal-3d skill state the output limit, that the payload is the whole design, and what a conversion stores and what a later call changes of it.

**Pro.** The same shared tools and findings. Pro-specific behaviour (its prompt, ledger, finish gate, toolset) is in the private PR.

**Hosted MCP.** The same findings and brief. Two tools are added to the package surface, `move_node` and `duplicate_node` (the editor's move and duplicate as shared agent tools; annotation justifications in `plugin-evals/tool-annotation-justifications.json`, rows in the OpenAI policy). The tool count goes from 87 to 89.

The standalone MCP binary and the editor app read the usage-checks flag from the environment (`PASCAL_SDF_CHECKS`, and its `NEXT_PUBLIC_` mirror in the app): off unless set to `1` or `true`. This repository does not turn them on.

## Visible differences from main

1. **`asIs` is gone.** Main made the model declare each catalog piece it wanted under an open source (`asIs`, with a reason) and view it first; the refusals `brief_as_is_furniture` and `brief_as_is_not_viewed` enforced it. Now the catalog's function tags and tags decide: technical equipment (sanitaryware, appliances, fixed services) and plants are placed from the catalog under an open source; furniture stays refused. A stored brief that holds `asIs` reads with it dropped.
2. **The brief has two more axes**, form and facade, and a rooms section, all optional fields: a `design_brief` call without `form` and `facade` is accepted (the `axis_missing` refusal does not apply to them); when given, an open form still states its massing and its rooms, an open facade its treatment (`form_massing_missing`, `rooms_missing`, `facade_treatment_missing`). A stored brief without them still reads.
3. **The open-source refusal names the tools that make the piece and their fields**, and a repeat of the same refusal in a session is short (the session keeps what was refused).
4. **New `verify_scene` findings.** Warnings unless noted.
   - Usage (flag on): `usage_passage_narrow`, `usage_pocket`, `usage_clash`, `usage_door_swing`, `usage_entry_narrow`, `usage_bed_clearance`, `usage_opening_blocked`, `usage_fixture_clearance`, `usage_door_over_stair`; `usage_turning_narrow` is information.
   - Usage rules after the 42-scene count: `usage_passage_narrow` is information when the pinch is one door frame drawn at 0.795 m or more, and says what the frame leaves clear; a whole-room `usage_pocket` is dropped when `room_unreachable` of the same result names the room (pockets beside objects stay); `usage_clash` on an approximate outline warns from 12 cm, and a bed against a window sill or frame is no finding.
   - Rooms: `room_wet_untiled`, `rooms_no_skirting`, `rooms_skirting_partial`, `wall_faces_default`, `rooms_floors_default`, `room_no_floor`, `room_unreachable`; `circulation_not_measured` names a room whose route the reading cannot measure, instead of calling it unreachable.
   - Walls and zones: `wall_nearly_aligned`, `wall_end_short`, `zones_overlap`, `floor_unclaimed`.
5. **`verify_scene` is grouped for the model**: findings come in groups with a count and a room scope, `type` and `room` inputs narrow the answer, the usage findings are folded per room, and the tool description names the finding types.
6. **Clearance findings.** `door_blocked`, `item_too_close` and `item_overlap` carry the figures and no longer name objects that are designed in place; `item_mid_room` names the piece by its kind and lets sofas and stools float; a bed head against a window is no finding; a bed with its bedside tables is read along its own head-to-foot axis. On twelve stored final scenes against main: `door_blocked` 23 to 12, `item_too_close` 34 to 11, `item_overlap` 12 to 2, `item_mid_room` 14 to 12.
7. **Stairs**: a flight of three risers or fewer has no going or comfort target.
8. **`run_batch`**: an unknown tool or an invalid input in a batch is that call's refusal, not a refusal of the whole batch. Under `stop` the batch stops at that call and applies nothing; under `skip` the other calls run.
9. **`author_scene`'s description and the pascal-3d skill state facts about the output limit**: the limit counts thinking and the call's arguments together; the payload is the whole design (a later payload with `replace: true` removes what it leaves out; one without `replace` on a converted scene is refused); a conversion stores one module and one adapter, and only when it succeeds; a later `replace: true` call with edits changes parts of them (each find text must occur once). The sentence that advertised "in one call" is gone; the skill states these facts, not an order.
10. **The usage checks stay off by default in this repository** (a host sets them), and the code table (`irc-2021`) holds values read in the code's own texts; a project's profile is read from `site.metadata.codeProfile`, which nothing in this repository writes.

## Deliberately left out

- `usage_headroom`, `usage_ceiling_coverage`: reading the roof over a room needs the free-form roof closure (about 2.9k lines) for three fixed findings in fourteen real runs. Back with the roofs.
- `hosting_item_opening_overlap`: its import closure is 16 files, 4.0k lines (coherence, cladding, free-form roofs). Back with those lots.
- The coherence engine (5.3k lines, a checklist in every write answer): `room_unreachable` ships as a plain `verify_scene` check instead.
- `room_unlit` (information): its roof and attic reading is 13 files, 2.8k lines. Back with the roofs.
- `facade_simpler_than_brief`, `facade_bounded_without_treatment`: they read the built facade through code that is not on main. The facade axis ships as an optional field.
- `room_dressing_plainer_than_brief`: measured with a dressing tool this repository does not have; 0 of 9 fixed without it. Back with a dressing lot.
- The announced-finish findings (`room_announced_*`), `rooms_announced_alike`, `rooms_same_furniture`: they read pieces that are not carried, and were fixed rarely or never.
- The direction axis, `roll_design_direction` and the style catalogue: not used in any of the real runs; the axis waits.
- `describe_circulation` and its overlay: not selected.
- Exact stair guards (posts, balusters, glass): the usage checks read each rail as a line; the guards ride with the stair lot.
- `stair_has_no_landing` and the other stair targets: rarely fixed; stair lot.
- Ramps, draped slabs and window treatments in the usage base: dead branches on main's node kinds, cut at no cost to a check.
- Flow widths and the placement guard (`place_in_room`, `furnish_room` hooks): read by no selected check.
- Setting the code profile (`set_code_profile`, the Australian NCC and French rows of the code table): no call in 43 stored projects, no panel here, and the private side does not list it. A code lot.
- The wall-object check (`usage_wall_object_protrudes`): already withheld from every report (most findings were towel rails and robe fit-outs, which stand out by design). Back with an improvement.
- Two wall-face checks, `walls_outside_finish_inside` and `room_wall_item_wrong_face`: raised in no stored run. Back when measured.
- The brief's end-of-turn findings, `form_simpler_than_brief`, `form_revised_simpler`, `facade_revised_simpler`, `room_dressing_revised_simpler`, `form_bounded_without_plan`, `rooms_not_listed`: the form finding was raised twice in 19 stored runs and never acted on, the others in none. They come back together with the refusal of an absent form or facade axis.
- `door_handle_on_hinge_side`: a joiner write rule with its check; a later joinery lot.
- Roof pierce, photo, plan and crew checks: private (Architect).

## Tests, by suite

On the head of this branch (`e490b8a4c`), in a standalone install of the editor repository (its own `bun install`, core and mcp rebuilt first):
- `packages/core`: 6,880 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail. Typecheck (`tsc -p tsconfig.contracts.json`) clean.
- `packages/mcp`: 1,419 pass, 0 fail (core and mcp rebuilt first).
- `packages/geometry-script`: 66 pass, 0 fail (the two tests that start a local Blender need more than their five-second default when the machine load is above 150).
- `skills:validate`: 75 pass, 0 fail.
- Lint (`biome`) clean on the 137 changed `.ts` and `.tsx` files; the files on the E-018 exclusion list that this branch brings are converted to `queryNodes`, no exclusion-list entry.
- The pre-push hook (lint, then `turbo run check-types` on the changed packages): 14 of 14 packages. Run inside the private repository's checkout, the `editor` package shows 2 type errors in `ceiling-bracket-batch.test.ts`, a file this PR does not touch.
- Rule tests per check: each shipping finding has its rule tests (the usage checks' tables, the room checks, wall joins, zone coverage, reachability, clearance figures, the brief's axes and gate, the batch policy). The per-call batch test was mutation-checked: without the per-object gate it fails. The v2.1 usage rules (standard door leaf, duplicate pocket, approximate clash, bed against a sill) each have a test that failed before the change.
- Replay, no model call, taken before the v2.1 usage rules above (which change severities): twelve stored final scenes of real runs read through main and through this branch. Passages 93/93, turning circles 130/130, bed clearance 22/22, clashes 17/17, wall joins 6/6 against the full lab version. Two differences, both explained: +4 pockets (the lab reads window treatments as floor prisms; main has no field for them), +2 door swings before the floor-mat rule that this branch carries.
- Tool-name audit, rerun at this head over every added non-test line: each verb-prefixed snake_case name is a tool defined here or a refusal or reason code; `place_by_relation` is matched by name in the brief gate's code and is named in no text the model reads.
- A test cleanup (builders, tables, overlapping cases) is planned as a follow-up; none is in this PR.

## Measured (3 Nov 2026, local runs; same inputs and scorer as production; Pro on Claude Opus 5.5)

Two real listings rebuilt from floor plan + front photo (A: two storeys, B: single storey). One run per cell unless noted.
- Pro furnishes (nearly) every room: rooms furnished 93–100 % on both houses, against 50 % and 11 % in production (corrected scorer: the old reading missed production's catalogue beds), on both delivery builds (4 runs).
- House A: v2.1 (before the slimming): plan "ready with retouches"; walls within 10 cm of the plan 85.3 % (production 62.9 %; earlier delivery builds 61.9 % and 63.8 %); plan score 64 → 78; rooms furnished 93 %; a bed in all 4 bedrooms. Cost 980 credit-eq and 119 min, against production's 577 and 63. The interior is still "not ready" on circulation: narrowest route 0.49 m. Across 4 runs on the same house, walls within 10 cm range from 62 % to 85 %, so single-run differences are within run-to-run variance.
- House B: plan score 81 → 69. That run's walls drift (walls within 10 cm 86 → 67 %); the v2.1 rerun, cut twice by test-runner freezes and finished in a third turn, built room by room the same way: walls within 10 cm 67.1 %, openings 65 %, every plan room furnished, 5 beds in 3 bedrooms; its time and cost are inflated by the freezes. Follow-up, not in this PR: shell tools on standby (lab switch; 1 run: 79 %).
- Medium: its request is byte-identical to production's (tool list, Author line, author_scene text). Walls within 10 cm 94.5 % and 94.8 %, inside production's 82–94 % range (11 runs).
- Known issue, not fixed here: in long local test runs the browser tab's tool executor stopped taking a pending call three times (13–22 min, with "Failed to get session" 5xx on the server). The tool executor and its tab client are unchanged from this PR's previous head. Under investigation.

These runs were measured on v2.1, before this PR was slimmed. What the slimming removed did not act in those runs: the wall-object check was already withheld from `verify_scene`, the two wall-face checks and the brief's revision/gap findings never fired in a stored run, the form read-back fired 2 times in 19 runs, and `set_code_profile` had 0 calls in 43 projects. A control run on this head follows.

## Follow-ups

- Rows in `packages/mcp/README.md` and sentences in `wiki/architecture/agent-surfaces.md` for `move_node` and `duplicate_node` are still to be written.
- `compare_to_plan` (the built house against the imported plan): its closure is the plan-import family, about 11.5k code lines; it ships with the plan lot.
- A test cleanup (shared builders, tables for repeated cases) after this PR.
- The code of every item under "Deliberately left out" that this PR moved out is kept on a branch for the later lots.

</details>

title: Sunken garage: openings reach the garage floor, doorway stays open, no veil
body:
## What does this PR do?

A wall can go below the floor it stands on: a garage sunk under the house, its wall's face going down to the garage floor. Its openings and the ground view can now follow it.

- **Openings below their floor.** author_scene doors and passages take their `sill`, negative included. Before, every door was written standing on the floor and its sill was ignored. A garage door can now fill its doorway down to the garage floor. `add_door` gets an optional `sillHeight`, rarely needed; without it a door stands on the floor as before. The window rule (editor and `add_window`) lets a window go down to the wall's real bottom, meaning the lowest of its centreline and either face. An opening's wall cut never goes below the wall itself.
- **Doorway floor.** An opening that reaches below its floor cuts its doorway, the wall's span plus 2 cm past both faces, out of every floor plate standing above its bottom. That's the band of floor plate left under the wall at the level's floor, which otherwise showed as a bar across the garage door. The plate at the door's bottom is untouched, and a door on its floor keeps its threshold.
- **Grade standing / veil.** A floor sunk below its level's floor that opens to the outside through a door reaching down to it (a walk-out garage) no longer makes the level "partly below grade". That floor counts at the level's floor, along with the other plates of the same room, or touching it, at that height. On a level with rooms, a slab outside every room (an entry pad, a stoop) is part of the site, like flatwork, not a floor the ground buries. `levelGroundBox` (the ground window's target) starts at the lowest such floor, so the window no longer opens round the whole house for a garage.

The opening clamp is deliberately not in `getOpeningFloorDatum`: the legacy-wall-datum load migration reads parsed legacy doors at `[0,0,0]` (a negative sill) and would write positions old scenes never stored.

## How to test

1. Make a house with a garage behind one front wall, sink the garage room's floor (`set_zone_intent` floor elevation −0.68), then `add_door` on the garage part of the front wall with `sillHeight` −0.73 (or re-run author_scene with that door's `sill`). The door and its wall cut reach the garage floor. From outside and from inside the garage, no band of floor crosses the doorway.
2. Same door with no sill: it stands on the floor as before, threshold included.
3. On a site with terrain, show that level alone: the level reads at grade (`list_levels`), and the ground around the house is not veiled because of the garage. Remove the door and the garage reads as a sunken room again (partly below grade).

Automated tests run locally: `bun test` in core (6513 pass), nodes (5185), viewer (949), editor (2829), mcp (1382), all 0 fail; core and nodes `tsc --build`; `bun check` (no errors). Also checked against a converted house (112 Chinaberry Bend) in the local community app.

title: nodes: the floor plan draws hosted items where they sit in 3D
body:
## What does this PR do?

Part of #992: the floor-plan half. The catalog drop on a standalone cabinet module is a separate problem and isn't changed here.

The item floor plan built each host's frame by hand in 2D (wall, item, shelf, roof face, block face). Core's `nodeLevelFrame`, which the viewer, MCP and cabinet hosting use, builds the same frames separately, and the two had drifted apart. I restored the 480-case grid from the deleted differential, but checked it against the committed 3D pose instead of the frozen copy. It fails on exactly the 76 combinations listed in the issue:

- **Block faces.** Shelves and items nested under a block-face item, and any item not at the face host's upright rotation, were composed from yaw alone. With a tilted face frame they landed up to ~0.6 m off.
- **Shelf on a wall.** An item chain under a transformed wall shelf went through the shelf's level-local pose instead of the wall's, and ended up several metres away.
- **Roof faces.** Wall-side items used their stored face depth, but `ItemSystem` seats them on the roof wall surface, so they were off by half the wall thickness.

Changes:

- `resolveItemTransform` now reads the item's level frame through `restingNodePlanFrame`. The plan uses the pose the viewer mounts, for every host chain, and about 230 lines of per-host 2D composition are gone.
- `nodeLevelFrame` (core) now applies the depth `ItemSystem` gives wall-mounted items: `wall` items are offset from the wall body's centre, and `wall-side` items sit on the chosen face of a wall or roof segment. Before this, the frame put them on the stored depth.
  - Side effect: MCP world points for wall-side items are now exact, so the "on the wall centreline" approximation note in `node-world-point.ts` is removed.
- Two floor-plan move overrides in `floorplan-move.ts` only copied the plan pose onto a frame that's now identical, so they're removed.
- The roof case in `floorplan-rendered-exits.test.tsx` pinned the stored face depth ("Production plan rendering uses stored roof-face Z…"). It now asserts the rendered pose, like the wall and ceiling cases do.

New tests:

- `column-audit3.test.tsx`: block-top, block-bottom, roof-face, shelf-on-wall and wall-back chains, three items deep. Each item's plan pose has to equal its mounted pose. On `main`, the first four fail and wall-back passes; wall-back guards the new core path.
- `level-frame-wall-mount.test.ts` (core): wall-side front/back faces, a `wall` item on a justified wall, and a wall-side item on a roof face. All four fail on `main`.
- `measure-world.test.ts` (mcp): a wall-side item is measured on its face and isn't flagged as approximate. Fails on `main`.

## How to test

1. In 2D, put an item on a block's top face, add a shelf on it, and put another item on that shelf. Rotate the block. The nested footprints stay under the items shown in 3D (on `main` they drift off).
2. Put a wall-side item on a roof segment's wall face. Its plan footprint starts on the roof wall's outer surface, where 3D draws it (on `main` it's half the wall thickness inward).
3. Put a shelf on a rotated wall, then an item, another shelf and another item on it. The whole chain lines up between 2D and 3D.
4. Run `bun --cwd packages/nodes run test`, `bun --cwd packages/core run test`, `bun --cwd packages/mcp run test` and `bun --cwd packages/editor run test`.

What I ran (Linux arm64, Bun 1.4.4):

- Test suites: nodes 5190 pass / 0 fail, editor 2829 / 0, mcp 1383 / 0, and core 6514 pass / 4 fail. The 4 core failures are the clean-bundle and scene-migrations bundle tests. They fail the same way on an unmodified `main` checkout in my environment (`Cannot find package 'undefined'` from the bundle eval).
- `check-types` for core, nodes and mcp passes.
- `bun check` reports no errors.

title: feat(wall): Dimension input overlay and continuous chain drafting in 3D and 2D floorplan
body:
### Problem or motivation

When drafting walls in Pascal Editor (in both the 3D canvas and the 2D floorplan view):
1. **Lack of numerical precision during drafting:** There is no floating dimension input overlay to enter exact wall lengths or angles via keyboard input while drafting.
2. **Discontinuous workflow:** Drafting walls currently stops after each segment instead of allowing continuous multi-point chain wall drafting.
3. **2D floorplan feedback:** During 2D wall drafting, real-time dimension input overlays and ghost wall previews are not rendered.

### Proposed solution

Implement an interactive numerical dimension input overlay and continuous multi-point chain drafting across both 3D and 2D floorplan modes:

1. **Dimension Input Overlay (packages/editor/src/components/tools/shared/dimension-input.tsx):**
   - Floating dimension input box that tracks cursor position during wall drafting.
   - Allows typing exact wall lengths (supports unit conversion via packages/core/src/lib/units.ts).
   - Managed via a dedicated dimension-draft-store.ts Zustand store for clean decoupled reactivity.

2. **Continuous Multi-Point Chain Drafting (packages/nodes/src/wall/tool.tsx &  loorplan-panel.tsx):**
   - Clicking places the current wall node and automatically starts the next wall segment from the previous endpoint.
   - Enter/Escape/double-click finalizes or cancels the drafting chain cleanly.

3. **2D Floorplan Drafting Preview (packages/editor/src/components/editor/floorplan-panel.tsx):**
   - Directly renders the dimension input overlay and ghost wall preview lines while drawing walls in the 2D floorplan view.

### Implementation

Implemented and tested on fork: https://github.com/saadmooh/parser-editor

title: Walls: repair T-junction cracks; rise to a raised upper floor
body:
## What does this PR do?

Two wall fixes from a fix pass:

- **No more dotted light leaks on baked walls.** Opening cuts and finish-band splits left T-junctions (a vertex lying on a neighbour triangle's edge without being shared). They look closed at full precision, but the bake's position quantization opens them into dotted bright cracks along wall seams and around windows. `repairWallTJunctions` now splits each affected triangle at the vertices on its edges, joining each one to the opposite corner, so no vertex is invented. Material groups are assigned first and carried to the pieces, so no face is reclassified. Band splitting also interpolates seam vertices from a canonical endpoint, so both triangles on an edge get a bit-identical vertex. Walls without T-junctions are returned untouched.
- **No slot under Floor 1 over an unraised building.** Floor 1 is one plane, lifted by the tallest foundation under it. A second ground plate without a foundation kept the plain storey height, leaving a gap the size of the other plate's lift. A base plate that carries the storey above (the same `upperStoreyFootprints` set that lifts it) now tops out at that storey's floor: its walls grow taller and its floor stays on grade, so no foundation is forced on it. A plate with nothing above keeps its own height.

Golden rebaseline (byte goldens in `viewer/src/systems/wall`): only the 40 fixture walls that had T-junctions changed (3199 → 0). Against the previous build, volume differs by ≤ 5e-8, per-material area by ≤ 7e-7 m², and bounds are identical. The other 18 walls stay byte-identical.

## How to test

1. Bake (or export to GLB and quantize) a house with windows and doors. Open it in a glTF viewer: interior walls show no dotted light seams at band heights or around openings.
2. Draw two separate ground-floor rooms with Floor 1 over both. Give one a foundation (floor height above ground). The other building's ground-floor walls rise to meet Floor 1 with no gap, and its floor stays on the ground with no foundation band.
3. A separate ground-floor room with nothing above keeps its normal wall height.

Automated (run locally): `bun test src` in `packages/core` (6515 pass), `packages/viewer` (951 pass), `packages/nodes` (5185 pass), `packages/editor` (2829 pass); `tsc --build` for core and viewer. New tests: `wall-t-junctions.test.ts` (fails with 117 T-junctions on a windowed wall without the repair) and the shed case in `floor-foundation-lift.test.ts` (fails with a 0.5 m gap without the fix).

title: test(cli,mcp): deterministic runner-safe tests + connect-phase download timeout
body:
Parity for the thilke-labs/pascal-vtt fork, where these surfaced as deterministic failures on a network-restricted self-hosted CI runner. All four files match upstream byte-for-byte before these edits.

- `packages/cli/src/http-download.ts` — Node's `request.setTimeout` only starts once the socket **connects**, so a connection that is *dropped* rather than refused hangs until the OS gives up. Arm an explicit connect-phase timer and clear it once the socket connects.
- `packages/cli/src/runtime-download.ts` — thread an optional `downloadTimeoutMs` through `EnsureWebRuntimeOptions` into `downloadToFile`.
- `packages/cli/src/runtime-download.test.ts` — the "download fails" test otherwise waits out the socket timeout and hits the 5s test limit; pass `downloadTimeoutMs: 500` so it fails fast with `runtime_download_failed`.
- `packages/mcp/src/transports/stdio.test.ts` — `createServer` uses the module-singleton live scene store; `loadScene()` skips when a scene is already loaded. Reset the store before `loadDefault()`.

Opened by a thilke-labs agent on eng-lead's request.

> **Low Risk**
> Localized network timeout and test-isolation changes; production behavior only tightens failed-connect handling within the existing timeout window.

> **Overview**

The runtime download failure test passes **`downloadTimeoutMs: 500`** so unroutable hosts that *drop* on CI fail quickly instead of outliving the test timeout.

Regroups the door and window panels around what people change first, with no new fields.

- Door order: Type → Style → Segments → Position → Dimensions → Top shape → Swing / Fold / Slide / Garage → Frame → Threshold → Casing → Hardware → Actions. title: viewer: door hardware drawn round — lever on a rose, hinge barrels, pulls, rollers
body:
## What does this PR do?

Every parametric door's hardware is drawn round instead of as flat boxes, and every saved door picks it up on load with no data change.

- Lever on a round rose at a 60 mm backset (was a 45 mm box stub), on both faces, pointing toward the hinges, seated on the raised panel under it.
- Hinges are 89 mm barrels on the knuckle axis; the swing leaf now pivots about that axis instead of its centreline, so an open leaf no longer passes through the jamb. The closed pose is unchanged.
- Closer body and arm, the arm reaching a bracket on the frame head; panic bar as a tube on end brackets; rounded pulls on folding, pocket and sliding doors; barn doors get round rollers, strap hangers and roller stops, and their X-brace now crosses in the leaf plane (it rotated about the wrong axis before).
- New kind-neutral builders in `viewer/src/lib/hardware-geometry.ts`: cached, shared geometry keyed by size, metre-scale UVs, mirrored by rotation only. Shared geometry is tagged and skipped by the door, window and generic dispose helpers; the GLB exporter strips the tag from its clones. Each builder has a triangle ceiling test.
- Budget: a default hinged door is 816 triangles (was 252 with boxes); with closer and panic bar 1344. Fewer meshes per door than before. Measured per family in the private plan; a GPU/castle receipt is not in this PR.

Passages, scripted `source` doors, curtain-wall and roof hosts, casing and the cutout proxy are untouched. First slice of the doors and windows pass (plan in the private repo); handle styles and finishes come in a later slice.

title: core: search_assets ranks matches and caps each query at 24
body:
## What does this PR do?

`search_assets` now scales to a library of thousands of items. Its result keeps the same shape for small catalogs.

- **Ranked.** Each query lists its best matches first: the exact name or id, then a whole word of the name ("bed" in "Platform Bed"), then a word that starts with the query ("Bedside Table"), then the category, then a tag or function tag, then a substring of the name, then a substring anywhere else. Ties sort by name and then keep catalog order. Every word of a query must still match somewhere across id, name, category and tags, and `functionTags` now count as tags.
- **Capped.** Each group lists at most `limit` items: 24 by default, and the new optional `limit` input goes up to 60. Each group gains `truncated`, and `total` still counts every match. When the limit cuts a group, the `hint` tells the model to add words or name a category, and lists the categories its matches fall in (e.g. `"chair" matches 30 items and lists the best 24: add words or a category to narrow it (furniture 20, outdoor 10).`). The no-match hint is unchanged.
- **MCP text no longer repeats the whole payload.** The text block keeps each item's id, name, dimensions and attachTo (only when set). `structuredContent` keeps the full capped result, including the category.

Result: `{ groups: [{ query, total, truncated, results: [{ id, name, category, dimensions, attachTo }] }], total, hint? }`. `place_items`, `furnish_room` and `place_in_room` don't use this search, so they are unchanged.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/agent-operations/operations.test.ts -t search_assets`: the shared case table passes, including the new ranking, function-tag, default-cap and `limit` cases.
2. `bun test packages/mcp/src/tools/shared-tools.test.ts -t search_assets`: the same cases pass over MCP. A 30-lamp catalog returns 24 items in both text and `structuredContent`, the text drops `category` and the floor's null `attachTo`, and the structured result keeps them.
3. Call `search_assets` with `{ queries: [{ query: "chair" }] }` on a large catalog. You should get 24 results, `truncated: true`, the full `total`, and a hint that names the categories.

title: mcp: stdio test no longer depends on scene left by earlier tests

## What does this PR do?

Makes `connectStdio > keeps one scene for the whole connection on 2026-07-28` deterministic. It failed intermittently in CI with `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'level.id')`.

The test's `createServer()` builds a `SceneBridge` on the shared live scene runtime and calls `loadDefault()`. That call keeps any scene already in the store, so when an earlier test file in the same bun process left a scene with no level, `get_scene` returned that scene and the test found no level. `createServer()` now empties the store with `bridge.setScene({}, [])` before `loadDefault()`, the same setup the other mcp tool tests use. Only the test changes; production code is untouched.

Reproduce the old failure: add a throwaway test file that calls `new SceneBridge().setScene({ [b.id]: b }, [b.id])` with a level-less `BuildingNode` `b`, then run it before the stdio test in one process (`bun test <that-file> packages/mcp/src/transports/stdio.test.ts`). On `main` this fails with the CI error. On this branch all 9 tests pass.

title: Doors and windows pass: carved leaves, handle styles, window realism, shutters, tilt-and-turn, sidelights
body:
## What does this PR do?

Doors and windows, round 2 and 3 of the pass (round 1 was #1212): the leaf, the windows, the options people reach for, and the types we were missing. Every saved door and window heals on load; no field is written to existing scenes. Validated together with the owner on a preview build before opening.

**Doors**
- A leaf that looks like a door: 110 mm stiles and rails on new doors and in the style presets (detection still recognises the legacy look), panels carved into the leaf with a sticking bevel (never standing proud), glazing beads, a 3 mm leaf-to-frame gap, a jamb stop bead on rectangular swing frames. A saved leaf that is exactly the legacy default Panel look draws with the new one.
- Hardware: `handleStyle` lever (default), lever-curved, knob, bar, plate; the closer sits on the pull side and articulates (two-link arm to a shoe on the head); panic bar `crossbar` or `touchbar` with optional latch rods; no lever beside a panic bar; hardware tessellation halved from round 1 (hinged door ≈ 3 500 triangles).
- New: sidelights and transom (`sidelightLeft`, `sidelightRight`, `transomHeight`; `getDoorOpeningSize` is the single source of the cutout for CSG, casing, reveal, floor plan, placement, clearance, curtain limits and IFC), sliding `slidingStyle` patio (2–4 panels) or bypass, folding up to 8 panels.
- Finishes: `metal-black`, `metal-bronze`, `preset-glass-frosted`, `preset-glass-tinted`.

**Windows**
- Realism heal: sash, mullion, grid and glass depth capped so thick walls stop growing block sashes; the frame-coloured hinge markers that poked through both faces are gone.
- Hardware slot following the frame finish, espagnolette handle and barrel hinges on casement, French, awning, hopper and tilt-and-turn (`windowHandle` turns them off).
- `openingDirection` outward | inward for casement and awning (new ones outward, saved ones keep their look). One helper decides the exterior face; the outside sill, inside sill, shutters and roller shutters use it (a window placed from inside a room keeps its sill outdoors).
- New type `tilt-turn` with `tiltTurnMode` tilt | turn, posed through `window-pose.ts` so the baked clip matches.
- `sashGrid`: the stored row and column ratios per operable sash; `add_window` sets it when a grid is asked for on an operable window.
- Sills: `sillInterior` (+ depth, thickness, overhang), `sillOverhang`, a `sill` paint slot.
- Shutters: louvered, panel or board-and-batten, `shutterSides`, `shutterWidth` defaulting to half the window per side (bifold above 0.75 m), `shutterOpen`, hung outside the casing; `rollerShutter` box (with `rollerShutterBoxHeight`) or concealed, `rollerShutterOpen`. Shutters animate as a mechanism *part*: `MechanismCapability.parts` (optional, plugin-safe), a second action-bar button, and in the bake a `<id>: shutters` clip the published viewer plays on a click on a shutter or F in the walkthrough.

**Panels** (both kinds): size first, then look, opening, frame and trim, hardware; Open slider on hinged doors; Handle side row removed (hinge side places the handle); segment Depth reaches recessed values; Finish rows (paint picker) for door hardware, window hardware, sill, shutters; every new field above has its control; two-line segmented labels wrap cleanly. Agent tools (`add_door`, `add_window`, `create_room`, `author_scene`) and the pascal-3d skill carry the new fields.

Plan and owner decisions live in the private repo.

## How to test

1. Open a scene with existing doors and windows. Expected: carved panels, round hardware, thin window sashes, no data change (no save prompt).
2. Add a hinged door; in Hardware switch Style through Lever, Knob, Bar, Plate; enable Panic bar, pick Touchbar, Latch rods. Expected: each renders; no lever on the push face with a panic bar; Open in Swing turns the leaf about the hinge knuckles and the closer arm follows.
3. In Dimensions set Left sidelight 0.35, Transom 0.4. Expected: the cutout and casing grow around the leaf; the floor plan symbol follows.
4. Add a casement in a wall between rooms from the room side. Expected: the outside sill is outdoors; Opens Outward/Inward swings the sash accordingly; `Divide each sash` draws bars in the sash.
5. Set Window type Tilt and turn; Mode Tilt then Turn; drag Open. Expected: tilts inward about the bottom, then swings inward about the hinges.
6. Shutters: Board and batten, Open 0 → closed shutters meet; a 2.4 m window gets bifold leaves; Roller shutter Box then Concealed with Open 50 %. Click the shutters button in the action bar. Expected: leaves swing on their hinge edge; the curtain rolls.
7. Export GLB. Expected: `<id>: open` and `<id>: shutters` clips; in the published viewer a click on the shutter toggles the shutters, a click on the sash the sash.
8. `cd packages/core && bun test src` (6 9xx pass), `cd packages/viewer && bun test src` , `cd packages/nodes && bun test src/door src/window src/shared`, `cd packages/editor && bun test src/lib src/components`; all green at push time.

title: core: a door's cutout stays put on a facing flip; a transom cannot rise through the wall
body:
## What does this PR do?

Two review findings on #1215, both about doors with sidelights or a transom.

- **A facing flip no longer shifts the cutout.** With unequal sidelights the cutout centre is offset from the leaf in the door's own frame; a 180° change of facing (`create_room`'s reconcile, Flip side, agent patches of `side` or `rotation`) mirrored that offset in the wall, so the opening, casing and keep-out jumped by the left/right difference. `doorPositionForFacing` moves the leaf so the cutout stays where it was, and every path that rewrites a door's facing uses it.
- **A transom cannot rise through the wall.** The agent paths (`add_door`, `create_room`, `author_scene`, `move_node`) refuse a cutout taller than the wall at that spot with `wall_too_low`, in the same voice as `wall_too_short` and not bypassable with `force`; the editor's placement and move trim the transom, never the leaf.

## How to test

1. `create_room` with an entry door `sidelightLeft: 0.6, sidelightRight: 0` on an exterior wall drawn in either direction. Expected: after reconcile the cutout is centred on the planned `t`; no overlap or off-wall state.
2. Select such a door, press Flip side. Expected: the opening in the wall does not move; the leaf shifts by the sidelight difference.
3. `add_door` with `transomHeight: 1.5` on a 2.7 m wall. Expected: refusal `wall_too_low`. Drag the Transom slider on a placed door past the wall top. Expected: it stops under the top.

title: Viewer: daylight look for the colored appearance; Quality tiers and a sky panel
body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives the viewer's **colored appearance** a physically based daylight look, and reworks its settings. The monochrome appearance is unchanged.

**Daylight rendering (`@pascal-app/viewer`)**
- A real sun position (site location and date) with a single shadowed key light, a PMREM sky environment, clouds, a ground that fades to the horizon, stars at night, and metered exposure with eye-like white balance.
- A room light system: rooms, window portals and openings are found from the scene; lamps light their rooms (virtual ceiling lamps where a room has none); light comes through windows by day and spills out at night. Exterior lamps keep their spot cones.
- Tuned materials: glass, EON rough diffuse, an albedo clamp (sRGB 40–243), and lamp emitters that follow their lamp's switch.
- Outside at night, the exposure and white balance also take the lit rooms in view into account, so lamplit interiors no longer blow out from outside.
- Exterior lamps shine at their authored intensity with plain N·L for spots, like the scene's real lights.
- The shadow frustum reaches to where shadows meet the ground, so long shadows are no longer cut off.
- three.js is bumped to **0.187**. That release depads WebGPU readbacks itself, so snapshot (and feed) readbacks no longer depad a second time, which sheared captures into horizontal streaks.

**Settings (`@pascal-app/editor`)**
- **Quality: Auto · Low · Medium · High**, replacing Solid/Rendered. Auto (the default) picks the tier from the device's capabilities: WebGPU availability, software adapter, GPU model, memory and form factor. It never uses frame rate. A manual pick still wins.
- Edges are monochrome only, on/off.
- **Time & weather** move to a chip beside the compass, in both the editor and the viewer, lined up with the bottom dock. It opens a Sky panel: drag the sun along its arc to any time, pick a preset (which eases the sun slowly), follow the live clock, or set cloud cover. The display menus point to it while it is mounted.

## How to test

1. Open a project in the editor or viewer with the colored appearance, then open the time/weather chip next to the compass.
2. Drag the sun across the day and click presets (the light eases there); cycle the cloud cover from the chip.
3. At night, compare a cutaway of lit rooms from outside with the view from inside a room, and check exterior wall lights and spots.
4. Display → Quality: Auto shows the tier picked for your device; switch tiers.
5. Take a snapshot at a canvas width that isn't a multiple of 64 px: the capture is intact.

## Screenshots / screen recording

## Notes

- Known gaps: heavy baked scenes can run slowly on High (baked GLBs get no static mesh merging yet); thumbnails still use SSGI ambient occlusion.
- Unit tests cover room lighting (hidden levels, viewed-room metering), device tiers, readback rows and the quality store.

## Summary

Adds `skills/architect/` — a small router skill for Architect (an AI building designer; higher effort on Pro/Max) on the hosted Pascal MCP — and wires it into marketplace plugin manifests.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Marketplace re-pin ordering:** Do **not** hand Aymeric the merge SHA for a Cursor marketplace re-pin until [private-editor#1477](https://github.com/pascalorg/private-editor/pull/1477) is **deployed to prod** and authorize with `architect:run` returns **302**. Re-pinning earlier will make clients request a scope prod does not yet allow (`invalid_scope`). If #1477 misses the window, strip `architect:run` from this PR's mcp.json scopes before pin.
>
> **Merge method:** **squash-merge** only, so intermediate branch commits with superseded public copy never land on `main`.

## Changes

### New skill: `skills/architect/`

`SKILL.md` documents:
- **When to use Architect vs scene tools**: generative design / BIM-style studies go to Architect; direct node edits stay with Pascal scene MCP tools.
- **MCP tool workflow**: `ask_architect` → poll `get_architect_turn` → surface `editorUrl`; `cancel_architect_turn` on user cancel.
- **Plans**: higher effort available on Pascal Pro/Max; if a tool returns an upgrade or top-up link, show it and stop.
- **Hard limits**: no fetching remote instruction URLs; no downloading or executing code from tool results.

Includes bounded evals and trigger-evals.

### Plugin wiring

- Plugin manifests add `./architect` to `skills`.
- Descriptor versions bumped `0.1.10 → 0.1.11`.

### MCP scope

- `architect:run` added to `pascal-hosted` OAuth scopes in `.cursor-plugin/mcp.json` and `skills/.cursor-plugin/mcp.json`. OAuth CLIENT_ID remains `pascal-cursor`; no API key headers.

### Scripts / docs

title: core, mcp: agent tools read a catalog source per call, not the whole list
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a host lend the agent tools a searchable item library instead of the whole list. Today every hosted MCP session and every chat tab holds the full `AssetInput[]`; at the 115k items the hosted library is growing to, that is about 80 MB per session or tab.

- **`AssetCatalog`** (core): a list held whole, as before (the standalone MCP's built-in list), or an `AssetCatalogSource`: `search({ text?, category?, limit })` returns `{ items, total, categories? }`, and `byId(ids)` returns the items a call names.
- **The operations stay sync.** `readCatalog(nodes, tool, input, catalog)` reads what a call names before it runs (`catalogReads`): the searches of `search_assets`, the items named by `place_items`, `place_in_room` and `view_assets`, `furnish_room`'s set for its room type (`FURNISH_ROOM_ASSETS`, held to the layout by the sets test), the catalog items a role-less `paint` finishes, and each call of a batch. A list is handed over whole. A call that names nothing reads nothing.
- **`search_assets`** lists a source's answers (`AgentContext.catalogSearches`) in the host's order, and keeps `total`, `truncated` and the narrowing hint. The hint uses the categories the host counted; without them it says to add words. A list is searched as before (`searchAssetList`). `rankAssets` is exported so a host that finds hits its own way can order them the same way: the exact name first.
- **MCP**: `createPascalMcpServer({ catalog })` takes the `AssetCatalog` as is. `builtInCatalog` is now the list, and the loader type and `cachedCatalog` are removed. Each tool call reads through `readCatalog`. Under an open brief the design-brief gate still reads only the pieces the call names. `pascal://catalog/items` lists a source's first 100 items with its total.
- `assetViewsReadCatalog` and `namesCatalogPieces` are removed: `readCatalog` now decides what a call reads. `placedAssets` and `roleLessPaints` are exported for it.
- `wiki/architecture/agent-surfaces.md` documents the source.

Breaking for hosts that passed `catalog` as a loader function or called `builtInCatalog()`: pass the list, or a source.

## How to test

1. `bunx tsgo --build editor/packages/core editor/packages/mcp` (from the private monorepo root): no errors.
2. `bun test editor/packages/core/src` (7059 pass) and `bun test editor/packages/mcp` (1515 pass). The core and MCP case runners now run every shared case that has a catalog twice, once on a list and once on a source (`(catalog source)` in the test name), so 85 more cases per runner.
3. `asset-catalog.test.ts`: what each call reads, a list handed over whole, a source asked only for what a call names, and `search_assets` keeping a source's order, total and hint.
4. `shared-tools.test.ts` (MCP): a host's source answers `search_assets` in its own order, and nothing else of it is read. `resources.test.ts`: `pascal://catalog/items` on a source lists the first items and the total.
5. `bun check`: no errors (the existing warnings are unchanged).

title: Viewer: cap the frame rate on software renderers
body:
## What does this PR do?

Caps the viewer's frame rate at 20 fps when the device renders on the CPU (a software WebGPU adapter, SwiftShader, llvmpipe), detected with the existing device tier. GPUs are unaffected.

On a software rasterizer the usual 50 fps cadence is out of reach, and chasing it starves the app of the cores it renders on. The daylight look from #1217 has heavier frames, which made this bite: editor E2E specs ran about 1.6× slower on CI's GPU-less browser and timed out.

Measured locally on SwiftShader (undo/redo E2E spec): 64 s before, 47 s with the cap (41 s in monochrome). The paint spec passes in 21 s.

## How to test

1. In a browser with hardware acceleration off (or headless Chromium with `--use-angle=swiftshader`), open a project: the device is detected as a software renderer, and frames are capped at 20 fps.
2. With a GPU, nothing changes.

> **Low Risk**
> Render-loop cadence change only when a software rasterizer is detected; GPU users and persisted preferences are unaffected.
> 
> **Overview**
> When WebGPU init completes, the viewer now records whether rendering is **CPU/software** (fallback adapter, SwiftShader, llvmpipe, etc.) via new **`isSoftwareRenderer`** in `device-tier`, stored as transient **`softwareRenderer`** in the viewer store alongside detected quality tier.
> 
> **`<FrameLimiter>`** then uses **`min(maxFps, 20)`** instead of the default 50 fps cap on those devices, so the loop does not burn CPU chasing an unreachable cadence. Hardware GPU paths are unchanged.
> 
> Unit tests cover software vs GPU detection strings.

title: Viewer perf: cached sun shadows, lit-only outside lighting, static merge for baked scenes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Ports the two big performance optimizations from the daylight look's reference renderer that #1217 didn't bring over, and trims the outside-lighting shader. Baked GLB scenes (viewer, walkthrough) were slow on big houses even on fast machines.

**1. Cached sun shadows.** The sun's shadow map (4096 px on High) re-rendered every frame, a full extra pass over every caster, moon included at night. It now re-renders only when something it depends on changes: the light's placement, frustum or settings, or a caster that moves, appears, vanishes or swaps geometry. That covers editing, opening doors, exploding or toggling levels, and time of day. It's tracked with a cheap per-frame signature, so no system has to remember to invalidate. Orbiting and walking reuse the map.

**2. Outside lighting from lit sources only.** The night window-spill and lantern loops ran over every window and exterior lamp, for every pixel, day and night. They now loop over compact lists of the windows whose room has a lamp on and the exterior lamps that are on, rewritten on lamp and door changes. Indoor pixels skip them. The output is pixel-identical.

**3. Static merge for baked artifacts** (`lib/glb-merge.ts`):
- A big baked house is ~4,000 meshes drawn once per pass, and on WebGPU each draw costs CPU to encode.
- Static meshes merge per level, ~24 m cell, material and surface role into one mesh under their level, so level visibility, explode and solo still apply.
- A moving part's meshes (sash, door leaf, shutter) merge under that part and swing with it.
- The originals stay on the existing `BATCHED_LAYER` via `hideFromScene(…, 'batched')`: never drawn or shadowed, but still hit by pointer, reticle and room rays and by the walkthrough collider, and still outlined.
- Interactive items, loose glass, ceilings and roofs, the site, zones and plugin kinds stay individual.
- Batches follow monochrome by role. The merge rebuilds if a merged mesh is shown or hidden on its own.
- `?merge=0` turns it off for comparison.

## Results

Median, M5 Max, headless, baked GLBs of two production projects:

| | Overview | Walkthrough |
|---|---|---|
| House, 4.3k meshes, midday | 10 → 32 fps | 22 → 50 fps (cap) |
| Condo, 72 windows, night | 10 → 42 fps | 18 → 50 fps (cap) |

The condo overview goes from ~8,600 to ~1,800 draws per frame. Merged and unmerged renders match (mean pixel difference ~1/255, day and night), monochrome and exploded levels look the same, the walkthrough collider is identical, and shadows still update on a time-of-day change.

## How to test

1. Open a big baked project in the viewer; compare with `?merge=0`; add `?perf` for the overlay.
2. In walkthrough, open a door or window: it swings (merged under its moving part).
3. Hover or select furniture: the outline still draws.
4. Change time of day: shadows follow.

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)

> **Overview**
> **Performs major baked-GLB optimizations** by introducing `mergeBakedStatic` batched meshes (toggleable via `?merge=0`) with lifecycle rebuilding when interactives or visibility signatures change, refreshes monochrome styling on merged batches, fixes outline proxies for batched geometry, and extends raycast/collider paths (including walkthrough BVHs) to respect the new layers.

## What does this PR do?

`SceneBridge` currently parses create patches and `validateScene()` against the built-in node union only. A node kind registered through the plugin registry can therefore work in core/plugin flows but still be rejected at the MCP bridge boundary.

This change keeps the built-in parser as the first path, then falls back to the registered schema for the node's `type` when the built-in parse fails. The same helper is used for create patches and scene validation.

A focused regression test registers a minimal plugin kind, creates it through `applyPatch`, and verifies that the resulting scene validates cleanly.

Built-in and unregistered node behavior is unchanged.

## How to test

Validated against current `main`:

- `bun x biome check packages/mcp/src/bridge/scene-bridge.ts packages/mcp/src/bridge/scene-bridge.test.ts`
- `bun test packages/mcp/src/bridge/scene-bridge.test.ts` → 56 passed, 0 failed
- `bunx turbo run test --filter=@pascal-app/mcp` → 1,516 passed, 0 failed
- `bun test packages/core/src/registry/plugin-v1-conformance.test.ts` → 12 passed, 0 failed
- `bun --cwd packages/mcp run build` → passed
- `bun run check` → exit 0

## Screenshots

Not applicable. This is a headless MCP bridge change.

- [x] My code follows the project's style (`bun check`)

> Localized parsing/validation change in the headless MCP bridge with regression tests; built-in node behavior is unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> The MCP **SceneBridge** no longer validates nodes only against the built-in `AnyNode` union. It now uses a shared **`parseRegisteredNode`** helper that keeps **`parseNode`** as the first path and, on failure, validates against the **plugin `nodeRegistry`** schema for the node's `type`.
> 
> That helper is wired into **`applyPatch`** create validation and **`validateScene`**, so plugin kinds can be created through patches and pass scene checks when they match their registered schema; invalid plugin payloads still fail with schema errors.
