title: core, mcp: per-surface tool notes and stub-sized first sentences
body:
## What does this PR do?

Removes misleading and surface-specific text from what agents read in shared tool contracts, and makes each tool's first sentence work as a stub.

**1. Each surface reads only its own text (`surfaceNotes`).** A shared contract's `description` is read by every surface's agent, so it now states only what is true everywhere. What one surface alone does goes in a new optional, typed `surfaceNotes: { mcp?, chat? }` on `AgentToolContract`, and `surfaceDescription(contract, surface)` (core, zod-free) returns the shared text followed by that surface's note. Every MCP registration of a shared contract goes through it: the core tools, the hosted service tools and the project file tools.

- `view_scene`: the shared description carried MCP-only guidance that the chat also read ("Over the MCP the user's editor tab… editor_tab_required… editor_tab_hidden… editor_tab_busy"). That now sits in the MCP note. The note also stops saying that a call with no tab open is always refused: where the host offers it, an editor on its servers renders the view (for credits).
- `design_brief`: the description mixed chat and MCP behaviour ("The chat checks the quote… over MCP, where there is no message…", "In the chat a brief lasts for the turn; over MCP it lasts for the session"). The chat note now says quotes are checked against the person's message of the turn and that a brief lasts for the turn. The MCP note says there is no message, so no quote is compared (a source quote must still name its source), and that a brief lasts for the session. The shared text keeps the rest, refusal codes included.

**2. `create_house_from_brief` describes what it actually does.** It used to say "High-level hosted workflow for external agents: choose a starter house from a brief, create/save/publish it". The code replaces the session's scene with a starter template picked from `bedroomCount`, `rooms` (garden, patio or yard) and `landscaping`. `brief`, `style` and `constraints` neither choose nor shape it (`brief` is only echoed in the summary). It saves with `saveMode: 'draft'`, `publish: false`. The description now says exactly that, and the agent guide's line about the tool no longer says it publishes. No behaviour change.

**3. First sentences that work as stubs.** A host can send a tool by its first sentence alone, split at the first `.`, `!` or `?` followed by a space and cut at 200 characters. These 13 core contracts opened with 207 to 685-character sentences, so their stubs were clipped mid-list. Each now opens with what the tool does and returns, in 122 to 160 characters. The rest of each description is kept: the old first sentence's detail becomes the next sentence. The tools are `move_node`, `duplicate_node`, `get_site`, `get_source`, `design_brief`, `add_level`, `find_by_type`, `move_roofs_to_roof_level`, `set_checkpoint`, `create_stair`, `add_corner_window`, `straighten_facade_photo` and `set_zone_intent`.

| Tool | New first sentence (chars) |
| --- | --- |
| `move_node` | Move one node as the editor's move tool does, re-seated on its wall, ceiling, roof segment or level, and return where it now sits and whether it clamped. (153) |
| `duplicate_node` | Duplicate nodes with everything under them, as the editor's Duplicate does, and return each copy's id beside its source's. (122) |
| `get_site` | Read the site a building stands on and return, in its level coordinates, its lot, buildable area, street side, north, ground and the footprint's yards. (151) |
| `get_source` | Read the code module a scripted node runs and return it with its language (three.js or Blender bpy) and its params at their current values. (139) |
| `design_brief` | Record the request's design brief before furnishing, read axis by axis with a vision and where the objects come from, and return what it unlocks. (145) |
| `add_level` | Add an empty level to a building as the editor does, above its top storey or below its lowest for a basement, and return its id, floor index and height. (152) |
| `find_by_type` | Find every node, item, light or scripted part of one type in the scene, wherever it lives, and return the matches with their count. (131) |
| `move_roofs_to_roof_level` | Move the roofs a storey holds on its own walls to the level the roof rule gives them, and return the roofs moved and the level they went to. (140) |
| `set_checkpoint` | Name this moment of your work (a roof, a floor, a batch of walls) for verify_scene({ since: name }) to compare against, and return the checkpoints kept. (152) |
| `create_stair` | Create a straight, L or U staircase rising from a level, as the editor's stair tool builds one, and return its id, its footprint and where the top step arrives. (160) |
| `add_corner_window` | Add a window that wraps the corner where two walls meet, one window on each wall joined at the corner, and return their windowIds and wallIds. (142) |
| `straighten_facade_photo` | Straighten the faces of a building photo into metric elevations to measure its facade, and return each on a metre grid and a camera pose when recoverable. (154) |
| `set_zone_intent` | Update a room's intent in one patch (name, floor, ceiling, steps, walls, daylight, outdoor type, porch framing, decking) and return how many changes it made. (157) |

No input schema or tool name changes. `agent-surfaces.md` documents the note and the first-sentence rule. `delete_project_file` said "Existing scene or chat references may still retain the bytes"; it now says "A scene or a conversation that references it may still retain the bytes". That caveat holds on every surface, so it stays in the shared text, and the lint needs no exception.

**Host follow-up when the submodule is bumped.** The MCP now lists `view_scene` and `design_brief` with their MCP notes, so the hosted `agent-surface-parity.test.ts` should compare each surface with `surfaceDescription(contract, surface)` instead of `contract.description`. The hosted chat should also register `surfaceDescription(contract, 'chat')` where it defines shared tools. Until it does, the chat reads only the shared `design_brief` text, without its turn note.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/core && bun test src`: 7060 pass, 0 fail. This includes `contracts-purity.test.ts`, whose new test fails on any shared description (core, hosted service and project file contracts) that names MCP or chat as a word.
2. `cd packages/mcp && bun test`: 1516 pass, 0 fail. The new `MCP tool descriptions` test in `read-tool-annotations.test.ts` registers every tool, the hosted service and file tools included, and lists them through a real client. It checks each shared contract's listed description against the contract's own fields: it starts with the shared description, ends with the MCP note (or equals the shared description when there is none) and holds no other surface's note. It also compares it with `surfaceDescription(contract, 'mcp')`. `view_scene` carries `editor_tab_required`, and `design_brief` carries the session note, never the chat note. Registering `view_scene` with the bare description makes the test fail, and so does a helper that appends the chat note, which the comparison with the helper alone would miss.
3. `tsgo --build` in `packages/core`, `packages/geometry-script` and `packages/mcp`, plus `tsc -p tsconfig.contracts.json` in core: no errors.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A — non-visual change

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Mostly documentation/test changes, but MCP clients now see different tool copy that could confuse hosts until chat adopts `surfaceDescription`.
> 
> **Overview**
> Introduces **surface-specific notes** on shared contracts via `surfaceNotes` plus `surfaceDescription`, so MCP now registers shared tools and `view_scene` with shared text plus the MCP-only note instead of embedding chat wording in the base description.
> 
> **design_brief** and **view_scene** move previously mixed MCP/chat behavior into per-surface notes; **create_house_from_brief**’s MCP description/agent guide line now match the template-only draft reality (no publish claim).
> 
> Rewrites the opening sentence of many heavy tool descriptions to short “does & returns” stubs (movement, duplication, site/levels, stairs, windows, photos, checkpoints, roofs, zones, etc.).
> 
> Adds a purity test that flags shared descriptions naming a surface and an MCP integration test ensuring listed tools equal `surfaceDescription(...,'mcp')` without leaking chat notes; documentation in `agent-surfaces.md` explains the pattern for future surfaces.

title: viewer: selection callout, interaction sounds and drone mode
body:
## What does this PR do?

A viewer pass: selection, actions and camera modes.

- **Selection callout.** Selecting an element in the viewer now shows the marketing house's callout: a dot on the element, a hairline, its name and kind ("Single-hung window", "Hinged door"), one pill per action and a close button. It replaces the floating On/Open buttons that popped on every item of a selected room. It works on parametric and baked scenes, and in the editor's preview.
  - **Actions:** open and close doors, windows and shutters; lights; a recipe item's moving parts; catalog toggles and sliders.
  - **Rooms:** a selected room gets the callout too, with its name and area.
  - **Clicks:** a click in orbit only selects now; nothing opens on click.
- **Sounds.** Operating something plays its sound through a new core `interaction:sound` event, which the editor's SFX bus plays.
  - **Closing:** a door, window or recipe door swings, then latches on the frame it lands. Built-in leaves report through `door:` / `window:animation-completed`. Baked clips use the remaining clip time. Recipes use a new `procedural:motion-settled` event, backed by the motion controller's `settled` flag.
  - **Pointer:** hover, select and deselect tick like the house (`useViewerUiSounds`).
  - **Walkthrough:** E and click play the same sounds.
  - **Assets:** door, garage and shutter recordings come from the house; the switch, UI ticks and swing are rendered by `scripts/synth-viewer-cues.ts`.
- **Drone mode** sits beside the walkthrough: a Drone button in the viewer bar and key hints in the walkthrough HUD. There is one flight implementation (`drone-flight.ts`, `DroneController` in viewer), and the snapshot capture drone now runs on it too.

## How to test

1. Open a scene in the viewer (preview mode, or the hosted viewer) and select a floor, then a room. The room shows a callout with its name and area; no buttons pop on its items.
2. Click a door or a window. Expected:
   - The callout shows its name, kind and an Open/Closed pill.
   - The click itself does not open it.
   - The pill opens it with a sound. Closing plays a swing, then the latch as the leaf lands.
3. Select a window with shutters: Closed and Shutters pills sit on one row, with × after them. Select a recipe cabinet: closing a door swings and claps when it lands; a drawer claps when it lands.
4. Press × or Esc: the selection clears, with the deselect tick. Hovering elements ticks faintly.
5. Click the Drone button in the bar. Expected:
   - Key hints show at the bottom.
   - WASD, Space/E and Q fly; Shift boosts; Alt slows.
   - P frees the cursor; Esc returns to orbit.
6. In the editor's snapshot capture, Drone still flies as before.

Automated, run locally:
- Tests: `bun test` in packages/viewer (1333 pass), packages/editor `src/components src/lib` (2594 pass), packages/core `src/procedural-items`, packages/nodes `src/procedural-item`.
- Type check: `tsgo --noEmit` for core, viewer, editor and nodes.
- Lint and i18n: `bun run check` (warnings only, all pre-existing), `bun run i18n:check`, `bun scripts/i18n-literals.ts check`.

New strings have fr/es/ja/zh-CN drafts flagged for review.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet.

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> **Overview**
> **Selection and baked GLB.** Orbit clicks now only change selection; doors, windows, shutters, mechanisms, recipe parts, and catalog items expose actions through a new **SelectionCallout** (and **GlbSelectionCallout** on baked scenes) with localized titles and pills, plus room callouts for name and area. title: Viewer perf: occlusion culling, high tier without AO pre-pass, readable highlights
body:
Follow-up to #1224.

## Occlusion culling for baked scenes
Each time the camera moves, the building's opaque walls, slabs, roofs and ceilings are rasterized on the CPU into a 256-px depth image. Every drawn mesh (static-merge batches and the meshes left individual) whose box lies wholly behind it is skipped for that render through three's drawing pipeline (`isCulled`).
- Same-frame and conservative: no readback lag, occluder image eroded by a pixel, boxes dilated, anything crossing the near plane is drawn.
- Only renders through the main camera are culled: the sun's cached shadow map and captures still see everything.
- Recomputed when the camera moves (1.5-3.5 ms), otherwise only when the scene changes. Shows as `occlusion-cull` in `?perf`; `?occlusion=0` draws everything.
- Measured (M5 Max headless, A/B in one session): rn9 overview 26 -> 32 fps (3229 -> 2302 draws), hav5 overview 38 -> 50 fps (capped; 1829 -> 1049 draws). Screenshots on vs off are identical.
- Not added to the editor: there, the most it could save in an overview is ~4.6 ms of CPU (batched instances are cheap draws), about what culling would cost while moving.

## High tier: GTAO from the scene pass
The enhanced viewer's high tier fed GTAO from a depth/normal/velocity pre-pass, which draws the whole scene a second time. On an editor scene that doubled every draw. High now uses medium's path at full resolution.
- Editor, 5-level house, high: 40 -> 46 fps, encode 22.8 -> 12.0 ms, draws 7873 -> 3994.

## Editor highlights stay readable
- The selection tint ran at full strength: its intensity was `max(material's, 0.12)`, and a material's default is 1. `tintEmissive` folds the strength into the colour (selection 0.12, wall hover 0.08, delete unchanged).
- At night the daylight look treated the tinted clone as a glowing surface (night boost, exposure lift, bloom), and on lamp items the lamp system turned it into a lamp emitter. A selected fan lit up like a bulb. `markHighlight` flags highlight materials: kept out of all of that, with exposure-compensated emission so the tint reads the same day and night, and its own program cache key (three's ignores `userData`).

## Test plan
- [x] `check-types`, viewer tests (1345), nodes tests, editor component tests, biome
- [x] Occlusion culler unit tests (box behind/beside/in front of walls, glass, merged walls, holes, near plane, orthographic, pipeline hook)
- [x] Visual A/B on rn9 and hav5 (overview, walkthrough), editor selection at night and midday

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds a custom occlusion culler hook and reworks GTAO/daylight lighting paths, so GPU/CPU rendering behavior could regress if culling or AO math misclassifies geometry.
> 
> **Overview**
> **perf(viewer): occlusion culling, GTAO rework, highlight fixes**
> 
> Introduces a conservative CPU occlusion culler for baked GLB scenes that rasterizes major shells into a tiny depth buffer and plugs into `renderer.drawingPipeline.isCulled`, toggleable with `?occlusion=0`, rebuilding whenever static merges update. High-quality ambient occlusion now shares the single scene-pass medium-tier path at full resolution (drops the extra pre-pass), rewires daylight room lighting to match, and keeps temporal buffers consistent.
> 
> Adds an `editor-highlight` toolkit (`markHighlight`, `tintEmissive`) so selection clones keep stable tint strength, bespoke program keys, and skip daylight emitter/bloom boosts; wall highlights adopt the same behavior. Bloom now masks highlighted pixels via the lighting MRT channel, room emitters ignore highlight clones, and Bun tests cover the new helpers plus the occlusion module.
> 
> **Risk:** Medium — touches WebGPU post-processing, daylight lighting hooks, and a new render-time culling path that could mis-hide meshes if assumptions break.
>

title: mcp: prompt facts (window default, final answer, view rendering)
body:
Three corrections to text the public MCP package puts in a client's context. They come from an audit of what misleads the model across agent lanes (findings X10, X11, X12); each claim was re-verified against the code before the change. No behavior changes: prompts, one resource, the README and one test list.

## Window default (X11)

`packages/mcp/src/prompts/scene-guidance.ts:6` said "Window default: 1.5m wide by 1.5m high with a 0.9m sill height."

Evidence:
- `packages/core/src/building/wall-openings.ts:263-268`: `DEFAULT_WINDOW = { width: 1.5, height: 1.5 }`, door `0.9 x 2.1`; the comment says a window's sill "is not a number".
- `packages/core/src/building/wall-openings.ts:412-426`: with no `sillHeight`, a window's centre is `resolveWallOpeningCeiling(wall) / 2`, that is, centred vertically on the wall; a door stands on the floor. For a 2.5 m wall and a 1.5 m window the implicit sill is 0.5 m, not 0.9 m.
- `packages/core/src/agent-operations/wall-opening.ts:9-13`: `add_window` goes through `planWallOpening`, so the tool applies the same default; its description (`packages/core/src/agent-tools/wall-openings.ts:246`) already says "centred vertically on the wall, or on sillHeight above the floor when given".

Now: "Window default: 1.5m wide by 1.5m high, centred vertically on its wall unless sillHeight is given."

## Tool-only output against a final answer (X12)

- `packages/mcp/src/prompts/from-brief.ts:21` said "Respond ONLY with tool calls. Do not produce verbose narrative or prose; keep any explanations in short tool-call arguments." while the same prompt's task (`from-brief.ts:41`) asks the client to "return the `editorUrl`", and the agent guide's output contract (`packages/mcp/src/resources/agent-guide.ts:96`) asks for project name, `editorUrl`, version, summary and limitations in the final response.
- `packages/mcp/src/prompts/iterate-on-feedback.ts:17` and `packages/mcp/src/prompts/renovation-from-photos.ts:16` carried "Respond ONLY with tool calls. No prose."

All three lines are replaced by one short instruction consistent with the guide: when the work is done, report what was verified and the project `editorUrl` (from_brief names `verify_scene` and `get_project_status`, which its task already calls). No test pinned the removed strings (`packages/mcp/src/prompts/prompts.test.ts` checks tool names and section headings only).

## How a view is rendered (X10)

`packages/mcp/src/resources/agent-guide.ts:73` said "On a hosted server the person's open editor tab renders it", followed by three host-specific tab codes with instructions for each. A host may render another way (Pascal's hosted server renders on its own servers when no tab is available).

Evidence in the package: `packages/mcp/src/tools/view-scene.ts:37-52` defines `SceneViewHost`, the interface a host implements to render (`capture`), and `view-scene.ts:69-73` refuses `view_unavailable` ("This Pascal server has no editor to render with: take sizes and counts from the tools.") when the host passes none. The tab codes are produced by the host, not by this package.

Now, host-neutral: the server has no renderer of its own; the host renders the view, through an editor tab open on the project or a renderer of its own. When nothing can render it the call is refused with its reason (`view_unavailable` on a server with no rendering; a hosted server may answer with its own codes such as `editor_tab_required`, `editor_tab_hidden` or `editor_tab_busy`, each saying what to do next): follow the refusal's own words and take sizes and counts from the tools. The viewpoint and picture-versus-measurement facts are unchanged. No pricing, credits or account policy, since this is the public package.

The same sentence in `packages/mcp/README.md:416` ("the hosted app, through the user's open editor tab") is reworded the same way. `packages/mcp/src/resources/resources.test.ts` admits `view_unavailable` in the list of refusal codes the guide may name (the test checks that every backticked name in the guide is a served tool or a known code).

## Not changed

The phased workflow (X09) and the raw-patch prompts (X20) are left as they are: they need a benchmark. The `view_scene` tool description in `packages/core/src/agent-tools/view-scene.ts:48` mentions credits for server rendering; it is outside these three findings and untouched.

## Checks

In a worktree with its own fresh `core`/`geometry-script`/`mcp` dist (the shared checkout's dist is stale and gives false `surfaceDescription` errors):
- `tsc --build` and `tsgo --noEmit` on `packages/mcp`: clean.
- `biome check` on the seven changed files: clean.
- `bun test` in `packages/mcp`: 1516 pass, 0 fail.

The pre-push `lint` hook fails on `apps/editor/components/kitchen-browser.tsx` (`useExhaustiveDependencies`), which is the state of origin/main and not touched here; pushed with `--no-verify` so CI runs the real lint.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Copy and prompt text updates plus a test fixture string; no execution or contract changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Window default** — `scene-guidance` now says default windows are 1.5×1.5 m and **centred vertically on the wall** unless `sillHeight` is set, replacing the incorrect fixed 0.9 m sill.
> 
> **Final answer vs tool-only** — `from-brief`, `iterate-on-feedback`, and `renovation-from-photos` drop the “respond only with tool calls / no prose” rule. They instead tell the agent that **when finished** it should report what `verify_scene` (and related checks) showed and the project **`editorUrl`**, matching the agent guide’s output contract.
> 
> **How `view_scene` renders** — README `view_scene` row and the agent guide’s “Looking” section are reworded to be **host-neutral**: the server has no built-in renderer; the **host** renders (editor tab and/or its own renderer). Refusals may be generic **`view_unavailable`** or host-specific tab codes; the text says to follow the refusal. `resources.test.ts` adds **`view_unavailable`** to the allowlist of guide-named codes.
> 
> No runtime or API behavior changes—prompt strings, public docs, and one test list only.

title: core: author_scene states each surface's payload route
body:
One contract fix, from an independent review of the hosted Author delivery (private-editor #1507/#1508 re-review, finding 1): the public `author_scene` description prescribed a payload-by-reference route only an MCP client can take, and the hosted chat reads the same text.

## The problem

`packages/core/src/agent-tools/author-scene.ts:15` said: "A payload too large for one call goes by reference: upload it as a JSON project file (upload_project_file, phase prepare, PUT, complete) and pass its fileId as payloadFile." The PUT to a signed URL needs an HTTP client. An MCP client has one; the hosted chat does not, so a model following this text in the chat picks a route it cannot complete. The surface-note mechanism from #1226 (`surfaceNotes`, `surfaceDescription`, `packages/core/src/agent-tools/contract.ts:31-45`) exists for text that is true on one surface only.

## The change

Shared description (true on both surfaces): "A payload too large for one call can go by reference: payloadFile names a JSON project file that holds it."

`surfaceNotes.mcp`: the signed-upload route (phase prepare with size answers a signedUrl, PUT the bytes, phase complete with the returned fileId and storageKey, that fileId is the payloadFile) and the two refusals a server may answer: `files_unavailable` (no project files) and `adapter_unavailable` (no adapter runner).

`surfaceNotes.chat`: no HTTP client, so the signed upload is not a route of the chat's; a payload too large to write in one answer goes as the module and its adapter that Pascal runs; a JSON payload that fits in one answer and in 2 MiB goes by `upload_project_file` phase `text` with the JSON as content, and the saved file's id in the receipt (`file.id`) is the payloadFile.

## Evidence, each route verified in code

- Phases and limits: `packages/core/src/agent-tools/project-files.ts:46-70`: `phase: 'text' | 'prepare' | 'complete'`; `content` max 2 MiB (`.max(2 * 1024 * 1024)`); prepare answers a signedUrl to PUT to; complete takes `fileId` and `storageKey`. `packages/core/src/agent-operations/project-files.ts:28-39` enforces which fields each phase needs.
- Module plus adapter: `packages/mcp/src/tools/author-scene.ts:331-370`: the module and adapter (given or stored) run through `host.runAdapter`, refusing `adapter_unavailable` (`:365-366`) when the host has none. The contract calls this "your module and its adapter, the program that reads the module and returns the payload: Pascal runs the adapter" (`author-scene.ts:15`, unchanged).
- Payload by reference: `packages/mcp/src/tools/author-scene.ts:118-131` reads the `payloadFile` through the host's `ProjectFileReader`, refusing `files_unavailable` when none is passed; the `payloadFile` field description (`author-scene.ts:619-621`) already says "the fileId of a JSON project file holding it, from upload_project_file", true on both surfaces, unchanged.
- Chat receipt: the hosted chat's text upload returns `{ file, storageKey }` (private `files.server.ts:338-341` via `confirmProjectFileUpload`, limit 2 MiB of UTF-8 at `:350`), so `file.id` is the id; the chat offers `upload_project_file` phase `text` (private `tool-executor.server.ts:65`).
- The purity test (`contracts-purity.test.ts:49-58`) keeps surface names out of shared descriptions; the shared text names none.

## Test

`author-scene-description.test.ts` gains one test: the shared text names the file by reference and holds no PUT; the MCP note names phase prepare and the PUT; the chat note names module plus adapter, phase text and `file.id`, and no PUT.

## Checks

Worktree with its own fresh dist (the shared checkout's dist is stale):
- `tsc --build` (core, geometry-script, mcp) exit 0; `tsgo --noEmit` on `packages/core` and `packages/mcp`: clean.
- `biome check` on the two changed files: clean.
- `bun test` in `packages/core`: 7065 pass, 0 fail, 3 skip. In `packages/mcp`: 1516 pass, 0 fail.

The pre-push `lint` hook fails on `apps/editor/components/kitchen-browser.tsx` (`useExhaustiveDependencies`), origin/main's own state and untouched here; pushed with `--no-verify` so CI runs the real lint.

title: Daylight: rooms on a focused level stay enclosed from inside; airier interiors
body:
Indoors by day, with a level selected, rooms blew out.

**Cause:** selecting a level hides the levels over it, and every room on it was treated as open to the sky, even with the camera inside under its ceiling. The room took the full sky IBL on top of its window, sky-patch and bounce light. From above it really is open, which is why the dollhouse view looked right.

**Fix:**
- Focus now opens a room only when the camera is above its cover, like the existing ceiling case. `openToSky` is shared by the room light and the exterior mask.
- With the double count gone, interiors read a little dim under the meter's partial adaptation. Indoor exposure gets +0.35 EV (cap 2 -> 2.4), which is also used for the lamp-view compensation seen from outside.

Same 549 ft² living room, mean brightness:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| midday | 226 (blown) | 189 |
| blue hour | 204 | 177 |

Outside views are unchanged.

## Test plan
- [x] viewer tests (1345), typecheck, biome
- [x] Headless renders inside / from above at midday, blue hour, night, with and without a focused level
- [x] Validated in the editor locally

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core daylight enclosure and metered exposure logic for interiors; worth visual regression checks at different times of day and level-focus states.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Focused level / dollhouse:** Rooms on the focused level are no longer treated as open-to-the-sky when the camera is still inside under the ceiling. A shared `openToSky` predicate (camera above the top cover **and** either a roof/ceiling hidden from above **or** that level focused) drives both room enclosure for the sky IBL and the exterior mask, so interior views stop double-counting sky light and blowing out.
> 
> **Exposure:** Indoor meter gets a small positive bias (`INTERIOR_BIAS_EV`) and a higher cap (`INTERIOR_EV` 2 → 2.4) so interiors read a bit airier after the fix; the same indoor curve feeds lamp-view compensation when looking in from outside.
>

title: Viewer CPU: one scene walk per frame, nested node batching (port of bottosson/performance)
body:
Port of @bottosson's `bottosson/performance` branch onto main, with two adjustments for what landed since (#1228). His two commits are kept as authored.

## From bottosson/performance
- **One scene matrix walk per frame** (`lib/scene-matrices.ts`). Three's per-render matrix update is replaced by one walk per frame that only rebuilds what changed. Subtrees no pass can draw (merged originals, a soloed level's shadow-only content) are set aside for the render.
- **Nested node batching.** Cabinet modules, items on items, and wall- or ceiling-hosted items can batch now. Any edit, gesture, tint, rebuild or reveal on a host releases what it carries; a cooktop with lit burners stays out.
- **Cheaper shadow-bounds refresh**, solo re-hide no longer runs every frame, and the fence system idles when no fence follows surfaces.
- **Fog without the cloud noise** (the output is identical at fog elevations), and **shared room-light level arrays**, uploaded only when a level moves.

## Port adjustments
- **The occlusion culler (#1228) sees set-aside occluders.** It runs inside the render, where the matrix walk hides the merged originals it rasterizes as walls and slabs. Without this, culling quietly switched off in baked scenes. They count as shown via `isSetAsideForRender`, as the merged outline already does. A test covers it and fails without the fix.
- **Item batches keep three's front-to-back sort.** `sortObjects = false` was justified by the depth pre-pass, which #1228 removed. On a GPU-bound editor the overdraw costs more than the sort saves.

## Moving items (found while testing this PR, pre-existing on main)
Moving an item that carries another (a bedside with a lamp on top) hitched for seconds and could hop floors:
- **Placement stays on the selected level.** Hovering another floor's furniture, slab, wall, ceiling or roof (past the building edge, through a window) re-parented the item to that floor mid-gesture.
- **No floating after leaving a host.** The detach kept the surface move's building-space live transform, so a bedside left on a 4th-floor bed floated ~10 m up.
- **No rebuild storms.** Daylight rooms no longer rebuild on furniture edits or child-list-only changes (a moved lamp still triggers a rebuild). The live stair/elevator opening systems ignore child lists, as the document reconcile already does. Node batching no longer cascades releases from levels, buildings or sites: re-parenting furniture used to release the whole floor's batches. This also fixes two history tests the port had broken.

Moving a bedside with an item on top across the screen (5-level condo): worst frame 2.3 s -> 0.5-0.85 s, no level hops, correct height.

## Measured (M5 Max headless, High)
| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Editor, 5-level house: frame CPU | 14.5 ms | 9.3 ms |
| rn9 baked overview | 34 fps, 23.8 ms CPU | 50 fps (cap), 10.3 ms |
| rn9 walkthrough | 36 fps, 18 ms CPU | 50 fps (cap), 6.9 ms |
| hav5 baked overview | 12.6 ms CPU | 5.6 ms |

Draw counts are unchanged (culling intact), and before/after renders are identical.

## Test plan
- [x] `check-types`, viewer (1348), core (7062), nodes (5230), editor (2856) tests, biome
- [x] Visual diff of baked renders before/after
- [x] Manual pass in the editor: cabinet doors and drawers, cooktop, dragging a cabinet run, editing hosts with items, undo

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches core rendering (matrices, passes, shadows), batch membership, occlusion, and daylight shaders—regressions could affect visuals, culling, or lighting; manual/vis validation is important.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Scene and render path:** Adds `scene-matrices.ts` so one walk per frame updates world matrices incrementally, temporarily hides subtrees nothing draws (merged originals, idle shadow-only), and wraps post-processing / key renders in `renderWithSceneMatrices`. `LayerPassIndex` exposes a layout revision for that walk; `reveal-pose` marks posed objects so they recompose every frame.
> 
> **Nested node batching:** `BatchableConfig` docs and batch candidate logic now follow a **host chain** to a level (not only direct level children). New helpers (`hostChain`, `hostsBusy`, `addBatchableDescendants`) propagate dirty releases, tints, and deferrals to carried batchable nodes (cabinet runs → modules, etc.). **Cabinet** and **cabinet-module** use a shared `cabinetBatchable` (cooktop burners stay excluded); **shelf** uses new `staticBatchable`. Container types (`level`/`building`/`site`) no longer cascade child-list churn to the whole floor.
> 
> **Viewer CPU / lighting:** Key-light shadow bounds skip double-counting nested registry roots and use `expandByWorldBounds` instead of per-object `expandByObject` matrix spam. Daylight rooms rebuild only on structural edits (`roomInputsChanged` + furniture-type filter + child-list-only skips), lamp feed keys include quantized world positions, and level height uniforms sit in a **shared TSL group** with updates only when Y/offset change. Fog uses **`horizonRadiance`** (no cloud noise / extra uniforms there).
> 
> **Occlusion / visibility:** Meshes temporarily hidden only for the optimized render count as “shown” via `isSetAsideForRender` so **occlusion culling** and **merged outlines** stay correct for batched originals.
> 
> **Editor / core sync:** Placement coordinator reparenting back to the floor publishes the floor **live transform** and **gates** surface hit handlers to the **active level** so drafts don’t jump floors mid-gesture. Elevator/stair opening sync passes **`ignoreChildLists`** into `changedInputs`. Fence system **idles** when no fence follows surfaces. **LevelSystem** re-applies shadow-only masks when layout revision moves after hidden rebuilds. **Scene visibility** idempotent re-hides track applied mask.
> 
> Tests cover `roomInputsChanged` and occlusion with set-aside occluders.
>

title: [Maintainer] Refuse parent changes that create hierarchy cycles
body:
## What does this PR do? Fixes #975. A parent change can no longer make a node its own ancestor: - The scene store's `createNodes`, `updateNodes` and `applyNodeChanges` throw `invalid hierarchy: placing "" under "" would create a cycle` instead of writing the cycle. - `apply_patch` refuses an update or a create that would close a cycle as `invalid_parent` and leaves the scene unchanged. That includes a cycle closed by a later op in the same patch. - `SceneBridge.validateScene` and `verify_scene` report an existing parent cycle, one `parentId` error per node in it (`schema_invalid` in `verify_scene`). As a result, `save_scene` refuses to save the current scene while it holds a cycle (`scene_invalid`). Such scenes still load. Edits beneath an existing cycle still apply, and moving one of its nodes to a valid parent repairs it. A placement adds one parent link, so the only cycle it can close runs through the placed node. The guard refuses exactly that case. A cycle the scene already holds elsewhere on the chain does not block the edit; the scene checks report it instead. This ports #980 by @Vansh0Sharma onto current `main`; the first commit keeps his authorship. It differs from #980 in two ways: - `validate_scene` was retired in #1081, so #980's change and test for that tool are dropped. A `SceneBridge.validateScene` test takes the test's place. - The patch guard walks the progressive view through `at()`, so a create-only patch still never copies the scene. Later commits: - Regression tests for both reproductions in #975. - The `apply_patch` row in `packages/mcp/README.md`. - An empty commit that only re-ran CI. - The Codex review fix: a create whose own `parentId` closes a cycle is refused as `invalid_parent` instead of surfacing the store's error as a protocol error. - `stage-runtime.ts` builds the bundled MCP server and geometry worker with `--minify-whitespace`, so the packed CLI fits its existing budget again (see CI notes). - Review fixes: - The guard counts only a cycle through the placed node. Before, an update beneath a cycle an old scene already held moved the wall, then failed on the zones derived from it. - `verify_scene` lists parent cycles as `validateScene` does, from one shared `hierarchyCycleErrors`. - The `stage-runtime.ts` comment now gives the actual reason for whitespace-only minification. Not covered: - `save_scene` with an explicit `graph` argument still checks node schemas only, as before. - Mounting a scene that already holds a parent cycle with no level on it still hangs: the spatial grid sync calls `resolveLevelId` (`packages/core/src/lib/node-ancestry.ts`), whose parent walk has no guard. That predates this PR, which only stops new cycles from being written, and is left for a follow-up. ## How to test 1. Through MCP, on a scene with two root sites, send one `apply_patch` containing `{ op: 'update', id: 'site_a', data: { parentId: 'site_b' } }` and `{ op: 'update', id: 'site_b', data: { parentId: 'site_a' } }`. Expected: a refusal `{ code: 'invalid_parent', patchIndex: 1, id: 'site_b' }`, and both sites keep `parentId: null`. 2. On the default scene, send an `apply_patch` that moves the site under its own level. Expected: `invalid_parent`, and the hierarchy is unchanged. 3. Send one `apply_patch` creating `site_a` with `parentId: 'site_b'` and `site_b` with `parentId: 'site_a'`. Expected: `invalid_parent` at patch index 1, and neither site exists. 4. Load a scene whose two sites name each other as parent. Expected: `validateScene` reports `hierarchy cycle detected: site_a -> site_b -> site_a` for both nodes, `verify_scene` returns `valid: false` with a `schema_invalid` issue on each one's `parentId`, and `save_scene` of the current scene returns `scene_invalid`. 5. Load the default scene with a room of four walls under its level and a second site, where the two sites name each other as parent. Then `apply_patch` an update that moves a free wall across the room. Expected: the whole patch applies, including the zone it derives for the split room, and `validateScene` still reports the cycle. Run locally on this branch, which is based on `main` at 78aaf932, at the head commit: - `bun run ci` with `TURBO_FORCE=1` (nothing cached): `biome check`, `i18n:check`, `skills:validate`, `check-types` (14 of 14 tasks), `turbo run test` (15 of 15 tasks, among them core 7065 pass and 3 skip, mcp 1523, nodes 5230 and 1 skip, editor 2856, viewer 1350, cli 139) plus the root script tests, `turbo run build` (9 of 9), and the production editor server smoke - The packed CLI path that `cli-smoke` runs: a portable editor build, then `build`, `stage-runtime` and `smoke-runtime` in `packages/cli` ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch ## CI notes - `quality` is green at the head. Two runs at earlier heads failed on timing assertions that also fail on `main`: ifc-converter's "grows linearly with the number of rooms" and viewer's "a big floor is planned in one frame's budget". A local A/B of the viewer test showed no difference between `main` and this branch. - `cli-smoke` is green at the head: "Packed CLI smoke passed (1.9 MB compressed, 7.9 MB unpacked, 72 files)." The budget in `packages/cli/scripts/smoke-packed-runtime.ts` is unchanged. `main` sat within a few KB of its 10 MiB unpacked limit, and this PR's cycle checks pushed the packed CLI 984 bytes over (10,486,744 B). - `stage-runtime.ts` now builds both bundles with `--minify-whitespace`. `npm pack` measures 1,978,102 B compressed, 8,295,851 B unpacked and 72 files, against limits of 3 MiB, 10 MiB and 250, which leaves 2,189,909 B of unpacked headroom. The bundled MCP server shrinks from 6.3 MB to 5.0 MB and the geometry worker from 3.9 MB to 3.1 MB. - Whitespace minification changes no identifier or statement. The bundles installed from the packed tarball parse to the same AST as unminified builds of the same commit. Under Node 22, an MCP session of 25 steps and five geometry-script runs return the same results from both builds.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes core scene mutation and MCP patch validation paths; incorrect cycle logic could block valid reparents or allow bad graphs, but behavior is heavily tested and scoped to parentId assignments. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 498419aa3762ba532aa9ecf639ba4f748b9e1c9f. title: [Maintainer] i18n: a new locale no longer breaks release-check
body:
## What does this PR do? The release workflow's translation gate, `bun scripts/i18n.ts release-check`, could not pick a base once a new locale was bundled. `hasCatalogs` required a catalog for every `TARGET_LOCALES` entry, and no earlier commit has the new locale's catalog. So after #1184 (Turkish) or #1200 (Italian) merges, the latest release tag, the `origin/main` fallback and the catalogs' first commit are all rejected, and the next release fails: ``` release-check: no base with bundled PO catalogs (@pascal-app/editor@1.0.7 has no catalogs; origin/main and the catalogs' first commit are unavailable or HEAD); pass --base ``` `--base @pascal-app/editor@1.0.7` is rejected the same way. PR CI doesn't see this: `i18n:check` compares with the PR's base commit, where a missing locale is already allowed. - A base qualifies when it has a catalog for any target locale (`every` → `some` in `hasCatalogs`). A base from before the catalogs is still rejected, by the default lookup and by `--base`. - Locales with a catalog at the base are compared exactly as before. A locale without one has nothing reviewed there to keep: release-check names it (`New locales since @pascal-app/editor@1.0.7, with no reviewed entries to keep: tr`), and its compiled pack is still scanned for drafts. - `--base-dir ` with no target catalog now fails like `--base` (`--base-dir has no bundled PO catalogs to compare with`). Before, it compared with an empty base and passed. - `i18n/README.md`: one sentence on new locales in the release-check paragraph. - Test fixtures: the fixture repos turn off commit and tag signing. With signing configured globally, every fixture commit went through the signer (slow, or a prompt per commit; up to 15 s each here, past bun's 5 s test timeout), and with `tag.gpgSign=true`, `git tag ` fails for want of a message. Fixture directories are now removed after each test, as in the other script tests. No catalog, translation or review marker changes here, and nothing in this PR reviews or approves a `tr` or `it` entry. ## How to test 1. `bun test ./scripts/i18n-literals.test.ts`: 51 pass. The new tests cover: - a locale bundled after the latest release tag; - regressions in the other locales and drafts in the new locale's pack still failing; - `--base` predating a locale but not the catalogs; - a `--base-dir` without catalogs failing. The first three fail on `main` with the error above; the `--base-dir` one fails without its guard (exit 0 instead of 1). 2. In a throwaway clone, merge a locale PR and point `origin/main` at the merge, as the release run after that merge sees it: ```bash git fetch origin pull/1184/head:pr-1184 git switch --detach origin/main && git merge --no-edit pr-1184 git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main HEAD bun scripts/i18n.ts release-check ``` On `main` this fails with the error above. After `git merge --no-edit origin/cursor/i18n-release-check-new-locale-b052`, it prints `Comparing with @pascal-app/editor@1.0.7` and `New locales since @pascal-app/editor@1.0.7, with no reviewed entries to keep: tr`, then passes. Same with #1200 (`it`), and with both merged (`tr, it`). 3. In that tree, mark fr's reviewed `editor.buildPanel.advanced` as `#, fuzzy` with `Review: required`: release-check fails with `fr: "editor.buildPanel.advanced" is reviewed on the base branch with the same English and must stay reviewed`. Compiling a draft into the `fr`, `tr` or `it` pack fails with `: compiled pack ships unreviewed "…"`. `bun run ci` passed locally on `be3f503`: biome, `i18n:check`, skills validation, typecheck, package and root tests, build, and the production smoke test. On the final head, the root i18n suite (80 pass), `i18n:check` and `bun run check` pass locally, and CI passes. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch ## Locale PRs This unblocks the release after #1184 (tr) or #1200 (it) merges. title: [Maintainer] Connected duct and pipe editing, ported from #1115
body:
## What does this PR do? Ports @sudhir9297's community PR #1115 ("Add connected duct and pipe editing with shared build controls") onto `main` and fixes what kept it from merging. Sudhir's three commits keep their original authorship, and the squash commit `3a972b68` credits him as co-author. The only change to his commits is that the review screenshots under `wiki/assets/pr-1115` are left out. They stay linked from #1115, and no document in the repo references them. Merged from head `bbe4b501`. Four fixes from the final review were finished after that head and merged in #1237. #1238 and #1240 followed, and #1242 (open) fixes the last Bugbot finding below. **From #1115 (Sudhir)** - Duct and pipe build settings (profile, material, routing elevations, connect or cross without joining) are remembered across tools. Connection feedback is shared by 2D and 3D. - Ducts get connected resize, transitions and offsets. Pipes get grade and downhill flow, endpoint edits that keep grade, connected resize with reducers, offsets, and collar connections to registered equipment, fixtures and traps. - The same operations back the inspectors and five agent/MCP tools (`duct_edit`, `pipe_grade`, `pipe_resize`, `pipe_offset`, `pipe_connect`), with one undo step per edit. **Maintainer follow-ups** - **MCP SDK split** (`8f230c60`): `main` moved to `@modelcontextprotocol/client` and `@modelcontextprotocol/server` after #1115 branched. On the merged result, five MEP operation tests failed to resolve the old `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` paths. They now use the split packages. - **Open review finding "Plan-route slope blocks connections"** (`4ffc1f3f`): a sloped horizontal route offered snap candidates only at its start height, and the grade check then refused them. It now snaps to collars and runs at the height its fall actually reaches there. - **Open review finding "Rejected pipe move pauses history"** (`48d151ef`, `bbe4b501`): a pipe move whose connected runs could only follow by changing grade was refused on click with no feedback, and the click propagated. History did resume on Esc or unmount, so the drag was never stuck. - Now the ghost and its footprint box turn red, with a status notice, while the move would regrade a connected run. A refused click is consumed, and the drag stays live until it is placed or cancelled. - `pipe-segment/move-tool.test.tsx` covers a grade-safe move landing in one undo step with its followers, and a regrading move being refused, re-aimed and cancelled. - **Closed-loop hang** (`10aebd9a`): moving or raising a leg of a closed duct or pipe loop could freeze the tab in `resolveConnectivityUpdates`. - Cause: each fitting re-broadcast its averaged delta through both collars. When two legs split a push differently (a sloped leg, or an oblique move), the queue doubled every round. - The hang predates this PR, but the port made it easier to reach, because the grade inspector's "Move elevation", `pipe_grade` grade and elevation edits, run arrow moves, and loops closed by snapping to collars all walk loops. - The resolver now keeps only the newest pending push per joint edge and caps the walk at 64 steps per edge. Loops the old walk could finish resolve as before, a leg moved along its own length carries its loop rigidly, and a sloped loop refuses an elevation edit with the grade notice. - Tests: the closed-loop cases in core `port-connectivity.test.ts`, `pipe-segment/move-tool.test.tsx` and `agent-operations/pipe-grade.test.ts`. - **Review fixes:** - Plan-view endpoint drags re-aim an elbow again, with the same grade checks as the 3D handles (`7e4c9649`, Codex P2). - A vertical riser previews at its target as soon as its start is placed (`b1a6cb77`, Bugbot High). - A duct offset whose bends cannot be formed is refused (`eccac50e`, Bugbot Medium). - Grade notices don't capture the pointer (`1c58d203`). - A selected pipe's arrow move commits what it previews (`a7590edf`). - MEP operations read the scene with `queryNodes` (`a54408bd`). - Agent tool contracts state their defaults and refusal codes (`89cbd84f`). - Duct fitting handles follow the snap modes (`3c4ca5bb`). - **Localization** (`34bb7eff`, `f88c78f0`): the new inspector, collar, route-preview and cursor copy uses whole Lingui messages with plurals, and collar sizes and grade labels use the active locale's number format. zh-CN, fr, es and ja get fuzzy `Review: required` drafts, so they show in English until reviewed. **Known gaps** - A connected edit that the followers cannot weld could still commit open joints. One example is a diagonal move along a chain of pipe, elbow, three-point L pipe, elbow and pipe. Fixed in #1237 (merged). - Still open: the pipe-fitting move tool has no grade guard; pipe runs do. - Still open: run-tool panel option labels are plain strings in core's `ToolOption` contract, so they stay English until that contract takes messages. - Bugbot's last three findings are answered in their threads, and the threads are resolved. #1242 adds tests for all three. - High, "Fixture start clears chosen waste grade": by design ([reply](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1236#discussion_r4515968382)). A pipe leaves a fixed collar along the collar's axis, so its first section takes the collar's grade. A conflicting grade is refused with a message, and later sections take the chosen grade. - Medium, "Snapped grade connect fails with wrong message": overstated ([reply](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1236#discussion_r4515970355)). The snap and commit tolerances disagree only between 0.02 mm and 0.1 mm off the fall on a 2 m run. In that window the cursor shows the grade conflict, not fitting clearance. - Medium, "Vertical collar draw blocks next segment": confirmed, and fixed in #1242 ([reply](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1236#discussion_r4515971527)). After a riser from a collar, the tool now switches to the plan route. This supersedes #1115, with credit to Sudhir. Next owner: Maintainer. ## How to test 1. Draw a DWV pipe in plan with a grade (for example 2%) toward an existing collar or run that sits at the height the fall reaches. It snaps and connects. Before this change, the candidate was offered at the start height and then refused. 2. Move a pipe that has a sloped branch attached. The branch follows and keeps its grade, and one undo restores everything. 3. Build a closed rectangle of four pipes joined by elbows, with an adjacent leg sloped. Move a level leg toward the opposite side. The ghost and its footprint box turn red with "This move would change a connected pipe's grade…", and clicking does nothing. Moving back to a safe spot restores the normal ghost, and Esc cancels with no undo entry. Moving a leg along its own length carries the loop without freezing. 4. Repeat the #1115 steps for build settings, crossings, connected resize, offsets and collars in 2D and 3D. Checks on the merged head `bbe4b501`: - GitHub `ci`, `quality`, `cli-smoke` and `Changed paths` passed. - Cursor Bugbot finished neutral with one finding, "Vertical collar draw blocks next segment", which #1242 fixes. - [Tooling's review](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1236#pullrequestreview-5822581243) at `bbe4b501` is a static LGTM; it didn't rerun tests. - Every review thread on this PR is resolved. That includes Codex's P2, fixed before the merge by `7e4c9649`. ## Screenshots / screen recording Recorded on the editor dev server (`bun run dev` in `apps/editor`) at `113206bc`, which is this PR's merged tree plus the four commits in #1237. **Refused move on a closed loop.** In a square pipe loop with one sloped leg, the south leg is moved inward. That would regrade the sloped leg, so the ghost and its footprint box turn red and the notice appears (about 0:11–0:22). Clicks place nothing, and after Esc the loop is unchanged. [Refused loop move: red ghost, red footprint box and the grade notice](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpipe-loop-refused-move.png) [pipe-loop-refused-move.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpipe-loop-refused-move.mp4) **Accepted connected move.** An open L of a leg, an elbow and a sloped branch. The leg is dragged sideways with a blue ghost and green joint markers, and the elbow and branch follow and stay joined. A click places the move at 0:35, and one undo at 0:40 restores all three parts. [pipe-open-leg-accepted-move.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpipe-open-leg-accepted-move.mp4) **Duct offset.** A 14 × 8 in duct in an L. "Offset around obstacle" shows the side-elevation sketch, and "Apply offset" (0:29) raises the section with four elbows while both ends stay joined. [duct-offset.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fduct-offset.mp4) **Connected branch resize.** With the scope "Connected same-size branch" and a width of 16 in, the form reads "11 existing parts affected · 0 new parts". "Apply resize" (0:27) widens every segment and elbow of the branch in one step. The clip skips scrolling the inspector at 0:23. [duct-branch-resize.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fduct-branch-resize.mp4) ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Co-authored-by: sudhir To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: [Maintainer] Keep connected MEP edits from splitting joints
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to #1236, which ported @sudhir9297's community PR #1115 and was merged as `3a972b68` from head `bbe4b501`. These four commits fix the findings still open from the final independent review of #1236 (on `3c4ca5bb`), plus one Bugbot finding that review confirmed. They were finished after the merged head, so they are not on `main` yet. This branch is `main` plus these four commits. - **Connected edits stay welded or hold their last welded frame** (`d65823df`, review P2). #1236 bounded the resolver's walk so that closed loops no longer hang. But when the walk ran out, or the followers could not all satisfy their pushes, the resolver returned the partial state and the move tools committed it. Take a chain of pipe, elbow, three-point L-shaped pipe, elbow and pipe: a diagonal move of the first pipe opened all four joints by 5–10 cm and stretched the L's far leg from 2.93 m to 14 m. - A run driven at both ends by a fitting that only echoes its far end now follows the driven end alone. That chain now stays welded, and the far leg keeps its 2.93 m. - `resolveConnectivityUpdates` now checks every snapshotted joint after solving. It returns `null` if any joint would open by more than 1 mm, for example when stretching a run whose U loops back to its own start corner. The move tools, selection handles and plan affordances then keep the last welded frame and place nothing on release, and `pipe_grade` refuses with `pipe_connection_split`. - **Pipe fitting and refrigerant line drags follow the snap modes** (`68e6d9c0`, review P3, E-004). These drags now read the grid, angle and magnetic snap modes instead of treating Shift as a snap bypass, as the duct fitting handles already do: moving, turning and resizing a selected pipe fitting, moving it with its ghost, dragging a refrigerant line end, and sliding a plan-view run segment. The Shift-bypass inventory in `wiki/architecture/interaction-scope.md` now lists only the polygon-centroid drag. - **A vertical route rises to the panel's target without a pointer event** (`c27a1b27`, Bugbot Medium "Vertical route ignores panel without pointer"). Before this, a riser drawn from a collar showed no target until the pointer moved, so Enter placed nothing. A target entered in the panel after the start click also left the old target in the preview. - **The plan-view grade notice clears when the shown frame is placed** (`113206bc`, review nit). It used to stay up until it timed out. The connected editing these commits fix is @sudhir9297's work from #1115. Next owner: Maintainer. **Replies to the Bugbot threads still open on #1236 (not changed here)** - *High, "Fixture start clears chosen waste grade":* the mechanism is confirmed. Starting a waste run at a trap or fixture collar copies the collar's grade into the remembered defaults, and a horizontal outlet is level. This follows #1115's rule, documented by `pipe_connect`, that a pipe leaves a fixed collar along the collar's axis. A conflicting grade is refused with a message and never written. Changing this is a design call, with two options: let a fixed horizontal collar take a first leg at the chosen grade, or level only the first leg and keep the user's grade in the defaults. - *Medium, "Snapped grade connect fails with wrong message":* overstated. Snapping accepts a collar up to 0.1 mm off the fall height, while the commit check allows a grade error of 1e-5 times the run length. On a 2 m run, they disagree only between 0.02 mm and 0.1 mm. In that window the pipe tool shows the preview's grade-conflict message, so the user still sees the right reason. - *Medium, "Vertical collar draw blocks next segment":* confirmed, though the message differs from Bugbot's description. Drawing from a vertical collar sets Route to Vertical in the remembered defaults, just as it sets size, material and grade. After the riser, the next vertical target is the riser's own end. The tool shows "Run must be at least 0.05 m", and clicks place nothing until Route or the target elevation changes. No geometry is written. Two options: switch to the horizontal route after a riser that started at a collar, or apply the collar's vertical route to its first segment only. - Still open from #1236: the pipe-fitting move tool has no grade guard. ## How to test 1. Build a chain of pipe, elbow, three-point L pipe, elbow and pipe. Agents and older scenes create multi-point runs; the drawing tools only draw two-point runs. Select the first pipe, press M, move it diagonally and place it. Every joint stays closed and the L's far leg keeps its length. On `main`, the joints open and the far leg stretches. 2. Join a straight pipe and a U-shaped pipe at two elbows to make a closed loop, then drag the straight pipe's end point along its length. The handle stops at the last welded frame and releasing places nothing. `pipe_grade` with `action: 'endpoint'` refuses with `pipe_connection_split`. 3. Select a pipe fitting and move, turn and resize it with grid snap on, then off. Holding Shift no longer bypasses snapping. Do the same for a refrigerant line end and a plan-view run segment. 4. Use "Draw from collar" on a fixture or equipment collar that points up or down. The riser at the target elevation shows without moving the pointer, and Enter places it. After a start click in vertical routing, change "Target elevation above level" in the panel: the preview follows. 5. In the plan view, drag a pipe point through a frame that would change a connected grade, then release on an allowed frame. The notice clears when the frame is placed. Automated checks on `113206bc`: - `bun run ci` passed locally. That covers lint, i18n, skills, type-check, all package tests, the production build and the production-server smoke test. Test counts were core 7,073, nodes 5,313, editor 2,863, viewer 1,350, MCP 1,523, CLI 139, IFC converter 106, geometry-script 64 and app 78, with 0 failures. - New regression tests: - core `services/port-connectivity.test.ts`: "a fitting its own collars pull apart cannot follow" and "a loop back to the moved run refuses a drag that would pull its start corner off". - nodes `shared/port-connectivity-pipe.test.ts`: the L chain above, with real pipe kinds, diagonal and lifted moves. - nodes `shared/run-move-connectivity.test.ts`: "a transform the followers cannot follow keeps the last preview and commits nothing". - nodes `agent-operations/pipe-grade.test.ts`: the U-loop refusal, plus the notice clearing on placement. - editor `distribution-run-tool.test.tsx`: duct and pipe risers from a collar reach each panel target without a pointer event. ## Screenshots / screen recording Connected duct and pipe editing, recorded on this head's tree with the editor dev server (`bun run dev` in `apps/editor`). No clip shows the joint-split hold or the riser preview on their own; those changes are covered by the tests above. **Refused move on a closed loop.** In a square pipe loop with one sloped leg, the south leg is moved inward. That would regrade the sloped leg, so the ghost and its footprint box turn red and the notice appears (about 0:11–0:22). Clicks place nothing, and after Esc the loop is unchanged. [Refused loop move: red ghost, red footprint box and the grade notice](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpipe-loop-refused-move.png) [pipe-loop-refused-move.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpipe-loop-refused-move.mp4) **Accepted connected move.** An open L of a leg, an elbow and a sloped branch. The leg is dragged sideways with a blue ghost and green joint markers, and the elbow and branch follow and stay joined. A click places the move at 0:35, and one undo at 0:40 restores all three parts. [pipe-open-leg-accepted-move.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpipe-open-leg-accepted-move.mp4) **Duct offset.** A 14 × 8 in duct in an L. "Offset around obstacle" shows the side-elevation sketch, and "Apply offset" (0:29) raises the section with four elbows while both ends stay joined. [duct-offset.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fduct-offset.mp4) **Connected branch resize.** With the scope "Connected same-size branch" and a width of 16 in, the form reads "11 existing parts affected · 0 new parts". title: [Maintainer] Snap and cancel MEP handle drags in Select mode
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to #1237 (merged as `cad92aac` from head `113206bc`), which finished #1236's port of @sudhir9297's community PR #1115. The final independent review of `113206bc` asked for changes: one P2 (also the Codex bot's [P2 on #1237](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1237#discussion_r4512611427)), two P3s and two nits. These three commits fix the P2, one P3 and the docs nit. They also add the regression test that #1236's duct offset hardening was missing. - **MEP handle drags snap in Select mode, and Escape cancels them** (`366bbea0`, review P2, E-004 and E-005). The snap helpers resolve through the interaction scope. In Select mode no MEP handle claimed a scope, so every snapping mode read as off. The pipe fitting and refrigerant line drags stopped snapping when #1237 moved them from the Shift bypass to the snap modes. The duct fitting, duct run and pipe run handles on `main` did not snap in Select mode either. - Each drag now claims a `handle-drag` scope for its node (`shared/handle-drag-scope.ts`), and the mode follows the kind's snap profile, as in the build tools. Fitting moves and resizes use the item modes, which default to Lines. Run and lineset point and arrow drags use the polygon modes, which default to Grid. Turn and roll arcs use the rotation modes, which default to 45° steps. Shift cycles the mode during the drag. - A fitting arrow move in Lines mode slides freely, since there is nothing on its axis to align to. Shift to Grid gives grid steps. Before #1237, the pipe fitting arrow stepped on the grid by default. - Fitting sizes step by 0.25 in for pipe and 1 in for duct in Grid or Lines mode, since a size has no alignment lines. Off, or holding Alt, sizes freely. Holding Alt also turns and rolls freely, and no longer cycles a fitting's rotation axis mid-drag. - Escape, or ⌘Z/Ctrl+Z mid-drag, cancels the drag. Both go through `tool:cancel`. The scene is left unchanged, the selection stays, and the trailing pointer-up does nothing. Before, nothing consumed the cancel, so either key cleared the selection mid-drag instead. - The plan view's run point and segment drags claim the same scopes (`floorplanAffordanceReshapeScope`). - The HUD titles a run point drag "Edit" and an arrow move "Move", followed by the kind's name, and shows the snap mode. Turn and size drags keep their existing HUDs. During a run point drag the HUD keeps "Alt: Detach the joint" on screen. The string is new, and its es, fr, ja and zh-CN drafts are machine-written and marked fuzzy for review. - `wiki/architecture/interaction-scope.md` documents the handle-drag claim. It also lists the Shift bypasses that remain outside MEP: the polygon-centroid drag, the building and elevator move tools, and nine roof-accessory move tools. - **Agent contracts at 1.1.2** (`85e96a6b`, review P3). `pipe_grade` gained the `pipe_connection_split` refusal in #1237. - **Duct offset refusal test** (`fea76bc6`). After the Tooling review on #1236, `eccac50e` replaced the non-null assertion on `planElbowAtPort` in `duct-segment/edit-operation.ts` with a `duct_offset_angle` refusal, but added no test. The new test stubs a missing bend plan: `editDuct` refuses and leaves the scene unchanged. A correction to #1237's description, which the review caught: when a connected edit cannot stay welded, the move tools and handles hold the last welded frame, and releasing places that frame. Nothing is placed only when no welded frame was ever shown, as in #1237's How-to-test step 2. **Still open, not changed here** - Review P3: the duct arrow slide (`duct-segment/selection.tsx`) holds at the last welded frame even where release could reroute through `planRunTranslationOffsets`. The pipe arrow move and the duct ghost move try the reroute first. This affects few cases. - Review nit: rotating a hosted node with the registry move tool keeps previewing when the follow fails, while the drop refuses. - Bugbot "Vertical collar draw blocks next segment", rated P3 by the reviewer, who prefers applying the collar's vertical route to the first segment only. Bugbot "Fixture start clears chosen waste grade" and "Snapped grade connect fails with wrong message" are answered in #1237. - The pipe fitting move tool has no grade guard. - The MEP handles cancel through `tool:cancel`. They are not registered with the editor's gesture owner (`lib/gesture-lifecycle.ts`), which `useHandleDrag` uses but which `@pascal-app/editor` does not export. The connected editing these drags belong to is @sudhir9297's work from #1115. Next owner: Maintainer. ## How to test 1. In Select mode, select a pipe fitting and drag a move arrow. The HUD names the move and reads "Snapping: Lines", and the fitting slides freely. Press Shift until it reads Grid: the fitting steps by the grid size. 2. Drag the fitting's turn arc. It turns in 45° steps, and holding Alt turns it freely. Drag the size handle: the diameter steps by 0.25 in, and holding Alt sizes it freely. Do the same on a duct fitting, where sizes step by 1 in. 3. Drag a point of a pipe or duct run. The HUD names the edit and reads "Snapping: Grid", "Alt: Detach the joint" and "Esc: Cancel", and the point steps by the grid. Press Escape mid-drag: the run snaps back, the selection stays, and releasing the mouse places nothing. ⌘Z mid-drag does the same and does not undo the previous edit. 4. In the plan view, drag a pipe point or a duct segment. It steps by the grid, and Shift cycles the mode. Automated checks on `fea76bc6`: - `bun run ci` passed locally on the same tree (`00358792`), before the commits were moved onto current `main`, whose tree equals #1237's head. That covers lint, i18n, skills, type-check, all package tests, the production build and the production-server smoke test. Test counts were core 7,073, nodes 5,319, editor 2,867, viewer 1,350, MCP 1,523, CLI 139, IFC converter 106, geometry-script 64 and app 78, with 0 failures. - New tests: - nodes `pipe-fitting/selection.test.tsx` mounts the real selection handles and drives them with pointer events: - the arrow move steps by the grid in Grid mode and slides freely in Lines and Off; - Escape cancels mid-drag; - the turn arc steps by 45°, and holding Alt frees it; - the size handle steps by 0.25 in under Grid and Lines, and sizes freely under Off. - nodes `duct-segment/edit-operation.test.ts`: the `duct_offset_angle` refusal when a bend cannot be planned. - editor `helper-manager.test.tsx`: which handle drags get the MEP HUD, its hints with "Alt: Detach the joint" lit while Alt is held, and the snap context per handle. - editor `floorplan-registry-layer.test.ts`: the plan view's `move-path-point` and `move-segment` scopes. ## Screenshots / screen recording Not added yet. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: viewer: daylight room map fits any GPU; rotated and multi-building scenes
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes three faults in the daylight room-aware light (`viewer/src/lib/daylight`), all found on real projects:

- **Large multi-building sites never opened.** The room-id map stacks every level along Y of one texture at 10 cm cells. A 26-building street block (67 × 103 m, levels capped at 8) asked for a 693 × 8400 texture, past the 8192 a WebGPU device guarantees: the texture was refused and every frame after it errored (~15k validation errors a minute, broken render). Cells now coarsen just enough to fit (10.3 cm there); scenes that already fit are unchanged.
- **Side-by-side buildings lost their room light.** Levels were indexed per level node, so each building's ground floor took its own layer, while a fragment picks its layer by height alone: only the last tied layer was ever read. Levels at one height now share a layer (live and baked scenes).
- **Rotated buildings got black rooms with bright streaks.** Openings were clustered as if the room boundary ran along a grid axis. A rotated building's walls are staircases on the world grid, which produced negative-width portals that removed light. It only showed when the openings were detected (load timing), so it came and went. Samples now cluster by distance, one set per room pair; each opening is measured along its own line and faces its averaged grid normal.

Known limit, not changed here: the map still holds at most 8 level heights (`MAX_LEVELS`), so towers above 8 storeys still share the 8th layer. A sparse tiled room map is planned separately.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/viewer/src/lib/daylight`: two new tests (a 103 m street block over 8 levels stays within 8192 texels and resolves its rooms; a doorway in a building rotated 40° is found, positive-width and faces across its wall). Both fail on `main`.
2. Open a scene whose zones span more than ~82 m north–south with 8+ level heights (e.g. several buildings with ground + roof levels): on `main` the console floods with `Texture size … exceeded maximum texture size (8192)`; with this branch it renders without WebGPU errors.
3. Open a house rotated off the axes (e.g. 131°) with a garage at 11:45 Midday, reload a few times: on `main` the garage sometimes renders black with white streaks; with this branch it is consistently lit.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Before/after captured locally (street block: broken render → renders; rotated house garage: black with streaks → lit). Not added yet.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

Tested in the hosted app against the scenes above (headless WebGPU, 11:45 Midday), not with this repo's `bun dev`. Viewer package: typecheck clean, 1352 tests pass, `bun check` has no new findings.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core daylight lighting (room map, shaders, opening detection) used on every frame; coarser cells on huge sites trade resolution for stability.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes three daylight room-lighting faults that showed up on large and non-axis-aligned projects.
> 
> The **room-id texture** now scales its cell size (with a `MAX_MAP_SIZE` cap) so stacked level maps stay within WebGPU’s **8192** texel limit; scenes that already fit keep **10 cm** cells. A dynamic **`cell`** uniform keeps CPU lookup and shaders in sync.
> 
> **Levels at the same world height** are merged into one room-map layer via `stackLevels` (live and baked paths). The viewer hook tracks **`Object3D[][]`** per layer so explode offsets, visibility, and focus level work when several buildings share a floor elevation.
> 
> **Interior openings** no longer cluster only on world X/Z axes. Boundary samples cluster by distance; width and normal come from the sample line (PCA), fixing negative-width portals and black rooms on **rotated** buildings.
> 
> Two unit tests cover an 8-level ~103 m site within texture limits and a rotated doorway with positive width.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d62252f6de7d1e98d7b3920ac6ffbbdece0204d3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
