title: [Maintainer] Restore joined MEP runs on Alt detach and drag cancel
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to #1238, merged by @Aymericr as `23f64785` from head `fea76bc6`. That was the last of the maintainer PRs (#1236, #1237, #1238) porting @sudhir9297's connected duct and pipe editing from #1115. The independent review of `fea76bc6` requested changes with 11 numbered findings: one P2, four P3s and six nits. This PR fixes the P2, P3 #2 and #3, and nits #6, #7, #9 and #10, and corrects #11 below. P3 #4 was tried here and reverted. It stays open with the two carried-over items. - **Joined runs go back when a drag detaches or comes back to its start** (`bcb861e4`; review P2 #1, P3 #3 and nit #9). - Some drags preview by writing the scene: the lineset and liquid-line handles, the pipe and duct fitting moves, and the plan view's run point drag. In them, a follower stayed where an earlier frame put it once a later frame left it out. That happened when Alt was held to detach the joint, or when the drag came back to a zero delta, which connectivity leaves unwritten. - In 3D, a lineset end dragged with Alt and then cancelled with Escape left the joined lineset displaced. Released instead, it took one undo step, and undo restored only the dragged lineset. The lineset tool draws every segment as its own node, so every interior joint of a drawn run has a follower. - `shared/follower-frames.ts` writes each such follower back to its drag-start fields, and the refrigerant drag's finish always reverts every connection. - The pipe and duct point drags preview through live overrides. They now drop the overrides of nodes the current frame no longer moves, instead of showing the follower at its old position until release. - **MEP handle drags run under the editor's gesture owner** (`43f4b7d3`; P3 #2 and nit #6). - `useHandleDragScope` starts each drag with `beginGesture`, which `@pascal-app/editor` now exports. Any history command, a mode, level or selection change, the node's deletion, or the handles unmounting now cancels the drag. - Before, an undo issued outside the keyboard landed under the live drag, and the release then committed over it. Unmounting left the scope claimed, history paused and window listeners writing the scene. Keyboard ⌘Z mid-drag still only aborts the drag, as in #1238. - A browser `pointercancel` now cancels the drag at all ten sites instead of committing it, as `useHandleDrag` does. - **Held Alt frees the move drags** (`42ce9ca6`; nit #7). The fitting arrow moves and the pipe and duct run slides ignored Alt in Grid mode, while their turns and resizes honoured it (E-004). Run point drags keep Alt for "Detach the joint". - **Tests and docs** (nit #10, plus two nits from the re-review of `f3b381d1`). - The new rendered tests mount the real handles: lineset ends, the duct point drag, the pipe and duct fitting arrows, the duct fitting resize, and the pipe and duct run slides (`49c84c19`, `0f529c01`). Between them they cover connected followers, undo, Alt, `pointercancel` and unmounting. The plan-view point drag tests call the lineset's and duct's registered `move-path-point` affordance directly, so they don't exercise the plan view's dispatcher. - Four of the ten `pointercancel` sites have no test: the pipe fitting resize, the duct point drag and roll, and the pipe point drag. With all four changed to commit on cancel, the nodes suite still passes. - `wiki/architecture/interaction-scope.md` records the gesture-owner claim. - The `onCancel` doc in `gesture-lifecycle.ts` said it "Never writes the scene", but every MEP drag reverts its paused preview writes there. It now says `onCancel` records no history, because undo and redo cancel the gesture before they jump (`e65a11d9`). Two corrections to #1238's description, from the review (#11): - Escape did not leave the scene unchanged for a lineset or liquid line dragged with Alt; that case is fixed here. - "There is nothing on its axis to align to" was inaccurate: the ghost move tool aligns in Lines mode. The arrow move neither aligns nor steps there; see P3 #4 below. **Still open, not changed here** - **P3 #4, tried and reverted.** In the default Lines mode, a fitting's move arrow slides freely while its size handles step by a fixed size increment. - `f3b381d1` made the arrow step on the grid in Lines mode too. Codex flagged that as a P1: E-004 gates grid steps on `isGridSnapActive()`, and the HUD would read "Snapping: Lines" while the arrow quantized to the grid. `44adc1f8` reverts it, so the arrow behaves as on `main`. - The fix that fits E-004 is for the arrow to align in Lines mode, as the ghost move tool does. That is a larger change than this PR. - **P3 #5, carried over.** The duct run arrow slide (`duct-segment/selection.tsx`) holds at the last welded frame, but its release first tries the elbow-and-connector reroute (`planRunTranslationOffsets`). This has two effects: - A slide that only the reroute can make is unreachable. - When an end moves at least two fitting legs plus 5 cm, the preview shows the joined runs following, while the release builds elbows and connectors instead. This dates from #438. The duct ghost move tool already previews the reroute first. - **Nit #8, carried over.** Rotating a surface-hosted node with the registry move tool (`move-registry-node-tool.tsx`) keeps previewing when the follow fails, while the drop refuses. - **The whole-run move tools ignore Alt** (re-review nit; older than this series). The pipe and duct run move tools step whenever Grid mode is on (`pipe-segment/move-tool.tsx:180`, `duct-segment/move-tool.tsx:209`), and `isGridSnapActive()` does not read Alt. So held Alt now frees a run's center arrow but not a move-tool move of the same run, which E-004 also covers. - **Per-frame scene writes** (re-review, informational; from #438). The fitting, lineset and plan-view drags write `useScene` on every frame, which E-007 and `wiki/architecture/tools.md` rule out; the duct and pipe point drags already preview through live overrides. The follower frames here build on that existing pattern, and moving these drags to live overrides is a follow-up. - **Selection lost on a late release, seen while recording.** Releasing the button after Escape can clear the selection, because the click that follows reaches the canvas: - In 3D, a cancelled handle drag swallows only a click within 300 ms, the same window the editor's `useHandleDrag` uses. - In the plan view, the dispatcher's Escape cancel (`floorplan-registry-layer.tsx`) swallows none. This happens on `main` too. - **From earlier rounds.** Bugbot's "Vertical collar draw blocks next segment" (rated P3) is fixed in #1242 (open). The pipe fitting move tool has no grade guard. The connected editing these drags belong to is @sudhir9297's work from #1115. Next owner: Maintainer. ## How to test 1. Draw a two-segment lineset run, select one segment and drag the shared end's arrow: the other segment follows. Hold Alt: the end moves alone and the other segment returns to where it was. Press Escape and release: both segments are back where they started. Repeat, but release with Alt held: there is one undo step, the other segment never moved, and undo puts the end back. Dragging the shared end's point in the plan view behaves the same way. 2. Drag the end of a lineset, fitting or run, then drag it back onto its start without releasing. Every joined node is back where it was. 3. In the plan view, drag the free end of a straight duct whose other end sits on an elbow: the elbow turns to follow. Hold Alt: the elbow turns back and the end moves alone. Release: the elbow keeps its original turn. 4. Press Shift until the HUD reads "Snapping: Grid". Drag a pipe fitting's move arrow: it steps by the grid. Hold Alt: it slides freely. Do the same on a duct fitting, and on a pipe or duct run's center arrow. In the default Lines mode, the fitting arrow slides freely, as on `main`. Automated checks: - `bun run ci` passed locally on this head, `0f529c01` (exit 0). - Biome, the i18n and skills checks, the root i18n and proxy tests and the production-server smoke test always run outside Turbo, so they ran fresh. - Turbo also ran the nodes build, both apps' type-checks and builds, and the editor, nodes and app test suites fresh. It replayed the other type-checks, package tests and builds from its cache. Turbo caches only tasks that succeed, and those inputs are unchanged since the earlier passing runs. - Test counts were core 7,073, nodes 5,337, editor 2,867, viewer 1,350, MCP 1,523, CLI 139, IFC converter 106, geometry-script 64 and app 78, with 0 failures. - New tests that fail on `23f64785`'s source and pass here (the re-review re-ran these on the base): - nodes `lineset/selection.test.tsx` mounts the real handles on two joined linesets: - Alt then Escape; - Alt then release, followed by undo; - `runUndo()` mid-drag cancels the drag and undoes the earlier edit, and the later release commits nothing; - after a `pointercancel` or an unmount mid-drag, the scope is idle, `inputDragging` is false, history is tracking again and there is no history entry. - nodes `shared/path-point-affordance.test.ts`: - a plan-view lineset end drag puts the joined lineset back on an Alt frame and on a zero-delta frame; - on a plan-view duct end drag, an Alt frame turns a re-aimed elbow back. - nodes `duct-segment/selection.test.tsx`: holding Alt on a duct end drag drops the joined duct's live preview, and the release commits one step without moving it. - nodes `pipe-fitting/selection.test.tsx`: - Alt slides the arrow freely in Grid mode, and a `pointercancel` drops the drag; - a joined pipe run goes back when the slide returns to the start. - New tests from `49c84c19` and `0f529c01`. Each was checked by reverting its fixed line at this head, one line at a time, and each revert fails exactly that test: - nodes `duct-fitting/selection.test.tsx` (new file): - Alt slides the arrow freely in Grid mode, and a `pointercancel` drops the drag. It fails when the arrow ignores Alt, and when `pointercancel` commits the move; - a joined duct goes back when the slide returns to the start. It fails when the move writes without its follower frame; - a `pointercancel` drops a resize. It fails when `pointercancel` commits the resize. - nodes `duct-segment/selection.test.tsx` and the new `pipe-segment/selection.test.tsx`, on the run center arrow: - Alt slides it freely in Grid mode. It fails when the slide ignores Alt; - a `pointercancel` drops the slide. It fails when `pointercancel` commits the slide. - Two more duct fitting tests pin behavior unchanged from `main`: in Grid mode the arrow claims a handle-drag scope and steps on the grid, and in Lines and Off it slides freely. ## Screenshots / screen recording Both clips play the same scripted input in the plan view of the local dev server. The "after" clip runs this branch. The "before" clip runs this branch with `shared/path-point-affordance.ts`, the file that drives this drag, swapped back to `23f64785`'s version; that file is unchanged on `main`. **Before and after, plan view, lineset joint.** Top row: `main`. Bottom row: this PR. Left: dragging A's corner with Alt held. Right: just after releasing with Alt held. [Top: main. Bottom: this PR. Left: dragging with Alt held. Right: released with Alt held](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Flineset-alt-detach-before-after-plan.png) **Before, on `main`'s plan-view drag (46 s).** - Holding Alt lights up the HUD's "Alt: Detach the joint" row, but B stays on A's dragged corner. - Escape restores both lines. - A second drag is released with Alt held: B is committed moved. Ctrl+Z puts both back. [lineset-alt-detach-before-plan.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Flineset-alt-detach-before-plan.mp4) **After, on this branch (45 s).** - Lineset A's corner end is dragged and Lineset B follows. - Holding Alt puts B back at its start, and the HUD's "Alt: Detach the joint" row lights up. Releasing Alt rejoins B; holding Alt again puts it back. - Escape restores both lines. The plan view drops the selection on that release, as on `main`, so A is selected again. - A second drag is released with Alt held: only A's end moves. Ctrl+Z puts it back. [lineset-alt-detach-escape-undo-plan.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Flineset-alt-detach-escape-undo-plan.mp4) [Left: B follows the drag. Middle: with Alt held, B is back at its start. Right: released with Alt, only A's end moved](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-4b42be0a-3a2d-5290-a138-983c625f14a6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Flineset-follow-alt-detach-release-plan.png) ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches core 3D/plan editing, scene history pausing, and live preview state across many MEP affordances; behavior is heavily tested but regressions in connected-run editing are possible. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 0f529c01fe8259dbc3d0151aa14c2474d5baf90e. title: Opening builds recompute the whole level's room graph, so load time grows with openings × walls per level
body:
### Summary

Every window/door build ends up calling `extractRooms` over **all walls and separators of its level**, with no caching. On scenes with a few hundred openings per level this dominates load time: one window build takes 40–60 ms, the viewer drops to 0–7 fps while loading, and a 2,000-wall building takes 75–99 s to finish building (5,000 walls did not finish within 10 minutes). The same scenes without openings build in seconds.

Versions: `@pascal-app/core`, `@pascal-app/viewer`, `@pascal-app/nodes` 1.0.7, `three` 0.187.0, `@react-three/fiber` 9.8.2, WebGPU backend, Chromium.

### Where the time goes

Call chain (paths are in the published `dist/`, 1.0.7):

1. `lib/opening-casing.js:37` → `roomSideFaces(nodes, opening.parentId)`, and for windows `lib/opening-casing.js:50` → `openingExteriorFace(opening, nodes)` → `roomSideFaces(...)` again (`lib/opening-exterior-face.js:8`).
2. `systems/wall/wall-room-sides.js:60` `roomSideFaces` → `roomFaceCover` (same file, line ~38).
3. `roomFaceCover` filters **every** wall/separator sharing the wall's parent, then calls `extractRooms(boundaries)` (`lib/room-graph.js:823`) to keep only the spans of a single wall.

So the full room graph of a level is rebuilt once or twice per opening. Nothing in the inputs changes between two openings of the same level during the initial build.

A Chrome CPU profile of a 1,000-wall / 4-level / 377-opening scene (unminified build, navigation until the build finishes, 22.9 s of CPU) shows:

| Function (`@pascal-app/core`) | Self time |
|---|---|
| `minRotationSignature` (`lib/room-graph.js:27`) | 2.85 s |
| `pointKey` (`lib/room-graph.js:13`) | 2.33 s |
| `extractRoomGraph` (`lib/room-graph.js:881`) | 0.73 s |
| other room-graph helpers (spatial index, near-miss junctions, …) | ~1.3 s |

With the viewer's `perf` prop on, the `window` span totals 9.8 s over 251 builds (~39 ms each, up to 56 ms). `wall-rebuild` takes only 1.6 s over 1,838 builds. Because the wall system's 8 ms frame budget is checked between items, one window build alone blows the budget, so frames stay at 40–60 ms throughout the load.

### Measurements

Headless Chromium on an Apple M4 Pro, production build, viewer defaults unless noted. Each scene has 4 levels made of 4-wall rooms; one wall in four has a window, and half the rooms have a door.

| Scene | Time until all walls are built | fps while loading (min/median) |
|---|---|---|
| 1,000 walls, 377 openings | 20.7 s | 10 / 15 |
| 2,000 walls, ~750 openings | 99 s | 0 / 6 |
| 5,000 walls, ~1,900 openings | not finished after 600 s | 0 / 1 |
| 1,000 walls, **no openings** | 3.8 s | 43 / 50 |
| 5,000 walls, **no openings** | 18.1 s (`disablePostFx`, shadows off) | 20 / 41 |

Once the build finishes, every scene settles at the `maxFps` cap (48–50 fps by default, 57–60 with `maxFps={120}`). The problem is the build only, not steady-state rendering.

### Repro

1. Create a level with N rectangular rooms (4 walls each) laid out on a grid, with a window on one wall in four and a door in half the rooms.
2. Load it with `createNodes` (or `setScene`, same result) and mount `<Viewer perf />`.
3. Compare the `window` spans with the `wall-rebuild` spans, and the time until the scene is built, against the same scene without openings.

### Suggested fix

- **Cache the room graph per level**, keyed on the level id plus a revision of its wall/separator geometry (ids, endpoints, thickness, curve). This could live next to the existing level miter cache (`viewer/dist/systems/wall/level-miter-cache.js`), which already does this for miters. `roomSideFaces`/`roomFaceCover` would then look up spans by `boundaryId` instead of re-extracting.
- Or at minimum, memoise `roomSideFaces` per `(wallId, level revision)`. That would also remove the second call that `openingExteriorFace` makes for windows.

### Related findings (happy to file these separately)

1. **Frame budget.** One opening build is not interruptible, so the 8 ms budget is ineffective while openings are being built. A per-item cost cap, or deferring casing/exterior-face work, would keep frames smooth even before the cache lands.
2. **`SceneBvh` misses meshes added after mount.** `viewer/dist/components/viewer/scene-bvh.js:84-94` only walks the scene in a mount effect, so walls built progressively never get a `boundsTree` (0 of 6,000 wall meshes in our test, with `useBvh` on).
3. **Material swap re-renders every wall renderer.** Updating a `scene:` material used by 200 walls (`updateSceneMaterial`) rebuilds no geometry but causes one 72–84 ms frame on a 1,000-wall scene. We use material changes to highlight element categories; a cheaper path for this would help.
4. **Neighbour rebuilds during the initial build.** Loading 1,000 walls produced 1,838 `wall-rebuild` spans, which suggests neighbours get rebuilt again as their adjacent walls arrive.

We consume Pascal as a viewer only (no fork, no patches), so a fix upstream is the only option on our side. Thanks for the library: once built, rendering holds the frame cap even at 5,000 walls.

title: [Maintainer] Leave vertical routing after a riser drawn from a collar
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to #1236, which @Aymericr merged as `3a972b68` from head `bbe4b501`. #1236 ported @sudhir9297's connected duct and pipe editing from #1115, and #1237, #1238 and #1240 followed it. This PR fixes the one Bugbot finding still open on #1236's merged head. It also adds a test for the collar-start behaviour behind two other Bugbot threads there. - **A riser drawn from a collar no longer blocks the next section** (`f0977ddd`; Bugbot Medium ["Vertical collar draw blocks next segment"](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1236#discussion_r4510067975)). - "Draw from collar" on a collar that points up or down sets Route to Vertical, along with the collar's size and system. A vertical route rises to the panel's target elevation. After the riser reached it, the next vertical section ran from the riser's top to that same height. - On `main`, the cursor then reads "Target elevation: … · click or Enter to place" next to "Run must be at least 0.05 m" (0.08 m for ducts), and clicks place nothing until Route or the target changes. - Now a riser placed from a fixed collar switches the pipe tool to "Plan route" and the duct tool to "Horizontal". The next click draws across from the riser's top at the same height. A vertical route chosen while drawing from a pipe or duct end is left as it was (`5a20e28c` tests this). - "Fixed collar" follows each tool's existing rule. For pipes, that is any port not on a pipe segment, including pipe fittings and traps; the pipe collar inspector is offered on both. For ducts, it is terminals and equipment, not duct fittings. - **The "Draw from collar" handlers sit next to the continuation starters** (`466f46f8`). `activatePipeCollarContinuation` and `activateDuctCollarContinuation`, in each kind's `continuation.ts`, hold the inspector buttons' code unchanged. Tests can now start a collar draw without rendering the inspector. - **A test pins how a pipe run leaves a fixed collar** (`d8c5cb2d`, `1a250ac0`). This behaviour is what Bugbot's High ["Fixture start clears chosen waste grade"](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1236#discussion_r4509406832) and Medium ["Snapped grade connect fails with wrong message"](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1236#discussion_r4509406836) describe. Both are answered on #1236 with no code change: - The first section follows the collar's axis. - A grade that cannot meet the collar is refused with the grade message. - The next section takes the chosen grade and joins without a bend. The collar draw these changes touch is @sudhir9297's work from #1115. Next owner: Maintainer. ## How to test 1. Place a P-trap and select it. Under "Connect pipe", click the Inlet's "Draw from collar"; the inlet points up. Click once: a riser rises to "Target elevation above level", and Route now reads "Plan route". Move the pointer: the preview runs across from the riser's top at the same height, and a click places it. On `main`, Route stays Vertical and clicks place nothing. 2. Do the same with a ceiling diffuser's "Draw from collar" under "Connect duct". After the riser, Route reads "Horizontal" and the next click draws across. 3. Choose Vertical yourself and draw a riser from the free end of a pipe. Route stays Vertical after the riser. 4. Start a waste pipe on a trap's Outlet, which points sideways, with Fall set to Graded at 2%. The start click sets Fall to Level. Set Graded at 2% again and click away from the outlet. Nothing is placed, and the cursor reads "The connection elevation conflicts with the chosen grade. Adjust the grade or target elevation." Set Level and click: the pipe leaves straight along the outlet. Set Graded at 2% and click further on: the next pipe falls at 2% from that pipe's end, with no bend fitting. Automated checks: - `bun run ci` passed locally on `f0977ddd` (exit 0). The two commits after it, up to this head (`5a20e28c`), only add assertions to the new test file. Biome and the whole nodes suite (5,340 pass, 0 fail) were run again on this head. - Biome, the i18n and skills checks and the production-server smoke test always run outside Turbo, so they ran fresh. - Turbo ran the nodes build and tests, the editor package's type-check and tests, the viewer tests, and both apps' type-checks, builds and tests fresh. - Turbo replayed core, MCP, CLI, the IFC converter and geometry-script from its cache. Turbo caches only tasks that succeed, and their inputs are unchanged since earlier passing runs. - Test counts were core 7,073, nodes 5,340, editor 2,867, viewer 1,352, MCP 1,523, CLI 139, IFC converter 106, geometry-script 64 and app 78, with 0 failures. - On GitHub at `5a20e28c`, CI's Changed paths, quality and cli-smoke jobs passed. `mcp-ci` doesn't run because no MCP paths changed. Cursor Bugbot passed, and Codex's code review completed; neither reported findings. - New tests are in nodes `shared/collar-draw.test.tsx`. They mount the real pipe and duct tools and drive them with plan-view pointer events. - "a riser drawn from a vertical pipe collar continues on the plan route" and its duct counterpart, "… continues on the horizontal route", fail when the route switch is removed from their tool. They also fail when the switch applies after every riser, because a riser drawn from the new run's end with Vertical chosen again must keep the vertical route. - "a pipe run from a fixed collar leaves along its axis, then takes the chosen grade" passes on `main`'s tools. It fails if the free end stops following the collar axis, or if the start keeps the chosen grade. It also fails if the refusal shows the fitting-clearance message instead of the grade message, or if the graded section gets a bend. ## Screenshots / screen recording Both images start the same way: select the P-trap, click the Inlet's "Draw from collar", click once to place the riser, then move the pointer to the right. They were captured in the local editor (`bun run dev` in `apps/editor`, with the nodes package built from this branch). title: templates: listing viewer for Pascal's public read
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `templates/viewer-listing`, the first viewer SDK template: a standalone Vite + React Three Fiber app that renders a Pascal project's published 3D file from Pascal's public read (`GET /api/projects/{id}/scene`). It uses no `@pascal-app/*` package, so it proves a custom viewer can be built, restyled and deployed anywhere without the editor packages.

- Floors control, room hover with name and area, door and window open clips.
- Renews expired signed links by reading the scene again.
- Loading, preparing, unavailable, not published and no-WebGL states.
- A strict Content-Security-Policy written at build time (it needs `'unsafe-eval'` for the KTX2 transcoder worker; documented).
- `AGENTS.md` for coding agents, `README.md`, `.env.example`.
- Not a workspace: it installs from its own folder with npm or bun and ships its own lockfile.

Production build: 376 KB gzipped JS (81.5 KB shell, 294.6 KB 3D chunk loaded in parallel with the read), plus the KTX2 transcoder when a file has KTX2 textures.

**Merge after** the hosted read is deployed (pascalorg/private-editor#1543): the template defaults to `https://editor.pascal.app`.

## How to test

1. `cd templates/viewer-listing && npm install && npm run typecheck && npm run test:e2e`: 7 Playwright tests pass against a mocked read and a small fixture GLB.
2. With the hosted read available, `VITE_PASCAL_BASE_URL=<host> npm run dev`, open `/?project=<public published project id>`: the model loads, the floors control lists the levels, hovering a room shows its name and area, clicking a door plays its clip.

title: [Maintainer] editor: restore scene auto-framing on load
body:
## What does this PR do? Maintainer port of #766 by @ActArtech, brought up to current `main`. The contributor's commits are kept with their authorship. Opening a project now frames the scene instead of leaving the camera at the default pose: - `EditorContent` mounts `useAutoFrame()` and sends `camera-controls:fit-scene` again once per load, when the viewer reports the scene ready. - **Bounds are in world space** (`3fe423cd`, Codex P1): `computeSceneBoundsXZ` accumulates each ancestor's `position` and `rotation` yaw, so a moved or rotated building frames on where it actually is. - Doors, windows and wall items are bounded by their wall, not by their wall-local `position` (`dd0570c3`). - **Orthographic zoom is fitted** (`cd4f3cf1`, Codex P1): the fit plan includes a sphere centred on the pivot, and an orthographic camera gets `fitToSphere` after `setLookAt`, the same way `frameViewerCamera` does it. Perspective is unchanged. - **Level follow** (`1df23a00`): a pure `planLevelFollow` decides between the default pose (first run, empty scene), a pivot rest (first run over a loaded scene, or a level, level-mode or camera change), or nothing. When the controls rebuild, for example after leaving XR, the pivot rests on the level instead of staying at the origin. - The merge keeps `main`'s sticky `lastLevelId`, `keepEyeOverGround` and the pivot re-rest when a new controls instance is built. - Fit planning lives in pure helpers in `fit-scene-framing.ts`. A fit requested in first-person, or before the orbit controls mount, is queued and applied when orbit resumes. Framing rests the pivot on the selected level's ground. - `window.__pascalCameraControls` stays dev-only. ## How to test 1. `bun dev`, open a project with content far from the origin, e.g. `/project/villa-offset` or `/project/seattle-parking`. 2. Don't touch the canvas: the camera animates to frame the scene. On `main` it stays on the default pose (zoomed into the middle of the site). 3. Switch to the orthographic camera and open a differently sized project: the zoom fits the new scene. 4. Switch levels and toggle Stack / Full height: the camera follows the level. 5. Enter first-person, load another project, exit first-person: the new scene is framed. 6. `bun test packages/editor/src/components/editor/fit-scene-framing.test.ts packages/editor/src/lib/scene-bounds.test.ts` ## Screenshots / screen recording | Scene | Before (`main`) | After (this PR) | |---|---|---| | villa-offset | [before](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpr766_before_villa_offset.png) | [after](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpr766_after_villa_offset.png) | | seattle-parking | [before](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpr766_before_seattle_parking.png) | [after](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpr766_after_seattle_parking.png) | Load of seattle-parking, before then after (no input): [pr766_load_framing_before_after.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fpr766_load_framing_before_after.mp4) These captures predate the bounds, zoom and level-follow commits. ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Local `bun run ci` passed on `dd0570c3` (exit 0). Remaining follow-ups: - Follow Pascal treats the automatic fit as the person taking over. - The pending-fit retry is a single animation frame. - Stair segments placed relative to the previous one, and openings on roof faces, are bounded approximately. Supersedes #766. Credit: @ActArtech. Co-authored-by: ActArtech To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: viewer: sparse tiled room map for daylight; rooms built from settled geometry
body:
## What does this PR do?

Replaces the daylight room-id map (`viewer/src/lib/daylight`) with a sparse tiled map, and fixes how the room light is built on large scenes.

**The map.** The old map was one texture with every level stacked along Y at 10 cm cells, levels found by height across the whole site and capped at 8. A 40-storey tower lit floors 8–39 with whichever room was rasterized last, a campus of buildings fell to ~80 cm cells and still mixed its buildings' floors, and a 300 × 200 m hall took 48 MB at 20 cm.

- **Per level, tiled.** Each level keeps its own 10 cm cells, cut into 1.6 m tiles. A tile inside one room (or outside every room) is one value; only tiles a room edge crosses keep their cells, in a shared two-byte atlas. A level's rooms are grouped into clusters with their own rects, so open ground between them costs nothing. Memory follows wall length, not site area, and nothing grows with the number of floors.
- **Per building.** A point finds candidate buildings in a coarse directory and its level by binary search over that building's live floor heights (sorted heights stay sorted when levels explode apart). Buildings side by side with different floor heights each keep their floors. No level cap.
- **Built tile row by tile row**, never a dense per-level grid; zone holes are rasterized; where zones overlap, the smallest room wins (an automatic floor-wide room or a unit no longer swallows the rooms in it).
- **Presentation.** "Open to the sky" and the meters read each level's real presentation (shown, not shadow-only; focused when every level over it in its building is hidden). Texture sizes come from the device. The lighting and the exterior mask share one lookup.

**Building the room light.**

- Doorway and cover rays test only the meshes near them (a 2 m grid of mesh bounds taken from current vertices) instead of every wall: room builds on a 2,560-wall scene drop from 37 s to 0.6 s.
- Rooms wait for the scene to settle and rebuild each time walls, slabs, openings or zones finish changing (they finish without a geometry revision). A scene still loading after 10 s builds anyway and again every 10 s while it progresses. Before, a large scene built its rooms from half-built walls and kept them: doorways read as whole walls and corner rooms got diagonal "openings" pouring outdoor light in.

**Measured** (CPU bench over every room of each scene, plus browser checks):

| Scene | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 40-storey tower | 96/480 rooms right | 480/480 |
| Campus, 10 buildings × 5 floors | 708/1770, ~80 cm cells, 35 MB | 1770/1770, 10 cm, 17 MB |
| 300 × 200 m, 8 floors | 48 MB at 20 cm, 1.1 s build | 14 MB at 10 cm, 0.3 s |
| Houses | | same room at every point sampled at 5 cm (differences only within one cell of room edges); main-pass GPU time within run-to-run noise |

Known limits, unchanged: double-height rooms read as outside above the next floor's line; stairs and atriums carry no light between floors.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/viewer/src/lib/daylight`: new tests for a 40-storey tower, buildings with different floor heights, courtyard holes, memory along walls for a 300 × 200 m hall, overlapping zones, a room off the tile grid, an index texture within a small device limit, and when a level opens from above.
2. Open a multi-storey building, select an upper floor at night: every room has its own lamp pool (on `main`, floors past the 8th share one map layer).
3. Open a large scene (thousands of walls) at night and let it load: rooms stay lit by their own windows and lamps, with no diagonal bright wedges in corner rooms.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet.

## Checklist

- [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

Tested in the hosted app (headless WebGPU and a desktop browser at night and midday), not with this repo's `bun dev`. Viewer package: typecheck clean, 1359 tests pass, `bun check` has no new findings.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Large refactor of viewer daylight shaders, GPU room lookup, and rebuild timing; behavior changes on multi-floor and large scenes, though coverage is broad in unit tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the daylight **room-id map** with a **sparse tiled** `RoomMap` (per level, per building, device-aware textures) so tall towers, multi-building sites, and huge floors resolve the correct room without blowing texture size or an 8-level cap. Zones can include **holes** (courtyards); overlapping zones prefer the **smallest** room.
> 
> **`RoomLighting`** now builds through that map, shares one probe between lighting and exterior mask, and tracks levels via **`setLevelPresentation`** (shown, shadow-only, focus / open-to-sky) instead of stacked `levelY` + offset uniforms. Doorway and cover rays use a **spatial mesh grid** so large wall counts build in sub-second time.
> 
> **`useDaylightRooms`** defers rebuilds until geometry **settles** (or after a 10s cap), skips builds while levels are exploding/moving, reapplies when loading still shrinks dirty nodes, and sets **`textureLimit`** from the renderer.
> 
> Scene input switches from height-stacked levels to **`MapLevel[]`** (floor Y + building index) in live and baked paths.
>

title: nodes: render-only entry for viewers without the editor
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `@pascal-app/nodes/render`: a render-only entry that lets an app rebuild a Pascal scene graph into geometry with `@pascal-app/core`, `@pascal-app/viewer` and `renderPlugin`, with no `@pascal-app/editor` and no `next` in its bundle, eager or lazy.

- Every built-in node definition is split into `definition.render.ts` (schema, geometry, renderer, system, bake, capabilities except paint, …) and `definition.edit.ts` (tools, panels, handles, floor-plan editing, paint, …). `definition.ts` composes both, so `builtinPlugin` registers exactly the definitions it did before.
- `renderPlugin` has the same 56 kinds, plugin id and `apiVersion`. An app loads exactly one built-in plugin; the registry and plugin contract v1 are unchanged (E-014).
- Render-side helpers move out of the editor: door and window interaction, measurement formatting and the room floor elevation rule to core; measurement labels and presentation to viewer. Separator focus and procedural-item placement previews become edit-only renderer wrappers; roof-segment slots are split from paint. All 918 editor barrel exports remain.
- The editor peer of `@pascal-app/nodes` is now optional (`peerDependenciesMeta`).
- `scripts/check-render-bundle.ts` (`bun run check:render-bundle`, in CI) builds the published `./render` export with esbuild and fails on any path to `@pascal-app/editor` or `next` in any chunk. It also parses every Pascal-owned module in the graph and rejects computed `import()`/`require()`, `import.meta.glob` and workers, which the resolver cannot see. It self-tests every case and checks a declaration consumer typechecks without editor or Next.
- E-001 records that `nodes/render` never imports `editor`.

Not in this PR: viewer configuration instead of `process.env`, decoder paths, storage guards and an external Vite fixture. Those come next, before the release that makes this usable from npm.

## How to test

1. `bun run check:render-bundle`: the self-test passes, 1,156 Pascal modules are scanned, and the render graph builds with no editor or Next edges.
2. `bun test packages/nodes/src`: 5,351 pass, including both entries registering the same 56 kinds and focused regressions for separator focus, procedural ceiling cuts (preview, cancel, commit, unmount), roof slots and transient door state.
3. Open the editor and the viewer on any scene: rendering, doors, windows, measurements and roofs behave as before.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A: no visual change. Checked in a browser against the private host on a sample scene; the editor and the live viewer render identically before and after.

title: [Maintainer] Fix node dragging and refine pillars, elevators, and roofs
body:
## What does this PR do? Maintainer port of #1112 by @sudhir9297, merged with current `main`, with the post-review fixes landed. Sudhir's seven commits keep their authorship. The follow-up commits carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer. From #1112, unchanged in intent: - **Node interactions:** handle previews stay in live overrides, and moving, snapping and selection cleanup for hosted openings and accessories are fixed. - **Pillars:** lower-polygon geometry, consistent bounds and plan drawing, paint coverage, property previews, and a single preset gallery with white as the default for new pillars. - **Elevators:** moves go through the generic mover. `movable.resolvePosition` recomputes the landing height on every frame and again at commit, in 3D and in the plan. Doors are recessed behind the entrance surround, and stops and openings stay in sync. - **Roofs:** surface queries and accessory cache invalidation are corrected, and editing limits aligned. Trim editing is a transient interaction scope. A failed geometry rebuild keeps the previous mesh and offers a retry. There's a four-column roof menu, and ghosts for all nine forms. Maintainer changes on top: - **Merges with `main`:** - The first merge resolved conflicts against main's i18n migration of panels and tools, MEP connected editing (duct and refrigerant-line selection keep main's gesture owner, Alt free-slide and paused history), and the move-tool changes. - Later merges brought in #1249, #1251, #1248 and #1244. Only the compiled en and en-XA catalogs conflicted; they were regenerated with `i18n:extract`. - **Lean-to managed posts can't be moved from the editor.** The column's `movable.override` returns `{ axes: [], gridSnap: false }`; `null` means "use the base config". A new core `isMoveLocked` check sits in `setMovingNode`, which every editor move entry goes through (3D drag, 2D Ctrl-drag, action-menu Move, move tool, group pick-up). The Move button is hidden for these posts. - **Lean-to posts can't be duplicated.** A new optional `duplicable.allow({ node })` opt-out is checked by `isNodeDuplicable`. Duplicate, copy and cut skip managed posts in the floating, 2D and mobile menus, `duplicateNodeAndPickUp` and the clipboard. - **Saved scenes keep their column finish (E-003).** The slot fallback stays concrete plaster and steel. New columns get explicit white slots from `defaults()`, the pillar tool and the material reset. - **Elevator landing:** the resolver takes the `nodes` it's given instead of reading the global store. - **Elevator runtime (Bugbot finding):** an idle cab on a landing that becomes disabled is sent to the nearest available landing instead of staying shut there (`cb4b4821`). - **Placement selection (Bugbot finding):** `selectPlacedNode` adopts the building of a building-parented node, such as an elevator, and keeps the current floor when it belongs to that building. Main's dedicated elevator handoff did this before (`bd1c3eca`). - **Cleanup:** the `resolvePosition` docs moved next to the other `movable` fields in `plugin-authoring.md`. Unreferenced roof-type WebP files and thumbnail-prompt JSON files are removed. ## How to test 1. Run `bun dev` and add a lean-to extension. Try to drag a post in 3D, Ctrl-drag it in 2D, and use Move and Duplicate from the action menu. Nothing moves or duplicates. Duplicating the whole lean-to still copies its posts. 2. Open an existing scene with unpainted columns: they still render concrete. A newly placed pillar is white. 3. Place an elevator across levels and move it over a raised slab: the landing height follows during the drag and on drop. One undo restores the move. After placing, the floor stays selected. 4. With an elevator idle on a floor, disable that floor in its panel: the cab moves to the nearest enabled floor. 5. Draw each roof type: the ghost matches the form and all nine thumbnails show. In roof trim mode, Escape in a number field cancels the field only; Escape over the canvas exits trim. 6. Focused tests: `bun test packages/nodes/src/column packages/nodes/src/elevator packages/core/src/systems/elevator packages/editor/src/lib/node-action-movement.test.tsx packages/editor/src/lib/level-selection.test.ts`. ## Screenshots / screen recording Captures from @sudhir9297's branch, unchanged by the port. The visuals for roofs, pillars and elevators are the same, and the follow-ups change no UI except hiding Move and Duplicate for lean-to posts. **Four-column roof menu and thumbnails** ![Roof menu and thumbnails](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/0ecb28179ae4e844196aed16d331f6a65096774d/wiki/images/node-tool-review/roof-menu-and-thumbnails.jpg) **Roof inspector thumbnails** ![Roof inspector thumbnails](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/0ecb28179ae4e844196aed16d331f6a65096774d/wiki/images/node-tool-review/roof-inspector-thumbnails.jpg) **Barrel roof** ![Barrel roof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/0ecb28179ae4e844196aed16d331f6a65096774d/wiki/images/node-tool-review/barrel-roof.jpg) **Pillar preset gallery** ![Pillar preset gallery](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pascalorg/editor/0ecb28179ae4e844196aed16d331f6a65096774d/wiki/images/node-tool-review/pillar-presets.jpg) ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Local `bun run ci` passed on `bd1c3eca` (exit 0). Independent read-only reviews approved `0ecb2817`, both merge heads (`eeb4de1a`, `0b06f914`), and `bd1c3eca` with the two Bugbot fixes. Follow-ups, including the three Codex P2s: - Group moves don't call `resolvePosition`, so an elevator in a group keeps its old landing height (Codex). - Erasing paint on a new white column falls back to concrete (Codex). - Column and elevator preset images load from host-relative `/icons/` paths that aren't in the published `@pascal-app/nodes` package (Codex). - The agent `move_node` doesn't check `isMoveLocked`, so an agent can still move a managed post. - Document `duplicable.allow` in `plugin-authoring.md`. - Have the agent `duplicate_node` use `isNodeDuplicable`. - `selectPlacedNode` can clear an active zone when `selection.buildingId` was null, and doesn't fall back to scanning a building's children for older scenes. - The panelled-pedestal base sizes depth with `baseWidthScale` in both the renderer and the bounds (Bugbot, low). Supersedes #1112. Credit: @sudhir9297. Co-authored-by: sudhir

title: [Maintainer] wall: add endHeightOffset for a sloped top edge
body:
## What does this PR do? Maintainer port of #640 by @vducasse, merged with current `main`, with review fixes on top. Vincent's commits keep their authorship. From #640: a wall gets an optional `endHeightOffset`, and its top slopes linearly from `height` at the start to `height + endHeightOffset` at the end. This covers knee walls, lean-to and attic partitions. - **Geometry and openings:** the viewer extrudes the slope and clamps opening cuts to the sloped top, on straight and curved walls. - **Doors and windows** must fit under the top over their whole span. - **Trims** slope their crowns. - **Print preflight** rejects sloped walls with `unsupported_wall_print_slope`. - **Inspector:** the full and compact panels get an end-height-offset row with no static max. The minimum keeps the low end standing. - **Old scenes:** the field is optional, so they load unchanged (E-003). Maintainer changes: - **Merge with `main`:** opening clamps moved to `core/building/wall-openings` with a `fits` result, and main's removed face bands dropped from the PR. New call sites on main choose a sample point along the wall: - opening fit: the lowest top over the opening's span; - envelope checks (roof bearing, clash checks, usage fields): the higher end; - handles: the midpoint; - reported and seeded heights: the start. - **Split:** each piece gets the parent's top at its start as its height and the parent's rise over its span as its offset, so drafting across a sloped wall no longer leaves a sawtooth top. - **Merge and auto-heal:** sloped walls merge only when their tops meet at the joint and rise at the same rate; the offsets add up. `reverseWallDirection` flips the slope. - **Flat walls place doors and windows exactly as on `main`.** The new `fits` gate applies only to sloped walls. - **Curved walls:** arc length is converted to chord position, so the fit and the drawn top agree. - **API:** the `t` parameter is the last argument of `resolveWallTop` and `resolveWallEffectiveHeight`, with a default, so existing four-argument calls keep their meaning. - **IFC export:** a sloped wall is exported as a body clipped by an inclined half-space, so its top is 3 m to 2 m rather than a flat box. Openings still cut through it. - **Agents (Bugbot finding):** `add_door`, `add_window` and `move_node` refuse with `wall_too_low` an opening that fits nowhere under a sloped wall's top (`bcace739`). - **Agents (Codex P2):** a door asked for over a sloped wall's low end is first slid to where it fits, then refused only if no stretch of the wall takes it, matching the editor path (`bc3b712a`). - **Viewer (Codex P1):** where a mitre extends past the wall's end, the sloped top is clamped so top vertices never drop below the base (`449d83e5`). - **Usage field (Codex P2):** a sloped wall's full-height prism, and its crown trim, are labelled approximate rather than exact, so clash findings over the low end are softened (`509b34f7`). - **Merged current `main` again** after #1249 (`fefd5cab`). Only the compiled en and en-XA catalogs conflicted; they were regenerated with `i18n:extract`. ## How to test 1. Run `bun dev`, select a wall, and set "End height offset" to −1.5 m: the top slopes down toward the wall's end. 2. Draw a new wall that T-joins the sloped wall. The two pieces continue the same top line, with no step. 3. Add a door near the low end: it's refused where it doesn't fit under the top, and allowed further along. 4. Put a window taller than a flat 1 m wall: it's placed and clamped as on `main`. 5. Export IFC with a sloped wall and open it in a viewer: the top follows the slope. 6. Give a wall that meets another at an acute corner a steep offset: the top stays above the base at the mitre. 7. Focused tests: `bun test packages/core/src/systems/wall packages/core/src/building packages/core/src/spatial/usage-field packages/viewer/src/systems/wall packages/ifc-converter`. ## Screenshots / screen recording Sloped walls in a demo scene from this branch: the east walls rise from 1 m to 4 m and the west walls fall from 4 m to 1 m. [Sloped walls](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fwall_end_height_offset_sloped_walls.png) The inspector field and the original captures are in #640. ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Local `bun run ci` passed on `509b34f7` (exit 0). An earlier `quality` failure on `4a951beb`, in the ifc-converter test "scaling > grows linearly with the number of rooms", was a timing flake: - The test scene has no walls. - The rerun on the same head passed. - The same test has failed on `main`'s CI with ratios of 6.3–11.5. P3 follow-ups from the earlier review: - Split pieces of curved sloped walls slope along their own chord, so the top drifts slightly inside a piece. - `reverseWallDirection` only flips the offset on storey-bound walls. - Heal resolves bases through the global spatial grid. - Door sidelights are ignored in the fit check. - MCP and point-ask report only the start height. Supersedes #640. Credit: @vducasse. Co-authored-by: vducasse To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: [Maintainer] Typed wall length and angle, and typed cabinet coordinates
body:
## What does this PR do? Combines three community PRs into one typed-entry feature, on current `main`: - **#883 by @dkbbdev (base):** type an exact wall length during two-click drafting (#308). - **#887 by @dkbbdev:** AutoCAD-style typed cabinet coordinates, a distance along the wall plus a perpendicular offset (#885). - **#1207 by @saadmooh:** the typed wall angle, adapted from its dimension input. dkbbdev's commits keep their authorship, including every Bugbot-round fix. Behaviour, the same in the 3D tools and the 2D plan: - **Walls:** while drafting, start typing to open a Length / Angle HUD. The normal draft label stays until the first keystroke. Tab switches fields, Enter commits, and the next segment starts empty. - Escape has two stages: the first clears what was typed and keeps the draft, the second cancels. - Untyped drafts keep run, angle and junction snapping. - The typed angle is an absolute heading in the plan frame, measured as the 15° angle snap measures it; the placeholder shows the live heading. - **Cabinets:** once a cabinet snaps to a wall, type a distance, then Tab or comma for the offset, and Enter to place. Escape has the same two stages. A rejected placement keeps the typed values. Maintainer changes on top of the two merges: - **One shared store:** a single `usePlacementTyping` store, key router (`routePlacementTypingKey`) and HUD serve walls and cabinets, replacing the two parallel implementations. - **Typed angle:** added for walls. - **2D-only keys:** typed keys are taken in a window capture listener ahead of the global shortcuts. Before this, typing `1` switched phase, `m` armed Measure, and the first Escape cancelled the tool. A regression test mounts the real `useKeyboard` handler first. - **2D HUD sizing:** the HUD takes `unitsPerPixel` and the plan rotation from its caller. The wall draft renders outside `FloorplanRenderProvider`, so the HUD was plan-metre sized and off screen in 2D-only view; I found this in manual testing. - **Pointer handling:** the 3D Enter commits before the pointer moves, and the 2D HUD passes clicks through to the cabinet ghost. - **Docs:** the typed-entry convention is described in `wiki/architecture/tools.md`. ## How to test 1. Run `bun dev`, pick Walls, click a start point, move the pointer, and type `4.5`. Then Tab, type `90`, and press Enter: a 4.5 m wall heading 90° is committed. 2. Start another wall and type `2`. Press Escape: the HUD clears and the draft follows the pointer again. Press Escape again: the draft is cancelled. 3. Switch to 2D-only view, start a wall, and type `12m`. The phase doesn't change, Measure isn't armed, and Enter commits exactly 12 m. 4. Pick a base cabinet, hover until it snaps to a wall, and type `1`. Then Tab, `0.1`, Enter: the cabinet is placed 1 m along the wall and 0.1 m off it. 5. Focused tests: `bun test packages/editor/src/store/use-placement-typing.test.ts packages/editor/src/components/editor/floorplan-wall-typing-keys.test.tsx packages/editor/src/components/editor-2d/renderers/floorplan-placement-typing-hud.test.tsx`. ## Screenshots / screen recording Wall typed entry in 3D, then 2D-only (idle frames removed): [wall_typed_entry_3d_and_2d_walkthrough.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fwall_typed_entry_3d_and_2d_walkthrough.mp4) | Typed length and angle (3D) | First Escape keeps the draft (3D) | 2D-only: `12m` typed, no shortcut fired | |---|---|---| | [3D HUD](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fwall_typed_3d_length_angle_hud.png) | [Escape](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fwall_typed_3d_first_escape_keeps_draft.png) | [2D HUD](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-15234f48-a313-50eb-b560-fd49006211c1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fwall_typed_2d_only_12m_hud.png) | Cabinet typed entry isn't in the recording: my scripted browser couldn't get the ghost to attach to a wall. It's covered by the cabinet placement and typing-store tests. ## Checklist - [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Local `bun run ci` passed on `d7aea0c0`; the head adds only a comment reflow. An independent read-only review approved `471747da` after an earlier round with one P1, the 2D-only shortcut leak, fixed here. Its remaining P3 follow-ups: - A second Escape in 2D-only exits to Select, as on `main`. - The capture listener skips the delete-confirmation and version-preview guards. - The angle placeholder rounds to whole degrees. Supersedes #883, #887 and #1207. Credit: @dkbbdev and @saadmooh. Co-authored-by: dkbbdev Co-authored-by: saadmooh To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: viewer: render live scenes in any browser app, proven by a packed fixture
body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes the render-only entry from #1246 usable from any browser app. An external Vite app that installs the packed `@pascal-app/core`, `@pascal-app/viewer` and `@pascal-app/nodes`, with no `@pascal-app/editor` and no `next` in its tree, can now hydrate a scene graph and render it live with `renderPlugin` and `<Viewer>`. Stacked on #1246.

- `configureViewer({ assetsBaseUrl, storageUrl, decoders })` replaces module-evaluation `process.env` reads. Defaults keep today's behaviour; `apps/editor` passes its environment explicitly.
- Draco and Basis decoder directories are configurable through every loader. Basis is pinned instead of `drei-assets@master`.
- Remaining render-path environment reads are guarded, so apps need no `process` polyfill.
- The Viewer's canvas background, transition and GPU fallback use inline styles, so they render without Tailwind; the editor looks the same.
- Viewer preferences tolerate denied storage.
- The viewer README and `wiki/architecture/viewer-isolation.md` document the boot sequence and the one-active-scene-per-page limit.
- `fixtures/viewer-live` and `bun run check:viewer-live` pack the three packages, install them outside the repo with npm, and assert neither the editor nor `next` is installed. They then build with Vite, and check `vite dev` and `vite preview`, with storage available and denied, reach scene-ready with geometry for every node (walls, door, window, roof, ceiling with a procedural downlight cut, zone, measurement, separator, a GLTF item), draw calls and no page errors. A separate CI job runs it.

## How to test

1. `bun run check:viewer-live`: about 45 s; prints the isolation check, the Vite build and four browser runs (dev and preview, storage available and denied), each with geometry for every node and its draw-call count.
2. `bun run check:render-bundle`: still passes.
3. Open the editor: canvas, loading transition and GPU fallback look unchanged; assets and textures load.

## Screenshots / screen recording

N/A: no visual change in the editor. The fixture is verified headlessly (SwiftShader) in dev and production builds.

title: [Maintainer] nodes: a cancel that only ends typed wall entry keeps the draft
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to #1249, addressing the Cursor Bugbot finding [Cancel during typed wall entry exits tool](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/pull/1249#discussion_r4519034229), which landed unfixed when #1249 merged. While a typed wall session is open, a first cancel from **any** source (Escape, ⌘Z mid-draft, a toolbar cancel) now only clears the typed values. The next cancel drops the draft, and the Wall tool stays armed. Before this change, Escape already behaved this way, but ⌘Z and other cancel sources fell through unconsumed, so the global handler exited to Select and discarded the draft. - **3D wall tool** (`packages/nodes/src/wall/tool.tsx`): the first-stage cancel now calls `markToolCancelConsumed()` before clearing the session, the same way the cabinet tool does. - **2D-only plan** (`floorplan-wall-typing-keys.ts`, `floorplan-panel.tsx`): the plan's `tool:cancel` handler had the same gap. A new `endFloorplanWallTypingOnCancel()` keeps the plan's draft. In 2D-only view it also clears the session and consumes the cancel. In split view it leaves both to the 3D wall tool. - **Docs**: the typed-entry convention in `wiki/architecture/tools.md` now says the first cancel from any source ends typed entry. There's one known limitation, which predates this PR: in split view, if the 3D tool's cancel listener runs before the plan's, the plan drops its copy of the draft while the 3D draft survives. Fixing it needs the 3D tool to publish a draft signal from the start click. Its chain start is only published after the first segment today, so this is left for a follow-up. Typed wall length and angle entry is by @dkbbdev (#883, #887), combined in #1249. The fix and its tests are one squashed commit, and the docs are a separate commit; both carry a `Co-authored-by` trailer. ## How to test 1. `bun dev`, open a level, and pick the Wall tool in 3D-only view. 2. Click a start point and type `3`. The length HUD appears. 3. Press ⌘Z (or Ctrl+Z). Expected: the HUD clears, the wall draft is still attached to the pointer, and the tool is still Wall. 4. Press ⌘Z again. Expected: the draft is cancelled, and the tool is still Wall. 5. Repeat in 2D-only view. title: [Maintainer] Sloped walls: moving a door with a transom can be refused even when it fits further up the slope
body:
Follow-up from #1248, which added sloped wall tops through `endHeightOffset`.

When an agent moves a door that has a transom along a sloped wall, the slide toward the taller end only checks that the door leaf fits. The refusal check measures the full opening, door plus transom. So a door that would fit higher up the slope can still be refused.

Expected: the slide and the refusal check both use the full opening height, so the door slides to a spot where the whole opening fits. It's refused only if no part of the wall is tall enough.

The independent review of #1248 found this as a P3. It's low severity, and the plain door case works.

title: [Maintainer] viewer: give bake replace renderers the published graph
body:
## What does this PR do? Maintainer port of #1011 by @AxiomeCG onto current `main`. It's the contributor's single commit, cherry-picked with their authorship kept. **For a user:** in a published project's baked viewer, ground that a plugin draws from its site (a painted surface, grass) can now render. Before, the lot was an empty grey plane in the baked viewer, while the editor showed the grass. **Why it was missing:** a kind with `bake: 'replace'` has its baked mesh hidden by `GlbScene` and is re-rendered live through its `bakeReplaceRenderer`. That renderer only received `{ nodes }`. The baked viewer never loads the scene graph into `useScene`, so a renderer that builds from its parent found no parent and drew an empty group. **What changes:** - `BakeReplaceRenderer`'s component takes an optional `resolve`, with the same signature as `GeometryContext.resolve`. - `GlbScene` builds one stable resolver from its existing `sceneNodes` prop, which #1227 added for the selection callout. `GlbReplaceInstances` passes that resolver to every replace renderer. The resolver doesn't read `useScene`, and it's memoized on `sceneNodes`, so the memoized replace subtree still skips re-rendering on camera moves. - `wiki/architecture/node-definitions.md` → Bake policy documents the prop. **Port notes:** - Only `glb-scene.tsx` conflicted. `main` already had `sceneNodes`, so the resolver reuses it rather than adding a second prop. The PR's old level, identity and hover callbacks were dropped, because `main` replaced them with `onObjectsChange` and `onPick`. - **Scope:** no built-in kind in this repo uses `bake: 'replace'`. The consumers are plugins, such as the environment plugin's ground cover. A host only gets the fix by passing `sceneNodes` to `GlbScene`, which the selection callout already asks for. A plugin only gets it by reading `resolve` instead of the scene store, which is a change on the plugin side. **Compatibility:** there's no schema change, so saved scenes and existing bakes load as before (E-003). A renderer that ignores `resolve` behaves exactly as before, and plugins keep loading (E-010). ## How to test 1. `bun test packages/viewer/src/components/viewer/plugin-dispatch.test.tsx`. The new case mounts a replace renderer with an empty `useScene` and checks that it resolves its parent through `resolve`. With `resolve={resolve}` removed from `glb-replace-instances.tsx`, that case fails. 2. In a host that renders the baked viewer with `sceneNodes`, a plugin replace renderer that reads `resolve(node.parentId)` draws its parent-dependent geometry. `bun run ci` passed locally on `2e7c1553` (exit 0). ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A. The baked `/viewer` host isn't in this repo, so the change is covered by the dispatch test rather than a capture. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch Supersedes #1011. Credit: @AxiomeCG.

title: [Bug] check_collisions and verify_scene silently ignore overlapping procedural-item nodes

### What happened?

## Summary

Two `item` nodes with identical `2 m × 2 m` footprints at the same pose are correctly reported as overlapping. | Group | Sandbox version | `get_project_status.graphHash` | `check_collisions.assessmentGraphHash` |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `item` | 13 | `bf710e249ff26797f97b95b544c79a746d69d48a4c8d52a98c3d8338e10ab787` | `d884d774fb398650b189203a77eefb7c630b90398b455950b94d56ada4b1e8d3` |

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. treat floor-standing `procedural-item` nodes as first-class furniture, include them in `checkedItems`, and report the `2 m × 2 m` overlap in `check_collisions.collisions` and `verify_scene` as `item_overlap`; or
2. if procedural recipes are intentionally unsupported, list both nodes in `skippedItems` with an explicit reason and return `insufficient_evidence` / a named `unsupportedChecks` entry.

In neither case should the tool report `status: "checked"` with no checked items, no skipped items, and no collision findings.

## Source analysis

At `85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc`:

- [`check-collisions.ts#L233-L235`](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/blob/85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc/packages/mcp/src/tools/check-collisions.ts#L233-L235) skips every node whose `type` is not exactly `item`.
- [`check-collisions.ts#L287-L290`](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/blob/85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc/packages/mcp/src/tools/check-collisions.ts#L287-L290) feeds collision detection with an item-only checked-ID set.
- [`layout-clearance.ts#L143-L151`](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/blob/85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc/packages/core/src/agent-operations/layout-clearance.ts#L143-L151) also skips non-`item` nodes in `collectOccupiedFootprints()`.
- [`layout-clearance.ts#L936-L953`](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/blob/85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc/packages/core/src/agent-operations/layout-clearance.ts#L936-L953) is the `verify_scene` path that reuses this item-only engine.
- [`check-collisions.ts#L299-L305`](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/blob/85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc/packages/mcp/src/tools/check-collisions.ts#L299-L305) returns `"checked"` when both `checkedItems` and `skippedItems` are empty.

Procedural items already have the data needed for this check:

- [`definition.ts#L178-L181`](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/blob/85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc/packages/nodes/src/procedural-item/definition.ts#L178-L181) declares `floorPlaced.footprint` and `floorPlaced.collides: true`.
- [`query.ts#L96-L101`](https://github.com/pascalorg/editor/blob/85d7f4cefae7529402b6a5686b2caf7f3b9a10fc/packages/core/src/procedural-items/query.ts#L96-L101) provides `proceduralFootprint()` from the evaluated recipe bounds and node pose.

`packages/mcp/src/tools/check-collisions.test.ts` contains no procedural/design/recipe test, and a docs/skills search found no documented intentional exclusion. The collision tool was introduced before procedural-item support and was refactored after it without adding support. This appears to be an omission rather than a documented limitation.

## Suggested fix

Use the node registry's `floorPlaced` capability (or `proceduralFootprint()` for `procedural-item` nodes) in `collectOccupiedFootprints()` and in `check_collisions`' evidence loop. Include such nodes in `checkedItems` with their evaluated bounds and an appropriate `source` value. Add regression tests for:

1. `procedural-item` ↔ `procedural-item` exact overlap;
2. `item` ↔ `procedural-item` exact overlap;
3. floor-only and unsupported-attachment skips;
4. status must not be `"checked"` when procedural furniture is present but omitted.

No source changes are included in this report; the reproduction and source checkout were read-only.

title: ci: run static checks, tests and build as parallel jobs
body:
## Why

`quality` runs lint, localization, typecheck, tests, build and the server smoke back to back: 7 to 8.5 min per run, of which typecheck, test and build take about 75 s, 180 s and 110 s. `cli-smoke` (macOS) adds 5 to 8 min on every PR that touches runtime code.

## What changes

- The `quality` steps run as three jobs side by side (`Lint, i18n, typecheck`, `Test`, `Build and smoke`). `quality` stays the required check and passes only when all three succeeded.
- `cli-smoke` runs on a PR only when packaging changed (the CLI, the portable build switch in the editor's Next config, the dependency set). It still runs on `main` after every runtime change, and the release workflow runs the same smoke before publishing. In the last 40 PR runs it failed four times, each time alongside `quality`.

No check is removed; `Packed live viewer` is untouched.

title: [Maintainer] core: reject scheme-relative asset URLs
body:
## What does this PR do? `isAllowedAssetUrl` in `packages/core/src/schema/asset-url.ts` accepted any string starting with `/` as an app-relative path, and that check ran before the https origin allowlist (`PASCAL_ALLOWED_ASSET_ORIGINS`). Browsers resolve `//evil.example/x.png` and `/\evil.example/x.png` against another origin, so these scheme-relative URLs got past both the allowlist and the http-only-on-localhost rule. `loadAssetUrl` then returned them unchanged. Changes: - New exported `isSchemeRelativeUrl(url)`. It normalises the input the way the WHATWG URL parser does: it removes tab, LF and CR anywhere and strips leading C0 control characters and spaces. It then flags input that starts with two slashes or backslashes in any mix, or with a single `\`. - `isAllowedAssetUrl` rejects those inputs before the app-relative branch. A single-slash path such as `/assets/x.png` is still accepted. - `loadAssetUrl` in `packages/core/src/lib/asset-storage.ts` returns `null` for those inputs. Every caller already handles `null`. ## How to test 1. `cd packages/core && bun test src/schema/asset-url.test.ts src/lib/asset-storage.test.ts`. All tests should pass. 2. The new rejected cases are `//evil.example/x.png`, `/\evil.example/x.png`, `\\evil.example/x.png`, `\/evil.example/x.png`, `//169.254.169.254/x`, and variants with a leading space, control characters, or an embedded tab or newline. The accepted cases are `/assets/x.png` and `/assets//x.png`. A separate test checks that `//evil.example/x.png` is rejected while `PASCAL_ALLOWED_ASSET_ORIGINS` is set. 3. Without the source change, 7 of the new tests fail. Each rejected input resolves to a non-app origin under `new URL(input, 'https://app.test')`. `bun run ci` passed locally. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A, non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: editor: named side menu, one side column and a single Plugins entry
body:
## What does this PR do?

Reworks the v2 desktop layout so the 3D view stays the biggest thing on screen and every menu entry says what it is. It comes from Pascal's navigation plan for the hosted editor (items 4, 5, 6 and 14: tool names, finding chats, a clean layout, chat first).

- **Side menu with names.** Entries are grouped under headings (a tab's `section`). **Hide menu** at the top hides the whole menu; a **Menu** button at the start of the view bar brings it back. The choice is remembered. Keyboard shortcuts (B, P, F), Paint following paint mode and the build-tool reset keep working while the menu is hidden.
- **One side column.** A host can give one tab the column beside the menu (`columnTabId`, e.g. a chat), and the editor opens on it. Opening a tool puts its panel in that column instead of over the 3D view; the close button, Escape or picking the column's tab brings the tab back and puts a build tool down, so a click on the 3D view selects instead of drawing. Before, a tool panel next to the chat left the 3D view under half the window; with Build open it now keeps 904 of 1,440 px.
- **One Plugins entry.** Plugins no longer get an entry each. **Plugins** opens a panel listing the project's plugins, plus **Browse plugins** for the directory. An open plugin's panel keeps Plugins lit, and clicking Plugins goes back to the list. The phone's tab bar folds the plugins under Plugins the same way. `pluginsMenuSection` lets the host put the entry under one of its own headings (Pascal puts it under Project, after Capture).
- **`sideMenuFooter`:** host content right after the entries. Pascal uses it for the project's recent chats, in the space the plugin list used to take.
- **The camera frames each project once it has opened** (including the next one opened in the same session), unless a saved view, an applied pose or the person has already moved it. A scanned house tens of metres across used to open on its roof.
- **New strings** in every catalog. es, fr, ja and zh-CN are fuzzy drafts for review.

The v1 layout is unchanged. On a phone, the column's tab stays one of the tabs.

New props: `columnTabId`, `sideMenuFooter`, `pluginsMenuSection` (README updated). New `SidebarTab` fields: `section` and `menuParent` (an entry left out of the menu that lights its parent, used for the plugins).

## How to test

1. In a host with `layoutVersion="v2"`, a `columnTabId` and a few installed plugins, open a project. It opens on the column's tab, and the camera frames the project.
2. Click **Build**. Its panel takes the column's place and the 3D view keeps its width. Press Escape and the column's tab comes back.
3. Click **Plugins**: the project's plugins are listed. Pick one: its panel opens and Plugins stays lit. Click Plugins again for the list; **Browse plugins** opens the directory.
4. Click **Hide menu**. The **Menu** button at the start of the view bar brings the menu back, and a reload keeps the choice.

Ran locally: `bun run check-types` and `bun test src` in `packages/editor` (2,933 pass), and `bun check` (no errors; the same 172 warnings as main, none in these files).

title: viewer: keep room light from leaking out through walls
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes full-height dark vertical stripes on outside wall faces in the daylight look.

The room map grows each room two cells (about 20 cm) past its outline, so wall thickness, window reveals and furniture against a wall count as indoors. That growth ignored the walls themselves. When a room's outline runs along its walls' outside faces (outside faces locked to the line, `justification` a/b), the growth spilled into the open air. An outside wall face looks 18 cm out for its room, so it found the room in some cells and not in others. On walls off the grid axes the spill is a staircase, which drew stripes; on axis-aligned walls a whole face could flip.

Now the map takes the walls' footprints and a room grows into a wall but never out of its far side:

- `RoomSceneInput.walls` carries each wall mesh's level (live and baked scenes).
- `rooms.ts` reads the footprints from the wall meshes (every triangle with an area seen from above).
- `room-map.ts` marks wall cells per tile row and blocks growth from a wall cell into a non-wall cell.

Outlines on a wall's outside face, centre line or inside face all end at the wall. Room edges with no wall grow as before.

Known limits:

- The first room build can run before walls have geometry, so the stripes can show while a scene loads and clear on the settle rebuild.
- Each room rebuild now reads every wall's triangles. Not measured on a large scene.

## How to test

1. Draw a four-wall room turned about 40° off the grid axes, 0.3 m walls, and lock its outside faces to the line (or load a scene whose walls have `justification` set and whose zone outline follows the wall lines).
2. Open it in the viewer with the daylight look, by day, and wait for the scene to settle.
3. Look at the outside wall faces. Before: irregular full-height dark stripes, and a sawtooth along the wall base on adjoining slabs. After: evenly lit faces.
4. Check a window in one of those walls: its reveals are still lit as part of the room.
5. `cd packages/viewer && bun test src/lib/daylight`: the new case `a room never reaches past its walls, wherever its outline runs inside them` passes. It fails when the wall strip is not passed to `dilate`.

Verified on a real 136-wall project in the hosted app's dev server (live scene, midday and 5:05 PM): stripes before, none after. The baked viewer path was not checked in a browser.

Checks run: `bun run check` (no errors), `tsgo --build` for core, viewer and nodes, `bun test src/lib/daylight` (23 pass). The full `packages/viewer` suite had one failure, `GlbScene resolves replace renderers through its sceneNodes` in `plugin-dispatch.test.tsx`; that file passes on its own (7 pass) and does not touch the daylight code.

## Screenshots / screen recording
