title: core: a roof holds the faces of plugin kinds that roof
body:
## What does this PR do?

**For a user:** a plugin's solved roof planes can live under their roof instead of standing on the roof level beside it. The site panel lists them under the roof, not as loose Elements, and selecting, hiding, moving, duplicating or deleting the roof takes them along. Until now `RoofNode.children` accepted segment ids only (`z.array(RoofSegmentNode.shape.id)`, the `rseg_` prefix), so a `roofplane_…` id failed the roof's schema.

**The capability.** A node kind declares that it roofs, meaning its nodes are faces of the roof that holds them, the way segments are its masses:

```ts
capabilities: {
  roofs: {
    outline: (node) => (node as RoofPlaneNode).polygon,                        // [x, z] corners, roof frame
    heightAt: (node, x, z) => roofPlaneHeightAt(node as RoofPlaneNode, x, z),  // top surface over the roof's origin
  },
},
```

The frame is the roof's. A roof standing unturned at its level's origin holds its faces in level metres, which is how the planes already store them, so nothing moves. A roof that is moved or turned takes its faces with it. A face carries its own heights, so a roof of faces stays where it is placed (`support: { kind: 'level' }`, the default).

**What changes:**
- **Hierarchy (core).** `RoofNode.children` accepts any id, including a plugin's own prefix. Which kinds a roof may hold is now checked against the scene, not inferred from the id prefix. The roof schema's `validateRelations` refuses a child that a write adds when its kind is registered and is neither a segment nor a kind that roofs. It runs wherever the store and `apply_patch` reparents validate relations. A child the roof already held stays. A kind this runtime has not registered also passes, because a server or viewer without the plugin cannot judge it. To support this, `validateNodeRelations` now passes the previous graph to validators as a third argument.
- **Rendering (viewer, nodes).** Two fixes in the roof system:
  - It merges only segments into the shell. Before, it cast every child to a segment.
  - It counts only segments when deciding whether a roof is a composite of pieces (shed fascia, wall shells).

  The record a construction reveal checks before re-merging a shell now lists only the roof and its segments. The roof renderer mounts faces through their own renderers in a `roof-faces` group inside the roof's group, which is why selecting, hiding, moving and deleting carry them. The roof keeps `rendersChildren: false`, so items still cannot be surface-hosted on a roof.
- **Readers (core).** `roofFaceShapes(roof, nodes)` returns each face's outline and its lowest and highest points in the frame of the roof's parent. These readers now count faces:
  - the storey a roof covers (`coveredStoreyId` / `roofsOver`): a roof of faces stands at its lowest eave;
  - where a roof bears and the walls under it (`roofWallTop`, the follow). `isRoofElevationInput` is now the single test that both the mounted roof sync and `reconcileDocument` use. It includes the roof's segments and faces; the sync used to miss segments as well;
  - the height of a roof level the seat creates. The seat test itself (`isRoofOnStoreyWalls`) still reads segments only: an outline and heights cannot tell a porch on posts from a roof on walls, so the planes' writer seats them by the roof-level rule;
  - a view's frame (`roofBox`). A host without the plugin cannot read a face's shape, so it frames that roof up to its level's top, as it framed planes standing on the level. A view aimed at that roof also takes in the storey it covers;
  - floor-plate support;
  - the structure presets of level duplication;
  - the alignment footprint;
  - the site plan's roof outline;
  - the level summary, which reports `segmentCount` for segments only and adds `faceCount`.
- **Editor.**
  - The site panel's roof row lists faces after the segments. A roof with faces and no segments falls back to the plain "Roof" label.
  - Duplicating a roof copies its faces. A face that does not parse fails the copy, as a segment does.
  - In the viewer surfaces, a click on a face selects its roof, as a click on a segment does.
  - Tree drops now land before a row id, not at an index into `children`, because faces have no drop row.
  - Roof edit mode marks only segments dirty.
- **Docs.** `node-definitions.md` gets a `capabilities.roofs` section, and the hosting note in `plugin-authoring.md` covers it.

**CI (two commits of their own, `turbo.json` and one test):** since #1256 the Test job runs apart from the build, and it races in three ways. Main fails the same way at fbc28d35 (`Cannot find module '@pascal-app/viewer'`). This branch's runs hit each race in turn:
- `test` waited only for the dependencies' builds, so the core, viewer and mcp suites that import their own package's `dist` raced its build. They now wait for it, as `@pascal-app/nodes#test` already does.
- A build replayed from cache restored `dist` without `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. A dependent's `tsc --build` then rebuilt the referenced package and rewrote its `dist` while other suites read it (`Export named 'viewerPreferenceStorage' not found`). The build info is now a build output.
- Core's `cuttable` scan read the scratch probes that editor's history suite writes and removes under `src/lib/.turbo` (ENOENT). It now skips dot directories.

I can split these into their own PR if you prefer.

**Old scenes (E-003):** there is no migration. Planes standing on a level load where they were (covered by a test). Roofs with only segments are unchanged: the frozen pre-host-children corpus and every roof suite pass.

title: viewer: turn each building's room map to its walls
body:
## What does this PR do?

Follow-up to #1259. That fix cleared the stripes on wall faces, but a building drawn at an angle to the world still showed saw-tooth light along wall bases, sills and terrace edges, and bars on windows and doors.

The cause is the room map itself: it was laid out along the world axes, so a building at 40° crossed its 10 cm cells diagonally and every room edge came out stepped.

- **Each building's room map is turned to its own walls.** The turn is the direction most of the building's room edges run along (folded to a quarter turn, weighted by length). Rooms and wall footprints are rasterized in that frame, lookups rotate the point into it, and the doorway search maps its samples back to the world. The directory of buildings stays on the world axes.
  - Cost per lookup: one 2D rotation, no extra texture reads.
  - A building square to the world keeps the plain frame exactly, so its results do not change.
- **A surface looks 30 cm sideways for its room instead of 18 cm** (still 18 cm up or down). A shutter, door leaf or pane set half-way into a 30 cm wall then looks out past the wall's face instead of into the cells along it.

Measured on the reported project's walls (changes of answer along a line just outside the face; 0 is a straight edge):

| Wall | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| House street wall, 10.5 m | 33–74 | 1 |
| House garden gable, 8 m | 40–97 | 0–2 |
| Garage street wall, 4.2 m | 0–40 | 0 |

The house keeps a step or two because its own walls are about 1° off square.

Known limits:

- Walls at other angles within one building (an angled wing, a curve) still cross the cells in steps.
- Edges become straight, not exact: a strip within a few centimetres of a wall is evenly lit one way or the other, as on a square building.
- The turn can shift slightly as rooms are edited, which re-lays the map. Not checked while drawing.
- With the longer look-ahead, the back of furniture within about 10 cm of a 20 cm outside wall can read partly as outdoors (29% in-room at 5 cm, 86% at 10 cm, by calculation). Against 30 cm walls it stays 100%.

## How to test

1. Open a project whose building is drawn at an angle to the world (walls not parallel to X or Z), in the daylight look.
2. Look at the base of the outside walls, window sills and any terrace or balcony edge. Before: saw-tooth edges. After: straight edges.
3. Look at shutters, door leaves and window frames in those walls. Before: irregular vertical bars. After: evenly lit.
4. Open a project drawn square to the world and compare with `main`: room light, doorway light and window light are unchanged apart from the look-ahead (surfaces within 30 cm of a room boundary switch rooms 12 cm earlier).
5. `cd packages/viewer && bun test src/lib/daylight`: the new case `a building turned off the world axes reads exactly like the same building drawn square` passes. With the turn disabled it fails (1,943 of the sampled points differ).

Verified on a real 136-wall project in the hosted app's dev server (live scene, 5:05 PM): walls, a shuttered window, the entrance door and a sill render clean, with no shader errors. Not checked by me: the lighting test projects, the terrace of that project, the baked viewer path, and frame time (expected unchanged).

Checks run: `bun run check` (no errors), `tsgo --build` for core, viewer and nodes, `bun test src/lib/daylight` (24 pass). The full `packages/viewer` suite has the same single failure as on #1259, `GlbScene resolves replace renderers through its sceneNodes`, which passes when its file runs alone and does not touch this code.

## Screenshots / screen recording

Not added yet.

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core room lookup and GPU shader paths used for all interior daylight; axis-aligned sites should behave as before, but probe offset and per-building turns can shift lighting at boundaries.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Buildings drawn off the world grid no longer get stepped room edges** in daylight: each building’s room-id map is built in a frame aligned to its dominant wall direction, then lookups rotate world XZ into that frame (CPU, GPU index, and doorway walking).
> 
> **`RoomMap`** derives a per-building turn from weighted room polygon edges, rasterizes turned rooms and wall footprints, keeps the building directory on world axes via inverse-transformed cluster boxes, and passes `turn` on tiles plus `dirOrigin` / `turn` uniforms into the shader.
>

title: viewer: sound effects as their own entry, @pascal-app/viewer/sfx
body:
## What does this PR do?

Pascal's sound effects become their own public entry, `@pascal-app/viewer/sfx`, so any viewer can play the interaction and viewer UI sounds without the editor, including viewers with a fully custom UI.

- **Exports:** player (`playSound`, `preloadSounds`, loops, volumes), the `SOUNDS` manifest, `useAudioSettings` (volume and mute), `initInteractionSounds` (core `interaction:sound` → door, window, garage, shutter, cabinet and switch sounds) and `useViewerUiSounds` (hover and select ticks, silent until the user has interacted and during walkthrough).
- **Sound file location:** resolved at play time from `configureViewer({ sfxBaseUrl })`. The default is `https://editor.pascal.app/audios/sfx`, which serves the files cross-origin. The standalone app configures `/audios/sfx`.
- **Editor:** keeps its editing-only cues on the shared player and settings store, so there's one Howler cache and one store. The editor's own copies of the player, the audio store and the UI-sounds hook are removed.
- **Saved settings:** the storage keys are unchanged, so users keep their volume and mute. Importing the entry does no work.
- **Editor exports:** `@pascal-app/editor` still exports `useAudio` and `useViewerUiSounds`, now re-exported from the new entry.
- **Gates:** the render bundle gate covers the new entry. The packed live fixture now plays a sound and checks that the file loads from `sfxBaseUrl`.

## How to test

1. `bun run check:viewer-live`. In dev and preview, with storage available and denied, the scene renders and the fixture's door sound loads `/fixture-sfx/door_open.mp3`. The test installs the packed core, viewer and nodes with no editor or Next.js.
2. `bun run check:render-bundle` ends with "Render and SFX declaration consumer: passed with editor/Next resolution forbidden".
3. `cd packages/viewer && bun test src/sfx` passes 10 tests, and `cd packages/editor && bun test src/lib/sfx-player.test.ts` passes 23.
4. In the editor, menu hover and click sounds, door opening in walkthrough, and the audio settings dialog behave as before. Not verified locally.

title: core: scripted library items place with their script and lead search_assets
body:
## What does this PR do?

Agents can place a library item built from a three.js script and keep it parametric. Until now every catalog entry was a flat GLB asset, so hosts could not hand agents their scripted items, and agents kept placing plain models.

- **`CatalogAsset`**: an `AssetInput` that may carry `script`, the `GeometryScriptSource` it was built from.
- **Placement**: `place_items`, `place_in_room` and `furnish_room` write that script as the item's `source`. `add_object` with `nodeId` and `params` can then resize or rework the placed item.
- **`search_assets`**: lists each scripted item's params (spec plus current value). `rankAssets` puts scripted items first among the hits the query names by name or by category, so a scripted sofa leads a GLB "Sofa". Hits that match only through a tag or elsewhere keep their usual order. The tool description says so.
- **`AssetCatalogSource.bring`** (optional): `readCatalog` calls it with the scripted items a call is about to place. The host copies their artifacts into the scene's project before the sync operation runs. `catalogReads` now also reports `placing`, the ids a call may place.
- **`view_assets` / `paint`**: a scripted item's surfaces come from its manifest's slots (`AssetViewSubject.surfaces`), so its `artifact://` model is never fetched.
- **Design brief**: "item library" and "library item(s)" now count as naming the catalog as a brief's source. In a live chat, "a sofa from the item library" was refused as naming no source, and nothing got furnished.
- **Docs**: `wiki/architecture/agent-surfaces.md` describes the catalog contract.

A list held whole (the built-in catalog) carries no scripts, so standalone MCP behaviour is unchanged.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/core && bun test src/agent-operations/asset-catalog.test.ts src/agent-operations/design-brief.test.ts`. Covers: scripted-first ranking (name and category), `bring` only for placed scripted items, params in `search_assets`, the new source phrases.
2. `bun test src/agent-operations/operations.test.ts`. The new place_items case places a scripted entry with `source.script` set, and with no `script` key on the asset.
3. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/tools/shared-tools.test.ts` runs the same cases through the MCP surface.

Ran locally: 1–3 green (core agent-operations 1567 + 12 + 69 tests, MCP shared tools 785), and `tsgo --noEmit` on core is clean. I also checked end to end against the hosted community app (paired private PR): Architect picked two forged scripted items, placed them, the project received their 8 artifacts, both rendered, and "make the sofa 2.8 m wide with 4 cushions" rebuilt the same node through `add_object` params.

## Screenshots / screen recording

title: core: a typed verify_scene takes only the usage measurements it needs
body:
## What does this PR do?

With the usage checks on (`setSdfChecks(true)`), `verify_scene` took every usage measurement on every call, whatever `type` it asked for. On a large building the circulation measurement (passages, turning circles, pockets) is nearly all of the cost, so a question about skirting or a blocked door paid for it too, and a `run_batch` of several typed checks paid for it once per call.

Two changes in `packages/core`:

1. **A typed question takes only the usage measurements its type needs.** `usageIssues` now lists its measurements with the finding types each gives (`types` option), and the usage check passes the type asked for. A usage type takes its own measurement; any other type takes none; `usage_room` takes the one behind the findings a room entry holds. A misspelt usage type still takes all of them, so its answer names the types there are.
2. **The path solver's heap allocates nothing per pop.** Same comparisons in the same order, so the same paths; it only removes the per-step temporaries.

Measured on a saved six-storey residential scene (1,244 nodes) on an Apple-silicon laptop, usage checks on:

| Call | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full check (no `type`) | 15.7 s | 11.2 s |
| `type` that is not a usage finding (`door_blocked`, `rooms_no_skirting`, `item_overlap`, …) | 14.3–15.3 s | 0.3 s |
| `usage_clash`, `usage_opening_blocked`, `usage_bed_clearance`, `usage_fixture_clearance`, `usage_door_over_stair` | 13.9–15.3 s | 0.3–0.4 s |
| `usage_door_swing` | 14.8 s | 1.4 s |
| `usage_entry_narrow` | 14.4 s | 1.6 s |
| `usage_passage_narrow`, `usage_pocket`, `usage_turning_narrow`, `usage_room` | 14.9–15.3 s | 8.0–8.9 s |

The circulation types still cost seconds: that measurement is where the time goes, and this PR only stops other questions from paying for it.

**Results.** On that scene the full report and the model's reading of it are byte-identical before and after, and so are the findings and their count for each of the 15 types asked. One thing differs: an answer with no findings lists the other types found (`types`), and that list now holds the types of what the question measured. For a type that is not a usage finding it no longer lists usage types.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/core && bun test src/agent-operations/verify-scene-typed.test.ts`: on a small two-room scene whose report holds six usage types beside the ordinary ones, each typed answer equals the findings of that type in the whole report; a room with a type answers the same; a misspelt usage type answers with every type; the report for a non-usage type holds no usage findings.
2. `bun test src/spatial/usage-field src/agent-operations src/agent-tools` (1,806 pass) and, in `packages/mcp`, `bun test src/tools/verify-scene.test.ts src/tools/scene-query.test.ts` (12 pass).
3. To see the timings: load a large multi-storey scene, call `setSdfChecks(true)`, and time `AGENT_OPERATIONS.verify_scene(nodes, { type: 'door_blocked' }, context)` against `{}`.

## Screenshots / screen recording

- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which usage measurements run for typed queries and how empty-result metadata lists types; heap refactor must preserve path results but is covered by existing usage-field tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> When `verify_scene` is called with a **`type`**, usage checks no longer run the full circulation and fixture suite on every request. **`usageIssues`** maps each measurement to the finding types it produces and runs only matching measurements; non-usage types skip usage work entirely, **`usage_room`** still folds to pocket/turning types, and unknown usage types fall back to measuring everything (so answers can list valid types).

title: mcp: a host can pause between the calls of a run_batch
body:
## What does this PR do?

`run_batch` is one synchronous operation: its calls run back to back and nothing else on the server runs until the last one returns. A batch of several expensive calls (whole-scene checks on a large building) holds the event loop for its whole length, so a host's timers and I/O wait for it. A host that keeps a lease alive with a timer loses it during such a batch.

This adds an opt-in pause after each call:

- **core:** the batch is a sequence that stops after each call (`createBatchSteps`, exported as `RUN_BATCH_STEPS`). `AGENT_OPERATIONS.run_batch` runs it through in one go, as before, so the chat and every existing caller are unchanged.
- **mcp:** `createPascalMcpServer({ betweenBatchCalls })`. When a host gives it, the batch tool runs one call at a time, each in the scene's scope, and awaits the host after each.

**Why opt-in.** Today a batch plans on the scene and applies its changes in one uninterrupted stretch, so no other call can reach the scene in between. A server that serves concurrent calls on one bridge (the standalone server) relies on that. With a pause, the batch is planned on the scene as its first call found it and applied after its last, so only a host that builds a scene of its own for each request should give the hook. Without it nothing changes.

**The batch's own behaviour is the same:** calls in order, each on the scene the calls before it left; `stop` applies nothing when a call is refused, `skip` reports it and applies the rest; same result shape; one history step.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/tools/run-batch-pause.test.ts`: with a pausing host, the pause runs after each of four calls and sees the scene as the batch found it; the batch then lands whole and one undo removes it. Four batches (plain, stopped by a refusal, past a refusal with `skip`, an unknown tool) answer the same with and without the pause.
2. `bun test src/tools` in `packages/mcp` (1,290 pass) and `bun test src/agent-operations` in `packages/core` (1,558 pass).

title: mcp: verify_scene runs in steps, so a host can pause inside a long check
body:
## What does this PR do?

`verify_scene` runs every check in one synchronous stretch. On a large building with the usage checks on that stretch is long: 16 to 18 seconds on an Apple-silicon Mac for a six-storey building of about 1,300 nodes, several times that on a small server. Nothing else on the server runs meanwhile, so a host's timers and I/O wait for it. `author_scene` ends with the same checks, so every conversion of such a building ends with that stretch, and a host that has to do something on a schedule while a call runs (renew a lock, answer a heartbeat) cannot.

#1271 let a host pause between the calls of a `run_batch`. This PR makes the checks themselves stop, so the pause reaches inside one long call:

- **`verify_scene` is written in steps** (`verifySceneSteps`): it stops after each registered check, and the circulation measurement, which is most of the time, stops after each floor (`measureUsageSteps`, `usageIssueSteps`). `verifyScene` runs the same steps through in one go, so its answer is unchanged.
- **A batch stops inside a `verify_scene` call too**, as well as after each call.
- **`author_scene`'s closing checks pause** on a host that gives the hook.
- **A registered check can answer in steps** by returning a generator (`SceneCheck.run`); one that returns its findings works as before.

Measured through a host that pauses, on that building: the longest uninterrupted stretch of an `author_scene` call goes from 18.5 s to 2.8 s. The call takes the same time in total (22 s).

**Renamed, since the hook is no longer about batches only:** `betweenBatchCalls` is now `betweenSteps` (`createPascalMcpServer`, `registerTools`). `RUN_BATCH_STEPS` is now `AGENT_OPERATION_STEPS.run_batch`, beside `AGENT_OPERATION_STEPS.verify_scene`, and `createBatchOperation` is gone (`AGENT_OPERATIONS.run_batch` runs the steps through). The hook was added in #1271; a host that passes the old name has to rename it.

**Is it safe?** The same contract as #1271. Without the hook nothing changes: every call is uninterrupted. With it, other work of the host runs between the steps, so only a host whose scene no other call can reach meanwhile (a bridge of its own for each request) should give it. `verify_scene` reads the scene it was handed at its start. In `author_scene` the design is already written when the checks run, so on a host that serves concurrent calls on one bridge another call could change the scene before the report is made; that host leaves the hook out, as before.

## How to test

1. `bun test` in `packages/core` (7,186 pass) and in `packages/mcp` (1,531 pass).
2. `packages/core/src/agent-operations/verify-scene-typed.test.ts`: taken a step at a time, `verify_scene` stops more than five times on a two-room scene and answers the report it answers in one go.
3. `packages/mcp/src/tools/paused-steps.test.ts` (was `run-batch-pause.test.ts`): on a host with the hook, `verify_scene` pauses between its checks, a batch pauses inside a `verify_scene` call as well as after each call, and both answer what they answer without the hook.
4. `packages/mcp/src/tools/author-scene.test.ts`: on a host with the hook, `author_scene` pauses during its closing checks and reports the same gate.

Ran locally: both suites above, `biome check` on both packages, `check-types` for the eleven affected packages. `apps/editor`'s `check-types` did not run clean in my checkout for unrelated missing modules (`react-scan`, `geist`), so CI is the check for it.

> **Overview**

title: Walls: run the T-junction repair on demand (export only), not on every rebuild
body:
### Problem or motivation

**Context.** #1208 added `repairWallTJunctions` (`packages/viewer/src/systems/wall/wall-t-junctions.ts`), called from `finishWallFaces` in `wall-system.tsx`. It closes the T-junctions that CSG cuts, finish-band splits and terrain-fill seams leave on wall faces. As the PR says, they look closed at full float precision and only crack open into dotted light leaks once a GLB bake quantizes positions. The repair itself is sound: it never invents a vertex and keeps each piece's material group.

**Problem.** The repair runs on every wall build, including every live rebuild while drawing and editing. It is a sizeable share of the build, and nothing on screen needs it: the live renderer draws unquantized positions.

**Measurements** (Apple M-series, Bun 1.4.4, three r187, machine shared with other jobs, so medians of alternated runs):

| What | Repair on every build | Repair deferred | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generatePlacedWall`, 60 walls with a door and a window (one third curved, half the doors arched), 12 alternated pairs | median 372 ms | median 284 ms | the repair is about 24% of the build |
| Same benchmark, earlier session | 271–309 ms | 212–239 ms | 20–25% |
| One-off repair at export time, same 60 walls (repair, normals, planar UVs) | — | median 122 ms | about 2 ms per wall, paid once per export |

Browser frame time for «send wall» (rAF, steady-state p50 in ms, editor dev build, our fork before the 1.0.7 merge versus after the merge with the deferred repair; medians of three alternated pairs, machine load 10–13). The numbers swing up to 3–5× between runs of the same build, so only large repeated differences mean something:

| Scene / view | Before the 1.0.7 merge | After, repair deferred |
|---|---|---|
| demo / plan | 134 | 80 |
| large (500 walls) / plan | 382 | 243 |
| large / plan + 3D side by side | 1403 | 1382 |
| demo / plan + 3D side by side | 114 | 154 |

With the repair on every rebuild (an earlier session) the same «send wall» was 20–26% slower than before the merge in demo/plan and large/side-by-side. The side-by-side 3D view is still slower than before the merge for reasons unrelated to this proposal (in our fork, mostly the retired `solid` look).

### Proposed solution

Let callers choose when the repair runs. A minimal version of what we ship in our fork:

```ts
/** `repaired` (default) removes the T-junctions on every build. `deferred` leaves them and marks the geometry. */
export type WallTJunctionMode = 'repaired' | 'deferred'

export function generateExtrudedWall(
  /* …existing parameters… */
  tJunctions: WallTJunctionMode = 'repaired',
): THREE.BufferGeometry
```

- `finishWallFaces` classifies the faces as today; with `deferred` it skips `repairWallTJunctions` and sets `geometry.userData.wallTJunctions = 'deferred'`.
- The live `WallSystem` (`updateWallGeometry`, and the collision mesh) passes `deferred`.
- A new `repairDeferredWallTJunctions(mesh)` runs the same repair on a marked mesh (position and groups, then the same face-reason remap, normals and level-relative planar UVs as the live build), and drops the mark.
- Export preparation (`startSceneExportPreparation` in `packages/editor/src/lib/glb-export.ts`, shared by GLB, USDZ, STL and 3MF) calls it on every cloned wall mesh, so every export is still crack-free. The live mesh is not touched: export works on its own clone.
- Every other caller keeps today's behaviour, because the default is `repaired`. The golden hashes and the existing T-junction tests are unchanged.

A test we added builds a T of two walls (one with a window) through `runWallBuildFrame`, exports it with `prepareSceneForExport`, writes a GLB with `GLTFExporter` and reads it back with `GLTFLoader`. The live mesh keeps its T-junctions, and the exported GLB has none (107 without the export hook, 0 with it). Area, UVs, normals and the per-triangle `wallSurfaceAssignments` are kept.

### Alternatives considered

A module-level switch (`setWallTJunctionRepair('export-only')`) would have the same effect, but an explicit parameter keeps the default visible to every caller.

### Additional context

**Related small fix (already in our fork).** Welding at `1e-6` m can merge two dense vertices of an arched or curved cut, which leaves a zero-area triangle. The section readers (`readWallSurfaceMesh`) reject it, so those walls dropped out of sections. In `emit`, a triangle without edge points that is degenerate after welding is now skipped (`isDegenerate`, exact cross product). Five hashes in `wall-finish-plain-golden.json` change; volume, bounds and per-material area do not.

We are happy to open a PR with both changes if that helps.

Reporter: Pietro Ditroia (Arkimensor).

title: cli: pascal viewer deploy uploads a static build to Pascal hosting
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `pascal viewer deploy <dir> --viewer <id> [--dry-run] [--json]` to the CLI. It deploys a static viewer build to Pascal viewer hosting (`https://<slug>.pascal-viewer.app`):

- Scans the build directory and checks it against the hosting rules before anything uploads: root `index.html`, 2,000 files, 100 MiB total, 25 MiB per file, allowed extensions, canonical paths. Hidden entries are skipped (except a top-level `.well-known/`); symlinks are refused. Up to 10 offending files are listed in one error.
- Creates the deployment, uploads each file to its signed URL (8 at a time, with a per-file deadline that scales with size and is capped by the 15-minute upload window), then activates it.
- `--dry-run` runs only the local checks: no API key, no network.
- `--json` prints one object; progress goes to stderr on a TTY only.
- `PASCAL_API_KEY` is read the same way as `pascal architect` and never stored. It is sent only to `editor.pascal.app`; upload requests carry only the headers the API returned, and every request refuses redirects.
- Exit codes follow the architect commands: `2` invalid usage, `75` temporarily unavailable or rate limited.

The viewer itself is registered in Pascal under Settings → Viewers → Host on Pascal; the CLI does not create viewers.

## How to test

1. `cd packages/cli && bun test src` → 258 pass.
2. `bun run check-types && bun run build`.
3. Build any static site with an `index.html` (for example `listing/` from `pascalorg/viewer-templates`), then `node dist/bin/pascal.js viewer deploy <its dist> --viewer viewer_Abc123DEF456ghi7 --dry-run` → `Checked 98 files (6.9 MiB). Ready to deploy to viewer_Abc123DEF456ghi7.`
4. `node dist/bin/pascal.js viewer --help` prints the command help.
5. With a hosted viewer and a key that manages its workspace: `PASCAL_API_KEY=… node dist/bin/pascal.js viewer deploy <dist> --viewer <id>` → the build is live at the viewer's address.

Ran 1–4 locally. The upload path was run under Node 26 against a local `node:http` stand-in for the API and storage (exact headers and bytes, no `Authorization` on uploads, an 8 MiB file over a 200 KiB/s link succeeds). Step 5 against production hosting has not been run yet.

title: nodes: a column built from a script settles, so a scene with one exports
body:
A scene with a column built from a script never becomes ready: the column stays in the scene's dirty set for good. Anything that waits for the scene to settle then fails or times out, the 3D export first: it refuses the scene as unsettled and names the column. A column without a script is unaffected.

## Cause

A column has no system of its own. Its dirty mark is consumed once `columnBatchable.settled` holds of the node's registered group, which for a scripted column means `itemModelSettled` on that group.

`ScriptedOpeningModel` set that flag on `ref.current.parent`, on the assumption that its parent is the node's group. The column renderer now has a wrapper group (`column-body`) between the two, so the flag landed on the wrapper and the node's group never got it.

## Fix

The column renderer passes its own group to the scripted model (`host`), and the model sets the flag there. No more reaching for a parent: the group is named by the renderer that owns it.

## Other kinds

Only windows, doors and columns render through `ScriptedOpeningModel`. A window's and a door's system reads the flag on the model's own group, which is a direct child of the node's mesh (`settleScriptedOpening`), so they were never affected. An item sets the flag on its own registered group.

## Test

`column/scripted-settle.test.tsx` mounts the real level, column renderers and frame systems with a scripted column and a parametric one beside it, marks both dirty and runs ten frames: no node is left dirty. On `main` the scripted column stays dirty.

## Not verified

The export itself was not run on a scene with a scripted column: this was checked through the dirty set it waits on, in the test renderer, not in a WebGPU page.

title: core: viewer labels with placeholders format in production
body:
## What does this PR do?

Viewer labels that contain a placeholder or a select now render formatted in production builds, with no host setup.

A site that renders only `@pascal-app/viewer` never loads the editor's English catalog, and Lingui compiles message strings at runtime only outside production. Every such label therefore showed its raw source: the selection callout button read `{state, select, open {Open} closed {Closed} on {On} other {Off}}`, tooltips read `Walkthrough: {state}`, `Levels: {mode}`, `Drone: {state}`, and the level list read `Floor {number}`.

- Core now loads a generated fallback, `packages/core/src/i18n/english-formatting-fallback.ts`. It holds only the English entries used by core, viewer and nodes whose compiled form differs from the source text: 120 entries, 15 KB raw, 4 KB gzip.
- Plain labels are not in it; they already render from the `message` at the call site.
- `i18n:extract` / `i18n:compile` write the file and `i18n:check` fails when it drifts.
- The editor's catalogs and their generation are unchanged; the editor still registers its full English catalog over the fallback.
- The viewer render bundle grows by 13,495 bytes (7,225,958 → 7,239,453); the viewer UI entry is unchanged.

## How to test

1. `bun test packages/core/src/i18n/production.test.ts scripts/i18n.test.ts` passes (12 tests). The production test runs a fresh process with `NODE_ENV=production`, no provider and no catalog registration, and expects `Closed`, `Walkthrough: On`, `Floor 2`, `Hanger 3 support` and the plain `Top view`.
2. `bun run i18n:check` reports the catalogs in sync.
3. In a production build of a viewer-only host, select a door: the callout button reads "Closed" or "Open", and the walkthrough button tooltip reads "Walkthrough: Off".

## What does this PR do? Brings @philpitus's editor layout work from #1258 into an in-repo branch so CI runs without the fork approval step. Phil's 16 commits are merged unchanged with his authorship. All credit for the layout goes to him; see #1258 for the full design discussion. From #1258 (v2 desktop layout): - The side menu shows every tool by name, grouped under section headings, with a host footer (`sideMenuFooter`) and a Hide menu / Menu toggle. - One side column: the host's column tab (`columnTabId`, e.g. a chat) shows beside the menu, an opened tool panel takes its place, and closing the tool (X or Escape) brings the tab back. The editor opens on that tab once per project. - A single Plugins entry (`pluginsMenuSection` picks its heading) opens a panel listing the project's plugins plus **Browse plugins**. On a phone, plugins also leave the tab bar. - Opening a project frames what it holds (buildings and scans), or the site's saved view, then yields to any camera move or command. On top of Phil's work, this branch: - **Resolves the merge conflict** in `editor/index.tsx` by keeping main's `@pascal-app/viewer` imports and adding `PLUGINS_MANAGER_PANEL_ID`. - **i18n:** ran `bun run i18n:extract`. The new es/fr/ja/zh-CN drafts get their `Source-Hash` and stay `fuzzy` with `Review: required`. Catalogs are back in sync. - **Bugbot fix: closing the tool column disarms any tool.** Previously only `build` mode was reset, so Paint's brush or the site editor stayed armed with its panel gone. Any mode other than select now returns to select. - **Bugbot fix: the hidden chat column releases focus.** It is now `inert` while a tool takes its place, and it drops focus as it hides. Before, typing could go into the hidden composer and Escape never closed the tool panel. - **`showSidebarPanel` / `openSidebarPanel` with the column's tab bring the chat back.** Previously they did nothing while a tool panel was open, and the chat stayed hidden behind it. That behavior dated from before the chat and tool shared a column. They still never reopen a closed tool panel. - **Narrow desktops:** the chat and tool columns are capped at 40% of the window. Next to the new 176px menu, a persisted 600px chat used to leave the stage a sliver just above the phone breakpoint. - **Only real plugin panels fold under Plugins.** Folding also requires a `pluginId` now, so a host panel whose heading happens to read "Plugins" keeps its own entry. - **The opening frame leaves hidden objects out.** `Box3.expandByObject` also walks invisible objects, so a hidden building used to widen the frame. - **Phone to desktop:** a project opened on a phone keeps its tab and tool when the window later widens past the desktop breakpoint. If drei rebuilds the camera controls during the opening, the opening frame is re-applied instead. - **Walking or previewing as a project opens settles the opening.** Before, leaving first person or preview later started the follow and pulled the camera away. ## How to test 1. With a host that passes `columnTabId` (the standalone app doesn't; to try it locally, add a tab and pass `columnTabId`), the chat shows beside the menu. Pick Build: its panel replaces the chat. Open Paint, then close the panel. The brush is put down, and a click on the 3D view selects. 5. Click **Plugins**: the panel lists the project's plugins and **Browse plugins**. title: [Maintainer] Saved camera views should restore projection and lens, not just position and target
body:
Follow-up from #1279 (review threads there).

When a project opens on a saved camera view, and when you use the existing "view saved camera" action, only the camera's position and target are applied. The saved projection (perspective vs orthographic) and lens (field of view / zoom) are ignored, so a view saved in orthographic or with a custom lens reopens looking different from how it was saved.

This was left out of #1279 on purpose, because both paths should change together.

**Scope**
- Apply the saved projection and lens wherever a saved view is restored: the opening camera in `custom-camera-controls.tsx` and the view-saved-camera action.
- Keep older saved views without these fields working (fall back to the current behavior).
- Add a test for a perspective view and an orthographic view round-tripping.

**Done when** a view saved in orthographic with a custom zoom reopens identically, on project open and from the views bar.

title: [Bugs] Clear scene loader after viewer readiness fallback
body:
## What does this PR do? After a reload, the full-pane scene loader (`data-scene-loading`, `absolute inset-0 z-50`) could stay up and keep taking pointer events, even after `[editor] viewer scene readiness timed out; showing editor shell anyway` was logged. There were three causes: - **The fallback was revoked.** The viewer's `SceneReadyTracker` lives inside the R3F ``, so it only mounts once the async GPU renderer resolves. Under software WebGL on a reload, that can happen after the 8 s fallback. On mount the tracker reports `false`, which set `isViewerSceneReady` back to false and put the overlay back. It stayed up until the tracker settled or the timer ran out again. - **The fallback only reset one input.** It set `isViewerSceneReady` and nothing else, so `isLoading`, `isSceneLoading` or `!hasLoadedInitialScene` could still keep `showLoader` true. - **The fallback didn't always start.** Its timer only ran once the scene data had loaded. A host `isLoading` that never cleared, or a load that never finished (for example one restarted repeatedly when `onLoad` changes identity), never started it. The fix: - A new `useSceneLoader` hook (`packages/editor/src/hooks/use-scene-loader.ts`) now decides whether the loader shows: - A fallback timer runs whenever the loader is up for any reason except a load error: 8 s while waiting on viewer readiness, 20 s while scene data is still loading. The load-error screen and its retry stay as they are. - Once the fallback fires for a load, the loader stays down for that load, even if the viewer later reports `false`. The overlay is unmounted, so it no longer intercepts pointer events. - Each load start bumps a load generation, so a project switch or a retry shows the loader again. - The post-load camera framing (`camera-controls:fit-scene`) now runs once the loader comes down. It used to depend on `isViewerSceneReady`, so it still runs after a fallback, as it did before. ## How to test 1. `bun test src/hooks/use-scene-loader.test.tsx` in `packages/editor`. The tests cover: - the loader clearing on normal ready - the loader clearing when readiness times out, and a later "not ready" not bringing it back - the loader clearing when `isSceneLoading` / `hasLoadedInitialScene` stay stuck - the loader clearing when a host `isLoading` stays stuck - a restarting stuck load keeping a single fallback timer - a new load showing the loader again - a load error keeping its screen up 2. In a browser with software WebGL (or a throttled GPU), open a project and reload. The overlay should come down within the fallback window and not return, and the canvas should accept clicks. Ran locally: - `bun test src` in `packages/editor`: 2757 pass, 0 fail - `turbo run check-types --filter=@pascal-app/editor`: passes - `bun run check`: no findings in the changed files ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change (the loader only comes down when it was previously stuck). ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Scoped to editor loading UI and camera framing timing; behavior is covered by new hook tests and does not change persistence or scene graph loading. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 20866780acfe699cf41f4057a54a05c1a8fad985. title: [Bugs] Expose scene data readiness separately from loading overlay
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to #1281. That change correctly takes the full-pane loader (`[data-scene-loading]`) down after the readiness fallback (about 20s), even if the editor's own scene data load is still in flight. During that window the scene is read-only and autosave is paused, so edits made right after the overlay clears are refused. In private-editor Browser smoke, `undo-redo-graph` failed with "the closed room never persisted four walls and a derived ceiling" right after the log `scene data loading timed out`. - The #1281 fallback is unchanged: the overlay still never blocks pointer events indefinitely. - New stable DOM signal, kept independent of the overlay. While the editor is mounted, `document.documentElement` carries `data-scene-data`: - `loading`: the editor's own `onLoad` (or local load) is in flight, nothing has loaded yet, or a new `onLoad` was received. That last case applies from the render that receives it, so a project switch never leaves a stale `ready`. The scene is read-only and autosave is paused. - `ready`: the load completed. The read-only lease is released and autosave has resumed, so the scene is editable. - `failed`: the load failed. The scene stays read-only behind the error/retry surface. A retry goes back to `loading`. - The attribute is written in a layout effect and removed when the editor unmounts. A host `isLoading` does not hold it, because it doesn't lock the scene. The fallback timer never changes it. - It goes on the document root because the v2 layout renders a fragment, so the editor has no single root element. - If the fallback took the loader down while data is still `loading`, the viewer area shows a small non-blocking `role="status"` pill ("Still loading the project. Editing is paused until it finishes.") with `pointer-events-none`. - `useSceneLoader` now takes `isHostLoading` and `isSceneDataLoading` separately and returns `{ showLoader, sceneData }`. Specs should wait on `html[data-scene-data="ready"]` rather than on `[data-scene-loading]` going away. ## How to test 1. `bun test packages/editor/src/hooks/use-scene-loader.test.tsx`: covers a normal load (`loading` → `ready`, removed on unmount), the fallback firing while data is still loading (loader down, attribute still `loading`, then `ready` once data arrives), a host `isLoading` not holding the state, and a load failure (`failed`, then `loading` → `ready` on retry). 2. In the app, delay the host `onLoad` past 20s. The loader clears, the "Still loading the project" pill shows, and `` has `data-scene-data="loading"`. When the load resolves, the pill disappears and the attribute becomes `ready`. Ran locally: `bun run check` (no errors, only existing warnings), `bun run check-types`, `bun run i18n:check`, and `bun test src` in `packages/editor` (2761 pass). ## Screenshots / screen recording Not added yet. ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: @pascal-app/ifc-converter: published ESM uses extensionless relative imports, failing in Node with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
body:
### What happened?

`@pascal-app/ifc-converter` is published as ESM (`"type": "module"`) and documents Node support in `packages/ifc-converter/README.md` (`"No DOM, no React"` and `Node callers can pass { wasmPath: '/absolute/path/to/web-ifc/' } in ConversionOptions`), but its emitted `dist/*.js` and `dist/*.d.ts` files keep extensionless relative specifiers (`from './beam-geometry'`, `from './export/guid'`, etc.).

Loading either `@pascal-app/ifc-converter` or `@pascal-app/ifc-converter/export` in Node fails immediately with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (and TypeScript projects using `moduleResolution: "nodenext"` without `skipLibCheck` fail with `TS2835` on `dist/*.d.ts`). `@pascal-app/core` loads fine in the same install because `core`, `geometry-script`, `nodes`, and `mcp` run `scripts/fix-node-esm-imports.ts` after `tsc --build`, whereas `packages/ifc-converter` still runs plain `tsc --build`.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"type":"module"}' > package.json
npm install @pascal-app/ifc-converter@1.1.4
node --input-type=module -e 'await import("@pascal-app/core"); await import("@pascal-app/ifc-converter");'
node --input-type=module -e 'await import("@pascal-app/ifc-converter/export");'
```

Actual output:

```text
node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:241
    throw new ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND(
          ^

Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '/path/to/repro/node_modules/@pascal-app/ifc-converter/dist/beam-geometry' imported from /path/to/repro/node_modules/@pascal-app/ifc-converter/dist/index.js
    at finalizeResolution (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:241:11)
    at moduleResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:846:10)
    at defaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:973:11)
    at #cachedDefaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:708:20)
    at #resolveAndMaybeBlockOnLoaderThread (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:728:38)
    at ModuleLoader.resolveSync (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:766:56)
    at #resolve (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:690:17)
    at ModuleLoader.getOrCreateModuleJob (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:610:35)
    at ModuleJob.syncLink (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:277:33)
    at ModuleJob.link (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:389:17) {
  code: 'ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND',
  url: 'file:///path/to/repro/node_modules/@pascal-app/ifc-converter/dist/beam-geometry'
}

Node.js v26.13.0
```

`await import("@pascal-app/ifc-converter/export")` fails the same way on `/path/to/repro/node_modules/@pascal-app/ifc-converter/dist/export/guid` imported from `dist/export/index.js`.

### Expected behavior

Both `@pascal-app/ifc-converter` and `@pascal-app/ifc-converter/export` load cleanly under Node.js (for example by running `bun ../../scripts/fix-node-esm-imports.ts dist` in `packages/ifc-converter`'s `build` script and adding a `smoke:node` check like `@pascal-app/core`).

### Browser & OS

Node.js v26.13.0, Linux x64 (no browser involved)

### Screenshots or screen recordings

N/A (Node CLI reproduction)

### Additional context

Reproduced on `@pascal-app/ifc-converter@1.1.4` (npm latest) and `main` (`559c0d161`). Related to #861, which wired `scripts/fix-node-esm-imports.ts` into `core` and `mcp`. Running `bun ../../scripts/fix-node-esm-imports.ts dist` on `packages/ifc-converter` makes both `./dist/index.js` and `./dist/export/index.js` import and run cleanly in Node v26.13.0.

title: viewer: light open rooms as outdoors, fix open-plan seams and T-junction wall faces
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes several daylight lighting artifacts and one wall-material bug that looked like a lighting problem:

- **Open rooms lit as outdoors.** Porches, decks, patios and rooms left open on a side (a wall switched off, a floor edge with no wall) are now lit as outdoor space, not as sealed rooms with a virtual ceiling lamp. Before, that lamp's light spilled out through the open side onto the ground. The new `isOpenAirRoom` check in core reads a room's unshared boundary separators. It ignores the wall-detection kernel's `enclosureStatus: 'enclosed'`, which is stamped on every room whose boundary loop closes, open sides included.
- **Open-plan rooms lit as one space.** `openPlanRoomGroups` groups indoor rooms joined by an open side. The daylight system pools their lamps and daylight and skips the opening portal between group members. That portal was drawing a diagonal seam across the threshold. GLB export stamps `open` and `group` on zones to match.
- **Wall faces at T-junctions.** `buildTaggedWallBoundaryEdges` assumed the junction at a wall's start adds one point to the footprint polygon. A T-junction's closing path can add two, which pushed the front-face tag onto the start cap. The face toward the room then rendered with the core material (a yellow strip in the colored look). Core now exports `getWallJunctionClosing`, which the footprint builder and the face tagger both use.
- **Add to rooms order.** The shelf moves from the top of the "Add to rooms" palette to after the kitchen items.

## How to test

1. Draw two rooms side by side so a small room sits against a larger one's wall (T-junctions at both ends of the partition). With textures on, the wall faces toward each room show their interior finish, with no yellow/core strip on one side.
2. Draw a room, switch off one or more of its walls, and keep its ceiling on. In daylight and at night it is lit as outdoors, with no glow spilling onto the ground outside the open side.
3. Make two rooms joined by an open side (no wall between them). They light evenly, with no diagonal seam across the opening.
4. Open "Add to rooms": the shelf now comes after the kitchen items, not first.

Automated: `bun test` for `packages/core/src/lib/outdoor-room.test.ts` and the core wall tests (281 pass) and for the viewer wall tests (182 pass, including the new `wall-junction-faces.test.ts`, which fails without the fix). Turbo build of core, viewer and editor passes. Biome is clean on the changed files.

Steps 2 and 3 were checked live in the local editor. The T-junction wall fix (step 1) is covered by the regression test but was not checked visually.

title: viewer: section cut, X-ray, touch walkthrough and host hooks for custom viewers
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds what a read-only viewer needs to offer a guided presentation of a project (a section cut, an X-ray by family, walking on a phone, its own camera feel and hover behaviour), on both the live scene and a baked GLB. It is built for a new `showcase` template in pascalorg/viewer-templates. Every new option is off or at today's value by default.

**New presentation state (`@pascal-app/viewer`)**

- **Section cut**: `useViewer` gains transient `sectionEnabled`, `sectionAxis`, `sectionPosition` (world metres), `sectionFlipped` and `sectionShadows`. One world plane clips the model on X, Y or Z. Picking skips removed geometry, room highlights and labels follow the cut, and the site ground and horizon are never cut. With `sectionShadows: 'full'` (the default) the removed part still casts its shadows, so the opened rooms keep the building's lighting and moving the plane re-renders no shadows; `'cut'` clips casters too. `sectionBounds()` gives a host the unclipped extent for a slider. Cut faces are open (no caps).
- **X-ray by family**: `useViewer.xrayFamily` shows one family of parts and hides the rest. Kinds declare their family through `extensions['pascal:viewer']`; `sceneFamilies(graph)` lists the families a scene has and `VIEWER_FAMILIES` gives the order. A part whose kind has no loaded definition is `other`.
- **Time of day**: a fifth `TimeOfDay` preset, `dawn` (golden's elevation on the rising side); a low rising sun now reads "Dawn" instead of "Golden hour". `transitionTimeOfDay(target, options)` exposes the sky control's clock tween to hosts, and a target can be a preset or a sun elevation (`{ elevation, side }`); `timeTargetMinutes` resolves one without animating. `useViewer.daylightSite` lets a host that renders a bake give the sun the project's north rotation.

**Host hooks**

- `ViewerCameraControls` (`@pascal-app/viewer/ui`) takes `mouseButtons`, `touches`, `limits`, `smoothTime` and `tap`. With `tap` given, a drag never selects and a tap does, on live and baked scenes.
- `GlbScene` takes `outlineSync` (a host can own the outliner) and `renderCallout`, and `GlbPickEvent` carries the world hit point, normal, object and pointer type. `InteractiveSystem` takes `renderCallout`. The section and X-ray hit filters are exported for custom picking.
- **Walkthrough**: `useViewer.walkthroughInputMode` and a shared input channel feed both walkthrough controllers by touch; `/ui` gains `WalkthroughTouchControls`. Both controllers take `speeds` and `seeDistance`, and the first-person HUD state reports an interactable that is seen but out of reach.

**`@pascal-app/core`**

- `roomCounts(graph)`: rooms, inferred bedrooms and modelled area, using the same rule as the viewer's room list. Bedroom names are recognised in eight more languages; every name that classified before keeps its class.

**Fixes to existing behaviour**

- The walkthrough spawn marker no longer renders in read-only viewers on the live path (the baked path already hid it).
- On a baked scene, a door stays the interact target after it opens, so `E` can close it from the same spot.
- Room lighting is built for a scene that opens with its levels exploded. Before, interiors stayed dark at night and had no window light until the levels were stacked once.

With every new field at its default, the scene hierarchy, room list, name classification and per-frame work are the same as on `main`; differential tests against `main`'s implementations cover this.

## How to test

1. `bun test src` in `packages/core`, `packages/viewer` and `packages/nodes`.
2. `bun scripts/check-render-bundle.ts`: the render, walkthrough, SFX and UI entries still build with the editor and Next forbidden.
3. Open a project in the editor: the scene, room list and labels are unchanged; the time-of-day panel shows five presets on one row; the spawn marker is visible and movable.
4. On a viewer page, with the store from `@pascal-app/viewer`: `useViewer.getState().setSectionEnabled(true)` cuts the model at Y = 0; move it with `setSectionPosition(1.2)`, switch axis with `setSectionAxis('x')`. `setXrayFamily('walls')` leaves only walls over the ground; `setXrayFamily(null)` restores everything.
5. Enter walkthrough on a baked scene, press `E` on a door, then `E` again: it closes.

Verified outside the unit suites: the editor, the hosted viewer and bake capture were compared side by side with `main` on one project before the host hooks, the shadow option, the walkthrough options and the exploded-open lighting fix were added (same room list, same selections over 228 test clicks, identical exported GLB contents); those later additions were exercised only through the template. The features themselves were exercised on the GPU through the template on live and baked projects, including frame rate with the cut on and off.

Not verified: touch walking on a physical phone (tested with emulated touch points), and the five-card time-of-day row in the translated locales.

## Screenshots / screen recording

- [x] I've tested this locally with `bun dev`
- [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify)
- [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable)
- [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

> **Medium Risk**
> Large cross-package changes to rendering, batching, and room classification, but new viewer state defaults off and classification is regression-tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends **`@pascal-app/viewer`** for guided presentation on live and baked scenes: **section cut** state and clipping (with optional shadow modes and cut-aware picking), **X-ray by family** via `useViewer.xrayFamily` and `LiveFamilyVisibility`, plus **touch walkthrough** (`walkthroughInputMode`, shared input channel, `WalkthroughTouchControls`) and **solar controls** (dawn preset, `transitionTimeOfDay` / `timeTargetMinutes`, `daylightSite` override).

Site ground/horizon use **`SiteSurfaceScope`**, with helpers like `temporarilyHideSiteSurfaces` for thumbnail baking.
> 
> **`roomCounts` / `isRoomZone`** in core summarize visible rooms, bedrooms, and unioned indoor area (aligned with the viewer room list). **`roomUseOfName`** adds multilingual bedroom nouns and annex handling while preserving prior English/French classifications.
>
