title: [For discussion] Terrain: shape the ground, seat a house, terraces, a hillside, the view under a slope
body:
**Draft, for discussion, not for merge.** This is the lab's whole terrain work, cut onto `main` (`abd6eee9f`). It is here so the team can look at it, run it and decide how to take it. It is not a request to merge it.

Branch `cut/terrain-for-discussion-20261116`, 11 commits: 6 layers, then 5 repairs found while making the pictures (D41, D43, the notation guard).

## What it is for

Today the editor's ground is one height field on the site (`site.terrain`), and you shape it with a brush. A house sits at height 0 whatever the ground does under it.

This branch lets a person, or an agent, work with ground that is not flat:

- **Shape the ground.** Sculpt it with the brush on a tiled terrain. Set a plane. Grade along a line, for example a drive at most 18 %. Carve a pad. Grade around a house.
- **Seat a house.** `seat_house` puts the house on the ground with a full-height storey. It has strategies: balance, walk-out, hillside, an areaway, retaining walls. It also re-solves the steps to the doors.
- **Terraces and breaks.** A cliff, a retaining wall or a soil face is a real edge in the ground (`terrain-break`). `add_terraces` builds stepped terraces.
- **A hillside.** The hillside strategy cuts the house into the slope and reports what it could not do (`unmet`).
- **The view under a slope.** The eye counts as under the ground only where ground is actually drawn. That means the sculpted lot up to the property line, and past the line the horizon disc. The orbit rests on the floor of a seated house, not on the datum. A walk-out's lower room is in daylight.
- **Read the ground.** `read_terrain_facts` says where water runs to a wall, which doors and windows are below ground, which faces are unheld, and which drives are too steep. `verify_scene` reports a slab or a wall that straddles a terrain break.

## Size

`git diff --shortstat upstream/main...HEAD`: **253 files, +32,986 / -736**. Code is +19,129 / -574 (168 files). Tests and fixtures are +13,857 / -162 (85 files, 42 %).

The per-package and per-layer tables below were measured on the first 6 commits; the 5 repair commits add about 530 code and 1,000 test lines in core, nodes and editor.

| Package | Code files | Code + / - | Test files | Tests + / - |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| core | 74 | +12,501 / -177 | 42 | +8,888 / -17 |
| nodes | 57 | +5,077 / -154 | 22 | +2,718 / -3 |
| editor | 11 | +547 / -167 | 5 | +590 / -109 |
| viewer | 4 | +76 / -6 | 3 | +100 / -4 |
| mcp | 3 | +167 / -2 | 4 | +552 / -2 |
| apps/editor, scripts, plugin-evals | 3 | +231 / 0 | 0 | 0 |

By commit:

| Commit | Layer | Files | Code + | Tests + |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0e7b7b33d` | core: node kinds, stored format, terrain authority, draped slab, floor-plate fix | 71 | 4,284 | 2,475 |
| `b0e3deda1` | core: the 16 terrain agent operations and tools, plus the verify_scene, get_node and delete_node additions | 43 | 8,209 | 6,403 |
| `51b441bfc` | viewer and editor camera: underground on slopes, orbit floor, implied-ground switch | 16 | 187 | 261 |
| `3b95a39f8` | nodes: composite ground, break faces, tile, break and ramp renderers, smooth-ground switch | 79 | 5,077 | 2,718 |
| `4267fc1ae` | editor: sculpt on tiles, grade along a line, site-plan outlines, palette tile | 10 | 451 | 439 |
| `eab0951f4` | mcp: serve the tools, measure a break, annotation policy | 9 | 391 | 552 |
| `2d15eb4fa`, `b23b94ded` | D43: a room keeps its floor when a plate is merged back; floorless rooms and split floors read on terrain | | | |
| `6120b27d0`, `f032655ee` | D41: a room's floor elevation is read relative to a base that follows the ground | | | |
| `83f02924d` | the notation guard back to exact paths for the terrain tools | | | |

Every commit builds on its own. At each one, core, viewer, nodes and mcp build (`tsc --build`), and editor `check-types` shows no error beyond main's two.

The order puts the agent operations before nodes and editor because the terrain-break draw tool and the panel's grading call them.

By feature (added lines, approximate, by path):

| Feature | Code | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Terraforming, terraces and facts (agent operations) | 7,725 | 6,328 |
| Ramp kind (schema, cut and fill, renderer, tools) | 3,211 | 656 |
| Terrain-break kind and its split ground | 2,709 | 2,836 |
| Terrain authority and field (core lib) | 1,626 | 733 |
| Ground rendering (nodes/site) | 908 | 427 |
| Draped slab | 631 | 232 |
| Terrain-tile kind | 453 | 623 |
| Editor sculpt and camera | 465 | 419 |
| MCP and annotation policy | 391 | 338 |
| Viewer | 76 | 100 |

## What the team must agree on: node kinds and stored format

Four format changes. Each one is stored in scenes, so it is hard to take back once shipped.

1. **`terrain-tile`** (new kind, child of the site). A 32 m tile holding 65 × 65 Int16 height samples, base64 encoded, with a quantization `step` (default 0.01 m). Authored ground is written as tiles. **The tools no longer write `site.terrain`.** The old field stays as a frozen legacy layer that the tiles override.
2. **`terrain-break`** (new kind, child of the site). A `line` in site XZ metres, a `kind` (`cliff`, `retaining` or `soil`), and `left` and `right` sides, each a height or `'ground'`. The line is either open and straight or a simple convex counter-clockwise ring. The kind has `strictMutations`, and the relation check refuses breaks that cross or touch.
3. **`ramp`** (new kind, child of the site). A centreline made of line and arc segments, with heights at both ends, transitions, a width and optional retaining sides. It also carries a `terrainEffect` receipt: the cut and fill it applied, so deleting the ramp gives the ground back. **Why it is here:** the terrain authority reads ramp cuts as part of the ground, so the kind has to be in `AnyNode`. Every `AnyNode` kind needs a definition, so the ramp comes whole, with its renderer, tools and `add_ramp`. It could be a PR of its own (see the split below).
4. **`slab.terrainMode`** (`'flat' | 'draped'`, optional). A draped outdoor slab follows the ground, and its elevation is read as clearance above it. This changes support election in the spatial grid for every scene that has a draped slab. There is no tool and no UI for it in this branch. On `main` nothing writes it yet.

Ground reading changes too. The authority now continues past the field as the field's own context plane instead of holding the edge height. Two existing expectations change because of this, as the lab changed them: `get_site` on a far-off field now reads 0 m of fall, and the first-person collider reaches ±1015 m (the lot) instead of ±1008 m.

## Switches, and what has no switch

Off by default:

- **Smooth ground beside a terrain break.** Faceted by default, which is today's lab look. Turn it on with `setTerrainBreakGround('smooth')` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_PASCAL_TERRAIN_BREAK_GROUND=smooth`.
- **Implied earth under the ground.** `useViewer.undergroundLook.ground`: `'drawn'` by default, `'implied'` to turn it on.

**No switch.** All of the following are on as soon as this lands:

- The 16 terrain tools are in `AGENT_TOOL_CONTRACTS` and the MCP. That means the editor MCP, the hosted MCP and the in-page panel all serve them. The lab's tool switch is not in this repository.
- The Terrain break tile in the Build palette. The Ramp also appears in the palette's advanced section: like every registered kind with `paletteSection: 'structure'` and a floor-plan tool, it is listed by `apps/editor/lib/build-palette.ts`.
- The sculpt panel's additions.
- The new `verify_scene` finding `terrain_break_straddled`. It only fires on scenes that have breaks.
- `get_node` and `measure` on a site now add `breaks: []`, or the break facts.
- Support election for draped slabs, and the floor-plate rules below.

## Changes to main's own code that need a decision first

- **The piers rule** (`terrain-support-query.ts`, lab commit `832c718a5`): `if (!isSiteDatum(baseWorldY) && building?.groundLevelId !== levelId) return null`. A house that names its ground level and stands on piers opens differently after this change. This is open lab decision 11, and defect D24 has not been rendered.
- **Floor-plate thickness** (from `e9defc6e4`: `floor-foundation-datum.ts`, `floor-intent-changes.ts`, `derived-node-guard.ts`). A floor put back under its own underside moves whole and is never stored thinner than a slab. The arithmetic it fixes is on `main`, but no `main` path has been shown to reach it.
- **The walk-out rule in `verify_scene`**: a ground level is no longer called unseated when the level under it is partly below grade.
- **`groundHeightAt(site, nodes, x, z)`**: this exported core function takes the scene's nodes now, so that it reads tiles and breaks. Any caller outside this repository breaks.
- **The eye past the property line**: past the line, the eye is measured against the ground drawn there (the horizon disc), not the height field. This moves where the dark mode starts on every sculpted lot. It is a look decision, still open in the lab. Taking it out is a small change in `underground-ambiance`.

## Non-terrain lab code this branch had to take

Each item is here because the terrain code would not build or pass without it:

- **The ramp kind, whole.** The terrain authority reads ramp cuts, and `AnyNode` needs a renderer for every kind. Comes with `add_ramp` and the release of ramp ground on `delete_node`.
- **`createSceneSpatialGrid`**: a 5-line helper over `createSnapshotSpatialGrid`, used by the drape tests.
- **`getWallTopLowest`** in `services/storey`: the unguarded-drop reading uses it.
- **`live-previews` moved from `store/` to `lib/`.** The terrain source reads it without loading the store; `structure-reconcile`'s clean-bundle test checks this.
- **Site-plan contributors**: site-scoped kinds (ramp, terrain break) draw their own outline on the site plan.
- **`unguarded-drop-observations.ts`**: terrain-break observations use it. It is not wired into `verify_scene` on its own.
- **`rock/material.ts`**: the stone colour of a cliff face.
- **The draped-slab slice of `b1929b5bf`**: spatial grid, item support, stair rise, circulation and layout clearance, and slab geometry. Terrain facts read draped surfaces. The slab panel's drape toggle was **not** taken, because `main` has rewritten that panel.

## Where this differs from the lab

- `unguarded-drop-observations.ts` leaves out the roof-wall guards. They need the lab's roof body and outline (a large non-terrain chain), so roof parapets are not counted as guards here.
- The zone-along-wall stretches that terrain facts read are in a small file of their own (`building/zone-wall-stretches.ts`). They are copied verbatim from the lab's `room-light-check.ts`, which drags in the roof chain.
- The 2D tools of ramp and terrain break draw in the floor-plan frame only. `main`'s `FloorplanToolContext` has no `drawingType`.
- The `verify_scene` walk-out check reads `levelGradeStanding` instead of the lab's per-level field.
- **N1 notation is owed on some fields of 6 tools** (`add_ramp`, `add_terrain_break`, `read_site_terrain`, `read_terrain_contours`, `sample_terrain_line`, `shape_site_terrain`). The notation test lists those exact field paths (written from the input schemas, each checked to still exist and still be bare); every other field of those tools stays under the guard, and their unit-aware fields have fixed conversion cases. Seven ratio and percent fields join `NOT_LENGTHS`.
- **5 core tests are skipped, each marked with the reason.** They need sibling tools this branch does not carry:
  - `terrain-facts`: 2 need `add_site_surface` and 1 needs `add_steps`.
  - `terrain-seated-ground`: 2 need `add_steps`.
- **Fixtures left out.** Four stored-scene fixtures (`.json.gz`) and their tests were left out: `seated-scene-load.test.ts`, `terrain-block-base.test.ts`, `stored-seated-scene-open.test.ts`, and one case of `terrain-bounds.test.ts`.
- **Not taken.** Terrain tools in `run_batch` (`BATCHABLE_TOOLS`). Revealing tiles when a lot grows (`lot-growth.ts` with the `revealRelated` capability). MCP README and agent-guide text. `add_site_surface`, `add_steps`, `add_rock` and `guard_edges`.
- **i18n.** The palette label id `app.lib.buildPalette.terrainBreak` is not extracted into the catalogs. The terrain-break and ramp panels use plain English strings.

## Gates on this branch

All run one test process at a time, after a clean rebuild of core, viewer, nodes and mcp. The baseline is an untouched `main` worktree. The table was taken on the 6-layer head; after the repairs and the rebase on `abd6eee9f`, core is **7,802 pass, 8 skip, 0 fail** and nodes **5,613 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail** (re-run by the reviewer).

| Gate | This branch | Baseline main |
|---|---|---|
| Build core, viewer, nodes, mcp (`tsc --build`) | pass | pass |
| core `check-types` (contracts) | pass | n/a |
| editor `check-types` | 2 errors | the same 2 errors |
| apps/editor `check-types` (`next typegen && tsc`) | 0 errors | 0 errors |
| biome on the touched files (213 checked) | 0 errors, 5 warnings, 32 infos | n/a |
| core `bun test src` | 7,731 pass, 8 skip, 0 fail | 7,184 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail |
| viewer `bun test src` | 1,569 pass, 1 fail | 1,567 pass, 1 fail (the same test) |
| nodes `bun test` | 5,610 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail | 5,512 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail |
| editor `bun test src` | 2,769 pass, 0 fail | 2,761 pass, 0 fail |
| mcp `bun test` | 1,544 pass, 0 fail | 1,531 pass, 0 fail |
| apps/editor `bun test lib` | 78 pass, 0 fail | 77 pass, 1 fail |
| `scripts/openai-tool-annotation-policy.test.ts` | 5 pass | n/a |

Notes on the table:

- **editor `check-types`:** main's two errors are both in `ceiling-bracket-batch.test.ts`.
- **biome:** the 5 warnings are the lab's `useExhaustiveDependencies` in the ground renderers.
- **viewer:** the one failure, on both trees, is "GlbScene resolves replace renderers through its sceneNodes" (`document.body` undefined).
- **core skips:** of the 8, 5 are this branch's and 3 are main's.
- **nodes skips:** the extra one is `terrain-reveal.test.ts`, a cost probe that runs only when `SCENE_JSON` points at a scene file.
- **render bundle:** `bun run check:render-bundle` passes on the head.
- **apps/editor:** the baseline failure is an environment artifact. The viewer's `theme.css` was not copied into the baseline's `dist`.
- **Goldens:** none was re-recorded. Two existing test expectations were changed to the lab's: `get_site` on a far-off field, and the first-person collider's ±1015 m. Both are explained in the commits.

## Known defects and what is not done

From the lab's terrain audit (the defects found in the picture series are listed further down):

- **D23:** a stored seated house with a stale floor plate was healed on open in a real tab on the lab head this code comes from; it is not reproduced by a test here (the stored-scene test was dropped with its fixture).
- **D24 (S2): a house on piers.** See D33b below; the piers rule changes how a lifted house opens.
- **D2, D8 (S2, S1): `grade_around_house {}`.** It fills a plinth, or digs a pit under a basement. The tool is unchanged on purpose; `seat_house` is the cure.
- **D3 (S2): a filled carve pad ends in a bare step.** A fact (`steep_bank`) says so.
- **D11 (S3): a guard fence outlives its drop.**
- **Still open in phase 2:**
  - On a non-convex outline, the hillside strategy excavates the hull.
  - A second seat with another strategy starts from already graded ground.
  - `add_terraces` takes only a straight line and rectangles.
- **Performance.** A terrain break rebuilds the ground with flat shading by default: about 5.8 times the vertices, and slower dabs. The smooth switch brings one sculpt dab from about 262 ms to about 15 ms on a test scene with breaks.

## Pictures

All pictures are of a plain test house built by the tools (an L of 9 x 16 m, rooms named Living, Room 1, Room 2, Garage), never a client scene. Rendered in a real editor tab on the lab head this branch was cut from.

1. [image 1] Seating a house on a 20 % and a 35 % slope (hillside strategy, areaway, retaining).
2. [image 2] The balance seat on four sloping lots: the low line round the house.
3. [image 3] Terraces that touch, with their flights.
4. [image 4] A walk-out on a house with a lower level.
5. [image 5] Steps re-solved after a seat; steps to the ground under a lifted house.
6. [image 6] A drive graded along a line (12 % refused with its reason, 18 % accepted).
7. [image 7] Swales.
8. [image 8] A cliff edge behind the house.
9. [image 9] Ramp sides, plain and retained.
10. [image 10] A house lifted on piers.
11. [image 11] Smooth ground beside a terrain break, switch off and on.
12. [image 12] The underground view diving beside the house, `undergroundLook.ground` 'drawn' and 'implied'.
13. [image 13] The underground view entering the hill at eye level, same switch.
14. [image 14] Defect D41: the floor splits when the ground rises under a house built with create_story_shell.

## Known defects found after the build (from the picture series)

Severity: S2 = wrong result a person would not notice; S3 = wrong or missing, visible; S4 = cosmetic.

- **S2, D26** The default hillside seat buries windows and the rear door (up to about 1.3 m below ground) and says nothing; only the areaway option clears it.
- **S2, D27** `verify_scene` does not see buried openings or earth against walls; only `read_terrain_facts` lists them.
- **S2, D38** A 6 m cliff 1 m behind the house: no guard is added and `verify_scene` says nothing (only `house_at_drop_edge` in the facts).
- **S2, D33b** Opening a scene re-seats the plate of a house the person lifted by hand on piers, without a word.
- **S3, D28** The batter stops at the property line and leaves a step (up to about 3 m on a 35 % lot); said in `unmet`.
- **S3, D29** The default seat leaves a bare vertical soil face behind the house; retaining and areaway are opt-in, with no warning.
- **S3, D30** Flights added by `add_terraces` raise `stair_has_no_landing` (4 and 6) in `verify_scene`.
- **S3, D31** No guard along retained terrace edges of about 1 m, and no finding; the lower 3-step flight has no handrails.
- **S3, D35** The walk-out strategy leaves the upper level's downhill door 2.75 m above the ground, with no stair and nothing in `unmet`.
- **S3, D36/D37** Swales 0.4 m deep are nearly invisible in renders; one swale call returns no `drains` block and `verify_scene` has no swale finding.
- **S3, D40** A ramp's end stays a few centimetres off the ground and the garage sill 0.3 m above it; `verify_scene` says nothing about ramps; 18 % passes without a warning.
- **S3, D34** A pale patch appears on the ground in front of a lifted house; cause not found.
- **S4, D32** Banks at the ends of terraces render as blocky 0.5 m steps with the faceted ground (the smooth-ground switch fixes it, picture 11).
- **S4, D39** A cliff face renders as a stretched, blurred rock texture.
- The low line round a seated house leaves a gutter up to about 0.7 m under the wall foot; the facts give its depth but no outlet.

## Fixed on this branch after the build

- D43 fixed (commits 9e581c77b, 8d574e08d): a room carried by a standing automatic plate keeps its floor when an older plate disappears (the reconcile after a paused call no longer reads it as a deletion); read_terrain_facts reads floorless enclosed rooms' walls and doors and names them (room_without_floor); seat_house says when a room has no floor plate and is not seated.
- **D41 fixed** (commits 6120b27d0, f032655ee; picture 14 shows the defect before the fix). A house built with `create_story_shell` kept its shell's floor elevation on one zone; when the ground rose under the house, the floor split into plates 2 m apart and a room was left with no floor. Now a room's stored floor elevation **E** is read relative to the automatic base **B** that follows the ground: it resolves to **E + B − 0.05 m**, so the intended step (E − 0.05) is kept. On flat ground (B = 0.05) nothing changes. A stored scene that was already lifted and split is repaired on its next reconcile. Authored foundation heights, keyed floors, suspended floors and manual slabs keep their rules. `floor_split` stays as a guard for real steps beyond tolerance. Also: walls of a floorless room on a lifted house stand at the plate; `seat_house` grades under a floorless wing like the rest of the house; floorless open rooms (a porch) are read by the terrain facts.

## Existing tests this PR changes

28 test files that exist on `main` are modified (63 hunks). Each hunk was classified: **44** add cases only, **8** update a count or an inventory for the added kinds and tools, **15** change an existing expectation because the behaviour deliberately changes, **0** loosen an expectation to fit the code (the one found was restored to exact paths). The 15 behaviour changes:

1. `scene-view.test.ts`: the missing-plugin roof case uses a genuinely unregistered roof-plane kind; its expected frame is unchanged.
2. `notation.test.ts`: tolerates the listed metres-only field paths of six terrain tools (exact paths only).
3. `site-ground-height.test.ts`: `groundHeightAt` is passed the scene's nodes so it sees tiles and breaks; every expected height is unchanged.
4. `structure-reconcile.test.ts`: a stored 0.42 m room intent above a 0.65 m moving base gives a 1.02 m platform (a 0.37 m step) instead of an absolute 0.42 m sunken plate (D41).
5. `terrain-source.test.ts`: returns a cached composite terrain authority instead of the identical input field; the sampled 2.5 m height is unchanged.
6. `room-built-on.test.ts`: with the 0.15 m shared base, the neighbouring stored-0.30 room walks at 0.40 m (D41).
7-10. `terrain-sculpt.test.ts`: a half-metre editing lattice covering the lot; the brush minimum no longer grows with a larger lot or a coarse imported base; the flatten read includes the scene's nodes (expected 3 m unchanged).
11-12. `raised-room.test.ts`: a fixed 0.55 m step above the moving base instead of a fixed absolute 0.60 m platform top, in the store and in the rendered raycast (D41).
13. `build-collider-world.test.ts`: the walkable skirt reaches the full 30 m lot (X bounds ±1008 m to ±1015 m), with the matching Z bounds.
(Some items cover two hunks of the same file, hence 15 hunks in 13 items.)

## Open questions for the team

1. **Size.** The team called a 15k-line PR too much, and this one is 33k (42 % tests). Proposed split, each PR building on the one before:
   1. **Terrain tiles and the authority** (core). The `terrain-tile` kind, the tiled authority, the continuation past the field, and the live-preview move. About 2.1k code and 1.4k tests. Changes no tool.
   2. **Terrain breaks** (core and nodes). The `terrain-break` kind, validation, the split ground (faceted by default, smooth behind the switch), the break faces, the draw tool, and `add_terrain_break`. About 2.7k code and 2.8k tests; tests to trim, including the golden hashes.
   3. **Ground rendering and the underground view** (nodes, viewer, editor camera). The composite ground, the orbit floor, the eye past the lot (if agreed), and the implied ground. About 1.5k code and 1k tests.
   4. **The older terrain tools** (reads, `shape_site_terrain`, `carve_terrain_pad`, `grade_around_house`, `set_site_lot`) and the sculpt panel. About 2.5k code.
   5. **Terraforming** (`seat_house`, `set_terrain_plane`, `grade_along_line`, `add_steps_to_ground`, `add_terraces`, `read_terrain_facts`), with the floor-plate and piers rules once decided. About 5k code and 5k tests; needs the most trimming.
   6. **Ramp and draped slab** as siblings. They could also come before 4.
   - Each PR keeps "off = main" where a switch exists. The team should say whether the agent tools need a switch in the public editor too.
2. **Stored format.** Tiles instead of `site.terrain`: is the team fine with a frozen legacy layer plus tiles, and with a 0.01 m quantization? Should breaks and ramps be site children?
3. **Tools without a switch.** Should the terrain tools be behind a word on `main` (MCP, hosted MCP, in-page panel), or offered only in a "casquette" (trade-focused mode) or Landscaper context?
4. **Test share.** 41 % tests, including golden hash files that pin the faceted build byte for byte. Which of these does the team want kept?

title: wall chaining, collinear transit, and lazy editor startup
body:
## What does this PR do?

- **Continuous wall chaining in `Walls` mode (3D and 2D/split):** Removes the early `!wallDraftIsRun()` stop in `packages/nodes/src/wall/tool.tsx` and `packages/editor/src/components/editor/floorplan-panel.tsx` so consecutive walls chain directly from the previous wall's exact resolved endpoint (`createdWall.end`). Chains still terminate cleanly on room close, T-junctions, double-click, or `Escape`.
- **Collinear wall tracking transit:** Exports `wallSegmentsCoverSegment` from `@pascal-app/core` (`packages/core/src/systems/wall/wall-topology.ts` and `packages/core/src/index.ts`) and handles collinear segments covered by existing walls in 3D and 2D drafting (gating the 2D collinear transit check to 2D-only mode in split view). Moving along an existing wall centerline advances the draft origin without duplicating the wall, so perpendicular partition walls start strictly on the host centerline and T-join cleanly.
- **Editor startup & bundle code-splitting:**
  - Moves 3D node-registry bootstrap (`apps/editor/lib/bootstrap.ts`) out of `RootLayout` (`apps/editor/app/client-bootstrap.tsx`) into 3D/scene entrypoints (`scene-loader.tsx`, `embed-viewer.tsx`, `import-client.tsx`) so non-3D routes (`/`, `/login`, `/settings`, `/setup`) do not load Three.js, `@pascal-app/viewer`, `@pascal-app/editor`, `@pascal-app/nodes`, or external 3D plugins.
  - Converts all external plugins in `apps/editor/lib/bootstrap.ts` to dynamic `import(...)` scheduled via `requestIdleCallback`, and isolates `@webxr/plugin` behind `React.lazy` in `webxr-feature-gate.tsx`, `webxr-enabled-runtime.tsx`, and `scene-loader.tsx`.
  - Adds `@pascal-app/editor/locales/lazy` (`packages/editor/src/i18n/lazy-locales.ts`) and updates `apps/editor` (`layout.tsx`, `client-bootstrap.tsx`, `dev-locales.ts`) to register English upfront and load non-English locales (`es`, `fr`, `ja`, `zh-CN`) and dev `en-XA` only on demand.
  - Lazy-loads heavy format exporters (`GLB`, `USDZ`, `IFC`, `STL`, `OBJ`, `3MF`, Manifold) inside `packages/editor/src/components/editor/export-manager.tsx`, and code-splits `FloorplanPanel`, `FirstPersonControls`/`FirstPersonOverlay`, `RiserDiagramPanel`, and `SnapshotCaptureOverlay` inside `packages/editor/src/components/editor/index.tsx`.
  - Adds a `dev:fast` script in root `package.json` and suppresses the `node:sqlite` `ExperimentalWarning` in Next.js dev scripts.
- **React 19 + `@react-three/drei` `<Html>` unmount patch:** Adds `patches/@react-three%2Fdrei@10.7.9.patch` via `patchedDependencies` so `<Html>` reuses its `ReactDOM` root across effect re-runs (StrictMode / target changes) and defers real unmounts via `queueMicrotask`, fixing React 19 synchronous unmount errors and `NotFoundError: removeChild`.
- **Tests:** Adds unit coverage for `wallSegmentsCoverSegment` in `packages/core/src/systems/wall/wall-topology.test.ts` and integration tests for chained off-grid typed walls and collinear transit T-junctions in `packages/nodes/src/wall/tool-chaining.test.tsx`.

## How to test

1. Start the editor locally with `bun run dev:fast` (or `bun dev`) and open `/` — confirm it renders cleanly without loading 3D plugin chunks or showing the `node:sqlite` dev overlay warning.
2. Open a project (`/project/<id>`) and verify the 3D scene loads cleanly with no `<Html>` synchronous-unmount or `removeChild` console errors, and that 2D floorplan, plugins, and exports still load and work on demand.
3. Select the **Walls** tool in default `Grid (0.5 m)` snapping mode (in 3D, 2D, or split view). Click a start point, type `3.2` and press Enter to place Wall 1 — verify the tool automatically chains from `[3.2, 0]` without a manual re-click, and closing a 4-wall room leaves zero `Not joined` gaps.
4. Click a corner of an existing wall, type `2.3` along its length and press Enter — verify no duplicate wall is created and the draft origin advances `2.3 m` along the host wall; turn 90° and place a partition wall to verify a clean T-junction.
5. Automated checks run locally:
   - `bunx biome check` on all changed/added files (0 errors)
   - `bun --cwd packages/editor check-types` (`tsgo --noEmit`, 0 errors)
   - `bun test packages/editor/src/i18n` (5 pass, 0 fail)
   - `bun --cwd apps/editor test` (76 pass; 2 pre-existing Windows path failures in `lib/css-build.test.ts`)
   - Verified `GET http://localhost:3002/` returns HTTP 200 on a fresh `.next` cache with `bun run dev:fast`

## Screenshots / screen recording

> **Medium Risk**
> Broad changes to bootstrap, plugin discovery, i18n hydration, and wall authoring logic; failures in lazy loading or chain sync could affect first paint or drafting in split view.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR **shrinks editor cold start** by deferring heavy work: the 3D node registry bootstrap moves from the root layout into 3D entry routes (`scene-loader`, `embed-viewer`, `import`), external plugins load via dynamic `import()` on `requestIdleCallback`, WebXR/UI chunks use `React.lazy`, non-English locales and dev `en-XA` load on demand, and large export pipelines plus floorplan/riser/snapshot panels code-split. title: viewer: capture point clouds as discs; editor: lot-patch export
body:
## What does this PR do?

- **viewer: capture point clouds draw as round discs.** Under WebGPU a point primitive is one pixel wide whatever its size, so saved scan clouds read as dust. Every path of `CapturePointCloudLayer` (PLY artifact, inline payload, live packets) now draws one instanced `SpriteNodeMaterial` of camera-facing discs, 2 cm wide, coloured per point. A PLY over `maxPoints` is thinned evenly. `PointDiscCloud` and `POINT_DISC_SIZE` are exported from `@pascal-app/viewer/capture` for hosts.
- **editor: `@pascal-app/editor/lot-patch` subpath.** Exposes the pure lot-patch module (`sitePatchFromParcel` and its types) so a host can write a site from a parcel server-side, with the same ring cleanup, front edge and setback defaults as Find parcel, without importing the editor UI.

## How to test

1. Open a project with a saved capture scan that has a point cloud: the cloud reads as coloured discs instead of a faint 1 px dust, walls still hide it, and switching the layer off hides it.
2. `bun test packages/viewer/src/capture`: 30 pass, including the new thinning and empty-cloud cases.
3. `import { sitePatchFromParcel } from '@pascal-app/editor/lot-patch'` resolves from a host without pulling React.

title: Trade tools for the Painter, the Roofer and the Landscaper
body:
# Trade tools for the Painter, the Roofer and the Landscaper

Branch `cut/hats-delivery-20261117`, merged with public main `cf37d32cd` on 19 November (one new commit, four lines in the viewer; clean merge, viewer suite 1,810 pass / 0 fail). Head: `6245cc2ce` (on top of `0d7f4969b`: the tree USDZ export fix `6d4f60f5f`, the lawn fixes and the garden hand tools' review below; on it: editor package 2,770 pass / 0 fail, nodes 6,046 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, the editor's two known type errors only); the checks listed below were run on `144572c0b` and `ec5d5fcf9` (see “Updates on 18 and 19 November” and “Trees, lawn and hand placement of garden objects”). On 19 November the scope grew by the Landscaper’s trees and lawn; the owner’s manual review remains outstanding.

## What it is
Three trades get their own tools, on the shared contract (core operation, batch step, MCP tool) and by hand in the editor:

- **Painter.** `set_wall_trim`: skirting, chair rail and crown bounded to one room's stretch of a wall, so a shared wall dressed from one room leaves the neighbour's face bare. `dress_room`: a room's whole finish stack in one atomic call (seven layers, dry run, refusals before any write), plus the selected room's Dress room panel.
- **Roofer.** `add_roof_element` (chimney, skylight, solar panel, cupola, four vents) and `add_dormer` (eight dormer roof forms, window included). Both read the physical finished covering; unknown geometry is refused, never guessed. The native manual tools share the same admission. Opt-in close covering detail (`covering`: tile, clay or slate courses near the camera, the original material far away; optional ridge and hip caps), and flashing on new dormers.
- **Landscaper.** `add_hedge`, `add_planting` (organic layered planting beds) and `add_rock` (seven rock types, outline or `at` + `size`), on main's Site ground, with their panels, plan tools and Outdoor tiles. `add_site_surface` lays a driveway, path, patio or lawn (site flatwork just above the ground, which main's site plan already reads; a new flat-green library material `preset-lawn`), and `add_steps` a short outside flight from the ground to a porch or sill, its run following its rise.

Also included: the roof hosting prep from the Mason's series (`95318e365`, `2afff767b`, `f91c47cee`, `a0c0c2671`): clipped-footprint roof fitting, floor intent kept when plates merge, roof edits prepared and roof batches admitted before writes. Roof-host refusals now travel through the writers; which level a roof lands on is unchanged.

**Left out: the Mason.** Its porch and volume tools were not activated, and its conventional roof hosting commit (`b2ef42f9c`) is not merged: it fails 13 existing behaviour tests (five `create_roof` / `move_roofs_to_roof_level` cases in core, the same five over MCP, three curved-wall roof builder cases) and one metadata inventory, because it changes which level a roof lands on. That change needs its own decision.

## Pictures
Standalone captures of the generators and shaders this branch carries.

**Hedge: clipped and loose, generations 1 and 2**

![Hedge: clipped and loose, generations 1 and 2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomeCG/editor/evidence/trade-tools-hats/trade-tools-hats/hedge-sheet.png)

**Planting beds**

![Planting beds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomeCG/editor/evidence/trade-tools-hats/trade-tools-hats/planting-sheet.png)

**The seven rock types**

![The seven rock types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomeCG/editor/evidence/trade-tools-hats/trade-tools-hats/rocks-types.png)

**Clay covering detail near, mid and far, on and off**

![Clay covering detail near, mid and far, on and off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomeCG/editor/evidence/trade-tools-hats/trade-tools-hats/clay-near-mid-far.png)

**Tile and slate detail**

![Tile and slate detail](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AxiomeCG/editor/evidence/trade-tools-hats/trade-tools-hats/tile-detail.png)


## How to test
- `bun test` in `packages/core`, `packages/nodes`, `packages/mcp`, `packages/editor`, `packages/viewer` (one at a time).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/<core|nodes|mcp|viewer|editor>/tsconfig.json`.
- `bun run i18n:check`.
- By hand: `apps/editor` → Build → Outdoor (hedge, planting bed, rock); select a roof → the roof accessory tools and the Dormer tool; select a room → Dress room.

## Main update and verification
The core export conflict keeps both roof exports and main’s `room-counts`. The wall definition keeps main’s `walls` viewer family and schema version 11. Compiled English and pseudo catalogs were bootstrapped from main, then regenerated with `bun run i18n:extract` (4,091 messages), never hand-merged. Hedge, planting and rock declare the `site` viewer family. Main’s section cut, X-ray and host hooks are retained.

Whole-package `bun test`, one package process at a time: core **7,947 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip**; nodes **5,846 / 0 / 1**; MCP **1,583 / 0**; viewer **1,810 / 0**; editor **2,764 / 0**. `bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/<pkg>/tsconfig.json`: core, nodes, MCP and viewer pass; editor reports the two ceiling-bracket-batch test errors. Fresh public main `ec5d5fcf9` package tests: core **7,312 / 0 / 3 skip**; nodes **5,525 / 0 / 1 skip**; MCP **1,531 / 0**; viewer **1,751 / 0**; editor **2,761 / 0**. Forced distribution rebuild and direct installed Biome check (501 files) pass. All five main typechecks pass after generating its build-only sandbox artifact. The merged editor also passes in an isolated snapshot; the assigned checkout’s unchanged ceiling test still reports two errors because TypeScript falls through to ancestor `@types/three` 0.184.1 rather than the installed 0.187.0. No test was edited to mask this environment difference. `i18n:check` and the render-bundle gate pass. No new browser or GPU proof is claimed.

## Every pre-existing test or fixture changed
Paths are relative to the public repository. These are the delivery’s cumulative changes against current main, not just this merge; no behavioral expectation was weakened to complete the main update.

- `packages/nodes/src/index.test.ts:69-70,223`: kind count 56 → 59; extend main’s new `site` taxonomy with hedge, planting and rock. **The only test edit during this main update is line 223.**
- `packages/core/src/schema/host-children.test.ts:37-49`: keep the old corpus frozen by excluding the three new garden kinds.
- `packages/core/src/schema/__fixtures__/node-fixtures.ts:32,69-71`: valid minimum garden-kind fixtures.
- `packages/core/src/agent-operations/__fixtures__/notation-cases.ts:329-334`: five dimensionless paths (hedge clip, planting share, rock weathering/moss/lichen).
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/measure-world.test.ts:69-74,111-119`: garden fixtures for exhaustive world-measure coverage.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/read-tool-annotations.test.ts:72-77,113-118,129`: nine trade tools in annotation inventories.
- `plugin-evals/tool-annotation-justifications.json:49,75,114-166,478,1167`: nine new annotation/justification records; consumed by the annotation tests. The policy inventory in `scripts/openai-tool-annotation-policy.ts:18-28,61` gains the same nine tools.
- `packages/mcp/src/resources/resources.test.ts:257-278`: three rock codes, `steps_too_tall` and `surface_degenerate` in the closed refusal-code whitelist (10 → 15).
- `packages/nodes/src/wall/definition.test.ts:18-19`: schema-version pin 10 → 11 for bounded trims.
- `packages/core/src/services/roof-level.test.ts:56-72`, `packages/core/src/building/level-duplication.test.ts:20-27`, `packages/core/src/agent-operations/roof-writes.test.ts:437-438,464-465`: positive cases throw on an unexpected planner refusal; existing roof-placement assertions remain.
- `packages/core/src/lib/structure-reconcile.test.ts:165,299-413`: stricter `hasFloor: false` assertion and an added merged-floor intent/carrier regression.
- `packages/nodes/src/shared/roof-accessory-move.test.tsx:21-42,96-105`: pointer fixtures raycast the real finished covering; snapping and undo assertions retained.
- Added cases only: `packages/core/src/spatial/usage-field/walls.test.ts:94-123` (bounded trims), `packages/nodes/src/wall/treatments.test.ts:83-108` (rendered trim extent), `packages/editor/src/lib/fresh-planar-placement.test.ts:396-508` (dormer subtree remapping, publication and undo).

## Earlier delivery integration fixes (unchanged by this update)
The attic level flag `add_dormer` reads is classified in the metadata inventory; a migrated legacy dormer window keeps main's nominal face (main's migration test failed otherwise); the garden panels' literals go through `i18n._`; the conical flashing test gets 30 s for its CSG cut.

## Updates on 18 and 19 November
Head moved from `302e22829` to `504b1b541`. The figures in the sections above describe `302e22829`.

**CI fixes (`85885376c`, `3cdd6349f`, `d6bda96d5`; 6 files, +72 / −23).** The first full CI run failed on two weaknesses of this branch, both in tests: packages imported a test dependency they did not declare (`happy-dom` in `packages/nodes`), and the saved-rock test compared mesh data with values recorded on macOS that differ on Linux. Each package now declares what it imports, the rock check holds across platforms, and the custom hedge generation tests no longer share state.

**Garden objects can be selected in 3D (`48c692bdb`).** Hedges, planting beds and rocks are children of the Site, and the 3D selection dropped anything the Site owns: a click on one selected nothing and its inspector never opened. A click now selects it, and the Site panel lists the garden objects and opens their inspectors (`selection-manager.tsx`, `selection-routing.ts`, the Site panel). Known limit: a click made from the Site phase selects the object and then switches to the building phase.

**Drawing a hedge or a planting bed no longer blanks the scene (`504b1b541`).** Under WebGPU, the outline shown while drawing used a line material the renderer refuses (an unbounded instance count): the whole scene was replaced by a flat field during the gesture, with 98 to 270 console errors per gesture. The outline is now drawn with three’s own `Line2` and a finite geometry, with no framebuffer capture (`packages/nodes/src/shared/garden-preview-line.tsx`, the hedge and planting tools).

The two fixes against `d6bda96d5`: 11 files, +981 / −46; four new test files carry 803 of the added lines. No pre-existing test was edited; the shared test harness `packages/nodes/src/__tests__/harness.tsx` gains 4 lines (added only).

Checks on `504b1b541`: `packages/editor` 2,770 pass / 0 fail; `packages/nodes` 5,870 run / 0 fail; type check = the editor package’s two known errors in `ceiling-bracket-batch.test.ts` and nothing new; render bundle check passed.

Not proven: the selection fix has automated tests but was not clicked through in a browser on this branch.

## Trees, lawn and hand placement of garden objects (added 19 November)
The owner decided on 19 November to deliver the Landscaper's trees and lawn in this PR rather than in a second one stacked on it. Head `144572c0b` contains the previous head `504b1b541`; against it: **160 files, +20,154 / −97 lines**. The sections above this one describe the branch before these additions.

Besides the two node kinds described below:

- **3D selection and inspectors** extend to trees and lawns: a click selects the object, the Site panel lists it and opens its inspector. A click on a tree follows the leaf silhouette: the transparent parts of the leaf cards do not catch the click (`packages/nodes/src/tree/geometry.ts`).
- **Lawn brush from the inspector.** A selected lawn's inspector exposes the brush controls, so the brush can be reached without re-entering the Lawn tool (`packages/nodes/src/lawn/parametrics-flowers.tsx`).
- **Drawing previews under WebGPU.** The shared outline that fixed the hedge and the planting bed (`packages/nodes/src/shared/garden-preview-line.tsx`) also draws the lawn area and the lawn brush. Brush rings remain faint over grass.
- Three test files added by the 18 November fixes (`site-panel/index.test.tsx`, `garden-selection.test.tsx`, `garden-preview.test.tsx`) are replaced by versions that also cover the tree and the lawn.

Checks on `144572c0b`, one package process at a time:

| Package | Pass | Skip | Fail |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| core | 8,123 | 3 | 0 |
| nodes | 6,015 | 1 | 0 |
| mcp | 1,617 | 0 | 0 |
| viewer | 1,810 | 0 | 0 |
| editor | 2,770 | 0 | 0 |

Type checks: core, nodes, MCP and viewer clean; the editor package keeps exactly its two known errors in `ceiling-bracket-batch.test.ts`. Render bundle check passed. `i18n:check` passed on the branch before the merge with the 18 November fixes (4,186 messages; the merge changed no catalog).

Not proven: the hand tools, the brush and the fixed previews were driven in a real browser tab on a local server at the same commits; no remote CI yet on this head; no native-device USDZ viewing; target-language translations are unreviewed drafts.

### Native garden additions

The built-in inventory grows **59 → 61**, with `tree` and `lawn` both in viewer family `site`. Full and render-only registrations, schemas, Site plans, agent operations/contracts and inventories retain both. English/pseudo catalogs were regenerated by the project commands: **4,186 messages**. Target-language drafts remain fuzzy and render English until reviewed; existing reviewed translations are preserved.

#### Trees

`add_tree` plants one to forty compact Site children atomically, with shared defaults and per-tree overrides: round, spreading, upright, conifer, weeping and multistem. Height, spread, foliage colour, density and signed 32-bit seed determine the result; density zero retains winter wood. Ground follows Site terrain/ground-storey slabs. Trunks inside buildings are refused; crown overlap is reported, not refused. Crown-disc facts are nominal, not union or leaf area.

The native Tree tool supplies preview, movement, inspector, plan symbol and undo. Near/far builders share seeded branch anchors; ordinary editing uses near detail, not automatic distance switching. The runtime generates wood, sprigs, bark and a shared 512² RGBA atlas; no image/model asset or new runtime dependency.

Incoming tree-report observations, not re-benchmarked here: at 8 m/density .85/seed19, six forms use 9,774–11,022 near triangles and 526–537 far triangles; warm local CPU medians 3.49–4.20 ms. Caps are 12,000/600 triangles, one colour-pass draw/tree. Seven-tree garden: 70,998/3,707 triangles and seven draws. Atlas payload: 1,048,576 base bytes / 1,398,100 with mips. Driver/shadow/first-use costs are outside these figures.

Tree GLB downloads and viewer bakes retain atlas, UVs, colours and cutouts. Scenes containing trees also export to USDZ, in all six forms, including bare winter trees (`6d4f60f5f`, added 19 November: before it, a mapped material with varying vertex colours stopped the whole USDZ export, so one visible tree was enough to lose it). Foliage keeps its embedded sprig atlas and leaf cutout. USDZ carries one representative tint per tree mesh instead of GLB's varying vertex tints, so trunk and foliage share it, and the export warns that foliage tints were simplified. The rule is general (any mapped material with varying vertex colours, USDZ only); GLB downloads and viewer bakes are unchanged. 31 tests added in `packages/nodes/src/tree/export.test.ts` unzip the real archive and check geometry, texture, cutout, colour and the warning; no existing test changed. Measured headless: one 8 m tree is 6.3 MB in USDZ against 0.9 MB in GLB.

#### Lawn and shared brush

`add_site_surface(kind: "lawn")` now creates an editable **Site-owned `lawn`**, not a raised slab. Paving still creates slabs. Saved data is outline, parameters, seed/generator and ordered vector strokes—not blade nodes, geometry or raster paint fields. Height, blade width, density, roughness, colour, edge fade, wind, flower density/species and season are explicit. Flowers are off by default.

The lawn follows retained Site terrain and excludes buildings, paving and beds. Facts distinguish requested/retained area, excluded union/owners, canonical blade/flower populations, thinning/work bounds and sampled brush-effect areas. A `lawnId` is not a `slabId`. Level-target coordinates transform once into Site space; explicit Site input uses Site metres.

The native Lawn tool draws areas in 2D/3D and switches to a brush. Both hand and agent save the same ordered `{points, radiusM, effect, strength}` strokes: bare, grass, taller, shorter, more-flowers, fewer-flowers. **20,000 total points/lawn replaces the 64-stroke cap.** Painting simplifies against actual samples within min(1 cm, 2% of radius), preserving endpoints/corners and never rewriting older intent. Near/full/compute-budget feedback is visible in both tool adapters; refusals name the bound. One successful stroke is one undo step; failed/cancelled strokes write nothing. Independent 32M generation-visit, 250k candidate-cell and terrain budgets remain and can bind earlier on complex lawns.

Environment retains its legacy raster paint/height fields, surface-material mixing, atmosphere controls and existing ground-cover nodes. Old plugin lawns and flat lawn slabs are untouched. No migration, implicit replacement, overlap arbitration or renderer precedence is introduced; replacement needs explicit intent.

### Chosen appearance and export

The chosen dense tuft look carries crossed curved leaf fans, mowing-direction tone, procedural ground grain and detailed daisy/clover/yarrow heads. Source look-report measurements: 600 m² lot retains 509.2 m² and 50,870 canonical roots; eye view 290,239 triangles / 16 lawn draws / 1.65 MiB uploaded geometry. Each root uses 32 bytes. Shared live base maps: 128 KiB tuft RG8, 64 KiB ground R8, 256 KiB flowering RGBA8 (payloads, not driver residency). Its brushed fixture yielded 261 heads versus 167 unpainted. These source measurements are not new timing claims.

Fresh hardware Chrome WebGPU reproduces 290,239 triangles/16 draws. WebGPU and WebGL2 exposed bright blade fringes from alpha-to-coverage; disabling that blade setting restores the chosen soft turf, protected by a RED→GREEN regression. Flower coverage remains unchanged after independent portrait probes.

The bake hook now carries the chosen tuft silhouettes/colour, two-frequency ground grain, and flower/leaf atlas pigments in ordinary mapped materials. Both windings retain the upward canopy normal; the generic exporter must not negate back copies. Affine alpha/cutoff remapping preserves effective filtered masks while preventing canvas-premultiplied PNG hue loss. No generic exporter or live appearance redesign was needed.

Real GLB reload: **37,500,600 bytes**, 612,778 submitted triangles / 24 draws, 20,165,488 resident geometry bytes. Foreground mean RGB error versus live is **1.046/255**, brushed frame **1.135/255**; source scene unchanged and no live resources disposed. Initial reload defects (downward normals and fringe hue loss) are corrected, not hidden. Comparison sheets show approved `ab-lawn.png` middle column, merged live and actual GLB reload.

Portable snapshots deliberately freeze wind, retain canonical all-near populations rather than camera LOD, quantize tuft tone into 32 bins/two 1K atlases, and rasterize ground at nominal 128 px/m capped at 1K/page. Static clover heads retain atlas florets but not live view-dependent rim coverage. Pascal's replace renderer still supplies live rendering from the baked graph/resolver. Native-device USDZ viewing and remote CI are not proven.

### Closed inventories and annotations

Extended schema exports/union/fixtures; render/edit registration and root exports; Site viewer-family taxonomy; native Site-plan/exterior inventories; hosted trade ownership in the private companion PR. MCP already exposes `add_site_surface`; its description/annotation justification now distinguishes Site lawn from level paving. No redundant lawn tool is added. Guides and public skill document shared point/work budgets and legacy preservation.

The guide whitelist adds actual lawn codes: `lawn_empty`, `lawn_material_unsupported`, `lawn_outline_required`, `lawn_target_conflict`, `lawn_terrain_budget`, `lawn_transform_unsupported`, `lawn_work_budget`. Existing tree tool/annotation/refusal inventories remain intact.

### Every pre-existing test/fixture touched

Relative to this branch as it stood before the garden additions (`d6bda96d5`); closed inventories are extended, not relaxed:

- `packages/core/src/agent-operations/__fixtures__/cases.ts`: include new shared lawn cases for all runners.
- `packages/core/src/agent-operations/__fixtures__/notation-cases.ts`: tree measurement/coordinate cases; classify lawn rates/fractions/stroke strength as dimensionless.
- `packages/core/src/agent-tools/notation.test.ts`: additional tree-coordinate notation cases; exhaustive plain-number assertion retained.
- `packages/core/src/schema/__fixtures__/node-fixtures.ts`: required lawn-outline fixture.
- `packages/core/src/schema/host-children.test.ts`: exclude tree/lawn from the frozen pre-separator corpus; historical records unchanged.
- `packages/mcp/src/resources/resources.test.ts`: actual tree/lawn codes join the closed refusal-name whitelist; unknown-name assertion retained.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/measure-world.test.ts`: required lawn outline and real Site host in the all-kinds fixture; resolution assertions retained.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/read-tool-annotations.test.ts`: tree joins write-tool inventory.
- `packages/nodes/src/__tests__/garden-registration.test.ts`: tree/lawn registration/default/geometry inventory, with generator/default assertions.
- `packages/nodes/src/__tests__/garden-support-invalidation.test.ts`: tree joins changed-ground ownership table.
- `packages/nodes/src/__tests__/site-plan-contributors.test.ts`: tree/lawn symbols join the same Site drawing comparison.
- `packages/nodes/src/__tests__/unrenderable-host-audit.test.tsx`: fixture reads allowed parents and `movable.resolvePosition`, links Site children and mounts real renderers instead of manufacturing invalid Level-owned/nonzero-Y Site nodes. All kinds, movers, event orders, pose/visibility and reload assertions retained.
- `packages/nodes/src/exterior-declarations.test.ts`: lawn joins the exterior inventory.
- `packages/nodes/src/index.test.ts`: count/uniqueness 59→61; Site taxonomy gains tree/lawn; registry/family comparisons retained.

**Owner-approved old statement change:** `packages/core/src/agent-operations/site-works.test.ts`:
- Old: “a lawn from two corners is the rectangle they span, green, 1 cm up, marked lawn” (a slab).
- New: “a lawn from two corners is an editable Site child with its retained area” (same 16 m² rectangle, Site parent, 6 cm default grass, no flowers and no slabId).

Incoming unreleased lawn tests also change where the owner explicitly superseded the old bounds/appearance:

- `packages/core/src/schema/lawn.test.ts` and `agent-operations/lawn.test.ts`: obsolete 65-stroke/129-point refusals become 20,000/20,001 combined-point boundaries and >64-stroke acceptance.
- `packages/mcp/src/tools/lawn-patch.test.ts`: the old 65-stroke refusal becomes combined 20,001-point refusal with a genuinely saved earlier stroke; adds 65-stroke acceptance and one-step undo. Atomic/no-eviction assertions remain.
- `packages/nodes/src/lawn/brush.test.ts`: full point-budget fixture, simplification/corners/reversals, bounded long jitter and one-undo checks; a real zigzag still exercises the compute refusal because straight paths now simplify. Controller tests add visible near/full/start/mid-gesture refusal checks.
- `packages/nodes/src/lawn/geometry.test.ts`: 15 old indices/blade becomes 36 per crossed tuft with explicit back windings. The unchanged 1,600 m² 16-bit flower-splitting fixture gets a 30-second execution allowance instead of Bun's 5 seconds because it now rasterizes ground maps too; geometric assertions are retained.
- `packages/nodes/src/lawn/export.test.ts`: the superseded 192 KiB colour ramp bound becomes at most two 1024² tuft maps, 4 MiB each / 8 MiB aggregate (ground and flower maps are separate). Appearance samples the first 20 tufts per mesh rather than every old blade vertex; the linear-colour tolerance changes from approximately .005 to .03 for the 32-bin snapshot approximation. These are explicit replacements/relaxations, not unchanged precision claims. All-canonical-root membership/count, finite/index bounds, paired winding/upward normals, immutability and disposal checks remain; new grain/species/cutout and filtered-mask oracles cover the changed representation.

New real portable/viewer GLB and USDZ tests run production export paths and decode serialized PNGs, bindings and cutoffs; GLB additionally checks serialized canopy normals. Only canvas/PNG/Blob transport is supplied in Bun; fresh hardware GLB reload is separate evidence. No machine-recorded geometry hashes/bytes are used. Test imports are declared in their owning package, including `happy-dom`.

## Lawn fixes from the owner's test (added 19 November)
**The lawn no longer flickers under temporal anti-aliasing (`bac2d7737`, test `55495a55c`).** With the camera still, the lawn flickered whenever the viewer's post-processing was on. Measured pass by pass: only the temporal anti-aliasing carries it (off: no change between frames; ambient occlusion, outline and bloom make no difference). Cause: the blades place themselves in the material's `positionNode`, which three's velocity output does not follow; with a still camera 87 % of the close lawn pixels reported motion (757 px a frame on average), so the temporal pass read its history elsewhere and showed the raw jittered cutouts. The blade material now assigns `positionPrevious` its placed position when a pass needs previous data (`packages/nodes/src/lawn/blade-material.ts`, +16 / −1). The pipeline is unchanged. Close view, medium quality: lawn pixel-frames changing by more than 4 levels go from 16.19 % to 0.13 %. A direct render is pixel-identical before and after; under the pipeline the still lawn is now temporally resolved, slightly softer than a single frame was. Other materials that place vertices in `positionNode` were not measured.

**A brush stroke in progress no longer rebuilds the whole lawn on every pointer sample (`4d505104e`, tests `f46398c00`, `6120c9ef4`).** During a stroke the lawn rebuilds at most every 120 ms (or five times its last build time), through the definition's `geometryKey`; release, cancel and every other change rebuild at once. The saved stroke, the rebuilt lawn and the single undo step are identical before and after. Measured in a harness without the editor shell, 600 m² lot: 26 to 45 frames a second while painting bare ground, 13 to 43 with flowers. The owner still found painting slow in the app after this first step; the chunked rebuild below replaces it during a stroke.

8 files, +367 / −4, all under `packages/nodes/src/lawn`; 10 tests added, none edited. On `6120c9ef4`: nodes 6,056 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, viewer 1,810 pass / 0 fail, type checks clean, render bundle check passed.

## Garden hand tools: interface review, and the lawn brush by chunks (added 19 November, from the owner's test)
27 commits on `6120c9ef4`: 70 files, +4,275 / −280.

**The lawn brush redraws only the chunks under it.** A lawn is built in 8 m chunks; one chunk can now be built exactly as the full build builds it (`buildLawnChunk`, core), and during a stroke only the chunks the changed part of the stroke can reach are rebuilt and re-uploaded; materials and every other chunk's buffers stay. At release the mounted lawn already is the saved lawn, so there is no whole rebuild; cancel and refusals rebuild in full. The 2D plan keeps its drawing during a stroke. Tests compare a chunked session with a full build chunk by chunk (blades byte for byte, ground triangle for triangle, flowers) on strokes crossing many chunks, along the edge, beside paving, changing the flower count, on slopes, on 30 m² and 2,000 m². Measured in the standalone editor (hardware Chrome, quality high, a 3 s stroke): worst frame 63.8 → 39.8 ms on 600 m², 102.1 → 40.8 ms on 2,000 m², with no whole rebuild. Known limit: flower thinning is global, so on a flowering lawn the flowers are still rebuilt whole, spaced in time (worst frame 65 ms on 600 m², 80 ms on 2,000 m²); the per-sample budget check still plans the whole lawn (1.2 to 2.0 ms).

**The garden tools look and behave like the native tools.** While a tree, rock, hedge, planting bed, lawn or the lawn brush is in hand: the editor's own target on the ground with the tool's icon (3D bubble and plan badge), drafts in the shared preview colour with a filled area and a marker per point (they were green lines), a refused draft in the native red, plan drafts through the native draft layer. The target and the placed object follow the pointer's own ray to the terrain or a slab: four tools took their point on the active floor's plane, so with an upper level active the object landed metres from the pointer. A planting bed and a lawn also finish with a double-click; the finishing key shows on the folded hint card as soon as it applies (shared helper: the slab's and ceiling's cards too). Previews: a ghost of the tree and of the rock under the pointer through the native `applyGhost` treatment (green where it will land, red where a tree is refused), a translucent volume and the segment's length while a hedge is drawn. The five kinds use new icons in the native violet clay style (`apps/editor/public/icons/garden-*.webp`).

**Polygon handles no longer jump when grabbed (shared `PolygonEditor`).** A corner drag set the corner to the ground point under the pointer, but the handle stands above that ground, so the corner jumped at the press: 2.4 to 2.9 m for a 4 px drag at a grazing angle on a rock; 5 to 7 cm after. The drag now keeps the offset between the grabbed point and the ground under the pointer. This changes corner drags of slabs, ceilings, zones and the site as well as rocks and lawns; edge drags are unchanged. Rock and lawn handles now stand on their ground on terrain.

**Smaller things.** Inspector actions can be hidden (`visibleIf`); the rock's generator upgrade no longer shows on a rock that is already current. A selected lawn shows its area.

Test statements changed (all in tests added by this PR): the three "draft submits finite screen-space outlines" tests state the shared preview colour instead of green; the cursor-icon and target tests state the new image icons. No other existing test was edited.

Checks: on the merge before the last two commits (`356f0c67a`): nodes 6,109 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail, editor 2,774 pass / 0 fail, type checks clean but for the editor's two known errors, render bundle check passed. On the head `6245cc2ce`: the tree, rock and shared garden test folders 959 pass / 0 fail and the cursor-icon test; the full suites run in CI.

Not proven: the owner is testing these by hand as they land; after the last two commits (icons in the target, tree ghost) nobody but him has looked at the result in a browser. Not done: a target while moving a garden object; a viewer outline on a hovered or selected lawn; previews on the 2D plan; the lawn and the brush over a slab are still offset by the slab's height (an existing brush test states it).

## Known limits
Conical dormers keep a circular wall with planar window frames (no flashing on them). Covering detail applies to plain untextured planar roofs only; caps to one simple gable or hip segment. Garden symbols on the Site plan are not click targets. Adaptive default dormer proportions and a ridge clearance rule are left out: they would change the pinned behaviour of dormer creation.

title: viewer: saved capture point clouds draw as the live stream does
body:
## What does this PR do?

Saved capture point clouds now look like the live stream of the same scan. A saved cloud was drawn in the scene pass, so the daylight exposure, grade and bloom turned light-coloured points into a warm, glowing haze; the live cloud is drawn on the overlay layer and keeps its flat colours. `CapturePointCloudLayer` now draws its discs on `OVERLAY_LAYER` too.

Trade-off: like the live cloud, the saved cloud is no longer hidden by scene geometry, so it shows through walls built later. It stays a reference layer that can be hidden from the capture's layers.

## How to test

1. Open a project with a saved LiDAR scan whose point cloud layer is on, in the daylight look at high render quality.
2. The points read in their own colours, as they did while the phone streamed them; before, light points glowed into a cream haze.

title: Share viewer / bake: images painted from project files are missing from lod0.glb (surfaces render white)
body:
### What happened?

Images applied to an item slot with a native material texture pointing at a **project file** (`.../storage/v1/object/public/project-assets/<project>/files/<asset>/<name>.png|jpg`) render correctly in the editor, but they are missing from the published bake. In the share link (`/s/pvg_…` → `/viewer/<project>`), those surfaces are plain white. They sometimes appear on the very first load (most likely from the browser cache) and disappear on reload.

Inspecting the baked `project-bakes/<project>/<hash>/lod0.glb`: the item nodes are there, but the painted primitive has `baseColorFactor [1,1,1,1]` and **no `baseColorTexture` at all**. Catalog items in the same GLB keep their textures (KTX2), so texture handling works in general, just not for project-file textures.

### Where I think it breaks

From the public code, the client side looks correct:

- `BakeExporter` exports with `textures: 'reference'` (`packages/editor/src/components/editor/bake-exporter.tsx`).
- `getTexture()` in `packages/viewer/src/lib/materials.ts` stamps project-file textures as `kind: 'project-asset'`.
- `replaceReferencedTextures()` in `packages/editor/src/lib/glb-export.ts` swaps them for a 1×1 placeholder that carries `extras.pascalTextureRef`.
- `GlbScene` (`packages/viewer/src/components/viewer/glb-scene.tsx`) does not resolve `pascalTextureRef` itself.

So the step that turns placeholders back into real textures happens in the hosted bake pipeline. That pipeline seems to resolve `item-glb` / `library-material` refs but drops `project-asset` ones. Since the final GLB has no texture at all on these primitives (not even the placeholder), the reference is probably stripped rather than left unresolved.

One other possibility worth ruling out: if `storageUrl` is unset or different in the bake worker, `stampPascalTextureRef` returns `null`. In that case the texture would be embedded only if its image had finished loading by capture time (`materialTextureLoadState()`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Upload an image to the project files (`upload_project_file`, or from the editor).
2. Create an authored item with a `PlaneGeometry` mesh whose material is named `slot_print`.
3. `paint` the item, role `print`, with `{ properties: { color: '#ffffff' }, texture: { url: '<public project-assets URL of the image>' } }`.
4. The image shows in the editor (`view_scene` confirms it).
5. Save a checkpoint, publish it, and open a share link. The surface is white. Download `lod0.glb`: there is no `baseColorTexture` on that primitive.

Example (live): project `project_bGCQgwm3yZkaidS1`. The items are the shop sign `item_zjui4njgl840ssom` and three hanging posters, `item_qgte22uxdntaqs7d`, `item_bf808zemjfqevntf` and `item_y5q4szowjejepe1s`, all with `project-assets` textures.

The bake and the share viewer show project-file textures, as the editor does. The same should hold for catalog textures.

### Browser & OS

Chrome (stable), macOS 15.

### Additional context

- Workaround that does survive the bake: rebuilding the image as per-colour meshes (one plain material per colour, max 29 colours to stay under the 32-material limit). It works, but the result is visibly pixelated.

title: Public embed (/embed/<id>) draws authored objects as empty placeholder boxes
body:
### What happened?

A shared project's public link (`/embed/<id>`) draws every authored object (`add_object`, scripted windows, doors and columns) as an empty placeholder box. The same project opened in the editor (`/project/<id>`) draws them correctly.

### Why

`EmbedViewer` never configures an artifact store. `resolveArtifactUrl()` and `getArtifactStore().text()` then fall back to core's default in-memory store, which is empty in a fresh tab, so every `artifact://<sha256>` resolves to `null`. The page makes no `/api/artifacts/*` requests at all.

The editor calls `useLocalArtifactStore()` in `SceneLoader`; the embed page doesn't. The server side is already in place: the artifacts route lets an unauthenticated `GET` through for an artifact referenced by a shared scene (`isArtifactShared`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project with at least one authored object (`add_object`), on the standalone editor.
2. Turn on its public link with **Share**.
3. Open `/embed/<id>`: the object is a placeholder box. Open `/project/<id>`: it renders.

Reproduced on `main` (`cf37d32c`) with `bun dev`, and first seen on the CLI runtime 1.0.6.

### Expected behavior

The public link shows authored objects as the editor does.

I have a small fix ready and will open a PR that links here.

title: [Deps] TypeScript 7.0.2 everywhere (drop native-preview), esbuild 0.28.2
body:
## What does this PR do? Moves every compile and typecheck onto the stable TypeScript 7 native compiler and removes the `@typescript/native-preview` dev build. TS 6 stays only where a tool needs the JavaScript compiler API. Also bumps esbuild, whose new versions are trivially compatible with how this repo uses it. ### Versions | Package | Old | New | |---|---|---| | `@typescript/native-preview` (root, provided `tsgo`) | 7.0.0-dev.20260707.2 | **removed** | | `tsc` used by `dev` / `check-types` in core, editor, ui, geometry-script, viewer, nodes, mcp, ifc-converter | `tsgo` from the July dev build (in `dev` and some `check-types`) | `tsc` from `typescript@7.0.2` (already declared by each package) | | root `typescript` | `npm:@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2` | unchanged (see below) | | `@typescript/typescript6` (root, core) | 6.0.2 | unchanged; root scripts now import it explicitly | | `@repo/eslint-config` → `typescript` | 6.0.3 | unchanged | | `esbuild` (root) | ^0.25.12 | ^0.28.2 | ### End state for TS 7, and why one TS 6 alias stays - `typescript@7.0.2` has no classic JS API. Its root export is only `lib/version.cjs`, plus `typescript/unstable/*` IPC APIs. Its only binary is `tsc` (the Go compiler), and there is no `tsgo` and no `tsserver.js`. - **`@typescript/native-preview` is no longer needed.** Every package already depends on `typescript@7.0.2`, so the `tsgo …` scripts now call `tsc …`, which resolves to that package's own TS 7 binary. - **Root scripts that use the compiler API** (`ts.createSourceFile`, `forEachChild`, …) now import `@typescript/typescript6` directly, as `scripts/fix-node-esm-imports.ts` and `packages/core` already did. The affected scripts are `i18n-literals(.test).ts`, `i18n-codemod.ts` and `check-render-bundle.ts`. They no longer rely on the root alias. - **The root `typescript` → `@typescript/typescript6` alias stays, only for typescript-eslint.** typescript-eslint 8.72 requires `typescript >=4.8.4 <6.1.0` (used by `packages/ui` `eslint`). With bun's hoisted linker, its transitive dependency `ts-api-utils` is hoisted to the root and resolves the root `typescript`. I tried pointing the root at `7.0.2`. ESLint then crashed in `ts-api-utils` (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Intrinsic')`). Declaring `ts-api-utils` in `@repo/eslint-config` did not change bun's hoisting, and bun has no nested overrides. The alias can go once typescript-eslint supports TS 7, or if the repo moves to bun's isolated linker. That is out of scope here. - Biome / ultracite don't load TypeScript, so they are unaffected. ### Breaking changes and code changes - **TS 7.0** (native Go compiler; the JS API is removed, as are legacy options such as `moduleResolution: node10`, `baseUrl` path lookup and ES5 targets): source and tsconfigs needed no changes. `turbo check-types` and `turbo build` were already running TS 7.0.2 `tsc` for builds, and they pass with the stable compiler for the packages that used `tsgo`. The only code change is the explicit `@typescript/typescript6` import in the four scripts above, with Biome's import reordering. - **esbuild 0.26 / 0.27 / 0.28**: 0.27 makes the `binary` loader use `Uint8Array.fromBase64` and raises the minimum OS to Linux 3.2 and macOS 12. 0.28 adds integrity checks to the fallback binary download and moves to Go 1.26. The repo only calls the `build()` JS API in `scripts/check-render-bundle.ts` (plugins, splitting, metafile, no `binary` loader), so no code changes were needed. `@lingui/cli` already requires `esbuild ^0.28.1` and now shares the root copy. - `bun.lock`: removes the native-preview packages and moves esbuild with its platform binaries to 0.28.2. No other dependency changed. ## How to test 1. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` 2. `bun run check`: no errors. 3. `bun run check-types`: all 14 turbo tasks pass (run locally with `--force`). 4. `bun run test`: turbo tests and root script tests pass (81 root tests). 5. `bun run build && bun run check:render-bundle`: the build succeeds and the render-boundary check passes on esbuild 0.28.2. 6. `bun run i18n:check`: catalogs in sync (uses the TS 6 API through `i18n-literals.ts`). 7. `cd packages/ui && bun run lint`: ESLint with typescript-eslint passes, as on `main`. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [ ] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: mcp: check floor procedural-item footprints in collision checks
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #1255

`check_collisions` and `layout-clearance` (`collectOccupiedFootprints` and `findItemItemCollisions`, used by `verify_scene`, `furnish_room`, and `place_in_room`) previously filtered strictly on `node.type === 'item'`. As a result, overlapping floor-standing `procedural-item` nodes returned `status: "checked"` with empty `checkedItems`, `skippedItems`, and `collisions`, while `verify_scene` reported `hasIssues: false`.

I updated `@pascal-app/core` and `@pascal-app/mcp` so floor-standing `procedural-item` nodes participate in plan footprint and vertical-interval collision checks under the same contract as `item` nodes:

- **Plan footprint and inspection (`door-clearance.ts`, `item-space.ts`)**: Added `proceduralNodePlanCorners`, `proceduralNodePlanAabb`, `inspectProceduralItemPlanFootprint`, and `proceduralItemLevelPose` using `@pascal-app/core/procedural-items` directly so standalone MCP bridges without `@pascal-app/nodes` loaded still evaluate recipe bounds accurately, including off-center recipe datums under yaw, named surface attachment host chains, and consistent `unsupported_attachment` skipping for `wall-side` and `ceiling` mounting designs parented to a level.
- **Layout clearance, stacking, and pair roles (`layout-clearance.ts`, `furniture-kind.ts`)**: Included `procedural-item` in `collectOccupiedFootprints` and `findItemItemCollisions`, extended `designedTogether` to `ProceduralItemNode` so procedural dining/bedside pairs within the 0.08 m clearance band are not false-positived as `item_too_close`, added `proceduralHeightsInLevel` and shared floor-lift election (`electFloorPlacedLift`) so items hosted on or resting atop procedural surfaces still honor `STACK_TOLERANCE`, filtered flat procedural rug underlays, and guarded `ItemNode`-only helpers (`isWallDressing`, `itemSolidsInLevel`, `boxSolid`).

title: editor: restore saved camera projection and lens on open and view
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #1280

When opening a project with a saved camera view (`site.camera` or `building.camera`) or invoking the saved-camera view actions (`camera-controls:view`, Preview mode, and header/room `frameViewerNode` framing), only `position` and `target` were previously applied, and `handleNodeCapture` only recorded `position`, `target`, and `mode` without `fov` or `zoom`. Views saved in orthographic mode or with a custom lens therefore reopened in the active projection and lens instead of the saved one.

I updated the saved-camera capture and restore paths so projection and lens round-trip together while keeping older saved views backwards-compatible:

- **Saved camera capture and application (`packages/editor/src/components/editor/saved-camera-view.ts`, `custom-camera-controls.tsx`)**: `captureSavedCameraView` records `fov` in perspective mode and settled `zoom` in orthographic mode alongside `position`, `target`, and `mode`. `CustomCameraControls` switches `cameraMode` when needed and defers pose + lens application until the matching Three.js camera and `CameraControls` instance mount across project open (`openingFrame`), `camera-controls:view` (`handleNodeView`), Preview entry, and `camera-controls:frame` (`handleFrame`), while ignoring initial `null` to `level_0` floor hydration so off-floor saved targets are not reset to `targetY`.
- **Views bar / node framing (`packages/core/src/events/bus.ts`, `packages/viewer/src/ui/lib/viewer-selection.ts`)**: `CameraControlFrameEvent.pose` and `viewerFrameEvent` forward optional `mode`, `fov`, and `zoom` from `node.camera`, and `frameViewerCamera` applies perspective `fov` and orthographic `zoom` when present.
- **Stable default camera prop (`packages/viewer/src/components/viewer/viewer-camera.tsx`)**: Hoisted `DEFAULT_CAMERA_POSITION` so React Three Fiber prop reconciliation does not reset `camera.position` to `[10, 10, 10]` when `ViewerCamera` re-renders after a non-transitioned camera restore.
- **Public schema change (`packages/core/src/schema/camera.ts`, `camera.test.ts`)**: Changed `CameraSchema.mode` from `.default('perspective')` to `.optional()`. For `@pascal-app/core` consumers and MCP clients reading `node.camera.mode`, legacy `{ position, target }` cameras now parse with `mode: undefined` instead of `'perspective'` so restoring an older saved view preserves the active projection and lens. Added `packages/core/src/schema/camera.test.ts` verifying legacy cameras parse without `mode` and round-trip cleanly.
- **Backwards compatibility**: Older saved views that omit `mode`, `fov`, or `zoom` keep the active projection and lens unchanged and apply `position` and `target` as before.

## How to test

1. Run `bunx biome check` on the modified files in `packages/core`, `packages/viewer`, and `packages/editor` (0 errors, 0 warnings).
2. Run `bunx turbo run build check-types test --filter=@pascal-app/core --filter=@pascal-app/viewer --filter=@pascal-app/editor` and `bun run check:render-bundle`.
3. Verify the new `#1280` round-trip suite in `packages/editor/src/components/editor/saved-camera-view.test.tsx`: perspective views with custom `fov` and orthographic views with custom `zoom` round-trip across capture, project open, `camera-controls:view`, and `frameViewerNode`, while legacy `{ position, target }` views preserve the current projection and lens.
