title: editor: thumbnails and snapshots keep the scans the view shows
body:
## What does this PR do?

A project whose only 3D is a capture (a point cloud, a mesh, a robot's walk) saved an empty frame as its thumbnail while the viewport showed the scan. Two things kept it out:

- every capture hid all `scan` nodes before it rendered;
- a scan's point cloud draws on `OVERLAY_LAYER` (since #1294), which no capture camera looks at.

A picture of the person's own view now keeps the scans that view shows: the autosave thumbnail, Settings > Generate thumbnail, and viewport or area snapshots. Their point clouds are lifted to `SCENE_LAYER` for the frame and put back after it (`temporarilyShowScanPoints` in the viewer). A scan the person hid stays hidden, and so does a cloud that isolation holds back. Guides and spawn points stay out, as before.

A view the caller poses itself (a sheet's orthographic or perspective view, an agent's, an authored shot's `cameraPose`) is unchanged: it still leaves scans out. The rule is `capturesScans` in `thumbnail-generator.tsx`.

Trade-off: a design traced over a scan that is still visible now shows the scan in its thumbnail too. Hiding the scan in the view takes it out.

## How to test

1. Open a project that holds a point-cloud scan and little or nothing built.
2. Settings > Thumbnail > Generate thumbnail. The new option shows the cloud as the viewport does. Before this change it was bare ground.
3. The viewport's cloud looks the same after the capture as before it.
4. Hide the scan in the scene tree and generate again: the scan is not in the picture.
5. `bun test packages/viewer/src/lib/scan-points.test.ts packages/editor/src/components/editor/thumbnail-generator.test.ts` passes.

title: Item panel: edit physical width / height / depth directly
body:
From discussion #830: when an agent or a user places an item with the wrong size, the only fix today is the **Scale** section of the item panel (`packages/nodes/src/item/panel.tsx`). The **Dimensions** row under it (W/H/D) is read-only, so to get "0.9 m wide" you have to work out the scale factor by hand.

### Proposal

Make the W/H/D values in the item panel editable:

- On edit, set `scale[axis] = requested / asset.dimensions[axis]`.
- Add a uniform / aspect lock. When it's on, apply the same factor to all three axes; when it's off, change only the edited axis.
- Accept the usual measurement input (respecting the metric/imperial setting, like the other unit-aware inputs).
- Guard against missing or zero `asset.dimensions`: fall back to the existing scale controls.
- Keep it in the shared item panel so hosted and standalone editors behave the same.

### Done when

- Typing a width/height/depth updates the item's scale and the 3D/2D views.
- Undo restores the previous scale in one step.
- A unit test covers the scale math, including the lock and the zero-dimension guard.
- A short screen recording is in the PR.

title: viewer,editor: defer wall T-junction repair to export preparation
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes #1273

Previously, `finishWallFaces` ran `repairWallTJunctions` on every wall geometry build, including every live rebuild during drawing and editing. The repair exists to prevent dotted light leaks once quantized by GLB/export bakes, while the live renderer draws full-precision float geometry.

I updated `@pascal-app/viewer` and `@pascal-app/editor` so live wall rebuilds defer T-junction repair and export preparation runs it on demand on cloned meshes:

- **Explicit repair mode (`packages/viewer/src/systems/wall/wall-system.tsx`, `packages/viewer/src/index.ts`)**: Added `export type WallTJunctionMode = 'repaired' | 'deferred'` and an optional trailing `tJunctions: WallTJunctionMode = 'repaired'` parameter on `generateExtrudedWall` (threaded through `finishWallFaces` and `mergeWallTerrainFill`). Because the default stays `'repaired'`, every existing caller, golden hash, and T-junction test keeps its existing behavior.
- **Deferred live rebuilds (`updateWallGeometry`)**: Both the live render wall mesh and its `collision-mesh` pass `'deferred'`, skipping `repairWallTJunctions` during interactive editing and marking `geometry.userData.wallTJunctions = 'deferred'`.
- **On-demand export repair (`repairDeferredWallTJunctions`, `packages/editor/src/lib/glb-export.ts`)**: Exported `repairDeferredWallTJunctions(mesh)`, which runs `repairWallTJunctions` on marked meshes, preserves material groups and non-marker `userData`, recomputes normals and level-relative planar UVs (`applyWorldPlanarWallUVs`), refreshes bounds, and clears `userData.wallTJunctions`. `finishSceneExportPreparation` (shared across GLB, USDZ, STL, 3MF, and viewer bakes) invokes it on cloned deferred wall meshes (cloning first if a geometry is shared) so exports remain crack-free without mutating live viewer meshes.
- **Tests**: Extended `packages/viewer/src/systems/wall/wall-t-junctions.test.ts` to verify deferred marking and `repairDeferredWallTJunctions`, and added `packages/editor/src/lib/glb-export-wall-t-junctions.test.ts` building a T-junction of walls with a window through `runWallBuildFrame`, exporting via `prepareSceneForExport` + `GLTFExporter`, and parsing back with `GLTFLoader` to verify live meshes stay deferred while exported GLB meshes have 0 T-junctions and preserved area, normals, and UVs.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes #1155

I addressed all seven deferred follow-up items from the #1148 i18n review:

- **Placeholder validation depth and stricter tag check (`scripts/i18n.ts`, `scripts/i18n.test.ts`)**:
  - Expanded tag scanning to treat any `<` followed by a letter, `!`, or `/` as a tag (catching `<img/src=x onerror=...>`, `<svg/onload=...>`, `<!-- -->`, and unclosed tags), plus Lingui numbered tags (`<0>`, `</0>`, `<0/>`), while ignoring spaced math comparisons like `Width < 5 m`.
  - Added stack-based tag nesting validation (`tagNestingErrors`) to catch broken nesting (`<0><1>...</0></1>`, `</0>...<0>`, mismatched or unclosed tags) and renumbered tags (`<0>` changed to `<1>`).
  - Added ICU `select` branch validation (`selects`) to catch missing or removed branches and missing `other` branches in both `select` and `plural`/`selectordinal` selectors.
- **Per-locale entry points (`packages/editor/src/i18n/locales.ts`, `locales/*/index.ts`, `packages/editor/package.json`, `apps/editor/app/layout.tsx`)**:
  - Added individual per-locale entry points (`@pascal-app/editor/locales/{en,es,fr,ja,zh-CN}`) and replaced top-level static imports of all five catalogs in `locales.ts` with dynamic per-locale loading (`loadBundledLocale`, `resolveBundledLocale`, `registerBundledCatalog`).
  - Updated `apps/editor/app/layout.tsx` and `client-bootstrap.tsx` to load only the active locale on the server and hand that single catalog to client hydration (avoiding both bundling all five locales up front and hydration mismatches).
- **Plural rules for fallback messages (`packages/core/src/i18n/registry.ts`, `i18n.test.tsx`)**:
  - Updated `PascalI18n` to resolve each message against a per-fallback-locale Lingui runtime so a `pt` message used under `pt-PT` evaluates with `pt` plural rules (`0 -> one`) while a `pt-PT` override uses `pt-PT` plural rules (`0 -> other`).
- **In-app `?lang=` navigation (`apps/editor/app/client-bootstrap.tsx`, `apps/editor/lib/ui-locale.ts`)**:
  - Added a `<Suspense>`-wrapped `LocaleQuerySync` hook using `useSearchParams()` and `resolveClientLangNavigation` so client-side navigation to `?lang=...` switches the active language and dynamically loads its catalog without a full reload, while preserving the SSR default locale on back/internal navigation.
- **Full `proxy()` tests (`apps/editor/proxy.test.ts`)**:

title: Unavailable view tab, room-scoped wall finishes, set_finish_script
body:
## What does this PR do?

- **Unavailable views get a tab.** A pane restored onto a view whose plugin isn't in the project (a Home Designer elevation opened in another project) now shows a selected amber tab named after the view, with a close button, and the pane offers **Close this view**. Both go back to 3D, or 2D when the other pane already shows 3D. The state waits until the project has loaded plus 0.6 s, so plugins that register their views as they load don't flash it.
- **A room's wall finish stops at the room.** Wall face scripts take an optional `u0`/`u1` stretch. `author_scene` builds a room's `wallCode` only on that room's stretch of each wall, so a bathroom's tile no longer runs into the bedrooms along a shared wall; rooms with the same code share one build. Wet-room, room and default-finish readings, the paint refusal and the skirting gap follow the stretch. Old scenes load unchanged (no stretch = whole face).
- **`set_finish_script`** (chat and MCP, one contract): builds a three.js finish on what already stands — a room's walls (only its own stretch, optionally to `toHeight`), a room's floor, one wall face or a slab's top. Core plans each surface and its module inputs; the host compiles once per surface. A face another room's script covers is skipped and named; `remove: true` takes a finish off.

## How to test

1. Open a project with Home Designer, open an elevation from Views, then open a project without Home Designer: the bar shows the amber elevation tab after loading (no flash during load); close it or press **Close this view** to return to 3D.
2. With an agent, in a house where a bathroom and bedroom share a wall: `set_finish_script` on the bathroom with `surface: 'walls'`, a tile module and `toHeight: 2.1`. The tile stops at the partition and at 2.1 m; the bedroom keeps its paint. `remove: true` takes it off.
3. `author_scene` with a room `wallCode` on a wall that runs past the room: the build covers only that room's stretch.

Ran: `bun test` in core (`src`, 7317 pass), mcp (full, 1532 pass), `editor` views tests; `tsgo --noEmit` for core, editor, geometry-script and mcp; `bun run i18n:check`.

## What does this PR do?

Extends the Comment (`point-ask`) tool so it works seamlessly across **2D Plan**, **Split (2D + 3D)**, **Walkthrough**, and **Drone** modes — both in edit mode and when entering Walkthrough/Drone from Preview — and records/restores 2D viewport camera poses accurately.

### Key changes
- **2D Plan & Split parity**:
  - Added `EditorFloorplanContext` bridge (`packages/editor/src/components/editor/floorplan-context-bridge.ts`) exposing 2D world/screen projection, picking, orthographic camera pose, and SVG region capture.
  - Added `applyFloorplanCameraPose` and `planOwnsNavigation()` guard to restore 2D comment camera poses cleanly without self-echo update loops (`floorplan-panel.tsx`, `custom-camera-controls.tsx`).
  - Added `PointContext.viewport?: '2d' | '3d'` (`packages/core/src/agent-operations/point-context.ts`) and per-viewport projection/pins/outlines/bubble placement across 2D-only, 3D-only, and Split layouts.
- **Walkthrough & Drone parity**:
  - Wired `externalOverlayActive` and `suspendOnUnlock` in `LiveWalkthroughController` so pressing `C` releases pointer lock cleanly without exiting Walkthrough/Drone, zeroes movement/drone velocity, and restores suspended state on `Esc`.
  - Mounted `PointAskLayer`, `HelperManager`, and `EditorThreeContextBridge` for Preview Walkthrough & Drone (`PreviewStage`), with `ViewerOutlineSync` hover/region outlines while `hoverHighlightMode === 'point'` and whole-building cross-level picking & pin visibility.
  - Updated `WalkthroughHud` and `DroneHud` so the `C comment` hint remains visible and clickable even when the cursor is freed via `P` (`suspended`).

  - Added unit coverage in `point-ask-modes.test.ts` and `walkthrough-hud.test.tsx`.

## How to test

1. Switch to **2D** or **Split (2D + 3D)** view, press `C` (or click the Comment tool), click an element or drag a region on the 2D plan, and post a comment.
2. Enter **Preview → Walkthrough** or **Preview → Drone**:

title: slab: add planar slope support (direction and pitch)
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds planar sloped slab support for manual solid slabs (ramps, driveways, sloped terraces, and flat-roof drainage falls), following the design suggested in #260 (Relates to #260; leaves roof-driven wall tops open in #260).

- **Schema and pure plane math (`@pascal-app/core`)**: Adds optional `slope: { direction, pitch }` (`pitch` in `0..45` degrees, `direction` uphill azimuth in degrees where `0 = +X` and `90 = +Z`) to `SlabNode`, keeping legacy flat scenes unchanged (E-003). `packages/core/src/systems/slab/slab-slope.ts` anchors `slab.elevation` at the low-edge projection (`minProj`) of the stored polygon so adding slope or extending the high edge never sinks a ramp below the floor plane, and keeps recessed slabs and reconciler-owned floor plates flat.
- **Position-dependent support, raycasting, and dirtying (`@pascal-app/core`)**: Updates `selectSlabSupportForItem`, `SpatialGridManager` (`getSlabElevationAt`, `getSlabSupportForItem`, `getPointedSupportSurface` exact analytical ray-plane intersection, `getSupportCandidatesForFootprint`, `getHostSlabElevationForFootprint`), `floor-placed-elevation`, `usage-field` (`floorUnder` and `approx` region tagging), `layout-clearance`, `procedural-items/query`, `clampSlabElevationForWalls`, and `spatial-grid-sync` dirty triggers so floor-placed items and cursor picks follow the inclined surface live.
- **3D solid and terrain-fill geometry (`@pascal-app/viewer`, `@pascal-app/nodes`)**: Extrudes coplanar sloped top/bottom caps, sloped outer/hole side walls, and per-vertex sloped `fillToTerrain` skirts (`buildTerrainPerimeterFillGeometry`). Keeps top vs. side face splitting clean up to 45 degrees (`cos(45°) > 0.5`).
- **2D floor plan, 3D handles, and Inspector UI (`@pascal-app/nodes`, `i18n`)**: Draws an uphill direction arrow on sloped slabs in 2D floor plans, places 3D thickness/base handles on the sloped surface, clears `slope` when toggling a slab to `recessed`, and adds a **Slope** section to `SlabPanel` (Pitch, Direction, Rotate 90°, Flip 180°, live Grade % and total rise readout, and Flat / Drainage 2% / Ramp 1:12 / Driveway 12% presets) with extracted and compiled Lingui catalogs.
- **IFC export, MCP, and agent authoring (`@pascal-app/ifc-converter`, `@pascal-app/mcp`, `skills/pascal-3d`)**: Exports sloped slabs as inclined `IFCSLAB` mesh geometry rather than flat `SweptSolid`, evaluates `node-world-point` on the sloped surface centroid, accepts optional `slope` in `author_scene` using shared `measurement('angle', 'deg')` notation, and documents the field in `skills/pascal-3d/SKILL.md`.

## How to test

1. Select a manual solid slab (or create one via the Slab tool) and open its inspector panel.
2. In the **Slope** section, pick a preset (such as `Ramp 1:12` or `Driveway (12%)`) or drag **Pitch** and **Direction**: the slab top and underside tilt from the low edge at `elevation`, **Grade** updates with the percentage and rise, and **Rotate 90°** / **Flip 180°** reorient the uphill direction.
3. Enable **Follows terrain** on a sloped ramp: the perimeter fill skirt meets the sloped underside cleanly.
4. Place floor items or columns at the low, middle, and high ends of the ramp: each lifts to the exact sloped surface height at its plan position and updates immediately when slope changes.
5. Switch to **2D** or **Split** view: sloped slabs display an uphill direction arrow that flips immediately when **Flip 180°** is clicked.
6. Run the automated verification suite I executed:
   - `bun run check`
   - `bun run check-types`
   - `bun run i18n:check`
   - `bun run skills:validate`
   - `bun run check:render-bundle`
   - `bun run --cwd packages/core test` (7,692 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail)
   - `bun run --cwd packages/viewer test` (1,769 pass, 0 fail)
   - `bun run --cwd packages/editor test` (2,792 pass, 0 fail)
   - `bun run --cwd packages/mcp test` (1,576 pass, 0 fail)
   - `bun test packages/nodes/src/slab packages/nodes/src/index.test.ts packages/ifc-converter/tests scripts/i18n.test.ts scripts/i18n-provider.test.ts scripts/i18n-literals.test.ts apps/editor/proxy.test.ts`
   - `bun run --cwd apps/editor build && bun run --cwd apps/editor smoke` (8/8 pass)

## Screenshots / screen recording

Verified live in Chrome (WebGPU) against the Next.js 16 production build (`node next start`) with zero console or page errors across 3D, 2D, and Split views:

**3D view showing a 12° entry ramp with `fillToTerrain` skirt meeting a flat upper landing, three columns stepping up the sloped surface, a hosted balustrade railing climbing the ramp, and a 15° sloped terrace with a rectangular cutout:**

![3D view of sloped ramp with fillToTerrain skirt, stepped columns, hosted railing, and sloped terrace with cutout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kruschdev/editor/pr-1318-assets/pr1318-3d-hero.png)

**2D floor plan and Slab inspector Slope controls (`Pitch`, `Direction`, `Rotate 90°`, `Flip 180°`, live `Grade` and rise readout, and presets), with uphill arrows anchored cleanly inside the solid slab regions (avoiding the terrace cutout):**

![2D floor plan with uphill slope arrows and Slab inspector Slope section](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kruschdev/editor/pr-1318-assets/pr1318-2d-floorplan.png)

**Split 2D + 3D view immediately after clicking `Flip 180°` (both the 2D uphill arrow and 3D ramp/railing/columns reorient live to `180°`):**

title: terrain: add planar ground slope, slope brush, and two-point grade picker
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds deterministic ground slope and elevation controls to the existing terrain heightfield (`site.terrain`) with zero schema changes, complementing the existing `raise`, `lower`, `flatten`, and `smooth` sculpting verbs.

- **Pure planar slope and two-point grade math (`@pascal-app/core`)**: Adds `packages/core/src/lib/terrain-slope.ts` with `clampTerrainSlopePitch` (`0..45°`), `normalizeTerrainSlopeDirection` (`0° = +X`, `90° = +Z`), `terrainSlopeGradePercent`, `compileTerrainSlopePlane` (hoisting trig out of per-sample loops), `resolveLotSlopePlane` (`center` datum anchor matching USGS DEM imports or `low-edge` anchor), `terrainSlopeBaseElevationForPlane`, `terrainSlopeElevationRange`, `deriveTerrainSlopeFromPoints`, and `buildSlopedTerrainField`.
- **5th `slope` brush verb (`@pascal-app/core`)**: Extends `TerrainVerb` in `packages/core/src/lib/terrain-brush.ts` with `'slope'` using the same saturating snapshot-and-falloff kernel (re-crossing strokes never compound). Exports `BaseTerrainVerb` so `useEditor.terrainVerb` stays narrowed to the four original verbs for full type and runtime compatibility with `@webxr/plugin`, while editor consumers read `selectActiveTerrainVerb` and `setActiveTerrainVerb`.
- **Whole-lot grading, two-point A -> B picker, cursor feedback, and UI (`@pascal-app/editor`, `i18n`)**:
  - Adds `slopeSite` (grades the full padded heightfield in a single undo step and drops in-flight live strokes) and `resolveSlopeStrokePlane` in `packages/editor/src/lib/terrain-sculpt.ts`.
  - Adds a teal (`#14b8a6`) brush ring color, a draped uphill direction arrow inside the brush ring (hidden when pitch is `0°`), an amber A -> B guide line, and a live grade `%` readout in the cursor pill during two-point picking (`TerrainBrushCursor`).
  - Adds the **Slope** tab in `TerrainSculptPanel` (`Flat`, `2%`, `5%`, `1:12`, and `12%` presets, `Pitch`, wrapping `Direction` with `Rotate 90°` and `Flip 180°`, `Elevation`, `Anchor: Center` / `Low edge`, live `Grade %` and lot elevation range readout, two-point `Pick A -> B` eyedropper with locked anchor indicator, and `Slope lot`), updates `useTerrainPanelRows`, and extracts/compiles Lingui catalogs across all 5 locales.

## How to test

1. Open any project, switch to **Build -> Outdoor -> Terrain**, and select the **Slope** tab.
2. Pick a preset (such as `5%` or `12%`) or adjust **Pitch**, **Direction** (`Rotate 90°` / `Flip 180°`), **Elevation**, and **Anchor** (`Center` vs `Low edge`), then click **Slope lot**. Verify the terrain grades smoothly across the lot, the readout shows the exact grade `%` and min-to-max elevation range, and `Ctrl+Z` / `Cmd+Z` undoes it in a single step.
3. Hover the cursor over the lot with a non-zero pitch: confirm the teal brush ring draws an uphill direction arrow pointing along **Direction** (and hides the arrow when **Flat** / `0°` is selected). Drag across the lot to locally grade along the inclined plane.
4. Click the eyedropper button (**Pick A -> B slope**), click a start point on the ground, move to a second point (confirming the amber guide line and live grade `%` pill), and click to lock the derived pitch, direction, lot base elevation, and plane anchor.
5. Run the automated verification suite I executed:
   - `bun run check` (0 errors across 4,595 files)
   - `bun run check-types` (14/14 packages pass, including `apps/editor` and `@webxr/plugin`)
   - `bun run i18n:check` (5/5 catalogs in sync, literal guard pass)
   - `bun run skills:validate` (75/75 pass)
   - `bun test packages/core/src/lib/terrain*.test.ts packages/core/src/store/use-live-terrain.test.ts` (147/147 pass)
   - `bun run --cwd packages/core test` (7,688 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail)
   - `bun run --cwd packages/editor test` (2,797 pass, 0 fail)
   - `bun test scripts/i18n.test.ts scripts/i18n-provider.test.ts scripts/i18n-literals.test.ts apps/editor/proxy.test.ts` (81/81 pass)
   - `bun run --cwd apps/editor build && bun run --cwd apps/editor smoke` (8/8 pass)
   - `bun run check:render-bundle` (pass)

## Screenshots / screen recording

Verified live in Chrome against the Next.js 16 production build with 0 console or page errors:

**1. Whole-lot planar grading (`Slope lot`) on a 12% hillside lot:** shows the **Slope** panel controls (`Flat / 2% / 5% / 1:12 / 12%` presets, `Pitch`, `Direction` with `Rotate 90°` / `Flip 180°`, `Elevation`, `Anchor: Center` / `Low edge`, live `Grade 11.9%` and `0'0" -> 9'5"` range readout, and `Slope lot`), 3D topographic contours, a hillside pavilion with `fillToTerrain` deck foundation, and the teal brush ring with draped uphill direction arrow and elevation pill.

Two-point `A -> B` grade picker on a terraced hillside ramp:** clicking near the foot of the carved ramp and moving uphill drapes the amber `A -> B` guide line and brush ring across the terrain, displays the live elevation and grade readout pill (`H 3'7" · 8.6%`), and shows the contextual `Pick end point to match slope` HUD prompt.

title: [Discovery] Prepare Pascal plugin for Claude and ChatGPT directories
body:
## What does this PR do? Gets the public `pascal-agent-skills` package ready to submit to Anthropic's plugin directory and OpenAI's ChatGPT/Codex plugin directory, following each directory's current docs. Nothing is submitted or published. **Listing copy.** All descriptors (root `plugin.json`, Codex, Claude, Cursor, Gemini, and both marketplaces) now describe what Pascal actually does: model a building, turn a floor plan into an editable 3D model, explore a renovation change, validate and save it, and share a 3D editor link. Furniture fit is no longer promoted. The `furniture-fit` skill is still bundled, because the validator requires every packaged skill to be listed. The copy says models are design aids, not measured surveys, engineering drawings or permit documents. Other listing changes: - OpenAI short description: "Model and share 3D buildings". - OpenAI category changes from Developer Tools to Productivity, matching the Claude and Codex marketplaces. **ChatGPT / OpenAI package** - New `packaging/chatgpt/mcp.json` declares only the hosted server, `https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. OAuth is declared under `extensions["com.openai"].auth` as `{ type: "oauth", client: { mode: "cimd" } }`, with no headers. `bun run plugin:chatgpt` (`scripts/stage-chatgpt-plugin.ts`) stages it as the ZIP's root `mcp.json` alongside `plugin.json`, `LICENSE`, `skills/` and the two icons, and writes `dist/pascal-agent-skills--chatgpt.zip`. - The repository root `mcp.json` stays the local `pascal mcp connect` server, unchanged from `main`. Codex Git-marketplace installs read it, and Pascal's OAuth server refuses the Codex client: - Codex's MCP OAuth (`codex-rs/rmcp-client/src/oauth_client_registration.rs`; the 0.172.0 binary embeds the same URL) sends the CIMD client `https://chatgpt.com/oauth/codex/client.json` with a loopback redirect `http://127.0.0.1:/callback`. Its only fallback is DCR, which Pascal doesn't offer. - Pascal's authorize endpoint answers that identity with `400 invalid_client`. ChatGPT's pinned client gets `302` to `/connect`. - Codex users keep the documented `codex mcp add --bearer-token-env-var PASCAL_API_KEY` path for hosted projects. - Adds `supportURL: https://editor.pascal.app/contact`, the page Pascal's site lists as its technical-support contact. **Claude package (`skills/`)** - `pascal-hosted` in `skills/.mcp.json` is now the plain `https://editor.pascal.app/api/mcp` URL with no headers, so Claude, Claude Desktop, Cowork and Claude Code connect through the server's OAuth (CIMD). The plugin no longer asks for a `pascal_api_key`, and the Claude MCP policy rejects any header or `userConfig`. The manual `claude mcp add --header` command stays documented as the API-key alternative. - Adds `icon` (`skills/.claude-plugin/icon.png`, a copy of the existing 1024×1024 `assets/pascal-mark-plate.png`) plus `documentationUrl`, `supportUrl`, `privacyPolicyUrl` and `termsOfServiceUrl`. The directory captures the icon only once, at first save or submission. - `skills/README.md` is the directory listing text. It now opens with what the plugin does and a "What the plugin runs and sends" section for the security scan. **Publishing suite.** `plugin-evals/publishing-cases.json` now has: - a `ready` list, which includes the live ChatGPT OAuth acceptance, and owner-tagged `blockers` (org verification, domain challenge, portal scan, reviewer account, video and submission, all human steps); - exactly 5 positive cases, each with `tools_triggered`, and 3 negative cases, the split OpenAI's initial MCP review requires. It previously had 6 and 5, mostly about furniture. The release notes say Architect needs a host that has been granted Architect access, and that ChatGPT's connection doesn't get it. **Tool annotations.** All 106 tools the MCP package registers already had a `title` and explicit `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint` and `openWorldHint` values that fit OpenAI's guideline 6.3, so no values changed. The gaps were in the checks: - The `tools/list` regression never listed the 10 tools that only register with hosted executors, and those are tools ChatGPT's scan will see. It now lists them and requires a title on every tool. - The annotation policy and packet now cover all 106 tools (they had 96). - The stale "65 tools" count is corrected. **Validator** (`scripts/validate-skills.ts`): - root `mcp.json` must be the local server, identical to Claude's; - `packaging/chatgpt/mcp.json` must be exactly the `server.json` remote with OAuth (CIMD) and no headers; - `supportURL` is required; - the Claude listing URLs must match the OpenAI ones, and the icon must be a PNG inside `skills/`; - the publishing suite must have exactly 5 positive and 3 negative cases, `tools_triggered` on positive cases, and a `ready` list; - the Claude hosted server must be a plain URL with no headers, and the Claude plugin must declare no `userConfig`; - the Gemini command is compared with the Claude local server. **Version.** The bundle goes from 0.1.11 to 0.1.12. Git-marketplace clients only pick up changes when the version changes, and both directories ask for a bump on each release. Nothing is tagged or published. npm packages and `server.json` are untouched. **Known schema lag.** The published Agent Plugins `mcp.schema.json` 1.0.0 doesn't yet allow `extensions` on a server entry, but OpenAI's packaging docs place OAuth exactly there with that `$schema`. `plugin.json` and the root `mcp.json` validate against their schemas; `packaging/chatgpt/mcp.json` validates once that one OpenAI object is removed. ## How to test 1. `bun run skills:validate` passes: 71 tests, and the validator reports manifests at 0.1.12. 2. `claude plugin validate ./skills --strict` (Claude Code 2.1.332) reports "These checks found nothing to report" and "Validation passed"; `claude plugin validate . --strict` passes for the marketplace. 3. `cd packages/mcp && bun test src/tools/read-tool-annotations.test.ts` passes. It lists 106 tools with titles and the expected hints. 4. With an isolated `CODEX_HOME`, run `codex plugin marketplace add `, then `codex plugin add pascal-agent-skills@pascal`. It installs 0.1.12, loads the three skills, and its cached `mcp.json` is the local `pascal mcp connect` server. 5. `bun run plugin:chatgpt` writes `dist/pascal-agent-skills-0.1.12-chatgpt.zip`, whose root `mcp.json` is the hosted OAuth server. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: [Discovery] Trim the ChatGPT plugin ZIP and zip without the zip CLI
body:
## What does this PR do? Follow-up to #1322 covering the maintainer's non-blocking notes. The version stays 0.1.12 (unpublished): nothing an installed client loads changes. - **Leaner ChatGPT ZIP.** The new `scripts/chatgpt-plugin-package.ts` lists exactly what `bun run plugin:chatgpt` packages: - included: `plugin.json`, `packaging/chatgpt/mcp.json` as the root `mcp.json`, `LICENSE`, the two listing icons, and only the `pascal-3d` skill; - left out: `skills/.mcp.json`, `skills/.claude-plugin/`, `skills/.cursor-plugin/`, the `.clawhubignore` files, `skills/README.md` and `skills/VALIDATION.md` (Claude listing and repo docs whose links point outside the ZIP); - also left out: the `architect` skill, because its tools need the `architect:run` scope and ChatGPT's connection isn't granted it; - also left out: the `furniture-fit` skill, because furniture fit isn't promoted in directory listings. `pascal-3d` uses either skill only "if installed". - ZIP entry names always use `/`, including on Windows. - **Validator.** It checks that inventory: - the skill list is exactly `pascal-3d`, so adding `architect` or `furniture-fit` makes it fail; - `mcp.json` comes from `packaging/chatgpt/`; - the required files are present; - there is no other skill, no dotfile and no loose `skills/` file. - **No `zip` executable needed.** When `zip` isn't on `PATH`, the stage script writes a deflate ZIP with `node:zlib` (`deflateRawSync` and `crc32`) instead of throwing. title: viewer: scan point outlines in place, saved clouds read their PLY
body:
Two viewer fixes for capture point clouds, needed by the Capture point recorder work in private-editor.

**Outline of a scan's points.** Hovering or selecting a scan outlined its instanced point sprites with the plain sprite mask, so every point became a 1 m quad at the origin (tens of thousands deep) and the editor dropped to ~30 fps when zoomed over a scan. The mask and the fallback depth sprite now use the cloud's own position, scale, rotation and cut-out nodes.

**Saved clouds read their PLY.** Three's `PLYLoader` converts vertex colours from sRGB to linear, so a cloud loaded from its file drew darker than the same points streamed live. A small reader (`point-cloud-ply.ts`) parses binary (either endian) or ASCII PLY and keeps colours as bytes / 255. Past the layer's cap it keeps the first points instead of every Nth, since capture clouds are stored shuffled.

## Validation
- `bun test src/capture/point-cloud-layer.test.ts src/lib/merged-outline-node.test.ts`: 23 pass
- `tsgo --noEmit` on `packages/viewer`: clean; biome: clean
- On device, through the private app: scans checked on the phone and their clouds viewed in the editor after upload

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Point caps use **`firstPoints`** instead of evenly striding geometry, on the assumption capture PLYs are stored shuffled.

title: Read-only viewer: keep sun and shadows on without slowing first view (daylight build, static shadow maps, batching at first build)
body:
### Problem or motivation

We use `@pascal-app/viewer` 1.1.6 read-only, so homeowners can see finished house designs. For them, sunlight and shade are part of the design: which rooms get morning light, where the yard is shaded, whether a porch keeps out summer sun. Today we have to turn shadows off, and the first view is still about 3.8 s for a large house (about 5,500 meshes, 5,450 draw calls, 509k triangles). That's a local production build in Chrome on an Apple M-series GPU at 1440×900 @2x. Frame rate (50, the cap) and GPU memory (about 190 MB) are fine. The costs:

1. **Daylight rooms after scene-ready.** About 0.5 s of daylight-room build and material recompile lands in a single frame right after the scene reports ready, so any "first frame drawn" mark waits for it. With daylight off, the first view is about 1 s sooner.
2. **Shadows.** We disable them, because each change costs an extra render pass plus soft-shadow settling.
3. **Mesh count from part builders.** Measured by stripping each kind out of the scene:

| Part | Meshes | First view without it |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Louvered shutters (a box mesh per slat) | 1,146 | about 0.3 s sooner |
| Windows, all | 1,700 | about 0.7 s sooner |
| Doors (about 33 meshes each) | 1,650 | about 0.5 s sooner |
| Columns, piers, posts (rounded, bevelled shafts) | 660 | about 0.5 s sooner |
| Cabinets | 680 | about 0.3 s sooner |

The viewer already batches doors, windows, columns and cabinets, but only after the scene has been idle for about 180 ms. That is after the first view, so it doesn't shorten it.

### Proposed solution

- Build the daylight rooms and their material recompile before the scene is marked ready, or spread that work across several frames.
- In a read-only scene, render the shadow map only when the sun or the scene changes, not every frame. Don't let soft-shadow settling hold up the first view; refine it afterwards.
- Merge or instance repeated sub-parts as they are built (shutter slats, window and door frame pieces and hardware, column shafts). Alternatively, give read-only viewers an option to batch on the first build, since no edits will invalidate the batches.
- Let the host set true north and the site location, and scrub date and time (a sun study across the day and the seasons) without a scene rebuild. This relates to #362.

### Alternatives considered

On our side, we hold back doors in interior walls until after the first view, which saves about 0.4 s of build time. Holding back more isn't workable: anything added later directly under a level makes the whole level rebuild on screen. Preloading the part modules up front made no measurable difference.

### Additional context

- Related: #588 (batching static walls per level), #362 (north direction).
- We're happy to share our measurement script or test a branch.

title: Document the licence and source of the bundled 3D assets (models, materials, HDRI, sounds)
body:
### Problem or motivation

Problem / motivation:
The repository LICENSE (MIT) covers the code, but there is no licence or source information for the assets in apps/editor/public: the item models (items/), materials and textures (material/), the HDRI (hdri/venice_sunset_1k.hdr) and the sound effects (audios/sfx/). Anyone building a commercial product on @pascal-app/editor can't tell whether these assets may be used commercially or how to credit them. This was asked in Discussion #844, which was closed without an answer.

Proposed solution:
Add an ASSETS.md (or a LICENSE file in apps/editor/public) that states:
1. the licence of each asset group, and whether commercial use in a hosted SaaS is allowed;
2. the original source of third-party assets (e.g. Poly Haven for the HDRI, if that is where it came from);
3. any attribution you would like users to show.

Additional context:
We're building a commercial home-design product on top of @pascal-app/editor under the MIT licence, with your copyright notice included. Thank you for open-sourcing the editor!

title: [Tooling] Enforce review-architecture rules as checks; flag one-way changes in PRs
body:
## What does this PR do? Three `review-architecture` blockers that had a "grep tell" become Biome GritQL rules in `scripts/biome/`, wired through `biome.jsonc` overrides. This follows DECISIONS.md T-001 ("no source-grep … tests (use Biome rules)") and the existing `raw-scene-enumeration` / `cross-package-src-in-tests` plugins. `packages/core/src/architecture.test.ts` is unchanged from `main`. - **`kind-switch.grit` (E-002), `packages/viewer/src` + `packages/editor/src`.** Flags a `case ''` arm of a `switch` on `.type` or `nodeType`. The discriminant is matched through parentheses, `!`, `as` and `satisfies`. Only arms of that switch count, not arms of a nested switch. Switches on other values whose labels happen to match a kind (breadcrumb kind, sidebar panel, annotation role) are not flagged. `packages/nodes/src/index.test.ts` fails if the rule's kind list misses a built-in kind. - **`move-handler-scene-write.grit` (E-007), `packages/nodes/src`.** Flags `updateNode` / `updateNodes` in a handler registered with `.on(':move', …)`. The handler can be inline, or a variable or function declared in the same file; a variable's whole initializer is searched, so `useCallback(…)` / `useMemo(…)` wrappers are covered. - **`shift-snap-bypass.grit` (E-004), `packages/nodes/src` + `packages/editor/src`.** Flags a Shift read that chooses between a snapped value (`Math.round`, or a `*snap*` / `*quantize*` call other than an `is…Snap…Active()` mode gate) and a raw one. That covers ternaries, if/else, and an early `return ` in a function that snaps. It also flags a `bypassSnap`-style flag read from Shift. Shift for multi-select, rotation direction, sounds, and modifier-click guards (`if (… || e.shiftKey) return false`) is not flagged. Each diagnostic tells the agent what to do instead and cites the DECISIONS id. Legacy files are `!` entries in each override. `scripts/biome-architecture-plugins.test.ts` (added to the root `test` script) runs each plugin on each listed file and fails once a file no longer violates, so the lists only shrink. The legacy sites, re-seeded against the Biome rules, are the same as before; the statement-form and wrapper cases found no new violations: - kind switch: `editor/src/lib/geometry-script/author.ts`, `editor/src/lib/point-ask/suggestions.ts`, `editor/src/lib/print-feature-thickness.ts`, `viewer/src/ui/lib/node-display-label.ts` - move write: `nodes/src/door/tool.tsx` (the draft door's `roof:move` hover) - Shift bypass: `editor/src/components/editor/floorplan-panel.tsx` (guide rotation), `nodes/src/building/move-tool.tsx`, `nodes/src/shared/polygon-centroid-move.ts` The allow-list works per file, the granularity Biome overrides support. Biome reports an unused `biome-ignore` only as a warning, and `biome check` doesn't fail on warnings, so per-site suppressions could not ratchet. The skill's prose for these three rules now points to the Biome rules, and the stale MEP Known-legacy entry is gone (those tools no longer read `shiftKey`). `DECISIONS.md` E-002, E-004 and E-007 name the rules under "Enforced". Across the docs the prose is shorter. `open-pr` §2 gains one sentence: the description must name any one-way change (migration, schema or contract change, production data, publish path) and keep it in its own small PR. Not enforced: the Alt alignment-bypass rule. Alt held is the sanctioned force/free modifier, and syntax alone cannot tell an alignment bypass in drafting apart from legitimate Alt-free placement. It stays as review prose. No one-way changes in this PR. ## How to test 1. `bun run check` reports no errors (warning count is unchanged from `main`). 2. Append `export function probe(node: { type: string }) { switch ((node as any).type) { case 'skylight': return 1 } }` to `packages/viewer/src/lib/reveal-candidates.ts` and run `bunx biome lint packages/viewer/src/lib/reveal-candidates.ts`. It should report the E-002 message on `'skylight'`. 3. `bun test scripts/biome-architecture-plugins.test.ts`: 11 pass. Add `"!packages/viewer/src/lib/reveal-candidates.ts"` (unmodified) to the kind-switch override and rerun. It should fail and ask you to delete the entry. 4. With packages built, `cd packages/nodes && bun test src/index.test.ts -t kind-switch` passes. Remove `|zone` from `kind-switch.grit` and it fails, naming `zone`. ## Screenshots / screen recording N/A — non-visual change ## Checklist - [ ] I've tested this locally with `bun dev` - [x] My code follows the existing code style (run `bun check` to verify) - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (if applicable) - [x] This PR targets the `main` branch

title: editor, viewer: Graphite chrome for the editor's menus, bars, docks and panels
body:
## What does this PR do?

Moves the editor's own chrome to the Graphite design system, so the hosted app and the standalone editor look like one product. It is a visual change only: no behaviour, store or schema changes.

**Tokens**
- `@pascal-app/viewer/ui/theme.css` now ships the Graphite palette for light and dark: canvas, panel, raised (`#18181b` / `#232327` / `#33333a`), hairlines at 7 %, a dim text colour, and violet (`#8b5cf6`) for state only. New utilities: `bg-canvas`, `bg-raised`, `bg-control`, `bg-selected`, `text-dim-foreground`, `bg-violet-accent`/`-soft`, `text-violet-ink`, `shadow-card`, `shadow-popover`, `shadow-control`, `shadow-selected`.
- `lib/floating.ts` (exported from `@pascal-app/viewer/ui`): one recipe for chrome that floats over the stage (frosted fill, hairline rim, soft drop) and its raised active item.
- The standalone app uses Inter at 13 px and takes its surfaces from the viewer theme; its own `:root` keeps only charts and the sidebar.

**Surfaces**
- **Side menu:** 28 px rows with a 7 px radius; 13 px medium labels; 18 px rich icons, greyed at 70 % until selected or hovered; 11.5 px dim section headings. The active row has no shadow, and the right hairline is gone. It still renders whatever groups the host passes in.
- **View bar:** a floating pill (3 px padding, frosted, soft shadow) with 28 px segments. The active view is raised. Split is now a ghost segment inside the same pill, not a separate box at the far right.
- **Level card and navigation hint:** floating cards with a 12 px radius. Level rows are 28 px with an 8 px radius, and heights are in Geist Mono at 10.5 px, dim.
- **Tool dock:** one floating pill of 28 px round buttons. The selected tool is raised rather than tinted blue, red, cyan or violet, and rich icons are grey until selected. Separators are `h-4 w-px` hairlines, and key hints are Geist Mono at 9 px. The time chip and the compass are their own floating pills, aligned to the 34 px dock.
- **Command palette:** 12 px radius on the popover surface, a 36 px search field over a hairline, and 28 px rows with a 7 px radius. Group labels are 11.5 px, dim and sentence case ("Viewer controls", "Export and share", "Wall mode", "Go to level"). Footer keys are Geist Mono keycaps.
- **Preview chrome:** the header and level cards float with a 12 px radius, and "Levels", "Zones", "Rooms" and "Units" are now sentence case. The stage switcher and the controls dock match the editor's view bar and dock. They stay dark-scoped, as before.
- **Tool panels:** panel headers are 13.5 px semibold.
  - Segmented controls are a raised track with a selected segment.
  - Select, toggle and action controls are 28 px with a 7 px radius on a control fill. The toggle check uses violet.
  - Build tiles lose their own box: the armed tile is raised.
  - Scene tree rows are 28 px with no hairline between rows.
  - "Scene materials" and the material editor labels are sentence case.

No one-way changes.

## How to test

1. `bun dev`, open a project in the editor, and switch between light and dark.
2. Side menu: rows are compact, icons are grey until you hover or select one, and there is no divider on the right.
3. View bar: 3D, 2D, ⋯ and Split sit in one floating pill. Press `\`: the split opens and Split is raised; swap appears beside it.
4. Bottom dock: pick Select, Measure and Delete. Only the picked one is raised and in colour. The time chip and the compass sit beside the dock at the same height.
5. ⌘K: the palette shows sentence-case group labels and mono keycaps in the footer.
6. Preview: the header and level cards, stage switcher and dock all use the floating style.
7. Build, Paint and Scene panels: check the segmented controls, tiles and tree rows in both themes.
